"Lord, have mercy" (12 times). Prayer: "And grant unto us, O Master..." And the Dismissal.*[^496]

*And in the same manner as the Service of Vespers and Compline of this Sunday was indicated (behold!), so let it be done on the remaining ones also, even unto the Fifth Sunday of the holy month [of the Fast], changing certain parts, concerning which it will be noted in their proper places.*

*It should be known: If it should happen that a brother of ours departs unto God during the days of the Holy Fast, during the week no third-day memorial is made for him until Friday evening; for then a Panikhida is celebrated for him. Likewise also on Saturday the Liturgy is offered for him. And on the next Saturday his ninth-day memorial is held, whether the number of days falls then or not. But his fortieth-day memorial takes place whenever the number of his days is fulfilled. But the oblation, that is, the Prosphora and commemorations for him, begin from New Sunday after Pascha [Thomas Sunday], even unto the completion of 40 days.*[^497]

*Concerning the Feast of the Meeting of the Lord, Chapter 49:*[^498]
*If it happens that the Feast of the Meeting falls on Monday of the First Week of the Fast (for it never occurs later according to the perpetually unalterable Paschalion):*[^499]
*On Cheesefare Sunday Evening: At Small Vespers, all the Stichera are of the Feast, and the Troparion; only at the Aposticha, the Idiomelon of the day twice, and of the Martyrs.*
*AT GREAT VESPERS: After the customary Psalm, we sing:* Blessed is the man *(Ps. 1), the first "Glory..." Stichera on 10: 2 Idiomela from the Triodion for the day, 2; and Prosomoia, 3; and of the Feast, 5. Glory... Both now... of the Feast. Entrance. Great Prokeimenon:* Turn not away Thy face... *with its verses. And the Readings of the Feast. At the Litiya and at the Aposticha, of the Feast. At the Blessing of Loaves, Troparion of the Feast, 3 times; and the customary order, and the Reading of the Feast.*
*AT MATINS: At "God is the Lord," Troparion of the Feast, 3 times. And we recite 3 Kathismata. After the 1st Kathisma: both Sessional Hymns in the Triodion, and the Reading of the Feast. After the 2nd Kathisma and after the 3rd: Sessional Hymns of the Feast, and the Reading of the Feast. Polyeleos. Megalynarion. And the Reading of the Feast.*
*CANON of the Feast with Heirmoi on 6; and the Triodion on 8; and after the Heirmos in the Triodion. But the remaining Odes of the Feast on 14, with the Heirmos; Katavasia of the Feast. After Ode 3, Sessional Hymn of the Feast, 2 times; and the Reading of the Feast. After Ode 6, Kontakion and Ikos of the Feast; and the Prologue. And the 4th Ode and the other we sing as also the 1st with the Triodion. We do not sing "More honorable than the Cherubim." Exapostilarion 3 times. At the Praises, all of the Feast. At the Aposticha, Idiomelon of the day twice, and of the Martyrs. Glory... Both now... of the Feast. After "Our Father," Troparion of the Feast. Litany. 3 great prostrations, and the Dismissal. And the First Hour: Troparion and Kontakion of the Feast; and at the end 3 great prostrations, and the Dismissal, and the customary exit. Likewise on the 3rd day, an exit outside the Monastery, and procession...*

*...of the Monastery. We chant the Third Hour with the Kathisma; Troparion and Kontakion of the Feast; and the Paroimia at the Sixth Hour of the day; and the Reading of the Feast. At the Ninth Hour, we chant the Ninth Hour with Kathisma; and the Reading from the Catechesis of the Studite. The Beatitudes without singing, and "Remember us, O Lord," we say simply. After "Our Father," Kontakion of the Feast; "Lord, have mercy" (40 times); and 3 prostrations, and the Dismissal. We chant Vespers without Kathisma and without prostrations.*
*Stichera on 10: 2 Idiomela of the Triodion for the day, 2; and Prosomoia, 3; and of the Feast, 3; and of Saint Symeon, 3. And we say the 3rd Sticheron of the Saint with the addition, Verse:* Thou art a priest forever after the order of Melchizedek *(Ps. 109:4). Glory... Both now... of the Feast. Entrance with the Gospel. Prokeimenon and Reading of the day. And "Let my prayer be set forth." And the Little Diaconal Litany. Troparion. Glory... Both now... Kontakion of the Feast in the Tone; and the Trisagion. Prokeimenon, Epistle, Alleluia, Gospel, and Communion Hymn of the Feast; and the Liturgy of Saint John Chrysostom.*
*At the Trapeza: we eat dry food and drink wine; but we do not eat fish.*
*On that same day, at Compline we chant according to custom from the Canon of Andrew the appointed portion, but we do not make prostrations; only at "Glory to God in the highest," and at the Trisagion, 3 great prostrations each; and at "More honorable than the Cherubim," 3 with the Prayer, and 12 other [metanias]; and at the final Trisagion, 3 prostrations, and the Dismissal.*[^500]

*If it happens that the Finding of the Head of the Forerunner falls on Monday of the First Week of the Fast, the feast of the Forerunner is sung entirely on Cheesefare Sunday, outside the church of the dedication; but if it is the church of the patron, it is chanted here, just as for the Meeting, only with the Liturgy of the Presanctified Gifts.*[^501]

---

# PART II: THE HOLY AND GREAT FORTY DAYS (FIRST THROUGH SIXTH WEEKS OF THE GREAT FAST)

## Monday of the First Week of Great Lent (Clean Monday)

*The Paraklesiarches strikes the simandron before dawn, as much as for the evening comfort. And we all assemble according to custom in the church.*[^502]

*We chant the MIDNIGHT OFFICE without prostrations, only at the end 3 great prostrations with the prayer: "O Lord and Master of my life..." which takes place on the first day only; for on the remaining days of the Holy and Great Fast we chant the Midnight Office all with their customary prostrations.*[^503]

*Then the Priest having arisen makes the customary bow to the Superior, and enters the holy Sanctuary, and taking the censer stands before the holy Table, and censing cross-wise, exclaims:*

**Priest:** *Blessed is our God always, now and ever, and unto ages of ages.*

*And we answering: Amen. The Priest goes forth and censes; and the appointed psalmist says the Trisagion, always without metanias. After "Our Father," the Priest exclaims:*

**Priest:** *For Thine is the kingdom...*

*And after "Amen," "Lord, have mercy" (12 times). [O come, let us worship (3 times) without metanias. And Psalms 19 and 20. At their conclusion, the Trisagion without metanias. After "Our Father," the customary Troparia. While these are sung, the Priest censes the holy Sanctuary and the whole Church. Then the Ektene: "Have mercy on us, O God..." then "For the pious sovereigns..." He commemorates neither the Hierarch nor the Igumen. Exclamation:* "For Thou art a merciful God and the Lover of mankind..." *Reader: "Amen. And say: In the name of the Lord, bless, father."][^504]*

*And again the Priest:*

**Priest:** *Glory to the Holy, Consubstantial, Life-creating, and Undivided Trinity, always, now and ever, and unto ages of ages!*

*And the brother whose day it is, standing in the appointed place, says: Amen.*

*And we recite the Six Psalms without metanias with all attention, not hurrying, but with the fear of God, as invisibly conversing with God Himself. And no one has authority to whisper, nor to spit or clear the throat, but rather to give heed unto the words spoken by the Psalmist, having hands folded upon the chest, heads bowed, and eyes directed downward, beholding with the eyes of the heart toward the East, that we may pray for our sins, remembering death, future torment, and life everlasting.*[^505]

*And at the beginning of the fourth psalm [Ps. 87 LXX], the Priest says the Morning Prayers.*
*At the conclusion of the Psalms: Glory... Both now... Alleluia (twice). The clerics sing "Alleluia" with chant. Then the Great Ektene by the Deacon, and the Priest gives the Exclamation.*
*The appointed monk sings "Alleluia" in the Tone of the Oktoechos appointed for the week.*
*Verse 1:* From night my spirit seeks Thee early in the morning, O God, for Thy commandments are a light upon the earth *(Isa. 26:9).*
*Verse 2:* Learn righteousness, ye that dwell upon the earth *(Isa. 26:9).*
*Verse 3:* Zeal shall take hold of an uninstructed people, and now fire shall devour the adversaries; Lord, add Thou evils unto them, add evils unto the glorious of the earth *(Isa. 26:11, 15).*
*Verse 4:* Like as a woman with child, that draws near the time of her delivery, is in pain, and cries out in her pangs; so have we been before Thee, O Lord *(Isa. 26:17).*
*And after each verse, Alleluia (3 times). Then the Trinity Hymns (Triadica) of the Tone, either three to one or thrice one, as seems best to the Superior. It is sung with compunction, loudly and slowly with melody. At the second verse: Glory... both parts... Both now...*[^506]
*Then we recite the Kathismata from the Psalter, censing 3 times. And after each Stasis [Antiphon] at the "Alleluia," we all make 3 metanias uniformly, following the Igumen or the Ecclesiarches.*

*At the 1st Kathisma: Penitential Sessional Hymns in the Tone of the Oktoechos.*
*Then the Reading from Saint Ephrem; for from this day Saint Ephrem begins, and is read until Tuesday of Palm Week [Behold!].*[^507]

*At the 2nd Kathisma: Sessional Hymn from the Triodion, of Lord Joseph, Tone 2, Podoben: "Being a wellspring of loving-kindness" (Милосе́рдїя сꙋ́щи и҆сто́чникъ):*[^508]

*Sessional Hymn:* With the divine beginning of the Fast, let us acquire compunction, crying aloud from the soul: "O Master Christ, receive our prayer as choice incense, and deliver us, we pray Thee, from foul corruption and terrible torment, as Thou alone art easy to be entreated!"

*Glory: the same. Both now: Theotokion:*

*Theotokion:* Being a wellspring of loving-kindness, account us worthy of mercy, O Mother of God; look upon the people who have sinned; show forth Thy power as always; for hoping in thee, we cry out unto thee: "Rejoice!" even as once did Gabriel, supreme commander of the bodiless hosts!

*And again a Reading from Saint Ephrem.*

*After the 3rd Kathisma: Sessional Hymn of Lord Theodore the Studite, Tone 2, Podoben: "We venerate Thine all-pure icon" (Пречи́стомꙋ ти ѻ҆́бразꙋ покланя́емся):*[^509]

*Sessional Hymn:* Let us begin the all-honorable abstinence with brightness, radiant with the rays of the holy commandments of Christ our God, with the brightness of love, the splendor of prayer, the chastity of purity, and the strength of manly courage; so that, bearing light, we may attain unto the Holy and Three-day Resurrection which grants incorruption unto the world!

*Glory: the same. Both now: Theotokion:*

*Theotokion:* Having acquired thine unconquerable prayer in afflictions, I am delivered beyond hope from those who trouble me, wonderfully, O Mother of God! Thou ever hastenest unto those who ask of thee with faith; receive, O Sovereign Lady, these small thank-offerings, and instead of them become my helper unto ages!

*Again a Reading from the Lausiac History. Then Psalm 50. And the customary prayer: "O God, save Thy people..." Then the exclamation. And immediately we begin Ode 1 from the Psalter. We chant: "Unto the Lord..." in the Tone of the Canon in the Menaion of the Saint of the day. And keep the verses on 14, beginning from: "The waters grew thick as a wall" (Exod. 15:8). And we sing in the Menaion to the Saint with the Heirmos...*[^510]

*...with the Heirmos on 6. And from the verse:* Then the dukes of Edom were amazed *(Exod. 15:15), the Triodion begins, and we recite 4 troparia of Lord Joseph. At the verse:* The Lord shall reign forever and ever *(Exod. 15:18), the Triodion of Lord Theodore the Studite begins. And one choir sings one Troparion, and the other choir the other. Then as both choirs are chanting thus, [the monks of each choir having come together, and the Canonarch standing in their midst,] we proclaim [or "Glory"] with the highest voice, and we sing the Trinity Troparion of the Triodion. "Both now": Theotokion. And again with the highest voice we say: "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee!" And we sing the other Troparion of Lord Theodore the Studite; for the ode has 5 troparia. And afterwards we sing the Katavasia, the Heirmos of the second Canon. Thus do we do throughout the whole Holy Forty Days.*[^511]

*For the Biblical Odes from the Psalter are recited across six days of the holy month [of the Fast] at Matins as follows: In the first week: on the 5th and on the 6th. On Monday, Ode 1; on Tuesday, Ode 2; on Wednesday, Ode 3; on Thursday, Ode 4; on Friday, Ode 5, Ode 6, Ode 7, Ode 8, and Ode 9. And the 9th Ode we always sing: "My soul doth magnify the Lord." And in the 2nd, 3rd, and 4th weeks of the Fast, the Odes are said as also in the 1st week. Only on Saturday do we sing the 2nd Ode entirely with refrains; likewise the 7th, 8th, and 9th. Know that when we say the regular Ode from the Psalter, then the other and the 4th according to the Triodia we always say.*[^512]

*Know this also: If it happens that two Saints fall in order in the Menaion: We sing in the Oktoechos the Penitential Canon with the Heirmos on 6, and of the Saints both canons on 8. But when the Triodion arrives in the Triodion, the Canon in the Oktoechos is omitted; and we sing both Canons in the Menaion to the Saints with the Heirmos on 6, and in the Triodion as was indicated before. And thus do we do on every day throughout the whole Holy Forty Days. After Ode 3, Sessional Hymn in the Menaion, and Reading in the Lausiac History. After Ode 6, Martyr's Sessional Hymn in the Oktoechos of the current Tone, and Reading in the Prologue for the day.*[^513]

*Triodion of Lord Joseph. Tone 2.*

*Ode 1, Tone 2. Heirmos: Come, ye peoples (Грядѣ́те, лю́дїе):*[^514]

*Troparion 1:* How shall I now bewail my falling away? What beginning of my salvation shall I make, who have lived prodigally? O compassionate One, save me by whatever ways Thou knowest!

*Troparion 2:* Lo, the time of repentance, lo, the saving day, the entrance of the fast! Be vigilant, O my soul, and shut the entries against the passions, looking up unto the Lord!

*Troparion 3:* The surging tempest of sins drags me down into the depth of despair; but fleeing unto the abyss of Thy mercy, save me, O Lord!

*Troparion 4:* I alone have enslaved myself to sin; I alone have opened the doors unto the passions! O Word, ready to forgive, turn me back, O Savior, by Thy tenderheartedness!

*Theotokion:* Having given birth unto the Wellspring of passionlessness, heal me who am wounded by passions, O Maiden, and snatch me from eternal fire, O only divinely graced one!

*Another Triodion, of Lord Theodore the Studite. Heirmos and Tone the same.*

*Ode 1, Tone 2. Heirmos: Come, ye peoples (Грядѣ́те, лю́дїе):*

*Troparion 1:* Come, ye peoples, today let us receive the gift of fasts as a God-given time of repentance, and in it let us entreat the Savior!

*Troparion 2:* The time of contests has arrived, it has been lifted up; the arena of the fast! Let us all zealously begin this, offering virtues unto the Lord as gifts!

*Glory: Trinity Hymn:*

*Trinity Hymn:* O simple Unity, thrice-radiant, sovereign Trinity, all-powerful and all-living, God and Lord, Father Almighty, Son, and Spirit: save those who honor Thee!

*Both now: Theotokion:*

*Theotokion:* Let us hymn the holy mountain of God, Mary undefiled, from whom the Sun of Righteousness has shone forth for those in darkness, Christ the Life of all (Mal. 4:2; Isa. 9:2)!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*

*Troparion 3:* A chariot of fire received the marvelous Elijah (4 Kings [2 Kings] 2:11); and Moses, armed with fasting, was shown forth a beholder of unspeakable [mysteries]...[^515]

...mysteries; and having received these things, let us behold Christ!

*Katavasia: Come, ye peoples, let us sing a song unto Christ God, Who divided the sea and led through the people whom He had released from the bondage of Egypt; for He is glorified!*

*At Ode 6, Martyr's Sessional Hymn in the Oktoechos in the Tone of the week.*[^516]

*Ode 8, Tone 2. Heirmos: In the fiery furnace (Въ пе́щи ѻ҆́гненной):*

*Troparion 1:* Consumed with fire by pleasures and darkened in the sight of the soul, having renewed me with the fire of Thy fear, O Christ, illumine me with the light of salvation, that I may glorify Thee unto all ages!

*Troparion 2:* Having hated the satiety of the passions, feed upon the sweet food of good deeds, and delight thyself yet more with the sweetness of the fast, turning away from the bitterness of pleasures, O my humble soul, and live unto the ages!

*Troparion 3:* Scorched in soul and darkened by the drunkenness of the passions, I look in no wise unto Thee, the only God. Therefore have compassion upon me and enlighten me, and open unto me the doors of repentance!

*Theotokion:* O pure one who hast made heavenly our earthly and corruptible nature, through thy fervent prayer make supplications and entreaties unto thy God and King and the God and King of all, that we may be directed aright!

*Another Canon, of Lord Theodore. Tone the same. Heirmos: Him Who of old dewed (Дре́вле ѡ҆роси́вшаго):*[^517]

*Troparion 1:* Let us, the faithful, brightly meet the entrance of the fast, and let us not mourn; but let us wash our faces with the water of dispassion, blessing and supreme-exalting Christ unto the ages!

*Troparion 2:* Having anointed the head of the soul with the oil of compassions, let us not speak much unto our Father Who is in the heavens, sending up prayers, blessing and supreme-exalting Him unto all ages!

*Glory: Trinity Hymn:*

*Trinity Hymn:* Let us, the faithful, hymn the co-eternal, unoriginate Father, the Son co-unoriginate, and the Spirit co-eternal and from the Father: consubstantial Persons of the one all-powerful Origin and Dominion!

*Both now: Theotokion:*

*Theotokion:* O Mary, divinely called, truly a place of propitiation for the faithful! For from thee forgiveness is richly granted unto all; cease not to implore Thy Son and Lord on behalf of those who hymn thee!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*

*Troparion 3:* The Lord, having fasted the measure of forty days, hath now sanctified and cleansed these days, O brethren, having reached which we cry aloud: "Bless and supreme-exalt Christ unto the ages!"

*We praise, we bless, and we worship the Lord.*

*Katavasia: Him Who of old dewed the Hebrew children in the flame, the Lord, and marvelously burned the Chaldeans in it, let us hymn, saying: "Bless and supreme-exalt Him unto all ages!"*

*Then the Stichologia of the Magnificat ("More honorable than the Cherubim").*[^518]

*Ode 9, Tone 2. Heirmos: From God, God the Word (Ѿ бг҃а бг҃а сло́ва):*

*Troparion 1:* Let the day of the fast be for thee, O soul, a putting away of sin, and at the same time an inclination toward God and adoption, so that thou mayest escape the precipices of evil, loving only the paths that lead unto that rest!

*Troparion 2:* Having stumbled in thoughts and sinned in the flesh, weep, groan, and cry aloud: "Save me, O Lord, save me, O only gentle One; condemn me not, who am worthy of condemnation, into the fire of that Gehenna!"

*Troparion 3:* Having clothed ourselves in the bright robe of the fast, let us strip off the dark and burdensome garments of drunkenness; and having become radiant with divine virtues, with faith let us behold the light-bearing Sufferings of the Savior!

*Theotokion:* Heal my passionate soul, enfeebled by all the assaults of the wicked demons, O all-pure Sovereign Lady, who didst bear the Healer, Christ the redemption of us who know thee as Maiden and incorrupt Virgin!

*Another Canon, of Lord Theodore. Tone the same. Heirmos: Surpassing nature (Па́че є҆стества̀):*[^519]

*Troparion 1:* Now the season of the holy fasts has arrived; let us begin it in good deeds; for "Fast not in judgments and strifes," He saith (Isa. 58:4)!

*Troparion 2:* Having purified himself with fasting on Mount Horeb, Elijah saw God (3 Kings [1 Kings] 19:8–12); let us also purify our hearts with fasting, and we shall behold Christ!

*Glory: Trinity Hymn:*

*Trinity Hymn:* I worship the one Essence, I hymn the three Persons of the one God of all: Father, and Son, and Holy Spirit, the co-eternal Origin!

*Both now: Theotokion:*

*Theotokion:* Pure one, thou givest birth to a Child; virgin, thou dost suckle with milk! How dost thou remain a virgin in both of these after childbirth? For it is God Who hath done this; inquire not of me how!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*

*Troparion 3:* "One day indeed," he saith, "is the whole life of those on earth; but for those laboring in love there are forty days of the fast," which let us accomplish brightly!

*Katavasia: Her who conceived in her womb according to the flesh, surpassing nature, the Word Who timelessly shone forth from the Father, let us, the faithful, magnify in unceasing hymns!*

*We sing:* It is truly meet to bless thee, O Mother of God, ever-blessed and all-blameless, and the Mother of our God. More honorable than the Cherubim, and beyond compare more glorious than the Seraphim, who without corruption didst bear God the Word: thee, truly the Mother of God, do we magnify. *One prostration.*

*Exapostilarion (Photogogicon): 3 times in the Tone. Ektene: "Again and again..." At the Praises: "Let every breath..." we do not sing stichera. But we recite: "Praise the Lord from the heavens" (Ps. 148), the customary 3 Psalms. And if it happens in the Menaion that two Saints occur in order (Behold!): we sing the stichera to the one in the evening, and to the other at the Praises, 4 stichera, if there are any; but if not, the Priest says:*[^520]

**Priest:** *Unto Thee glory is due, O Lord our God, and unto Thee do we send up glory: to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen. Glory to Thee Who hast shown forth the light and enlightened the world!*

*And he begins the Doxology hymn: "Glory to God in the highest..." and the rest, in a quiet and even voice. And we make 3 prostrations, evenly, each standing in his place. After this, the Priest:*

**Priest:** *Let us complete our morning prayer unto the Lord...*

*And the exclamation. And both choirs having come together, we sing at the Aposticha:*

*At the Aposticha, Idiomelon Stichera, Tone 5:*

*Sticheron 1:* The fast has come, the mother of chastity, the accuser of sins, the herald of repentance, the citizenship of angels, and the salvation of men! O faithful, let us cry aloud: "O God, have mercy on us!"

*Verse:* We were filled in the morning with Thy mercy, O Lord, and we rejoiced and were glad (Ps. 89:14). *And again the same sticheron.*

*Verse 2:* And let the brightness of the Lord our God be upon us (Ps. 89:17).

*Martyr's Troparion:* Blessed is the army of the Heavenly King! For even though the passion-bearers were earthly, yet they hastened to attain the angelic dignity, taking no heed for their bodies, and through their sufferings being accounted worthy of the honor of the incorporeal hosts! By their prayers, O Lord, save our souls!

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*

*Theotokion:* Thee, the Mother of God, the Virgin more honorable and more holy than the Cherubim, do we magnify in voices of hymns; for with soul and body we confess thee as the Mother of God, as having truly given birth unto God incarnate: pray, O all-pure one, for our souls!

*Then: "It is good to give thanks unto the Lord, and to sing praises unto Thy name, O Most High; to proclaim Thy mercy in the morning, and Thy truth every night" (twice) (Ps. 91:2–3). Trisagion, 3 metanias. After "Our Father," when the Priest has said: "For Thine is the kingdom..." we say the Troparion to the Mother of God:*

*Troparion:* Standing in the temple of thy glory, we seem to stand in heaven, O Mother of God, heavenly gate: open unto us the door of thy mercy!

*"Lord, have mercy" (40 times) in a gentle voice. Then: "Lord, bless!" And the Priest begins and says:*

**Priest:** *He that IS blessed is Christ our God, always, now and ever, and unto ages of ages.*

**Choir:** *Amen. O Heavenly King...*

*After this we stand and pray in all mindfulness, saying the Prayer of our Venerable Father Ephrem, dividing it into 3 stases, making also 3 prostrations: "O Lord and Master of my life..." with the individual metanias, during which we say again the prayer likewise, and it takes place.*[^521]

*Then the Superior begins: "O come, let us worship" (3 times), and 3 metanias. And we join the First Hour. And when the third psalm is ended, we say: "Alleluia" (3 times), 3 metanias.*

*It should be known that on all Mondays of the Holy Forty Days, at the First Hour we do not recite a Kathisma.*[^522]

*...but on the other days recite the regular Kathisma, and make 3 metanias at each stasis. Likewise also on Friday the First Hour and the Ninth Hour are without a Kathisma.*

*And the monk appointed for this, standing in the midst of the church, chants with a loud voice the Troparion in Tone 6:*[^523]

*Troparion, Tone 6: In the morning hear my voice, O my King and my God (Ps. 5:4).*

*And we answering and singing with a loud voice on both choirs, 3 times: the choir that began, twice, and the other, once. Then make a genuflection to the ground. Likewise also at the other two verses:*

*Verse 1: Give ear unto my words, O Lord; consider my cry (Ps. 5:2).*
*Verse 2: For unto Thee will I pray, O Lord (Ps. 5:3).*
*And again: In the morning hear my voice...*

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*

*Theotokion:* What shall we call thee, O full of grace? Heaven: for thou hast made the Sun of Righteousness to shine forth! Paradise: for thou hast budded forth the flower of incorruption! Virgin: for thou hast remained undefiled! Pure Mother: for thou hast held in thine arms the Son, the God of all! Implore Him that our souls may be saved! *And 3 metanias.*

*Then we sing on both choirs:*
Order my steps according to Thy word, and let no iniquity have dominion over me (Ps. 118:133).
*And we repeat this.*
Deliver me from the false accusation of men, and I will keep Thy commandments (Ps. 118:134).
*Again the same.*
Make Thy face to shine upon Thy servant, and teach me Thine ordinances (Ps. 118:135).

*And this we say 3 times with a loud voice and slowly:*
Let my mouth be filled with praise, that I may hymn Thy glory and Thy majesty all the day long (Ps. 70:8).

*Trisagion, 3 metanias. After "Our Father," Troparion, Tone 4:*
*Troparion, Tone 4:* Speedily anticipate before we are enslaved unto the enemies who blaspheme Thee and threaten us, O Christ God! Destroy by Thy Cross those who war against us, that they may understand what the faith of the Orthodox can do, through the prayers of the Mother of God, O only Lover of mankind!

*Glory: Tone 6:*
*O Instructor of wisdom... (see fol. 188)[^524]. Both now:*

*Theotokion:* The all-glorious Mother of Christ, holier than the holy angels, let us unceasingly hymn with heart and lips, confessing thee as the Mother of God, as having truly given birth unto God incarnate for us, who prayest unceasingly for our souls!

*"Lord, have mercy" (40 times). "Thou Who at all times and every hour..." "Lord, have mercy" (3 times). Glory... Both now... "More honorable than the Cherubim..." and one prostration. "In the name of the Lord, bless, father." Priest: "O God, be gracious unto us, and bless us, and cause His face to shine upon us..." And we make 3 great prostrations with the Prayer of Saint Ephrem, as written above. Then 12 small metanias. And having kept silence a little, the Superior begins: Trisagion, and 3 prostrations. "Lord, have mercy" (12 times). And the Prayer:*[^525]

*O Christ, the true Light, Who enlightenest and sanctifiest every man that comes into the world: let the light of Thy countenance be signed upon us...*

...that in it we may behold the unapproachable light; and direct our steps unto the doing of Thy commandments, by the intercessions of Thine all-pure Mother and of all Thy saints. Amen.

**Priest:** *Glory to Thee, O Christ God, our hope, glory to Thee!*

**Reader:** *Glory... Both now... Lord, have mercy (twice). Lord, bless!*

*And the Dismissal. Then the Polychronion. And we venerate the Precious Cross which each of us wears upon our breasts, and the holy icons at our places.*

*Then we go out for the Litiya into the narthex. And there the customary prayers are said. And the Catecheses of our Venerable Father Theodore the Studite are read. And they are read without fail on every Wednesday and Friday of the Holy Forty Days, by the Superior or by the Ecclesiarches, as was written above (see fol. 17)[^526]. And there is the conclusion and the dismissal.*

*This order takes place throughout the whole Holy Forty Days at Matins and at the First Hour. And after the dismissal, departing from the church, we go in all silence into our cells, or unto our obedience; and it is not fitting for us to hold conversations with one another in the monastery on the way: for this was maintained by the holy Fathers.*[^527]

*AT THE THIRD HOUR, the Candlelighter strikes the semantron 3 times. And we assemble in the church, each of us making 3 metanias before the holy doors before the beginning, and we venerate the holy icons at our places, and another single metania, and a small bow toward each of the choirs.*

*When the Priest has given the blessing, we begin: "O Heavenly King..." and a bow. Trisagion, and 3 bows. After "Our Father," Exclamation: "For Thine is the kingdom..." Lord, have mercy (12 times). "O come, let us worship" (3 times) and 3 metanias.*

*And the Third Hour is recited according to custom. At the end of the three Psalms, at "Alleluia," 3 metanias. And we begin to recite the regular Kathisma; and at each stasis we make 3 metanias to the ground. And after the Kathisma, the appointed monk, standing in the midst of the church, chants the present Troparion in Tone 6:*[^528]

*Troparion, Tone 6: O Lord, Who didst send down Thine all-holy Spirit at the third hour upon Thine Apostles: take Him not away from us, O Good One, but renew Him in us who pray unto Thee!*

*And while we sing in response, make a genuflection to the ground, and likewise at the other two verses:*
*Verse 1: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me (Ps. 50:12).*
*Verse 2: Cast me not away from Thy presence, and take not Thy Holy Spirit from me (Ps. 50:13).*

*And make a prostration to the ground. And he says: "Glory..." Then: "Both now..."*

*Theotokion:* O Mother of God, thou art the true Vine that didst bud forth for us the Fruit of life: we implore thee, intercede, O Sovereign Lady, together with the holy Apostles, that our souls may find mercy! *And 3 bows. And immediately the Reading from the Ladder (The Climax of Saint John Climacus).*[^529]

*And after the Reading: "Blessed is the Lord God; blessed is the Lord day by day; may the God of our salvation make haste for us: our God is the God of salvation" (Ps. 67:20–21). Trisagion, and 3 metanias. After "Our Father," Troparion, Tone 8:*

*Troparion, Tone 8:* Blessed art Thou, O Christ our God, Who hast shown forth the fishermen as supremely wise, having sent down upon them the Holy Spirit, and through them caught the universe in a net: O Lover of mankind, glory to Thee!

*Glory:*

*Troparion:* Grant speedy and steadfast consolation unto Thy servants, when our spirit is distressed; turn not away from our souls in afflictions, depart not from our thoughts in tribulations! Draw nigh unto us, draw nigh, Thou Who art everywhere; as Thou art ever with Thine Apostles, so also unite Thyself unto us who desire Thee, O compassionate One, that being joined together we may hymn Thee and glorify Thine all-holy Spirit!

*Both now: Theotokion:*

*Theotokion:* The hope and protection and refuge of Christians, the unconquerable wall, the haven of the tempest-tossed for those who grow weak and toil in the deep: thou art she, O all-pure Mother of God! But as one who deliverest the world by thy ceaseless prayer, remember us also, O all-hymned Virgin!

*Then: "Lord, have mercy" (40 times). And the Prayer: "Thou Who at all times and every hour..." etc. And 12 metanias with the Prayer of Saint Ephrem. And 12 others slowly, so that all may be synchronized, and praying a little in silence, according to what was written before. Then the Superior begins the Prayer: "O Master God, Father Almighty..."*

*And the Candlelighter, having made the customary metania to the Superior, goes forth and strikes the semantron 6 times.*

*And after the prayer the appointed monk says: "O come, let us worship" (3 times) and 3 metanias.*

*And we recite the SIXTH HOUR according to the order and rite set forth here, with prostrations. And we recite the regular Kathisma. At each stasis, "Alleluia" and 3 metanias.*

*And after the Kathisma, we sing this Troparion in Tone 2:*[^530]

*Troparion, Tone 2: O Thou Who on the sixth day and hour didst nail to the Cross the sin boldly committed by Adam in Paradise: tear up the handwriting of our sins, O Christ God, and save us!*

*Verse: Give ear, O God... I called upon God, and the Lord heard me (Ps. 54:17).*
*Verse: Evening, and morning, and at noonday will I declare and tell, and He shall hear my voice (Ps. 54:18).*
*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*

*Theotokion:* Seeing that we have no boldness on account of our manifold sins...

...do thou implore Him Who was born of thee, O Virgin Mother of God; for a mother's prayer avails much unto winning the favor of the Master. Despise not the supplications of sinners, O all-pure one; for He is merciful, and able to save, Who also willed to suffer for our sake! *And 3 prostrations.*

*On Monday of the First Week of the Fast, at the Sixth Hour:*

*Troparion of the Prophecy, Tone 5:*[^531]
*O Lord, before Whom all things are terrified and tremble before the face of Thy power: unto Thee do we fall down, O Immortal One, and unto Thee do we pray, O Holy One: Save our souls, by the prayers of Thy saints!*

*Glory: Save our souls... Both now: O Lord...*

*Prokeimenon of the Paroimia, Psalm 1, Tone 4:*
*The Lord knows the way of the righteous, and the way of the ungodly shall perish (Ps. 1:6).*
*Verse: Blessed is the man that hath not walked in the counsel of the ungodly, nor stood in the way of sinners (Ps. 1:1).*

*Reading from the Prophecy of Isaiah (Isaiah 1:1–20):*[^532]

The vision which Isaiah the son of Amoz saw against Judea and against Jerusalem, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, who reigned over Judea (Isa. 1:1).

Hear, O heaven, and give ear, O earth, for the Lord hath spoken: "I have begotten and brought up sons, but they have rejected Me! (Isa. 1:2)

The ox knows his owner, and the donkey his master's crib; but Israel hath not known Me, and My people hath not understood" (Isa. 1:3).

Ah, sinful nation, a people full of sins, an evil seed, lawless sons! Ye have forsaken the Lord, and provoked the Holy One of Israel! (Isa. 1:4)

Why should ye be stricken anymore, adding lawlessness? Every head is for sickness, and every heart for grief (Isa. 1:5);

From the feet even unto the head...

...there is no soundness in it: neither wound, nor bruise, nor festering ulcer; there is no plaster to apply, neither oil, nor bandage (Isa. 1:6).

Your land is desolate, your cities are burned with fire; your country, strangers devour it before your eyes, and it is made desolate and overthrown by foreign peoples (Isa. 1:7).

And the daughter of Zion shall be left like a booth in a vineyard, and like a watch-lodge in a cucumber garden, like a besieged city! (Isa. 1:8)[^533]

And except the Lord of Sabaoth had left us a seed, we would have been as Sodom, and we would have been made like unto Gomorrah! (Isa. 1:9)

Hear the word of the Lord, ye rulers of Sodom; give ear unto the Law of God, ye people of Gomorrah: (Isa. 1:10)

"What unto Me is the multitude of your sacrifices?" saith the Lord. "I am full of the burnt offerings of rams, and the fat of lambs, and the blood of bulls and of goats I desire not! (Isa. 1:11)

Neither if ye come to appear before Me: for who hath required this at your hands? Ye shall no more tread My court! (Isa. 1:12)

If ye bring fine flour, it is vain incense; an abomination it is unto Me! (Isa. 1:13)

Your new moons and Sabbaths and the great day I cannot endure; your fasting and day of rest and your feast days My soul hates! Ye have become a satiety unto Me; no longer will I endure your sins! (Isa. 1:14)

When ye stretch forth your hands unto Me, I will turn away Mine eyes from you; and even if ye multiply your supplication, I will not hear you, for your hands are full of blood! (Isa. 1:15)

Wash yourselves, be ye clean; take away the evil from your souls before Mine eyes; cease from your wickednesses! (Isa. 1:16) Learn to do good; seek judgment, deliver the wronged; judge for the orphan, and plead for the widow! (Isa. 1:17)

And come, let us reason together, saith the Lord: though your sins be as scarlet, I will make them white as snow; and though they be as crimson, I will make them white as wool! (Isa. 1:18)

If ye be willing and obedient unto Me, ye shall eat the good things of the earth; (Isa. 1:19)

But if ye be unwilling and will not obey Me, the sword shall devour you; for the mouth of the Lord hath spoken these things!" (Isa. 1:20)

*Prokeimenon, Tone 7, Psalm 2:*
*Serve the Lord with fear, and rejoice unto Him with trembling (Ps. 2:11).*
*Verse: Why did the heathen rage, and the peoples imagine vain things? (Ps. 2:1).*

*And there is the Reading from the Ladder. Then the Troparion:*
*Let Thy tender mercies speedily anticipate us, O Lord, for we are become exceedingly poor; help us, O God our Savior, for the glory of Thy name! O Lord, deliver us, and purge away our sins, for Thy name's sake (Ps. 78:8–9).*

*Trisagion, with bows. After "Our Father," "For Thine is the kingdom..."*

*Then these Troparia, Tone 2:*

*Troparion 1:* Thou hast wrought salvation in the midst of the earth, O Christ God: Thou hast stretched out Thine all-pure hands upon the Cross, gathering together all the nations who cry: "O Lord, glory to Thee!"

*Glory:*

*Troparion 2:* We venerate Thine all-pure icon, O Good One, asking forgiveness of our transgressions, O Christ God; for of Thine own will Thou wast pleased to ascend the Cross, that Thou mightest deliver those whom Thou hast fashioned from the bondage of the enemy! Therefore with thanksgiving we cry aloud unto Thee: "Thou hast filled all things with joy, O our Savior, Who didst come to save the world!" *And 1 bow.*

*Both now:*

*Theotokion:* Being a wellspring of loving-kindness... (see fol. 174)[^534]. *But on Wednesday and on Friday we say the Stavrotheotokion:* Most glorified art thou, O Virgin Mother of God... *"Lord, have mercy" (40 times). "Thou Who at all times and every hour..." "Lord, have mercy" (3 times). Glory... Both now... "More honorable than the Cherubim..."*

*Priest:* "O God, be gracious unto us..." *And we make the customary metanias with the Prayer of Saint Ephrem. Then the Superior begins the concluding Trisagion, 3 metanias. And we venerate the holy icons at our places, and the Precious Cross upon our breasts. After "Our Father," "Lord, have mercy" (12 times). Then:* "Glory to Thee, O Christ God, our hope, glory to Thee!" *And there is the Dismissal. He commemorates the Saint whose day it is, and the Polychronion. And each of us makes 3 prostrations. This pattern and order ought to take place throughout the whole holy month [of the Fast] at the Third and at the Sixth Hour.*

*CONCERNING THE NINTH HOUR:*
*The Candlelighter strikes nine times upon the semantron[^535]. And we assemble in the church.*
*And when the Priest has given the blessing, we begin: Trisagion, and 3 metanias.*
*After "Our Father," the Exclamation:*
**Priest:** *For Thine is the kingdom...*
**Reader:** *Lord, have mercy (12 times).*
*Then: "O come, let us worship" (3 times) and 3 metanias.*
*And we chant the NINTH HOUR according to custom, with the stichologia and with prostrations. We recite the regular Kathisma of the Psalter, making "Alleluia" with metanias. And after the Kathisma, the Troparion, Tone 8:*[^536]

*Troparion, Tone 8:* O Thou Who at the ninth hour for our sake didst taste death in the flesh, mortify the wisdom of our flesh, O Christ God, and save us!

*Verse 1:* Let my supplication draw near before Thee, O Lord; give me understanding according to Thy word *(Ps. 118:169).*
*Verse 2:* Let my petition come before Thee; deliver me according to Thy word *(Ps. 118:170).*
*And chant this, making a prostration to the ground at each verse.*
*Glory...*
*Then, Both now... Theotokion:*

*Theotokion:* O Good One, Who for our sake wast born of the Virgin, and didst endure crucifixion, Who by death didst overthrow death, and as God didst manifest the Resurrection: despise not those whom Thou hast fashioned with Thy hand; show forth Thy love for mankind, O merciful One; accept the Mother of God who bare Thee, who prays for us; and save, O our Savior, a despairing people!

*3 metanias. And the Reading from the Ladder takes place.*[^537]
*And after the Reading:*
Cast us not off utterly, for Thy holy name's sake; and do not abolish Thy covenant, and take not away Thy mercy from us, for Abraham's sake who was beloved of Thee, and for Isaac Thy servant's sake, and Israel Thy holy one *(Song of the Three Holy Children / Dan. 3:34–35).*

*Trisagion with prostrations. After "Our Father," speak these Troparia:*

*Troparion 1:* Seeing the Author of life hanging upon the Cross, the thief said: "If He Who is crucified with us were not God incarnate, the sun would not have hidden its rays, nor would the earth have quaked in trembling! But Thou Who endurest all things: remember me, O Lord, in Thy kingdom!"

*Glory...*

*Troparion 2:* In the midst of two thieves Thy Cross was found as a balance of righteousness: the one being drawn down into hell by the weight of his blasphemy, while the other was lightened of sins unto the knowledge of theology. O Christ God, glory to Thee!

*Both now...*

*Theotokion:* Beholding the Lamb and Shepherd and Savior of the world upon the Cross, she who bare Him wept and said: "The world indeed rejoices, receiving redemption, but my womb burns, beholding Thy crucifixion, which Thou endurest for all, O my Son and my God!"

*"Lord, have mercy" (40 times). "Thou Who at all times and every hour..." "Lord, have mercy" (3 times). Glory... Both now... "More honorable than the Cherubim..." and the prostrations according to custom, as was indicated beforehand.*[^538]
*Then we stand in order in the choirs.*

*And the choir to whom it falls begins. In Tone 8:*[^539]
In Thy kingdom when Thou comest, remember us, O Lord. Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven. *And the remaining verses, Glory... Both now... And after each verse we sing the refrain:* Remember us, O Lord, when Thou comest into Thy kingdom. *And we sing these Beatitudes loudly and slowly.*
*Then, both choirs having joined together, they sing loudly and with the highest voice:*
Remember us, O Lord, when Thou comest into Thy kingdom. *(1 prostration, all alike to the ground).*
*And again with a higher voice:*
Remember us, O Master, when Thou comest into Thy kingdom. *(1 prostration to the ground).*
*Then with a still higher voice:*
Remember us, O Holy One, when Thou comest into Thy kingdom. *(1 prostration to the ground).*[^540]
*Then the right choir: Verse:* Come unto Him, and be enlightened, and your faces shall not be ashamed *(Ps. 33:6).*
*Left choir: Glory:* The heavenly choir of holy Angels hymns Thee, saying: Holy, Holy, Holy, Lord of Sabaoth, heaven and earth are full of Thy glory!
*Both now:* I believe in one God...
Remit, forgive, pardon, O God, our offenses, voluntary and involuntary...
Our Father...
*Kontakion: the customary of the day, and to the Saint whose temple it is. But if the temple is of Christ, we say first that of the temple, then of the day, and to the Saint of the day, if he have one. Glory: Kontakion:* With the saints give rest... *(for the Forty Days). Both now: Kontakion of the Mother of God:*[^541]

*Theotokion:* Steadfast protectress of Christians, constant mediatrix before the Creator: despise not the cries of prayer of us sinners, but anticipate as good one to help us who faithfully cry unto thee: hasten unto prayer and speed unto supplication, ever protecting, O Mother of God, those that honor thee![^542]

*"Lord, have mercy" (40 times). Glory... Both now... "More honorable than the Cherubim..." "In the name of the Lord, bless, father." Priest: "O God, be gracious unto us..." And 3 great prostrations, and 12 other metanias, as has been indicated many times.*
*And the Paraklesiarches, having made a prostration to the Superior and received a blessing, goes and rings the bells.*
*Then the Beginning of Vespers by the second choir. The appointed monk says:*
*O come, let us worship (3 times), and 3 prostrations.*
*And we chant VESPERS:*
*Psalm 103, with a quiet and gentle voice. The Priest says the 12 evening prayers before the holy doors. After the Psalm: Glory... Both now... Alleluia (3 times), and 3 prostrations. Ektene: 12 [Lord have mercy]. And we recite the Kathisma from the Psalter: Unto the Lord when I was in trouble (Kathisma 18, Ps. 119 LXX)[^543]. At each Antiphon: Glory... Both now... Alleluia (3 times), and three prostrations.*

## Monday of the First Week of the Fast, at Vespers

*At "Lord, I have cried," we set 6 stichera, Tone 2. Composition of Lord Joseph.*
*Tone 2, Podoben: "Surpassing all" (Всѣ́хъ пре́йдꙋ):*[^544]

*Sticheron 1:* I have committed every sin, I have surpassed all in prodigality; if I wish to repent, I have no streams of tears; if I live in slothfulness even now, I am guilty of torment! But grant me amendment, O only Good God, and have mercy on me!

*Sticheron 2:* Grant me a shower of tears, O Christ, on the fair day of the Fast, that I may weep and wash away the defilement that comes of pleasures, and may appear cleansed before Thee, when Thou shalt come as Judge from heaven, O Lord, to judge mankind, as the only Judge and righteous One!

*Another Sticheron, Tone 5. Of Lord Theodore the Studite.*
*Tone 5, Podoben: "O venerable father" (Преподо́бне ѻ҆́тче):*[^545]

*Sticheron 3:* Come ye fervently, O faithful! Having the firm armor of the Fast as a shield, let us turn aside every wile of the enemy's deception! Let us not be burned by lustful passion, nor fear the fire of temptations, for the sake of which Christ God crowns us with the rewards of endurance! Therefore praying with boldness, we fall down crying aloud, asking peace, and great mercy for our souls!

*And in the Menaion of the Saint, 3 stichera.*
*Glory... Both now... Theotokion in the same Tone, and the same Podoben. O Joyous Light (Phos Hilaron).*
*Then the Prokeimenon, Tone 6, Psalm 3:*
*Salvation is of the Lord, and Thy blessing is upon Thy people (Ps. 3:9).*
*Verse: O Lord, why are they multiplied that afflict me? (Ps. 3:2).*

*Reading from Genesis (Gen. 1:1–3):*[^546]
*(Chapter 1)*
1. In the beginning God made heaven and earth.
2. But the earth was invisible and unformed, and darkness was upon the abyss, and the Spirit of God was borne above the water.
3. And God said: "Let there be light," and there was light.

4. And God saw the light, that it was good; and God divided between the light and between the darkness.
5. And God called the light, Day; and the darkness He called Night. And there was evening, and there was morning, one day.
6. And God said: "Let there be a firmament in the midst of the water, and let it divide between water and water." And it was so.
7. And God made the firmament; and God divided between the water which was under the firmament, and between the water which was above the firmament.
8. And God called the firmament, Heaven. And God saw that it was good; and there was evening, and there was morning, a second day.
9. And God said: "Let the water which is under heaven be gathered together into one collection, and let the dry land appear." And it was so. And the water which was under heaven gathered together into its collections,
10. and the dry land appeared. And God called the dry land, Earth; and the gatherings of the waters He called Seas. And God saw that it was good.
11. And God said: "Let the earth sprout herb of grass, sowing seed according to its kind and according to its likeness; and fruit trees bearing fruit, whose seed is in itself according to its kind upon the earth." And it was so.
12. And the earth brought forth herb of grass, sowing seed according to its kind and according to its likeness upon the earth; and fruit trees bearing fruit, whose seed is in itself,
13. according to its kind upon the earth. And God saw that it was good. And there was evening, and there was morning, a third day.

*Prokeimenon, Tone 5, Psalm 4:*[^547]
*The Lord will hear me when I cry unto Him (Ps. 4:4).*
*Verse: When I called upon Thee, Thou heardest me, O God of my righteousness (Ps. 4:2).*

*Reading from Proverbs (Prov. 1:1–7):*[^548]
*(Chapter 1)*

1. The Proverbs of Solomon, son of David, who reigned in Israel:
2. To know wisdom and instruction, and to understand words of discernment;
3. To receive also turning of words and resolution of dark sayings; to understand true righteousness, and to direct judgment;
4. That he might give shrewdness unto the simple, and to the young youth perception and understanding.
5. Hearing these things, the wise man shall be wiser, and the discerning man shall acquire guidance.
6. Understand ye a parable and a dark saying, the sayings of the wise and their riddles.
7. The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord; and good understanding have all they that do it. Piety toward God is the beginning of perception, but wisdom and instruction the ungodly set at naught.
8. Hear, my son, the laws of thy father, and reject not the covenants of thy mother;
9. For thou shalt receive a crown of graces upon thy head, and a gold chain about thy neck.
10. My son, let not ungodly men entice thee, neither consent thou!
11. If they entreat thee, saying: "Come with us, take part in blood; let us hide in the earth a righteous man unjustly;
12. And let us swallow him alive as hell, and let us take away his memory from the earth;
13. His precious possession we shall take, and we shall fill our houses with spoils;
14. Cast in thy lot among us, let us all acquire a common purse, and let one pouch be for us!"
15. Walk not in the way with them, turn aside thy foot from their paths;
16. For their feet run to evil, and are swift to shed blood!
17. For not without cause...

17. ...are nets stretched out for winged birds.
18. For they that partake in murder treasure up evils for themselves;
19. and the destruction of lawless men is evil. These are the ways of all that commit iniquity; for by ungodliness they take away their own soul.
20. Wisdom is hymned in the exits, and in the broad squares she walks with boldness!

*Then: "Vouchsafe, O Lord, in this evening..." and 3 metanias.*
*Priest: "Let us complete our evening prayer unto the Lord..." After the exclamation, both choirs chant together:*[^549]

*At the Aposticha, Idiomelon Sticheron, Tone 3:*

*Sticheron 1:* Let us fast with an acceptable fast, well-pleasing unto the Lord! True fasting is the estrangement from evils, the restraint of the tongue, the putting aside of wrath, the severance of lusts, of slander, falsehood, and perjury: the diminution of these is true fasting and acceptable!

*Verse: Unto Thee have I lifted up mine eyes, O Thou that dwellest in heaven (Ps. 122:1).*
*And again the same Sticheron.*
*Verse 2: Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us (Ps. 122:3). Martyr's Sticheron:*

*Sticheron 2:* Great is the power of Thy martyrs, O Christ! For they lie in the tombs, and drive away evil spirits, and have abolished the power of the enemy, contending for piety through faith in the Trinity!

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*

*Theotokion:* O Mother of God, mediatrix for all who have need! In thee we take courage, in thee we boast, in thee is all our hope: pray thou to Him Who was born of thee for thine unprofitable servants!

*Then the Canonarch makes the customary metania to the choirs, and likewise both choirs toward each other; and they step back to their places.*
*"Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart in peace..." and the rest as yesterday evening (see fol. 170)[^550].*
*And after the prayer "O Heavenly King..." we say secretly the prayer of our Venerable Father Ephrem: "O Lord and Master of my life..." and we make 3 great prostrations and 12 small ones. And again the aforementioned prayer, and one prostration. Then the Superior begins the Trisagion; after "Our Father," 3 prostrations. After "For Thine is the kingdom..." "Lord, have mercy" (12 times).*

*Then the prayer:*
All-holy Trinity, consubstantial dominion, undivided kingdom, cause of all goods: be well-pleased also toward me, a sinner! Confirm and give understanding to my heart, and take away all my defilement; enlighten my mind, that I may always glorify, hymn, and worship Thee, saying: One is Holy, One is Lord, Jesus Christ, unto the glory of God the Father. Amen.[^551]

*Then: "Blessed be the name of the Lord..." (3 times) and 3 metanias. Glory... Both now...*
*I will bless the Lord at all times (Ps. 33).*

*When we set the Trapeza, we say Psalm 144:*[^552]
*I will extol Thee, my God, my King...*
*It is truly meet... and a metania. "In the name of the Lord, bless, father." Priest: "O God, be gracious unto us..." And the other choir sings: "Amen." And: Glory... Both now... "Lord, have mercy" (twice). "Lord, bless." And the dismissal; and 3 prostrations after this. "Amen." The Polychronion.*
*And going down into the narthex, we sing according to custom the Sticheron of the Saint of the Temple. Glory... Both now... Theotokion. The customary Prayers of Departure are said by the Priest. And he commemorates the departed brethren. And the complete Dismissal takes place.*[^553]

*This order takes place throughout the entire week at Vespers when the Presanctified Liturgy is not celebrated; for they have not received the tradition of celebrating the Presanctified Liturgy until Wednesday. Let the whole brotherhood fast according to tradition for the salvation of their souls until Wednesday; but those who are able, let them fast even until Friday.*[^554]
*The Rule of the Holy Mountain [Athos]: On the first day there is absolutely no eating. On Tuesday, on Wednesday, and on Thursday it is fitting to eat one litra of bread and water, and nothing else except salt needed with the bread.*[^555]

*If the Finding of the Precious Head of John the Forerunner (chapter 62)[^556] falls on Tuesday of the Fast, or on other Lenten days:*
*The prostrations are omitted, except three great prostrations at the end of every service.*
*At Vespers: the customary Kathisma. At "Lord, I have cried," stichera on 10. And we chant the Idiomelon of the day, twice; and the Martyr's; and 2 Prosomoia in the Triodion, 3; and of the Forerunner, 4. Glory: of the Forerunner. Both now: Theotokion: "Who would not bless thee..." Entrance. Prokeimenon of the day. The Readings of the day, and of the Forerunner, 3. "Let my prayer be set forth..." And in order, the Divine Liturgy of the Presanctified Gifts.*
*But where the Presanctified Liturgy is not celebrated: after the Kathisma, stichera on 6: 2 of the Triodion, 3 Prosomoia, and of the Forerunner, 3. Glory: of the Forerunner. Both now: Theotokion: "Who would not bless thee..." Entrance. Prokeimenon of the day. Reading of the day, and of the Forerunner. We do not say "Let us all say," but: "Vouchsafe, O Lord, in this evening..." Then: "Let us complete our evening prayer..." Aposticha: 2 of the Triodion, customary; Glory: of the Forerunner; Both now: Theotokion: "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart in peace..." and after the Trisagion, Troparion of the Forerunner; Glory... Both now... Theotokion: "The mystery hidden from the ages..." Ektene: "Have mercy on us, O God..." After this, 3 great prostrations. "Blessed be the name of the Lord..." and "I will bless the Lord..." "It is truly meet..." and the Dismissal, and the Litiya.*
*The Great Midnight Office without prostrations[^557]. After the 1st Trisagion, we say the Troparion of the Forerunner; Glory... Both now... Resurrectional Theotokion in the Tone of the Saint. After the 2nd Trisagion, we say the customary Troparia: "Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us..." "It is truly meet..." and the Trisagion; but "The Lord of hosts is with us" we do not chant, but we say the Kontakion of the Forerunner. Then after "More honorable than the Cherubim..." 3 great prostrations; after "O spotless, undefiled, uncorrupt..." we do not say the Trisagion, and there is the small dismissal.*
*AT MATINS: At "God is the Lord," Troparion of the Forerunner, twice; Glory... Both now... Resurrectional Theotokion in the same Tone. After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymn in the Triodion, and Reading from Saint Ephrem. After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymn in the Triodion, and again Reading from Saint Ephrem. And after the 3rd Kathisma, both Sessional Hymns of the Forerunner, and Reading of the Forerunner. Polyeleos, and Sessional Hymn of the Forerunner, twice; Glory... Both now... Theotokion, and Reading of the Forerunner. Songs of Ascents: 1st Antiphon of Tone 4. Prokeimenon, Tone 4:* There will I make the horn of David to bud *(Ps. 131:17); Verse:* Lord, remember David *(Ps. 131:1). "Let every breath praise the Lord." Gospel of Luke, pericope 31:* A report went out concerning Jesus... *(Luke 7:17–30). Psalm 50. Sticheron of the Forerunner. But we do not say the Canticles in the Psalter. Canon of the Mother of God with the Heirmos on 6, and of the Forerunner on 8; Katavasia:* I shall open my mouth... *And where there is a Tri-Ode, we sing the Canon of the Forerunner with the Heirmos on 6, and the Tri-Ode on 8. After Ode 3, Sessional Hymn of the Forerunner, twice; Glory... Both now... Theotokion, and Reading of the Forerunner. After Ode 6, Kontakion and Ikos of the Forerunner, and the Prologue is read. Exapostilarion of the Forerunner, twice; Glory... Both now... its Theotokion. At the Praises, Stichera of the Forerunner, on 4; Glory: of the Forerunner; Both now: its Theotokion. At the Aposticha: Idiomelon of the day, twice; and the Martyr's; Glory: of the Forerunner; Both now: Theotokion. After "Our Father," Troparion of the Forerunner; Glory... Both now... Resurrectional Theotokion. Ektene: "Have mercy on us, O God..." and 3 great prostrations. And the First Hour.*
*At the First Hour: the regular Kathisma; Troparion and Kontakion of the Forerunner. Likewise also the remaining Hours with the Kathisma, and the Troparion and Kontakion of the Forerunner. And at the end of each service and Hour, 3 great prostrations. The Beatitudes quickly without chanting; after "Our Father," Kontakion of the Forerunner. At Vespers: customary Kathisma; Stichera on 10: 2 Idiomela of the Triodion of the day, twice; and the Martyr's; and 3 Prosomoia; and of the Forerunner, 4 (which are at the Aposticha); Glory: of the Forerunner; Both now: customary Theotokion according to the Tone. Entrance with the Gospel. Prokeimenon and Readings of the day; "Let my prayer be set forth..." Ektene is not said. Prokeimenon, Epistle, Alleluia, and Gospel of the Forerunner. Presanctified Liturgy. Communion Hymn:* Taste and see... *and:* The righteous shall be in everlasting remembrance *(Ps. 111:6). And:* I will bless the Lord... *and the customary conclusion.*[^558]
*This same Typikon is chanted also for the Forty Martyrs, and for any other of the Saints if it falls during the Fast, except Saturdays and Sundays.*[^559]

*Only on Monday at Vespers: Idiomelon Sticheron of the day, twice, in the Triodion; and 3 Prosomoia; and to those Holy Forty Martyrs, 5. The second Canon we chant prior to that day, at Compline: because it is inadmissible for a second Canon with the Forty Martyrs to be chanted at Matins on Lenten days.*[^560]

*ON MONDAY OF THE FIRST WEEK OF THE FAST: CONCERNING COMPLINE:*[^561]
*It is fitting to know that in the Lavra of our Venerable Father Sabbas we do not chant Compline in the Church, but each of us chants it in the cells: for so have we received.*[^562]
*BUT IN PALESTINIAN COENOBIA THEY CHANT COMPLINE THUS:*
*At the 10th hour, the Taper-lighter enters, and having made a metania to the Superior, strikes upon the semantron 12 times. And we assemble in the Church; and each having made the appointed metanias, and having sat down a little, so that all or the majority may assemble.*
*The Priest having arisen from his seat, and having made the customary bow to the Igumen, and standing in his place, gives the blessing, saying:*
**Priest:** *Blessed is our God always, now and ever, and unto ages of ages.*
*And we begin Great Compline with prostrations and with singing. The appointed Monk says: Amen. And he says: "O Heavenly King..." at the end, one prostration; Trisagion, with prostrations as customary. Likewise also at "O come, let us worship": 3 metanias.*
*And straightway he says Psalm 69:* O God, give heed unto my help *(Ps. 69:2). Then he begins the Great Canon, dividing it into 4 parts with the Heirmos, so as to complete it on Thursday evening. At each Ode we sing: Glory... Trinity Hymn; Both now... Theotokion.*
*And at the conclusion of the Canon, he begins Psalm 4:* When I called... *(Ps. 4:2), and the rest in order unto the end, as is depicted in the Horologion.*[^563]

*Canon of Andrew of Crete, the Hierosolymite:*[^564]
*And make 3 metanias at each Troparion:* Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!

*Tone 6. Ode 1. Heirmos:*
*Ode 1. Heirmos:* He was unto me a helper and a protector unto salvation; He is my God, and I will glorify Him, the God of my father, and I will exalt Him: for He is gloriously glorified! (Exod. 15:1–2)[^565]

*Refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee!*

*Troparion 1:* Whence shall I begin to weep for the deeds of my passionate life?

...deeds? What beginning shall I lay, O Christ, for my present lamentation? But as Thou art compassionate, grant me remission of transgressions!

*Refrain:* Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!

*Troparion 2:* Come, wretched soul, with thy flesh: confess unto the Creator of all, and abstain henceforth from former unreason, and offer tears unto God in repentance!

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*[^566]

*Troparion 3:* Emulating the transgression of Adam the first-fashioned, I have recognized myself stripped naked of God, and of the everlasting kingdom and its delight, because of my sins!

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*

*Troparion 4:* Woe is me, wretched soul! Why hast thou become like unto the first Eve? For thou hast looked evilly, and wast wounded bitterly; and thou hast touched the tree, and hast tasted audaciously of the deceitful food!

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*

*Troparion 5:* Instead of the sensory Eve, an intelligible Eve has arisen in me: the passionate thought in the flesh, displaying sweet things, yet ever tasting of a bitter drink!

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*

*Troparion 6:* Worthily was Adam cast out of Eden, because he did not keep Thy commandment, O Savior! What then shall I suffer, who ever cast aside Thy life-giving words?

*Glory... Trinity Hymn:*

*Troparion 7:* Super-essential Trinity, worshipped in Unity: take away from me the heavy burden of sin, and as Thou art compassionate, grant me tears of compunction!

*Both now... Theotokion:*

*Theotokion:* O Mother of God, protectress and hope of them that hymn thee: take away from me the heavy burden of sin, and as pure Sovereign Lady, receive me in repentance!

*Ode 2. Heirmos:*[^567]
*Ode 2. Heirmos:* Attend, O heaven, and I will speak, and will hymn Christ, Who came in the flesh from the Virgin! (Deut. 32:1) *Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 1:* Attend, O heaven, and I will speak; give ear, O earth, to the voice of one repenting before God and singing His praise![^568]

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 2:* Attend unto me, O God, as Thou art compassionate, with Thy merciful eye, and accept my fervent confession!

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 3:* I have sinned more than all men, I alone have sinned against Thee; but take pity, as Thou art good, O Savior, upon Thine own creation!

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 4:* Having fashioned within me the deformity of passions by voluptuous impulses, I have corrupted the beauty of my mind!

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 5:* A tempest of evils holds me fast, O compassionate Lord; but as unto Peter, stretch forth Thy hand unto me also!

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 6:* As the harlot, I also, O compassionate One, offer tears; cleanse me, O Savior, by Thy tender mercy!

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 7:* I have defiled the garment of my flesh, and have sullied that which is according to Thine image, O Savior, and according to Thy likeness!

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 8:* I have darkened the beauty of my soul with the pleasures of passions, and in every way have turned my whole mind into mire!

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 9:* I have rent now my first garment, which the Creator wove for me from the beginning, and therefore I lie naked![^569]

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 10:* I have clothed myself in a torn garment, which the serpent wove for me by his counsel, and I am ashamed!

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 11:* The tears of the harlot, O compassionate One, do I also offer; cleanse me, O Savior, by Thy tender mercy!

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 12:* I looked upon the beauty of the garden, and was deceived in my mind; therefore I lie naked and am ashamed!

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 13:* All the leaders of wickedness have wrought upon my back, lengthening their iniquity upon me! (Ps. 128:3 LXX)[^570]

*Glory... Trinity Hymn:*
*Troparion 14:* Thee, the One God in Three Persons, do I hymn, the God of all: the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit!

*Both now... Theotokion:*

*Theotokion:* O all-pure Virgin Mother of God, who alone art all-hymned, pray fervently that we all may be saved!

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*[^571]
*Ode 3. Heirmos:* Establish Thy Church, O Christ, upon the immovable rock of Thy commandments! (1 Kings / 1 Sam. 2:2 LXX)

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 1:* The Lord once raining down fire from the Lord, burned up the land of Sodom of old! (Gen. 19:24)[^572]

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 2:* Save thyself upon the mountain, O soul, as did that Lot, and escape into Zoar! (Gen. 19:17–22)

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 3:* Flee the conflagration, O soul, flee the burning of Sodom; flee destruction from the divine flame!

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 4:* I confess unto Thee, O Savior: I have sinned, I have sinned against Thee; but remit, forgive me, as Thou art compassionate!

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 5:* I alone have sinned against Thee, I have sinned more than all; O Christ Savior, despise me not!

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 6:* Thou art the Good Shepherd; seek me, the lamb, and despise me not that have gone astray!

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 7:* Thou art sweet Jesus, Thou art my Creator; in Thee, O Savior, shall I be justified!

*Glory... Trinity Hymn:*
*Troparion 8:* O Trinity, One God, save us from delusion, and from temptations and distresses!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* Rejoice, O womb that received God; rejoice, O Throne of the Lord; rejoice, O Mother of our Life!

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*[^573]
*Ode 4. Heirmos:* The Prophet heard of Thy coming, O Lord, and was afraid, how Thou wast to be born of a Virgin and to appear unto men, and he said: "I have heard Thy report, and was afraid; glory to Thy power, O Lord!" (Hab. 3:2 LXX)

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 1:* Despise not Thy works, forsake not Thine own creation, O righteous Judge, though I alone have sinned as a...

...man, more than any man, O Lover of mankind! But Thou hast power as Lord of all to forgive sins!

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 2:* The end draws near, O soul, it draws near, and thou art heedless, thou dost not prepare thyself; the time grows short; arise! The Judge is near, at the very doors! As a dream, as a flower, the time of life passes away; why do we trouble ourselves in vain?

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 3:* Rouse thyself, O my soul! Consider the deeds which thou hast committed, and bring them before thy face; shed drops of thy tears, and speak with boldness thy deeds and thoughts unto Christ, and be justified!

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 4:* There has been no sin in life, nor deed, nor wickedness, which I, O Savior, have not committed: having sinned in mind and word, in choice and purpose, in understanding and action, as no one else ever did!

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 5:* Thence also am I condemned, and convicted am I, wretched one, by my own conscience, than which nothing in the world is more compelling! O Judge, my Redeemer and Knower of hearts: spare and deliver, and save me, wretched one!

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 6:* The ladder which the great one among the Patriarchs beheld of old is a parable, O my soul, of active ascent and of spiritual entrance; if, therefore, thou desirest to live in action and knowledge and contemplation, be renewed![^574]

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 7:* The Patriarch endured the burning heat of day because of privation, and bore the frost of night, making daily provision, pasturing, laboring, and serving, that he might unite two wives unto himself! (Gen. 31:40)[^575]

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 8:* Understand for me two wives to be action and knowledge in contemplation: Leah indeed as action, as having many children; and Rachel...

...as knowledge, as involving much labor; for without labors neither action nor contemplation, O soul, will succeed!

*Glory... Trinity Hymn:*
*Troparion 9:* Undivided in Essence, unconfused in Persons, do I confess Thee in theology: the One Triune Godhead, as co-regnant and sharing one Throne! I cry aloud unto Thee the great hymn, thrice sung on high!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* Thou both givest birth and remainest a maiden, and in both respects abidest a Virgin by nature: He Who is born renews the laws of nature, and the womb gives birth without child-bearing! Where God wills, the order of nature is overcome; for He does whatsoever He wills!

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*[^576]
*Ode 5. Heirmos:* Rising early from the night, O Lover of mankind: enlighten me, I pray Thee, and guide me in Thy commandments, and teach me, O Savior, to do Thy will! (Isa. 26:9 LXX)

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 1:* In night have I passed my life continually; for darkness has been unto me, and deep gloom, and the night of sin; but show me forth, O Savior, as a son of the day!

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 2:* Emulating Reuben, I, wretched one, have wrought an unlawful and lawless counsel against God the Most High, defiling my bed as he did that of his father! (Gen. 35:22)[^577]

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 3:* I confess unto Thee, O Christ King: I have sinned, I have sinned, as of old the brethren who sold Joseph, the fruit of purity and chastity! (Gen. 37:28)

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 4:* By his kinsmen was the righteous soul bound and sold into slavery, sweet one, as a type of the Lord; but thou, O soul, hast wholly sold thyself by thine evils!

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 5:* Emulate the righteous and chaste mind of Joseph, O wretched and inexperienced soul, and commit not fornication in unlawful impulses, continually lawbreaking!

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 6:* Though Joseph lived in a pit at one time, O Master Lord,...

...yet it was as a type of Thy Burial and Resurrection! But what such thing shall I ever offer unto Thee?[^578]

*Glory... Trinity Hymn:*
*Troparion 7:* Thee, O Trinity, do we glorify, the One God: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, Father, and Son, and Spirit: simple Essence, Unity ever worshipped!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* From thee did God, Who created the ages, clothe Himself in my mingled substance, O incorrupt, unwedded Virgin Mother, and united human nature unto Himself!

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*[^579]
*Ode 6. Heirmos:* With my whole heart I cried unto the compassionate God, and He gave ear unto me from the lowest depths of hell, and brought up my life from corruption! (Jonah 2:3–7 LXX)

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 1:* The tears of mine eyes and the sighs from the depths do I purely offer, O Savior, my heart crying aloud: "O God, I have sinned against Thee, cleanse me!"

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 2:* Thou hast turned away from thy Lord, O soul, as Dathan and Abiram; but cry out: "Spare, from the lowest depths of hell, that the chasm of the earth may not swallow thee!" (Num. 16:31–33)[^580]

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 3:* As an enraged heifer, O soul, hast thou become like unto Ephraim; as a gazelle from the snares, preserve thy life, having taken wing by action and mind and contemplation! (Hos. 4:16)

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 4:* The hand of Moses assures us, O soul, how God can whiten and cleanse a leprous life; and despair not of thyself, even though thou art leprous! (Exod. 4:6–7)[^581]

*Glory... Trinity Hymn:*
*Troparion 5:* "I am the Trinity, undivided, divided in Persons, and I am the Unity, united in Nature," says the Father, and the Son, and the Divine Spirit!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* Thy womb bare God unto us, formed in our likeness; but as the Creator of all, do thou implore Him, O Mother of God, that through thy prayers we may be justified!

*Penitential Sessional Hymn, Tone 6:*
*Tone 6, Podoben: "Hope of the world" (Оу҆пова́ніе):*[^582]
*Sessional Hymn:* The tempest of passions and the fierce storm have drowned me in the depth of despair, O Word! But stretch forth Thy mighty right hand, and save me as Peter, through the sacred intercessions of the Mother of God, from the depth of my fierce transgressions! (Matt. 14:30–31)

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*[^583]
*Ode 7. Heirmos:* We have sinned, we have transgressed, we have done unrighteously before Thee, neither have we kept nor done as Thou hast commanded us; yet deliver us not up utterly, O God of the fathers! (Dan. 3:27–34 LXX)

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 1:* I have sinned, I have transgressed, and have rejected Thy commandment, for in sins was I brought forth, and have added sores to my wounds; but do Thou Thyself have mercy on me, as Thou art compassionate, O God of the fathers!

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 2:* The secrets of my heart have I confessed unto Thee, my Judge; behold my humility, behold also my affliction, and give heed to my judgment now, and do Thou Thyself have mercy on me, as Thou art a merciful God of the fathers!

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 3:* When Saul of old lost his father's asses, he suddenly found a kingdom unto renown; but take heed, O soul, do not forget thyself, having preferred thy brutish lusts rather than the kingdom of Christ! (1 Kings / 1 Sam. 9:1–27)[^584]

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 4:* David the forefather of God of old, though he sinned doubly, O my soul, pierced indeed by the dart of adultery, and captured by the tormenting spear of murder; yet thou thyself art diseased with far heavier deeds through thy willful impulses! (2 Kings / 2 Sam. 11–12)

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 5:* David indeed once joined iniquity unto iniquity, for mingling adultery with murder, he showed forth two-fold repentance; but thou thyself, most wicked soul, hast done deeds yet worse, without repenting before God!

*Troparion 6:* David of old depicted, having inscribed as on an icon, a hymn by which he exposed the deed which he had committed, crying: "Have mercy on me, for against Thee only have I sinned, the God of all; do Thou Thyself cleanse me!" (Ps. 50:3–6 LXX)[^585]

*Glory... Trinity Hymn:*
*Troparion 7:* O simple Trinity, undivided, consubstantial, holy Unity, Thou art Light and Lights, and Three Holies, and One Holy is God the Trinity hymned! But sing and glorify, O soul, the Life and Lives, the God of all!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* We hymn thee, we bless thee, we worship thee, O Mother of God; for from the undivided Trinity hast thou brought forth Christ God, and hast opened the heavenly realms unto us who dwell upon earth!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*[^586]
*Ode 8. Heirmos:* Him Whom the heavenly hosts glorify, and before Whom Cherubim and Seraphim tremble, let every breath and creation hymn, bless, and exalt supremely unto all ages! (Dan. 3:57–88 LXX)

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 1:* Have mercy upon me who have sinned, O Savior; raise up my mind unto conversion; receive me repenting, take pity upon me crying aloud: "I have sinned against Thee, O Savior, I have transgressed; have mercy on me!"

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 2:* The charioteer Elijah, having ascended in a chariot of virtues as into heaven, was borne far above earthly things of old; consider his ascent, O my soul! (4 Kings / 2 Kings 2:11)[^587]

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 3:* Elisha of old, having received the mantle of Elijah, received a double grace from the Lord; but thou, O soul, hast had no part in this grace through intemperance! (4 Kings / 2 Kings 2:9–14)

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 4:* The stream of the Jordan was parted of old hither and thither by Elijah's mantle through Elisha; but thou, O my soul, hast had no part in that grace through intemperance! (4 Kings / 2 Kings 2:8, 14)

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 5:* The Shunammite woman of old entertained the righteous man with good disposition, O soul; but thou hast not brought into...[^588]

...thy house either stranger or traveler; therefore shalt thou be cast out of the bridal chamber weeping! (4 Kings / 2 Kings 4:8–10; Matt. 25:10–12)

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
