*Troparion 6:* Thou hast ever emulated the defiled mind of Gehazi, O soul; put away his avarice at least in old age; flee the fire of Gehenna, departing from thine evil deeds! (4 Kings / 2 Kings 5:20–27)[^589]

*Glory... Trinity Hymn:*
*Troparion 7:* O unoriginate Father, Son co-unoriginate, good Comforter, Spirit of uprightness, Begetter of the Word of God, Word of the unoriginate Father, living and creating Spirit: Trinity, Unity, have mercy on me!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* As from crimson dye, O all-pure Virgin, was the spiritual purple robe of Emmanuel[^590], His flesh, woven within thy womb; therefore do we truly honor thee as Mother of God![^591]

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
*Ode 9. Heirmos:* Seedless conception, ineffable birthgiving, of a mother unwedded, incorrupt parturition; for the birthgiving of God renews nature; therefore do all generations magnify thee in orthodox faith as Bride of God and Mother! (Luke 1:48)

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 1:* The mind is wounded, the body has become feeble, the spirit is sick, the word has grown faint, life is mortified, the end is at the doors! What then wilt thou do, O my wretched soul, when the Judge shall come to examine thy deeds?

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 2:* I have brought before thee the Genesis of Moses, and from thence all the covenant Scripture, telling thee of righteous and unrighteous men: of whom thou, O soul, hast emulated the latter and not the former, having sinned against God![^592]

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 3:* The Law has grown weak, the Gospel is idle, and all the Scripture has been neglected in thee; the Prophets have grown powerless, and every righteous word; thy wounds, O soul, have multiplied, there being no physician to heal thee!

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 4:* I have brought before thee examples of the New Scripture, leading thee, O soul, unto compunction; emulate therefore the righteous, but turn away from sinners, and appease Christ through prayers, through fastings, through purity, and through reverent restraint![^593]

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 5:* Christ became man, calling robbers and harlots unto repentance; repent, O soul! The door of the Kingdom is already opened, and Pharisees and publicans and repenting adulterers seize it before thee! (Matt. 11:12; 21:31–32)

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 6:* Christ became man, partaking of my flesh, and all things that belong to nature did He willingly fulfill, sin alone excepted: showing forth unto thee, O soul, a likeness and an image of His own condescension! (Heb. 2:14; 4:15)

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 7:* Christ summoned the Magi, O Savior, called together the Shepherds, showed forth a multitude of infants as martyrs, glorified the Elder and the aged Widow: whom thou, O soul, hast not emulated, neither in action nor in life; but woe unto thee when thou shalt be judged! (Matt. 2:1–18; Luke 2:8–38)

*Refrain: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!*
*Troparion 8:* Having fasted forty days in the wilderness, the Lord afterward hungered, showing forth His human nature; be not slothful, O soul, if the enemy assault thee: by prayer and fasting let him be beaten back from thy feet! (Matt. 4:1–11)[^594]

*Glory... Trinity Hymn:*
*Troparion 9:* Let us glorify the Father, let us exalt the Son, let us faithfully worship the Divine Spirit: the undivided Trinity, Unity according to Essence, as Light and Lights, and Life and Lives, giving life and enlightening the ends of the world!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* Preserve thy flock, O all-pure Mother of God; for in thee does it faithfully dwell as monastics, in thee is it established, and through thee conquering, it is above...

...every temptation, and captures enemies, and accomplishes obedience!

*Troparion to St. Andrew of Crete:*
*Troparion:* O blessed Andrew, thrice-blessed father, shepherd of Crete: cease not to pray for those who hymn thee, that we all may be delivered from affliction, and sorrow, and corruption, and that we who ever honor thy memory may be freed from sins![^595]

*And both choirs sing the Heirmos: "Seedless conception," and a prostration to the ground. After this, "When I called..." (Ps. 4:2), and the rest of Great Compline in order, as is set down in the Horologion. Canon to the Mother of God. Trisagion. After "Our Father," the Troparia: "O Lord of hosts, be with us," with chanting.*[^596]

*And be it known that we have set down this one day of the Holy Forty Days carefully and accurately, that it may be a model and demonstration and spiritual rule in Christ Jesus our Lord for the whole Holy Forty Days.*[^597]

## Tuesday of the First Week of Great Lent

*The Midnight Office we chant with the Blameless [Kathisma 17], with metanias, as also the rest of the service.*
*AT MATINS, after the 1st Stichologia, Sessional Hymns from the Octoechos.*
*After the 2nd Stichologia: Sessional Hymns, Tone 2.*
*Tone 2, Podoben: "Most blessed" (Преблгⷭ҇ве́ннаѧ):*[^598]
*Sessional Hymn 1:* Most blessed is the grace of the all-honorable Fast; for Moses was glorified thereby, and received the Law in letters upon tablets; and other youths were shown forth stronger than fire! In this fast, therefore, quench the flaming passions of the flesh, crying aloud unto Christ the Savior: "Grant conversion unto us all, and deliver us from Gehenna!" (Exod. 34:28; Dan. 3:19–27)

*Glory... Another Sessional Hymn, in the same Tone:*
*Tone 2, Podoben: "The doors of compassion" (Млⷭ҇рді́а две́ри):*[^599]
*Sessional Hymn 2:* The time of repentance has arrived, to show forth the fruits of abstinence; O my soul, look upon those who repented before thee, cry aloud unto Christ: "I have sinned, save me, as Thou didst save..."

...the Publican, O Master, who sighed from his heart, O Good One, Who alone art plenteous in mercy! (Luke 18:13)

*Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* Fervent protectress of Christians, ever pray to Thy Son, O Mother of God, that we may be delivered from all malice and cruelty of the adversary, and that forgiveness may be granted us for what we have sinned, for the sake of the tender compassion of His mercies, through thy prayers, O Virgin Mother!

*After the 3rd Stichologia: Sessional Hymn, Tone 5.*
*Tone 5, Podoben: "O Lord, the cup of torment" (Гдⷭ҇и, ча́шу му́ки):*[^600]
*Sessional Hymn:* Today, as we keep the second day of saving abstinence, we cry aloud unto Thee: soften the hearts of us Thy servants, and accept our prayers offered in fear, granting us the course of the Fast well run, purification, and great mercy!

*Glory... the same. Both now... Theotokion.*
*Tone 5, Podoben: "The Word co-unoriginate" (Собезнача́лное Сло́во):*[^601]
*Theotokion:* Divine flower that sprouted from the root, Ark, and Lampstand, and all-golden Jar, Holy Table bearing the Bread of Life: as Thy Son and God, implore Him together with the holy Forerunner, that He may show compassion and save those who confess thee as the Mother of God!

*And we sing from the Octoechos: both Canons, with the Heirmos, on 10; and from the Menaion of the Saint, on 4. But when the Triodion has a Triode, then the Octoechos is omitted, and we sing from the Menaion with the Heirmos on 6, and from the Triodion the Triode on 8. And do thus every day throughout the entire Holy Forty Days.*[^602]

*Triode. Ode 2, Tone 2.*
*And the Second Canticle of the Psalter is chanted.*[^603]
*Ode 2. Heirmos:* See, see that I am God, Who saved the people of Israel in the sea, and fed them in the wilderness, and gushed forth water from the rock for mankind, that bearing him who fell into corruption of old, I may draw him to Myself, through Ineffable mercy! (Deut. 32:39; Exod. 14:21–31; 16:4–36; 17:6)

*Troparion 1:* Be sober, be watchful, sigh, weep, cast off by fasting the whole burden of sin, O soul; by fervent...

...repentance flee the fire, and through mourning for the passions rend the garment of mourning, receiving divine raiment!

*Troparion 2:* Let us all approach the Mountain of excellent deeds through fasting, having forsaken the assaults of pleasures that drag downward; and entering into the darkness of honorable visions, let us behold alone the beloved beauty of Christ, being mystically deified by divine ascents! (Exod. 19:16–20; 24:15–18)[^604]

*Troparion 3:* Woe is me! What shall I become? What shall I do, having wrought sin, without conscience and without fearing the Master? Therefore am I condemned before the judgment; O righteous and good Judge, turn me and save me, who have grieved Thee more than all men!

*Theotokion:* O unplowed land, that didst bring forth the Nourisher of all, Who opens His hand and satisfies every living thing with His good pleasure: by divine power strengthen with the Bread of Life our hearts that are weakened through satiety of our grievous sins! (Ps. 103:28; 144:16)

*Another Heirmos, Tone 5: "See, see."*[^605]
*Troparion 1:* Come, let us enter into the chamber of the soul, offering prayers unto the Lord and crying aloud: "Our Father Who art in the Heavens, release and remit our debts, as Thou alone art merciful!" (Matt. 6:6, 9–12)

*Troparion 2:* Showing forth the joy of our soul in the Fast, let us not grieve at the changing of these longed-for days, for the corrections of piety have blossomed forth for us! (Matt. 6:16–18)

*Glory... Trinity Hymn:*
*Troparion 3:* Unoriginate, uncreated, tri-hypostatic Unity, O Lord, Kingdom of the ages: the multitude of Angels and the whole human race glorifies Thee, the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* Thee, the all-virtuous glory of the human race, do we hymn...

...for on thy account, O Virgin, have we been deified, because thou didst bear for us Christ our Savior and God, Who loosed us from the curse!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*
*Troparion 4:* Who quenched the fire? Who shut the mouths of the beasts? The Fast: which delivered the Youths from the furnace, and the Prophet Daniel from being devoured by lions; let us also embrace it, brethren! (Dan. 3:19–27; 6:16–23)

*Heirmos:* See, see that I am God, Who was clothed in flesh of My own free will, that I might save Adam, who fell through deceit by transgression through the serpent!

*Ode 8. Heirmos: "In the bush to Moses."*[^606]
*Troparion 1:* Cast off, O soul, the sleep of grievous sloth, and watch zealously unto the divine commandments; the Bridegroom bearing lamps draws near, make haste to meet Him! (Matt. 25:1–13)

*Troparion 2:* Grievously wounded by the weapon of pleasures, heal me, O Word, by the remedy of Thy bountiful loving-kindness, that I may thankfully glorify Thee unto the ages!

*Troparion 3:* Abstain, O soul, from hurtful passions, from envy and hatred, and from all malice, feeding on that nourishment which substantially ministers the heavenly food!

*Theotokion:* O pure Mother of God, heal the festering sores of my soul, the passions of my heart, and the perversion of my mind, as thou alone art the helper of sinners, and the rampart of the afflicted!

*Another Heirmos, Tone 5: "The Creator of creation."*[^607]
*Troparion 1:* Having winged our souls with abstinence, let us all offer acceptable prayers to Heaven unto the Lord!

*Troparion 2:* Having received the spirit of compunction, let us weep for the liberation of our souls, singing praises unto Christ unto the ages!

*Let us bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, the Lord. Trinity Hymn:*

*Troparion 3:* O Trinity consubstantial, and Unity uncreated, God of all: we exalt Thee unto all ages!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* Make supplication for those who hymn thee, O All-pure One, that we may be delivered from all manner of assaults and afflictions!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*
*Troparion 4:* Having spurned the rich man's indulgence, let us fast with poor Lazarus, that Abraham's bosom may warm us also! (Luke 16:19–31)[^608]

*We praise, we bless, and we worship the Lord. Heirmos:*
*Heirmos:* The Creator of creation, before Whom the Angels tremble, hymn, O ye peoples, and exalt Him unto all ages!

*Ode 9. Heirmos: "Who of the earthborn hath heard?"*[^609]
*Troparion 1:* Who of the earthborn, having stumbled thus, hath ever so provoked God to anger? Who hath so followed the impulse of malice, and continued in sin, as I, wretched one? But O God, Who desirest mercy, do Thou have compassion on me!

*Troparion 2:* Ye Powers of godlike Angels, entreat the approachable God to save a soul swimming in the abyss of worldly pleasures, tossed by the tempestuous surges of the passions, and imperiled by the assaults of adversary spirits!

*Troparion 3:* Come, O soul, lightened with wings through the virtues of the Fast, soar up from downward-dragging malice, and take delight in higher visions through the virtues that minister food, becoming godlike through faith!

*Theotokion:* Who can utter the praises worthy of thee, who beyond understanding didst bear the praised Master and Lord, O Pure One, Whom the angelic ranks glorify? Implore Him, therefore, for the people who have sinned, O unwedded Virgin!

*Another Heirmos, Tone 5: "Rejoice, O Isaiah."*[^610]
*Troparion 1:* An acceptable time, the day of salvation: let us offer... (2 Cor. 6:2; Isa. 49:8) ...unto God the gifts of virtues, in which, having cast aside the works of darkness, brethren, let us put on the armor of light, even as Paul cries aloud! (Rom. 13:12)

*Troparion 2:* Come, even as the Lord smote the enemy through fasting, so let us also by it shatter his arrows and snares, each of us saying: "Get thee behind Me, Satan!" whenever he desires to tempt us! (Matt. 4:10; 16:23)

*Glory... Trinity Hymn:*
*Troparion 3:* In one essence do I hymn Thee, O unoriginate Trinity, honorable, life-originating, indivisible Unity: unbegotten Father, and begotten Son and Word, and Holy Spirit: save us who hymn Thee!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* Beyond understanding is thy childbearing, O Mother of God; for without man was the conception in thee, and virginal was the birth, for He Who was born is God: Whom magnifying, we call thee blessed, O Virgin!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*
*Troparion 4:* Having joined ourselves through fasting to the mountain of prayer, let us also with a pure heart behold God, receiving inwardly the tablets of the commandments, even as Moses, being illuminated with glory by the countenance of His love! (Exod. 24:12–18; 34:28–35; Matt. 5:8)

*Heirmos:* Rejoice, O Isaiah! A Virgin hath conceived in the womb, and brought forth a Son, Emmanuel, both God and Man; Dayspring is His name: Whom magnifying, we call thee blessed, O Virgin! (Isa. 7:14; 9:6; Zech. 6:12; Luke 1:78)

*Then the Photagogicon.*[^611]
*At the Aposticha: Stichera, Tone 3.*
*Idiomelon:* Let us begin, O peoples, the blameless Fast, which is the salvation of souls; let us serve the Lord in fear, let us anoint our heads with the oil of almsgiving, and wash our faces with the water of purity; let us not babble in prayers, but even as we have been taught, so let us cry aloud: "Our Father Who art in the Heavens, forgive us our trespasses, as Thou art the Lover of mankind!" (Matt. 6:7, 9–17; Ps. 2:11)[^612]

*Stichos: We were filled in the morning with Thy mercy, O Lord... (Ps. 89:14)*[^613] *Again the same Sticheron. Stichos 2: And let the brightness of the Lord our God be upon us... (Ps. 89:17)*
*Martyrion:* The warriors of Christ cast aside the fear of kings and tyrants, and with good courage and valor confessed Him, the Lord God of all and our King; and they pray for our souls!

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* O Mother of God, protectress of all who pray to thee: in thee do we place our hope, and in thee do we boast; in thee is all our expectation: pray unto Him Who was born of thee for thine unprofitable servants!

*On the same Tuesday, at the Sixth Hour:*
*Troparion of the Prophecy, Tone 4:* As we are sojourners upon the earth, even as all our fathers were: preserve our brief life free from sin, O our Savior, and have mercy on us, as Thou art the Lover of mankind! (Ps. 38:13; 1 Chron. 29:15)[^614]

*Glory... to the end. Both now... the same.*
*Prokeimenon, Psalm 5, Tone 4: Attend unto the voice of my prayer, my King and my God. (Ps. 5:3)*[^615]
*Stichos: Give ear to my words, O Lord, understand my cry. (Ps. 5:2)*

*Reading from the Prophecy of Isaiah (Isa. 1:19–2:3):*[^616]
Thus saith the Lord: "If ye be willing and obedient, ye shall eat the good of the land.
20. But if ye refuse and will not hear Me,
21. the sword shall devour you; for the mouth of the Lord hath spoken these things. How is the faithful city of Zion become a harlot, which was full of judgment? Righteousness lodged in her, but now murderers!
22. Your silver is not approved, your wine-merchants mix
23. wine with water. Thy princes are rebellious, companions of thieves, loving bribes, chasing after recompense...

...judging not for the fatherless, neither taking heed unto the cause of the widow.
24. Therefore thus saith the Master, the Lord of Sabaoth: "Ah, woe unto the strong ones in Israel! For My wrath against the adversaries shall not cease, and I will execute judgment on Mine enemies.
25. And I will bring My hand upon thee, and purge thee thoroughly unto purity; but the disobedient I will destroy, and I will take away from thee all the lawless, and all the proud.
26. And I will restore thy judges as of old, and thy counselors as at the beginning; and afterward thou shalt be called the City of Righteousness, the faithful Mother-City."
27. Zion: with judgment shall her captivity be saved, and with mercy.
28. And the lawless and the sinners shall be crushed together, and they that forsake the Lord shall be consumed.
29. For they shall be put to shame concerning their idols, which they desired, and ashamed of the gardens which they coveted.
30. For they shall be as a terebinth that hath shed its leaves, and as a garden that hath no water.
31. And their strength shall be as the tow of refuse, and their works as sparks of fire; and the lawless shall be burned together, and there shall be none to quench them!

The word that came to Isaiah the son of Amoz concerning Judea and concerning Jerusalem:
2. For it shall come to pass in the last days, that the mountain of the Lord shall be manifest, and the House of God upon the top of the mountains; and it shall be exalted above the hills, and all nations shall come unto it.
3. And many peoples shall go and say: "Come, and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, and to the House of the God of Jacob; and He will declare unto us His way, and we will walk in it." For out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem!

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 6, Tone 4: O Lord, rebuke me not in Thine anger... (Ps. 6:2)*[^617]
*Stichos: Have mercy on me, O Lord, for I am weak. (Ps. 6:3)*

## Tuesday of the First Week of the Fast, at Vespers

*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera, Tone 2.*
*Tone 2, Podoben: "When Thou didst appear" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ ꙗ҆ви́сѧ):*[^618]
*Sticheron 1:* Cast out of Paradise of old through bitter eating, let us make haste to enter through restraint of passions, crying aloud unto our God: Thou Who didst stretch out Thy palms upon the Cross, Who didst drink vinegar and taste gall, and didst endure pains from the nails, pinning away all most bitter pleasures from our souls for the sake of the loving-kindness of Thy compassions: save Thy servants! (Gen. 3:6, 23–24; Matt. 27:34, 48)

*Sticheron 2:* Driven out of Paradise of old through eating of the tree, we have been settled therein again through Thy Cross; bringing it in supplication unto Thee, O Plenteous in mercy, and all reverently honoring Thee, send down upon us now a fountain of tears in this time of abstinence, cleansing all the defilement of passions and of our transgressions, that we all may diligently cry aloud unto Thee: "O Lord, glory to Thee!"

*Another Sticheron, Tone 2.*
*Tone 2, Podoben: "For the deeds done by me" (Съдѣ́ланныхъ ми):*[^619]
*Sticheron 3:* Grant also unto me, O Word, the enjoyment of abstinence, even as Paradise to Adam of old: to taste of Thine every commandment, O our God, and ever to abstain from the fruit of sin which Thou didst forbid, that I may anticipate with joy Thy life-bearing Passion of the Cross!

*And from the Menaion, 3 stichera. Glory... Both now... Theotokion.*
*At Vespers, Prokeimenon, Psalm 7, Tone 6: O Lord my God, in Thee have I put my trust: save me. (Ps. 7:2)*[^620]
*Stichos: Deliver me from all them that persecute me. (Ps. 7:2)*

*Reading from Genesis (Gen. 1:14–23):*[^621]

God said: "Let there be lights in the firmament of heaven to give light upon the earth, to divide between the day and between the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and for years.
15. And let them be for illumination in the firmament of heaven, so as to give light upon the earth"; and it was so.
16. And God made two great lights: the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night; and the stars.
17. And God set them in the firmament of heaven, so as to give light upon the earth,
18. and to rule over the day and over the night, and to divide between the light and between the darkness; and God saw that it was good.
19. And there was evening, and there was morning: the fourth day.
20. And God said: "Let the waters bring forth reptiles of living souls, and winged creatures flying above the earth across the firmament of heaven"; and it was so.
21. And God created great sea-monsters, and every living soul of reptiles which the waters brought forth after their kinds, and every winged fowl after its kind; and God saw that they were good.
22. And God blessed them, saying: "Be fruitful, and multiply, and fill the waters in the seas, and let the winged creatures multiply upon the earth."
23. And there was evening, and there was morning: the fifth day.

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 8, Tone 5: O Lord, our Lord, how marvelous is Thy name in all the earth! (Ps. 8:2)*[^622]
*Stichos: For Thy magnificence is lifted up above the heavens. (Ps. 8:2)*

*Reading from Proverbs (Prov. 1:20–33):*[^623]

[Woodcut engraving: Vignette of Divine Wisdom / King Solomon preaching at the city gates, within an ornate woodcut strapwork frame preceding the reading from Proverbs.]

Wisdom sings aloud in the streets, and in the open squares she raises her voice with boldness.
21. Upon the tops of the walls she proclaims, at the gates of the mighty she sits, at the gates of the city boldly she speaks:
22. "How long soever the simple cleave unto righteousness, they shall not be put to shame; but the foolish, being desirers of insolence, having become ungodly, have hated knowledge,
23. and have become subject to reproofs. Behold, I will pour out the utterance of my breath, and I will teach you my word.
24. Because I called, and ye did not obey; and I stretched out words, and ye did not heed,
25. but made my counsels of none effect, and heeded not my reproofs:
26. therefore I also will laugh at your destruction, and I will rejoice when ruin comes upon you;
27. and when turmoil suddenly falls upon you, and overthrow comes like a whirlwind; or when tribulation comes upon you, and destruction of the city.
28. For it shall come to pass, when ye call upon me, I will not hear you; the evil shall seek me, and shall not find me.
29. For they hated wisdom, and did not choose the fear of the Lord;
30. neither would they attend to my counsels,
31. but mocked at my reproofs. Therefore they shall eat the fruits of their own way, and be filled with their own ungodliness.
32. For because they wronged infants, they shall be slain, and scrutiny shall destroy the ungodly.
33. But whoso listens unto me shall dwell in hope, and shall rest without fear of any evil."

*Then: "Vouchsafe, O Lord."*[^624]

*At the Aposticha, Idiomelon Stichera, Tone 8:*
*Idiomelon:* Let us accomplish a Fast not by distancing from foods alone, but by estrangement from every material passion, that having enslaved the flesh which tyrannizes over us, we may be worthy of the Communion of the Lamb slain of His own will for the world, the Son of God, and may spiritually celebrate the Savior's Resurrection from the dead, being lifted up to the height of virtues in brightness, and delighting in excellent deeds, gladdening the Lover of mankind!

*Stichos 1:* Unto Thee have I lifted up mine eyes, unto Thee that dwellest in heaven. Behold, as the eyes of servants look unto the hands of their masters, as the eyes of a maiden unto the hands of her mistress, so do our eyes look unto the Lord our God, until He have mercy on us. (Ps. 122:1–2)[^625]

*Again the same Sticheron.*

*Stichos 2:* Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us: for we are exceedingly filled with contempt; our soul is exceedingly filled with the reproach of the prosperous, and with the contempt of the proud. (Ps. 122:3–4)[^626]

*Martyrikon:* Thy Martyrs, O Lord, forgetting the things of this life, and taking no heed of torments for the sake of the life to come, were shown forth as heirs thereof; therefore do they also rejoice with the Angels. By their prayers grant unto Thy people great mercy!

*Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion:*
*Stavrotheotokion:* O most marvelous wonder! O new mystery! O awesome undertaking! cried the Virgin when she beheld Thee suspended upon the Cross between two thieves, Whom she had borne without pain in marvelous manner; and she wept, saying: "Woe is me, my most beloved Child! How has a fierce and ungrateful people nailed Thee to the Cross?"

*Then: "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart." And the rest of the order as previously indicated.*[^627]

*On that same second day of the Fast, at Compline:*
*According to custom: "O Heavenly King"; "O come, let us worship"; Psalm 69: "O God, give heed unto my help." We sing the Great Canon, Tone 6. Ode 1.*[^628]
*Ode 1. Heirmos:* A helper and a protector [He became unto me for salvation; this is my God, and I will glorify Him; the God of my father, and I will exalt Him, for gloriously is He glorified! (Exod. 15:1–2)]

*Troparion 1:* Surpassing the murder of Cain, by deliberate choice I have become a murderer of the conscience of my soul, having quickened the flesh and...

...waged war against her by my wicked deeds! (Gen. 4:8)

*Troparion 2:* I have not resembled the righteousness of Abel, O Jesus: never have I offered unto Thee acceptable gifts, nor divine actions, nor a pure sacrifice, nor a blameless life! (Gen. 4:4)

*Troparion 3:* Like Cain, we also, O wretched soul, have together offered unto the Creator of all defiled deeds, and a blemish-stained sacrifice, and an unprofitable life; therefore are we also condemned! (Gen. 4:3–5)

*Troparion 4:* Fashioning clay into life, the Creator placed within me flesh and bones, and breath and life; but O my Maker, my Deliverer, and my Judge: accept me who repent! (Gen. 2:7; Job 10:8–12)

*Troparion 5:* I confess unto Thee, O Savior, the sins which I have wrought, and the wounds of my soul and body, which murderous internal thoughts, like thieves, have inflicted upon me! (Luke 10:30)

*Troparion 6:* Though I have sinned, O Savior, yet I know that Thou art the Lover of mankind: Thou chastisest with strictness, yet Thou showest fervent mercy; Thou seest him that weeps, and runnest to meet him like the Father, calling back the Prodigal! (Luke 15:20)

*Glory... Trinity Hymn:*
*Trinity Hymn:* O transcendent Trinity, worshipped in Unity: take from me the heavy burden of sin, and as Thou art compassionate, grant me tears of compunction!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* O Mother of God, the hope and protectress of those who praise thee: take from me the heavy burden of sin, and as pure Sovereign Lady, accept me who repent!

*Ode 2. Heirmos:* Give heed, O Heaven, and I will speak, and hymn Christ, Who came in the flesh from the Virgin! (Deut. 32:1)[^629]

*Troparion 1:* Sin stitched together coats of skins for me, having stripped me of the former God-woven raiment! (Gen. 3:21)

*Troparion 2:* I am clothed with a garment of shame as with...

...fig leaves, in condemnation of my self-governing passions! (Gen. 3:7)

*Troparion 3:* I have clothed myself in a shameful garment, and one shamefully stained with blood by the flux of a passionate and pleasure-loving life!

*Troparion 4:* I have fallen into passionate ruin and material corruption; and from that time until now, the enemy afflicts me!

*Troparion 5:* Preferring a life of material indulgence and greed to restraint, O Savior, I am now burdened with a heavy load!

*Troparion 6:* I adorned the carnal image with diverse investitures of defiled thoughts, and I am condemned!

*Troparion 7:* I was diligent in caring only for outward ornamentation, while despising the inner, God-formed tabernacle!

*Troparion 8:* By passions I have buried the beauty of the primal icon, O Savior; seek and find it as a lost drachma! (Luke 15:8–10)

*Troparion 9:* I have sinned like the Harlot; I cry aloud unto Thee: "I alone have sinned against Thee; accept also my tears, O Savior, even as myrrh!" (Luke 7:37–38)

*Troparion 10:* Cleanse me like the Publican; I cry aloud unto Thee, O Savior: "Cleanse me! For no one among the descendants of Adam has sinned against Thee as have I!" (Luke 18:13)

*Glory... Trinity Hymn:*
*Trinity Hymn:* Thee, the One God of all in three Persons, do I hymn: the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* O pure Virgin Mother of God, who alone art all-praised: pray fervently that we may be saved!

*Ode 3. Heirmos:* Establish, O Lord, upon the rock of Thy commandments my wavering heart, for Thou alone art holy and righteous! (1 Kings [1 Sam.] 2:2)[^630]

*Troparion 1:* In Thee, the Destroyer of death, I possess the Fountain of Life, and I cry aloud unto Thee from my heart before the end: "I have sinned; cleanse and save me!" (Ps. 35:10) *Troparion 2:* I have sinned, O Lord, I have sinned against Thee, cleanse me! For there is no one among men who has sinned whom I have not surpassed by transgressions!

*Troparion 3:* Having imitated those who acted impiously in the time of Noah, O Savior, I inherited their condemnation of drowning in the Deluge! (Gen. 6:5–7; 7:17–24)

*Troparion 4:* Having imitated that Ham, O soul, who mocked his father, thou didst not cover the shame of thy neighbor, turning back with backward gaze! (Gen. 9:22–23)

*Troparion 5:* Like Lot, flee, my soul, from the conflagration of sin; flee Sodom and Gomorrah; flee the flame of every irrational desire! (Gen. 19:15–26)

*Troparion 6:* Have mercy on me, O Lord, have mercy on me, I cry unto Thee, when Thou comest with Thine Angels to render unto all according to the desert of their deeds! (Matt. 16:27; 25:31)

*Glory... Trinity Hymn:*
*Trinity Hymn:* Simple, uncreated Trinity, unoriginate Essence praised in a Trinity of Hypostases: save us who in faith worship Thy dominion!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* In time, O Mother of God, without knowing man, thou didst bear the Son Who is timeless from the Father; a strange wonder, remaining a Virgin while nursing!

*Ode 4. Heirmos:* The Prophet heard [of Thy coming, O Lord, and was afraid; that Thou wast about to be born of a Virgin and shown unto men, and he said: "I heard report of Thee, and was afraid: glory to Thy power, O Lord!"] (Hab. 3:2)[^631]

*Troparion 1:* Watch, O my soul, and play the man, even as of old the greatest among the Patriarchs, that thou mayest acquire action with knowledge, that thou mayest become a mind beholding God, and attain to the unwaning cloud in vision, and become a great merchant! (Gen. 28:10–22; 32:24–30)

*Troparion 2:* Having begotten the twelve Patriarchs, the great one among the Patriarchs mystically established for thee a ladder of active ascent, O my soul, wisely setting his children as foundations and his steps as ascents! (Gen. 28:12–13; 35:22–26) *Troparion 3:* Thou hast imitated the hated Esau, O soul: thou didst surrender the birthright of primal beauty to thy deceiver, and didst fall away from the father's blessing; and twice wast thou tripped up, O wretched one, in action and in mind; therefore repent now! (Gen. 25:29–34; 27:34–40; Heb. 12:16–17)

*Troparion 4:* Esau was called Edom because of the extreme frenzy of his mingling with women; for ever burning with intemperance and defiled by pleasures, he was named Edom, which is interpreted "Inflammation," being a sin-loving soul! (Gen. 25:30; 26:34–35)[^632]

*Troparion 5:* Having heard of Job justified upon the dung-heap, O my soul, thou didst not emulate his fortitude; thou didst not acquire firmness of resolve in all the things which thou knowest, wherein thou wast tempted; but thou wast shown forth as impatient! (Job 1:21–22; 2:8–10)

*Troparion 6:* He who was formerly on a throne is now naked on a dung-heap, covered with sores; he who was rich in children and glorious suddenly became childless and homeless; for he accounted the dung-heap a palace, and the worms pearls! (Job 1:1–3, 18–19; 2:7–8)

*Glory... Trinity Hymn:*
*Trinity Hymn:* Inseparably in Essence, unconfusedly in Persons do I confess Thee in theology, the One Triune Divinity, as of one sovereignty and enthroned together, crying unto Thee the great hymn thrice-hymned in the highest!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* Both bearing and keeping virginity, thou remainest in both natures a Virgin: He Who was born renews the laws of nature, and the womb brings forth without travail; for where God so wills, the order of nature is overcome, for He does whatsoever He wills!

*Ode 5. Heirmos:* Watching early out of the night, [O Lover of mankind, enlighten, I pray Thee, and guide even me; and teach me Thy commandments, O Savior!] (Isa. 26:9)[^633] *Troparion 1:* Thou hast heard of the ark of Moses of old, O soul, borne upon the waters and the waves of the river as in a bridal chamber, fleeing the deed of the bitter decree of Pharaoh! (Exod. 2:1–3)

*Troparion 2:* If thou hast heard of the midwives of old slaying the male infants, O wretched soul, now like great Moses, suckle wisdom, the work of chastity! (Exod. 1:15–17; 2:7–10)

*Troparion 3:* Like great Moses who struck the Egyptian, O wretched soul, thou hast not slain the wounded mind; and how wilt thou dwell, tell me, in the wilderness of passions through repentance? (Exod. 2:11–15)

*Troparion 4:* Great Moses settled in the wilderness: come then, emulate his life, that thou mayest also be in the vision of the Divine appearance in the Bush, O soul! (Exod. 3:1–6)

*Troparion 5:* Imagine the rod of Moses, O soul, striking the sea and solidifying the deep into an image of the divine Cross, through which thou also canst accomplish great things! (Exod. 14:16, 21–22)

*Troparion 6:* Aaron offered unto God pure and undefiled fire; but Hophni and Phinehas, like thee, O soul, offered unto God an alien and defiled life! (Lev. 10:1–2; 1 Kings [1 Sam.] 2:12–17, 22)

*Glory... Trinity Hymn:*
*Trinity Hymn:* Thee, O Trinity, do we glorify, the One God: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, O Father, Son, and Spirit, simple Essence, Unity ever worshipped!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* From thee did He clothe Himself in my clay, O incorrupt, unwedded Virgin Mother: God, Who created the ages, united human nature unto Himself!

*Ode 6. Heirmos:* The waves of my transgressions, O Savior, returning as in the Red Sea, have suddenly overwhelmed me, even as once they overwhelmed the Egyptians and their captains! (Exod. 14:26–28)[^634]

*Troparion 1:* Thou hast acquired an unreasonable will, O soul, even as Israel of old; for instead of the divine manna, thou didst...

...irrationally prefer the pleasure-loving gluttony of passions! (Num. 11:4–6)

*Troparion 2:* Thou hast preferred the cisterns of Canaanite thoughts, O soul, rather than the cleft of the rock from which, like a cup, wisdom pours forth streams of theology! (Jer. 2:13; Exod. 17:6; Prov. 9:1–5)

*Troparion 3:* Swine's flesh and cauldrons, the food of Egypt, hast thou chosen instead of the heavenly food, O my soul, even as of old the senseless people in the wilderness! (Exod. 16:3; Num. 11:4–5)

*Troparion 4:* When Moses Thy servant struck the rock with his rod, he typically prefigured Thy life-giving side, from which we all draw the drink of life, O Savior! (Exod. 17:6; John 19:34; 1 Cor. 10:4)

*Troparion 5:* Search and see, O soul, like Joshua the son of Nun, what the Promised Land is like, and settle therein through good obedience to the law! (Num. 13:17–20; Josh. 1:1–9)

*Glory... Trinity Hymn:*
*Trinity Hymn:* "I am the Trinity, simple and undivided, yet divided in Persons, and I am a Unity united in Essence," said the Father, and the Son, and the Divine Spirit!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* Thy womb bare God unto us, formed in our likeness; but implore Him as Creator of all, O Mother of God, that through thy prayers we may be justified!

*Lord, have mercy (thrice). Glory... Both now...*

*Tone 4, Podoben: "Hope of the world" (Оу҆пова́нїе мі́рꙋ):*[^635]
*Sessional Hymn:* When I ponder the fearful day of Thy Coming and Thine unbribable judgment seat, O Christ, I am terrified, I fear and tremble, having a multitude of transgressions; but before the end, as Thou art a merciful God, turn and save me, through the prayers of her that bare Thee, O compassionate Savior, Who alone art the Lover of mankind!

*Ode 7. Heirmos:* We have sinned and committed lawlessness, [and have dealt unrighteously before Thee; neither have we kept nor done as Thou hast commanded us; but deliver us not up unto the end, O God of the fathers!] (Dan. 9:5; Song of Three Youths 1:6–7)[^636]

*Troparion 1:* When the Ark was being carried upon a cart, and the ox turned aside, that Uzzah, merely touching it, experienced the wrath of God; but fleeing his presumption, O my soul, revere divine things with honor! (2 Kings [2 Sam.] 6:6–7; 1 Chron. 13:9–10) *Troparion 2:* Hast thou heard of Absalom, how he rose up against nature? Hast thou learned of his defiled deeds, whereby he defiled the bed of David his father? Yet thou hast followed after his passions and pleasure-loving pursuits! (2 Kings [2 Sam.] 16:21–22)

*Troparion 3:* Thou hast subjected thy non-servile dignity unto thy body; for having found another Ahithophel in the enemy, O soul, thou didst heed his counsels; but Christ scattered them, that thou mayest by all means be saved! (2 Kings [2 Sam.] 15:31; 17:14, 23)

*Troparion 4:* Solomon the marvelous, who was filled with the grace of wisdom: having once wrought evil before God, he departed from Him; and unto him, O soul, hast thou likened thyself by thy cursed life! (3 Kings [1 Kings] 11:1–9)

*Troparion 5:* Drawn away by the pleasures of his passions, he was defiled—alas for me! The lover of wisdom became a lover of wanton women and an alien from God; and him, O soul, hast thou imitated in mind by the defilements of voluptuousness! (3 Kings [1 Kings] 11:1–4)

*Troparion 6:* Thou hast imitated Rehoboam, who did not heed his father's counsel, and together with him that most evil servant Jeroboam, the ancient apostate, O soul; but flee imitation of them, and cry unto God: "I have sinned, have compassion on me!" (3 Kings [1 Kings] 12:1–16, 26–33)

*Glory... Trinity Hymn:*
*Trinity Hymn:* O Trinity, simple, undivided, transcendent, holy Unity: Lights and Light, and Holy Three, and One Holy is God the Trinity hymned! But praise, O my soul, and hymn the Life and Lives, the God of all!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* We hymn thee, we bless thee, we worship thee, O Mother of God: for of the inseparable Trinity thou didst bear the One Son and God, and didst thyself open the heavenly realms unto us who are upon earth!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:* Him Whom the armies of the heavens glorify, [and before Whom the Cherubim and Seraphim tremble: every breath and creation, hymn, bless, and highly exalt unto all ages!] (Dan. 3:57–88)[^637]

*Troparion 1:* Having emulated Uzziah, O soul, thou hast acquired his leprosy doubly within thyself; for thou thinkest unfitting things and doest lawless deeds; abandon what thou hast, and run to repentance! (2 Chron. 26:16–21)

*Troparion 2:* Thou hast heard of the Ninevites repenting before God in sackcloth and ashes, O soul; yet thou hast not imitated them, but hast shown thyself more hardened than all who sinned before the Law and after the Law! (Jonah 3:5–9)

*Troparion 3:* Thou hast heard of Jeremiah in the mire of the pit, O soul, crying with lamentations for the city of Zion and seeking tears; liken thyself unto his mournful life, and thou shalt be saved! (Jer. 38:6; Lam. 1:1–2; Jer. 9:1)

*Troparion 4:* Jonah fled to Tarshish, foreseeing the conversion of the Ninevites; for as a Prophet, he understood the loving-kindness of God, and was zealous that his prophecy should not prove false! (Jonah 1:1–3; 4:1–2)

*Troparion 5:* Hast thou heard how Daniel shut the mouths of the beasts in the den, O soul? Hast thou learned how the Youths who were with Azariah quenched the burning flame of the furnace through faith? (Dan. 6:16–22; 3:19–27; Heb. 11:33–34)

*Troparion 6:* All the figures of the Old Testament have I brought before thee as examples, O soul: emulate the God-pleasing deeds of the righteous, and flee again from the sins of the wicked!

*Glory... Trinity Hymn:*
*Trinity Hymn:* Unoriginate Father, co-unoriginate Son, good Comforter, upright Spirit; Begetter of the Word of God, Word of the unoriginate Father, living and creating Spirit: Trinity in Unity, have mercy on me!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* As from dipping in purple dye, O most pure Lady, the spiritual purple robe of Emmanuel, His flesh, was woven within thy womb; therefore do we truly honor thee as the Mother of God!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:* Conception without seed, [ineffable childbirth; birth without a father of a Mother without husband: the birth of God renews natures. Therefore, all generations magnify thee in orthodox manner as Mother of God!][^638]

*Troparion 1:* Christ was tempted, the devil tempted Him, showing stones that they might become bread; he led Him up into a mountain to behold all the kingdoms of the world in an instant; fear the snare, O soul: be watchful, and pray to God at every hour! (Matt. 4:1–11; Luke 4:1–13)

*Troparion 2:* The desert-loving turtledove, the voice of one crying aloud, the lamp of Christ, sounded forth proclaiming repentance; Herod acted lawlessly with Herodias: take heed, my soul, that thou be not entangled in the snares of lawlessness, but embrace repentance! (Matt. 3:1–3; 14:3–4; Mark 1:3–4; 6:17–18)

*Troparion 3:* The Forerunner of grace dwelt in the wilderness; hearing this, all Judea and Samaria ran together and confessed their sins, being baptized eagerly; yet thou, O soul, hast not emulated them! (Matt. 3:5–6; Mark 1:5)

*Troparion 4:* Marriage is honorable and the bed undefiled, for Christ blessed both beforehand, eating in the flesh and changing water into wine at the marriage in Cana, revealing His first miracle, that thou mightest be transformed, O soul! (Heb. 13:4; John 2:1–11)

*Troparion 5:* Christ braced the paralytic so that he took up his bed; and He raised up the dead youth, the son of the widow, and the centurion's servant; and by revealing Himself to the Samaritan woman, He depicted beforehand for thee, O soul, worship in the spirit! (Matt. 8:5–13; 9:2–7; Luke 7:11–16; John 4:7–26)

*Troparion 6:* By the touching of the hem of His garment the Lord healed the woman with an issue of blood; He cleansed lepers; enlightening the blind and making straight the lame, He healed the deaf, the dumb, and the woman bent double by a word, that thou, O wretched soul, mightest be saved! (Matt. 9:20–22, 27–33; 11:5; Luke 13:11–13)

*Glory... Trinity Hymn:*
*Trinity Hymn:* Let us glorify the Father, let us highly exalt the Son, and let us faithfully worship the Divine Spirit...

...and let us faithfully worship the Divine Spirit: Trinity undivided, Unity in essence, as Light and Lights, and Life and Lives, giving life and enlightening the ends of the world!

*Theotokion:* Preserve thy city, O all-pure Mother of God; for reigning faithfully in thee, in thee it is also made strong, and conquering through thee, it is delivered from every trial, and takes the enemy captive, and maintains obedience.

*Then both choirs sing the Heirmos:* Conception without seed...[^639] *And a prostration to the ground. After this: "When I called upon Thee..." and the rest of the order of Great Compline.*[^640]

## Wednesday of the First Week of Great Lent

*At Matins, the Trinity Hymns of the Tone.*[^641] *After the first Kathisma Stikhologia, Sessional Hymns in the Octoechos. After the second Kathisma Stikhologia, Sessional Hymns, Tone 2:*
*Tone 2, Podoben: "The noble Joseph" (Благоѡбра́зный І҆ѡ́сифъ):*
Thou Who by Thy Passions didst grant passionlessness unto all, O Lover of mankind: put to death the passions of my flesh by Thy Cross; and make me worthy to behold Thy divine Passion, having well-pleased Thy glory by fasting, that we may richly receive great mercy!

*Glory... The same.*
*Both now... Stavrotheotokion, the same Tone:*
*Tone 2, Podoben: "Being the wellspring of loving-kindness" (Мл҃рдїѧ сꙋ́щи):*
When the Virgin and Thy Mother beheld Thee, O Christ, stretched out dead upon the Tree, weeping bitterly she said: "O my Son, what is this awesome mystery? Bestowing eternal life upon all, how diest Thou willingly upon the Cross by a shameful death?!"

*After the third Kathisma Stikhologia, Sessional Hymn, Tone 2, Podoben: "Unto the Life-giving Cross" (Животворѧ́щему Крестꙋ̀):*

The light-creating season of abstinence which Thou hast now sanctified and granted unto us, O Lord: do Thou make us all worthy, living in peace, to pass through in compunction and purity, by the power of the Cross, O only Lover of mankind!

*Stavrotheotokion:* Preserved by the precious Cross of thy Son, O pure Sovereign Lady Mother of God, we all easily cast down every assault of the adversary; therefore, as is our duty, we bless thee as the Mother of Light and the only hope of our souls.

*Then, Reading in the Lausaic History.*[^642] *Psalm 50. Canon in the Menaion, and the Triodion. We recite Ode 3 of the Psalter.*[^643] *Joseph:*
*Ode 3, Tone 2. Heirmos:* The desert has blossomed [as a lily, O Lord, the barren Church of the Gentiles by Thy coming, wherein my heart is established!] (Isa. 35:1–2; 1 Kings [1 Sam.] 2:1)[^644]
*Troparion 1:* Let us crucify our members through abstinence, and be watchful in prayers as it is written, and let us follow the manner of life of Him Who suffered and put passions to death! (Gal. 5:24; 1 Pet. 4:1–2)

*Troparion 2:* Having vomited forth bitter sin, let us now hasten to well-please Christ, Who willingly tasted gall, and Who by the Cross cast down the author of evil! (Matt. 27:34)

*Troparion 3:* Sin, having become a habit, drags me into utter perdition; but do Thou deliver me therefrom by Thy Cross, O compassionate and most merciful One!

*Theotokion:* O Sovereign Lady who rulest over all creatures, in that thou didst bear the Master: deliver me from the servitude of the deceitful one who fights against me!

*Another Canon [by St. Theodore the Studite]. Ode 3, the same Tone. Heirmos:* Establish us in Thee, [O Lord, Who by the Tree didst put sin to death, and plant Thy fear in the hearts of us who hymn Thee!]
*Troparion 1:* The Tree of the Cross made abstinence blossom for the world; kissing it with love, let us enjoy the rich fruit of Christ's divine commandments!

*Troparion 2:* Bearing now the restraint of passions, let us crucify the flesh, O Lord, and show all its mortal mindedness dead through divine life! (Rom. 8:6)

*Glory... Trinity Hymn:*

*Trinity Hymn:* Three Persons of one form do I glorify: the Father, the Son, and the Spirit: one dominion of the Godhead, the Kingdom and splendor of all.

*Theotokion:* Thy childbirth, O pure one, is an awesome manifestation; for He is God made man, Who was born unoriginately of the Father, and was born of thee at the end of times without a husband!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*
*Troparion:* I hymn Thy Crucifixion and the Piercing of Thy divine Side, O Christ, from which I ever draw forth the drink of immortality and am cleansed! (John 19:34)

*Heirmos:* Establish us in Thee, O Lord, Who by the Tree didst put sin to death, and plant Thy fear in the hearts of us who hymn Thee!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:* The furnace of fire [once in Babylon, dividing its action by the divine decree, burned the Chaldeans, but bedewed the faithful who sang: "Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!"] (Dan. 3:46–50)[^645]
*Troparion 1:* The furnace of passions inflames my soul, but quench it with the dew of Thy mercy, O Thou Who didst pour forth drops of immortality from Thy incorruptible side when Thou wast crucified, O Benefactor, by reason of Thine abundant condescension! (John 19:34)

*Troparion 2:* By Thy lifting up upon the Cross, O Christ, Thou hast raised us who had fallen into wickedness; therefore raise me up who have slipped into the abyss of sin, and establish me upon the rock of salvation, that I may glorify Thy dominion! (Ps. 39:3)

*Troparion 3:* By Thy spear, O Christ, cleanse the corruption of passions from my heart and heal me entirely, whom the serpent wounded with venomous teeth; and grant me to walk steadfastly in the divine paths!

*Theotokion:* Thee, the radiant candle and lampstand wherein the Fire of the Godhead dwelt, enlightening those held by nighttime corruption, O undefiled one: all of us honor, blessing thy blessed childbirth!

*Another Canon [by St. Theodore the Studite]. Ode 8. Heirmos:* In the bush unto Moses [on Mount Sinai, Thou Who didst prefigure of old the miracle of the Virgin: hymn, bless, and highly exalt unto all ages!] (Exod. 3:2)
*Troparion 1:* Him Who was crucified on the Tree between thieves, and was pierced with a spear...

...and whose life-flowing side was pierced: hymn, bless, and highly exalt unto all ages! (John 19:34)

*Troparion 2:* O Judge of all the earth, Thou didst stand before the judgment seat; Thou wast struck with blows and mocked, and wast suspended upon the Cross, delivering me from the corruption of ancient sin: I hymn Thee unto all ages! (Matt. 26:67; 27:26–31)

*Verse: We bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, the Lord.*
*Trinity Hymn:* One Godhead, the Trinity: essence undivided, yet distinct in Persons, unshakable dominion, O Father, Son, and Spirit: we hymn Thee unto all ages!

*Theotokion:* O pure Mother of God, heavenly door, portal of salvation: accept the supplications of all Christians who bless thee unto all ages!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*
*Troparion:* O Cross of Christ, who didst guide the thief unto faith: make me also worthy to run well through the course of the Fast, to come beforehand unto the veneration of thee, and to be quickened! (Luke 23:40–43)

*Verse: We praise, we bless, and we worship the Lord.*
*Heirmos:* Him Who in the bush unto Moses on Mount Sinai prefigured of old the miracle of the Virgin: hymn, bless, and highly exalt unto all ages! (Exod. 3:2)

*Ode 9. Heirmos:* Of the unoriginate Begetter [the Son, God and Lord, becoming incarnate of the Virgin, appeared unto us to enlighten the darkened and to gather together the scattered: therefore the all-praised Mother of God do we magnify!][^646]
*Troparion 1:* Shining brighter than the sun, the Fast, an abundant-beaming grace, proclaims unto all the rays of the Cross, and the dawn of the precious Passion, and the saving day of the Resurrection!

*Troparion 2:* Let us love purity, let us flee fornication, let us gird our loins with chastity, that we may appear honorable unto Him Who is honored and Who alone dwells in purity unto ages, the Savior of our souls! (1 Pet. 1:13; 1 Cor. 6:18)

*Troparion 3:* Nail my flesh through Thy fear, O Christ, Who didst nail the sin of Adam to the Cross; loose the bonds of my evils, crush the arrows of the deceitful one by Thy spear, O Master, and deliver me from his harm! (Ps. 118:120; Col. 2:14)

*Theotokion:*

O Maiden Virgin who didst bear Christ the Lord, the most righteous and only well-entreated Judge: deliver me from judgment, and from fire, and from torment, which the enjoyment of sin procures for me!

*Another Canon [by St. Theodore the Studite]. Ode 9. Heirmos:* Pure and most pure [Mother and Virgin, in songs of praise let all of us, the faithful, magnify the Mother of God with gratitude!][^647]
*Troparion 1:* O Thy loving-kindness! For Thou didst endure the Cross, the Nails, and the Spear, O Lord, for my sake who was condemned to corruption; therefore do I hymn Thee, O Christ! (John 19:34)

*Troparion 2:* Worshipping the Cross, the Reed, the Nails, the Spear, and Thy life-giving Passions, all we the people magnify Thee in songs!

*Glory... Trinity Hymn:*
*Trinity Hymn:* O Trinity in three Persons, consubstantial Unity, sovereign Dominion, nature equal in glory: Father, Son, and divine Spirit, save us all!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* Rejoice, mercy seat of the world, O Mother of God, fleeing into which all we sinners ever find reconciliation unto God!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*
*Troparion:* Strengthening me also by Thy Cross, O Lord: grant me, O Good One, to finish the course of the Fast with blessed strength!

*Heirmos:* Pure and most pure Mother and Virgin, in songs of praise let all of us, the faithful, magnify the Mother of God with gratitude!
*Then: "It is truly meet to bless thee."*[^648]

*At the Aposticha, Idiomelon Stichera, Tone 8:*
*Idiomelon:* By fasting let us strive to subjugate the passions of our thoughts, clothing ourselves with spiritual wings, that having easily crossed the storm raised by the enemy, we may be worthy of the veneration of the Cross of the Son of God, Who was willingly sacrificed for the world; and spiritually celebrating the Savior's Resurrection from the dead, ascending the mountain with the Disciples, let us glorify the Son, Who received all dominion from the Father, the Lover of mankind! (Matt. 28:16–18)

*Stichos 1:* We were filled in the morning with Thy mercy, O Lord, and we rejoiced and were glad. In all our days let us be glad for the days wherein Thou didst humble us, for the years wherein we saw evils; and look upon Thy servants and upon Thy works, and guide their sons. (Ps. 89:14–16)[^649]

*Again the same Sticheron.*

*Stichos 2:* And let the brightness of the Lord our God be upon us, and direct Thou the works of our hands over us; yea, the work of our hands direct Thou. (Ps. 89:17)[^650] *Martyrikon:* O invincible Martyrs of Christ, having conquered deception by the power of the Cross, ye received the grace of eternal life, and feared not the threats of the torturers; and now your blood has become healing for our souls: pray that our souls may be saved!

*Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion:*
*Stavrotheotokion:* "What is this visible sight which is beheld by mine eyes, O Master? Thou Who holdest all creation art lifted up upon the Tree and put to death, bestowing life upon all!" cried the Mother of God weeping, when the all-pure one beheld upon the Cross Him Who had ineffably shone forth from her, God and Man.

*Then: "It is good to give praise unto the Lord."*[^651] *The First Hour, and the Dismissal.*

*On the same Wednesday, at the Sixth Hour:*
*Troparion of the Prophecy, Tone 4:*
Thou knowest our frame, Thou knowest our weakness, O Lover of mankind: we have sinned, yet we have not departed from Thee, O God, nor lifted up our hands unto a strange god: spare us by Thy grace, O compassionate One! (Ps. 102:14; 43:21)

*Glory... Spare us by Thy grace... Both now... Thou knowest our frame...*
*The Second Prokeimenon.*[^652] *Prokeimenon, Psalm 9, Tone 4:*
*Reader:* I will confess Thee, O Lord, with my whole heart; I will tell of all Thy marvelous works. (Ps. 9:2)[^653]
*Stichos:* I will be glad and rejoice in Thee: I will sing to Thy name, O Thou Most High. (Ps. 9:3)[^654]
*Reading from the Prophecy of Isaiah (Isa. 2:3b–5):*
**Reader:** Thus says the Lord: Out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.
And He shall judge among the nations, and shall rebuke many people; and they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their scythes into pruning-hooks; nation shall not take up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more.
And now, thou...

...O house of Jacob, come ye, and let us walk in the light of the Lord.
For He has forsaken His people the house of Jacob, because their land is filled from the beginning, as at first, with foreign soothsayers, and many foreign children were born unto them.
For their land is filled with silver and gold, neither was there any number to their treasures;
their land also is full of horses, neither was there any number to their chariots; and their land is filled with abominations, the works of their hands, and they worshipped that which their own fingers made.
And the mean man bowed down, and the great man was humbled: therefore I will not forgive them.
And now enter ye into the rocks, and hide yourselves in the earth, from before the terror of the Lord, and from the glory of His majesty, when He arises to smash the earth.
For the eyes of the Lord are high, but man is humble; and the loftiness of men shall be bowed down, and the Lord alone shall be exalted in that day! (Isa. 2:5–11)[^655]

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 10, Tone 6:*
*Reader:* The Lord is righteous, and He hath loved righteousness: His countenance hath beheld uprightness. (Ps. 10:7)[^656]
*Stichos:* In the Lord have I put my trust: how will ye say to my soul, Flee as a bird to the mountains? (Ps. 10:1)[^657]

*Then: "Let Thy tender mercies speedily anticipate us."*[^658] *And the rest of the order of the Hours, as previously ordained; and the Dismissal.*

*Be it known when the Presanctified [Liturgy] occurs:*
*Selected from the Divine Liturgy of Basil the Great by the most holy Gregory the Dialogist.*[^659][^660]
*After "Remember us, O Lord," and the Dismissal, the Reader says [the Prayer of St. Ephrem], the silent Choir [does not sing]:*[^661]
*The Priest and the Deacon make a metania to the Superior, or toward his place.*
*Then they make two prostrations before the Holy Doors, saying the secret prayer: "O Lord, send down Thy hand..."*[^662] *The third prostration; and toward each of the Choirs one bow. And thus they enter into the holy Sanctuary [and vest in the Prothesis]. And they vest themselves in all the priestly vestments, saying over each of them only: "Blessed is our God..."*

..."[Blessed is our God,] be merciful unto me a sinner." They go before the Holy Table, and lifting up their hands, they say: "O Heavenly King..." and make three prostrations; "Glory to God in the highest..." twice; and "O Lord, open Thou my lips..." once. The Deacon, bowing his head unto the Priest, asks not for the time [of the service], but waits until the metanias are completed; after which they say the Trisagion, and "Lord, have mercy" twelve times. The Priest performs the Dismissal of the Hours, commemorating the Saint (by name) of the present day, and having closed the doors.
The Deacon goes out, and standing in the customary place, makes three prostrations, and proclaims:
**Deacon:** Bless, Master.
**Priest:** Blessed is the Kingdom of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages.
**Choir:** Amen.
*And they begin: "O come, let us worship..." three times, and three prostrations; Psalm 103, the Introductory Evening Psalm.*[^663] *The Deacon comes and stands before the Icon of Christ, looking toward the people.*
*The Priest says in secret the first three customary Prayers of Vespers.*[^664] *And at the completion of the Psalm: "Glory... Both now... Alleluia" three times, and three prostrations.*
*And the Deacon, standing in the customary place, says the Great Ektenia:*
**Deacon:** In peace let us pray to the Lord.
*The Priest makes the Exclamation. The Deacon enters the Table of Oblation [Proskomide], and sets the Sacred Vessels in order according as is custom.*
*And the Priest censers, and taking the Presanctified Holy Lamb, places It upon the Holy Diskos according to the rite. The Deacon pours wine and water into the Holy Chalice according to custom; and they say nothing, save only:* "Through the prayers of our holy fathers, O Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on us." *This the Priest says, and covers the Holy Gifts; for They are presanctified and consecrated, and need no other addition, save only the censer and the Prayer of Incense.*[^665]
*We then recite the customary 18th Kathisma: "Unto the Lord in mine affliction..." (Ps. 119–133).*[^666] *And after each Antiphon: "Glory... Both now... Alleluia" three times, and three prostrations; and the Deacon goes out and says the Little Ektenia (and if there is no Deacon, then the Priest himself says it in the Sanctuary).*
*The Psalmist does not say: "Both now," but begins each Antiphon from the Psalm itself.*[^667] *After the Stikhologia we sing "Lord, I have cried." The Deacon censers according to custom the Holy Table, and the Table of Oblation [Prothesis], and the entire Sanctuary according to the rite, and the whole Altar and the Priest. As the Stichera are sung, we place them on 10 verses, beginning with: "Bring my soul out of prison" (Ps. 141:8).*[^668] *In the Tone, the Idiomelon of the day:*
*On the same Wednesday of the First Week of the Fast, at Vespers:*
*At "Lord, I have cried," Idiomelon Stichera, Tone 8:*
*Idiomelon:* Fasting bodily, brethren, let us also fast spiritually...

...let us loose every bond of iniquity; let us tear apart the crooked cords of forced exchanges; let us tear up every unjust contract; let us give bread to the hungry, and bring the roofless poor into our homes: that we may receive great mercy from Christ our God! (Isa. 58:6–7)

*Twice. Martyrikon:* If there be any virtue, and if there be any praise, it befits the Saints; for they bowed their necks to the sword for Thy sake, Who didst bow the heavens and come down; they shed their blood for Thy sake, Who didst empty Thyself and take the form of a servant; they humbled themselves unto death, following Thy poverty: by whose prayers, according to the multitude of Thy tender mercies, O God, have mercy on us! (Phil. 4:8; Ps. 17:10; Phil. 2:7–8)

*Then, 3 Stichoi. Stichos 4: Let Thine ears be attentive to the voice of my supplication. (Ps. 129:2)*[^669]
*Then we sing the Stichera of Joseph, Tone 2, Podoben: "When from the Tree" (Егда̀ ѿ дрѐ):*
*Sticheron 1:* Sending you forth into the whole world like lightening rays, O Apostles who beheld God, Jesus, the true spiritual Sun, by the splendors of your divine preaching drove away the darkness of deception, and enlightened those who were grievously held in the darkness of ignorance: Him do ye therefore beseech to send down upon us also illumination and great mercy!

*Sticheron 2:* Having mounted upon the divine chariot by virtues, and having been enlightened by fasting, Elijah was borne up to the heavenly height: emulate him, my humble soul, and fast from all malice, envy, hatred, and from flowing sweetness and sensuality, that thou mayest escape the grievous afflictions of eternal Gehenna, crying aloud unto Christ: "Lord, glory to Thee!" (4 Kings [2 Kings] 2:11)

*Stichos 5: For Thy name's sake have I waited for Thee, O Lord; my soul hath waited for Thy word, my soul hath hoped in the Lord. (Ps. 129:5–6a)*[^670]
*Tone 5, Podoben: "O venerable father" (Преподо́бне ѻ҆́тче). By Sir Theodore the Studite:*
*Sticheron 1:* O divine Apostles, fervent intercessors for the world...

...and defenders of the Orthodox: having the strength of boldness before Christ our God, pray for us, we entreat you, O all-honored ones, that we may pass through the good season of the Fast in brightness, and receive the grace of the consubstantial Trinity! O glorious great heralds, pray for our souls!

*Stichos 6: From the morning watch until night, from the morning watch let Israel hope in the Lord. (Ps. 129:6b)*[^671]
*In the Tone of the Menaion.*
*And we sing 3 Stichera in the Menaion, unto 4 [verses] for the Saint, Idiomelon. Glory, if there be one; but if not, Glory... Both now... Theotokion (or if it happen somewhere on Wednesday or Friday, Stavrotheotokion) of the same Tone which is in the Menaion.*[^672] *The Entrance is not made with the Gospel, but only with the Censer and a taper (yet when the Gospel is to be read, then with the Gospel also).*[^673] *Then: "O Gladsome Radiance."*[^674]
*Prokeimenon of the Paremia, Psalm 11, Tone 6:*
*Reader:* Thou, O Lord, shalt keep us and shalt preserve us, from this generation and unto the age. (Ps. 11:8)[^675]
*Stichos:* Save me, O Lord, for the godly man hath ceased. (Ps. 11:2)[^676]
*Reading from Genesis (Gen. 1:24–28):*
**Reader:** God said: Let the earth bring forth the living soul according to its kind: quadrupeds and reptiles, and wild beasts of the earth according to their kind; and it was so.
And God made the wild beasts of the earth according to their kind, and cattle according to their kind, and all the reptiles of the earth according to their kind: and God saw that they were good.
And God said: Let Us make man according to Our image and likeness, and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the birds of heaven, and over the cattle and all the earth, and over all the reptiles creeping upon the earth.
And God made man, in the image of God made He him; male and female made He them.
And God blessed them, saying: Increase and multiply, and fill the earth, and have dominion...

...and have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the birds of heaven, and over all the cattle, and over all the earth, and over all the reptiles creeping upon the earth.
And God said: Behold, I have given you every seed-bearing herb sowing seed, which is upon the face of all the earth, and every tree which has in itself the fruit of a seed-bearing seed, to you it shall be for food.
And to all the wild beasts of the earth, and to all the birds of heaven, and to every reptile creeping upon the earth, which has in itself the breath of life, even every green herb for food: and it was so.
And God saw all things whatsoever He had made, and, behold, they were very good. And there was evening, and there was morning, the sixth day.
And heaven and earth were finished, and all their adornment.
And God finished on the sixth day His works which He had made; and He rested on the seventh day from all His works which He had made.
And God blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it, because in it He rested from all His works which God began to make. (Gen. 1:28b–2:3)[^677]

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 12, Tone 6:*
*Reader:* Look upon me and hear me, O Lord my God. (Ps. 12:4)[^678]
*Stichos:* How long, O Lord, wilt Thou forget me unto the end? How long wilt Thou turn away Thy face from me? (Ps. 12:2)[^679]

*Then the Deacon proclaims:* Command!
*And the Priest, having taken the Censer and a burning taper having three branches [or a single candlestick, for want of means] in his left hand [according to others, in his right hand, or in both hands] together with the Censer, stands before the Holy Table, and the Deacon says: "Wisdom, upright!" And the Priest, signing cruciformly with the Censer and the taper, looking toward the east, says: "The Light of Christ" (and turning toward the west, he says:) "Illumines all!" And they fall prostrate.*[^680]
*Reader:* The Reading from Proverbs.
*Deacon:* Let us attend.
*And they close the Holy Doors.*

**Reader:** My son, if thou wilt receive the words of my commandment, and hide them within thee:
thine ear shall hear wisdom, and thou shalt apply thine heart to understanding, and thou shalt apply it for instruction to thy son.
For if thou shalt call upon wisdom, and utter thy voice for understanding, and seek discernment with a loud voice;
and if thou shalt seek her as silver, and search for her as for treasures:
then shalt thou understand the fear of the Lord, and find the knowledge of God.
For the Lord gives wisdom, and from His presence come knowledge and understanding;
and He treasures up salvation for the upright, and He protects their walking,
that He may guard the ways of judgments, and He will preserve the way of them that fear Him with reverence.
Then shalt thou understand righteousness and judgment, and shalt direct all good paths.
For if wisdom come into thy mind, and discernment seem good to thy soul:
good counsel shall preserve thee, and holy thinking shall keep thee,
to deliver thee from the evil way, and from the man that speaks nothing faithfully:
O ye that leave the straight ways, to walk in the paths of darkness!
O ye that rejoice in evils, and delight in wicked perversity!
Whose paths are crooked, and their courses perverse;
to remove thee far from the straight way, and make thee a stranger to righteous understanding. My son, let not evil counsel overtake thee,
which forsakes the instruction of youth, and has forgotten the divine covenant:
for she has placed her house near death, and near Hades with... (Prov. 2:1–18a)[^681] ...earthly beings her paths. None that go by her shall return, neither shall they take hold of the straight paths:
for they are not overtaken by the years of life. For if they had walked in good paths, they would have found the paths of righteousness smooth; and good shall be the inhabitants of the earth, and the harmless shall remain upon it.
For the upright shall dwell in the land, and the holy shall remain upon it.
But the paths of the ungodly shall perish from the earth, and the transgressors shall be driven out from it. (Prov. 2:18b–22)[^682]

*Then the Priest says:* Peace be unto thee.
*And the Deacon:* Wisdom!
*And immediately the Cantor sings outside [the Sanctuary], with the Verses:*[^683]
*Cantor:* Let my prayer be set forth as incense before Thee, the lifting up of my hands as an evening sacrifice. (Ps. 140:2)
*And he prostrates his face to the ground.*
*Then the First Choir sings the same:* Let my prayer be set forth...
*Again the Cantor, Verse 1:* Lord, I have cried unto Thee, hear me; attend to the voice of my supplication, when I cry unto Thee. (Ps. 140:1)
*Second Choir:* Let my prayer be set forth...
*Cantor, Verse 2:* Set, O Lord, a watch before my mouth, and a door of enclosure about my lips. (Ps. 140:3)
*First Choir:* Let my prayer be set forth...
*Cantor, Verse 3:* Incline not my heart unto words of evil, to make excuses for sins. (Ps. 140:4)
*Second Choir:* Let my prayer be set forth...
*When one choir sings, we kneel in prayer; and when we arise, that other choir kneels and prays.*[^684]
*Then the Cantor:* Let my prayer be set forth as incense before Thee.
*And we:* The lifting up of my hands as an evening sacrifice.
*If it be the Feast of the Finding of the Precious Head [of the Forerunner], or of the Holy Forty Martyrs: after "Let my prayer be set forth," if it is celebrated for the Saints, there follow the Prokeimenon, the Epistle, Alleluia, and the Gospel; and the rest according to custom.*[^685]
*Apart from a Feast: after "Let my prayer be set forth," the Deacon says the Ektenia, and the Priest the Fervent Prayers. And we make 3 metanias. And there follows the rest of the order of the Presanctified.*
*Hymn at the Transfer of the Holy Gifts:*[^686]
Now the Powers of Heaven invisibly serve with us: for, behold, the King of Glory enters. Behold, the mystical Sacrifice, fully accomplished, is escorted in triumph:

...with faith and love let us draw near, that we may become partakers of eternal life: Alleluia, Alleluia, Alleluia. Then, 3 metanias, having bare heads.

*Be it known that when the Divine Mysteries are being transferred, all the people and the singers, falling prostrate, make godly adoration unto Christ God present in the Mysteries: for They are completely presanctified.*[^687]
*And the Priest takes the veils from the Holy Gifts, and covers Them with the Anaphora, which is the Aer, or Vozdukh (for thus they are accustomed to call it in the regions of Jerusalem).*[^688]
*When he finishes "Our Father", and is about to elevate the Holy Bread, he does not uncover It, but while the Holy Things remain covered, the Priest places his hands with great fear, and touches the Holy Bread. The Deacon says in a loud voice:* Let us attend! *And the Priest proclaims:* The Presanctified Holy Things unto the holy!
*The Priest does not elevate the Holy Lamb here, for It is already consecrated, as has been said; but the Priest uncovers It as is customary, and fractures the Holy Lamb; and they perform Holy Communion according to the order of the Divine Liturgy of Basil the Great.*[^689]
*And the Choir sings the Kinonikon, this one with Alleluia twice:*
*Kinonikon:* Taste and see that the Lord is good. Alleluia, [alleluia]. (Ps. 33:9)
*After the opening of the doors, the Deacon says:* Draw near! *And we make one bow.*
*And we sing another Kinonikon:* I will bless the Lord at all times: Alleluia, once. (Ps. 33:2)
*And the Priest communicates those who desire to receive Communion; and those who receive Communion drink warm water [ukrop].*[^690]
*Then the Priest with the Deacon transfers the Holy Things as is customary. Taking the Holy Chalice, the Priest proclaims:* Always, now and ever, and unto ages of ages.
*Choir:* Let our mouths be filled with Thy praise, O Lord...; *or:* We thank Thee, O Christ our God, that Thou hast accounted us worthy to be partakers of Thy most pure Body, and of Thy precious Blood, poured out for the whole world unto the remission of sins, into the mystery of Thy dispensation: Alleluia. *And one bow.*
*Then the Ektenia, and the Prayer Behind the Ambon. And at its conclusion, one bow; and at "Blessed be the name of the Lord," 3 prostrations. And Psalm 33: "I will bless the Lord at all times." The Antidoron is distributed to us; and the complete Dismissal.*
*This order is observed throughout the entire Holy Forty Days whenever the Presanctified [Liturgy] is celebrated.*
*Where there is no Presanctified [Liturgy], Stichera are sung at Vespers on 6: we sing 2 in the Triodion and 2 in the Menaion; Glory... Both now... Theotokion according to the Tone of the 2nd in the Menaion. At the Aposticha: 2 in the Triodion, the Idiomelon of the day twice, and the Martyrikon which is at "Lord, I have cried." Glory... Both now... Theotokion of the same Tone. And the customary conclusion.*

*And as we go to the Refectory, we eat xerophagy, such as nuts, figs, dates, olives, and other things similar to these. We also drink warm water with honey, which is on Wednesday.*[^691]
*On Thursday of that week we do not set a table, but remain fasting even until Friday: for then, entering the Refectory, we eat.*

*On the same Wednesday of the First Week of the Fast, at Compline:*
*The beginning as on the preceding days.*
*Canon of [St.] Andrew. Tone 6. Ode 1.*
*Heirmos:* He was my helper and protector unto salvation; this is my God, and I will glorify Him; the God of my father, and I will exalt Him: for gloriously has He been glorified! (Exod. 15:2)[^692]

*Troparion 1:* From my youth, O Savior, I have transgressed Thy commandments in all passions; careless and indolent have I passed my life. Therefore do I cry unto Thee, O Savior: at least at the end, save me!

*Troparion 2:* Cast down before Thy gates, O Savior, at least in old age cast me not empty into Hades; but before the end, as Lover of mankind, grant me remission of transgressions!

*Troparion 3:* My wealth, O Savior, I have squandered in prodigality; I am barren of godly fruits, and hungry I cry: O Father of compassions, prevent me and have compassion on me! (Luke 15:13–14)

*Troparion 4:* Having fallen among thieves by my thoughts, I am now wounded all over by them and filled with sores; but do Thou Thyself come unto me, O Christ Savior, and heal me! (Luke 10:30)

*Troparion 5:* The priest, seeing me, passed by, and the Levite, beholding me in afflictions naked, overlooked me; but do Thou, O Jesus, Who didst shine forth from Mary, come and have compassion on me! (Luke 10:31–32)

*Glory... Trinity Hymn:*
*Trinity Hymn:* O Trinity above all essence, worshipped in Unity: take from me the heavy burden of sin, and in Thy loving-kindness grant me tears of compunction!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* O Mother of God, the hope and protectress of them that hymn thee: take...

...from me the heavy burden of sin, and as pure Sovereign Lady, receive me who repent!

*Ode 2. Heirmos:* Give ear, O heaven, and I will speak, and hymn Christ Who came in the flesh from the Virgin! (Deut. 32:1)[^693]

*Troparion 1:* I have stumbled like David in prodigality, and have defiled myself; but wash me also, O Savior, with tears! (2 Kings [2 Sam.] 11:2–4)

*Troparion 2:* Neither tears nor repentance have I, nor compunction; but do Thou Thyself, O Savior, as God grant these unto me!

*Troparion 3:* Shut not Thy door against me then, O Lord, Lord; but open it unto me who repent! (Matt. 25:11–12)

*Troparion 4:* O Lover of mankind, Who desirest all to be saved: do Thou call me back and receive me, as Good One, who repent! (1 Tim. 2:4)

*Troparion 5:* In the night my soul groans, and receive the drops of mine eyes, O Lord, and save me! (Ps. 6:7)

*Glory... Trinity Hymn:*
*Trinity Hymn:* Thee, One in three Persons, the God of all do I hymn: the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* O pure Virgin Mother of God, alone all-hymned: pray fervently that we all may be saved!

*Another Heirmos:* See ye, see ye, that I am God, Who rained down manna and poured forth water from the rock of old in the wilderness for My people, by My sole right hand and by My strength! (Deut. 32:39; Exod. 16:4, 17:6)[^694]

*Troparion 1:* See ye, see ye, that I am God: give ear, my soul, unto the Lord crying aloud, and depart from former sin, and fear Him as Avenger, and Judge, and God!

*Troparion 2:* To whom hast thou likened thyself, O much-sinning soul? Woe is me! Unto the first Cain, and unto that Lamech, having stoned the body with evil deeds, and slain the mind with irrational cravings! (Gen. 4:8, 23)

*Troparion 3:* Having run past all who lived before the Law, O soul, unto Seth...

...thou hast not likened thyself, nor hast thou emulated Enos, nor Enoch by translation, nor Noah; but thou hast been shown destitute of the life of the righteous! (Gen. 4:26; 5:6, 24, 29)

*Troparion 4:* Thou alone hast opened the cataracts of the wrath of thy God, O my soul, and hast drowned all thy flesh as the earth, and thy deeds and life, and hast remained outside the ark of salvation! (Gen. 7:11)

*Glory... Trinity Hymn:*
*Trinity Hymn:* O unoriginate, uncreated Trinity, undivided Unity: receive me who repent, save me who have sinned! I am Thy creation: despise me not, but spare me, and deliver me from the fiery condemnation!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* O pure Sovereign Lady, Birthgiver of God, hope of them that flee unto thee, and haven of them that are in the storm: make the merciful Creator, even Thy Son, propitious unto me also by thy prayers!

*Ode 3. Heirmos:* Establish, O Lord, upon the rock of Thy commandments my shaken heart, for Thou alone art holy and Lord![^695] (1 Kings [1 Sam.] 2:2)

*Troparion 1:* The blessing of Shem hast thou not inherited, O wretched soul, nor a spacious possession like Japhs hast thou obtained in the land of forgiveness! (Gen. 9:26–27)
