*Troparion 2:* Depart from the land of Haran—from sin—O my soul, unto the land that of old ever flowed with living incorruption, which Abraham inherited! (Gen. 12:1–5)

*Troparion 3:* Thou hast heard of Abraham, O my soul, who of old left the land of his fatherland and became a sojourner: emulate his choice! (Gen. 12:1; Heb. 11:8)

*Troparion 4:* At the Oak of Mamre the Patriarch entertained the Angels, and inherited in old age the prize of the promise! (Gen. 18:1–10)

*Troparion 5:* Having understood Isaac, O my wretched soul, as a new sacrifice...

...mystically offered as a whole burnt offering unto the Lord, emulate his [Isaac's] resolved will! (Gen. 22:1–14; Heb. 11:17)

*Troparion 6:* Thou hast heard of Ishmael cast out as the offspring of a bondwoman: be sober, O my soul, watch lest thou suffer something similar by reason of wanton lust! (Gen. 21:9–14; Gal. 4:22–30)

*Glory... Trinity Hymn:*
*Trinity Hymn:* O Trinity simple, uncreated, unoriginate nature, in a Trinity of Hypostases hymned: save us who in faith worship Thy dominion!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* Without knowing man, O Mother of God, in time thou didst bear the timeless Son from the Father: a strange wonder, having remained a Virgin while suckling!

*Ode 4. Heirmos:* The Prophet heard of Thy coming, O Lord, and was afraid: that Thou wast about to be born of a Virgin and appear unto men, and he said: "I heard the report of Thee, and was afraid; glory to Thy power, O Lord!" (Hab. 3:1–2)[^696]

*Troparion 1:* Clothed with royal dignity, a crown, and purple, a man of great possessions and righteous, abounding in wealth and herds, suddenly growing destitute, was stripped of wealth and royal glory! (Job 1:1–3, 13–22)

*Troparion 2:* If he was righteous and blameless above all, yet did not escape the snares and net of the deceitful one: what wilt thou do, O wretched soul that lovest sin, if any unforeseen trial happen to fall upon thee? (Job 1:8; 2:3)

*Troparion 3:* I have defiled my body, I have fouled my spirit, I am covered all over with sores; but as Physician of both, O Christ, through my repentance heal, wash, and cleanse me, and show me whiter than snow, O my Savior! (Ps. 50:9)

*Troparion 4:* When Thou wast crucified, O Word, Thou didst lay down Thy Body and Blood for all: Thy Body that Thou mightest renew me, Thy Blood that Thou mightest wash me, and Thou didst surrender Thy spirit that Thou mightest bring me unto Thy Parent, O Christ! (Matt. 27:50; 1 Pet. 3:18)

*Troparion 5:* Thou hast wrought salvation in the midst of the earth, O compassionate One...

...that we might be saved: willingly crucified upon the Tree, Eden that was closed was opened; and things above and things below, all creation and all nations, being saved, worship Thee! (Ps. 73:12)

*Troparion 6:* May the Blood from Thy side be a font for me, together with the drink pouring forth the water of forgiveness, that on both sides I may be cleansed, anointing myself and drinking, as anointing and drink, O Word, Thy life-bearing words! (John 19:34)

*Troparion 7:* The Church has acquired as a chalice Thy life-bearing side, from which a twofold stream flowed forth for us: of remission and understanding, after the pattern of both the old and the new covenants together, O our Savior! (John 19:34)

*Troparion 8:* I am naked of the bridal chamber, I am naked also of the wedding and the supper; my lamp has gone out for lack of oil; the bridal chamber was locked while I slept; the supper was consumed; and I, bound hand and foot, am cast out! (Matt. 22:11–13; 25:1–12)

*Glory... Trinity Hymn:*
*Trinity Hymn:* Undivided in essence, unconfused in Persons, I theologize Thee, the one Trinitarian Godhead, of one reign and enthroned together: I sing unto Thee the great hymn, in the highest thricely hymned!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* Both thou bearest and remainest a maiden, and in both continuest a virgin by nature: He Who is born renews the law of nature, and the womb brings forth without having conceived: where God wills, the order of nature is overcome, for He does whatsoever He wills!

*Ode 5. Heirmos:* From the night rising early unto Thee, O Lover of mankind, I pray: enlighten me and guide me in Thy commandments, and teach me, O Savior, to do Thy will! (Isa. 26:9)[^697]

*Troparion 1:* Like Jannes and Jambres unto bitter Pharaoh, O Master, have I been heavy in character, in soul and body, and submerged in mind: but help me! (2 Tim. 3:8; Exod. 7:11)

*Troparion 2:* I am mingled with mire, wretched in mind...

...wash me, O Master, I entreat Thee, in the bath of my tears, having made the garment of my flesh white as snow! (Ps. 50:9)

*Troparion 3:* If Thou examine my deeds, O Savior: having surpassed every man in sins, I see myself; for with conscious mind have I sinned, and not in ignorance!

*Troparion 4:* Spare, spare, O Lord, Thy creation! I have sinned, forgive me: for Thou alone art pure by nature, and none other besides Thee is without defilement! (Job 14:4)

*Troparion 5:* Being God, for my sake Thou didst take form in me; Thou hast shown forth miracles, healing lepers and strengthening the paralytic; and Thou didst stop the flow of the woman with an issue of blood, O Savior, by the touching of Thy hem! (Matt. 8:1–3, 9:2–6, 20–22; Phil. 2:7)

*Glory... Trinity Hymn:*
*Trinity Hymn:* Thee, O Trinity, do we glorify, the one God: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, O Father, and Son, and Spirit: simple essence, Unity ever worshipped! (Isa. 6:3)

*Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* From thee, O incorrupt Virgin Mother who knewest not man, God Who created the ages clothed Himself in my mingled substance, and united human nature unto Himself!

*Ode 6. Heirmos:* I cried with my whole heart unto the merciful God, and He heard me from the lowest Hades, and brought up my life from corruption! (Jonah 2:3, 7)[^698]

*Troparion 1:* Resist and conquer the bodily passions, as Joshua conquered Amalek, ever overcoming the deceptive thoughts as the Gibeonites! (Exod. 17:8–13; Josh. 9:3–27)

*Troparion 2:* Pass through the flowing nature of time as the Ark of old, and possess that land of promise, O soul: God commands! (Josh. 3:14–17; 4:1–18)

*Troparion 3:* As Thou didst save Peter when he cried out: "Save me!", prevent me, O Savior, and deliver me from the beast, stretching forth Thine hand and leading me up from the depth of sin! (Matt. 14:30–31) *One choir sings:*
*Troparion 4:* I know Thee as a tranquil haven, O Master, Master Christ! Anticipating me, save me from the inescapable depths of sin and from despair!

*Glory... Trinity Hymn:*
*Trinity Hymn:* I am a simple and undivided Trinity, divided in Persons; and I am a Unity, united in essence: so speaks the Father, and the Son, and the Divine Spirit!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* Thy womb bare God unto us, formed in our likeness: beseech Him as the Creator of the ages, O Theotokos, that through thy prayers we may be justified!

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 6, Podoben: "Hope of the hopeless" (Оу҆пова́нїе):*[^699]
The tempest of passions and the fierce surging billows of transgressions have submerged me in the depth of despair, O Word! But stretch forth Thy mighty right hand and save me as Thou didst Peter, through the honored prayers of the Theotokos, from the depth of my grievous iniquities! (Matt. 14:30–31)

*Ode 7. Heirmos: We have sinned, [transgressed, and dealt unrighteously before Thee; neither have we kept nor done as Thou hast commanded us; but deliver us not up utterly, O God of our fathers!] (Dan. 9:5; Song of Three Youths 1:6–7)*[^700]

*Troparion 1:* Thou hast gathered the transgressions of Manasseh by deliberate choice, setting up the passions as abominations, and multiplying indignation, O my soul! Yet imitating his repentance, acquire fervent compunction! (2 Chron. 33:1–13; Prayer of Manasseh)[^701]

*Troparion 2:* Thou hast imitated the defilements of Ahab, O my soul! Woe is me! Thou hast become a dwelling place for fleshly defilements and a shameful vessel of passions! But sigh from thy depth, and confess thy sins unto God! (3 Kings [1 Kings] 16:30–33; 21:25–26)

*Troparion 3:* Heaven was shut up against thee, O my soul, and a famine from God overtook thee, when, like Ahab of old, thou didst not believe the words of Elijah the Tishbite; but imitating the widow of Zarephath, feed the Prophet's soul! (3 Kings [1 Kings] 17:1–16)[^702]

*Glory... Trinity Hymn:*
*Trinity Hymn:* O simple, undivided Trinity, consubstantial and holy Unity, Radiance and Light, and holy...

...three; and one Holy is chanted, God the Trinity! But sing, glorify Life and Lives, O my soul, the God of all! (Isa. 6:3)

*Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* We hymn thee, we bless thee, we worship thee, O Mother of God: for from the undivided Trinity thou didst bring forth the Son and God, and thou thyself hast opened heavenly things unto us who dwell upon earth!

*Ode 8. Heirmos: Him Whom the heavenly hosts glorify, [and before Whom the Cherubim and Seraphim tremble: all that have breath and creation, hymn, bless, and exalt Him above all unto all ages!] (Dan. 3:57–88)*[^703]

*Troparion 1:* O righteous Judge and Savior, have mercy and deliver me from the fire and the threatening which I must justly endure at the Judgment! Grant me remission before the end through virtue and repentance!

*Troparion 2:* Like the thief I cry unto Thee: "Remember me!"; like Peter I weep bitterly: "Pardon me, O Savior!"; I call aloud like the publican; I shed tears like the harlot! Accept my lamentation, as Thou didst once accept that of the Canaanite woman! (Luke 23:42; Matt. 26:75; Luke 18:13; 7:38; Matt. 15:22)

*Troparion 3:* Heal the festering sore of my wretched soul, O Savior, Thou only Physician! Apply unto me a plaster, and oil and wine: the works of repentance, compunction with tears! (Luke 10:34)

*Troparion 4:* Imitating the Canaanite woman, I cry out: "Have mercy on me, O Son of David!"; I touch the hem of Thy garment like the woman with an issue of blood; I weep like Martha and Mary over Lazarus! (Matt. 15:22; 9:20; John 11:32–33)

*Glory... Trinity Hymn:*
*Trinity Hymn:* O unoriginate Father, co-unoriginate Son, good Comforter, upright Spirit, Begetter of God the Word, Word of the unoriginate Father, living and creating Spirit: O Trinity, Unity, have mercy on me!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* As from purple dye, O most pure Lady, the spiritual scarlet robe of Emmanuel—His flesh—was woven within thy womb! Therefore we honor thee in truth as the Theotokos!

*Ode 9. Heirmos: Conception without seed, [birth-giving ineffable: of a mother who knew not man is the childbearing incorrupt; for the birth of God renews the natures. Therefore in orthodox manner all generations magnify thee as Mother and Bride of God!] (Luke 1:46–55)*[^704] *One choir sings:*
*Troparion 1:* Healing diseases, Christ the Word proclaimed the good tidings unto the poor: He healed the crippled, ate with publicans, conversed with sinners, and by the touch of His hand recalled the departed soul of Jairus' daughter! (Matt. 4:23; 9:10–11; 9:18–25)

*Troparion 2:* The publican was saved and the harlot was brought to chastity, while the Pharisee, boasting, was condemned! For the one cried: "Be merciful unto me!"; the other: "Have mercy on me!"; but he boasted, shouting: "O God, I thank Thee!" and other senseless words! (Luke 18:9–14)

*Troparion 3:* Zacchaeus was a publican, yet he was saved; while Simon the Pharisee was scandalized, the harlot received absolution and remission from Him Who has power to forgive sins: strive to imitate her, O my soul! (Luke 19:1–10; 7:36–50)

*Troparion 4:* O my soul, sharing the passions of the harlot, thou hast not rivaled her, who, taking an alabaster flask of myrrh, anointed the feet of the Savior with tears, and wiped them with her hair: for He tore up the handwriting of her ancient transgressions! (Luke 7:37–38; Col. 2:14)[^705]

*Troparion 5:* O my soul, thou hast learned how the cities unto which Christ announced the Gospel were cursed! Fear their example, lest thou become like them, whom the Master, comparing them unto Sodom, condemned even unto Hades! (Matt. 11:20–24)

*Troparion 6:* Appear not worse, O my soul, through despair, having heard of the faith of the Canaanite woman, whose daughter was healed by the word of God! Cry out from the depth of thy heart, like her unto Christ: "O Son of David, save me also!" (Matt. 15:21–28)

*Glory... Trinity Hymn:*
*Trinity Hymn:* Consubstantial Trinity, three-hypostatic Unity, we hymn Thee, glorifying the Father, magnifying the Son, and worshipping the Spirit, truly one God by nature, Life, and living, endless Kingdom!

*Both now... Theotokion:*

*Theotokion:* Thou hast borne the one God, and alone remained a Virgin! O marvelous birth-giving! O marvelous conception! Conception without seed, and birth-giving beyond nature! But O pure Bride of God, preserve the holy flock which Thy Son acquired! (Acts 20:28)[^706]

*Then the Heirmos: "Conception without seed..." Both choirs together. And the rest of the Order of Great Compline.*[^707]

## Thursday of the First Week of Great Lent

*At Matins: Triadica of the Tone.*[^708] *After the first stichology, sessional hymns from the Octoechos.*

*After the second stichology, Sessional Hymn, Tone 2, Podoben: "Thou Who didst put to death" (Оу҆́мрщвы́й па́че):*[^709]
O Word of God, Who by preaching didst show forth the Disciples as luminaries unto the ends of the earth: enlighten our hearts with the light of virtues and cleanse them through fasting, giving unto Thy servants repentance of conversion, that we may glorify Thee, O Savior, Who alone art supremely good!

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* O pure Virgin who knewest not wedlock, unwedded Mother of God: with the Apostles ever entreat Thy Son, Whom thou didst bear in the flesh beyond nature, to grant forgiveness of transgressions, amendment of life, and deliverance from passions unto all who hymn thee!

*After the third stichology, Sessional Hymn, Tone 5, Podoben: "More holy than the Cherubim" (Ст҃ѣ́йшаѧ херꙋ́:). By Theodore:*[^710]
We pray you, O twelvefold company of the Apostles, that through your guidance we may peacefully pass through abstinence, the most radiant of virtues and our heavenly companion, and receive the fruits of salvation; for truly you are the strength of earthly mortals and the refuge of our souls!

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* More holy than the Cherubim, thou who hast become higher than the heavens, all-hymned...

...Theotokos! Truly confessing thee, we sinners have salvation, and in temptations find protection! Therefore cease not to pray for us, O strength and refuge of our souls!

*We sing the Canon in the Menaion on 6, and the Triodia according to their order. And the Biblical Canticles from the Psalter are chanted.*[^711]

*Triodion of Joseph, Tone 2. Ode 4:*
*Heirmos: Coming forth from the Virgin, [neither an ambassador nor an angel, but the Lord Himself incarnate, Thou didst save my whole humanity. Therefore I cry unto Thee: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!] (Hab. 3:1–3)*[^712]

*Troparion 1:* Receiving the ray of abstinence, shine forth, O my soul, and flee the darkening of sin, so that the light of forgiveness may enter into thee through the Holy Spirit!

*Troparion 2:* Having beguiled me with the hook of pleasure, the deceiver took me captive; but O Apostles who caught the world with the Word, deliver me from his malice! (Matt. 4:19)

*Troparion 3:* Ye appeared as the dawnings of the Sun of glory, O glorious Apostles, driving away the darkness of delusion: enlighten me also, who am darkened by great wickedness!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* Afflicted by night and by day, I cry unto thee and am delivered; I pass through the shadow of pleasures and am saved, protected by thy power, O Virgin!

*Another Canon [Ode 4], Tone 5. By Master Theodore:*
*Heirmos: The works of Thy dispensation, [O Lord, astonished the Prophet Habakkuk; for Thou didst go forth for the salvation of Thy people, to save Thine anointed ones!] (Hab. 3:1–3, 13)*[^713]

*Troparion 1:* Being all-radiant luminaries of the Sun of righteousness, O Apostles, ye enlighten the earthly world, driving away the gloom of deception! (Mal. 4:2)

*Troparion 2:* Being the Savior's lyre moved by the Spirit, O Apostles, having made yourselves known on earth, ye sing unto us a melodious song and convert the world unto God!

*Glory... Trinity Hymn:*
*Trinity Hymn:* Glorifying the Trinity in one sole essence, let us hymn the one Lord God: the unbegotten Father...

...and the begotten Son, and the living Spirit!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* A Virgin conceived in her womb, O Lord, and bare Thee, Emmanuel; for Thou didst go forth for the salvation of Thy people, to save Thine elect, O Lover of mankind! (Isa. 7:14; Hab. 3:13)

*Refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*
*Troparion:* O divine and all-honored twelvefold company of the Apostles: entreat Christ God for us, we pray, that we may powerfully traverse the forty-day arena of the fast!

*Katavasia: The works of Thy dispensation, O Lord, astonished the Prophet Habakkuk; for Thou didst go forth for the salvation of Thy people, to save Thine elect hast Thou come!* (Hab. 3:1–3, 13)[^714]

*Ode 8. Heirmos: The tyrant's decree [which was contrary to God, the three youths regarded not; and being cast into the midst of the furnace of fire, being moistened with dew, they sang: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!] (Dan. 3:57–88)*[^715]

*Troparion 1:* Let us fast from every pleasure, nourishing the senses through the fast, and let us fervently drink the draught of compunction, singing: "Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!"

*Troparion 2:* Entreat that I may become a partaker of the standing at the right hand, when ye sit with Christ to judge mankind, O Apostles—me who am guilty of many sins and subject to judgment! (Matt. 19:28; 25:33)

*Troparion 3:* Having cleansed ourselves through the fast, let us ascend the chariot of divine virtues, and give wings unto our mind toward the aerial height, singing: "Bless the Lord, all ye works!" (4 Kings [2 Kings] 2:11)

*Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* Thou didst remain unconsumed, having given birth unto the Fire of the Godhead, O Virgin! Consume the passions of the souls of those who in faith sing unto thee the Angel's greeting, O sole Mediatress of joy! (Luke 1:28)

*Another Heirmos [Tone 5, Theodore]: Thy highly hymned children, [delivered from the furnace by Thy word, cried aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto all ages!] (Dan. 3:57–88)*[^716]

*Troparion 1:* Hymning the Disciples of Christ as trumpets of the Spirit, let us cry aloud: "Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!"

*Troparion 2:* Let us hymn the Disciples of Christ as intercessors for the world and expellers of delusion, crying aloud: "Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!"

*Refrain: Let us bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, the Lord.*

*Trinity Hymn:* Praising the all-holy Trinity—in Father, and Son, and Spirit—we sing: "Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!"

*Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* All of us mortals hymn thy ineffable childbearing, piously crying out, O pure Virgin: "Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!"

*Refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*
*Troparion:* O Apostles, pray that in peace we may finish the cleansing days of the fast, who cry: "Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!"

*Refrain: We praise, we bless, and we worship the Lord.*
*Katavasia: Thy highly hymned children, singing in the furnace, O Christ, said: "Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto all ages!"* (Dan. 3:57–88)[^717]

*Ode 9. Heirmos: The uncontainable God, [Whom the heavens could not contain, was contained within thy womb, O Mother of God, and bare the Salvation of the world: therefore with unceasing hymns we magnify thee!] (Luke 1:46–55)*[^718]

*Troparion 1:* Cast into the deep abyss of pleasures, I call upon the deep of Thy compassion: O Pilot, save me!

*Troparion 2:* O Wellspring of mercy, grant me now a drop of compunction, that I may weep for my wicked deeds, which are measureless beyond the sea!

*Troparion 3:* Through the honored prayers of Thy Disciples, O Jesus, grant that I may venerate Thy precious Resurrection and Thy divine Passions!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* O all-immaculate Lady, who by the dwelling of God within thee hast made heavenly our earthly clay: deliver us from all afflictions!

*Another Canon [Ode 9], Tone 5. By Theodore:*
*Heirmos: We magnify, O Christ, [Thy most pure Mother, whom Thou didst give unto us as an intercessor, to save us who sing: Blessed is the God of our fathers!] (Luke 1:46–55)*[^719]

*Troparion 1:* Having drawn the water of immortality from the prophetic wellsprings of salvation, the Apostles ever give drink unto the thirsty by the commandment of life! (Isa. 12:3)

*Troparion 2:* Having been revealed as princes of the Heavenly King, O Apostles, ye subject the whole universe to honor, worship, and glorify Him alone as God! (Ps. 44:17 [LXX])

*Glory... Trinity Hymn:*
*Trinity Hymn:* O undivided Trinity, Unity, all-creating and all-powerful Father, and Son, and Holy Spirit: Thou art my God...

...Lord, and Light, and hymning Thee, I worship Thee!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* Generation of generations, we call thee blessed, O Mother and pure Virgin, for thou wast the cleansing place for the world, having ineffably given birth unto the Savior and Creator! (Luke 1:48)

*Refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*
*Troparion:* As we hymn Thee, the Savior, vouchsafe us, through the company of Thine Apostles, to pass in compunction of heart through all the days of the light-bearing fast!

*Katavasia: We magnify Thee, O Christ, and Thy most pure and all-immaculate Mother, for beyond nature she bare Thee in the flesh, Who deliverest us from all delusion and corruption!*[^720]

*Then: "It is truly meet..." Exapostilarion of the Tone.*[^721]

*At the Aposticha, Idiomelon Stichera, Tone 3:*[^722]
O Lord, Thou hast appointed repentance for me, a sinner, wishing to save me, unworthy though I be, by Thy measureless mercy! Falling down before Thee, I pray: bow down my soul through fasting, for I have fled unto Thee, Who alone art plenteous in mercy!

*Verse 1: We were filled in the morning with Thy mercy, O Lord, and we rejoiced and were glad. [In all our days, let us be glad for the days wherein Thou didst humble us, for the years wherein we saw evils. And look upon Thy servants and upon Thy works, and guide their sons!] (Ps. 89:14–16 [LXX])*[^723]
*And again we chant the same Sticheron.*
*Verse 2: And let the brightness of the Lord our God be upon us, [and establish Thou the works of our hands upon us, yea, the work of our hands establish Thou!] (Ps. 89:17 [LXX])*[^724]

*Martyrion:*
As luminaries ye shine in the world, and after death also, O holy Martyrs! Having fought the good fight and possessing boldness, entreat Christ that our souls may find mercy! (Phil. 2:15; 2 Tim. 4:7)

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* O Theotokos, mediatress for all who pray unto thee: in thee do we place our trust, in thee do we boast, in thee is all our hope! Entreat Him Who was born of thee for thine unprofitable servants!

*Then: "It is good to give praise unto the Lord..." (Ps. 91:2 [LXX]). And the rest (see fol. 180).*[^725]

*On the same Thursday of the First Week of the Fast, at the Sixth Hour:*
*Troparion, Tone 3:*

*Troparion:* Deliver us from enemies visible and invisible, O Lord, lest the gentiles say at any time: "Where is their God?" (Ps. 78:10; 113:10 [LXX]). Let them know, O Master, that Thou overlookest the sins of Thy people who repent!

*Glory... the ending:* That Thou overlookest the sins of Thy people who repent!
*Both now... the whole Troparion:* Deliver us from enemies visible and invisible...
*Without metanias.*[^726]

*Prokeimenon 1, Tone 4:* When the Lord turns back the captivity of His people! (Ps. 13:7b [LXX])[^727]
*Verse:* The fool has said in his heart: "There is no God!" (Ps. 13:1a [LXX])[^728]

*Reading of the Prophecy of Isaiah (2:11–21 [LXX]):*[^729]
The Lord alone shall be exalted in that day! (v. 11b). For the day of the Lord of Sabaoth is coming upon every insulter and proud one, and upon every high and haughty one, and they shall be brought low (v. 12); and upon every cedar of Lebanon, high and exalted, and upon every oak of the acorn of Bashan (v. 13); and upon every high mountain, and upon every high hill (v. 14); and upon every high tower, and upon every high wall (v. 15); and upon every ship of the sea, and upon every spectacle of the beauty of ships (v. 16). And every man shall be brought low, and the haughtiness of men shall fall; and the Lord alone shall be exalted in that day (v. 17). And all handmade idols they shall hide (v. 18), carrying them into caves and into clefts of the rocks and into the dens of the earth, from before the face of the fear of the Lord and from the glory of His strength, when He shall arise to shatter the earth (v. 19). For in that day a man shall cast away his abominations of silver and of gold, which they made for themselves that they might worship vanities and bats (v. 20), to enter into the dens of the solid rock and into the clefts of the stones, from before the face of the fear...

...of the Lord and from the glory of His strength, when He shall arise to shatter the earth! (Isa. 2:21b [LXX]).

*Prokeimenon 2, Tone 4:* Lord, who shall abide in Thy tabernacle? (Ps. 14:1a [LXX])[^730]
*Verse:* He that walks blamelessly and works righteousness (Ps. 14:2a [LXX])[^731]

*Then: "Let Thy tender mercies speedily anticipate us..." (Ps. 78:8 [LXX]). And if thou wilt, a Patristic reading takes place.*[^732]

*On that same Thursday evening, at "Lord, I have cried":*
*Stichera, Tone 2, Podoben: "Our Enlightener" (Просвѣти́телѧ на́ше). By Joseph:*[^733]
*Sticheron 1:* Enlighten me, who am darkened by the deceits of the adversary, O my Christ, Thou Who of old, hanging upon the Cross, didst darken the sun, and openly didst enlighten the faithful with the true light of forgiveness: that walking in the light of Thy commandments, I may attain unto the saving dawn of Thy Resurrection! (Matt. 27:45; Isa. 2:5)

*Sticheron 2:* As a cluster of the vine hanging upon the Tree, O Savior, with the wine of incorruption Thou hast given drink unto the ends of the earth, O Christ! Therefore I cry aloud: Having given me, who am ever grievously darkened by the drunkenness of sin, to drink of the sweetness of true compunction, strengthen me now to fast from pleasures, O Savior, as Thou art good and the Lover of mankind! (Num. 13:23; John 15:1–5)

*Another Sticheron, by Master Theodore, in the same Tone, Podoben: "O the great mystery" (Ѽ вели́кагѡ та́инства):*[^734]
O the power of Thy Cross! It has blossomed forth abstinence unto the Church, tearing up by the roots Adam's ancient lack of abstinence in Eden: that brought death unto mankind, but this incorruptibly pours forth immortality unto the world, as from another fountain of paradise, through the outpouring of Thy life-flowing Blood together with water, whence all things have been brought to life! Thereby sweeten for us our fasting food, O Christ, God of Israel, Who hast great mercy! (Gen. 2:9, 3:6; John 19:34)[^735]

*And in the Menaion. Glory... Both now... Theotokion from the Octoechos or the Menaion.*[^736]
*Then:*

*Then: "O Gladsome Radiance."*[^737]

*Prokeimenon 1, Tone 6:* I will bless the Lord Who has given me understanding! (Ps. 15:7a [LXX])[^738]
*Verse:* Keep me, O Lord, for in Thee have I hoped! (Ps. 15:1 [LXX])[^739]

*Reading from Genesis (2:4b–15 [LXX]):*[^740]
This is the book of the origin of heaven and earth, when the day was wherein the Lord God made heaven and earth (v. 4); and every plant of the field before it was upon the earth, and every herb of the field before it sprang up; for God had not rained upon the earth, and there was not a man to work it (v. 5). But a fountain went up out of the earth and watered all the face of the earth (v. 6). And God formed man, taking dust from the earth, and breathed into his face the breath of life; and man became a living soul (v. 7). And God planted a Paradise in Eden eastward, and there He put the man whom He had formed (v. 8). And God made to spring up yet out of the earth every tree that is beautiful to the sight and good for food, and the Tree of Life in the midst of Paradise, and the Tree to know understanding of good and evil (v. 9). And a river went forth out of Eden to water Paradise; from thence it was separated into four headwaters (v. 10). The name of the one is Pishon; this is that which encompasses all the land of Havilah, where there is gold (v. 11); and the gold of that land is good; and there is carbuncle and the green stone (v. 12). And the name of the second river is Gihon; this is that which encompasses all the land of Ethiopia (v. 13). And the third river is the Tigris; this is that which flows opposite the Assyrians; and the fourth river is Euphrates (v. 14). And the Lord God took the man whom He had formed, and put...

...him into Paradise, to work it and to keep it (v. 15). And the Lord God commanded Adam, saying: "Of every tree that is in Paradise thou mayest freely eat (v. 16); but of the Tree to know good and evil, ye shall not eat of it; for in whatsoever day ye eat of it, ye shall die by death" (v. 17). And the Lord God said: "It is not good that the man should be alone; let Us make him a helper suitable for him" (v. 18). And God formed yet out of the earth all the beasts of the field and all the birds of the heaven, and brought them unto Adam to see what he would call them; and whatsoever Adam called each living soul, that was its name (v. 19).

*Prokeimenon 2, Tone 4:* Keep me, O Lord, as the apple of Thine eye! (Ps. 16:8a [LXX])[^741]
*Verse:* Hear, O Lord, my righteousness! (Ps. 16:1a [LXX])[^742]

*Reading from Proverbs (3:1–9 [LXX]):*[^743]
My son, forget not my laws, but let thine heart keep my words (v. 1); for length of life, and years of life, and peace shall they add unto thee (v. 2). Let not mercy and faithfulness forsake thee; bind them upon thy neck, write them upon the tablet of thine heart (v. 3). And thou shalt find grace; and provide good things before the Lord God and men (v. 4). Trust in God with all thine heart, and be not exalted in thine own wisdom (v. 5). In all thy ways acknowledge her, that she may make straight thy paths, and thy foot shall not stumble (v. 6). Be not wise in thine own eyes; fear God, and depart from all evil (v. 7). Then shall there be healing unto thy body, and care unto thy bones (v. 8). Honor the Lord from thy righteous labors, and give tithes unto Him of the first-fruits of thy...

...fruits of righteousness (v. 9). So shall thy barns be filled with fullness of wheat, and thy vats shall overflow with wine (v. 10). My son, despise not the chastening of the Lord, neither faint when thou art reproved by Him (v. 11); for whom the Lord loves He chastens, and scourges every son whom He receives (v. 12). Blessed is the man that finds wisdom, and the mortal that knows understanding (v. 13); for it is better to traffic for her than for treasures of gold and silver (v. 14). Yea, she is more precious than costly stones; nothing that is evil can resist her; she is well-known unto all that approach her, and nothing precious is worthy of her (v. 15). For length of life and years of existence are in her right hand, and in her left hand are riches and glory; [out of her mouth proceeds righteousness, and law and mercy she bears upon her tongue] (v. 16). Her ways are good ways, and all her paths are in peace (v. 17). She is a tree of life unto all that lay hold upon her, and steadfast unto those that rely upon her, as upon the Lord (v. 18).

*Then: "Vouchsafe, O Lord."*[^744]

*Then, at the Aposticha, Idiomelon Stichera, Tone 4:*[^745]
Desiring to partake of the divine Pascha, not that which comes from Egypt, but that which proceeds out of Zion, let us put away the leaven of sin through repentance! Let us gird our loins through the mortification of pleasures; let us adorn our feet with sandals that protect us from every evil deed; and let us be strengthened by the staff of faith! Let us not emulate the enemies of the blessed Cross, making a god of the belly; but through fasting let us follow Him Who showed us victory over the devil, the Savior of our souls! (Exod. 12:11; 1 Cor. 5:7–8; Eph. 6:14–15; Phil. 3:18–19; Matt. 4:1–11) *Verse 1: Unto Thee have I lifted up mine eyes, [O Thou that dwellest in heaven! Behold, as the eyes of servants look unto the hands of their masters, and as the eyes of a maiden unto the hands of her mistress, so our eyes look unto the Lord our God, until He have mercy on us!] (Ps. 122:1–2 [LXX])*[^746]
*And again we chant the same Sticheron.*

*Verse 2: Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us, [for we are greatly filled with contempt!] (Ps. 122:3a [LXX])*[^747]

*Martyrion:*
Glorified in the memories of Thy Saints, O Christ God, entreated by them: send down upon us Thy great mercy!

*Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion, Tone 4, Podoben: "As one valiant" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*[^748]
When she beheld Thee nailed upon the Cross, O Lord, the Ewe-lamb and Thy Mother marveled, and cried aloud: "What a spectacle is this, O most desired Son? This is what the faithless and lawless assembly renders unto Thee, having enjoyed Thy many wonders! But glory to Thine ineffable condescension, O Master!" (John 19:25–27)

*Then: "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart..." (Luke 2:29–32). And the rest: the usual conclusion.*[^749]

*Rule concerning the Refectory (see fol. 241).*[^750]

*On the same Thursday of the First Week of the Fast, Canon at Compline, Tone 6:*[^751]
*Ode 1. Heirmos: A helper and a protector [became my salvation: He is my God, and I will glorify Him; the God of my father, and I will exalt Him; for gloriously has He been glorified!] (Exod. 15:1–2)*[^752]

*Troparion 1:* O Lamb of God, Who takest away the sins of all: take from me the heavy burden of sin, and as Thou art compassionate, grant me tears of compunction! (John 1:29)

*Troparion 2:* Abhor me not, O Savior; cast me not away from Thy presence! Take from me the heavy burden of sin, and as Thou art compassionate, grant me remission of sins! (Ps. 50:13 [LXX])

*Troparion 3:* Before Thee I fall down, O Jesus: I have sinned against Thee, cleanse me! Take from me the heavy burden of sin, and as Thou art compassionate, grant me tears of compunction!

*Troparion 4:* Enter not into judgment with me, bringing forth my deeds, inquiring into my words, and examining my inclinations; but in Thy compassions, looking past my wicked deeds, save me, O Almighty! (Ps. 142:2 [LXX])

*Troparion 5:* Having wasted the wealth of my soul in sin, I am empty...

...of pious virtues; and hungering I cry: "O Giver of mercy, O Lord, save me!" (Luke 15:13–17)

*Troparion 6:* My voluntary and involuntary sins, O Savior, both manifest and hidden, known and unknown: having forgiven them all as God, cleanse and save me!

*Glory... Trinity Hymn:*
*Trinity Hymn:* O superessential Trinity, worshipped in Unity: take from me the heavy burden of sin, and as Thou art compassionate, grant me tears of compunction!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* O Theotokos, hope and protectress of all who hymn thee: take from me the heavy burden of sin, and as Lady, accept me who repent!

*Ode 2. Heirmos: See, see that I am God, [Who rained manna, and poured forth water from the rock of old in the wilderness for My people, by My right hand alone and by My strength!] (Deut. 32:39; Exod. 16:4; 17:6)*[^753]

*Troparion 1:* "I have slain a man unto my wounding, and a young man unto my hurt," Lamech cried aloud, lamenting! Yet thou tremblest not, O my soul, having defiled the flesh and polluted the mind! (Gen. 4:23)

*Troparion 2:* Thou hast devised to build a tower, O my soul, and to establish a fortification for thy lusts, had not the Creator confounded thy counsels and dashed thy contrivances down to the earth! (Gen. 11:4–8)

*Troparion 3:* O how I have emulated Lamech, the former murderer, slaying the soul as a man, the mind as a young man, and my body as a brother, like Cain the murderer, through voluptuous strivings! (Gen. 4:8, 23)

*Troparion 4:* I have been wounded and stricken! Behold the enemy's arrows that have pierced my soul and body! Behold the sores, festerings, and darkenings that cry aloud, the self-willed wounds of the passions! (Ps. 37:6 [LXX]) *Troparion 5:* The Lord rained fire from the Lord of old upon lawlessness that provoked His wrath, and burned up the Sodomites! But thou, O my soul, hast kindled the fire of Gehenna, wherein thou art about to be burned! (Gen. 19:24)

*Another Heirmos:*[^754]
Understand and see that I am God, examining hearts, testing thoughts, reproving deeds, consuming sins, and judging the orphan, the humble, and the poor! (Deut. 32:39; Jer. 17:10; Ps. 81:3 [LXX])

*Glory... Trinity Hymn:*
*Trinity Hymn:* O unoriginate, uncreated Trinity, undivided Unity: accept me who repent; save me who have sinned! I am Thy creation, despise me not, but spare me, and deliver me from condemnation to the fire!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* O pure Lady, Mother of God, hope of those who flee unto thee, and haven in the storm: entreat the merciful Creator and Thy Son to have mercy on me also through thy prayers!

*Ode 3. Heirmos: Establish, O Lord, upon the rock [of Thy commandments my wavering heart, for Thou alone art holy and the Lord!] (1 Kings [1 Sam.] 2:2)*[^755]

*Troparion 1:* Of old, O my soul, thou hast likened thyself unto Hagar the Egyptian, having enslaved thyself by thy choice, and given birth unto a new Ishmael: arrogance! (Gen. 16:1–16)

*Troparion 2:* Thou hast known Jacob's ladder, O my soul, appearing from earth unto heaven: why hast thou not a steadfast ascent of piety? (Gen. 28:12)

*Troparion 3:* Emulate the Priest of God and solitary King, the image of Christ's manner of life in the world among men! (Gen. 14:18; Heb. 7:1–3)[^756]

*Troparion 4:* Become not a pillar of salt, O my soul, turning back! Let the example of Sodom terrify thee; save thyself high up in Zoar! (Gen. 19:22, 26; Luke 17:32)

*Troparion 5:* Turn, groan, O wretched soul, before...

...the end takes hold of the solemnity of life, before the Lord shuts the door of the bridal chamber! (Matt. 25:10–12)

*Glory... Trinity Hymn:*
*Trinity Hymn:* O simple, uncreated Trinity, unoriginate Essence, hymned in a Trinity of Persons: save us who in faith worship Thy sovereignty!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* The timeless Son from the Father thou hast in time borne without knowing man, O Theotokos: a strange marvel, remaining a Virgin while nursing!

*Ode 4. Heirmos: The Prophet heard [of Thy coming, O Lord, and was afraid: that Thou wast about to be born of a Virgin and appear unto men, and he said: "I have heard Thy report, and was afraid; glory to Thy power, O Lord!"] (Hab. 3:1–2)*[^757]

*Troparion 1:* The time of my life is short and filled with sicknesses and wickedness; but accept me in repentance and summon me unto understanding, lest I become the possession and food of the stranger: O Savior, do Thou Thyself have compassion on me!

*Troparion 2:* Now I am boastful in words, and insolent in heart, in vanity and all things: condemn me not with the Pharisee, but rather grant me the Publican's humility, O Thou Who alone art compassionate, Thou righteous Judge, and count me with him! (Luke 18:11–14)

*Troparion 3:* Having defiled the vessel of my flesh, I know that I have sinned, O compassionate One! But accept me in repentance and summon me unto understanding, lest I become the possession and food of the stranger: O Savior, do Thou Thyself have compassion on me!

*Troparion 4:* I have become a very idol-temple to the passions, having defiled my soul, O compassionate One! But accept me in repentance and summon me unto understanding, lest I become the possession and food of the stranger: O Savior, do Thou Thyself have compassion on me!

*Troparion 5:* I did not listen to Thy voice, I disobeyed Thy law-giving Scripture; but accept me in repentance and summon me unto understanding, lest I become the possession or food...

...of the stranger: O Savior, do Thou Thyself have compassion on me!

*Glory... Trinity Hymn:*
*Trinity Hymn:* Undivided in essence, unconfused in Persons, I theologize Thee, the one Trinitarian Godhead, as co-reigning and enthroned together; I cry aloud unto Thee the great hymn thrice-praised on high! (Isa. 6:3)

*Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* Thou both givest birth and remainest a virgin, and abidest in both by nature a virgin! He Who was born renews the laws of nature, and the womb gives birth without labor: where God wills, the order of nature is overcome, for He does whatsoever He wills!

*Ode 5. Heirmos: Rising early from the night [I seek Thee, O Lover of mankind: enlighten me, I pray Thee, and guide me in Thy commandments, and teach me, O Savior, to do Thy will!] (Isa. 26:9)*[^758]

*Troparion 1:* Imitating the woman bowed down to the earth, approach, O my soul, and fall at the feet of Jesus, that He may straighten thee, and thou mayest walk uprightly in the paths of the Lord! (Luke 13:11–13)

*Troparion 2:* Though Thou art a deep well, O Master, pour forth water unto me from Thy most pure streams, that like the Samaritan woman I may thirst no more; for Thou pourest forth the streams of life! (John 4:7–15)

*Troparion 3:* Let my tears be Siloam unto me, O Master Lord, that I also may wash the apple of my heart, and see Thee spiritually, the Light before the ages! (John 9:7)

*Glory... Trinity Hymn:*
*Trinity Hymn:* Thee, O Trinity, we glorify, the one God: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, Father, Son, and Spirit, simple Essence, Unity ever worshipped! (Isa. 6:3)

*Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* From thee God Who created the ages was clothed in my clay, O incorrupt, unwedded Mother and Virgin, and united human nature unto Himself! (Heb. 1:2)

*Ode 6. Heirmos: I cried with my whole heart [unto the merciful God, and He heard me from the lowest Hades, and brought up my life from corruption!] (Jonah 2:3–7)*[^759]

*Troparion 1:* "Take what is thine," may I not hear, O Lord, dismissed...

...from Thee; nor: "Depart into the accursed fire!"; but rather the good voice spoken unto the righteous! (Matt. 20:14; 25:41)

*Troparion 2:* I am that royal drachma, O Savior, which of old was lost; but having kindled the lamp, Thy Forerunner, O Word, search and find Thine image! (Luke 15:8–9; John 5:35)[^760]

*Glory... Trinity Hymn:*
*Trinity Hymn:* I am a simple Trinity, undivided, divided hypostatically, and a Unity united in essence: so speaks the Father, and the Son, and the Divine Spirit!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* Thy womb bare God unto us, formed in our likeness: beseech Him as the Creator of all, O Theotokos, that through thy prayers we may be justified!

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 6, Podoben: "Hope of the hopeless" (Оу҆пова́нїе):*[^761]
The terrible day of Thy coming and Thine inexorable judgment seat I fear, O Christ, and shudder and tremble, as one who has a multitude of sins! But before the end, as merciful God, turn and save me, through the entreaties of her who bare Thee, O compassionate Savior, Who alone art the Lover of mankind!

*Ode 7. Heirmos: We have sinned, [transgressed, and dealt unrighteously before Thee; neither have we kept nor done as Thou hast commanded us; but deliver us not up utterly, O God of our fathers!] (Dan. 9:5; Song of Three Youths 1:6–7)*[^762]

*Troparion 1:* My days have vanished like a dream of one awaking; therefore like Hezekiah I shed tears upon my bed, that years may be added unto my life! But what Isaiah shall stand before thee, O my soul, if not the God of all? (Ps. 72:20 [LXX]; 4 Kings [2 Kings] 20:1–6; Isa. 38:1–8)[^763]

*Troparion 2:* I fall down before Thee and bring Thee my words as tears: I have sinned as the harlot never sinned, and have committed iniquity as no other upon earth! But have compassion upon Thy creation, O Master, and summon me! (Luke 7:37–38)

*Troparion 3:* I have buried Thine image and corrupted Thy commandment; all my beauty has been darkened, and by passions the lamp has been extinguished, O Savior! But having compassion, restore unto me the joy, as David sings! (Ps. 50:14 [LXX])[^764] *Troparion 4:* Turn, repent, disclose hidden things, say unto God Who knows all things: "Thou knowest my secrets, Thou only Savior; but do Thou Thyself have mercy on me, as David sings, according to Thy mercy!" (Ps. 50:3 [LXX])

*Glory... Trinity Hymn:*
*Trinity Hymn:* O simple, undivided, consubstantial Trinity, holy Unity, Lights and Light, and three Holies, and one Holy is chanted, God the Trinity! But sing, glorify Life and Lives, O my soul, the God of all! (Isa. 6:3)

*Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* We hymn thee, we bless thee, we worship thee, O Mother of God: for from the undivided Trinity thou didst bring forth the one Son and God, and thou thyself hast opened heavenly things unto us who dwell upon earth!

*Ode 8. Heirmos: Him Whom the heavenly hosts glorify, [and before Whom the Cherubim and Seraphim tremble: all that have breath and creation, hymn, bless, and exalt Him above all unto all ages!] (Dan. 3:57–88)*[^765]

*Troparion 1:* Pouring out an alabaster flask of tears upon Thy head like myrrh, O Savior, I cry unto Thee as the harlot seeking mercy: I offer supplication and seek to receive remission! (Matt. 26:7; Luke 7:37–38)

*Troparion 2:* Though no one has sinned against Thee as I, yet accept even me, O compassionate Savior, repenting with fear and crying out with love: "I have sinned against Thee alone, have mercy on me, O merciful One!" (Ps. 50:6 [LXX])

*Troparion 3:* Spare Thine own creation, O God, and seek what is lost as the Shepherd: anticipate the strayed one, snatch me from the wolf, and make me as a sheep upon the pasture of Thy sheep! (Luke 15:4–6; John 10:11–12)

*Troparion 4:* When as Judge Thou shalt sit as compassionate, and reveal Thy terrible glory, O Savior: O what fear shall there be then, the furnace burning, while all tremble before Thine inexorable judgment seat! (Matt. 25:31; Dan. 7:9–10)

*Glory... Trinity Hymn:*
*Trinity Hymn:* O unoriginate Father, co-unoriginate Son, good Comforter...

...good Comforter, good Spirit, upright Spirit, Begetter of the Word of God, Word of the unoriginate Father, living and creating Spirit: Trinity, Unity, have mercy on me!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* As from a dye-pot, O all-pure Virgin, the spiritual purple cloth—the flesh of Emmanuel—was woven within thy womb; therefore we honor thee in truth as the Theotokos!

*Ode 9. Heirmos: A conception without seed, [an ineffable childbirth, of a Mother unwedded the birth was incorrupt! For the birth of God renews natures; therefore all generations magnify thee in orthodox manner as the Mother of God!] (Luke 1:48)*[^766]

*Troparion 1:* Have mercy on me, O Savior; Son of David, have mercy! (Matt. 9:27; 15:22) Thou Who with a word didst heal the demon-possessed, speak also unto me that merciful voice as unto the thief: "Truly I say unto thee, with Me shalt thou be in Paradise, when I come in My glory!" (Luke 23:43; Matt. 25:31)

*Troparion 2:* One thief reviled Thee, the other thief confessed Thee as God, for both hung with Thee upon the Cross! (Luke 23:39–42) But O most merciful One, as unto Thy faithful thief who acknowledged Thee to be God, open also unto me the door of Thy glorious Kingdom!

*Troparion 3:* Creation trembled seeing Thee crucified; mountains and rocks split with fear, the earth shook, Hades was stripped bare, and the light grew dark at midday, seeing Thee, O Jesus, nailed to the Cross! (Matt. 27:45, 51; Luke 23:44–45)

*Troparion 4:* Demand not of me worthy fruits of repentance, for my strength has failed within me! (Matt. 3:8; Luke 3:8; Ps. 30:11 [LXX]) Grant me ever a contrite heart and spiritual poverty, that I may offer these unto Thee as an acceptable sacrifice, O only Savior! (Ps. 50:19 [LXX]; Matt. 5:3)

*Troparion 5:* O my Judge and my Knower, Who art to come again with the angels to judge all the world: seeing me then with Thy merciful eye, spare me and have compassion upon me, O Jesus, who have sinned beyond all human nature! (Matt. 25:31–32) *To St. Andrew:* O blessed Andrew, father most thrice-blessed, shepherd of Crete: cease not praying for those who praise thee, that we all may be delivered from wrath, affliction, corruption, and be set free from sins, who ever honor thy memory!

*Glory... Trinity Hymn:*
*Trinity Hymn:* O consubstantial Trinity, tri-hypostatic Unity, we hymn Thee, glorifying the Father, magnifying the Son, and worshiping the Spirit: the one Essence, truly God, Life and the Living One, Kingdom without end!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* Alone thou didst bear God, alone remaining a Virgin! O marvelous birthgiving! O marvelous conception! A conception without seed, and a childbirth beyond nature! O pure Bride of God, preserve the flock which thy Son acquired! (Acts 20:28)

*Then both choirs chant the Heirmos: A conception without seed.*[^767]

*Then: Lord, I have cried.*[^768]

## Friday of the First Week of Great Lent

*At Matins.*

*Instruction: See fol. 172.*[^769]

*After the Second Stychology, Sessional Hymn, Tone 2, by Lord Joseph.*

*Tone 2, Podoben: "Noble Joseph" (Бл҃гоѡ́бразный І҆ѡ́сифъ):*
By Thy sufferings grant dispassion unto all, O Lover of mankind! Having put to death the passions of my flesh by Thy divine Cross, make me worthy also to behold Thy venerable Resurrection, O Lord, pleasing Thy glory through fasting, that I may richly receive Thy great mercy! (Twice)

*Glory... both now... Stavrotheotokion:*
Preserved by the venerable Cross of thy Son, O pure Lady Theotokos, we easily vanquish every assault of the enemy! Therefore as is due we ever bless thee...

...as the Mother of God and the only hope of our souls!

*After the Third Stychology, Sessional Hymn, Tone 2:*

*Tone 2, Podoben: "Since thou art a well-spring" (Млⷭ҇рдїа сꙋ́щи и҆сто́чни):*
Being the fountain of purity, preserve us through fasting, O merciful One; look down upon us who fall down before Thee! Give ear unto the lifting up of our hands, Thou Who didst stretch out Thy palms when crucified upon the Wood for all the earthborn, O only Lord of the bodiless hosts! (Twice) (Ps. 140:2 [LXX])

*Glory... both now... Stavrotheotokion:*
Beholding Thee dead and stretched out upon the Wood, O Christ, the Virgin and Thy Mother weeping bitterly cried out: "O my Son, what is this strange mystery? O Giver of eternal life unto all, how dost Thou die of Thine own will upon the Cross by an ignominious death?"

*Then we chant the Canon in the Menaion for six; and the Triodion according to their order. And the Canticle from the Psalter is chanted as usual:*[^770]

*Triodion, Tone 1. Ode 5. Heirmos: O Light in darkness, [Savior of the hopeless, Christ Who by Thy Cross didst illumine our souls: unto Thee do we rise early, and we hymn Thee, O only Lover of mankind!] (Isa. 9:2; 26:9)*[^771]

*Troparion 1:* Seeing the sin dwelling within me, the deceitful-minded one hastens and cooperates with sin, for he truly rejoices over my destruction! But do Thou, O Savior, grant me correction, praying for his overthrow!

*Troparion 2:* Having vanquished the principalities of darkness upon Thy Cross, deliver me from their wickedness, who have fallen into the depth of sin and into the pit of improper deeds, yet hoping by Thy mercy to be saved! (Col. 2:15)

*Troparion 3:* O Thou Who wast stretched out dead upon the Cross, quicken my soul which has been slain by sin, and make me worthy in peace to attain Thy venerable Resurrection, O Christ, fervently working Thy statutes! (Rom. 6:11)

*Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* O pure Maiden, the illumination of my weakness and the salvation of my darkened...

...soul: save me, save me who am perishing, O Maiden, and clothe me in the garment of incorruption, who have rotted through grievous transgressions! (1 Cor. 15:53)

*Another Heirmos, in the same Tone. Heirmos: The night having passed, [the day has drawn near, and light has shone forth upon the world; therefore the angelic ranks hymn Thee, and glorify Thee, O Lord!] (Rom. 13:12)*[^772]

*Troparion 1:* On the Place of the Skull Thou didst accept crucifixion in the flesh, O only immortal One, granting immortality unto the human race and refashioning it, O Lord! (Matt. 27:33)

*Troparion 2:* Seeing the insult of Thy passion, all creation was transformed, O Lord, lamenting the murder committed by the Judeans; yet Thou didst endure it, that Thou mightest save all things! (Matt. 27:51)

*Glory... Trinity Hymn:*
*Trinity Hymn:* O all-holy Trinity, Thou art our structure, Thou art our refuge and might: unto us who hymn Thee as one in essence, send down cleansing from sins!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* O Virgin of many names, rejoice, O Theotokos: Ark, Urn, and Table, light-bearing Lampstand, bush unconsumed by fire, overshadowing Mountain of God! (Heb. 9:4; Exod. 3:2; Hab. 3:3 [LXX])

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*

*Troparion:* Having renounced the world and those in the world, that we might rejoice: now being co-crucified with Christ, let us endure insult and the mockery of companions, that we may be glorified together with Him! (Rom. 8:17; Gal. 2:20; 6:14)

*Heirmos: The night having passed, the day has drawn near, and light has shone forth upon the world; therefore the angelic ranks hymn Thee, and glorify Thee, O Lord!*

*Ode 8. Heirmos: In the fiery furnace [the children of Israel, as in a crucible, shone more brightly than gold with the beauty of piety, saying: "All ye works of the Lord, bless the Lord, hymn and exalt Him above all unto all ages!"] (Dan. 3:57)*[^773]

*Troparion 1:* Having humbled Thyself, Thou didst ascend upon the Cross out of compassion, lifting up the one who fell of old through the eating from the tree; therefore we hymn Thee, the only all-good One, glorified unto the ages! (Phil. 2:8; Gen. 3:6)

*Troparion 2:* By the slumber of heedlessness, the heavy sleep of sin has blown upon me; but do Thou Who didst fall asleep upon the Cross for my sake, O my Christ, raise me up who am fallen, that the night of death may not overtake me! (Ps. 12:4 [LXX]) ...Blinded by pleasures, my wretched and darkened soul is mocked by the deceitful-minded enemy seeing me; therefore enlighten me, and deliver me from his malice, O Christ, unto the ages!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* Having spent my life in slothfulness, I have weighed down my soul with the slumber of sin; yet fleeing unto thy sleepless intercession, allow me not, O all-pure Virgin, to fall asleep in death! (Ps. 12:4 [LXX])

*Another Heirmos. Heirmos: In the bush unto Moses [the Virgin's childbearing upon Mount Sinai was prefigured of old: sing, bless, and exalt Him above all unto all ages!] (Exod. 3:2)*[^774]

*Troparion 1:* Crowned with thorns and clothed in a garment of purple, Thou didst appear most beautiful in goodness, O Christ, flashing with glory beyond the sons of men! (Matt. 27:28–29; Ps. 44:3 [LXX])

*Troparion 2:* Drinking gall and vinegar, Thou didst pour forth two streams of life and incorruption from Thy divine side for those who hymn Thee with faith and glorify Thee, O Christ, unto all ages! (Matt. 27:34; John 19:34)

*Let us bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, the Lord.*

*Trinity Hymn:* One Godhead, O Trinity: indivisible Essence, yet divided in Persons; indestructible dominion, O Father, Son, and Spirit: we hymn Thee unto all ages!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* Pure Mother of God, heavenly gate, saving portals: receive the supplication of all Christians who bless thee unto all ages!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*

*Troparion:* O Cross, scepter of Christ, horn of churches, victory of rulers, guardian of Christians: Thou art my illumination, my very boast unto all ages! (1 Cor. 1:31; Gal. 6:14)

*We praise, bless, and worship the Lord.*

*Heirmos: In the bush unto Moses, the Virgin's childbearing upon Mount Sinai was prefigured of old: sing, bless, and exalt Him above all unto all ages!*

*Ode 9. Heirmos: The Luminary before the sun, [God Who shone forth bodily unto us from a Virgin's womb ineffably: O blessed and all-pure one, thee do we magnify as the Theotokos!] (Luke 1:48)*[^775]

*Troparion 1:* By the sprinkling of Thy blood, O divine Word, cleanse my soul which is leprous with improper thoughts, and make me a partaker of Thy glory...

...Who didst endure an inglorious crucifixion for my sake, O Christ!

*Troparion 2:* Bowed down completely under the weight of improper deeds, O Christ, and grieving, I cry unto Thee, O Lover of mankind: heal the incurable wounds of my soul by Thy precious blood, that I may hymn Thy Godhead!

*Troparion 3:* Making food out of malice and drink out of negligence, remaining uncorrected in everything, yet untimely rejoicing in abstinence from foods—for the Lord declared that not such is the fast! (Isa. 58:3–6)

*Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* Renunciation of ancient sudden ruin, and correction of our foremother; cause of reconciliation of our race unto God, bridge unto the Creator: thee, O Theotokos, do we magnify!

*Another Heirmos. Heirmos: The pure and most pure [Mother and Virgin let all us faithful magnify in songs of praise as the Mother of God!]*[^776]

*Troparion 1:* When Thou wast crucified upon the Wood, creation was shaken! Being God, Thou didst suffer in the flesh out of the mercy of Thy compassions, that Thou mightest save us! (Matt. 27:51)

*Troparion 2:* Great is the power of Thy Cross, O Lord! By portraying it within ourselves, we straightway repel the might of the demons!

*Glory... Trinity Hymn:*
*Trinity Hymn:* Tri-hypostatic Unity, consubstantial Trinity, Sovereign Lordship, Essence equal in glory, Father, Son, and Divine Spirit: save us all!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* Rejoice, propitiation of the world, O Theotokos, in whom fleeing, all we sinners find reconciliation of our sins unto God!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*

*Troparion:* Strengthen me by the divine power of Thy Cross, O Lord, that I may offer unto Thee the blameless and pure time of the fast!

*Heirmos: The pure and most pure Mother and Virgin let all us faithful magnify in songs of praise as the Mother of God!*

*Tone of the Exapostilarion.*[^777]

*At the Aposticha, Idiomelon Stichera, Tone 8:*
Joyfully let us receive the precept of the fast...

...for if our forefather had kept this, we would not have suffered the fall from Eden! Beautiful to behold and good for food was the fruit that brought death upon me! Let us not be enticed, nor let our palate be sweetened by foods that are prized but after consumption are dishonored! Let us flee intemperance, and let us not submit to the passions that follow after satiety! Let us mark ourselves with the blood of Him Who was led willingly unto death for our sake, and the destroyer shall not touch us; and we shall eat the most holy Pascha of Christ unto the salvation of our souls! (Twice) (Gen. 2:16–17; 3:6; Exod. 12:13, 23; 1 Cor. 5:7)

*We were filled in the morning with Thy mercy... and again the same Sticheron.* (Ps. 89:14 [LXX])

*Verse 2: And let the brightness of the Lord our God be upon us... Then, Martyrikon:* (Ps. 89:17 [LXX])

*Martyrikon:* What shall we call you, O holy ones? Cherubim, for Christ rested upon you? Seraphim, for unceasingly you glorified Him? Angels, for you turned away from the body? Powers, for you work miracles? Many are your names, and greater are your gifts: pray that our souls may be saved!

*Glory... both now... Stavrotheotokion:*

*Tone 8, Podoben: "O most marvelous wonder" (ѽ пресла́вное чꙋ́до):*
When she saw Thee crucified upon the Place of the Skull, O Savior, all creation was transformed and trembled, shaking in agitation, unable to endure it! And the pure Virgin and Thy Mother weeping bitterly cried unto Thee: "Woe is me, O my Child, my sweetest Savior! What is this new, most marvelous, and strange sight?" (Matt. 27:33, 51)

*Then: It is good to give thanks unto the Lord... and the rest.* (Ps. 91:2 [LXX])

*At the Hours, without stychology. Likewise also on the other Fridays of the holy Great Forty Days.*

*On the same Friday, at the Sixth Hour, Troparion, Tone 5:*
Our life of many sins, and unrepentant...

...disposition, anticipate with compassions, O Lord! For we know none other beside Thee, Who hast dominion over life and death: save us, as the Lover of mankind!

*Glory... the end. Both now... Theotokion.*

*Prokimenon, Psalm 17, Tone 7: I will love Thee, O Lord, my strength: the Lord is my foundation.* (Ps. 17:2–3 [LXX])

*Verse: My God is my helper.* (Ps. 17:3 [LXX])

*Reading from the Prophecy of Isaiah (Isa. 3:1–8).*

*Verse 1: Behold, the Master, the Lord of hosts, takes away from Israel and from Judea the strong man and the strong woman, the strength of bread and the strength of water;*

*2: The giant, and the strong man, and the warrior, and the judge, and the prophet, and the discerning one, and the elder, and the captain of fifty; and the marvelous counselor, and the wise architect, and the intelligent hearer.*

*3: And I will make youths their princes, and mockers shall rule over them.*

*4: And the people shall rush together, man against man, and man against his neighbor; the child shall dash against the elder, and the dishonorable against the honorable.*

*5: For a man shall lay hold of his brother, and of his father's kinsman, saying: "Thou hast a cloak: be thou our leader, and let my food be under thee."*

*6: And he shall answer in that day, saying: "I will not be thy leader, for there is neither bread nor cloak in my house; I will not be ruler over this people."*

*7: For Jerusalem has been forsaken, and Judea has fallen, and their tongues with iniquity disobey the Lord; therefore their glory has now been brought low;*

*8: And the shame of their face has stood against them; and they have declared and revealed their sin, like Sodom. Woe unto their soul, because they have devised an evil counsel among themselves!*

*Namely: "Let us bind the righteous man, for he is burdensome unto us!" Therefore they shall eat the fruit of their deeds.* (Wis. 2:12)

*9: Woe unto the lawless man: evil things according to the works of his hands shall befall him!*

*10: O My people, your exactors glean you, and extortioners rule over you! O My people, they that call you blessed deceive you, and disturb the path of your feet!*

*11: But now the Lord stands up for judgment, and shall bring His people into judgment.*

*12: The Lord Himself shall come into judgment with the elders of the people and with their princes.*

*Prokimenon, Psalm 18, Tone 6: O Lord, my helper and my redeemer.* (Ps. 18:15 [LXX])

*Verse: The heavens declare the glory of God.* (Ps. 18:2 [LXX])

*Be it known that the office of the Menaion for the saint that falls on Saturday and on Sunday is chanted at Compline, or whenever the Ecclesiarch desires.*[^778]

*On Friday of the First Week of the Fast, at Vespers: ordinary stychology.*

*At Lord, I have cried, we set 10 stichera. Idiomelon of the day, Tone 5:*
Come, O ye faithful, let us perform the works of God in the light, that we may walk becomingly as in the day! Let us take away from ourselves every unjust writing concerning our neighbor, placing no stumbling-block unto him as an offense! Let us abandon the voluptuousness of the flesh; let us increase the spiritual gifts of the soul; let us give bread unto those in need, and let us approach Christ, crying out in repentance: "O our God, have mercy on us!" (Twice) (Rom. 13:12–13; 14:13; Isa. 58:6–7)

*Then 4 Martyrika of the current Tone in the Oktoechos.*[^779]

*And after these, 4 Idiomela to Saint Theodore, Tone 2:*
Come, all ye lovers of the martyrs, let us spiritually rejoice and keep festival! For today the Martyr Theodore sets forth a mystical banquet...

...gladdening us who love the feast, that we may cry unto him: "Rejoice, unconquered passion-bearer, who didst overthrow the threats of the torturers upon earth! Rejoice, who didst give up thy corruptible body unto tortures for Christ God! Rejoice, who in diverse perils didst appear an experienced warrior of the heavenly host! Therefore we pray thee, the adornment of martyrs: pray for our souls!"

*Sticheron 2:* The God-given grace of thy miracles, O Martyr Theodore, thou dost extend unto all who flee unto thee with faith! Therefore we praise thee, saying: thou deliverest the captives, thou healest the sick, thou enrichest the poor, and thou savest those who sail; thou imposest vain flight upon slaves, and makest exposure of thefts unto those who rob, O passion-bearer; and thou dost instruct soldiers to refrain from plundering; unto those who pray thou mercifully grantest petitions; thou art found a fervent protector unto those who celebrate thy sacred memory! Together with them, also for us who hymn thy martyrdom, O most sacred passion-bearer, ask of Christ great mercy![^780]

*Sticheron 3:* As a greatest gift of God hast thou been shown forth, O Martyr Theodore: for even after thy demise, as one alive thou dost grant petitions unto those who flee unto thee! Therefore when a certain woman's son had of old been snatched away and taken captive by alien soldiers, the widow came and drenched thy temple with tears; and thou as merciful, having descended upon a white horse, didst restore the boy unseen!

...and after this, working other miracles, thou hast not ceased; but pray thou unto Christ God, that our souls may be saved!

*Sticheron 4, Tone 2:* I honor thee, the namesake of divine gifts, O thrice-blessed Theodore; for having appeared as an unsetting luminary of the divine Light, thou hast illumined the whole creation by thy sufferings, and appearing stronger than fire, thou didst extinguish the flame, and didst crush the head of the deceptive serpent. Therefore in thy sufferings Christ bowed down and crowned thy divine head, O great martyr, athlete: as thou hast boldness unto God, pray fervently for our souls!

*Glory... Tone 6. Idiomelon:*
Using the apostate tyrant as his tool, the enemy full of hatred sought by an evil design to defile with foods from unclean sacrifices the pious people who were cleansing themselves by fasting. But thou by a stronger counsel didst destroy his stratagem: appearing in a dream unto the Hierarch of that time, revealing the depth of thy wisdom and exposing the unseemly scheme. Therefore, offering thee thanksgiving, we record our salvation, celebrating the annual commemoration of the miracle that was wrought; and we pray that through thy supplications unto God, O Martyr Theodore, we also may be preserved unharmed from the schemes of the evil one![^781]

*Both now... Theotokion from the Octoechos, in the current Tone of the week.*

*Entrance with the Gospel. "O Gladsome Light."*

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 19, Tone 6:*[^782] *The Lord hear thee [O king] in the day of affliction!* (Ps. 19:2 [LXX 19:2 / MT 20:1])

*Verse: The name of the God of Jacob defend thee!* (Ps. 19:2 [LXX 19:2 / MT 20:1])

*Reading from the Book of Genesis (Gen. 2:20–3:20).*

*20: And Adam gave names to all cattle, and to all the birds of heaven, and to all the wild beasts of the field; but for Adam there was not found a helper comparable unto him.* (Gen. 2:20)

*21: And the Lord God brought a trance upon Adam, and he slept; and He took one of his ribs, and filled up flesh instead thereof.* (Gen. 2:21)

*22: And the Lord God fashioned the rib, which He had taken from Adam, into a woman,* (Gen. 2:22)

*[Narrative Woodcut Illustration: The Creation, Fall, and Expulsion of the First-Created (Gen. 2–3). On the left: the creation of Eve from the rib of sleeping Adam, inscribed "The Creation of Eve" (СЪЗДАНИЄ ЄVЫ) and "Adam" (АДАМ). In the center: the serpent on the Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil tempting Adam and Eve, inscribed "Adam" and "Eve". In the upper right: the expulsion of the first-created from Paradise by an angel with a flaming sword through an architectural portal, inscribed "Expulsion from Paradise" (ИЗГНАНИЄ ИЗ РАЯ). In the lower right: life after the Fall, with Adam tilling the ground with a spade and Eve nursing an infant, beneath an inscribed scroll: "In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread" (С ПОТЄМ ЛИЦА СНЄСИ ХЛЄБ ТВОЙ; Gen. 3:19).]*[^783]

*...and brought her unto Adam.* (Gen. 2:22)

*23: And Adam said: "This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of her Man."* (Gen. 2:23)

*24: Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife; and they two shall be one flesh.* (Gen. 2:24)

*25: And they were both naked, Adam and his wife, and were not ashamed.* (Gen. 2:25)

*(Chapter 3) 1: Now the serpent was more subtle than all the beasts which were upon the earth, which the Lord God had made. And the serpent said unto the woman:* (Gen. 3:1) *1 (continued): ..."Why hath God said: 'Ye shall not eat of every tree of paradise'?"* (Gen. 3:1)

*2: And the woman said: "Of the fruit of the tree of paradise we may eat;* (Gen. 3:2)

*3: But of the fruit of the tree which is in the midst of paradise, God hath said: 'Ye shall not eat of it, neither shall ye touch it, lest ye die.'"* (Gen. 3:3)

*4: And the serpent said unto the woman: "Ye shall not surely die by death!* (Gen. 3:4)

*5: For God knew that in whatsoever day ye eat thereof, your eyes shall be opened, and ye shall be as gods, knowing good and evil."* (Gen. 3:5)

*6: And the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was pleasant for the eyes to behold, and fair to contemplate; and taking of the fruit thereof, she ate, and gave also unto her husband with her, and they ate.* (Gen. 3:6)

*7: And the eyes of them both were opened, and they knew that they were naked; and they sewed fig leaves together, and made themselves girdles.* (Gen. 3:7)

*8: And they heard the voice of the Lord God walking in paradise at midday; and Adam and his wife hid themselves from the presence of the Lord God in the midst of paradise.* (Gen. 3:8)

*9: And the Lord God called Adam, and said unto him: "Adam, where art thou?"* (Gen. 3:9)

*10: And he said unto Him: "I heard the sound of Thy voice walking in paradise, and I was afraid, because I am naked; and I hid myself."* (Gen. 3:10)

*11: And God said unto Adam: "Who told thee that thou art naked, unless thou hast eaten of the tree whereof I commanded thee alone not to eat?"* (Gen. 3:11)

*12: And Adam said: "The woman whom Thou gavest to be with me, she gave me of the tree, and I ate."* (Gen. 3:12)

*13: And God said unto the woman [Eve]: "Why hast thou done this?" And the woman said: "The serpent deceived me, and I ate."* (Gen. 3:13)

*14: And the Lord God said unto the serpent [the adversary creature]: "Because thou hast done this, cursed art thou above all cattle, and above all the beasts that are upon the earth!* (Gen. 3:14) *14 (continued): ...Upon thy breast and thy belly shalt thou go, and dust shalt thou eat all the days of thy life.* (Gen. 3:14)

*15: And I will put enmity between thee and between the woman, and between thy seed and between her seed: He shall watch against thy head, and thou shalt watch against His heel.* (Gen. 3:15)

*16: And unto the woman He said: "Multiplying I will multiply thy sorrows and thy sighing; in sorrow shalt thou bring forth children; and thy desire shall be unto thy husband, and he shall rule over thee."* (Gen. 3:16)

*17: And unto Adam He said: "Because thou hast listened unto the voice of thy wife, and hast eaten of the tree whereof I commanded thee, saying: 'Thou shalt not eat of this alone,' yet of it hast thou eaten: cursed is the ground in thy labors; in sorrows shalt thou eat of it all the days of thy life.* (Gen. 3:17)

*18: Thorns also and thistles shall it bring forth unto thee, and thou shalt eat the herb of the field.* (Gen. 3:18)

*19: In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat thy bread, until thou return unto the ground out of which thou wast taken; for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return."* (Gen. 3:19)

*20: And Adam called his wife's name Life [Eve], because she was the mother of all living.* (Gen. 3:20)

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 20, Tone 4:*[^784] *Be Thou exalted, O Lord, in Thy strength: we will sing and praise Thy power!* (Ps. 20:14 [LXX 20:14 / MT 21:13])

*Verse: O Lord, in Thy strength the king shall be glad!* (Ps. 20:2 [LXX 20:2 / MT 21:1])

*Reading from the Book of Proverbs (Prov. 3:19–34).*

*19: God by wisdom hath founded the earth, and prepared the heavens by understanding.* (Prov. 3:19)

*20: In His perception the depths were broken up, and the clouds dropped down dew.* (Prov. 3:20)

*21: My son, pass them not by, but keep my counsel and understanding:* (Prov. 3:21)

*22: That thy soul may live, and grace may be about thy neck;* (Prov. 3:22)

*23: And there shall be healing unto thy flesh, and care for thy bones.* (Prov. 3:23) *23 (continued): ...That thou mayest walk relying in peace on all thy ways, and thy foot shall not stumble.* (Prov. 3:23)

*24: For if thou sit down, thou shalt be without fear; and if thou sleep, thou shalt sleep sweetly.* (Prov. 3:24)

*25: And thou shalt not be afraid of fear coming upon thee, nor of the assault of the ungodly coming upon thee.* (Prov. 3:25)

*26: For the Lord shall be in all thy ways, O son, and shall establish thy foot, that thou be not shaken.* (Prov. 3:26)

*27: Refrain not from doing good unto the needy, whensoever thy hand hath power to help.* (Prov. 3:27)

*28: Say not: "Go, and return, and tomorrow I will give," when thou hast power to do good; for thou knowest not what the day to come shall bring forth.* (Prov. 3:28)

*29: Devise not evil against thy friend who comes and relies upon thee.* (Prov. 3:29)

*30: Be not an enemy unto a man in vain, lest he work some evil against thee.* (Prov. 3:30)

*31: Acquire not the reproach of evil men, neither be jealous of their ways.* (Prov. 3:31)

*32: For unclean before God is every transgressor of the law, and with the righteous He combines not.* (Prov. 3:32)

*33: The curse of the Lord is in the houses of the ungodly, but the dwellings of the righteous are blessed.* (Prov. 3:33)

*34: The Lord resists the proud, but gives grace unto the humble.* (Prov. 3:34)

*Then: "Let my prayer arise." And the Divine Liturgy of the Presanctified Gifts. Dismissal, and the rest.*

*After the Ambo Prayer, we chant the following Molieben Canon unto Saint Theodore.*[^785]  
*And having set forth the Kolyvo, the Priest performs the censing.*  
*"O Lord, hear my prayer." Then: "God is the Lord, and hath appeared unto us," in Tone 2.*

*Troparion of the Saint, Tone 2:* Great are the achievements of faith! In the fountain of flame, as upon the water of rest, the holy Martyr Theodore rejoiced; for having been wholly consumed by fire, he was offered unto the Trinity as sweet bread. By his prayers, O Christ God, have mercy on us![^786] (Twice)

*Glory... The same. Both now... Theotokion:*

*Theotokion, Tone 2:* All thy mysteries are beyond comprehension, all are most glorious, O Mother of God! Sealed in purity and preserved in virginity, thou wast known to be a true Mother, having given birth unto the true God: Him do thou entreat, that our souls may be saved!

*And the 50th Psalm: "Have mercy on me, O God."* (Ps. 50 [LXX 50 / MT 51])

*Then the present Canon, the composition of John of Damascus, whereof the acrostic is: "God's namesake of gifts I sing thee" (Бж҃їй тѧ пою̀ да́рѡвъ тезоимени́те).*[^787]

*Tone 8.*

*Ode 1. Heirmos:* Having passed through the water as upon dry land, and having escaped the evil of Egypt, the Israelite cried aloud: "Unto our Redeemer and God let us sing!" (Exod. 14:21–31)

*Troparion:* Knowing thee as a lover of God, O Theodore, and held fast by thine inevitable love, I dedicate soul, body, and words of praise unto thee!

*Troparion:* A God-abhorred decree was written, to offer sacrifice unto idols and not unto the living God; but thou wast brought forth, not willing to sacrifice, O passion-bearer, but having thyself to be brought as an offering unto God!

*Glory...*  
*Troparion:* Fastened by divine love unto the only-begotten Son of God Most High, O blessed Theodore, thou didst enlist as His soldier, and didst not miss the prize!

*Both now...*  
*Theotokion:* The ranks of Angels and of men unceasingly praise thee, O Bride of God and Mother; for in thine embrace thou didst carry their Creator as an infant!

*Ode 3. Heirmos:* Thou art the firm foundation of those that flee unto Thee, O Lord; Thou art the light of the darkened, and my spirit hymns Thee!

*Troparion:* A song from my lips and a prayer from an aching soul do I offer: have compassion on it, O passion-bearer Theodore!

*Troparion:* Thou didst subject the flesh unto the Sovereign mind, O glorious martyr; by both dost thou please the Creator!

*Glory...*  
*Troparion:* Thou wast an instrument in the judgment-hall of the torturer, theologizing Christ the King; for thou didst renounce sacrificing unto foul idols, O Theodore!

*Both now...*  
*Theotokion:* Thee have all we Christians acquired as a refuge and a wall; thee do we unceasingly glorify in song, O unwedded Bride!

*Ode 4. Heirmos:* I have heard, O Lord, the mystery of Thy dispensation; I have considered Thy works, and have glorified Thy Divinity!

*Troparion:* As a knower of divine mysteries in understanding, O blessed Theodore, thou didst confess the shameless proclamation of the Divine Nativity!

*Troparion:* They who served the passions accounted the Godhead to be passible; but illuminated by the Spirit, thou didst convict them, O athlete Theodore!

*Glory...*  
*Troparion:* By thy prayer, O blessed Theodore, entreat the Redeemer that He may be merciful unto those who hymn thee, delivering them from diverse tribulations and passions!

*Theotokion:* O unplowed field that didst grow the life-creating ear of corn which gives life unto the world: O Mother of God, save those who hymn thee!

*Ode 5. Heirmos:* Rising early, we cry unto Thee: "Lord, save us, for Thou art our God, and beside Thee we know none other!"

*Troparion:* "Love God Who hath loved you!" didst thou cry aloud, O athlete Theodore, unto the martyrs suffering together with thee!

*Troparion:* Inflaming thy heart with zeal, O passion-bearer, thou didst burn up with fire the falsely named goddess together with her pagan altar![^788]

*Glory...*  
*Troparion:* By invincible power, O passion-bearer Theodore, destroy the pride of the barbarians and put to death my passions!

*Both now...*  
*Theotokion:* As a Virgin after childbearing do we hymn thee, O Mother of God; for thou didst bear God the Word unto the world!

*Ode 6. Heirmos:* Cleanse me, O Savior, for many are my transgressions, and lead me up from the abyss of evils, I pray Thee; for unto Thee have I cried, and do Thou give ear unto me, O God of my salvation!

*Troparion:* How weak, how powerless is the haughtiness of vain gods! Pleading with men for their own avenging, defeated in the contest by true martyrs who proclaim the truth!

*Troparion:* Strengthened by the power of God, O Theodore, glory of martyrs, thou didst look upon the torments of the ungodly as the shooting of children's arrows, O blessed one, despising them for the sake of the eternal future!
