*Troparion:* Being a most fervent champion of piety and a reprover of idol deception: consume the phantoms of demons and the images of passions from my soul!

*Theotokion:* That we may be delivered from grievous transgressions through thy prayers, O pure Mother of God, and that we may obtain the divine illumination of the Son of God Who was ineffably incarnate of thee, O all-pure one!

*Lord, have mercy (Thrice).*  
*Glory... Both now... Kontakion, Tone 8:*  
Having received the faith of Christ into thy heart as a shield, thou didst trample down the opposing powers, O much-suffering athlete; and thou hast been crowned forever with a heavenly crown, O Theodore, as unconquered!

*Ode 7. Heirmos:* The Children of Judea who of old came down to Babylon trampled underfoot the flame of the furnace by faith in the Trinity, chanting: "O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!" (Dan. 3:23–26)

*Troparion:* Thou wast wounded in body for the sake of the Word Who was wounded in the flesh for our sake; and rejoicing nobly therein, thou didst cry aloud, O passion-bearer Theodore: "O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!"

*Troparion:* As the Redeemer was laid in the tomb and voluntarily sealed, so in every way in a sealed prison wast thou shut up, crying aloud, O passion-bearer Theodore: "O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!"[^789]

*Troparion:* Having been mortified, and by thy free choice having shaken off bodily passions, not nourished by food, O passion-bearer, but fed by divine love, thou didst sing: "O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!"

*Glory...*  
*Troparion:* In the prison, O passion-bearer, even as of old in the furnace unto the youths, One of the undivided Trinity appeared strengthening thee, as thou didst cry: "O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!"

*Both now...*  
*Theotokion:* As Thou didst desire to accomplish our salvation, O Savior, Thou didst dwell in the womb of the Virgin, whom Thou hast shown forth unto the world as a protectress: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:* Sevenfold the tyrant in his rage did heat the furnace for the God-fearing ones; but beholding them saved by a greater power, he cried unto the Creator and Redeemer: "Ye children, bless; ye priests, hymn; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages!" (Dan. 3:19–57)

*Troparion:* Blinded in mind, the leader of the lawless impiously threatened thee who worshippest God, saying: "Why hast thou senselessly placed thy hope in a mere man who died by violence?" But thou didst cry aloud: "Ye children, bless; ye priests, hymn; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages!"

*Troparion:* As a prudent and most wise steward of the grace given thee from God, thou didst cry aloud, O Theodore, unto him that commanded impiously: "Let this shame be unto me and unto them that sing: Ye children, bless; ye priests, hymn; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages!"

*Glory...*  
*Troparion:* Thou didst contend youthfully, boldly convicting him, crying: "Why, O senseless torturer, dost thou bid us falsely serve creation rather than the Creator? But I sing: Ye children, bless; ye priests, hymn; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages!"

*Both now...*  
*Theotokion:* By bodily prefigurations, diverse riddles, and signifying prophetic utterances, the God-inspired prophets foretold thy supernatural and marvelous childbearing, O Virgin; therefore, rejoicing, we piously praise thee, supremely exalting Christ unto all ages!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:* Thee who art unwedded, Mother and Virgin of God, who didst bear the divine Word beyond understanding, truly God, higher than the most pure powers: with unceasing glorification do we magnify!

*Troparion:* The fuel of thy martyrdom, O Theodore, was the divine desire; therefore fuel did thy body become unto the material fire, through which, rejoicing, thou didst go forth unto the divine fire, O passion-bearer, favorite of God, Theodore!

*Troparion:* O all-honored martyr, thou didst burn up, but wast not consumed! For thou didst burn up the deception of idols, and didst stand living before God, rejoicing in martyrdom in Him, O passion-bearer, favorite of God, Theodore!

*Glory...*  
*Troparion:* Thee do we know as the One Christ, One of the Trinity...

*Troparion (continued):* ...in two perfect natures: save Thy people, whom Thou hast acquired with Thy precious Blood, through the prayers of the passion-bearer Theodore!

*Both now...*  
*Theotokion:* Thee who didst hold in thine arms the invisible God Who is hymned in the heavens by all the angelic Powers, and through whom salvation is ever granted unto us in tribulation: we magnify!

*Heirmos (repeated):* Thee who art unwedded, Mother and Virgin of God, who didst bear the divine Word beyond understanding, truly God, higher than the most pure powers: with unceasing glorification do we magnify!

*Then: Trisagion. Troparion: "Great are the achievements of faith" (see fol. 281).*[^790] *Glory... Kontakion of the holy Martyr Theodore: "Having received the faith of Christ into thy heart as a shield" (see fol. 284).*[^791] *Both now... Theotokion:*  
*Theotokion:* As a protectress of all and a mighty defense have we sinners acquired thee, O all-pure one: thy fervent help, O Virgin Mother Mary, the salvation of Christians! Therefore cease not to entreat the Savior on our behalf, that He may grant us forgiveness!

*And there is the blessing over the Kolyvo. Then: "Blessed be the name of the Lord," thrice. And: "I will bless the Lord at all times" (Ps. 33 [LXX 33 / MT 34]). Then the Priest distributes the broken morsels. And the Dismissal takes place.*  
*And at the meal, those who have communicated have warm water with honey, as was also said on Wednesday (see fol. 240).*[^792]

*And where the Presanctified Liturgy is not celebrated, we finish the Hours thus:*[^793]  
*After "Pardon, remit, forgive" and the final bows, we say: Trisagion. After "Our Father": "Lord, have mercy," 12 times. Then the Prayer: "All-Holy Trinity." And the Dismissal.*  
*And we begin Vespers. "Come, let us worship," 3 times. Psalm 103 (Ps. 103 [LXX 103 / MT 104]). Customary Kathisma.*  
*And at "Lord, I have cried," we sing 6 Stichera: Martyrika from the Octoechos, 3, in the Tone of the week; and unto Saint Theodore, 3. Glory... unto Theodore: "Employing the apostate tyrant as his tool..." Both now... Tone 2: of the week. "O Gladsome Light," without entrance. The Readings.*  
*At the Aposticha: Idiomelon of the day, twice; and Martyrikon, Tone 5: "Blessed is the army of the King of heaven..." Glory... unto Theodore, Tone 2: "I honor thee, the namesake of divine gifts..." (it was written among the Stichera at "Lord, I have cried"). Both now... Theotokion: "All my hope..."*  
*"Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart." Trisagion. After "Our Father," Troparion: "Great are the achievements of faith." Glory... Both now... Theotokion: "All thy mysteries are beyond comprehension." Then the Litany: "Have mercy on us, O God."*  
*And the Priest vests in a purple phelonion, and begins: "Blessed is our God." And we say Psalm 142: "O Lord, hear my prayer." And the rest, as indicated above. The Canon on 4. And after the completion of the Canon, instead of "It is truly meet," we sing the Heirmos of Ode 9: "Thee who art unwedded..."*

*Thee who art unwedded: Thrice. Trisagion. After "Our Father": Troparion: "Great are the achievements of faith." Glory... Kontakion: "Having received the faith of Christ into thy heart as a shield." Both now... Kontakion / Theotokion: "As a protectress of all" (see fol. 286).*[^794]  
*Then: Prayer over the Kolyvo, Blessing of the Kolyvo. After this: "Blessed be the name of the Lord." And: "I will bless the Lord at all times." And the Dismissal.*  
*And we enter the Trapeza, and we partake of wine and oil, for the sake of the Saint. This we received in the Lavra of our venerable Father Sabbas, and in the Coenobium of our venerable Father Euthymius the Great. Yet we do not do this now because of the morning of the day. Instead, we eat cooked food with prunes, without oil, and pickled cabbage in brine (armea).*[^795] *Those who desire may eat dry food, as on Wednesday.*  

*If the Finding of the Honorable Head of John the Forerunner concur on the First Saturday of the Fast. Mark's Chapter 23.*[^796]  
*On Friday evening: Customary Kathisma. At "Lord, I have cried," we sing 2 Idiomela of the day, and 1 Martyrikon; and of the Forerunner, 3 Prosomoia; and of Theodore, 4. Glory... unto Theodore; Both now... Theotokion in the 1st Tone. Entrance, Prokeimenon, and the Readings of the day and of the Forerunner. And the rest of the Presanctified Liturgy. 13 great prostrations:*[^797] *and after "Let my prayer arise," 3; and at "Blessed be the name of the Lord," 3.*  
*After the dismissal of the Liturgy, we sing the Canon unto the holy Theodore over the Kolyvo.*  
*At Compline we sing the Canon for the departed in the Tone of the week, and in the Menaion the canon of the day. Troparia as customary, and the Kontakion of the Forerunner. At Matins, at "God is the Lord": Troparion of the Forerunner, twice; Glory... unto Theodore; Both now... Theotokion in the 1st Tone. After the Kathismata, Sessional Hymns of the Forerunner, and the reading of the Forerunner. Polyeleos, and the Gradual Hymns (Antiphons of the Steps), and the Prokeimenon: "Let every breath"; Gospel of the Forerunner. After Psalm 50: Sticheron of the Forerunner. We sing "O Lord, have mercy" [to Psalm 50], not recite it. Canon of the Saint whose Temple it is, with the Heirmos, on 4; and of the Forerunner, on 4; and of Theodore, on 6. Katavasia: "I shall open my mouth." After Ode 3: Kontakion and Sessional Hymn of the Forerunner; Glory... Sessional Hymn of Theodore; Both now... Theotokion. After Ode 6: Kontakion of Theodore. After Ode 9: Exapostilarion of Theodore, and of the Forerunner. At the Praises: of the Forerunner, 3 Prosomoia; and of Theodore, 3 Prosomoia. Then the verse: "The righteous man shall be glad in the Lord" (Ps. 63:11 [LXX 63:11 / MT 64:10]).*[^798] *And we sing the Sticheron of the Forerunner, Idiomelon, Tone 6: "All-honored head..."; Glory... unto Theodore, Tone 6: "A double crown of consecration..."; Both now... "O Theotokos, thou art the vine..." Great Doxology. Troparion of the Forerunner; Glory... unto Theodore; Both now... Theotokion; and the Dismissal. And the customary procession to the Narthex, and Psalm 30 (Ps. 30 [LXX 30 / MT 31]).*[^799] *At the Hours: Troparion of the Forerunner; Glory... of Theodore; Both now... Theotokion of the Hour, changing the Kontakia alternately.*  
*At the Liturgy: Beatitudes of the Forerunner, Ode 3, on 4; and of Theodore, Ode 6, on 4. After the Entrance: Troparion of the Forerunner, and of Theodore, and his Kontakion; Glory... of the Forerunner; Both now... Kontakion / Theotokion: "O Protectress of Christians."*

*If it be a Temple of the Theotokos, Both now... Kontakion of the Temple. Prokeimenon, Alleluia, and Communion Hymn of the Forerunner, and of Theodore, one. Epistle and Gospel, first of the Saturday, then of Theodore in order, and after that of the Forerunner.*  
*If the commemoration of a monk concur on this First Saturday of the Fast, service is sung for them as also for the Forerunner.*  
*It is fitting to know that on all Fridays of the Holy and Great Forty Days, at Vespers and at Compline we make no prostrations, except those appointed at the Presanctified Liturgy, that is: after "Let my prayer arise," 3 prostrations; after the Entrance of the Holy Gifts, 3 prostrations; and at "Blessed be the name of the Lord," 3 prostrations.*  
*And we sing Great Compline, at which we sing the Canons for the departed in the current Tone in the Crypt.*[^800] *And the Canons in the Menaion of the current Saturday and Sunday we sing when the Ecclesiarch appoints: one we sing at Compline on Friday with the Canon for the departed, and the other Canon we sing at Compline on Sunday. Thus do we do on all Fridays, in the evening, of the Holy and Great Forty Days.*  

## On the First Saturday of the Fast

*At Matins.*  
*At "God is the Lord," Troparion: "Great are the achievements of faith," twice.*  
*Glory... both now... Theotokion: "All thy mysteries are beyond comprehension" (see fol. 282).*[^801]  
*Then the Psalter: Kathisma 16, "The Lord said unto my Lord" (Ps. 109 [LXX 109 / MT 110]).*[^802] *And we sing the Sessional Hymns in the Octoechos. And we read the Martyrdom of Saint Theodore. Then from the Psalter we chant the Amomos (Ps. 118 [LXX 118 / MT 119]).*[^803]  
*After the Amomos, Sessional Hymn of the holy Theodore, Tone 3, Podoben: "Of the divine faith" (Бо́жїѧ вѣ́ры):*[^804]  
*Troparion:* By the cause of faith through Orthodoxy, thou didst extinguish the deception of blasphemy, having abolished idol godlessness; and having become a divine burnt offering, thou enlightenest the ends of the earth with wonders, O all-glorious Martyr: entreat Christ God to grant us great mercy!  

*Glory...*  
*Troparion:* A divine gift unto salvation did the Lord Who strengthened Thee in sufferings give Thee unto the whole world, healing our spiritual...

*Troparion (continued):* ...diseases and driving away the bodily passions, O Martyr Theodore: entreat Christ God to grant us great mercy!  

*Both now...*  
*Theotokion:* O all-pure Virgin who didst bear in thy womb the uncontainable God Who shone forth incorruptibly from the Father before all ages, the hypostatic Word and co-essential Son: entreat Him together with the Prophets and Martyrs, the Venerable Ascetics, and the Righteous, to grant us remission of our transgressions!  

*And if thou wilt, read.*  
*Then Psalm 50. Canon of the Saint whose Temple it is, on 6; and of Saint Theodore, on 8. We chant the verses and sing: "Let us sing unto the Lord."*  
*Canon, whose Acrostic is:*  
*Tyro the renowned, the first glory of Saturdays.*[^805]  
*In the first Troparia of the Canon, there is another Acrostic.*  
*The Canon: The composition of John, Metropolitan of Euchaita.*[^806]  
*Ode 1, Tone 4. Heirmos: "I shall open my mouth":*  
*Theotokion:* Higher than all, He Who ineffably was born of thee made thee superior to all His chosen ones; therefore today, chanting of His crowned one, O all-hymned one, we begin with thee!  

*Troparion:* Great among the martyrs, the radiant and renowned soldier, glorious in wonders from the ends of the earth unto its ends, the marvelous Theodore shall I hymn in songs!  

*Troparion:* Today a joyful cry hath stilled the weeping and mourning among those who sorrow, having shone forth the pre-festal beginnings from afar through the grace of the divine Martyr!  

*Troparion:* The holy slaughter which He Who was slain and accepted as a sacrifice received, sprinkles the cleansings of the Church with blood, for the sake of the divine glory of Him Who suffered!

*Troparion:* Goodly it is, though not yet fully ripe, to celebrate according to the law; for the Sovereign Lady who hath adorned all things hath appeared now also unto thy memory, communicating and sheltering it with her protection!  

*Another Canon. By the same Metropolitan of Euchaita. Ode 1, Tone 6. Heirmos: "Having walked as on dry land":*[^807]  
*Troparion:* O God Who art truly marvelous in Thy saints, magnify Thy mercies in me, O Christ, granting me speech, that I may praise the marvelous deeds of Thy Martyr!  

*Troparion:* Steadfastness in passions and endurance in labors didst thou display, O passion-bearer of Christ; and in turn, reveal thy speedy help unto us, O Theodore!  

*Glory...*  
*Troparion:* Driving wickedly from his soul the pious faith of the fathers, the tormentor, conceiving an impious counsel, desired to go boldly against God!  

*Both now...*  
*Theotokion:* The divine prophecies of the men of old have manifestly been fulfilled in thee, O Virgin Mother: for thou didst bear true God and true Man beyond nature and awesomely!  

*Katavasia: "I shall open my mouth, and it shall be filled with the Spirit, and I shall utter speech unto the Queen Mother, and I shall appear radiant in celebration, and rejoice as I sing of her wonders."*  

*Ode 3. Heirmos: "Establish Thy singers":*  
*Theotokion:* Desiring to behold the day of Thy Son, O Sovereign Lady, the people named after Christ now celebrate beforehand in His likeness, bearing the example of thee and of thy glorious Passion-bearer!  

*Troparion:* A fitting and proper gift unto thee, as from thy own, O Passion-bearer; for those whom thou thyself didst settle as partakers of all thy grace, with joy do we offer gifts of praises unto thee!  

*Troparion:* The better things conquer in every way: for the great...

*Troparion (continued):* ...one among the champions turned temporary sorrow into joy, turning the course of the all-radiant fast into relief!  

*Troparion:* A most noble foundation didst thou lay by thy brave deeds, O valiant one, having cast down as naught, by beyond-natural bravery, the all-destroying beast that breathed fire and slaughter!  

*Troparion:* Having spoken much, the new Apostate,[^808] like to the cruel one of old, mixed the sacrifice of meat like poison; but the false and wretched one was outwitted by the Martyr!  

*Both now...*  
*Theotokion:* All the earth was filled, O Virgin, with the knowledge of the Lord Who appeared unto the world from thee; but great is the grace of the divine martyrs, who confirmed the truth in their very selves!  

*Another Heirmos: "There is none holy as Thou":*  
*Troparion:* He who formerly whispered deceitfully into the ears of Eve, and through her deceived Adam by guile, the same also now poured out the poison of malice unto deceit!  

*Troparion:* He had a deceiver for this, who harbored fury against those who live uprightly; he sought a fitting time wherein to work abomination, the most lawless one strived!  

*Glory...*  
*Troparion:* The beginning of the days of the holy fasts is at hand, wherein every Christian, having purified himself by much abstinence, abstains from all things!  

*Both now...*  
*Theotokion:* Mighty hope of the world, protection and defense, all-holy Virgin: despise not, O good one, the supplications of thy servants, who ever bless thee from love!  

*Katavasia: "Establish Thy singers, O Theotokos, thou living and plentiful fountain, who assemble together in spiritual choir; and in thy divine glory, vouchsafe unto them crowns of glory."*  

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "Of Wisdom and the Word" (Премꙋ́дрость Сло́ва):*[^809]

*Sessional Hymn:* Having received the divine armor, and having overthrown the deceit of idols, thou didst arouse the Angels to praise thy struggles! For having inflamed thy mind with divine desire, thou didst valiantly despise death in the fire. Therefore, according to thy name, bestow divine gifts and dispensations of healings upon those who ask of thee, O passion-bearer Theodore: entreat Christ God to grant remission of sins unto those who celebrate thy holy memory with love!  

*Glory... Podoben:*  
*Troparion:* Not turning aside unto the flatteries of Maximian,[^810] but showing manhood through the words of Christ, thou didst reduce the idol temple to ashes with fire, gloriously conquering the adversary in martyrdom; running ahead, thou didst pass through fire as through water. Therefore, receiving a worthy recompense for thy struggles, thou pourest forth healings, O passion-bearer Theodore: entreat Christ God to grant remission of sins unto those who celebrate thy holy memory with love!  

*Both now...*  
*Theotokion:* As the all-immaculate bride of the Creator, as the unwedded Mother of the Deliverer, being the receptacle of the Most High, O all-hymned one: because I am a defiled dwelling of lawlessness, and have become in understanding a plaything of demons, make haste to deliver me from their evil deeds, O thou who hast acquired a radiant dwelling of virtues, O incorruptible receiver of light! Drive away the cloud of passions, and vouchsafe unto me the past radiance and the unwaning light!  

*And the Martyrdom of Saint Theodore is read: concerning the miracles, the discourse of Nectarius, Archbishop of Constantinople, the beginning of which is: "Because of the great multitude of Thy goodness."*[^811]  

*Ode 4. Heirmos: "He Who sits in glory":*  
*Theotokion:* O new and most glorious mingling and compounding! Born as God-man, He united childhood with birthgiving; and honoring His champion, He mingled joy with the days of mourning!  

*Troparion:* Behold how the soldier of Christ loved Christ! For he destroyed His enemies with zeal and fire, and fervently offered himself as a perfect, good sacrifice and an acceptable slaughter unto Him!  

*Troparion:* The victorious and valiant champion, being released from passions by bold speech and a multitude of lightning-flashes, astonished...

*Troparion (continued):* ...the beholder, and became a new and most glorious spectacle unto all creation!  

*Troparion:* A bone indeed of my God and Master was not broken;[^812] O His longsuffering! And even after dying, He suffers. But the fire, receiving His soldier, was ashamed to touch Him as He died!  

*Both now...*  
*Theotokion:* Those who died together with the Master, being servants of life, and who rose together with Him, live with Him now unto the ages, and together they glorify the Mother of the Son, blessing the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit!  

*Another Heirmos: "Christ is my power":*  
*Troparion:* The most impious one takes counsel, and considers how he might set up this terrible thing: for the wretched one intended to defile the people of Christ by means of abominable foods!  

*Troparion:* He brought the lawless counsel into deed: for he commanded that the food of pure meals be forbidden, and that they substitute those things which he had defiled with blood!  

*Glory...*  
*Troparion:* The lawlessness became manifest and proclaimed unto all Christians; therefore, as soon as they learned of it, they all ran together into the holy temple of the Lord!  

*Both now...*  
*Theotokion:* Thee who didst bear Christ, Who was begotten of the Father before the ages, do we the faithful now set forth as an intercessor: bowed down by her prayers, be Thou gracious unto Thy servants!  

*Katavasia: "He Who sits in glory upon the throne of the Godhead, Jesus the most divine, came on a light cloud from the most pure Virgin, and saved those who cry aloud: Glory to Thy power, O Christ!"*  

*Ode 5. Heirmos: "All things were amazed":*  
*Theotokion:* The gates of grace are opened today, and rest itself now foreshadows the Resurrection, so radiantly honoring the radiant Sovereign Lady and the glorious Martyr!

*Troparion:* The namesake of God's gift, God grants Theodore,[^813] an apparition of the beloved one appearing unto those who love Him, a worker of most glorious deeds, and one made an agent of the divine Powers!  

*Troparion:* Thy bows and arrows against the Martyr are as naught, O enemy of human salvation; for he who died lives, and has awakened, and opposing thy evil deeds, saves every Orthodox believer!  

*Both now...*  
*Theotokion:* A strange wonder was wrought of old, O Maiden of God, and through the testimonies of martyrdom it received unquestioning faith; and that which is believed ever remains marveled at and faithfully worshiped!  

*Another Heirmos: "With Thy divine light":*  
*Troparion:* The Archbishop of that time was in dismay,[^814] when he learned of the counsel of the impious one; with all-night hymns he entreated God not to despise the people of His inheritance utterly!  

*Troparion:* But the speedy helper in truth, Who calls in truth and warmth, by no means despised the supplications, but wrought for them a most speedy release from the scheme!  

*Troparion:* A helper from on high is sent as quickly as possible unto the earth, the Passion-bearer Theodore, and appears unto the Chief Pastor, revealing the overturning of the lawless counsel!  

*Both now...*  
*Theotokion:* No one who warmly hastens unto thy protection, O Sovereign Lady, was ever put to shame; but he asks for mercy and receives a gift, a most speedy fulfillment of his petition unto profit!  

*Katavasia: "All things were amazed at thy divine glory: for thou, O unwedded Virgin, didst hold in thy womb the God Who is over all, and didst bear the timeless Son, granting salvation unto all who hymn thee."*

*Ode 6. Heirmos: "This divine and all-honored [feast]":*  
*Troparion:* The friends and sons of Thy bridechamber cannot fast, O Savior;[^815] for they feast Thee, the Bridegroom, Who hast come with Thy Mother and with Thy friend, and they minister unto Thee!  

*Troparion:* He who was evil of name apostatized from God Who saves, he apostatized also from understanding, and by craftiness rose up against the faith; but against this he found one great of name!  

*Troparion:* The valiant and most patient champion ceased the battle against the tyrants, and having held fast the victory well, not even having died did he abandon righteous deeds!  

*Both now...*  
*Theotokion:* Having been delivered today, O Sovereign Lady, from soul-corrupting ruin by the wonders of thy Passion-bearer, according to thy divine providence, we ascribe thanksgiving unto you both!  

*Another Heirmos: "Beholding the sea of life":*  
*Troparion:* Dismayed at the strange vision of thee, the Archbishop replied: Who art thou, my lord? Tell me; instruct and teach me, how we may find speedy help!  

*Troparion:* Theodore said: I am manifestly the Passion-bearer; and hear: having boiled wheat, distribute it to the people, and thus shall they be saved from the defiled food of the deceiver!  

*Glory...*  
*Troparion:* How great is thy wonder, and how most glorious thy protection, O Theodore! Therefore, taking courage, all of us purely run unto thee, and we pray: Save thy servants!  

*Both now...*  
*Theotokion:* Thou wast a radiant dwelling and a pure receptacle of the Word by the goodwill of the Father, and through the visitation of the Holy Spirit within thee: therefore enlighten me!  

*Katavasia: "Celebrating this divine and all-honored feast of the Mother of God, come, O God-wise ones, let us clap our hands, and glorify with faith the God Who was born of her."*  

*Kontakion, Tone 8:*

*Kontakion:* Having received the faith of Christ into thy heart as a shield, thou didst trample down the opposing powers, O much-suffering one; and with a heavenly crown hast thou been crowned eternally, O Theodore, as one unconquered!  

*Ikos:* Faithfully and piously do we hymn Thee Who art borne upon the Throne of light, for Thou hast granted a divine gift, the noble Theodore in his sufferings, thrice-blessed in life, as a champion of truth, who, having acquired Christ by pious contemplation, became a mighty victor over the deceiver, as one unconquered!  

*Synaxarion on the First Saturday of the Holy Forty Days.*  
*Verses:*[^816]  
*With the food of Kolyva Tyro feeds the city,*  
*Having rendered defiled food useless.*  

On this day, on the First Saturday of the Fasts, we celebrate a greatly renowned wonder which was wrought through kolyva—that is, boiled wheat—by the holy and all-glorious Great-martyr Theodore the Tyro; which came to pass in this manner.  
When Julian the Apostate held the sceptre of the empire after Constantius,[^817] son of Constantine the Great, and passed over from Christ unto idolatry, and apostatized, a very great persecution arose and was perceived against the Christians, both openly and in secret. The impious one therefore, not wishing to disturb them so violently, and being ashamed thus to plunder and openly torment the Christians, fearing moreover lest the number of the faithful increase still more, treacherously and impiously took counsel in secret how he might defile and pollute them. And having observed that our Christian people purify themselves most especially during the first week of the holy fasts, and draw nearer unto God, having summoned the city prefect,[^818] he commands him that all goods for sale which are customarily sold should immediately be removed and cleared away from their places, and that other provisions should be displayed in the marketplace—namely, breads and drinks—having first mingled them and defiled them in a single mixture with blood flowing from their sacrifices. Perchance, buying these during the Fast, and most especially during such purification, they might defile themselves. Immediately therefore the prefect put the imperial order into effect, and set out throughout the entire marketplace the foodstuffs and drinks mingled with the sacrifices and sorceries.[^819] But the all-seeing Divine Eye, which confounds the wise in their craftiness,[^820] and that servant...

...continually taking care of His servants, and He scattered the foul schemes and contrivances of the transgressor. For unto Eudoxius, the Archbishop of that city, who as yet had no accurate knowledge of that decree,[^821] He sends His great Passion-bearer Theodore, a soldier from the Tyronian regiment, who was likewise called Tyro—that is, a young soldier—who, appearing before him in a waking vision and not in a dream, spoke thus unto him: "Having risen up as swiftly as possible, gather the flock of Christ, and strictly command that none of them purchase any of the wares found in the marketplace; for all of these have been defiled by the most godless Emperor with the blood of sacrifices." But when the Archbishop fell into perplexity, and questioned him, saying: "And how shall it be an easy matter for those who are in want at home to refrain from buying what is sold in the market?" the Saint said: "Distributing kolyva unto them, relieve their need." And when he asked again what this kolyva might be, the Great Theodore said: "Boiled wheat; for thus are we accustomed to speak in the region of Euchaita."[^822] And when the Patriarch diligently inquired who he might be, who thus comforts the people called by Christ's name and takes care of them, the Saint said again: "I am Theodore, the Martyr of Christ, sent now by Him unto you for help and succor!"  

Having immediately risen up, therefore, and declared unto the multitude of the people what he had seen, and having acted accordingly, the Patriarch preserved the flock of Christ uninfected by the schemes and will of the enemy and transgressor. And when the tyrant saw that his treason had been uncovered and thwarted, having produced no effect, and being himself thoroughly covered with shame, he commanded that the customary wares be set out in the marketplace once again. But when the week was ended, the people of Christ, rendering thanksgiving unto their Benefactor and unto the Martyr, celebrated his memory with kolyva on that Saturday, rejoicing. From that time forth, therefore, the faithful even unto this day, renewing that wonder so that so great a deed of the Martyr may not pass into oblivion and forgetfulness with time, honor and venerate the Great Theodore with kolyva—that is, as they call it among us, with Kutia. Well before that time, the godless governor Vrinkas put this Great-martyr to death during the reign of Caesar Maximian in the East;[^823] who first endured great torments, and afterwards burned down the temple of their goddess, distributing all her furnishings and adornments among the poor; and although certain men came to converse with him...[^824]  

*Troparion:* ...of the [impious] counsel;[^825] for the King Who reigns over all, the Lord of all, has broken thy might!  

*Glory...*  
*Troparion:* O senseless Julian, thy heart is filled with all malice, and rages against our most good God; yet He manifestly grants grace against the schemes crafted deceitfully against us who cry unto Him!  

*Both now...*  
*Theotokion:* Beyond nature was Thy conception, and beyond understanding was Thy birthgiving, O all-immaculate one; for in the flesh hast thou borne God, Who saved all from corruption, O blessed one: therefore do we all glorify thee!  

*Katavasia: "The three God-wise children worshipped not the creation rather than the Creator, but having manfully trampled down the threat of fire, they rejoiced, singing: Blessed art Thou, the all-hymned Lord and God of our fathers!"*  

*Ode 8. Heirmos: "The Redeemer of all":*[^826]  
*Troparion:* She who by her birthgiving filled heavenly and earthly things with joy, through her heavy carrying gives timely joy unto the mortal man, shining forth brightly in festive celebration!  

*Troparion:* Let us keep the Sabbath today, O men, resting from yesterday's labors; let us find rest on the present day from what went astray,[^827] and in the present triumph of the Martyr!  

*Troparion:* Truly this is the first among Sabbaths, and is called the Sabbath of Sabbaths, filled with the Martyr's grace and divine power, a remembrance of great salvation!  

*Troparion:* Honoring God the King with honorable foods, the honorable one abolished the defilements of the lawless empire, and in a most glorious manner of wonder-working sanctified the holy Week!  

*Another Heirmos: "Out of the flame for the holy ones":*[^828]  

*Troparion:* As thou wast delivered out of the flame by divine power, O Martyr Theodore, so even now hast thou saved us through thine own intercession from the most lawless and malicious counsel!  

*Troparion:* Weeping took up its abode at evening for thy servants because of the crafty counsel of our apostate; but in the morning joy shone forth,[^829] O long-suffering Martyr, through thy warm help!  

*Glory...*  
*Troparion:* Having found thee as a deliverer, we who had fallen into perils, and a rescuer from the enemy's wiles, O Martyr of Christ, Passion-bearer Theodore, we praise thee unto all ages!  

*Both now...*  
*Theotokion:* Human mind is at a loss, O Pure One, to recount the mystery of thy birthgiving; therefore with faith and piety do we honor thee as the Mother of God, and we praise thee unto all ages!  

*Katavasia: "The birthgiving of the Mother of God saved the pious children in the furnace: then prefigured, but now in truth fulfilled, it moves the whole universe to sing: Praise ye the Lord, all His works, and exalt Him above all unto all ages!"*  

*Ode 9. Heirmos: "Thy birthgiving was incorrupt":*[^830]  
*Troparion:* The multitude from every quarter is comforted in the tabernacle of testimony, and having shown forth life-giving grace in the glory of all, we magnify the Martyr together with the Sovereign Lady of all!  

*Troparion:* Take courage, O Church of Christ, and reign in joy; for the friends of Christ who are near Thee and surround Thee care for Thee as noble champions, unto Whom thou dost offer thanksgiving!  

*Troparion:* Those things which of old were thought to have died show forth that they live even after departure; and the defeat of the faith having ceased, zeal shows forth again: enriching ourselves with which, we magnify the Benefactor!  

*Both now...*  

*Theotokion:* Bearing thee as a divine seal in hymns, a sealed Book of God, and gathering praises unto thee, O Virgin, in like manner I greatly glorify thy Martyr!  

*Another Heirmos: "It is not possible for men to behold God":*[^831]  
*Troparion:* Rightly hast thou appeared as a most glorious champion and mighty defense unto those who now honor thy venerable and eternal memory, and the achievements of thy sufferings, and the divine defense which came upon us!  

*Troparion:* Thy wonder, O all-blessed Theodore, perfected by holy rains, is carried forth unto the whole world, O blessed one: therefore, gathering year by year, we send up glory unto Christ Who glorified thee!  

*Glory...*  
*Troparion:* Beholding the love of those who praise thee, O Martyr of Christ, bestow grace upon those who call thee blessed; and knowing how great is their faith, O most glorious one, cease not to show thyself unto God as our most fervent intercessor and mediator!  

*Both now...*  
*Theotokion:* We cease not to hymn thee, O Mother of God, our helper, protection, speedy defense, and unashamed advocate: preserve thy servants from every affliction, delivering them ever from all the wiles of the evil one!  

*Katavasia: "Let every earthborn mortal leap for joy in spirit, being enlightened; and let the nature of the bodiless minds celebrate with joy, honoring the holy festival of the Mother of God, and let them cry aloud: Rejoice, O all-blessed Mother of God, pure and ever-virgin!"*  

*Exapostilarion. Podoben: "With the Disciples":*[^832]  
O holy crown-bearer, standing now with the Angels before the Throne of Christ, and filled with light from thence, O Passion-bearer, continually entreat peace for the world and salvation for us who piously celebrate thy light-bearing memory, O all-blessed Theodore, most adorned martyr!  

*Both now... Theotokion:* Desiring to recall the perishing world from corruption, the Lord took up His dwelling within thy womb, as He Himself knew, O Mother of God: having found salvation, therefore, let us all cry aloud unto thee the angelic salutation: Rejoice, O all-hymned one, blessed among women; for thou hast brought forth joy for the whole universe!  

*At the Praises, we set 4 Stichera. Tone 1, Podoben: "Joy of the heavenly ranks" (Нб҃нымъ чи́нѡмъ):*[^833]  
Having assembled in concord, O ye faithful, let us praise with mystical hymns the mighty man of the heavenly army, the patient warrior of our piety, saying: O marvelous Martyr Tyro, pray for those who honor thee!  

By thy namesake calling, truly a gift of God, thou hast granted comfort unto all who are in affliction,[^834] O thrice-blessed Theodore; for everyone who truly hastens unto thy temple, receiving with joy the recompense of thy wonders, honors Christ!  

Having treasured up for thyself all thy strength through the struggles of suffering, as a wealth of piety and radiance, thou didst offer an acceptable gift unto God, completing through struggles with zeal thy God-given name!  

Let all of us, lovers of the feasts, be nourished by the all-radiant festival of the divine Martyr, and let us faithfully rejoice, honoring the bright feast of his end, singing in hymnody unto Jesus Who glorified his memory!  

*Glory... Tone 6:*[^835]  
A gift of consecration and wealth of divine life hast thou appeared unto the world, O Theodore; for Christ, O Martyr, glorified thy memory, in which we the faithful, rejoicing in concord, sing the struggles of thy labors!  

*Both now... Theotokion: "O Mother of God, thou art the true vine that didst bud forth..."*  

*Theotokion:* "...the fruit of life: unto thee do we pray; intercede, O Sovereign Lady, together with the Passion-bearer and all the Saints, that He may have mercy on our souls!"  

*Then: "Unto Thee glory is due."*  
*After that: "Glory to God in the highest."*  

*And we sing Stichera on the Aposticha, Tone 4, Automela:*[^836]  
The assemblies of martyrs dance for joy today in thy temple, O Passion-bearer Theodore, and angelic ranks hymn the sufferings of thy patience; and Christ Himself, the Bestower of crowns, stands by, granting with His right hand rich gifts unto thy hymns; Whom having longed for, thou didst seek, and having found Him, thou didst unite thyself unto Him Whom thou didst desire: entreat Him to save and enlighten our souls!  

*Stichos:* The righteous man shall flourish like a palm tree; he shall be increased like the cedar in Lebanon.[^837]  

The honorable and immaculate fast, having now come unto us, has introduced the perfection of the Martyr's wonders. For having cleansed our spiritual defilements through the fast, and having manfully armed ourselves against the passions through the Martyr's wonders and sufferings, being enlightened from on high by the grace of holy abstinence, and strengthened in faith toward Christ by the wonder-working deeds of the Martyr Theodore, we pray that He may grant salvation unto our souls!  

*Stichos:* Planted in the house of the Lord, in the courts of the God of our salvation.[^838]  

By thy martyr's boldness toward God, O Theodore, thou didst overthrow the vain craftiness of the apostate aimed against the faith of Christ. Thou wast a champion unto the pious people through thy wise protection, delivering them from the defiled food of idol sacrifices: therefore...  

...honoring thee in hymns as the destroyer of idols, as the savior and guardian of the flock of Christ, and as our attentive advocate, we pray that cleansing and enlightenment may be granted unto our souls through thee!  

*Glory... Tone 8:*  
Having piously armed thyself with the fortitude of suffering, O Passion-bearer of Christ, and mystically defending the spiritual sacrifice by His power, thou didst show the impiety of idols and the threats of tyrants to be powerless, despising torments and temporal fire. But O thou who hast both the deed and the name of divine gifts, by thy prayer save from every distress those who celebrate thy memory!  

*Both now... Theotokion: "Receive, O Sovereign Lady, the prayers of thy servants, and deliver us from every necessity and sorrow!"*  

*And the remainder of the order of Matins.*  

*At the Liturgy:* The Beatitudes from the Canon of the Saint, Odes 3 and 6.  
*Prokeimenon, Tone 7:* The righteous man shall be glad in the Lord, and shall hope in Him.  
*Stichos:* Hear my prayer, O God.  
*Epistle to the Hebrews, Pericope 303:* "In many parts..."[^839]  
*For the Saint, Epistle to Timothy, Pericope 292:* "My child Timothy, be strong..."  
*Alleluia, Tone 4. Stichos:* The righteous man shall flourish like a palm tree. *Stichos:* Planted in the house of the Lord, in the courts of the house of our God.  
*Gospel according to Mark, Pericope 10:* "At that time, Jesus was walking on the Sabbath..."  
*For the Saint, Gospel according to John, Pericope 52:* "The Lord said unto His disciples: These things I command you..."  
*Communion Verse:* In everlasting memory shall the righteous be: he shall not fear evil tidings.  

*At the Refectory:* We read the Encomium on the Holy Great-martyr Theodore by Saint Gregory of Nyssa.[^840] And we eat boiled fava beans with white and black olives; and we partake also of cooked food with oil if it be at hand, and of kolyva. And we drink wine by measure (*krasovolion*), for the Saint's sake.[^841] This have we received from the Lavra of our venerable Father Sabbas and from our God-bearing Father Euthymius.  
Be it known that we have received to eat fish only twice [during Lent]: on the Feast of the Annunciation and on Flowery Sunday [Palm Sunday].  

*[Diplomatic description of the full-page woodcut icon engraving: At the top within a decorative strapwork cartouche appears the polyglot Cyrillic-Greek inscription: (ПРОZАХАPIA HAPEYEHOE HMДEMYIΣ). In the central architectural field Christ Pantocrator is enthroned in majesty, blessing with His right hand and holding in His left an open Gospel book inscribed: "To him that overcoms will I grant to sit with Me in My throne, even as I also overcame..." Flanking Him in six circular roundels are the holy images: above, the Holy Great-martyrs Theodore Tyro and George the Victorious; in the middle, the Holy Preeminent Apostles Peter and Paul; below, the Holy Evangelists. In the lower arcade appear the foundational monastic patrons of the Kyiv-Pechersk Lavra, Venerable Theodosius of the Caves and Venerable Anthony of the Caves, flanking the Seventh Ecumenical Council. The architectural border is adorned with floral rosettes.]*[^842]  

## First Sunday of the Holy Fast: The Sunday of Orthodoxy[^843]
*In which Orthodoxy is commemorated.*  
*The usual Vigil.*  

*On Saturday evening: At Small Vespers:*  
*Stichera on 4, Podobna. The composition of Nicholas.*[^844]  
*Tone 1, Podoben: "Joy of the heavenly ranks" (Нб҃нымъ чи́нѡмъ):*  
Now has the brightness of piety spread forth unto all, driving away the deceit of impiety like a cloud, ...and enlightening the hearts of the pious: come, let us all fall down, piously venerating the honorable icons of Christ, bowing down as the Orthodox!

With most holy icons the Church of Christ blossoms today as an adorned bride, and summons all to celebrate spiritually: let us come together in concord and faith with joy, magnifying the Lord!  

Rejoice, O whole world: for behold, the Lord has cast down from on high the dominion of impiety by His ineffable dispensation; and we the humble have been exalted today unto the faith of Orthodoxy, guided by the pious Empress!  

"The honor rendered unto the icon passes over unto the Prototype," said Basil:[^845] therefore in continuity do we honor the icons of Christ the Savior and of all the Saints, that having taken them up, we may never again be led astray by impiety!  

*Glory... both now... Theotokion, Podoben:*[^846]  
He Who is invisible in His beginningless and divine nature was seen as man, O Maiden, from thy precious blood, by reason of His extreme loving-kindness: having depicted the likeness of His flesh, we the faithful all piously bow down and devoutly magnify Him!  

*On the Aposticha, Tone 2, Podoben: "O House of Ephratha" (До́ме Є҆ѵфра́ѳ):*[^847]  
Having escaped the corrupting ruin of the evil-minded, let us enlighten our hearts with the proclamation of Orthodoxy, O ye faithful, glorifying God!  

*Stichos:* Bring unto the Lord, O ye sons of God, bring unto the Lord the young of rams.  

Abolished is the unclean delusion of Arius, of Macedonius, of Peter, of Severus, and of Pyrrhus;[^848] and the thrice-radiant Light shines forth!  

*Stichos:* Worship the Lord in His holy court.  

*Troparion:* No longer is the dark teaching of the impious praised, for unto the Orthodox, through the nodding assent of Theodora,[^849] God gives the rod of strength!  

*Glory... both now... Theotokion, Podoben:*  
Thou hast exalted the horn of the humble, O Mother of God, who didst bear God the Word: therefore do we all faithfully magnify thee, honoring thee!  

*Then: "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart in peace."*  
*Troparion, Tone 2:*[^850]  
To Thy most pure Icon we bow down, O Good One, asking forgiveness of our transgressions, O Christ God; for of Thine own will wast Thou pleased to ascend the Cross in the flesh, that Thou mightest deliver those whom Thou didst create from the bondage of the enemy: therefore with thanksgiving we cry unto Thee: Thou hast filled all things with joy, O our Savior, Who didst come to save the world!  

*Litany and Dismissal.*  

*At Great Vespers:* We chant the Psalter:[^851]  
*"Blessed is the man,"* the entire Kathisma.  
*On "Lord, I have cried," we sing 10 Stichera: Resurrectional stichera from the Octoechos, 3, and Anatolian stichera, 3; and from the Triodion, 4. Tone 6, Podoben: "Having laid aside all earthly hope" (Всѐ възло́жше):*[^852]  
The Prophets, O Lord, inspired by Thy Spirit, foretold that Thou, the Incomprehensible One, Who before the morning star didst shine forth without beginning out of the immaterial and bodiless womb of the Father, wouldest become a Child, incarnate of the unwedded Maiden, united unto men, and seen by those upon the earth: for their sake, as Thou art compassionate, vouchsafe Thy light unto us who hymn Thine ineffable and honorable Resurrection!  

The God-speaking Prophets, who proclaimed Thee by word and honored Thee by deeds, gained endless life:

...for enduring not to serve the creature rather than Thee the Creator, they turned away from all the defilements of the world, and were conformed unto Thee, and foretold Thy Passions: by whose prayers vouchsafe us blamelessly to traverse the stadium of abstinence, O Thou Who alone art greatly merciful![^853]

*Tone 6, Podoben: "Having laid aside all earthly hope" (Всѐ възло́жше):*  
Uncircumscribable in Thy divine nature, O Son, at the last, O Master, having become incarnate, Thou wast pleased to be circumscribed; for by assuming flesh, Thou didst take unto Thyself all its properties.[^854] Therefore, depicting the likeness of Thy form, we kiss it with love, being raised up unto Thy love, and drawing forth the grace of healings from it, following the divine traditions of the Apostles.

*Tone 6, Podoben: "Having laid aside all earthly hope" (Всѐ възло́жше):*  
A most honorable adornment hath the Church of Christ received in the reception of the venerable holy Icons: the most radiant depiction of Christ the Savior, of the Mother of God, and of all the Saints, whereby she is enlightened and adorned with grace; and driving out the assembly of the heretics, she casts it away, and rejoicing, she glorifies God the Lover of mankind, Who for her sake endured voluntary sufferings.

*Glory, Tone 2:*[^855]  
The grace of God's truth, prefigured of old in shadows, has now visibly been fulfilled: for behold, the Church is robed in the incarnate Image of Christ as in a most beautiful vesture, delineating the pattern of the Tabernacle of Testimony and holding fast the Orthodox Faith; that holding the image of Him Whom we honor, we may not go astray. Let those who do not believe thus be clothed in shame! For unto us, our glory is the likeness of Him Who became incarnate, piously venerated, and not deified: kissing it, let us the faithful cry out: O God, save Thy people, and bless Thine inheritance!

*Now and ever: Theotokion: Tone of the week.*

*At the Litiya, the customary Idiomela of the temple. Glory: Tone 2:*[^856]  
Rejoice, O venerable Prophets, who well expounded the Law of the Lord, and by faith were shown to be invincible and unyielding pillars! For ye were shown to be the mediators of the New Covenant of Christ; and having translated unto the heavens, entreat Him to pacify the world and to save our souls!

*Now and ever: Tone the same (Dogmatikon):*  
A wonder new beyond all ancient wonders! For who hath known a mother who gave birth without a husband, and carried in her arms Him Who upholds all creation? It was the will of God that was born: Whom, as an infant, O all-pure one, carrying in thine arms, and having acquired maternal boldness toward Him, cease not to pray for those who honor thee, to have compassion upon the world and to save our souls!

*On the Aposticha, in the Octoechos. Glory... both now... Tone 2:*[^857]  
Having passed from impiety unto piety, and having been enlightened by the light of knowledge, let us clap our hands like the psalmist, offering thanksgiving and praise unto God; and unto the sacred Images depicted on walls, and boards, and sacred vessels—of Christ, of the All-pure One, and of all the Saints—let us devoutly bow down, casting away the impious faith of the heterodox. For the honor rendered unto the image, as Basil says, passes over unto the Prototype: asking, through the prayers of Thine All-pure Mother, O Christ our God, and of all the Saints, that great mercy be granted unto us!

*Then: "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart in peace." Trisagion. Troparion: "To Thy most pure Icon:" written at Small Vespers. And the rest of the service of the Vigil.*

*Mark's Chapter: If the Finding of the Precious Head of John the Forerunner, or the Memory of the Forty Martyrs, should happen to fall on the First Sunday of Lent, it is chanted for them as indicated on the Third Sunday of Lent.*[^858]

*At Matins. At "God is the Lord," Troparion: Resurrectional.*  
*Glory: Troparion: "To Thy most pure Icon:" (see fol. 307).[^859]*  
*Now and ever: "All beyond understanding:" (see fol. 282). Sessional hymns: Psalter reading in the Octoechos, and the Undefiled (Kathisma 17). Then: "The angelic host;" Litany, and the rest, written on Cheesefare Sunday (see fol. 154). Then: "Save, O God, Thy people;" "Lord, have mercy," 12 times, loud and slow. After this, Canons: Resurrectional and the Theotokos, both together for 8; and in the Triodion, for 6.*

*Tone 4. Ode 1. The composition of the Lord Theophanes.*[^860]  
*Whose Acrostic is:*  
*Today the radiant proclaimed grace of piety hath arrived.*[^861]  
*Heirmos: "The Red Sea:"*  
Clapping our hands with rejoicing today, let us the faithful cry aloud: How marvelous are Thy works, O Christ, and great is Thy power, Who hast wrought our unanimity and concord!

*Troparion:* Come, O ye wise in God, let us accomplish a joyful day: now heaven and earth make merry, and the angelic hosts and assemblies of men celebrate in various manners!

*Troparion:* Beholding the exceeding great benefaction, let us clap our hands: the divided members of Christ gathered together into unity; and let us praise God Who grants peace!

*Troparion:* Trophies of victory were given this day unto the Church, moved by God through the assent and counsel of Michael and Theodora,[^862] our Sovereigns excelling piously in the faith!

*Theotokion:* The weapons of the impious heresies have manifestly vanished; for beholding thy temple, O most pure and undefiled Virgin, all-piously adorned with images, we now rejoice all-sacredly!

*Katavasia:* Traversing with unwetted feet the abyss of the Red Sea, ancient Israel of old, by the cross-shaped hands of Moses, overcame the power of Amalek in the wilderness.[^863]

*Ode 3. Heirmos: "Thy Church rejoices in Thee:"*  
No longer now shall the eyebrows of the impious heretics be lifted up; for the power of God hath strengthened Orthodoxy!

*Troparion:* Let the clouds of the Prophets sprinkle down upon us this day life-creating dew from heaven, unto the exaltation of the faith!

*Troparion:* Let the mystical trumpets of Christ's Apostles, in voices divine, cry out beyond nature the restoration of the honorable Images!

*Troparion:* Let us hymn Christ, Who hath shown forth unto us a pious and Christ-loving Empress with her God-crowned offspring!

*Theotokion:* Having reached thy sacred dwelling, O All-pure One, we the faithful pray that we may now be illuminated with light-bestowing grace!

*Katavasia: "Thy Church rejoices in Thee, O Christ, crying: Thou art my strength, O Lord, and my refuge and my firm support!"*

*Sessional Hymn: Tone 1, Podoben: "The angelic choir" (Ли́къ А҆́гг҃лскїй):*[^864]  
Depicting Thy divine likeness upon the Icon, O Christ, we understand Thy Nativity, Thine ineffable wonders, and Thy voluntary Crucifixion: therefore the demons are driven away in fear, and the heterodox weep in grief, as being partakers with them!

*Glory...*  
The likenesses of the Prophets, the appearances of the Apostles, of the holy Martyrs, and of all the Saints, doth Zion the Mother on high depict on Icons, and brightly makes merry, being adorned with spiritual beauties of the noetic Bridegroom and the bride!

*Now and ever... Theotokion:*  
Unto those who with love honor thy holy Icon, O pure Virgin, and who with one voice proclaim thee the true Mother of God, and who faithfully bow down before thee, appear as guardian and mighty protector, turning away from them every evil, as thou canst do all things!

*Ode 4. Heirmos: "Beholding Thee lifted up:"*  
By the visitation of the divine Comforter, sanctify Thy temple, and by His coming drive away heretical deceit, O Word of God Who art greatly merciful!

*Troparion:* Having delivered Thy people from the most Jewish impiety, show them burning with the zeal of piety and crying out with faith: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

*Troparion:* Beholding the divine tabernacles shining with sacred representations of the Images of Christ and of the Mother of God, we rejoice in a manner becoming the sacred!

*Troparion:* The Empress adorned with a crown, having longed for the true Kingdom of Christ, inscribed His most pure Image and the representations of the Saints!

*Theotokion:* Having given birth unto the incarnate divine Word, O Virgin full of grace, thou didst show forth His sanctification becoming God: therefore do we renew thy light-bearing temple!

*Katavasia: Beholding Thee lifted up upon the Cross, O Sun of Righteousness, the Church stood in her place, worthily crying out: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!*

*Ode 5. Heirmos: "Thou, O Lord, art my light:"*  
Establish, O Lord, a firm foundation for Thy Church, that she may remain unshaken unto ages of ages from the tempest of heresies!

*Troparion:* Unto all the earth the brightness of the joy given from on high unto the faithful hath shone forth, and of the divine protection!

*Troparion:* Thou Who alone art good and the fountain of grace, exalt Thou the horn of Orthodox Rulers who honor Thine Image![^865]

*Troparion:* The unwaning Light of piety hath shone upon us by the God-inspired command of faithful Rulers, and by their God-wise decree!

*Theotokion:* Renew for us the ancient beauty, O most pure Mother of God, and sanctify this thy temple by thy grace!

*Katavasia: Thou, O Lord, art my light, Who hast come into the world: a holy light turning those who hymn Thee in faith away from gloomy ignorance.*

*Ode 6. Heirmos: "I will sacrifice unto Thee:"*  
Inscribed and honored is the venerated Image; and again the Church takes boldness, piously glorifying the Savior!

*Troparion:* The Church of Christ is stripped of the sorrow and darkness of heresy, and wears the garment of rejoicing, and is overshadowed with divine and light-bearing grace!

*Troparion:* The assembly of the Orthodox hath received the radiance of ancient renown through the decree of Empress Theodora and of her pious son, Michael the Autocrat!

*Theotokion:* He Who of old commanded the Tabernacle of Testimony to exist dwelt in thee as in a spiritual tabernacle, the One Most-glorified, glorifying thy temple, O Virgin, with wonders.

*Katavasia: I will sacrifice unto Thee with the voice of praise, O Lord, the Church cries unto Thee, having been cleansed from the deceit of demons by the mercy flowing from Thy side in blood!*

*Kontakion: Tone 8, Automelon (Самогласенъ):*[^866]  
The uncircumscribable Word of the Father was circumscribed in the flesh from thee, O Theotokos; and having restored the defiled image to its ancient state, He united it with divine beauty: but confessing salvation in word and deed, we depict it.

*Ikos:*[^867]  
Behold the mystery of the dispensation! The Prophets inspired of old by the vision of God foretold it for our sake, who have reached the end of the ages, having received its radiance. Taking from it divine understanding, we know the one Lord God, glorified in three Hypostases; and serving Him alone, having one faith and one baptism, we have put on Christ. But confessing salvation, in likeness, in deed, and in word, we depict it.

*Synaxarion for the First Sunday of Holy Lent:*[^868]  
*Verses:*  
*Unfittingly were the Icons cast out,*  
*I rejoice, seeing them fittingly venerated.*

*[Diplomatic description of the woodcut engraving: At the top is depicted the Sacred Seventh Ecumenical Council and the Triumph of Orthodoxy. In the center beneath a canopy stand the pious young Emperor Michael and holy Empress Theodora holding the venerable Icons of Christ the Savior and of the Most-holy Mother of God, flanked by holy hierarchs and confessors in omophoria, with the Cyrillic inscription: SEVENTH COUNCIL. In the lower register, the assembly of the Holy Fathers and Confessors in two facing tiers holds scrolls and books in conciliar session.]*[^869]

On this day, the First Sunday of Holy Lent, the Church of Christ accepted the celebration of Orthodoxy,[^870] that is, the Exaltation of the holy and venerable Icons, which took place under Emperor Michael, and Theodora, his modest and blameless mother and Empress, and under Saint Methodius, Patriarch of Constantinople. This came to pass in the following manner:

*George Kedrenos, book 3.*[^871] When Leo the Isaurian, from being a donkey-driver and from the manual trade by which he had gained his sustenance, obtained the scepter of the Empire [following the voluntary abdication of Theodosius the Evil], by divine permission: Saint Germanus, who at that time held the supreme governance and administration of the Church, was immediately summoned by him, and heard him say: "It seems to me, Master, that holy Icons are in no way different from idols. Command therefore that they be cast out from our midst as quickly as possible; or, if they be true representations of the saints, let them be lifted higher and hung up, lest wallowing always in great sins, we defile them by kissing." But the Patriarch dissuaded the Emperor from such great hatred and rebuked him for this, saying: "Be not such a one, O Emperor! For we hear that there will be one who speaks much and madly against the icons, whose surname is Konon." And he replied: "Indeed, when I was still young, I was called by that name." When therefore the Patriarch would not be persuaded to obey him, [and generally resisted him, speaking and demonstrating how the holy images had already endured for seven hundred and twenty-five years in the Church, and how the Holy Fathers at the Six Councils, seeing them in the churches where they assembled, never condemned them, but honored them; and by other proofs from Holy Scripture stoutly defending the images against him for several years,] he was driven into exile by him.[^872] In his place he installed Anastasios. And thus at that time war against the holy images was declared and publicly proclaimed.

They relate also that first of all Jewish sorcerers instilled such great hatred into him; who, when they saw his manual trade, told him from their sorceries that he was to become Emperor, [in return for which they asked him to swear unto them that when he became Emperor, he would perform whatever they asked of him; and he swore unto them in the church of Saint Theodore], for being poor, while grazing donkeys with them, he labored for his livelihood.[^873]

And when that Emperor Leo the Iconoclast brought his life to an evil end, from him a yet more dreadful lion's whelp, Constantine Copronymus, that is, the Dung-named, became heir to the Empire, or rather, to his father's fury and madness against the holy images:[^874] [being twenty-one years of age, a truly venomous brood of vipers, who in malice and infidelity either equaled his father or surpassed him: he renounced God, and the All-pure Theotokos, and His Saints; he learned sorceries and demonic rites, and defiled himself with every uncleanness; he shed human blood in service to demons, and knew all spiritual defilements from his youth, having learned all this from his father;] how many and what kind of wickedness this transgressor of the law committed, who can utter? Yet when he also ended his life still more shamefully, his son Leo, born of the Khazar woman, was set over the Empire.

And because he also departed this life by an evil death, Irene his wife and Constantine his son [crowned while he was still living] became heirs to the Empire and supreme rule.[^875] These—Irene, I say, and Constantine—guided and instructed by Tarasios, the most holy Patriarch of Constantinople, convened the Seventh Ecumenical Council, and the Church of Christ once again received the holy Icons, that is, the images. And when they also laid down the imperial rule, Nikephoros the Patrician [and Grand Logothete] was brought unto the throne, who was equal unto his predecessors in cruelty. After him, Staurakios his son. After him, Michael Rangabe, who held the holy Images in reverence. While Michael was still living, upon his own voluntary abdication, there succeeded to the Empire the beast-like Leo the Armenian, who, corrupted by the deceit of a certain anchorite monk of Philomelion, an impious man, stirred up the second Iconoclasm; and the Church of God was once again stripped of her first adornment.[^876]

[Concerning whose seduction Kedrenos the historian relates this narrative: A certain monk of Philomelion, he says, when that Leo was at war, prophesied unto him that he was to become Emperor. And remembering him, Leo sent him rich gifts; with which the envoy, not finding him alive, came upon his disciple, the monk Sabbatios, and offered the gifts unto him. But that monk, being a great iconoclast, said: "I will not take gifts from him who bows down unto idols and obeys Empress Irene and Patriarch Tarasios. Tell him: he shall lose his life and his Empire unless he casts out the images!" When the envoy related this unto Leo, he was alarmed, and summoned to counsel Theodore Melissenos, infected with the same heresy, who said: "There is, he says, in the Monastery of the Dexiokrates a certain monk who works wonders; let us speak with him and do whatever he commands." The Emperor promised to go unto him unrecognized, having changed his garments. Meanwhile Theodore forewarned that monk and taught him what he should do and say when the Emperor should arrive in mean clothing. The monk said: "Hide not thyself, O Emperor, I know who thou art!" And the Emperor, being terrified, attributed the Holy Spirit unto him; and he accepted his counsel to cast out the images; and without delay he issued an open edict that the images be desecrated and cast down. Thus far Kedrenos.]

Then after some years, Michael the Amorian succeeded to the throne,[^877] *John Zonaras, History, vol. 3.* [who sorely oppressed the Orthodox, and having dealt cruelly with them as with others, rose up even against Saint Methodius: he sent Euthymius, Archbishop of Sardis, into exile for venerating the holy Icons; then he imprisoned Methodius in Akritas; and the illustrious Euthymius, cruelly scourged by his son Theophilus, he added unto the number of the Martyrs, imitating Copronymus in all things and siding with the Jews.]

After him, Theophilus his son became heir to the Empire, and to madness against the images, surpassing others therein.[^878] This Theophilus, though he delivered many holy Fathers unto diverse punishments and torments, namely for the sake of the venerable images, nevertheless claimed civil justice most especially unto himself and championed it for the wronged; so that even if anyone sought out and inquired whether there was anyone in the city who caused grievance unto another, for many days, as they say, he found not one such person.

And when he had been Monarch for twelve years, being seized with the disease of dysentery, that is, the bloody flux, so that his life was about to be undone, his mouth opened excessively wide, so that even the inner parts of his entrails were exposed.[^879] But Empress Theodora, being grieved at such a misfortune, thereupon fell asleep; and in a dream she saw the All-pure Theotokos holding in her bosom the pre-eternal Child, and round about her stood all-radiant Angels, who were striking Theophilus her husband and mocking him. When therefore her sleep left her, and Theophilus, having revived a little, cried out: "Woe, woe unto me, a wretched man! Because of the holy Images they beat me!"

Straightway the Empress placed upon him an Image of the All-pure Theotokos, praying unto her with tears. Thus Theophilus, wandering in mind, saw one from among those who stood before him carrying an Icon; and seizing it, he began to kiss it. And forthwith his mouth, which had gnashed against the Images, and his shameless, gaping throat, were restored unto their former nature, and became just as they had been before; and from the injuries and torment wherewith he had been held, he grew calm and fell asleep, confessing that it is a good thing to hold the holy Images in reverence and esteem. Then the Empress, bringing forth from her coffers the venerable and holy Images, brought it to pass that Theophilus her husband kissed those Images and honored them with all his soul.

Then after a short time, Theophilus departed this life. And Theodora released all who were in exile and prisons, commanding them to live in freedom; and John also, who was called Jannes, was cast down from the throne—a chief sorcerer and chief heresiarch rather than a chief father.[^880] And Christ's Confessor Methodius ascended that Throne, having suffered much before that, and having been buried alive in a tomb. And when this had come to pass, a certain divine visitation occurred unto Joannicius the Great, who was living in asceticism upon Mount Olympus. For ...Arsakios the great faster, having come unto him, says: "God hath sent me unto thee, that having gone unto Isaiah the most venerable man, the recluse in Nicomedia, we may learn from him what is pleasing unto God, and becoming and proper for His holy Church."[^881] And having thus come unto that holy man Isaiah, they hear from him: "Thus saith the Lord: Behold, the end hath drawn nigh for the enemies of My depiction! Go ye therefore unto Empress Theodora, and likewise unto Patriarch Methodius, and speak thus: Cast out the coterie of the unconsecrated and defiled, and thus with the Angels offer sacrifice unto Me, having the Image of My countenance and the Cross in honor!" Hearing this, they immediately hastened unto Constantinople, and made known unto Patriarch Methodius and unto all the chosen of God what had been shown unto them. And having gathered together, they come unto the Empress, and find her calmed and inclined in all things, since from her parents she had been pious and God-loving. Forthwith therefore the Empress, having brought forth an Icon of the Mother of God hanging upon her neck, kissed it in the presence and before the eyes of all, saying: "If anyone bows not down unto these, and kisses them not with a sincere heart, and not with the manner of servile worship, not honoring them as gods, but thus respecting out of love the images of those whom they represent,[^882] let such a one be Anathema, that is, accursed!"

Hearing this, they rejoiced with great joy. Immediately also the Empress entreats them to make supplication concerning Theophilus her husband. And they, beholding her faith, although they excused themselves, nevertheless consented. And Saint Methodius, having assembled all the people, and the entire clergy, and the hierarchs, gathered in the Great Church, among whom were also those most excellent men from Mount Olympus: the great Joannicius and Arsakios; Naukratios also and the disciples of Theodore the Studite; and from the Great Village, Theophanes and Theodore the Branded, the Confessors; Michael of the Holy City and Euggelos, and very many others;[^883] and they offered an all-night prayer unto God for Theophilus, all praying with tears and concordant and humble supplications. And this was performed throughout the entire first week of Great Lent. Empress Theodora herself also, with other women and a multitude of people, offered the same prayers. And while this was being performed there, Empress Theodora, having fallen asleep at dawn on Friday, seemed unto herself to be at the Pillar of the Cross,[^884] and saw certain persons who...

...who with tumult were passing along to cross that road, carrying diverse instruments of torment, and in their midst led bound Emperor Theophilus, having his hands tied behind him; whom the Empress, having recognized, herself followed in the steps of those who led him. And when they reached even unto the Bronze Gate,[^885] she beheld a supernatural vision of a certain Man, seated before an Icon of Christ, Which they had placed opposite Theophilus. Touching His feet, the Empress pleaded for the Emperor. And He, barely opening His mouth, said: "Great is thy faith, O woman! Know therefore, that for the sake of thy tears and faith, and moreover for the sake of the prayers and intercessions of My servants and My Priests, I grant forgiveness unto Theophilus thy husband." Then He says unto those who led him: "Untie him, and give him back unto his wife." And she, having taken him, departed rejoicing and being glad; and forthwith her sleep left her.

And this Empress Theodora beheld.

Patriarch Methodius, for his part, during that time when the supplications and prayers were being offered, having taken a new parchment, wrote upon it the names of all the heretical emperors, and in that same order inscribed also the name of that Theophilus, and placed it secretly from all under the Holy Table.[^886] And about Friday, he himself saw a certain fearful and great Angel entering into the Church, and approaching unto him, and saying: "Thy prayer hath been heard, O Priest, and Emperor Theophilus hath obtained forgiveness; henceforth therefore trouble God no more concerning this matter!" And he, testing whether that which he had seen was true, having stepped away from the place where he was standing, and having taken the parchment, and read it, found—O the divine judgments!—the name of Theophilus completely erased by God! The Empress, having learned of this, was exceedingly glad, and announces unto the Patriarch that he should assemble all the people with the Honorable Crosses and holy Icons in the Great Church, that the adornment of the holy Images might be restored unto her, and that this new wonder of God might become known unto all.

When therefore all had quickly assembled in the Church with candles, the Empress arrived with her son, and a Litiya, that is, a devout supplication unto God, was begun there, with holy Icons, and the divine and venerable wood of the Cross, and with the Holy and Divine Gospel; and they conducted a Procession for as much as a mile, crying out: "Kyrie eleison," that is, "Lord, have mercy."[^887] And having thus returned again unto the church, they served the Divine Liturgy, having set in their places the holy and venerable Images...

...by the aforesaid holy men. There also the pious and Orthodox were proclaimed, and the contrary godless ones, and those who did not receive the honor of the holy Icons, were cried out and given over unto Anathema, that is, unto utter destruction.[^888]

And from that time forth, those holy Confessors established that each year in like manner this holy assembly should take place, lest perchance we fall again into that same godlessness. O unchangeable Image of the Father, through the prayers of Thy holy Confessors, have mercy on us, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

*Ode 7. Heirmos: "The children did not obey":*[^889]  
Let the angelic host join in dance with the splendor of the Church with divine love, singing in a God-acceptable manner: Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord!

*Troparion:* The Church of the firstborn and the festive assembly rejoices, beholding now the divine people singing in unison: Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord!

*Troparion:* Delivered from the dark heresy of before, by the nodding command of Theodora the worthy Empress, we sing: Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord!

*Theotokion:* Exalted above the choirs on high, O pure one, having alone been the Mother of the Creator: rejoicing therefore we cry out: Blessed art thou among women, O all-immaculate Sovereign Lady!

*Katavasia: In the furnace the Persian children of Abraham, bedewed with love of piety rather than with flame, cried out: Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord!*

*Ode 8. Heirmos: "Stretching out his hands":*[^890]  
Preserving the ancestral laws of the Church, we depict images, and kiss them with lips, and heart, and desire—of Christ, and of His Saints, crying: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Troparion:* Paying honor and veneration manifestly unto the Prototype of the Image, we honor it, following the teaching of the God-inspired; and with faith in Christ we cry: Bless the Lord, all ye works![^891]

*Troparion:* Having enlightened her mind with the illumination of the Divine Spirit, the venerable Empress, possessing God-measured fruits, loved the goodly majesty and beauty of the Church of Christ, blessing together with the faithful Jesus the God-man!

*Theotokion:* Illuminated by the rays of the noetic Light, thy divine house now enlightens all with the cloud of the Spirit, and sanctifies the faithful who harmoniously sing: Bless the Lord!

*Katavasia: Daniel, stretching out his hands, stopped the mouths of the lions in the pit; and the young men, lovers of piety, girded about with virtue, quenched the power of the fire, crying: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!*

*Ode 9. Heirmos: "A stone cut without hands":*[^892]  
Beholding again the honorable Church adorned with the sacred inscriptions of images, let us all run with devotion, and let us cry aloud unto Christ: We magnify Thee, O Savior!

*Troparion:* Having acquired Thy Cross, and honorable Icons, and the representations of the Saints as honor and glory, O Church, with gladness, O Master, and with joy do we magnify Thee!

*Troparion:* Illumine our Rulers with Thy divine glory, O Bountiful One, and with angelic hosts and their panoply hedge them about, subduing the ferocity of the nations before them, O Master!

*Theotokion:* The condemnation of Eve our first mother is wiped away, O Mother of God; for ineffably, O pure one, hast thou given birth unto the Master of all, Whose likeness on Icons we now kiss!

*Katavasia: A stone cut without hands from an unquarried mountain, O Virgin, was Christ the cornerstone, Who united the separated natures: therefore, rejoicing, we magnify thee, O Mother of God!*

*Exapostilarion: Resurrectional. And another. Podoben: "With the disciples let us go up" (Съ Оу҆чени́ки вни́демъ):*[^893]  
Leap for joy, clap your hands, sing with rejoicing, crying: How marvelous and strange are Thy works, O Christ! And who shall be able to utter Thy mighty acts, O Savior, Who hast united our unanimity and concord into one Church?

*Theotokion:* The weapons of hostile heresy have now failed, and the memory thereof hath perished with a noise: for beholding thy house, O All-honorable One, all-comely, adorned with the grace of the honorable Icons, we are all filled with joy!

*At the Praises: Resurrectional stichera, 4; and these present, 3, repeating one. Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast given a sign" (Да́лъ є҆сѝ знаме́нїе):*[^894]  
In Thee now rejoices the Church, O Lover of mankind, her Bridegroom and Creator, Who by Thy divine will didst deliver her from idol deception, and didst betroth her unto Thyself by Thy precious Blood, brightly receiving the sacred elevation of the Icons; and rejoicing, she faithfully hymns and glorifies Thee!

*Verse: I will praise Thee, O Lord, with my whole heart.*  
The depiction of Thy flesh, Thy portrayal, O Lord, we lovingly kiss, explaining the great mystery of Thy dispensation; for not in semblance, as the God-fighting children of Manes say, didst Thou appear unto us, O Lover of mankind, but in truth and by the nature of the flesh, raising us up unto Thy love and longing!

*Verse: I will be glad and rejoice in Thee.*  
A day full of joy and gladness hath appeared this day; for the splendor of the truest Dogmas gleams and shines forth! The Church of Christ is adorned with the elevation of the holy Icons...

...now depicted, and with their radiance; and there comes to pass the divinely ordered unanimity of the faithful!

*Then we say the verse, Tone 6: Arise, O Lord my God, let Thy hand be lifted up! And we chant the idiomelon sticheron:*[^895]  
Moses received the Law in the time of abstinence, and drew the people; Elijah by fasting shut the heavens; and the three children of Abraham overcame the lawless tyrant by fasting: by these vouchsafe us also, O Savior, to attain the Resurrection, crying thus: Holy God, Holy Mighty, Holy Immortal, have mercy on us!

*Glory: Tone the same.*  
*Now and ever: Most blessed art thou, O Virgin Theotokos. Great Doxology. After the Trisagion, Resurrectional Troparion only. Litany and Dismissal. Then the Gospel Sticheron. And First Hour. At the First Hour: Troparion: Resurrectional. Glory: To Thy most pure Icon. Now and ever: Theotokion of the same. After the Trisagion, Kontakion: The uncircumscribable Word of the Father (see fol. 313). And final Dismissal.*

*At the Liturgy:*[^896]  
*The Beatitudes in the Octoechos, on 6; and from the Triodion, Ode 6, on 4. After the Little Entrance: Troparion: Resurrectional, and of the Feast.
