Glory, both now: Kontakion of the Feast: The uncircumscribable Word of the Father. Prokeimenon, Tone 4. Song of the Fathers: Blessed art Thou, O Lord, God of our fathers, and praised and glorified is Thy name unto the ages. Verse: For Thou art righteous in all that Thou hast done for us. Epistle to the Hebrews, Pericope 324 (Heb. 11:24–26, 32–40): Brethren: By faith Moses, when he was come to years... Alleluia, Tone 4: Moses and Aaron among His priests, and Samuel among them that call upon His name. Verse: The heavens are Thine, and the earth is Thine. Gospel according to John, Pericope 5 (John 1:43–51): At that time, Jesus would go forth into Galilee... Communion Hymn: Praise the Lord from the heavens. Another: Rejoice in the Lord, O ye righteous.*

*At the Refectory:*[^897]  
*We eat cooked food with oil, but not fish. And if it happen, we drink the appointed wine to the glory of God, two cups; likewise in the evening, two cups.*

## The Order on the Sunday of Orthodoxy: For the Anathema of Heretics[^898]

*Be it known that after the Dismissal of Matins we pray together, with the holy Woods of the Cross and honorable Icons, and we go forth unto an appointed place where it is proper to read the Conciliar Decree. And as we go and as we return, we chant the present Canon. The composition of the holy Father Theodore the Studite.*[^899]

*Ode 1, Tone 6. Heirmos: "He is my helper and protector":*  
Let us the faithful sing a thankful song unto God the Benefactor of all; for He hath raised up a horn of salvation: a mighty kingdom, the champion of Orthodoxy!

*Troparion:* In truth divine grace hath appeared unto the universe; glory and honor have shone forth; the Church claps her hands, having received a vesture for her nakedness!

*Troparion:* The shroud of Christ, torn to pieces before by deceptive and apostate John, the divine Fathers have sewn together and manifestly given unto the Church.

*Troparion:* Beholding the Lord, having received Him, the Church rejoices and claps her hands with her children, having received from Him the prize of victory, the trophy of Orthodoxy!

*Troparion:* Let the frantic ones henceforth be put to shame and confounded: fierce Lyzix, and Antony with John, and Theodore—both apostates from the faith![^900]

*Troparion:* Jannes and Jambres, having opposed Moses the Lawgiver of old, were put to shame; and now deceitful John in truth appears with Antony![^901]

*Troparion:* Thou, O Christ, hast dashed in pieces the chariot of the God-fighters, and hast granted adornment unto Thy Church, for which, as Thou art good, Thou didst pour out Thy Blood!

*Triadikon:* Thee, O Trinity, do I glorify in theology, and I bow down before Thy divine dominion: deliver me from all temptations; for in Thee do I believe: the Father, and the Son, and the All-holy Spirit!

*Theotokion:* Clothed from thee, O Virgin, in an imperial vesture, God appeared unto men in human form, twofold in nature: Whose appearance of countenance we hold in veneration!

*Ode 3. Heirmos: "Establish, O Lord, upon the rock":*  
Be glad, all ye choirs of Fathers and Apostles, beholding the veneration of the Icons which ye manifestly handed down!

*Troparion:* "I have received my beauty, and have clothed myself in my vesture," let the all-immaculate Church sing, which John had stripped bare!

*Troparion:* Be ashamed, ye lawless ones who speak heretically against the Lord; for He became incarnate and appeared in an image, which we firmly kiss!

*Troparion:* The foul commands and lawless teachings of senseless John, who can utter, expounding his serpentine ways?

*Troparion:* Anathema unto Lyzikos, and unto John with Antony, and unto senseless and blasphemous Theodore, together with senseless Theodotos![^902]

*Troparion:* The poured-out blood cries aloud concerning the divine flesh-bearing likeness of the Master, which blood John shed!

*Troparion:* The Lord hath driven away the chariot of strangers, and restored His own...

...unto His own: glory to His loving-kindness!

*Glory... Triadikon:* Unto the beginningless Will, and dominion, and kingdom, unto the Trinity let us bow down in an Orthodox manner, ever dishonoring Arius!

*Both now... Theotokion:* In truth do we confess thee, O Sovereign Lady, as having given birth unto God, heeding not the words of Nestorius, but the ancestral commands!

*Ode 4. Heirmos: "The Prophet heard":*  
Rejoice, O Church, and every city and country in gladness! Let the wilderness dwellings now be opened, and let the virgin relics be adorned, and let the representations of the Martyrs be worthily venerated![^903]

*Troparion:* Christ summons you: assemble now with love, O divine Fathers, and recount in apostolic manner the form of His Incarnation, the wonders and the Passions, as the divine Gospel writes!

*Troparion:* Assemble, ye earthborn, multitudes of monastics, with boldness; for even if the wretched ones prevail evilly, they shall be vanquished again; and whatever counsel such men take, the Lord shall scatter it!

*Troparion:* The wounds of the Fathers, the blood of their stripes have truly ceased; the frequent banishments have ended; and peace shall dwell among all; no longer do the Baalite blasphemies prevail: for God is with us!

*Troparion:* The vine of malice spread forth branches of impiety, and a bitter cluster blossomed, and the venom of serpents is their wine; wherewith they made the Lord's people drink in truth the dark cup of malice![^904]

*Troparion:* They defiled Thy Church with lawless ordi-...

...-nations, blows of destruction; and canonically they are swept away like mire, and have fallen from divine glory: Simon Magus, and with him John, and fierce Antony![^905]

*Troparion:* Having assembled, let us cry aloud against the wild beasts and God-fighters: foul Antony, and the transgressor John taught by this age, the combatant against the Church, as against grievous wolves who are accursed!

*Triadikon:* Uncreated Monarchy, Father, Son, and Spirit, Thee do we worship; Whom the many-eyed Cherubim and the six-winged Seraphim hymn, crying aloud: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, O Highest Ruler of all!

*Theotokion:* Holier than the holy, and higher than all creatures, hast thou alone appeared, O Virgin Mother, having given birth unto Thine own Creator: therefore do we hold thy holy image, O Mother of God, in veneration![^906]

*Ode 5. Heirmos: "Rising early from the night, O Lover of mankind":*  
Christ hath conquered, let the earth dance! The tumult hath ceased, the weeping of Christ's servants hath ceased, and the faith hath spread everywhere in the world!

*Troparion:* Gazing upon the Icon, honoring the Crucifixion, we love and kiss Christ and His signs, and we bow down before them, not honoring them as gods!

*Troparion:* The talkative and blasphemous spirit of Lyzikos hath ceased, which continually spoke, day by day, against the divine image of Christ and of the Saints!

*Troparion:* Why, O thrice-wretched one, didst thou hate the most pure representation of the Incarnation of Christ and of all the Saints? For not unto deaf idols do we the faithful bow down!

*Troparion:* Being instruments of impiety, they gathered a council of impious priests against the most high God, even as the Jews of old, Annas and Caiaphas!

*Troparion:* In the Day of Judgment, O wretched one, there shall stand as reprovers of thy godless soul the council of the Fathers, whose bodies thou didst strip bare with countless wounds!

*Troparion:* Let all churches cry aloud, all calling out, having been deprived by thee of the form of the Lord, and of His Saints, of the consecrated Icons!

*Triadikon:* All-ruling by Thy dominion, glory to Thee, glory to Thee, O Tri-hypostatic Unity, Father, Son, and Spirit! Deliver from every harm those who hope in Thee!

*Theotokion:* As a golden-adorned lamp do we honor thee, O Sovereign Lady, who didst bear the spiritual Light unto the world, and didst abate the dark tempest, O Virgin!

*Ode 6. Heirmos: "Cry aloud with all thine heart":*  
The vigilant guardians of the Church of Christ cried aloud, praying unto Him to grant peace; and He heard, and gave heed unto their prayer!

*Troparion:* And the snares of deceit were exposed by the teachings of the Fathers; and God is praised, depicted in the flesh, though uncircumscribed in Divinity!

*Troparion:* Be ashamed, ye accomplices of deceit, and let Theodotos perish together with Antony, and Lyzikos, and Theodore, the abyss of destruction![^907]

*Troparion:* Thou didst open thy mouth, O wretched one, not in spiritual hymns, but in blasphemies against thy Master, casting away the venerable making of Icons!

*Troparion:* Thou hast perverted the commands of the Fathers and the teachings of the Apostles, writing differently and otherwise according to thine own idol-temple...

...lawless one, O John, fighter against Christ![^908]

*Troparion:* Thy smoke filled the eyes of the pious with tears, but by the wind of the divine Teachers it hath been scattered, O foolish-minded John!

*Troparion:* Thou hast torn the divine robe, even as Arius tore the tunic of Christ of old; therefore art thou cast far from the Church, having been cast out like a dog![^909]

*Triadikon:* As one Origin do I glorify the Godhead in three Hypostases; for God is one: Father, Son, and Spirit, even though distinguished in depictions and Persons!

*Theotokion:* Prophetically, O pure one glorious in God, hast thou appeared as the City of God, from which Thine own Creator was born, preserving thee after childbirth even as before!

*Ode 7. Heirmos: "Unto those who have sinned and done iniquity":*  
The fire of heresies hath divine grace now extinguished, which burns the noetic Chaldeans, and bedews those who serve the Trinity, holding the praises throughout the four weeks![^910]

*Troparion:* The Church is adorned, clothed, and beautified, bearing the depiction of the Incarnation of the Master of all, and His Passions and signs, fully according to divine laws!

*Troparion:* Feast, celebrate, ye people of the Lord named after Christ, seeing the Church shone forth again with the beauty of the divine form, which He Who is God bore as man, in order to save us!

*Troparion:* The Word suffered poverty, and hungered, and thirsted in the flesh; these are properties of human nature, whereby He is circumscribed, but He Himself is simple and uncircumscribed in Divinity!

*Troparion:* Brought to naught are the phantasms and sorceries...

...of the fighter against Christ; for equal unto the pagans did this writer appear in his frenzy, who unrighteously rejected also the voices of the Prophets!

*Troparion:* Thy secret, all-defiled, and soul-destroying teachings, what tongue can declare? Or the divination of thy sorcery, O falsely-named John, forerunner of the Antichrist of Satan![^911]

*Troparion:* It befitted thee not, O lawless one, to be called by such a name, but rather Pythagoras, and Kronos, and Apollo, or some other of the gods, whose manner of life thou didst emulate, delighting in their impurities![^912]

*Glory... Triadikon:* Unto the Co-eternal, All-powerful, Incomprehensible Trinity, all ye faithful, unto the Father, the Son, and the Spirit let us bow down; and in theology unconfusedly crying aloud: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, O God!

*Both now... Theotokion:* All-hymned, most glorious Virgin, Mother and Theotokos, deliver from grievous transgressions those who honor thy most pure childbirth; for no other help besides thee have we acquired, O Bride of God!

*Ode 8. Heirmos: "Him Whom the heavenly hosts glorify":*  
Prophetically let us rejoice and be glad, all ye faithful, mystically; for this is the day wherein Christ the Word gave His raiment unto the Church!

*Troparion:* In martial array they set themselves against the form of Christ, with one soul, Lyzikos and John, a yoke of Belial, hewing the Church with the ax of malice!

*Troparion:* Who shall not weep over the great audacity of Lyzikos and John, beholding the divine form which was upon the Bronze Gate of the Palace being stoned by lawless men through the teaching of John?[^913]

*Troparion:* How didst thou not understand, O blind man all-wretched, darkened in mind, seeing the sky adorned with the delineation of Christ; but thou thyself didst hold Jewish mindedness!

*Troparion:* Thou didst think utterly to destroy from the divine Churches the flesh-wrought form of the Lord and of all the Saints; but divine grace destroyed thy tyranny!

*Troparion:* Unto the sacred relics of the Saints and unto their Icons, fierce Lyzikos together with John expressly commanded not to bow down, speaking lawlessly, the apostates from piety![^914]

*Triadikon:* Honoring the all-effecting Godhead in three Persons, all of us piously, let us glorify unto ages of ages the beginningless Father, the co-beginningless Word, and the co-shining Spirit!

*Theotokion:* A sure bridge for Christians, the boast of the faithful, and refuge, O Sovereign Lady Theotokos, thou art the sole helper of all, and the one who saves from perils!

*Ode 9. Heirmos: "A conception without seed":*  
Clap your hands, ye nations! Make haste, ye choirs of Fathers! And ye ascetics who are in the mountains, assemble; come, ye who were exiled of old by deceitful and impious John, to expose his sorceries and enchantments!

*Troparion:* Rejoice, O wilderness, and all the inhabited world! All ye mountains, drop down sweetness, ye hills, be glad; for Christ the Word hath given peace unto those on earth, and unity of faith unto the divine Churches!

*Troparion:* The God of consecrations hath now boldly proclaimed, most holy Christ, strengthening today the divine Teachers with boldness to speak, that His condescension and Incarnation be surely depicted upon the Icon!

*Troparion:* O longsuffering Lord, how marvelous are Thy works! Who can recount Thy love for mankind? How, beholding priests and ascetics slain according to Thine image, didst Thou not consume the deceitful ones with fire, but didst endure being insulted?[^915]

*Troparion:* Thou Who didst establish the immovable Church, O Lord, and the gates of hades could not prevail against her, do Thou Thyself grant Thy peace unto Thy people, that honoring Thee, we may all bow down and glorify Thee in one doxology!

*Troparion:* Accursed be they who honor not the delineations of Thy flesh, O Master, before all others John, together with Antony, and Theodore, and impious Theodotos, and the other destroyers of the faith![^916]

*Troparion:* Thou Who gavest Thy peace unto the Apostles, O Master, grant now also tranquility unto all, gathering with Thy hand those who are scattered, and assemble them like spiritual sheep into the sheepfold of Thy holy Church!

*Glory... Triadikon:* I glorify the Godhead of the Father, the Son, and the Spirit, one nature in three Hypostases, an indivisible essence, distinct in Persons, of one sovereignty, all-effecting, perfect, primal, upholding all things!

*Both now... Theotokion:* O Help of all, and protection, and shelter, Theotokos, show forth that thou art able to pray for all who flee unto thee, and that thou drivest away the impious by the power of thy Son, for as Mother thou canst do all things!

*And when we reach the appointed place, we say the Troparion:*  
*To Thy most pure image (see fol. 307);[^917] Glory... Both now... Tone 2:*

*Troparion, Tone 2:* The choir of the Prophets, with Moses and Aaron, is glad today with joy; for bringing the end of prophecy, the Cross shines forth, upon which Thou didst save us. By their prayers, O Christ God, save our souls!

*And immediately, the Prologue.*

## The Conciliar Decree of the Holy Seventh Ecumenical Council. Bless, Father.[^918]

*The due annual thanksgiving unto God, on the day wherein we received the Church of God, with the exposition of the dogmas of piety, and the shaming of the malice of the impious.*

Following the prophetic utterances, and conforming ourselves unto the apostolic teachings, and being instructed by the evangelical narratives, we celebrate the Day of Dedication.[^919] For Isaiah said: *Keep dedication toward God, ye islands* (Isa. 41:1), enigmatically signifying the churches from among the Gentiles. Now the churches were not simply the structures and embellishments of temples, but the fulness of those who practice piety within them, and wherewith they serve the Godhead with hymns and doxologies.

And the Apostle, teaching this very thing, commands us to walk in newness of life (Rom. 6:4); and if anyone be a new creature in Christ, to be renewed (2 Cor. 5:17).

And the words of the Lord also indicate the prophetic intention: *It was,* He says, *the Feast of Dedication in Jerusalem, and it was winter* (John 10:22). Either a spiritual winter, wherein the Jewish race bound the sickle of foul murder and turmoil against the common Savior; or that which grieves the bodily senses by the change of the air unto coldness. And there was indeed upon us also a winter, not accidental, but truly a great winter of malice, pouring forth cruelty. But there hath blossomed forth for us by the grace of God an eternal spring, wherein we have come together to produce a thankful harvest in good deeds unto God!

So that we may say the words of the Psalm: *Summer and spring, Thou hast formed them; remember this* (Ps. 73[74]:17–18). For in truth the enemies who reproached the Lord, and who dishonored His holy veneration in the holy Icons, who were haughty and exalted in impiety, God cast them down with wonders, and trod underfoot upon the earth the insolence of their apostasy!

Nor did He despise the voice of those who cry aloud unto Him: *Remember, O Lord, the reproach of Thy servants, which I have held in my bosom, of many nations, wherewith Thine enemies have reproached, O Lord, wherewith they have reproached the footsteps of Thine Anointed* (Ps. 88[89]:51–52).[^920] Now the recompense of Christ was those who were redeemed by His death and who believed in Him, both by the word of the Preaching and by the depiction of the Icons, whereby the great work of the Dispensation...

...is made known unto those who are redeemed: by the Cross, and before the Cross, and after the Cross, and by His Passions and miracles. From which also the imitation of His Passions passes over unto the Apostles, and thence unto the Martyrs, and through them it extends even unto the Confessors and Ascetics.

Remembering this reproach, therefore, wherewith the enemies of the Lord reproached, wherewith they reproached the recompense of His Christ, our God, being appeased by His compassion and inclined by the prayers of His Mother, and furthermore by those of the Apostles and of all the Saints who were likewise insulted together with Him and dishonored in the Icons; that just as they suffered in the flesh, so also, as was fitting, they who shared in the insults against the venerable Icons should be judged at last; when He willed it, He hath accomplished today a second time that which He performed at first!

For at first indeed, after a certain time of many years of humiliation and dishonor of the holy Icons, He restored them unto His piety;[^921] and now, which is the second time, after nearly thirty years of affliction, He hath wrought for us unworthy ones a change from evil days, and deliverance for those in sorrow, and the proclamation of piety, and the confirmation of the veneration of Icons, and a festival bearing unto us all things conducive unto salvation![^922]

For upon the Icons we behold the Master's Passions for our sake: the Cross, the Tomb, hades slain and destroyed, the contests of the Martyrs, their crowns, and salvation itself, which our first Contest-master, Contest-giver, and Crowner wrought in the midst of the earth! This celebration do we observe today; and rejoicing and being glad therein with prayers and supplications, let us cry aloud with psalms and hymns:  
*Outside, thrice:*

*Who is so great a god as our God? Thou art our God, Who alone doest wonders!* (Ps. 76[77]:14).

For from the abusers of Thy glory Thou hast humbled the rulers, and those who insulted the Icons Thou hast shown forth as wretched fugitives!

Now thanksgiving unto God and the Master's victory over the adversaries belong unto all; but the contests and struggles against the iconoclasts, another and more extensive treatise and narrative shall show forth. As in a certain rest after wandering in the wilderness, standing in possession of the spiritual Jerusalem, in a certain imitation of Moses, and yet more by divine command (cf. Deut. 27:1–8), as upon a certain pillar composed of the greatest stones, and adapted for the reception of writing for the hearts of the brethren: the blessings which are due unto the keepers of the Law, and the curses which the transgressors bring upon themselves, we have deemed it righteous and incumbent upon us to write down. Therefore let us say these things:  
*Outside:*

Unto those who confess the bodily coming of the Word of God, in word with the mouth, in heart, and...

...in mind, and in writing and by Icons:  
*Memory eternal! (Thrice)*

Unto those who know that of one and the same Hypostasis of Christ, in different essences, there is that which is created and uncreated, visible and invisible, passible and impassible, circumscribed and uncircumscribed; and who ascribe the uncreated and what is fitting unto the divine essence, while confessing the others and the circumscribed according to human nature, and depicting it in word:  
*Memory eternal! (Thrice)*

Unto those who believe and proclaim, or preach the Good Tidings, words in writings and deeds in depictions, and that both accomplish one and the same benefit: the preaching through words, and the confirmation of the truth through Icons:  
*Memory eternal! (Thrice)*

Unto those who know and proclaim that by the word the lips are sanctified, and likewise the hearers by reason of the word; and that in like manner by reason of the venerable Icons the eyes of those who behold them are sanctified, and through them the mind is elevated unto the vision of God, as also by divine churches, sacred vessels, and other sacred offices:  
*Memory eternal! (Thrice)*

Unto those who know that the Rod, and the Tablets, the Ark, and the Candlestick, and the Table, and the Censer, prefigured and foreshadowed the Virgin and Theotokos Mary; and that while these things indeed prefigured her, she was not those things; but she was a Maiden, and remains a Virgin after the birth of God; and who therefore rather depict this Maiden in likenesses, or foreshadow her in outlines:  
*Memory eternal! (Thrice)*

Unto those who know, accept, and believe the prophetic visions, even as the Godhead Itself formed and outlined them, which the choir of the Prophets, having seen, declared; and who hold the tradition that hath passed down to the Apostles and to the Fathers, both written and unwritten, and therefore depict holy things and honor them:  
*Memory eternal! (Thrice)*

Unto those who understand Moses saying: *Take heed unto yourselves, for on the day when the Lord God spoke at Horeb on the mountain, ye heard the voice of words, but saw no similitude* (Deut. 4:12, 15); and who know how to answer rightly: If we see anything, we truly see it, even as the Son of Thunder taught us: *That which was from the beginning, which we have heard, which we have seen, which we have looked upon with our eyes, and our hands have handled, of the Word of life; and these things we testify* (1 John 1:1–2);[^923] and again, as the other disciples of the Word said: *We ate and drank with Him* (Acts 10:41), not only before the Passion, but also after the Passion and Resurrection: in order that by God there might be shown unto those confirmed in the Law a sanctification, and a teaching toward grace; and that in the former indeed was the invisible, but in the latter also the visible and...

...sensible; and who therefore depict and bow down before things seen and sensible:  
*Memory eternal! (Thrice) Outside.*

As the Prophets saw, as the Apostles taught, as the Church received, as the Teachers commanded, as the inhabited world agrees, as grace shone forth, as truth was shown, as falsehood perished, as wisdom prevailed, as Christ ordained: thus do we mind, thus do we speak, thus do we proclaim Christ our true God, and His Saints, honoring them in words, in writings, in thoughts, in sacrifices, in temples, in depictions; bowing down before Him and honoring Him as God and Master, and honoring them for the sake of the common Master, as His closest servants, and rendering unto them relative veneration![^924]

*This is the faith of the Apostles! This is the faith of the Fathers! This is the faith of the Orthodox! This is the faith which hath established the universe!*

Concerning these Preachers of piety, both fraternally and filial-lovingly, unto the glory and honor of piety for which they contended, let us glorify them and say:  
*Upon the earth:*

Unto Germanus, Tarasius, Nicephorus, and Methodius, as truly the Hierarchs of God, and champions and teachers of Orthodoxy:  
*Memory eternal! (Thrice)*[^925]

Unto Ignatius, Photius, Stephen, Antony, and Nicholas, most holy and Orthodox Patriarchs:  
*Memory eternal! (Thrice)*[^926]

All things written or spoken against the holy Patriarchs Germanus, Tarasius, Nicephorus, and Methodius, Ignatius, Photius, Stephen, Antony, and Nicholas:  
*Anathema! (Thrice)*

All things renovated or hereafter wrought contrary to the Church's tradition and teaching and the depiction of the holy and ever-memorable Fathers:  
*Anathema! (Thrice)*

Unto Stephen the Venerable Martyr, the New Confessor:  
*Memory eternal! (Thrice)*[^927]

Unto Euthymius, Theophilus, and Emilian, ever-memorable Confessors and Archbishops:  
*Memory eternal! (Once)*[^928]

Unto Theophylact, Peter, Michael, and Joseph, blessed Metropolitans:  
*Memory eternal! (Once)*[^929]

Unto John, Nicholas, and George, thrice-blessed Confessors and Archbishops, and unto all the Bishops of like mind with them:  
*Memory eternal! (Thrice)*[^930]

Unto Theodore, all-venerable Abbot of the Studion:  
*Memory eternal! (Thrice)*[^931]

Unto Isaac the Wonderworker, and Joannicius the Most Prophetic:  
*Memory eternal! (Thrice)*[^932] Unto Hilarion, most venerable Archimandrite and Abbot of the Dalmatoi:
*Memory eternal! (Thrice)*[^933]

Unto Symeon, most venerable Stylite:  
*Memory eternal! (Thrice)*[^934]

Unto Theophanes, most venerable Abbot of the Great Field:  
*Memory eternal! (Thrice)*[^935]

These blessings of the Fathers pass over from them unto us their sons who emulate their piety; and in like manner do the curses fall upon the apostates and despisers of the Master's commandments. Therefore let all of us together, as many as are the fulness of piety, pronounce upon them the curse which they have laid upon themselves!

Unto those who accept in word the bodily dispensation of the Word of God, but do not accept to behold this through Icons, and who therefore feign in words to accept that He is depicted, but in reality cast away our salvation:  
*Anathema! (Once)*

Unto those who maliciously appropriate the title of the uncircumscribed, and who therefore refuse to depict Christ our true God Who took part in flesh and blood near unto us, and who show Him forth as a mere phantasm:  
*Anathema! (Once)*

Unto those who accept the prophetic visions, even if unwillingly, yet do not accept the depictions that appeared unto them of the Holy One even before the Incarnation of the Word; but either babble that the incomprehensible and invisible essence itself appeared unto those who saw it, or agree that these were true icons and types and outlines revealed unto the beholders, yet do not accept to depict in icons the incarnate Word and His Passions for our sake:  
*Anathema! (Thrice)*

Unto those who hear the Lord saying: *For if ye had believed Moses, ye would have believed Me* (John 5:46), and the rest; and who understand Moses saying: *A Prophet shall the Lord our God raise up unto you like unto me* (Deut. 18:15); and who then say that they accept indeed the Prophet, yet do not introduce by depictions the grace of prophecy and universal salvation: how He was seen, how He dwelt among men, how He healed diseases and sicknesses with better cures, how He was crucified, how He was buried, how He arose, how He suffered and did all things for our sake; unto those, therefore, who do not accept to behold these universal and saving works upon Icons, neither honoring them nor bowing down before them:  
*Anathema! (Thrice)*

Unto those who persist in the iconoclast heresy, or rather the Christ-fighting apostasy, and who are willing neither to be led unto their salvation by the Mosaic legislation, nor choose to live in grace according to the apostolic teachings, nor...

...to be persuaded by the teachings and admonitions [of the Fathers] to turn away from their deception, nor to be entreated by the agreement of the Churches of God throughout the whole world, but liken themselves unto the portion of the Jews and Greeks alone; for that which the latter blaspheme against the Archetype directly, these do not blush to dare against the very Prototype through His Icon; who therefore cling inflexibly unto this deception and have stopped their ears to every divine word and spiritual instruction, seeing they are already rotten and have cut themselves off from the common Body of the Church:  
*Anathema! (Thrice)*[^936]

Unto those who introduce certain vain fancies into the ineffable dispensation in the flesh of our Lord and God and Savior Jesus Christ, and say or hold that the humanity of Christ is worshipped with servile homage by the intangible Godhead, and that it acquired an everlasting servitude as essential and inalienable:[^937]  
*Anathema! (Thrice)*

Unto those who do not with all reverence employ the distinction of the mind solely for the showing forth of the difference of the two natures ineffably met together in Christ and united in Him without confusion and without division; but employ that same distinction and say that the assumed nature is other not only in nature but also in dignity, and that it serves God and offers servile worship, and renders diligent honor as a debt, just as the ministering spirits serve and bow down servilely, and who teach that by its proper assumed nature it is High Priest, and not the God-Word inasmuch as He became man, and who through such notions dare apostolically to divide the one Christ our Lord and God:[^938]  
*Anathema! (Thrice)*

Unto those who say that at the time of the world-saving Passion of our Lord and God and Savior Jesus Christ, the sacrifice of His precious Body and Blood offered for our salvation—as by an High Priest acting according to what is human for our sake, seeing that He is Himself both God, and Priest, and Sacrifice, according to Gregory the renowned in Theology[^939]—was indeed offered by Himself unto God the Father, but was not received as God together with the Father by the Only-begotten Himself and the Holy Spirit, so that thereby they alienate from the God-befitting equal essence and dignity God the Word Himself, and the Comforter Spirit Who is consubstantial and co-glorified with Him:[^940]  
*Anathema! (Thrice)*

Unto those who do not accept that the Sacrifice offered every day by those who have received from Christ the sacred administration of the Divine Mysteries is offered unto the Holy Trinity, as being utterly in opposition to the sacred and divine Fathers, Basil and Chrysostom, with whom...

...agree also the rest of the God-bearing Fathers in their words and writings:[^941]  
*Anathema! (Thrice)*

Unto those who hear indeed the Savior saying concerning the sacred administration of the Divine Mysteries delivered by Him: *Do this in remembrance of Me* (Luke 22:19), but do not accept the remembrance rightly, and dare to say that the sacrifice offered every day by those who minister the Divine Mysteries—as our Savior and Master of all delivered—renews only in appearance and figuratively the Sacrifice of His own Body and Blood offered upon the precious Cross by our Savior for the common redemption and purification of human nature; and who therefore introduce this sacrifice as being another from that which was accomplished from the beginning by the Savior, and referring to that one only in appearance and figuratively, as they that make light of the fearful and divine mystery of the sacred ministration, through which we receive the earnest of the life to come, and this though our divine Father John Chrysostom asserts the unchanging nature of the sacrifice and declares it to be one and the same in many commentaries upon the sayings of the great Paul:[^942]  
*Anathema! (Thrice)*

Unto those who surmise and introduce temporal intervals into the reconciliation of human nature unto the divine and blessed nature of the life-originating and all-spotless Trinity, and who first lay down that we were reconciled unto the only-begotten Word from the very assumption of our nature, and afterwards unto God the Father by the saving Passion of Christ the Savior; and who divide the indivisible, whereas the divine and blessed Father teaches that for the sake of the mystery of the whole dispensation the Only-begotten reconciled us by Himself, and by Himself and in Himself unto God the Father, and consequently in every way unto the all-holy and life-creating Spirit also; as inventors of novel inquiries and alien notions:[^943]  
*Anathema! (Thrice)*

Unto Anastasius, Constantine, and Nicetas, the ringleaders of the heresies under the Isaurians, as abominable ones and leaders of perdition:[^944]  
*Anathema! (Thrice)*

Unto Theodotus, Antony, and John, mutually succeeding one another in evils, successors in impiety:[^945]  
*Anathema! (Thrice)*

Unto Paul who turned into Saul, and unto Theodore called Gastes, and Stephen Molites, and furthermore unto Theodore Krithinos, and Laloudios Leo, and beside them, if any be like unto those aforesaid in impiety, in whatever catalogue of the clergy, or rank, or dignity, or occupation he may be found, unto all these who abide in their impiety:[^946]  
*Anathema! (Thrice)* Unto Gerontios, who took refuge in Sougdaia, and poured out the poison of his hateful heresy upon Crete, and styled himself wretched, regarding the corruption of the saving dispensation of Christ in his perverse teachings and writings, and unto them that contend together with him:[^947]
*Anathema! (Thrice)*

*Chapter 33: Of John Italus.*[^948]

Unto those who attempt to introduce any kind of investigation and teaching into the ineffable dispensation in the flesh of our Savior and God, and seek after what manner God the Word Himself was united unto the human compound, and by what manner of reason He deified the assumed flesh, and who attempt with dialectical terms—nature and position—to dispute concerning the supernatural new doctrine of the two natures of God and Man:[^949]  
*Anathema! (Thrice)*

Unto those who promise indeed to act piously, but shamelessly or rather impiously introduce into the Orthodox and Catholic Church the impious teachings of the Greeks concerning human souls, and heaven, and earth, and the rest of creation:[^950]  
*Anathema! (Thrice)*

Unto those who prefer the vain so-called wisdom of the profane philosophers, and follow their teachers, and accept the transmigration of human souls, or that like unto irrational animals they perish and are reduced unto nothing, and who on this account reject the resurrection, the judgment, and the final retribution of life:[^951]  
*Anathema! (Thrice)*

Unto those who teach that matter is unoriginate, and that Ideas are co-eternal with the Fashioner of all and God; and that heaven and earth and the rest of creation are everlasting and without beginning, and abide unchangeable; and who enact laws contrary to Him Who said: *Heaven and earth shall pass away, but My words shall not pass away* (Matt. 24:35); and who speak vainly concerning the earth, and bring down a divine curse upon their own heads:[^952]  
*Anathema! (Thrice)*

Unto those who say that the Greek sages and the foremost of the heresiarchs—who were placed under anathema by the holy Seven Ecumenical Councils and by all the Fathers who shone forth in Orthodoxy as alien unto the Catholic Church because of the filth and impurity of their verbiage—are far better, both here and at the future judgment, than pious and Orthodox men who have sinned in some other way through human passion or ignorance:[^953]  
*Anathema! (Thrice)* Unto those who do not accept with a pure and simple faith and with a whole-hearted spirit the marvelous miracles of our Savior and God, and of our Lady the Theotokos who bore Him, and of the rest of the saints; but attempt by sophistical proofs and words to show them impossible, or interpret them according to their own opinion, and configure them according to their own mind:[^954]
*Anathema! (Once)*

Unto those who pursue Greek learning, and do not study therein for education only, but follow their vain opinions and believe them as true, and so cleave unto them as having certainty, so as to lead others unto them, sometimes secretly and sometimes openly, and to teach them without hesitation:[^955]  
*Anathema! (Once)*

Unto those who together with other mythical inventions remodel creation of themselves and over us, and accept Platonic Forms of essences as true, and say that material substance is formed from the forms of essences, and openly reject the sovereign will of the Fashioner Who brought all things from non-existence into being, and Who as Creator sovereignly and Masterfully appointed the beginning and end for all:[^956]  
*Anathema! (Once)*

Unto those who say that in the final and general resurrection men will rise and be judged with other bodies, and not with those in which they ended the present life, as though these had rotted and perished; and who utter vain and empty babblings against Christ our God Himself, and His Disciples, and our Teachers who have thus taught, that with the same bodies wherein men lived, with them also shall they receive retribution; and moreover when the great Apostle Paul in his discourse on the resurrection showed forth the truth extensively by proofs (1 Cor. 15), and exposed those that thought otherwise as foolish; unto those therefore who enact laws contrary to his commands and teachings:[^957]  
*Anathema! (Once)*

Unto those who accept and spread the vain and Greek words that there is a pre-existence of souls, and that not all things were made and brought out of non-existence; that there is an end unto torment, or a restitution of creation and of human affairs; and by such words introduce that the Kingdom of Heaven is altogether dissoluble and transitory, which Christ our God Himself taught and delivered to be eternal and unsearchable, and as we have received through all the Old and New Scripture that both torment is unending and the Kingdom everlasting; and who by such words destroy themselves and become the cause of eternal condemnation unto others:[^958]  
*Anathema! (Thrice)* Unto those who have learned impiously from the false-monk Nilus, and unto all that have communion with them:[^959]
*Anathema! (Thrice)*

Unto those who wrongly receive the divine voices of the holy Teachers of God's Church, and attempt otherwise to interpret and pervert that which was spoken clearly and distinctly in them by the grace of the Holy Spirit:[^960]  
*Anathema! (Thrice)*

Unto those who accept the voice of the true God, our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ: *My Father is greater than I* (John 14:28), and interpret it, together with the other expositions of the holy Fathers, as spoken according to His humanity in which He suffered, as the holy Fathers clearly proclaim in many of their God-inspired sayings; and furthermore unto those who say that Christ suffered in His own flesh:[^961]  
*Memory eternal! (Thrice)*

Unto those who understand and proclaim the deification of the assumed nature to be a transformation of human nature into Godhead; and who do not understand that from that same union the Body of the Lord indeed partook of divine dignity and majesty, and is worshipped with one adoration together with God the Word Who assumed it, and is of one honor, of one glory, life-creating, of equal glory with God the Father and the all-holy Spirit, and sharing the same throne, yet that this Body is not consubstantial with God, seeing it remains distinct in the natural properties of the Creator, being circumscribed and possessing the other properties visible in the human nature of Christ; but blend it into the essence of the Godhead, so as to be exalted out of this, or say that the Incarnation of the Lord and His Passions were an appearance and not truth, or that the Only-begotten suffered in His Godhead:[^962]  
*Anathema! (Thrice)*

Unto those who say that the flesh of the Lord, exalted by that same union and set above every honor, as having become deified by the supreme union, unalterably, unchangeably, without confusion, without transmutation, on account of the hypostatic union, and abiding undivided and inseparable from God the Word Who assumed it, is honored with equal glory with Him, and is worshipped with one adoration, and is seated in imperial and divine places at the right hand of God the Father, as being enriched with the exaltations of the Godhead, while the proper characteristics of the natures are preserved:[^963]  
*Memory eternal! (Thrice)*

Unto those who reject the voices of the holy Fathers that were in harmony concerning the establishment of the right dogmas of God's Church—of Athanasius, Cyril, Ambrose, Amphilochius the God-befitting, of Leo the most holy Archbishop of Old Rome, and the rest; and moreover unto those who do not kiss the acts of the Ecumenical Councils, I say the Fourth and the Sixth:[^964]  
*Anathema! (Thrice)*

Unto those who do not accept the voice of the true God and our Savior Jesus Christ:...

...*My Father is greater than I* (John 14:28), as the saints interpreted this in diverse ways: some indeed saying that it was spoken according to His Godhead, by reason of His caused generation from the Father; while others saying it was according to the natural properties of the flesh assumed by Him and hypostatically united to His Godhead, that is: being created, circumscribed, mortal, and the rest of the natural and blameless passions, on account of which the Lord said that He was less than the Father; but who say that such a voice is to be understood only when in subtle consideration the flesh is understood as separated from the Godhead, as though it were not even united; and unto those who do not accept such a saying according to subtle consideration of division—as was spoken by the holy Fathers at that time when servitude and ignorance are mentioned, as not enduring that the deified and equal flesh of Christ should be insulted by such words; but who say that according to subtle consideration of the assumption the natural properties are not truly existing in the Lord's flesh in the hypostasis of His Godhead and abiding inseparable; and who teach these things concerning non-hypostatic and false things, which apply to hypostatic and true things:[^965]  
*Anathema! (Thrice)*

Unto Constantine the Bulgarian, who was Metropolitan of Corfu, who wickedly and impiously taught concerning the voice of the true God and our Savior Jesus Christ: *My Father is greater than I* (John 14:28); and who did not believe and say that although indeed according to another pious understanding this is received from the holy God-bearing Fathers, yet also according to the very flesh assumed from the holy Virgin and Theotokos by the Only-begotten Son of God and made subsistent in His Godhead, without confusion, having with inseparable union those same properties according to which the Lord called the Father greater than Himself, in one adoration with His assumed nature, as deified and of equal glory, He is worshipped together and glorified together with the Father Himself and the All-Holy Spirit; but who objected that it was not fitting that such a voice should be understood when the Lord is understood as one hypostasis having two united natures, but only when in subtle consideration the flesh is taken as separated from the Godhead and such as to be of any man whatsoever; and this though the most theological Damascene teaches the division in subtle consideration then, when anything is spoken of Christ's flesh that is not abiding, of some natural property, but showing servitude or ignorance; and unto him that would not follow the holy Ecumenical Councils, both the Fourth and the Sixth, which...

...rightly and piously commanded concerning the two natures united without confusion in Christ, and taught the Church of Christ to confess the Orthodox faith; and who thus fell into diverse heresies:[^966]  
*Anathema! (Thrice)*

Unto all that are of like mind with that Constantine the Bulgarian, and are persuaded by his deadly error, and who contend not for the sake of the beloved truth, but that his impiety may be established:[^967]  
*Anathema! (Thrice)*

Unto the most unlearned and false-monk John Eirenikos, and unto the impious writings composed by him, and unto those who kiss these writings, as glorifying and saying that not by reason of the hypostatic and united humanity in our Lord Jesus Christ Himself, the Savior and God, by His Godhead, undivided and inseparable, and without confusion, is His voice in His holy Gospels: *My Father is greater than I* (John 14:28) spoken by Him as perfect Man; but who say that this was spoken by Him according to His humanity only in such wise as when this humanity, stripped bare and in subtle consideration divided in every way from His Godhead, as though it were not united unto Him, is taken as common and ours:[^968]  
*Anathema! (Thrice)*

Unto the assembly raging against the Honorable Icons:[^969]  
*Anathema! (Thrice)*

Unto those who apply sayings from the Divine Scripture concerning idols unto the honorable Icons of Christ our God and of His saints:[^970]  
*Anathema! (Thrice)*

Unto those who knowingly have communion with them that insult and dishonor the Honorable Icons:[^971]  
*Anathema! (Thrice)*

Unto those who say that Christians approach the Icons as unto gods:[^972]  
*Anathema! (Thrice)*

Unto those who say that another beside Christ our God delivered us from the deception of idols:[^973]  
*Anathema! (Thrice)*

Unto those who dare to say that the Catholic Church once received idols, as putting to shame the whole foundation and insulting the Christian Faith:[^974]  
*Anathema! (Thrice)*

If anyone avenges someone who was of the Christian-accusing heresy, or who ended his life therein:[^975]  
*Anathema! (Thrice)*

If anyone does not bow down before our Lord Jesus Christ circumscribed upon an Icon according to His humanity:  
*Let him be Anathema! (Thrice)*[^976]

Unto all heretics:  
*Anathema!*  
Unto Barlaam and Akindynos, and unto their followers and successors:[^977]  
*Anathema! (Thrice)*

*Chapters Against Barlaam and Akindynos.*[^978]

Unto those who think with them, and say that the Light that shone forth from the Lord at His divine Transfiguration was at one time a phantom and a creature and an apparition that appeared for a little while and was quickly dissolved, and at another time the very essence of God, as into the very...

...most contrary absurdities, and utterly cast themselves down into impossibilities; and on the one hand, raving with the madness of Arius, cut the one Godhead and one God into created and uncreated; and on the other hand, agreeing with the Messalian impiety, say that the divine essence is visible; and do not confess, according to the holy God-inspired theologies of the saints and the pious churchly understanding, that that most divine Light is neither a creature nor the essence of God, but uncreated and natural grace, illumination, and energy, inseparably and ever-existing from that same divine essence:[^979]  
*Anathema! (Thrice)*

Furthermore, unto those who think with them and say that God has no natural energy, but is essence alone; and who consider the divine essence and the divine energy to be in no way different, and that there is understood between them no distinction whatever, but that the same is called at one time essence and at another time energy; so that they foolishly take away the divine essence itself in every way, and reduce it unto non-existence; for the Teachers of the Church say that only non-existence is deprived of energy; and who are sick with the disease of Sabellius, and dare now to renew in the divine essence and energy his ancient division, confusion, and blending in the three hypostases of the Godhead, and similarly and impiously blend these together; and do not confess, according to the God-inspired theologies of the saints and the pious understanding of the Church, both essence in God and the essential energy thereof, as many others of the saints and especially those of the holy and Ecumenical Sixth Council clearly showed forth concerning the two energies of Christ, divine and human, and the two wills, having composed all this; and who are not willing to understand that as the union of the divine essence and energy is unconfused, so also their distinction is inseparable, in another manner, and especially as cause and caused, and incommunicable and communicable—the one indeed of essence, and the other of energy; unto those therefore who think such impious things:[^980]  
*Anathema! (Thrice)*

Furthermore, unto those who agree with them and say that every natural power and energy of the Tri-hypostatic Godhead is created, so that from this they are compelled in every way to proclaim the very divine essence also to be created; for according to the saints a created energy manifests a created nature, but an uncreated energy outlines an uncreated essence; and who from this are already judged in every way to fall into godlessness...

...and to append Greek fable-telling and the worship of creatures unto the holy and spotless Christian Faith; and who do not confess, according to the holy God-inspired theologies of the saints and the pious churchly understanding, that every natural power and energy of the Tri-hypostatic Godhead is uncreated:[^981]  
*Anathema! (Thrice)*

Furthermore, unto those who agree with them and say that by reason of these things there is in every way a certain composition in God; and who do not believe the teaching of the saints who teach that no composition whatsoever from what is natural exists in the divine nature, and who from this sally forth to slander not only us, but also all the saints who clearly teach in many places and many times that God is simple and uncompounded, and that the distinction between the divine essence and energy in no way whatever harms the divine simplicity; for they would not have begun so clearly to theologize things contrary to themselves; unto those therefore who speak such vain words, and do not confess, according to the God-inspired theologies of the saints and the pious churchly understanding, that with this God-befitting distinction divine simplicity is right well preserved:[^982]  
*Anathema! (Thrice)*

Furthermore, unto those who think with them and say that the name 'Godhead' is applied unto the divine essence alone; and who do not confess, according to the God-inspired theologies of the saints and the pious understanding of the Church, that this name is applied no less unto the divine energy, and so again in all ways honor the one Godhead of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, whether someone calls their essence or their energy 'Godhead,' as the divine mystagogues taught us:[^983]  
*Anathema! (Thrice)*

Furthermore, unto those who think with them and say that the divine essence is communicable, who do not blush to introduce into our Church the Messalian impiety of those who anciently were sick with such an opinion; and who do not confess, according to the God-inspired theologies of the saints and the pious churchly understanding, that it is incomprehensible and in every way incommunicable, but that divine grace and energy is communicable:[^984]  
*Anathema! (Thrice)*

Unto all their impious words and writings:[^985]  
*Anathema! (Thrice)*

Unto Isaac called Argyros, who throughout his whole life was sick with the disease of Barlaam and Akindynos, even if at the end of his life, as also previously many times, he promised return and repentance unto the Church of Christ, yet remained in impiety, and wickedly poured out his soul in the confession of heresy:[^986]  
*Anathema! (Thrice)* Unto Arius, the first fighter against God, and the ringleader of heresies:[^987]
*Anathema! (Thrice)*

Unto Peter the Fuller the foolish, who said: *Holy Immortal, Who wast crucified for us*:[^988]  
*Anathema! (Thrice)*

Unto Nestorius the God-hated, who said that the Holy Trinity is passible:[^989]  
*Anathema! (Thrice)*

Unto Valentinus, the impious and foolish:[^990]  
*Anathema! (Thrice)*

Unto Paul of Samosata, and Theodotion, his fellow-conspirator and like-minded one, together with the other foolish Nestorius:[^991]  
*Anathema! (Thrice)*

Unto Peter the wretched heretic, and Peter named the Wolf, and unto Eutyches and Sabellius who think evilly:[^992]  
*Anathema! (Thrice)*

Unto Jacob the Armenian Tzanzalus, Dioscorus Patriarch of Alexandria, and Severus the impious, together with Sergius, Paul, and Pyrrhus who were like-minded, with Sergius the disciple of Peter the Wolf:[^993]  
*Anathema! (Thrice)*

Unto all Eutychians, and Monothelites, Jacobites, and Artzibourites, and simply unto all heretics:[^994]  
*Anathema! (Thrice)*

*Here takes place the commemoration of departed Emperors, who were Orthodox.*[^995]

Unto Michael, our Orthodox Emperor, and Theodora, most blessed Empress:[^996]  
*Memory eternal! (Thrice)*

Unto Andronikos of ever-memorable memory, our blessed Emperor Palaeologus, who convoked the first Synod against Barlaam, and manfully stood as defender of the Church of Christ and of that sacred Synod, and by deeds and words and marvelous instructions from his own lips confirmed the evangelical and apostolic commands, and destroyed and proclaimed against the very heresies, writings, and idle fancies of the aforesaid Barlaam against our Orthodox Faith, and who in his sacred struggles and contest for grace blessedly ended this life, and passed over unto that better and most blessed repose:[^997]  
*Memory eternal! (Thrice)*

Unto Gregory, the most holy Metropolitan of Thessalonica, who synodically in the Great Church destroyed Barlaam and Akindynos, the ringleaders and inventors of new heresies, together with their wicked fellowship—who dared to call the natural and indivisible energy and power of God, and simply all the natural properties of the Holy Trinity together, created things, and the unapproachable Light of the Godhead that shone forth on the Mount from Christ a created Godhead, and who began evilly to introduce again into the Church Platonic forms and Greek fables...[^998]

...and into the Church of Christ; and who very wisely and manfully championed the common, true, and unerring commands of the Church of Christ concerning the Godhead, both by writings, and words, and discourses; and who proclaimed, according to the Divine Scriptures, not one Godhead only, but one God in three Hypostases, active, willing, all-powerful, uncreated in all respects; and who preached the Theologians and expositors of these things—I mean Athanasius, Basil, Gregory, and John Chrysostom,[^999] and Cyril in addition to them, and Maximus the most wise, and the God-proclaiming [John] of Damascus; and who showed himself both in words and deeds to be not only [a follower] of these, but also of the other Fathers and Teachers of Christ's Church, a companion, fellow-traveler, harmonizer, zealous confessor of all these:  
*Memory eternal! (Thrice)*

Unto all who contend together with this ever-memorable and blessed Emperor for Orthodoxy, and who together with him, both by words and discourses, writings and teachings, and by every word and deed, manfully championed the Church of Christ; and who together exposed and drove out of the Church the wicked and multiform heresies of Barlaam and Akindynos and those of like mind with them; and who proclaimed the apostolic and patristic commands of piety; and because of this suffered evil report from the evil-minded, being slandered and abused together with our sacred Theologians, God-bearing Fathers, and Teachers:[^1000]  
*Memory eternal! (Thrice)*

Unto those who confess one God in three Hypostases, all-powerful, not only uncreated according to essence and hypostasis, but also according to energy; and who say that the Divine energy indeed proceeds from the Divine essence, yet proceeds indivisibly; for by proceeding they signify an ineffable distinction, but by indivisibility they demonstrate a supernatural union, even as the holy Sixth Ecumenical Council showed:[^1001]  
*Memory eternal! (Thrice)*

Unto those who confess that God, even as He is uncreated and without beginning according to essence, so also according to energy, manifestly accepting Him as without beginning not according to time; and who say that according to the Divine essence God is altogether unapproachable and incomprehensible, yet can be partaken of by the worthy according to His Divine and deifying energy, even as the Theologians of the Church say:[^1002]  
*Memory eternal! (Thrice)*

Unto those who confess that the Light which shone forth ineffably upon the Mount of the Lord's Transfiguration is unapproachable light, and great light, and an incomprehensible outpouring of Divine radiance, and ineffable glory, and the all-perfect glory of the Godhead, and...

...and transcendent, and the timeless glory of the Son, and of the Kingdom of God, and true beauty, and that which is beloved concerning the Divine and blessed nature, and the natural glory of God, and the Godhead of the Father and the Spirit shining forth in the Only-begotten Son, as our Divine and God-bearing Fathers said: Athanasius, and Basil the Great, Gregory the Theologian, and John Chrysostom, and furthermore John of Damascus; and who for these reasons glorify this most divine Light as uncreated:[^1003]  
*Memory eternal! (Thrice)*

Unto those who glorify the light of the Lord's Transfiguration as uncreated indeed because of the aforesaid reasons; yet do not say that this is the supersubstantial essence of God, since that remains invisible everywhere and unpartaken of—for *no man hath seen God at any time* (John 1:18), that is to say, as the Theologians state, as He is in His essence; but who rather say that this is the natural glory of the supersubstantial essence, proceeding from it indivisibly, and manifested because of the love of God toward mankind unto those that have purified the mind; and in His own glory our Lord and God shall come at His second and dread Coming to judge the living and the dead, as the Theologians of the Church have said:[^1004]  
*Memory eternal! (Thrice)*

Unto Michael our Orthodox Emperor, and Theodora his holy mother:[^1005]  
*Memory eternal! (Thrice)*

Unto Basil, and Constantine, Leo, and Alexander; Christopher, and Romanus, Constantine, Romanus, Nicephorus, and John; Basil, and Constantine, Andronicus, and Romanus, Michael, Nicephorus, Isaac, Alexius, and John; Manuel, renamed Matthew the Monk in the Divine and Angelic Habit; Isaac, Alexius, and Theodore, who exchanged an earthly kingdom for the Heavenly:[^1006]  
*Memory eternal! (Thrice)*

Unto John Ducas, our ever-memorable Emperor of pious memory, who was likewise renamed Theodore the Monk in the Divine and Angelic Habit:[^1007]  
*Memory eternal! (Thrice)*

Unto Michael Palaeologus the New, our ever-memorable Emperor of pious memory:[^1008]  
*Memory eternal! (Thrice)*

Unto Andronicus Palaeologus, our ever-memorable Emperor of pious memory, renamed Antony the Monk in the Divine and Angelic Habit:[^1009]  
*Memory eternal! (Thrice)*

Unto Andronicus Palaeologus, our ever-memorable, most pious, and Christ-loving Emperor, who died in piety:[^1010]  
*Memory eternal! (Thrice)* Unto John Cantacuzene, our ever-memorable, most pious, and Christ-loving Emperor, who died in piety, renamed Joasaph in the Divine and Angelic Habit:[^1011]
*Memory eternal! (Thrice)*

Unto Eudokia, and Theophano, Theodora, and Helen; Theophano, and Theodora; Catherine, Eudokia, Mary, Irene, and Mary, renamed Xene the Nun in the Divine and Angelic Habit; Euphrosyne, Anna, and Helen, most pious Empresses:[^1012]  
*Memory eternal! (Thrice)*

Unto Irene, our pious and ever-memorable Sovereign Lady of pious memory, renamed Eugenia the Nun in the Divine and Angelic Habit:[^1013]  
*Memory eternal! (Thrice)*

Unto Theodora, our ever-memorable Sovereign Lady of pious memory, renamed Eugenia the Nun in the Divine and Angelic Habit:[^1014]  
*Memory eternal! (Thrice)*

Unto Irene, our ever-memorable Sovereign Lady of pious memory:[^1015]  
*Memory eternal! (Thrice)*

Unto Mary, our ever-memorable Sovereign Lady of pious memory, renamed Xene the Nun in the Divine and Angelic Habit:[^1016]  
*Memory eternal! (Thrice)*

Unto Anna, our ever-memorable Sovereign Lady of pious memory, renamed Anastasia the Nun in the Divine and Angelic Habit, who in deeds and words, with her whole soul strove in life for the stability of the apostolic and patristic ecclesiastical commands, and for the overthrow of the wicked and godless heresy of Barlaam and Akindynos and those of like mind with them:[^1017]  
*Memory eternal! (Thrice)*

Unto Irene, our ever-memorable Sovereign Lady of pious memory, renamed Eugenia the Nun in the Divine and Angelic Habit:[^1018]  
*Memory eternal! (Thrice)*

Unto Germanus, Tarasius, Nicephorus, and Methodius, ever-memorable and blessed Patriarchs:[^1019]  
*Memory eternal! (Thrice)*

Unto Ignatius, Photius, Stephen, and Antony; Nicholas, and Euthymius, Stephen, Tryphon, and Theophylact; Polyeuktos, Antony, Nicholas, Sisinnius, Sergius, Eustathius, Alexius, Michael, John, Constantine, Cosmas, Eustratius, Nicholas, Leo, Michael, Theodore, Luke; Michael, Chariton, Theodotus, Basil, Nicetas, Leontius, Dositheus, Meletius...[^1020]

...Peter, George, Michael, Theodore, John, Maximus, Manuel, Methodius, renamed Acacius the Monk in the Divine and Angelic Habit; Manuel, renamed Matthew the Monk in the Divine and Angelic Habit: Orthodox Patriarchs:[^1021]  
*Memory eternal! (Thrice)*

Unto Germanus, our ever-memorable Patriarch who died in a blessed end, renamed George the Monk in the Divine and Angelic Habit:[^1022]  
*Memory eternal! (Thrice)*

Unto Arsenius, our most holy and ever-memorable Patriarch who died in a blessed end:[^1023]  
*Memory eternal! (Thrice)*

Unto Joseph, our most holy and ever-memorable Patriarch who died in a blessed end:[^1024]  
*Memory eternal! (Thrice)*

Unto Athanasius, our most holy and ever-memorable Patriarch who died in a blessed end:[^1025]  
*Memory eternal! (Thrice)*

Unto Gerasimus, our most holy and ever-memorable Patriarch:[^1026]  
*Memory eternal! (Thrice)*

Unto Isaiah, our most holy Patriarch:[^1027]  
*Memory eternal! (Thrice)*

Unto Isidore, our most holy and ever-memorable Patriarch who died in a blessed end:[^1028]  
*Memory eternal! (Thrice)*

Unto Callistus, our most holy and ever-memorable Patriarch who died in a blessed end:[^1029]  
*Memory eternal! (Thrice)*

Unto Philotheus, our most holy and ever-memorable Patriarch who died in a blessed end, who firmly contended for the Church of Christ and for Her right commands, both in words, and deeds, and discourses, and teachings, and writings:[^1030]  
*Memory eternal! (Thrice)*

Unto Christopher, Theodore, Agapius, and John; Nicholas, Elias, and Theodore, Basil, Peter, Theodosius, Nicephorus, and John, ever-memorable Patriarchs of Antioch:[^1031]  
*Memory eternal! (Thrice)*

Unto Damian, Basil, Constantine, Nicephorus, Leontius, and Sisinnius, Basil, and Joseph; Michael and Christopher; Nicephorus, George, Pantoleon, and Alexander, Cosmas, and Constantine; Theophanes, Peter, John, Nicetas, George, Nicholas, and John, Orthodox Metropolitans:[^1032]  
*Memory eternal! (Thrice)*

Unto Michael, Metrophanes, Meletius, Ignatius, and Maximus, ever-memorable Metropolitans, ancient Fathers:[^1033]  
*Memory eternal! (Thrice) From here takes place the commemoration of the Emperors, and Patriarchs, and all the living. May the Holy Trinity glorify them! Outside.*[^1034]

Instructing ourselves and being strengthened by these struggles and contests and teachings on behalf of piety even unto death, beseeching God, and praying that we may show ourselves imitators of their godly way of life unto the end, that we may be accounted worthy of our petitions, through the compassions and grace of the Great and First High Priest, Christ our true God; through the intercessions of our all-glorious Lady, the Theotokos and Ever-Virgin Mary, the godlike Angels, and of all the saints.[^1035]  
**Amen.**

## Monday of the Second Week of Great Lent

*On that same Sunday of the First Week of Lent, at Vespers, there is no kathisma:*

*On "Lord, I have cried," we set 10 Stichera: 4 Penitential stichera of the Oktoechos in the Tone, which are written: 2 on the Aposticha and 2 at Matins in the sessional hymns; and of the Triodion, 3:*

*By Sir Joseph. Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast given a sign" (Далъ еси знаменїе):*

Grant me compunction, and estrangement from evils, and complete correction, unto me who am buried in carnal passion and alienated from Thee, O God, King of all, and have hope from nowhere; and save me, the prodigal, for Thy great goodness, O Jesus all-powerful, Savior of our souls.[^1036]

*Troparion:* Marvelous Moses, having cleansed himself by fasting, beheld the Desired One. Having emulated him, O my humble soul, make haste in the days of abstinence to cleanse thyself from evils, so that thou mayest now behold the Lord Who grants thee remission, Who is good and the Lover of mankind, the all-powerful Lord, and save our souls.[^1037]

*Another, by Sir Theodore. Tone 6, Podoben: "Ye Angelic Powers, go before" (Агглскїѧ пре):*

Let us now brightly begin the second week of the Fasts, fulfilling day by day, O brethren, having made for ourselves a fiery chariot, as did Elijah the Tishbite, the four great virtues; let us lift up our mind by dispassion, let us arm the flesh with purity, repelling and conquering the enemy.[^1038]

*Other Stichera of the Menaion, 3.*

*Glory... both now... Theotokion. Entrance. "O Gladsome Light." Prokeimenon, Tone 8:*  
Thou hast given an heritage unto them that fear Thee, O Lord. (Ps. 60:5)  
*Verse 1:* From the ends of the earth have I cried unto Thee. (Ps. 60:2)  
*Verse 2:* I will be sheltered under the covert of Thy wings. (Ps. 60:4)  
*Verse 3:* So will I sing unto Thy name unto ages of ages. (Ps. 60:8)  
*And again:* Thou hast given an heritage unto them that fear Thee, O Lord.[^1039]

*It should be known that these two Great Prokeimena, namely: "Turn not away Thy face" and "Thou hast given an heritage," with their verses, are chanted alternately throughout the whole of holy Lent. We begin from Cheesefare Sunday until the Fifth Sunday of Lent. And from "Vouchsafe, O Lord," the prostrations begin: (see fol. 38v)[^1040]*

*Then, on the Aposticha: Idiomel Stichera, Tone 8:*

Come, let us cleanse ourselves in almsgiving and compassions toward the poor, not sounding a trumpet, nor making a public display of our beneficence; let not the left hand know the work of the right; let not vainglory scatter the fruit of almsgiving; but in secret let us cry unto Him Who knows secret things: Father, remit our transgressions, for Thou art the Lover of mankind.[^1041]

*For the Martyrs:* O Martyrs of the Lord, ye sanctify every place and heal every sickness; and now pray that our souls may be delivered from the snares of the enemy, we beseech you.[^1042]

*Glory... both now... Theotokion:* The heavenly choir sings Thy praise, O full of grace, unwedded Mother; and we glorify Thine unsearchable birthgiving, O Theotokos: pray that our souls may be saved.[^1043]

*After "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart," the Troparia: "O Theotokos Virgin," and the rest of the directives (see fol. 38v)[^1044]. And the customary Litiya in the narthex.*

*At Compline, we sing the Canon of the Holy Prophets.*  
*Its Acrostic: "Let the choir of the Prophets clap their hands with flowing bounty."*  
*By Theophanes. Tone 5. Ode 1. Heirmos:* The horse and his rider [He hath cast into the sea]...[^1045]

*Troparion:* Beseech Christ the Author [of all] to grant me the grace of the Divine Spirit as I sing your precious memory, and remission of transgressions, as ye are Prophets of Divine grace.[^1046]

*Troparion:* Let us hymn all the God-wise Prophets, the concordant vessels of God-inspired words and mirrors of Divine flashing, who divinely received the Divine manifestation.[^1047]

*Troparion:* Moses the God-beholder, having received the words of the Law from God upon Mount Sinai, shone in face with the grace of the vision of God, marvelous in signs.[^1048]

*Glory...*

*Troparion:* With showers of divine knowledge, the clouds of God by grace broke up the sea of the polytheism of the nations with a crash, preaching with divine wisdom the one sovereign Power.[^1049]

*Both now...*

*Theotokion:* As God-proclaiming trumpets, the Prophets proclaim Thee to be the Mother of God, O all-spotless one, who at the end of the ages hast given birth, having been taught from on high Thy mysteries, O Theotokos.[^1050]

*Ode 3. Heirmos:* Thou Who didst establish the heavens in the beginning [by Thy wisdom]...[^1051]

*Troparion:* As spiritual harps struck by the plectrum, all the Prophets, proclaiming to all the voice of the knowledge of Thee, O Christ God, sang in a God-pleasing manner, richly receiving radiance from on high.[^1052]

*Troparion:* Rising up as weapons by Thy command, all the Prophets cut down the turbulent deceit, O Christ, having been piously clothed with Thy Divine power and incomprehensible might.[^1053]

*Glory...*

*Troparion:* As Divine and spiritual cups of understanding, all the Prophets gave the earth to drink, clearly prefiguring the unapproachable mystery of Thy Dispensation, one in one way and another in another proclaiming Thee.[^1054]

*Both now...*

*Theotokion:* The mystery commanded of old, O Virgin, and foreknown before the ages by God Who knows all things, was manifested at the end of time, having received its fulfillment in Thy womb, O all-immaculate one.[^1055]

*Ode 4. Heirmos:* Thy Divine understanding [perceiving, O Christ]...[^1056]

*Troparion:* Speaking by the Spirit, ye appeared as true and unbeguiling luminaries, O most wise Prophets, enlightening all the nations with the radiance of your life.[^1057]

*Troparion:* Beholding the clear fulfillment of the things spoken by you, O Divine Prophets, we glorify Him Who was proclaimed by you and Who fulfilled the prophecies in deed.[^1058]

*Glory...*

*Troparion:* Enlightened by Divine wisdom, ye foresaw by God's grace the ingathering of the Gentiles, and the fall of Israel, and the desolation of all good things.[^1059]

*Both now...*

*Theotokion:* Beholding God incarnate, having stood upon the Divine watch, O all-glorious ones, ye were accounted worthy to see Him coming from the overshadowing mountain.[^1060]

*Ode 5. Heirmos:* Thou Who clothest Thyself with light [as with a garment]...[^1061]

*Troparion:* Thy spirit rose early at dawn unto Him Who sits upon the exalted Throne, O most wise Isaiah, and thou didst sing with the choirs on high.[^1062]

*Troparion:* Moving your tongues by the Spirit, O holy ones, steadfastly preaching His words to the universe, ye made clear the radiance of divine knowledge.[^1063]

*Glory...*

*Troparion:* Having become dwellings of God, performing things above nature, ye have Him within yourselves; and standing now before Him, pray for us.[^1064]

*Both now...*

*Theotokion:* God, as alone wise, revealed unto you, O true Prophets, His most wise mind and ancient counsel concerning His birth from the Virgin.[^1065]

*Ode 6. Heirmos:* Surging [with the tempest of life's billows]...[^1066]

*Troparion:* Having acquired a godly life and the true word of piety, ye became most true preachers of the Divine incarnation, O holy ones.[^1067]

*Troparion:* Possessing Divine power, ye checked the unrestrained fury of kings, and stopped the mouths of beasts, and were saved unharmed from the belly of the whale.[^1068]

*Glory...*

*Troparion:* Shining upon the whole world, O holy ones, ye were set forth as...

...teachers and planters did all ye exceedingly rich Prophets become.[^1069]

*Both now...*

*Theotokion:* Holding thoughts befitting God, the Prophets proclaimed Thy birthgiving, O Sovereign Lady, by multiform outlines and types, O pure one.[^1070]

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 2. Automelon:* Today the prophetic choir, together with Moses and Aaron, rejoices with gladness, because the Cross, which brings the fulfillment of prophecy, shines forth, whereby Thou hast saved us: by their prayers, O Christ God, save our souls.[^1071]

*Ode 7. Heirmos:* Exalted by the Fathers [and God, blessed art Thou]...[^1072]

*Troparion:* The unsearchable power of the Lord's command curbed the lions in the pit, while the Prophet cried: Blessed art Thou, O God![^1073]

*Troparion:* The three young men, equal in number to the Trinity, precious sheep, Thy all-wise children, quenched the flame, chanting in unison: Blessed art Thou, O God![^1074]

*Glory...*

*Troparion:* Shining like luminaries, having adorned the earth with the flowers of virtue, the Prophets, offspring of Abraham, sang: Blessed art Thou, O God![^1075]

*Both now...*

*Theotokion:* Thou hast transcended the laws of nature, O Sovereign Lady, having given birth unto the Lord Who rules over the Law, unto Whom we all sing: Blessed art Thou, O God![^1076]

*Ode 8. Heirmos:* Unto Thee, the Creator of all...[^1077]

*Troparion:* Dwelling within the delights of paradise, O God-bearing Prophets, having formed a choir, beseech Christ that all who praise you with faith may be delivered from tribulations.[^1078]

*Troparion:* Let us offer a choral song unto all the God-proclaiming Prophets, all having woven a choir, having been established by their words, that by their prayers we may be justified.[^1079]

*Glory...*

*Troparion:* Ye all became spiritual vessels of sweet fragrance unto the Spirit, O Prophets, manifestly guiding all nations unto understanding, and supremely exalting Christ unto the ages.[^1080]

*Both now...*

*Theotokion:* O Virgin, Thou hast given birth unto the unoriginate Radiance from the Father through the assumption of flesh...[^1081]

...reception [of flesh]; therefore, Rejoice! we unceasingly cry unto Thee, and we supremely exalt Thee, O pure one, unto the ages.[^1082]

*Ode 9. Heirmos:* Isaiah, dance...[^1083]

*Troparion:* With one accord and simply, O all-honorable Prophets of all God's mysteries, praise Christ, the Worker of supernatural miracles, as having proclaimed the venerable Counsel, the chosen portion of Jacob!

*Troparion:* Ye were the fore-announcers of joy to the whole world, manifest heralds, and radiant divine treasures of understanding, O truly wise ones, pure mouths, and all-honorable tongues of the Holy Spirit!

*Glory...*

*Troparion:* As most wise Prophets, beholding the Creator and God of all as mighty, and being enlightened by light from Him: save from afflictions those who piously with faith honor your memory![^1084]

*Both now... Theotokion:* Thou wast the Mediatress of salvation unto men, O pure one, having in the flesh given birth unto the Creator and Lord, Who for Thy sake grants cleansing unto all who magnify Thee, O Virgin!

*Then Stichera to the Prophets. Tone 1, Podoben: "O all-lauded martyrs" (Прехва́льнїи му́ченицы):*[^1085]

*Sticheron 1:* O all-glorious Prophets, ye reproved kings, and opposed insolent peoples, preaching the one God in Trinity, and fervently driving away from the earth the delusion of polytheism. And now pray, that peace and great mercy be granted unto our souls!

*Sticheron 2:* O all-glorious Prophets, ye who piously wandered in deserts and mountains, and were afflicted in hunger and thirst, as God's well-pleasing servants: ye dwell with Christ in the heavens. And now pray, that peace and great mercy be granted unto our souls!

*Sticheron 3:* O all-lauded Prophets, patiently sawn asunder, and...

...stoned with stones, and put to death by the slaughter of the sword: for the sake of piety and because of your sufferings ye became radiant! And now pray, that peace and great mercy be granted unto our souls!

*Glory... both now... Theotokion:* Truly beyond understanding, O marvelous Bride of God, are the wonders of Thy childbearing, which all the Prophets foretold: the all-glorious conception, and the celebrated childbearing, incomprehensible and ineffable, whereby the world was saved!

*Concerning the rest, (see fol. 170)[^1086]*

*If the Finding of the Precious Head of John the Forerunner, or the Forty Martyrs, falls on Monday of the Second, or Third, or Fourth, or Fifth Week of the Holy Fast:*  
*On Sunday evening we chant "Blessed is the man," 1st Antiphon. On "Lord, I have cried," 10 Stichera: in the Triodion, 3, on 4; to the Forerunner, on 6; Glory... to the Forerunner; Both now... Theotokion according to the Tone. Entrance. Great Prokeimenon in the Triodion. And 3 Readings. Then "Vouchsafe, O Lord," and "Let us complete our evening prayer." On the Aposticha, in the Triodion, Idiomels, 2, and Martyrikon. Glory... Both now... Resurrectional Theotokion according to the Tone. After "Our Father," Troparion of the Forerunner; Glory... Both now... Resurrectional Theotokion in that same Tone. "Blessed be the name of the Lord," "Have mercy on us, O God," and 3 great prostrations. After this, at the calming, Glory... Both now... dismissal, and polychronion. At Matins on Monday, the entire service and the Hours as shown, (see fol. 193)[^1087], Chapter 2.*

## Monday of the Second Week of Great Lent

*The service is performed at Matins, just as on the first week; see instructions concerning everything, (see fol. 172)[^1088], and following:*

*After the 1st Stichologia, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Joseph was amazed" (Оудиви́ся Іѡ́сифъ):*[^1089]

Slain in soul by the fruit of transgression, make me alive, O Christ, through true fasting and repentance, I pray Thee, as Thou art compassionate; and grant me to walk uprightly in the paths of Thy upright and good, honorable commandments, so that having also attained unto Thy divine glory, with all who love Thee, I may glorify Thy bounties in all things, O Jesus! *(Twice)*

*Glory... both now... Theotokion:*

Surges of...

...passions, an abyssal hades, enveloped in smoke, O pure one, I call upon Thee fervently: despise me not, wretch that I am, that I perish not, O Thou who hast given birth unto the abyss of mercy, for other than Thee I possess no hope! Let me not, therefore, become an object of rejoicing and mockery unto my enemies, trusting in Thee; for Thou canst do all things whatsoever Thou willest, as Thou art the Mother of the God of all.

*After the 2nd Stichologia, Sessional Hymn, Tone 6, Podoben: "Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us" (Поми́луй на́съ, Го́споди, поми́луй):*[^1090]

O Lord, direct us who keep the fast of the second week; shine forth upon us cleansing, and the enlightenment of Thy statutes, and account us worthy to offer unto Thee acceptable prayer, as we bow our knees; for Thou art our Father, and we are Thy sons, and unto Thee with fear we sing, and Thy Name we call upon. *(Twice)*
