*Glory... both now... Theotokion:* The beginning of salvation was Gabriel's greeting unto the Virgin; for hearing the "Rejoice," she fled not from the salutation, nor did she doubt as did Sarah in the tent, but cried thus: Behold the handmaid of the Lord: be it unto me according to thy word!

*Triode Canon, Tone 4. By Joseph, Ode 1. Heirmos:* The mighty captains...[^1091]

*Troparion:* O only Good One, Wellspring of mercy, Lamb of God Who takest away as God the sins of the world: save me, overwhelmed by the storm of transgressions, guiding me unto the haven of repentance!

*Troparion:* Pure fasting, departure from sin, estrangement from passions, love toward God, diligence in prayer, tears with compunction, and care for the destitute: these hath Christ commanded in the Scriptures.

Wounded in...

*Troparion:* Wounded in soul by the weapon of sin, and stricken by many evils, O Physician of our souls, heal me as Thou art good, applying to me the remedies of Thy measured commandments, O Lover of mankind!

*Theotokion:* O undefiled Tabernacle, all-holy Virgin, cleanse me, defiled by the assaults of grievous passions, by the fountain of Thy mercy, and grant me showers of compunction, O Sovereign Lady, consuming the deep of sin!

*Another Heirmos. Tone 6. By Sir Theodore. Heirmos:* He was my helper and protector...[^1092]

*Troparion:* As festive joy, having received the second week of the light-bearing Fast, O brethren, let us lovingly sing unto Christ, rejoicing divinely!

*Troparion:* Having now found the fasting season of compunction, let us weep bitterly and sigh, and let us lift up our hands unto the only Redeemer, that He may save our souls!

*Trinity:* O Tri-hypostatic Unity, most Sovereign Ruler of all, beginning of all perfections and primordial: do Thou Thyself save us, O Father, and Son, and all-holy Spirit!

*Theotokion:* Who ever brought forth a Son unknown to the paternal law? Him indeed the Father begets without a mother—O all-glorious wonder! For Thou, O pure one, hast given birth unto God and man together.

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*

*Troparion:* How shall I endure Thy wrath, O my Christ, when Thou comest unto judgment? What answer shall I find to give there, having neither accomplished nor done Thy will, O Christ? Therefore, before the end, grant me remission!

*Heirmos:* He was my helper and protector, and is become my salvation: He is my God, and I will glorify Him; the God of my father, and I will exalt Him; for gloriously hath He been glorified.[^1093]

*Ode 8. Heirmos:* O Redeemer of all, Almighty One...[^1094]

Traversing...

*Troparion:* Traversing the instability of life, I have fallen among thievish thoughts; wounded unto festering sores, O Physician of the sick: stretch forth Thy hand unto me, through the supplications of all Thy saints!

*Troparion:* The storm of grievous sin confounds my mind; as once Peter, save me, O Jesus, as I sing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto the ages!

*Troparion:* By abstinence let us mortify the passions, through fasting let us give wings to the spirit toward heaven, and let us cry out with compunction of heart: We have sinned against Thee, O God, as Thou art compassionate, forgive!

*Theotokion:* Having dwelt within Thy womb, the Most High showed Thee to be more spacious than the heavens, and an invincible protectress unto them that cry, O Virgin: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and supremely exalt Him!

*Another Heirmos:* Whom the hosts...[^1095]

*Troparion:* Show my soul to be unenslaved to the tyranny of passions, O Lord, that freely doing Thy will, I may rejoice and glorify Thy dominion unto the ages!

*Troparion:* Having hated Esau's lack of self-control, O my soul, emulate the good deeds of Jacob: trip up Beliar through abstinence, enrich thyself with divine things, and sing unto the ages!

*We bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, the Lord.*

*Trinity:* Worship the one God according to essence; sing the three Hypostases definitely distinct yet not of other nature: for the Godhead is one in three dominions, namely: the Father, the Son, and the Divine Spirit!

*Theotokion:* Having come forth from Thy radiant womb as a bridegroom from his bridal chamber, Christ, the Great Light, hath shone forth...

...in darkness; for the Sun of Righteousness, having shone forth, hath enlightened the world, O pure one!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*

*Troparion:* No one drinking water ever lost his mind; but Noah was seen naked, having become drunken with wine, and Lot thereby engendered seeds of malice. Flee therefore, O my soul, their emulation, singing unto Christ unto the ages!

*Heirmos:* Him Whom the heavenly hosts glorify, and Cherubim and Seraphim tremble before: every breath and creation, sing, bless, and supremely exalt unto all ages![^1096]

*Ode 9. Heirmos:* Eve indeed through disobedience...[^1097]

*Troparion:* Let us fast from the passions of anger; let us delight in unfeigned love; let us nourish the poor with bread, being nourished by divine grace, and with tears let us quench tears of future condemnation!

*Troparion:* Sigh, O wretched soul, lament, show forth the images of repentance! Now at the doors is the Day; the impartial Judge sits, rendering unto each according to the worth of his deeds, as it is written.

*Troparion:* I have not acquired good works; I have defiled the garment which I received, the vesture of Divine Baptism, and I walk in the darkness of ignorance: by the light of Thy countenance, O Lord, restore me now who am in despair!

*Theotokion:* O Mary, Sovereign Lady of all creation, do Thou set me free who am enslaved to every sin, O Virgin who didst bear the Deliverer of our souls; for beyond speech Thou hast given birth unto the essential Goodness!

*Another Heirmos:* Seedless...[^1098]

*Troparion:* Now let us suffer hardship, as soldiers of Christ; for as time passes by, crowns are being woven for them that struggle...

...which Christ shall render when He comes with the Angels to judge the whole earth upon the earth!

*Troparion:* I am entirely wounded, I am wholly putrid, O Christ! Heal my painful wounds, the passionate bites which are from sin, that like the leper I may hear Thy holy voice: "I will; be thou cleansed!"

*Glory... Trinity:* O Father, sole Begetter of the only-begotten Son, and Thou, O Light from the one Light, Radiance of the Light; and Thou, O Holy Spirit, truly the speaking God of the one God: O holy Trinity in Unity, save me who theologize Thee!

*Theotokion:* The wonder of Thy childbearing strikes me with awe, O all-immaculate one: how conceivest Thou seedlessly the Incomprehensible? Say, how remainest Thou a virgin, having given birth as a Mother? Having received by faith that which is above nature, worship Him Who is born, for whatsoever He wills, that He can also do!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*

*Troparion:* Fasting showed forth Moses of old as the God-beholder, and Elijah as the fiery charioteer, and Paul, O my soul, as the awesome traveler unto heaven: therefore let us fast from evils, and let us also be caught up unto the height of dispassion!

*Heirmos:* Seedless is the conception, ineffable the childbearing of the unwedded Mother, incorrupt the birth; for the birthgiving of God renews nature: therefore all generations orthodoxly magnify Thee as the Mother and Bride of God.[^1099]

*Concerning the rest, (see fol. 174)[^1100]*

*On the Aposticha, Idiomel Stichera, Tone 5:*

A marvelous weapon are prayer and fasting! This showed forth Moses as the Lawgiver, and Elijah as a zealot in sacrifices; abiding therein, O faithful, let us cry unto the Savior: Against Thee only have we sinned, have mercy on us! *(Twice)*

*Verse 1: Unto Thee have I lifted up mine eyes... (Ps. 122:1 [LXX 122:1 / MT 123:1]) Martyrikon:* The blessed army of the King of Heaven: for though the Passion-bearers were earth-born, yet they made haste to attain unto the angelic rank, having despised their bodies, and by their sufferings were counted worthy of the honor of the bodiless hosts! By their prayers, O Lord, save our souls.

*Glory... both now... Theotokion:* Unto Thee do we pray, as unto the Mother of God: O blessed Mary, that our souls may be saved!

*On Monday of the Second Week of the Holy Fast, at the Sixth Hour.*

*Troparion of the Prophecy, Tone 5:*

*Troparion:* O Thou Who hast fashioned our hearts one by one, remember that we are dust; condemn us not unto the nethermost parts of the earth, O Sinless One!

*Glory... the end:* Condemn us not... *Both now... the whole:* O Thou Who hast fashioned...

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 21, Tone 6:* Ye that fear the Lord, praise Him! (Ps. 21:24 [LXX 21:24 / MT 22:23])*[^1101]*  
*Verse:* O God, my God, attend to me: why hast Thou forsaken me? (Ps. 21:2 [LXX 21:2 / MT 22:1])

*Reading from the Prophecy of Isaiah (Chapter 4:2–5:7):*[^1102]

Thus saith the Lord: In that day God shall shine forth in counsel with glory upon the earth, to glorify and exalt the remnant of Israel. [4:2] And it shall come to pass, that the remnant in Zion, [4:3] and the remnant in Jerusalem, all they that are written unto life in Jerusalem, shall be called holy. [4:4] For the Lord shall wash away the filth of the sons and daughters of Zion, and shall purge away the blood of Jerusalem from the midst of them, by the spirit of judgment and the spirit of burning. [4:5] And He shall come, and it shall be that every place of Mount Zion, and all the round about it, a cloud shall overshadow by day, and as of smoke, and as the light of a burning fire by night; by all the glory shall it be sheltered; [4:6] and there shall be a shadow by day from the heat...

...from the heat, and for a covering and for a secret place from storm and rain.  
Now will I sing unto my Beloved the song of my Beloved touching my vineyard: My Beloved had a vineyard on a horn [of a hill], in a fertile place. [5:1] And I made a hedge about it, and dug about it, and planted a choice vine, and built a tower in the midst of it, and dug out a winepress in it; and I waited for it to bring forth grapes, and it brought forth wild grapes. [5:2] And now, O man of Judah, and ye that dwell in Jerusalem, judge between Me and My vineyard. [5:3] What could have been done more to My vineyard, that I have not done in it? For what reason, when I looked that it should bring forth grapes, brought it forth wild grapes? [5:4] And now I will tell you what I will do to My vineyard: I will take away the hedge thereof, and it shall be eaten up; and break down the wall thereof, and it shall be trodden down. [5:5] And I will leave My vineyard: it shall not be pruned, nor dug; and thorns shall come up upon it as on waste ground; and I will also command the clouds that they rain no rain upon it. [5:6] For the vineyard of the Lord of Sabaoth is the house of Israel, and the men of Judah His pleasant plant. [5:7]

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 22, Tone 6:* Thy rod and Thy staff, they have comforted me. (Ps. 22:4 [LXX 22:4 / MT 23:4])*[^1103]*  
*Verse:* The Lord shepherds me, and I shall lack nothing. (Ps. 22:1 [LXX 22:1 / MT 23:1])

*Concerning the Forty Martyrs, (see fol. 381)[^1104]*

*On that same Monday of the Second Week of the Fast. At Vespers.*

*Stichera, Tone 8, Podoben: "What shall we call you, O holy ones" (Что́ вы нарече́мъ): By Sir Joseph:*[^1105]

*Sticheron 1:* Unto whom hast thou likened thyself, O wretched, sluggardly soul, doing not good things, but constantly fulfilling diligence in evils? The Judgment is at the doors...

...repent! Through fasting and prayer cleanse thyself, and cry aloud unto thy Master: I have sinned against Thee; forgive, as Thou art merciful, and grant me pardon!

*Sticheron 2:* Possessing an ocean of goodness, dry up the depths of my deceitful sins, O Christ, as the Sinless God; and grant compunction unto my heart, cleansing the torrents of lawlessness, that I may sing and glorify Thine ineffable loving-kindness, O long-suffering Benefactor of our souls!

*Another Sticheron, by Sir Theodore, Same Tone [Tone 8], Podoben: "In Eden of old" (Въ Е҆де́мѣ ра́й):*[^1106]

O God, Who hast brought us also now to accomplish the circuit of the time of the all-honorable Fast, and hast granted us to enter into the holy arena of the second week: do Thou Thyself, O Lord, account us worthy also to run well toward that which is to come, strengthening our body and our soul in well-doing, so that, having manfully finished our course, we may attain unto the true day of Thy Resurrection, and all joyfully bearing the crown, may unceasingly praise Thee!

*And in the Menaion, 3. Glory... both now... Theotokion.*

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 23, Tone 4:* The Lord strong and mighty, the Lord mighty in battle. (Ps. 23:8 [LXX 23:8 / MT 24:8])*[^1107]*  
*Verse:* The earth is the Lord's, and the fullness thereof. (Ps. 23:1 [LXX 23:1 / MT 24:1])

*Reading from Genesis (Chapter 3:21–4:7):*[^1108]

And the Lord God made for Adam and his wife coats of skins, and clothed them. [3:21] And God said: Behold, Adam is become as one of Us, to know good and evil; and now, lest he put forth his hand, and take of the tree of life, and eat, and live unto the ages! [3:22] And the Lord God sent him [Adam] forth from the paradise of delight, to till the ground from which... [3:23] ...he was taken. [3:23] And He cast out Adam, and caused him to dwell over against the paradise of delight. And He placed the Cherubim, and a flaming sword that turned every way, to guard the way of the tree of life. [3:24]

And Adam knew Eve his wife, and she conceived and bore Cain, and said: I have acquired a man through God. [4:1] And she added to give birth unto his brother Abel; and Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground. [4:2] And it came to pass after some days, that Cain brought of the fruits of the ground a sacrifice unto God. [4:3] And Abel also brought, even he, of the firstborn of his sheep, and of their fat. And God looked upon Abel and upon his gifts; [4:4] but unto Cain and unto his sacrifices He attended not. And Cain was exceedingly grieved, and his countenance fell. [4:5] And the Lord God said unto Cain: Why hast thou become grieved, and for what cause is thy countenance fallen? [4:6] If thou hast offered rightly, but hast not rightly divided, hast thou not sinned? Be still. Unto thee shall be his turning, and thou shalt rule over him.[^1109] [4:7]

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 24, Tone 6:* Look upon me and have mercy on me. (Ps. 24:16 [LXX 24:16 / MT 25:16])*[^1110]*  
*Verse:* Unto Thee, O Lord, have I lifted up my soul. (Ps. 24:1 [LXX 24:1 / MT 25:1])

*Reading from Proverbs (Chapter 3:34–4:22):*[^1111]

The Lord resists the proud, but gives grace unto the humble. [3:34] The wise shall inherit glory, but the ungodly have exalted dishonor. [3:35]

Hear, ye children, the instruction of a father, and attend to know understanding. [4:1] For I give you a good gift; forsake ye not my law. [4:2] For I also was a son obedient unto my father, and beloved in the sight of my mother... [4:3] ...who taught me, and said: Let our word be established in thine heart; keep our commandments, forget them not. [4:4] Acquire wisdom, acquire understanding; forget not, neither neglect the speech of my mouth. [4:5] Forsake her not, and she shall defend thee; love her dearly, and she shall keep thee. [4:6] The beginning of wisdom is to acquire wisdom; and with all thy acquisition acquire understanding. [4:7] Enclose her, and she shall exalt thee; honor her, that she may embrace thee. [4:8] That she may give unto thine head a crown of graces, and with a crown of delight she shall shield thee. [4:9] Hear, my son, and receive my words, and the years of thy life shall be multiplied unto thee, that the paths of thy life may be many. [4:10] For I teach thee the paths of wisdom, and I guide thee into right tracks. [4:11] For if thou walkest, thy steps shall not be hindered; and if thou runnest, thou shalt not be weary. [4:12] Lay hold on my instruction, and let it not go; but keep it for thyself unto thy life. [4:13] Go not into the ways of the ungodly, neither be zealous for the paths of transgressors. [4:14] In whatever place they pitch their camp, go not thither; turn aside from them, and pass by. [4:15] For they cannot sleep unless they have done evil; sleep is taken away from them, and they sleep not. [4:16] For they feed on the bread of wickedness, and are drunken with the wine of transgression. [4:17] But the paths of the righteous shine like light; they go forth and enlighten, until the day is fully ordered. [4:18] But the ways of the ungodly are dark; they know not how they stumble. [4:19] My son, attend unto my speech... [4:20] ...attend; and incline thine ear unto my words. [4:20] That thy fountains may not fail thee, keep them in thine heart: [4:21] for they are life unto [all] that find them, and healing unto all their flesh. [4:22]

*On the Aposticha, Idiomel Stichera, Tone 3:*

*Sticheron 1:* Let us fast a spiritual fast; let us break asunder every provocation; let us abstain from the stumbling blocks of sin; let us forgive our brethren their debts, that our sins also may be forgiven us! For so shall we be able to cry aloud: Let our prayer be set forth as incense before Thee, O Lord! *(Twice)*

*Martyrikon:* The Prophets and Apostles of Christ, and the Martyrs, taught men to sing the Holy Trinity, and enlightened the wandering nations, and made the sons of men partakers with the Angels.

*Glory... both now... Theotokion, Same Tone:* Unto the end forget not Thy needy ones, O Sovereign Lady, but by Thy prayers deliver us from future condemnation, and rescue Thy servants, O Mother of God, from present harm and the wrath of the Lord!

*Be it known that: from this Monday of the second week of the Fast, there are chanted at Compline the Canons from the Menaion of the Saints who occur from Lazarus Saturday until Thomas Sunday, together with the Theotokion Canons. First the Canon to the Mother of God is sung, and after it that in the Menaion. After Ode 3, Kontakion and Sessional Hymn in the Menaion; and after Ode 6, Sessional Hymn of the Mother of God. And after the Canon, Stichera in the Menaion.*

## Tuesday of the Second Week of Great Lent

*At Matins:* As usual, (see fol. 172)[^1112]

*After the 2nd Stichologia, Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "Having risen from the dead" (Въскр҃съ и҆з̾ мр҃твы):*[^1113]

Restraining the passions with the bridle of undefiled fasting, [and directing] our mind unto honorable divine visions with faith most...

...perfect, let us all strive to take wing, that we may despise the low-loving sweetness of life, and obtain heavenly life and divine radiance! *(Twice)*

*Glory... both now... Theotokion:* Into a dire abyss of wicked deeds am I fallen, from the multitude of my deceitful and unclean works; I have come into perplexity, and am now held fast by despair. O Sovereign Lady Theotokos, do Thou Thyself save me, do Thou Thyself help me; for unto sinners Thou art the propitiation and saving cleansing!

*After the 3rd Stichologia, Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "The shepherd's pipe" (Па́стырскїй сопль):*[^1114]

Setting forth the fast as a mystical table, He commands us richly to be filled: let us eat the ever-living gifts of the Spirit as food, let us drink the God-flowing streams of tears as water, and having rejoiced, let us unceasingly offer praise unto God! *(Twice)*

*Glory... both now... Theotokion:* From every threat and affliction of man, save us, O all-pure Virgin; for we possess Thee as protection and intercession, who flee unto Thee, O Mother of God, and unto our God Who was born of Thee: do Thou entreat Him to deliver us from tribulations and afflictions!

*Triode Canon, by Sir Joseph, Tone 8. And the Biblical Ode of the Psalter is chanted.*[^1115]  
*Ode 2. Heirmos:* See, see that I am your God, begotten of the Father before the ages, and born of the Virgin in the last times without a husband, and Who dissolved the sin of forefather Adam, as the Lover of mankind![^1116]

*Troparion:* Sigh, shed tears, O my soul, turn, repent! The hour draws near, the Judge is at the doors; make ready for the defense, and cry aloud: I have sinned against Thee, O Compassionate, Merciful, and Good One, have compassion on me!

*Troparion:* Having hated the all-destroying greed of sin, O my soul, take delight diligently in the fullness of the fast; make the saving commandments thy food, which procure through faith the delight of eternal good things!

*Troparion:* Angels, Powers, Principalities, Archangels, Dominions, Thrones, Authorities, Cherubim, and Seraphim: pray ye unto the Giver of grace and God, that He grant unto us forgiveness of sins and turning away of passions!

*Theotokion:* O all-immaculate one, who alone didst bear the unoriginate Word incarnate of Thee without change, remaining after childbirth the unwedded Virgin: pray Thou for all, that our life may be delivered from corruption!

*Another Heirmos, by Theodore, Same Tone [Tone 8]. Heirmos:* See, see...[^1117]

*Troparion:* We have seen, we have known that good for us is the season unto repentance which Thou hast appointed. But in this season, O God, receive our prayers, and direct them before Thee, O Compassionate One, as good incense, as an acceptable sacrifice!

*Troparion:* I am terrified and afraid, considering how many things I have sinned: how shall I entreat Thee? How shall I appear before Thee, O Awesome One? And how shall I stand before Thy righteous tribunal? Therefore spare me, O Compassionate One, in the hour when Thou shalt judge all the earth!

*Glory... Trinity:* O all-perfect Unity, transcendent in divinity, Tri-hypostatic: Unbegotten Father, and Only-begotten Son, and Spirit proceeding from the Father, yet made manifest through the Son: one Essence and Nature, Dominion and Kingdom, save us all![^1118]

*Both now... Theotokion:* Ineffable is the wonder of Thy childbearing, O Virgin Mother: for how dost Thou give birth, and yet remainest chaste therein;...

...how dost Thou bear a child, and knowest no experience of man at all? Even as He knows Who was born of me in a new and fitting manner surpassing nature: the Word of God Who was born!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*

*Troparion:* Thou didst deliver the Ninevites who repented and fasted from the threatening wrath; but the Sodomites who strayed in satiety Thou didst burn with fire: yet deliver me, O Christ, from their condemnation!

*Heirmos:* See, see that I am your God, Who have sanctified for you an acceptable beginning, a tithing from the days of the whole year; and this have I given unto My people for the deliverance from passions, as a beginning unto salvation![^1119]

*Ode 8. Heirmos:* God-fearing children in the furnace...[^1120]

*Troparion:* O Thou Who didst justify the Publican when he sighed, Who didst have compassion on the harlot weeping from her heart: save and have compassion, O Savior, on the souls of them that sing to Thee!

*Troparion:* Let us bear the fruit of virtuous deeds by the fast, O Lord, and let us drive away harmful thoughts, that we may obtain divine sweetness!

*Troparion:* Choirs of Angels entreat Thee, assemblies of Apostles, and ranks of Martyrs: O Jesus, grant forgiveness unto Thy people!

*Theotokion:* The unhewn mountain, the Virgin, the light-bearing lampstand, the well-traversed ladder, the receptacle of God: let us, the faithful, bless her!

*Another Heirmos. Tone 8. Heirmos:* On the holy Mountain...[^1121]

*Troparion:* On the appointed day of abstinence, come, let us all sound the trumpet in songs, that being feasted with divine sweetness, we may sing hymns and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparion:* Honoring the fast as the guardian of purity, and the mother...

...of dispassion, come, O people, let us embrace it with love, singing and supremely exalting the Lord!

*We bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, the Lord.*

*Trinity:* As a Unity according to essence I sing Thee; as a Trinity according to Hypostases I honor Thee: O Father, and Son, and all-holy Spirit, I glorify the unoriginate dominion of Thy kingdom unto the ages!

*Theotokion:* Thou hast been shown to be the Mountain of God, O Theotokos, into which Christ entered, and made those who sing divine temples: Bless the Lord, all ye works, and supremely exalt Him unto the ages!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*

*Troparion:* Who of old devoured the man of God? A beast, a lion, because the Prophet accepted the food of disobedience.[^1122] Beware therefore, O my soul, lest the serpent of belly-madness beguile thee!

*We praise, we bless, and we worship the Lord.*

*Heirmos:* Him Who was glorified on the holy mountain, and in the bush through fire revealed unto Moses the mystery of the Ever-Virgin: sing and supremely exalt the Lord unto all ages![^1123]

*Ode 9. Heirmos:* The [One] manifest on the mountain...[^1124]

*Troparion:* The good fast that enriches hearts divinely sprouts the ripe ear of virtues; let us love it, receiving cleansing in these holy days!

*Troparion:* Beholding me defiled in many sins, bound fast and condemned, O Merciful One, have compassion on me by Thy mercy, and save me through the prayers of Thy saints!

*Troparion:* Woe is me, all-passionate soul! How wilt thou answer? What fear shall seize thee when the Judge sits, and ten thousands of Angels stand before Him? Strive therefore, repent before the end!

*Theotokion:* Royal chariot, bright cloud, fertile mountain, curdled mountain, unwedded one, ark of manna, O Virgin: heal Thou the passions of our souls!

*The same Heirmos.*

*Troparion:* Let us fast a true fast unto the Lord, as abstinence from foods, estrangement from anger of the tongue, and lying, and every other passion, that in purity we may behold Pascha!

*Troparion:* Possessing the Holy Spirit of the fast as a rich entertainer, let us be filled with His gifts, and richly take delight, hymning Him as our God!

*Glory... Trinity:* The thrice-radiant light of Thy sole sovereignty, O Lord, shine forth into our mind with bright radiances; turn us away from manifold delusion, unto Thine only embracing!

*Both now... Theotokion:* Thou art our weapon and wall, O Theotokos; Thou art the protection of them that flee unto Thee. Thee do we move now unto prayer, that we may be delivered from our enemies!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*

*Troparion:* Thou, O Fast, didst nurture Samuel as fruit; thou didst nurse Samson the great warrior; thou dost perfect Priests and Prophets; do thou sanctify us, O venerable Fast![^1125]

*Katavasia. Heirmos:* The childbearing of the Ever-Virgin manifest on the mountain unto the Lawgiver in fire and the bush, for the salvation of us the faithful, with unceasing hymns we magnify![^1126]

*Exapostilarion [Photogogic], Tone.*[^1127]

*On the Aposticha, Idiomel Stichera, Tone 5:*

*Sticheron 1:* Why despondent, O my soul, art thou in bondage unto sin? And why being infirm dost thou not flee unto the Physician? Behold the acceptable time; behold now is the true day of salvation! Arise, wash thy face with the tears of repentance, and illuminate the lamp with the oil of well-doing, that thou mayest find cleansing from Christ God, and great mercy! *(Twice)*

*Martyrikon:* Thy Passion-bearers, O Lord, having likened themselves unto the angelic ranks, as bodiless ones endured torments, possessing a single-minded hope of the promised...

...good things, the reception: by their prayers, O Christ our God, grant peace unto Thy world, and unto our souls great mercy!

*Glory... both now... Theotokion:* We bless Thee, O Virgin Theotokos, and we the faithful glorify Thee as is due: an immovable city, an unbreakable wall, a firm intercession, and refuge of our souls!

*Then: "It is good to give thanks...", Trisagion, and the rest, (see fol. 180)[^1128]*

*On Tuesday of the Second Week of the Holy Fast, at the Sixth Hour.*

*Troparion of the Prophecy, Tone 6:*

*Troparion:* We are not able to hymn Thee worthily, but we pray entreating Thee: destroy us not with our iniquities, O easily appeased Lord!

*Glory... the end:* Destroy us not... *Both now... the whole:* We are not able...

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 25, Tone 4:* O Lord, I have loved the beauty of Thine house, and the place of the dwelling of Thy glory. (Ps. 25:8 [LXX 25:8 / MT 26:8])*[^1129]*  
*Verse:* Judge me, O Lord, for I have walked in my innocence. (Ps. 25:1 [LXX 25:1 / MT 26:1])

*Reading from the Prophecy of Isaiah (Chapter 5:7–16):*[^1130]

Thus saith the Lord: The vineyard of the Lord of Sabaoth is the house of Israel, and the man of Judah His pleasant newly planted garden: I looked that it should work judgment, but it wrought iniquity; and not righteousness, but a cry. [5:7] Woe unto them that join house to house, and bring field near to field, that they may take away somewhat from their neighbor! [5:8] Will ye dwell alone upon the earth? For these things were heard in the ears of the Lord of Sabaoth: For if many houses shall be built, great and good houses shall be desolate, and there shall be no inhabitants in them. [5:9] For where... [5:10] ...ten yoke of oxen work, it shall make one jar [keramion], and he that sows six artabae shall make three measures.[^1131] [5:10] Woe unto them that rise up early in the morning, and follow strong drink; who wait for the evening: for wine shall inflame them! [5:11] For with lute and harps, and with tabrets and pipes, they drink wine, but they regard not the works of God, neither consider the works of His hands. [5:12] Therefore My people are taken captive, because they know not the Lord; and there was a multitude of dead because of famine and thirst for water. [5:13] And hades has enlarged its desire, and opened its mouth without ceasing; and the glorious, and the great, and the rich, and their destroyers, shall go down, rejoicing within it. [5:14] And man shall be brought low, and a man shall be dishonored, and lofty eyes shall be humbled. [5:15] And the Lord of Sabaoth shall be exalted in judgment, and the Holy God shall be glorified in righteousness. [5:16]

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 26, Tone 3:* The Lord is my light and my Savior: whom shall I fear? (Ps. 26:1 [LXX 26:1 / MT 27:1])*[^1132]*  
*Verse:* The Lord is the defender of my life: of whom shall I be afraid? (Ps. 26:1 [LXX 26:1 / MT 27:1])

*On that same Tuesday of the Second Week of the Fast. At Vespers.*

*On "Lord, I have cried," Stichera, by Sir Joseph, Tone 1, Podoben: "O all-lauded martyrs" (Прехва́льнїи му́ченицы):*[^1133]

*Sticheron 1:* Having stretched out Thy most pure hands upon the Cross, O Christ, gathering the ends [of the earth]: therefore I cry unto Thee: Gather my scattered mind, taken captive and dragged by passions, and show me forth to be a partaker of Thy sufferings, cleansed in all things through abstinence!

*Sticheron 2:* The fast having once sharpened the children showed them to be mightier, as it is written, than the burning fire.[^1134] Humble soul of mine, fast, kindling in thyself...\n ...vigilant thanksgiving, for the sake of which thou shalt be able to escape the coming Gehenna and burn up ruinous passions!

*Another Sticheron, Tone 3, Podoben: "O valiant martyrs" (До́блїи му́ченицы):*[^1135]

The joyous time of the fast is come; therefore, having been richly filled with radiant purity, pure love, light-bearing prayer, and every other virtue, let us brightly cry out: O Christ God Most High, Who hast made the sweetness of life to grow for all, vouchsafe us to worship Thee with a pure heart, granting us cleansing and great mercy!

*Rubric: If there is no Menaion, we repeat these.*

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 27, Tone 6:* Save, O Lord, Thy people, and bless Thine inheritance. (Ps. 27:9 [LXX 27:9 / MT 28:9])*[^1136]*  
*Verse:* Unto Thee, O Lord, will I cry, O my God. (Ps. 27:1 [LXX 27:1 / MT 28:1])

*Reading from Genesis (Chapter 4:8–14):*[^1137]

And Cain said to Abel his brother: Let us go out into the field.[^1138] And it came to pass, when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother and slew him. [4:8] And the Lord God said unto Cain: Where is Abel thy brother? And he said: I know not; [4:9] am I my brother's keeper? And God said: [4:9] What hast thou done? The voice of thy brother's blood cries unto Me from the ground! [4:10] And now accursed art thou from the earth, which hath opened her mouth to receive thy brother's blood from thy hand: [4:11] when thou tillest the ground, it shall not henceforth yield unto thee her strength; groaning and trembling shalt thou be upon the earth. [4:12] And Cain said unto the Lord God: My guilt is greater than that it may be forgiven me. [4:13] If Thou castest me out this day from the face of the earth, and from Thy face... [4:14] ...shall I be hidden; and I shall be groaning and trembling upon the earth, and it shall come to pass, that everyone that finds me shall slay me. [4:14] And the Lord God said unto him: Not so; whosoever slays Cain shall suffer vengeance sevenfold. And the Lord God set a mark upon Cain, lest anyone finding him should kill him. [4:15]

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 28, Tone 7:* The Lord will give strength unto His people; the Lord will bless His people with peace. (Ps. 28:11 [LXX 28:11 / MT 29:11])*[^1139]*  
*Verse:* Bring unto the Lord, O ye sons of God. (Ps. 28:1 [LXX 28:1 / MT 29:1])

*Reading from Proverbs (Chapter 5:1–15):*[^1140]

My son, attend unto my wisdom, and bow down thine ear to my words: [5:1] That thou mayest keep good counsel, and the knowledge of my lips commands thee. [5:2] [Give no heed unto an evil woman],[^1141] for honey drops from the lips of a harlot, who for a season sweetens thy palate; [5:3] yet afterward thou shalt find her more bitter than wormwood, and sharper than a two-edged sword. [5:4] For the feet of folly lead down those who use her, with death into hades; [5:5] and her steps are not established; for she goes not upon the paths of life, and her ways are wandering and not well understood. [5:6] Now therefore, my son, listen unto me, and make not my words of none effect. [5:7] Remove thy way far from her, and come not near unto the doors of her houses: [5:8] lest thou give thy life unto others, and thy living unto the unmerciful; [5:9] lest strangers be filled with thy strength, and thy labors enter into the houses of strangers; [5:10] and thou repent... [5:11] ...at the last, when the flesh of thy body is consumed, [5:11] and thou say: How have I hated instruction, and mine heart turned away from the reproofs of the righteous? [5:12] And I obeyed not the voice of him that instructed me and taught me, neither applied mine ear! [5:13] I was almost in all evil, in the midst of the congregation and assembly. [5:14] My son, drink waters out of thine own vessels, and out of thine own well of a spring! [5:15]

*Then: "Vouchsafe, O Lord, this evening...", and three prostrations.*

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 3:*

*Sticheron 1 (twice):* O Lord, Who wast crucified in the flesh and didst crucify with Thyself our old man, and pierced with a spear in the ribs didst banish the serpent the murderer of man: nail my flesh with Thy fear, and wound my soul with Thy love, that contemplating Thy passion, I may abstainingly pass through the term of the fast, ruling not only over the belly, but also over the other entrances of sin; and may offer unto Thee contrition of heart and humility of spirit for my former transgressions, from which deliver me, O Lover of mankind!

*For the Martyrs:* The Prophets, and Apostles of Christ, and the Martyrs taught [us] to hymn the consubstantial Trinity, and enlightened the deceived nations, and made the sons of men partakers with the Angels!

*Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion, the same Tone [Tone 3], Podoben: "Great is the power of Thy martyrs" (Ве́лїя му́ченикъ):*[^1142]

Beholding Him Who was born of thee hanging upon the Tree, O all-immaculate one, thou didst lament, crying aloud: O my most beloved Child, whither is Thy light-bearing beauty set, which adorned human nature?

*The commemoration of the holy Forty Martyrs begins with Tuesday of the first week of the fast, then from Monday of the first week of the fast until Monday of the sixth week, we chant Vespers and the Presanctified in like manner; at Matins we chant according to the fast, but for the Canons, (see chapter 62, fol. 193 and 194)[^1143]*

*If the [commemoration of the] Forty Martyrs happens on Monday of the second week of the fast, or the third, or the fourth, or the fifth, or the sixth: it is chanted according to the order of the Finding of the Honorable Head, (see fol. 354)[^1144]*

## Wednesday of the Second Week of Great Lent

*At Matins, the Triadica. After the first stichology, the Sessional Hymn of the Cross in the Octoechos. After the second stichology, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thy tomb, O Savior" (Гро́бъ тво́й):*[^1145]

*Sessional Hymn:* Stretched out upon the Cross, O Christ, Thou wast put to death, having slain the enemy and author of evil, the serpent, and having made alive those who died through his bite. Therefore I pray Thee: Make alive my deadened soul, O Savior, which gazes unto Thee in prayer and fasting!

*Glory... the same. Both now... Stavrotheotokion:* When the Ewe-lamb beheld Thee, the Lamb, hanging upon the Cross, O Christ, in the midst of evildoers, she cried aloud weeping, and bitterly lamenting: O my most beloved Child, what a wonder is seen! The pure Mother [cries]: Thou art recognized as the life of all the world, as Thou didst foretell!

*After the third stichology, Sessional Hymn, Tone 3, Podoben: "The beauty of Thy virginity" (Красоту̀ дѣ́вства):*[^1146]

*Sessional Hymn (twice):* Let us sound the trumpet with the trumpet of songs on this solemn day, passing through the time of abstinence and vigilantly crying aloud: Make this our life to bud forth in peace, having withered the passion of intemperance; by the power of Thy Cross, O Christ the Word, preserve Thy servants therein!

*Stavrotheotokion:*...

...A reproachful death, O compassionate One, Thou didst endure of Thine own will by crucifixion; and she that bare Thee, O Christ, beholding Thee, was consumed in her bowels, and beating herself wailed as a Mother: By her prayers, for the sake of the compassions of Thy mercy, have pity and save the world, O Thou that takest away the sin of the world!

*Triodion, by Sir Joseph, Tone 4.*

*Ode 3. Heirmos: Let my heart be established in Thy will, O Christ God...*[^1147]

*Troparion:* Thou didst stretch out Thy palms upon the Cross, taking away the sin of the hands of Adam formerly stretched out toward the intelligible tree, for the sake of the mercy of Thy compassions, O all-good Word of God!

*Troparion:* Establish my mind, shaken by the envy of the serpent; by Thy passion still the assaults of passions, O Thou Who didst suffer and grant dispassion unto the faithful!

*Troparion:* The grace of the fast hath shone forth, driving away the darkness of intemperance. Behold the acceptable time and the day of salvation; let us show forth fruits of repentance, and we shall live! (2 Cor. 6:2).

*Theotokion:* O restoration of the fallen, raise me up who have fallen into the precipice of pleasures and plunged into the abyss through grievous sins, O pure one, and guide me unto life!

*Another [Triodion], by Sir Theodore. Heirmos, Tone 3: Establish, O Lord, our hearts...*[^1148]

*Troparion:* Establish, O Lord, our hearts by Thy Cross, that we may not turn away from Thee into deceitful words and defiled deeds!

*Troparion:* Feeling Thy passion, O Master, heaven and earth were visibly changed, showing Thee forth in truth as the King of all!

*Glory... Triadikon:* Equal in honor, unoriginate, all-holy Trinity, life-creating and primordial-light Unity: Father, and Son, and Spirit, save me!

*Both now... Theotokion:* O Mother of God without husband, thou alone barest God without corrupting the purity of virginity, but remainest pure even as thou wast before childbearing!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*

*Troparion of the Cross:* We bow down, O Jesus, before Thy purple robe, the nails, the Cross, the sponge, and the spear, and we hymn Thee Who hast revived [us]!

*Katavasia. Heirmos:* Establish, O Lord, our hearts, and enlighten [us] unto Thy hymnody, to glorify Thee, O Savior, unto all ages![^1149]

*Ode 8. Heirmos: Ye hymn-singers...*[^1150]

*Troparion:* Thou Who for the multitude of Thy mercy didst deign to be numbered with the transgressors, blot out my sins, that with faith I may glorify Thee unto all ages! (Isa. 53:12).

*Troparion:* Tear up the handwriting of my sins with Thy spear, and heal the sicknesses of my heart, O Lord, which is wounded by the arrows of the malice of deceitful demons! (Col. 2:14).

*Troparion:* Wash my darkened heart from the burden of sins with Thy blood that flowed from Thy side, O my Christ, that I may glorify Thee unto all ages!

*Theotokion:* O Virgin, who didst uncreatedly bring forth the heavenly ear of grain that feeds all things by divine power, fill my hungry, humble soul!

*Another Heirmos [Sir Theodore]: In the flame unto the children...*[^1151]

*Troparion:* Rejoice, O Cross, through which in a single moment the robber was revealed as a theologian, crying aloud: Remember me, O Lord, in Thy Kingdom! Show us forth to be partakers of his portion! (Luke 23:42).

*Troparion:* Pierced [with the spear], O Christ, Thou dost turn back the flaming sword and open Paradise again unto men, entering wherein we ever delight in Thine immortal life! (Gen. 3:24).

*Glory... Triadikon:* With the Father let us worship the Son and the Holy Spirit in one essence, unceasingly crying with clay lips: Glory in the highest unto God in Trinity!

*Both now... Theotokion:* Thou bringest forth a Child while remaining a virgin, O only God-graced one: a great mystery, a dreadful wonder! For thou hast borne God incarnate, the Savior of the world!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*

*Troparion of the Cross:* O Christ God, the Hope of the ends of the earth, vouchsafe us quietly to cross the deep of the good fast through Thy pilotage, saving us from the tempest of transgressions!

*We praise, we bless, and we worship the Lord:*

*Katavasia. Heirmos:* Him Who descended in the flame unto the Hebrew children with divine power, and appeared as Lord: bless, ye priests, and exalt Him above all forever![^1152]

*Ode 9. Heirmos: The life-receiving fountain...*[^1153]

*Troparion:* Elisha, by fasting, raised up the dead youth, as it is written; and having fasted, let us the faithful hasten to mortify the carnal mind, that we may obtain life there! (4 Kings 4:32–37 [LXX 4 Kings 4 / MT 2 Kings 4]).

*Troparion:* Woe is me, O soul! Dreadful is the tribunal, and dreadful is the sentence of the Judge! Hasten, repent, stand in awe of Christ Who was hanged upon the Cross for thy sake and delivers the faithful from condemnation!

*Troparion:* Open unto me the doors of repentance, shut the entrances of my passions, O Christ, Who through Thy crucifixion didst make the entrance of Paradise readily accessible unto the robber, that I may glorify Thy goodness!

*Theotokion:* Since I am cast into the deep of malice, and rambling in contrary thoughts, unto the demons...

...I submit myself, having been enslaved to pleasures: help me, O pure Virgin Mother, guiding me unto the paths of salvation!

*Another Heirmos [Sir Theodore]: On Mount Sinai...*[^1154]

*Troparion:* Of Thine own will Thou didst deliver Thyself up and bring Thyself unto the murderers; Thou didst stand before the judgment seat, beaten by the hands of those whom Thou didst create; Thou wast crucified and mocked; Thou wast pierced, O Lord; Thou didst suffer in the flesh, enduring all things mercifully, that Thou mightest save us!

*Troparion:* The angelic hosts trembled, seeing Thee upon the Cross; the luminaries hid their light, and the earth shook; all things were moved at Thine outrage, O Lord; yet by Thy divine passions Thou hast wrought salvation for us, O God!

*Glory... Triadikon:* In essence the indivisible Monad is the Super-divine Trinity, united in nature, divided properly in Persons; for being indivisible It is divided, and being One It is threefold: It is Father, and Son, and living Spirit, preserving all things!

*Both now... Theotokion:* Who hath heard of a childbearing virgin and a mother without a husband? O Mary, thou dost accomplish a wonder! But tell me, how? Search not the depths of childbearing: this is truly comprehension beyond human mind!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*

*Troparion of the Cross:* By Thy wound we all have been healed from sinful passions; for being lifted up upon the Cross, Thou didst smite with wounds the author of evil, the enemy. But account us who have passed through the time of the fast uncondemned, also to attain unto the Resurrection! (Isa. 53:5).

*Katavasia. Heirmos:* Moses beheld thee on Mount Sinai in the bush, having received unburnt the fire of the Godhead in thy womb; and Daniel beheld thee as the uncut mountain; and Isaiah cried aloud: A rod budded forth from the root of David![^1155]

*Exapostilarion, Tone...*[^1156]

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 7, Automela:*

*Sticheron 1 (twice):* O Lord, Who by Thy Cross didst destroy death that came into the world because of the eating from the tree, which Thou didst doom to destruction: do Thou Thyself, through the fast, deliver us who are filled from every soul-destroying pleasure, and vouchsafe us to work for the food that endures unto everlasting life, that we may obtain the crowns of incorruptible sweetness which Thou hast prepared for true fasters, we pray Thee! (John 6:27).*

*For the Martyrs:* Ye were revealed as luminaries of the universe, O all-lauded passion-bearers, crying unto Christ: O Lord, glory to Thee!

*Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion, Tone 7, Podoben: "No longer are we forbidden" (Не ктому̀ возбраня́еми):*[^1157]

When the all-immaculate one beheld Thee nailed of Thine own will upon the Tree, she wailed, praising Thy dominion, O Lord!

*On Wednesday of the Second Week, at the Sixth Hour.*

*Troparion of the Prophecy, Tone 5:*

*Troparion:* O Most High Who dwellest in the heavens, Who didst create every breath, save us, O God, for in Thee have we hoped, O our Savior!

*Glory... the end:* Save us, O God... *Both now... the whole:* O Most High...

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 29, Tone 4:* Unto Thee, O Lord, will I cry, and unto my God will I make supplication. (Ps. 29:9 [LXX 29:9 / MT 30:8])*[^1158]*  
*Verse:* I will exalt Thee, O Lord, for Thou hast lifted me up. (Ps. 29:2 [LXX 29:2 / MT 30:1])

*Reading from the Prophecy of Isaiah (Chapter 5:16–25):*[^1159]

And the Lord of Sabaoth shall be exalted in judgment, and the Holy God shall be glorified in righteousness. [5:16] And they that were scattered shall feed as bullocks, and lambs shall feed upon the desert places of the taken-away. [5:17] Woe unto them that draw their sins as with a long rope... [5:18] ...and their iniquities as with the thong of a heifer's yoke! [5:18] That say: Let Him make speed and hasten His work, that we may see it; and let the counsel of the Holy One of Israel draw near and come, that we may know it! [5:19] Woe unto them that call evil good, and good evil; that put darkness for light, and light for darkness; that put bitter for sweet, and sweet for bitter! [5:20] Woe unto them that are wise in their own eyes, and prudent in their own sight! [5:21] Woe unto them that are mighty among you to drink wine, and men of strength to mingle strong drink! [5:22] Who justify the wicked for rewards, and take away the righteousness of the righteous from him! [5:23] Therefore as stubble is burned by coals of fire, and is consumed by a burning flame, their root shall be as dung, and their blossom shall go up as dust: because they rejected the law of the Lord of Sabaoth, and provoked the word of the Holy One of Israel. [5:24] And the Lord was stirred up with wrath against His people, and laid His hand upon them, and smote them; and the mountains were troubled, and their carcasses became as refuse in the midst of the way: for all this His anger is not turned away, but His hand is stretched out still! [5:25]

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 30, Tone 6:* In Thee, O Lord, have I hoped, let me never be put to shame. (Ps. 30:2 [LXX 30:2 / MT 31:1])*[^1160]*  
*Verse:* In Thy righteousness deliver me and rescue me. (Ps. 30:2 [LXX 30:2 / MT 31:1])

*On that same Wednesday of the Second Week of the Fast. At Vespers.*

*On "Lord, I have cried," Stichera, Tone 4, Automela:*

*Sticheron 1:* Having taken up the spiritual fast, O brethren, speak not deceitful things with the tongue, neither set a stumbling block as an offense for a brother; but having enlightened with repentance...

...the lamp of the soul, let us cry aloud with tears unto Christ: Remit our transgressions, as Thou art the Lover of mankind!

*For the Martyrs:* O all-praised martyrs, the earth hath not concealed you, but heaven hath received you; the gates of paradise have been opened unto you. And having entered within, ye delight in the Tree of Life; pray unto Christ, to grant unto our souls peace and great mercy!

*Another Sticheron, of Kyr Joseph, Tone 3, Podoben: "Great is the power of Thy Cross" (Ве́лїе Креста̀):*[^1161]

*Sticheron 1:* By the prayers of the divine Apostles, O Lord, vouchsafe us well to accomplish the term of the fast with contrition of thought, as Thou art good and merciful, that being saved, we all may glorify Thee!

*Sticheron 2:* Thy coming is great and fearful, O Lord, wherein Thou shalt execute righteous judgment; condemn me not therefore, who am already condemned, but as God spare me, by the acceptable prayers of Thine Apostles!

*Another Sticheron, of Kyr Theodore, Tone 6, Podoben: "Having laid aside all earthly hope" (Всѐ ѿло́жше):*[^1162]

*Sticheron 3:* Apostles of Christ, luminaries unto those on earth, world-enriching treasures of the all-wise knowledge of our God: deliver from temptations those who hymn you, by your holy prayers; and granting us youthfully to complete the term of the fast, preserve our life in peace, that having well-pleasingly anticipated the holy [Passover], we may with boldness bring hymns unto Christ our God! From the Menaion, 4 [stichera].

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 31, Tone 6:* Be glad in the Lord, and rejoice, ye righteous. (Ps. 31:11 [LXX 31:11 / MT 32:11])*[^1163]*  
*Verse:* Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven. (Ps. 31:1 [LXX 31:1 / MT 32:1])

*Reading from Genesis (Chapter 4:16–26):*[^1164]

And Cain went out from the presence of God, and dwelt in the land of Naid, over against Eden. [4:16] And Cain knew his wife, and having conceived she bore Enoch; and he was building a city, and called the city after the name of his son, Enoch. [4:17] And to Enoch was born Gaidad; and Gaidad begat Maleleel; and Maleleel begat Mathusala; and Mathusala begat Lamech. [4:18] And Lamech took unto himself two wives: the name of the one was Ada, and the name of the second Sella. [4:19] And Ada bore Jobil: he was the father of those that dwell in tents, feeding cattle. [4:20] And his brother's name was Jubal: he was the one that showed the pipe and the harp. [4:21] And Sella, she also bore Thobel, and he was a hammerer, a smith in copper and iron; and the sister of Thobel was Noema. [4:22] And Lamech said unto his wives Ada and Sella: Hear my voice, ye wives of Lamech, give ear unto my words: for I have slain a man to my wounding, and a youth to my hurt! [4:23] For sevenfold vengeance hath been taken for Cain, but for Lamech seventy times seven! [4:24] And Adam knew Eve his wife, and having conceived she bore a son, and called his name Seth, saying: For God hath raised up for me another seed instead of Abel, whom Cain slew. [4:25] And to Seth was born a son, and he called his name Enos: this man hoped to call upon the name of the Lord God. [4:26]

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 32, Tone 4:* Let Thy mercy, O Lord, be upon us, according as we have hoped in Thee. (Ps. 32:22 [LXX 32:22 / MT 33:22])*[^1165]*  
*Verse:* Rejoice in the Lord, O ye righteous. (Ps. 32:1 [LXX 32:1 / MT 33:1])

*Reading from Proverbs (Chapter 5:15–6:3):*[^1166]

My son, drink waters out of thine own vessels, and out of thine own wells of a spring. [5:15] Let waters from thy spring be poured out abundantly for thee, and let thy waters go forth into thine open streets. [5:16] Let them be thine own possessions alone, and let no stranger partake with thee. [5:17] Let the spring of thy water be thine own, and rejoice with the wife of thy youth. [5:18] A hind of love, and a filly of thy favors: let her converse with thee, and let what is thine own come unto thee, and let her be with thee at all times; for being encompassed in her friendship, thou shalt be multiplied. [5:19] Be not much with a strange woman, neither embrace her with thine arms. [5:20] For before the eyes of God are the ways of a man, and He inspects all his courses. [5:21] Iniquities ensnare a man, and each one is bound with the cords of his own sins. [5:22] Such a man dies with the uninstructed; and from the abundance of his livelihood he is cast out, and he perishes through folly. [5:23] My son, if thou become surety for thy friend, thou shalt surrender thine hand to the enemy. [6:1] For a strong snare unto a man are his own lips, and he is taken captive by the words of his mouth. [6:2] Do, my son, what I command thee, and save thyself! [6:3] *The rest, (see fol. 354).*

## Thursday of the Second Week of Great Lent

*At Matins, the Triadica. After the first stichology, the Apostolic Sessional Hymns of the Octoechos, with the Theotokion. After the second stichology, Sessional Hymn, Tone 3, Podoben: "The beauty of Thy virginity" (Красоту̀ дѣ́вства):*[^1167]

*Sessional Hymn:* The vine of Christ hath brought you forth as beautiful clusters, gushing forth the saving...

...sweetness unto the earth, O God-bearing Apostles. Therefore deliver me from the drunkenness of pleasures by your prayers, granting a stream of contrition unto my soul in the divine day of the fast, that having been saved, I may obtain life! (Twice).

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:* Taking into mind the wealth of thy tender mercy and the unconquerable dominion of thy might, I have fled unto thy shelter, held fast by grief and sorely in perplexity; I cry from the depth of my heart with tears: O Virgin Theotokos, help me, the only protectress of the world!

*After the third stichology, Sessional Hymn, Tone 6, Podoben: "O Lord, standing before" (Го́споди престоя́ще):*[^1168]

*Sessional Hymn (twice):* O Lord, be Thou favorable unto us in this divine season, and vouchsafe us ever to pour forth tears from the heart for the washing away of the defilements of the soul, unto the blossoming of Thy holy commandments; that thus fasting, we may worthily be well-pleasing unto Thee; and deign that all may behold Thy most honorable Passion, by the prayers of Thine Apostles that save the world: Glory to Thee!

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:* O all-immaculate fountain of tender mercy, honorable Virgin Mother and Theotokos, richly pour forth upon us, O pure one, and grant unto us the remission of transgressions; for thou art our protectress and divine shelter!

*Triodion [Canon of Three Odes], of Kyr Joseph, Tone 3. Ode 4:*[^1169]

*Ode 4, Tone 3. Heirmos: In the years Thou art known:*

*Troparion:* Having quenched the drunkenness of soul-corrupting pleasures with the water of contrition, let us enrich ourselves through fasting!

*Troparion:* Fast, O soul, from soul-corrupting food, and take delight in the contemplation of good things, that thou mayest attain unto the heavenly banquet!

*Troparion:* Being coals of the immaterial fire, burn up the matter of my passions, O divine Apostles of the Savior!

*Theotokion:* O pure Virgin who didst give flesh unto Christ from thine own in loan, mortify the passions of my flesh, O mother who gavest birth to Life!

*Another Triodion [Canon of Three Odes], of Kyr Theodore, Tone 6. Ode 4:*[^1170]

*Ode 4, Tone 6. Heirmos: Having heard, the Prophet:*

*Troparion:* O twelveness of the Apostles: Peter, Paul, James, and John, Andrew, Bartholomew, Philip, Thomas, and Matthew, and James with Simon, and Jude: offer prayers unto Christ, that we may be saved!

*Troparion:* Having cast the net of teachings strangely into the sea of life, mystically ye caught the nations like the hundred and fifty and three fishes of old, bringing them unto the Lord, O holy Apostles! (John 21:11).

*Glory... Triadicon:* I glorify the Son from the Father, and the Spirit, as light and rays from the sun: the One indeed begottenly, as a generation, and the Other proceedingly, as a procession: the co-unoriginate single Trinity, worshipped by all creation!

*Both now... Theotokion:* O Virgin who didst bear the Infant, yet didst preserve purity: thou hast appeared as pure, having given birth to God and man, the selfsame One in both natures; thy wonder, O Virgin Mother, amazes every hearing and thought!

*Troparion:* Ye are the light of the world, even as Christ said unto you, by the shining of the Word; but pray, O Apostles, that we may magnanimously pass through the stadium of abstinence, and worship His Resurrection! (Matt. 5:14).

*Heirmos:* The Prophet heard of Thy coming, O Lord, and was afraid: that Thou wast to be born of a Virgin and appear unto men, and he said: I heard the report of Thee and was afraid: glory to Thy power! (Hab. 3:2).

*Ode 8, Tone 3. Heirmos: Unto the children in the flame:*[^1171]

*Troparion:* Having been slain by many sins, I bring a dead soul into life; therefore have compassion upon me by your life-bearing prayers, O God-beholders, disciples of the Savior!

*Troparion:* Having been seized by the darkness of sin, I have in truth drawn near to the hades of despair; therefore enlighten me, being mystical rays of the Sun of Glory, O God-beholders!

*Troparion:* Abstain from passions, and feed [on the virtues], O passionate soul; for the setting aside of foods is a fast unacceptable to righteousness and unprofitable, if there be not also amendment of sins!

*Theotokion:* Moses foresaw thee as the bush burning with fire, O Virgin Mother of God; therefore quench the furnace of my passions, and snatch me from the fire of Gehenna, and save me!

*Another Heirmos, Tone 6: "Him Whom the hosts..." (Е҆́гоже во́инства):*[^1172]

*Troparion:* As a twelve-tribed offspring from Jacob, another twelveness of Apostles from Thee appeared in the world, O Christ, through whom every faithful one was begotten in the word, hymning Thee unto the ages!

*Troparion:* Having drowned the chariots of the spiritual Pharaoh mystically as in a river, ye brought out the people of the Lord unto the land of God-contemplation, O Apostles, hymning the Giver of life unto the ages!

*Triadicon:* I hymn one God according to essence, I hymn three hypostases distinctly, different [in person] but not of different nature; because the Godhead is one, a single dominion in three: namely the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit!

*Theotokion:* Truly coming forth from thy radiant womb as a Bridegroom from His chamber, Christ is a great Light unto those that are in darkness; for having shone forth as the Sun of righteousness, O pure one, He enlightened the world!

*Troparion:* Mystics and enthroned companions of Christ, who ever diligently pray for us sinners: pray also now, that we may pass through the fast in all honor!

*We praise, bless, and worship the Lord.*

*Heirmos:* Him Whom the heavenly hosts glorify, and before Whom Cherubim and Seraphim tremble: let every breath and creation hymn, bless, and supreme-exalt unto all ages!

*Ode 9, Tone 3. Heirmos: On Mount Sinai:*[^1173]

*Troparion:* Having become rivers of the spiritual fountain, and piously gushing forth living water unto pure hearts, dry up the streams of my sin by your prayers, O Apostles, and guide me unto the path of salvation!

*Troparion:* A wave of sin tempest-tosses my wretched soul: stretch forth Thine hand unto me as unto Peter, O good Pilot, that the deep of despair cover me not, and that I become not food for the soul-corrupting sea-monster, O most merciful Christ! (Matt. 14:31).

*Troparion:* The choir of the Apostles and the ranks of the Angels pray Thee, O Jesus, King of all: according to the multitude of Thy tender mercies, grant unto Thy people deliverance from evils, amendment of life, and the inheritance of Thy Kingdom!

*Theotokion:* Virginity and childbearing met together beyond nature in thee, O ark of honorable sanctification, pure Virgin Mother; therefore with faith I cry unto thee: Wholly sanctify me, wholly deliver me from every working of the passions that afflict me!

*Another Heirmos, Tone 6: "The seedless conception..." (Безсѣ́мена зача́тїѧ):*[^1174]

*Troparion:* In the world as bodiless, and in the flesh as Angels, bearing the one consubstantial Word, ye drew the nations unto the one faith of Christ, having by understanding refuted the wise and rhetors as foolish, O all-blessed Apostles!

*Troparion:* Peter, rock and foundation of the faith; Paul, preacher and teacher...

...of the nations; sons of Zebedee, with the remaining eight: pray diligently unto Christ, that we may powerfully pass through the stadium of the fast!

*Triadicon:* O Father, sole Begetter of the One, of the only-begotten Son; and Thou, O Light from the one Light, radiance of the Light; and Thou, O Holy Spirit, sole [Spirit] of the one God, truly being Lord of the Lord: O Holy Trinity, Unity, save me who theologize Thee!

*Theotokion:* The wonder of thy childbearing astonishes me, O all-immaculate one: how conceivest thou without human seed? Tell me, how art thou a virgin, having given birth as a Mother? That which is beyond nature having received by faith, I shall worship Him Who was born; for whatsoever He wills, that He can do also!

*Troparion:* By the power of the Spirit having gone unto kings and princes, ye in no wise feared fire, nor sword; ye conquered every deceit, and save men, being soldiers of the Lord, O all-blessed Apostles!

*Heirmos:* A seedless conception, an ineffable childbearing: of an unwedded Mother, an incorrupt offspring! The birth of God makes nature anew: therefore all generations orthodoxly magnify thee as Mother and Bride of God!

*And "It is truly meet...". Exapostilarion, Tone...*[^1175]

*At the Aposticha, Idiomelon Stichera, Tone 8:*

*Sticheron 1 (twice):* The time of repentance and of eternal life, the ascetic labor of the fast is our intercessor, if we stretch forth our hands unto well-doing; for nothing so saves the soul as giving unto the needy: almsgiving mingled with fasting delivers a man from death. Let us kiss this, to which nothing is equal, for it is sufficient to save our souls!

*Verse: We were filled in the morning with Thy mercy... (Ps. 89:14 [LXX 89:14 / MT 90:14])*[^1176] *For the Martyrs:* Having well clothed yourselves in the armor of faith, and armed yourselves with the sign of the Cross, ye proved to be valiant soldiers, manfully resisting the tormentors, and ye destroyed the deceit of the devil; having become victors, ye were accounted worthy of crowns: pray now unto Christ for us, that our souls may be saved!

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:* I flee unto thy protection, O holy Virgin Theotokos; I know that I shall obtain salvation, for thou art able, O pure one, to help me!

*On that same Thursday of the Second Week of the Fast, at the Sixth Hour.*

*Troparion of the Prophecy, Tone 1:*

*Troparion:* Raise us up who are fallen, and turn us unto Thyself who have turned away, O God, as Thou art the Lover of mankind, Who upholdest the ends of the earth!

*Glory... the end: [Turn us unto Thyself...]. Both now... the whole: [Raise us up who are fallen...].*

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 33, Tone 6:* I sought the Lord, and He heard me, and delivered me from all my afflictions. (Ps. 33:5 [LXX 33:5 / MT 34:4])*[^1177]*  
*Verse:* I will bless the Lord at all times. (Ps. 33:2 [LXX 33:2 / MT 34:1])

*Reading from the Prophecy of Isaiah (Chapter 6:1–12):*[^1178]

In the year that King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord sitting upon a high and lifted up throne, and the temple was full of His glory. [6:1] And the Seraphim stood round about Him: each one had six wings; with two they covered their face, and with two they covered their feet, and with two they flew. [6:2] And one cried unto another, and said: Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of Sabaoth: the whole earth is full of His glory! [6:3] And the lintel was lifted up at the voice wherewith they cried, and the temple... [6:4] ...was filled with smoke. [6:4] And I said: Woe is me, wretched man! for I am pricked to the heart; because being a man, and having unclean lips, I dwell in the midst of a people having unclean lips: and mine eyes have seen the King, the Lord of Sabaoth! [6:5] And there was sent unto me one of the Seraphim, and he had in his hand a live coal, which he had taken with tongs from off the altar. [6:6] And he touched my mouth, and said: Lo, this hath touched thy lips, and shall take away thine iniquities, and shall purge thy sins! [6:7] And I heard the voice of the Lord, saying: Whom shall I send, and who will go unto this people? And I said: Here am I, send me! [6:8] And He said: Go, and say unto this people: By hearing ye shall hear, and shall not understand; and seeing ye shall see, and shall not perceive. [6:9] For the heart of this people is grown fat, and their ears hear heavily, and their eyes have they closed; lest they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and be converted, and I should heal them. [6:10] And I said: How long, Lord? And He said: Until the cities be desolate without inhabitant, and the houses without men, and the land be left desolate. [6:11] And after this God shall remove men far away, and they that are left upon the earth shall be multiplied. [6:12]

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 34, Tone 6:* Arise, O Lord, and attend unto my judgment. (Ps. 34:23 [LXX 34:23 / MT 35:23])*[^1179]*  
*Verse:* Even unto my cause, my God and my Lord! (Ps. 34:23 [LXX 34:23 / MT 35:23])

*On that same Thursday evening, on "Lord, I have cried," Stichera, Tone 4, of Joseph, Podoben: "Thou hast given a sign" (Да́лъ есѝ зна́меніе):*[^1180]

*Sticheron 1:* Pierced in the ribs, and hanged upon the Tree, [Thou didst spring forth] life unto me...

...Thou didst spring forth unto me who was slain through the malice of the serpent by the eating of the tree. Therefore, O Christ, I glorify Thee; have tender mercy, and show me to be a worshipper of Thy Sufferings and Resurrection, having accomplished the stadium of the fast in contrition!

*Sticheron 2:* Having found sickness from the garden, Thou didst drive the first-created out of Paradise; but being nailed as man upon the Tree, O Savior, Thou bringest him in. Therefore I cry unto Thee, O Deliverer: come upon me and heal me from my sicknesses, having purified me by fasting, and repentance, and tears, O most good Jesus, Savior of our souls!

*Another Sticheron, of Kyr Theodore, Tone 5, Podoben: "O Lord, at the time of Moses" (Го́споди при Мѡѷсе́и):*[^1181]

*Sticheron 3:* O Lord, we hymn Thy life-creating Cross: for this has blossomed forth life in the world, having slain death; which also now we bring unto Thee in prayer in these holy days: strengthen us who fast, and grant strength against the passions and victory over the world, for the multitude of Thy mercy, O Lover of mankind! *And from the Menaion, 3 [stichera]. Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 35, Tone 4:* Thy mercy, O Lord, is in the heavens, and Thy truth reaches unto the clouds. (Ps. 35:6 [LXX 35:6 / MT 36:5])*[^1182]*  
*Verse:* Thy righteousness is as the mountains of God; Thy judgments are a great abyss. (Ps. 35:7 [LXX 35:7 / MT 36:6])

*Reading from Genesis (Chapter 5:1–24):*[^1183]

This is the book of the generation of men, in the day that God made Adam: in the likeness of God He made him. [5:1] Male and female He made them, and blessed them; and He called his name Adam, in the day that He made them. [5:2] And Adam lived two hundred and thirty years, and begat a son after his own form, and after his own image, and called his name Seth. [5:3] And the days of Adam... [5:4] ...which he lived after he begat Seth, were seven hundred years, and he begat sons and daughters. [5:4] And all the days of Adam which he lived were nine hundred and thirty years, and he died. [5:5] And Seth lived two hundred and five years, and begat Enos. [5:6] And Seth lived after he begat Enos seven hundred and seven years, and begat sons and daughters. [5:7] And all the days of Seth were nine hundred and twelve years, and he died. [5:8] And Enos lived one hundred and ninety years, and begat Cainan. [5:9] And Enos lived after he begat Cainan seven hundred and fifty years, and begat sons and daughters. [5:10] And all the days of Enos were nine hundred and five years, and he died. [5:11] And Cainan lived one hundred and seventy years, and begat Maleleel. [5:12] And Cainan lived after he begat Maleleel seven hundred and forty years, and begat sons and daughters. [5:13] And all the days of Cainan were nine hundred and ten years, and he died. [5:14] And Maleleel lived one hundred and sixty-five years, and begat Jared. [5:15] And Maleleel lived after he begat Jared seven hundred and thirty years, and begat sons and daughters. [5:16] And all the days of Maleleel were eight hundred and ninety-five years, and he died. [5:17] And Jared lived one hundred and sixty-two years, and begat Enoch. [5:18] And Jared lived after he begat Enoch eight hundred years, and begat sons and daughters. [5:19] And all the days of Jared were nine hundred and sixty-two years, and he died. [5:20] And Enoch lived one hundred and sixty-five years, and begat Methuselah. [5:21] And Enoch was well-pleasing unto God, and lived... [5:22] ...after he begat Methuselah, two hundred years, and begat sons and daughters. [5:22] And all the days of Enoch were three hundred and sixty-five years. [5:23] And Enoch was well-pleasing unto God, and was not found, because God translated him. [5:24]

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 36, Tone 6:* Wait on the Lord, and keep His way. (Ps. 36:34 [LXX 36:34 / MT 37:34])*[^1184]*  
*Verse:* Fret not thyself because of evildoers, neither be thou envious against them that work iniquity. (Ps. 36:1 [LXX 36:1 / MT 37:1])

*Reading from Proverbs (Chapter 6:3–20):*[^1185]

Do, my son, what I command thee, and save thyself: for thou art come into evil hands on behalf of thy friend; be not faint-hearted, but stir up thy friend, for whom thou hast become surety. [6:3] Give not sleep to thine eyes, nor slumber to thine eyelids, [6:4] that thou mayest be saved as a roe from a snare, and as a bird from a net. [6:5] Go to the ant, O sluggard, and having seen his ways, emulate him, and be wiser than he! [6:6] For having no husbandman, nor anyone to compel him, neither being under a master, [6:7] he prepares his food in the summer, and makes great provision in the harvest. [6:8] [Or go to the bee, and learn how industrious she is, and how honorable a work she performs; whose labors kings and private men bring unto health: and she is beloved of all and glorious, though she be weak in strength, having honored wisdom, she is advanced.]*[^1186]* How long wilt thou lie down, O sluggard? and when wilt thou arise from sleep? [6:9] Thou sleepest a little, and sittest a little, and slumberest a little, and a little foldest thine hands over thy chest: [6:10] then poverty shall come upon thee as an evil traveler... [6:11] ...poverty, and want as a swift runner. [6:11] [But if thou be diligent, thy harvest shall arrive as a fountain, and want as an evil runner shall depart from thee.]*[^1187]* A foolish man and a transgressor of the law walks in paths that are not good: [6:12] the same winks with his eye, stamps with his foot, and teaches by gestures of his fingers. [6:13] With a perverse heart he devises evil, at all times such a one stirs up tumults for a city. [6:14] Therefore his destruction shall come suddenly: severance and ruin incurable. [6:15] For he rejoices in all things that the Lord hates, and is ruined through impurity of soul: [6:16] the eye of the insolent, a tongue unrighteous, hands shedding righteous blood, [6:17] and a heart devising evil thoughts, and feet hastening to do evil. [6:18] [Consuming:]*[^1188]* an unrighteous witness kindles lies, and sends judgments in the midst of brethren. [6:19] My son, keep the laws of thy father, and reject not the instructions of thy mother! [6:20]

*Then: "Vouchsafe, O Lord..."*

*At the Aposticha, Idiomelon Stichera, Tone 5:*

*Sticheron 1 (twice):* Not having fasted according to the commandment of the Creator, from the garden of understanding the first-created brought forth death through disobedience, and were estranged from the Tree of Life and the sweetness of Paradise. Therefore, let us fast, O ye faithful, from corruptible foods and all-destructive passions, that we may embrace life from the divine Cross, and with the prudent thief return unto the first fatherland, receiving great mercy from Christ God!

*For the Martyrs:* Having disregarded all earthly things, and manfully ventured unto torments...

...ye failed not of your blessed hopes, but became heirs of the Heavenly Kingdom, O all-praised martyrs! Having boldness unto God the Lover of mankind, entreat peace for the world, and great mercy for our souls!

*Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion, Tone 5, Podoben: "Rejoice, O container of ascetics" (Ра́дꙋйсѧ по́стникѡмъ):*[^1189]

The ewe-lamb, once beholding her Lamb hastening unto slaughter, eagerly followed, crying aloud these words unto Him: Whither goest Thou, my sweetest Child, O Christ? For what cause dost Thou run this swift course without indolence, O longsuffering One? O Jesus most desired, sinless, greatly merciful Lord! Grant a word unto Thy handmaid, O my all-beloved Son; overlook me not in silence, O compassionate One, who strangely gave Thee birth, O Benefactor God, and grant great mercy unto the world!

## Friday of the Second Week of Great Lent

*At Matins, the Triadica of the Tone. After the first stichology, the Sessional Hymns in the Octoechos. After the second stichology, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Speedily anticipate" (Ско́ро предварѝ):*[^1190]

*Sessional Hymn (twice):* Having become higher through fasting from creeping passions below, let us exalt the Lord Who was lifted up upon the Cross and Who exalted the world; let us drink the drink of contrition in perception; let us today receive into mind also the hour wherein we shall stand before the eternal Judge!

*Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion:* Thy Mother who knew not wedlock, when she beheld Thee lifted up upon the Cross, groaning and weeping, uttered such words: What is this new and strange wonder, O my Son!...

...how hath the lawless people nailed Thee to the Cross, Thee the Life of all, my sweetest Light!

*After the third stichology, Sessional Hymn, of Kyr Theodore, Tone 5, Podoben: "Today shines forth" (Сїѧ́етъ дне́сь):*[^1191]

*Sessional Hymn (twice):* O Lord, the grace of Thy Cross shines forth, irradiating the whole universe; it destroys the power of the demons, and now adorns the course of the fast, wherein strengthening us, have mercy on us!

*Stavrotheotokion, Tone 5, Podoben: "The Word co-unoriginate" (Собезнача́лное [Сло́во]):*[^1192]

When Thy Mother, who bore Thee without pain, beheld Thee lifted up upon the Tree, she wept with lamentation and cried out: Woe is me, my sweetest Son! I am consumed in soul, beholding Thee upon the Cross between two evildoers, nailing up the vengeance of the evildoer!

*Triodion [Canon of Three Odes], of Kyr Joseph, Tone 4. Ode 5:*[^1193]

*Ode 5, Tone 4. Heirmos: The ungodly shall not behold Thy glory, O Christ:*

*Troparion:* Of Thine own will, O Master, Thou wast lifted up upon the Cross, and cast down the enemy; but me, cast down by my own will into the pit through lusts, set upright by Thy tender mercy!

*Troparion:* Me, darkened in soul by disorderly passions, guide with Thy light, O Jesus, Who darkened the sun while hanging upon the Cross, and enlightened all the ends of the universe!

*Troparion:* Vouchsafe me, O Christ, peacefully to sail across the deep of the fast, calming the waves of my thought, and pilot me into the haven of the Resurrection!

*Theotokion:* With pure mind let those who lead pure lives honor the beauty of Jacob; adorning ourselves with divine deeds, let us graciously hymn her as the Mother of our God!

*Another Triodion [Canon of Three Odes], of Kyr Theodore, Tone 5. Ode 5:*[^1194]

*Ode 5, Tone 5. Heirmos: Unto those who worship from the night:*[^1195]

*Troparion:* Being crucified, Thou deliverest me from corruption; and being pierced, Thou makest me immortal. I glorify Thine ineffable mercy, for Thou hast come, O Christ, to save me!

*Troparion:* Having stretched forth Thy palms upon the Cross, Thou slewest the spiritual Amalek, saving Thy people, O Lord; therefore we hymn Thy dominion!

*Glory... Triadicon:* In three Persons, the Godhead, one all-transcendent Principle, let us hymn: the unoriginate Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit!

*Both now... Theotokion:* Him Whom heaven could not contain, thou didst conceive in the womb and give birth unto: O strange and ineffable wonder! Therefore all of us hymn thee, O all-immaculate one!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*

*Troparion:* Having endured crucifixion for my sake, having drunk vinegar, and having said: "It is finished": finish my stadium of the fast, accounting me worthy to behold Thy Resurrection! (John 19:30).

*Heirmos:* Unto those who worship Thee from the night, O Christ, have mercy, and grant peace, because light and Thy commandments have become healing unto Thy servants, O Lover of mankind!

*Ode 8, Tone 4. Heirmos: The pious children in the furnace:*[^1196]

*Troparion:* Nailed upon the Cross through tender mercy, Thou openedst Paradise unto the thief; heal me also, broken by demonic cruelty and having received an all-fleshly wound in soul, opening unto me the doors of repentance by Thy love for mankind!

*Troparion:* Having enlightened the flesh by fasting, let us enrich the soul with virtues, by feeding the poor, buying an inexhaustible treasure in the heavens, and let us cry aloud: Hymn the Lord, ye works, and supreme-exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparion:* At Thy Passion creation was shaken, beholding Thee nailed upon the Cross, O most good Savior; therefore...

...I pray Thee, who am ever shaken by the serpent's assaults: establish my mind, O compassionate One, upon the unshakable rock of Thy desires!

*Theotokion:* O closed gate of God, through which the Lord alone passed, guide me unto divine paths, and open unto me the gates of salvation, O thou who hast found favor with God; for unto thee I flee, O Virgin, the only protectress of the human race! (Ezek. 44:2).

*Another Heirmos, Tone 5: "The Creator of creation..." (Творца̀ тва́ри):*[^1197]

*Troparion:* O all-holy Tree, whereon Thou, my Christ, wast crucified: hymning, I supreme-bless Thee unto all ages!

*Troparion:* On Golgotha, having crucified Thee, the lawless slew Thee, O Christ; yet Thou livest, and savest us unto the ages!

*Let us bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit: the Lord.*

*Triadicon:* In a marvelous manner befitting God the Trinity is distinguished, and abides indivisible, as God, Whom we supreme-exalt unto all ages!

*Both now... Theotokion:* Make prayer, O all-immaculate one, for those who hymn thee, to be delivered from all assaults and tribulations!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*
