*Troparion:* Having brought me to life by the power of Thy Cross, O Lord, vouchsafe me with good courage to complete the course of the fast!

*We praise, bless, and worship the Lord.*

*Heirmos:* The Creator of creation, before Whom the Angels tremble: hymn, ye peoples, and supreme-exalt unto all ages!

*Ode 9, Tone 4. Heirmos: A stone cut without hands from a mountain:*[^1198]

*Troparion:* The Prophet foresaw Thee, O Savior, as a stone cut from the mountain of the Virgin, Who crushest the stones by Thy Crucifixion; therefore, as Thou art all-compassionate, liberate me who am weighed down by the stones of insensibility! (Dan. 2:34, 45).

*Troparion:* Fast from malice, O my soul, enjoying...

...divine love; shut the door of all-passionate visions, shutting the entrance against wickedness by temperance and prayer!

*Troparion:* Save me who am condemned, O Master, my Savior, Who by Thy Cross didst condemn the enemy; and show me not to be liable unto Gehenna, defiled by passions and darkened by sins!

*Theotokion:* Spare me, O Christ, when Thou comest to judge the world with glory; disperse the gloom of my evils by the prayers of her who gave Thee birth, and make me an heir of Thy Heavenly Kingdom!

*Another Heirmos, Tone 5: "Rejoice, O Isaiah..." (И҆са́їа ликꙋ́й):*[^1199]

*Troparion:* Once for all by Thy Crucifixion Thou openest Paradise again, wherein taking my fill of life I rejoice, being delivered from the death of eternal disobedience; therefore, O Lover of mankind, as my God I magnify Thee!

*Troparion:* The instrument of the curse has appeared as the seal of blessing, even Thy life-creating Cross, O Lord, beholding whereon we who were formerly dead are brought to life, and hymning Thee as Master, we magnify Thee!

*Glory... Triadicon:* One in essence I hymn Thee, O unoriginate Trinity, honorable, life-originating, indivisible Unity: unbegotten Father, and begotten Word and Son, and Holy Spirit: save us who hymn Thee!

*Both now... Theotokion:* Beyond mind is thy childbearing, O Mother of God: for without man was the conception in thee, and virginal was the birth, for God is the Offspring: Whom magnifying, we call thee blessed, O Virgin!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*

*Troparion:* Honorable Cross, my strength and refuge...

...be now my enlightenment in abstinence, gladdening and cleansing me, and delivering me from temptations, that glorifying thee, I may magnify Christ the Master!

*Heirmos:* Rejoice, O Isaiah! For the Virgin had in womb, and bore a Son, Emmanuel, God and man, Dayspring is His name; Whom magnifying, we call thee blessed, O Virgin! (Isa. 7:14; 9:6; Zech. 6:12).

*The Photogogic [Exapostilarion] of the Tone.*

*At the Aposticha, Idiomelon Stichera, Tone 8:*

*Sticheron 1 (twice):* The fast that slays the passions having arrived, promises to heal those who are afflicted by sin. Let us honor it as a God-given helper; having received the God-written tablets by Moses, let us not be partakers with him who through intemperance cast them down and broke them, whose bodies fell in the wilderness! Let us not mourn like the Jews, but be enlightened in the manner of the Church; let us not play the hypocrite like the Pharisees, but adorn ourselves in an evangelical manner, glorying in the Cross of Christ, the Deliverer of our souls!

*For the Martyrs:* What shall we call you, O saints? Cherubim? For upon you Christ rested. Seraphim? For unceasingly ye glorify Him. Angels? For ye turned away from the body. Powers? For ye work in wonders. Many are your names, and greater are your gifts: pray that our souls may be saved!

*Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion, Tone 8:* What wonder and terror is this! The Virgin of the Lord cried out as a mother: The pangs which I knew not in giving birth unto Thee, O Son, pierce my heart sharp as swords! I endure not seeing Thee nailed upon the Cross, O Light of mine eyes! Make haste therefore, arise, that I may glorify with the world this Thy divine Dispensation!

*The rest: (see fol. 273).*[^1200]

*Note: That on the Fridays of the Weeks [of the Fast], we sing the Hours, the 3rd, 6th, and 9th, together, as was indicated on Wednesday of this week (see fol. 244 in order)[^1201]. But at Vespers we set aside the prostrations from the beginning, except for those concerning which (see fol. 288)[^1202].*

*On the same Friday, or at the Sixth Hour.*

*Troparion of the Prophecy, Tone 1:*

*Troparion (twice):* By night and by day we fall down before Thee, O Lord, that Thou mayest grant remission of sins unto our souls, that in peace we may worship Thee and glorify Thee, O Lover of mankind!

*Glory... the end:* That in peace... *Both now (twice):* By night and by day...

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 37, Tone 4:* O Lord, rebuke me not in Thine anger, nor chasten me in Thy wrath. (Ps. 37:2 [LXX 37:2 / MT 38:1])  
*Verse:* For Thine arrows are fastened in me. (Ps. 37:3 [LXX 37:3 / MT 38:2])

*Reading from the Prophecy of Isaiah (Chapter 7:1–4a):*[^1203]

It came to pass in the days of Ahaz, the son of Jotham, the son of Uzziah, king of Judah, that Rezin the king of Syria [Aram], and Pekah the son of Remaliah, king of Israel, went up toward Jerusalem to war against it, and could not prevail to conquer and take it. [7:1] And it was told unto the house of David, saying: Syria is agreed with Ephraim. And his heart was moved, and the heart of his people, as when a tree is shaken by the wind in a grove. [7:2] And the Lord said unto Isaiah: Go forth now to meet Ahaz, thou, and Shear-jashub thy remaining son, to the conduit of the upper pool in the highway of the fuller’s field. [7:3] And thou shalt say unto him: Take heed to keep silence, and fear not, neither let thy soul be faint because of these two smoking firebrands: [7:4a] when the anger of fury is fierce, again I will heal, even the son of Aram and the son of Remaliah. [7:4b] For Ephraim and the son of Remaliah have taken evil counsel against thee, saying: [7:5] Let us go up against Judah, and vex it, and talking with them let us turn them unto ourselves, and set up the son of Tabeel as king in it. [7:6] Thus saith the Lord of Sabaoth: This counsel shall not stand, neither shall it come to pass. [7:7] But the head of Syria is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin; yet within threescore and five years the kingdom of Ephraim shall fail from being a people. [7:8] And the head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is the son of Remaliah. If ye believe not, neither shall ye understand. [7:9] And the Lord spake again unto Ahaz, saying: [7:10] Ask thee a sign of the Lord thy God, in the depth or in the height! [7:11] And Ahaz said: I will not ask, neither will I tempt the Lord. [7:12] And Isaiah said: Hear ye now, O house of David! Is it a small thing for you to weary men, that ye will also weary the Lord? [7:13] Therefore the Lord Himself shall give you a sign:[^1204] [7:14a]

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 38, Tone 6:* Hear my prayer, O Lord, and my supplication. (Ps. 38:13 [LXX 38:13 / MT 39:12])  
*Verse:* I said: I will take heed to my ways, that I sin not with my tongue. (Ps. 38:2 [LXX 38:2 / MT 39:1])

*Troparion:* Let Thy tender mercies speedily prevent us...

*On the same Friday Evening [at Vespers].*

*We chant the Kathisma:* Unto the Lord when I was in affliction: (Kathisma 18) *in the Tone of the week. And after each Antiphon the Priest makes a little litany. And concerning the rest: (see fol. 234)[^1205].*

*At "Lord, I have cried", Stichera on 10. Idiomelon of the day, Tone 4:*

*Sticheron:* Now is the acceptable time, now is the day of salvation!

...in the multitude of Thy mercy visit my soul, and lighten the burden of my transgressions, O Thou Who alone art the Lover of mankind! *(twice)*

*Then, 4 Martyr Stichera in order of the Tone from the Oktoechos. And from the Menaion of the saint, 3 [stichera], on 4. Glory: Idiomelon, see the Typikon; if of St. John, in the Tone of the day. Both now: Dogmatikon Theotokion from the Oktoechos in the same Tone. Entrance with censer and candle (see fol. 236)[^1206]. O Gladsome Light:*

*Prokeimenon of the Readings, Psalm 39, Tone 4:* Thy mercy and Thy truth have continually upheld me. (Ps. 39:12 [LXX 39:12 / MT 40:11])  
*Verse:* Patiently I waited for the Lord, and He inclined unto me. (Ps. 39:2 [LXX 39:2 / MT 40:1])

*Reading from Genesis (Chapter 5:32; 6:1–7a):*[^1207]

And Noah was five hundred years old, and he begat three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japhs. [5:32] And it came to pass, when men began to multiply on the earth, and daughters were born unto them, [6:1] that the sons of God saw the daughters of men, that they were fair; and they took them wives of all whom they chose. [6:2] And the Lord God said: My Spirit shall not abide in these men forever, for that they are flesh; yet their days shall be a hundred and twenty years. [6:3] There were giants on the earth in those days; and also after that, when the sons of God came in unto the daughters of men, and bare children to them, the same were the giants from of old, men of renown. [6:4] And the Lord God saw that the wickedness of men was multiplied on the earth, and that everyone in his heart intently imagins evil all his days. [6:5] And God repented that He had made man on the earth, and He deliberated; [6:6] and He said: I will destroy... [6:7a] ...man whom I have created from the face of the earth, from man even unto beast, and from creeping things even unto the fowls of heaven; for I repent that I have made them. [6:7b] But Noah found grace before the Lord God. [6:8]

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 40, Tone 6:* I said: Lord, be merciful unto me; heal my soul, for I have sinned against Thee. (Ps. 40:5 [LXX 40:5 / MT 41:4])  
*Verse:* Blessed is he that considers the poor and needy. (Ps. 40:2 [LXX 40:2 / MT 41:1])

*Reading from the Proverbs (Chapter 6:20–31a):*[^1208]

My son, keep the laws of thy father, and forsake not the instruction of thy mother. [6:20] Bind them upon thy heart continually, and tie them about thy neck. [6:21] Whensoever thou walkest, lead it, and let it be with thee; and when thou sleepest, let it keep thee, that when thou awakest it may talk with thee. [6:22] For the commandment of the law is a lamp, and light, and a way of life, and reproof, and instruction: [6:23] to keep thee from an evil married woman, and from the flattery of a strange tongue. [6:24] My son, let not the desire of beauty overcome thee, neither be thou caught with thine eyes, nor captivated by her eyelids. [6:25] For the price of a harlot is as much as one loaf of bread, but a married woman hunts for the precious souls of men. [6:26] Can a man bind fire in his bosom, and his clothes not be burned? [6:27] Or shall a man walk upon coals of fire, and his feet not be burned? [6:28] So is he that goes in to a married woman; he shall not be free from evil punishment, neither shall anyone be guiltless that touches her. [6:29] It is no marvel if one be caught stealing, for he steals to satisfy his soul when he is hungry; [6:30] but if he be taken, he shall restore... [6:31a] ...sevenfold; and giving all his substance, he shall deliver himself. [6:31b] But the adulterer, through lack of understanding, gets destruction to his own soul; [6:32] he endures griefs and dishonor, then his reproach shall never be wiped away. [6:33] For the heart of her husband is full of fury; he will not spare in the day of judgment. [6:34] He will not exchange his enmity for any ransom, neither will he be appeased by many gifts. [6:35] My son, keep my words, and hide my commandments with thee. [7:1] [My son, honor the Lord, and thou shalt be strong; and beside Him fear none other.][^1209] [7:2]

*Then: Let my prayer be set forth: and the rest: (see fol. 234)[^1210].*

*If the Presanctified Liturgy is not celebrated:*  
*We chant the usual Kathisma [Kathisma 18]. At "Lord, I have cried", in the Tone from the Oktoechos: and we sing 3 Martyr Stichera, and 3 from the Menaion. Glory: see the departed in the Oktoechos. Both now: 1st Theotokion in the order of the Tone. Prokeimenon and Readings of the day.*  
*At the Aposticha: in the Triodion, Idiomelon of the day (twice), and for the Martyrs, and Theotokion in the same Tone.*  
*After "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart", Troparia: Apostles, Prophets, and Martyrs: Glory: Remember, O Lord: Both now: Theotokion: look on Saturday at "God is the Lord". Litany: Have mercy on us, O God: and 3 great prostrations. Blessed be the name of the Lord: and: I will bless the Lord: and dismissal.*  
*In this manner the service of Vespers is completed on every Friday from the Friday of the Second Week until the Friday of the Fifth Week, whether the Presanctified Liturgy is celebrated or not.*

*At Compline:*  
*After the 1st Trisagion, Troparion: Apostles, Prophets: Glory: Remember, O Lord: Both now: Theotokion: Holy Mother: look on Saturday, the same. After the 2nd Trisagion: Have mercy on us, O Lord: After "It is truly meet": after the Trisagion, Kontakion: With the Saints give rest: (see fol. 40)[^1211]. Glory... Both now: Kontakion: To thee, the Champion Leader: look on the Saturday of the Akathist. But if it be a Temple of the Mother of God: Glory... Both now: Kontakion of the Temple.*

*If the Finding of the Precious Head of the Forerunner, or the Forty Martyrs, occur on the Second, Third, or Fourth Saturday of the Fast:*  
*On Friday evening, as always, without change. But at Compline on Friday we sing the Four-Ode Canon of the Saturday. At Matins, the entire service of the saint according to custom, and the Polyeleos. Canons: in the Oktoechos on 4, Temple with Heirmoi on 4, and Forerunner on 6. Katavasia: I will open my mouth: And the rest of the service, see the Typikon. Great Doxology. At the Liturgy, the service of the day and of the Forerunner.*

## Saturday of the Second Week of Great Lent

*At Matins, after the Six Psalms, Alleluia, Tone 2. And we sing the Troparia:*

*Troparion, Tone 2 (twice):* Apostles, Martyrs, and Prophets, Hierarchs, Venerable and Righteous ones, who have fought the good fight and kept the faith, having boldness toward the Savior: pray Him for us, we entreat you, to save our souls!

*Glory...*

*Troparion for the Departed:* Remember Thy servants, O Lord, since Thou art good, and forgive whatever sins they have committed in this life: for none is sinless, save Thee Who art able to give rest even unto the departed!

*Both now... Theotokion:*

*Theotokion:* O holy Mother of the ineffable Light, honoring thee with angelic hymns, we magnify thee!

*Then the usual Kathisma: The Lord said unto my Lord: (Kathisma 16) and the Sessional hymns for the departed in the Oktoechos. Glory... Both now... Theotokion: (see fol. 38)[^1212]. And a reading from the Hexaemeron.*

*And we chant the Amomos (Kathisma 17) in Tone 5, with the refrain:* Blessed art Thou, O Lord: *making two stations. And at the conclusion of the Amomos:* Blessed art Thou, O Lord: *and the Troparia of the Saints [Evlogetaria for the dead]: "The choir of the saints..." Look on Meatfare Saturday (see fol. 33)[^1213].*

*After Glory... Both now... Litany: Have mercy on us, O God, according to Thy great mercy: And the Priest commemorates our fathers and brethren who have fallen asleep before us, reciting the Prayer: O God of spirits and of all flesh: And we say: Lord, have mercy (40 times). In like manner he does after the stations.*

*Then the Sessional hymns for the departed: Rest, O our Savior: and its Theotokion (see fol. 34)[^1214]. And a reading from the Hexaemeron of Chrysostom, the first book. Then Psalm 50.*

*And we sing the Canon: from the Menaion of the saint with the Heirmos on 6. We sing the Heirmos once, and 2 Troparia. And of the Saint whose Temple it is, on 4. (If it be a Temple of Christ, or of the Mother of God, we sing the Canon of the Temple with the Heirmos on 6, and from the Menaion of the saint on 4.) And in the Oktoechos on 4, until Ode 6. The Biblical Odes are not chanted from the beginning.*

*From Ode 6, the Four-Ode Canons come in, and the Canons of the Temple and the Oktoechos are omitted.*

*And the Canons are sung thus: from the Menaion with the Heirmos on 6. And the Heirmos is said for the day that has begun, and the second Troparion, and we keep the verses, and...*

*...we begin from: "Then were they in haste," since the Heirmos and one Troparion are sung without verse. And of the Temple, on 4. From Ode 6 the Four-Ode Canons begin, and the Odes are sung according to the order. The Sixth Ode of the Psalter we do not say, but we sing it all in the refrains. The Canons from the Menaion of the saint precede with the Heirmos on 6. We place at Ode 6: from "The waters were poured out." And at Ode 7: from "Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers." Likewise also at Ode 8: from "Bless, all ye fowls." So also at Ode 9: from "The oath which He sware unto Abraham."*

*Four-Ode Canon, by Kyr Joseph, whose acrostic is: "This song is of Joseph." The Biblical Odes are chanted.*

*Tone 8. Ode 6. Heirmos:* I will pour out my prayer unto the Lord, and to Him will I declare my sorrows, for my soul is filled with evils, and my life hath drawn near unto Hades, and like Jonah I pray: Lead me up from corruption, O God!

*Troparion:* The saints, because of their manifold torments, were vouchsafed, O Savior, to cast down many myriads of enemies, and obtained many of Thy good things: through their prayers, since Thou art good, cleanse mine abundant transgressions!

*Troparion:* Let us hymn the passion-bearers of Christ, and cry unto them with one voice: O imitators of the Master's Passions, heal the passions of our souls, and strengthen us to fast from evil habits!

*Troparion [for the Departed]:* Thou didst change death into sleep, and didst painfully sleep in the tomb, and bestowed life upon the dead; therefore, O Savior, vouchsafe the departed to stand among the elect, through the prayers of the holy passion-bearers!

*Theotokion:* Strengthen me, O Maiden, to fast and to depart from every sin, who ineffably gavest birth to the mighty and sinless Word incarnate, and grant me, O all-immaculate one, a cleansing tear for my defilements!

*Another Heirmos, by Kyr Theodore the Studite. For both choirs, by one in order. Tone 3:* The depth of passions hath risen against me...

*Troparion:* As we celebrate the memory of the Martyrs divinely, O lovers of the Martyrs, come, let us rejoice, crowning them with hymns, and blessing Christ the Arbiter of the contest!

*Troparion:* Having first received the trial of stripes, and then having been stoned with stones, sawn asunder, given unto wild beasts for food, and slaughtered like lambs of Christ: yet ye live forever, O passion-bearers!

*Note: Glory: 1st choir:*

*Triadicon:* Uniting the Three in one essence, and dividing the One into three persons, which is the Godhead, I flee the equal precipices of Sabellius and Arius![^1215]

*The other choir: Both now... Theotokion:*

*Theotokion:* A Virgin didst thou appear, and after childbearing thou remainest in purity, for both thou didst bear and suckle. A marvelous and dread vision, spoken and understood, in thee, O Mother of God!

*Then the 1st choir sings both verses, for the Martyrs and the Departed refrains:*  
*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*  
*Or, verse:* God is wonderful in His saints, the God of Israel. (Ps. 67:36 [LXX 67:36 / MT 68:35])

*Troparion for the Martyrs:* By the protection of your patient endurance, pray unceasingly unto the Lord for us, O martyrs! Therefore now also have mercy, that we may fast from the passions of dishonor!

*And again, verse:* Their souls shall dwell amid good things. (Ps. 24:13 [LXX 24:13 / MT 25:13])  
*For the Departed:*

*Troparion for the Departed:* Thou Who art to judge the world with all, before myriads of Angels: vouchsafe them that have fallen asleep in faith to stand uncondemned before Thee, O all-compassionate One!

*Heirmos [Katavasia]:* The depth of passions hath risen against me, and the tempest of contrary winds: but preventing me, save me, O Savior, and deliver me from corruption, even as Thou didst save the Prophet from the beast! (Jonah 2:1–11).

*Then, the litany for the departed. Kontakion: With the saints give rest: Oikos: Thou alone art immortal: (see fol. 40)[^1216]. And we read the Prologue. Ode 7.*

*Tone 8. Ode 7. Heirmos:* The Hebrew children in the furnace boldly trampled upon the flame, and turned the fire into dew, crying: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, forever!

*Troparion:* With showers of your blood, O glorious ones, ye quenched the flame of deceit: deliver us from the fire to come, O passion-bearers of the Lord, by your prayers unto Christ!

*Troparion:* Having stopped the mouths of lions, and endured the burning of tortures, O passion-bearers, ye inherited the better delight: pray that we also may obtain it unto ages of ages! (Dan. 6:22; Heb. 11:33).

*Troparion [for the Departed]:* Enlightened with the all-radiant light of the Spirit, O valiant passion-bearers: ask relief, and dwelling in Paradise, and communion of life, for those who have departed in faith!

*Theotokion:* A hymn I offer unto thee, O Virgin: despise me not who am held fast by evils, but grant me, O pure one, perfect amendment through fasting and a life of goodly conduct!

*Another Heirmos. Tone 3:* The flame was transformed into dew...

*Troparion:* Accounting fire, sword, and wild beasts as sweetness, O passion-bearers, ye astonished your murderers, singing unto the God of our fathers!

*Troparion:* Being dismembered in your limbs, and burned with fire, ye were offered unto Christ as an acceptable sacrifice, O Martyrs of Christ: but pray unceasingly unto Him for us!

*Glory... Triadicon:*

*Triadicon:* In Trinity I glorify the one God, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit: simple Unity, honorable Trinity, principle before all principles, and consubstantial!

*Both now... Theotokion:*

*Theotokion:* O all-holy Lady, Mother of God, receiving the prayers of thy servants, offer them unto the God of all, that He may save us from every temptation!

*Verse:* Unto the saints that are in His earth hath the Lord been wonderful; He hath accomplished all His desires in them. (Ps. 15:3 [LXX 15:3 / MT 16:3])

*Troparion:* Honorable choirs of Martyrs, standing in your assembly, we who hymn you...

...bless and sanctify us, that we may eagerly accomplish the time of the fast!

*Verse:* Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen and taken to Thyself, O Lord. (Ps. 64:5 [LXX 64:5 / MT 65:4])

*Troparion for the Departed:* Knowing the deeds of men, do Thou Who art God give rest unto those who have departed unto Thee in faith, pardoning their voluntary and involuntary transgressions!

*Heirmos [Katavasia]:* Thou Who didst dew the flame of the furnace, and didst save the Children unconsumed: blessed art Thou forever, O Lord God of our fathers!

*Tone 8. Ode 8. Heirmos:* The conquerors of the tyrant and the flame, having by Thy grace kept Thy commandments exceedingly, the Children cried out: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and exalt Him above all forever!

*Troparion:* Having endured kinds of torments in the weakness of the flesh, ye were revealed as physicians to the sick, O passion-bearers: therefore I cry out: heal my ailing soul during this time of the fast for the sake of repentance!

*Troparion:* Woe is me! How have all my days passed away in slothfulness, and lo, the end draws near, and overtaks me unperfected in good deeds: O Martyrs who have finished the course well, pray that my end may be good!

*Troparion [for the Departed]:* By drops of your blood ye quenched the burning of godlessness, O divine passion-bearers: ask for them that have departed from this life truly divine rest and remission of deeds committed unto ages of ages!

*Theotokion:* Ezekiel foresaw thee as the closed gate, O pure one, who openest the gates of repentance unto all who despair: therefore I pray thee, open the paths that lead unto that rest! (Ezek. 44:2).

*Another Heirmos, by Kyr Theodore. Tone 3:* From the unoriginate Father...

*Troparion:* Having diversely endured wounds from many arrows, some being consumed by fire, and others burned...

...and some being cut down: rejoice, O passion-bearers, singing unto Christ: Praise, bless, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparion:* With your blood the ends [of the earth] are sanctified, and by slight sprinklings ye pour forth streams of healings unto all, O all-praised Martyrs; therefore ye cry continually: Praise, bless, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*We bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit. Triadicon:*

*Triadicon:* O Trinity in three Hypostases: O Father, Son, and living Spirit, one Godhead, one Kingdom! Thee do the Angelic hosts of unwaning Light praise; and we who are upon earth sing, bless, and supremely exalt Thee unto all ages!

*Both now... Theotokion:*

*Theotokion:* Behold, all generations call thee blessed, O all-pure one, beholding thy greatness; for beyond nature thou didst bear the Creator of all, Who is God and Man. Therefore we bless thee and supremely exalt thee unto ages! (Luke 1:48).

*Verse:* God is wonderful in His saints, the God of Israel. (Ps. 67:36 [LXX 67:36 / MT 68:35])  
*For the Martyrs:*

*Troparion for the Martyrs:* O choir of passion-bearers, pray unto the Savior that we may be saved, making intercessions continually, that we may purely serve Him through self-control; chant, bless, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Verse:* Their souls shall dwell amid good things. (Ps. 24:13 [LXX 24:13 / MT 25:13])  
*For the Departed:*

*Troparion for the Departed:* Vouchsafe them that have fallen asleep in piety in the hope of the resurrection to rise unto life eternal, O Lord, to praise Thee purely and to glorify Thee psalmody-wise; chant, bless, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*We praise, bless, and worship the Lord.*

*Heirmos [Katavasia]:* Born of the unoriginate Father, God before the ages, and in the last days clothed in flesh from the Mother of God, as perfect Man and God of God: praise, bless, and supremely exalt Him [unto all ages]!

*Tone 8. Ode 9. Heirmos:* Thou hast surpassed the boundaries of nature...

*Troparion:* Ye were filled with divine fire like coals, O godly ones, burning up the evil substance of godlessness, and with the sword cutting down the demon hosts, O valiant passion-bearers, illuminators of our souls!

*Troparion:* Ye passed through the darkness of torments, and passed over unto the noetic Light, O valiant passion-bearers; therefore enlighten my humble soul, darkened by transgressions!

*Troparion [for the Departed]:* Having suffered, enduring pains, O all-glorious Martyrs, they now ask painless rest and the delight of Paradise for those who have departed in faith.

*Theotokion:* Be revealed, O pure Mother of God, as a divine helper unto thy unprofitable servants during this time of self-control, offering our prayers unto the Lord, the Eternal King!

*Another Heirmos, by Kyr Theodore. Tone 3:* Thee, the font of immortality...

*Troparion:* Placed by God in the earth like fire, ye burned up every idolatrous deceit, kindling the lamp of piety unto the ends [of the earth], O Martyrs of Christ!

*Troparion:* O honorable multitude of Martyrs, pray Christ that we may in peace finish the course of the fast, and behold and worship also His Passions!

*Glory... Triadicon:*

*Triadicon:* One and Three I sing, the godly Divinity, uniting and dividing the Persons according to form: the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, these are They!

*Both now... Theotokion:*

*Theotokion:* Thee, the rod that budded from the root of Jesse and of David our forefather, the all-immaculate and pure one, do we magnify, for thou savest our souls! (Isa. 11:1).

*Verse:* Unto the saints that are in His earth hath the Lord been wonderful; He hath accomplished all His desires in them. (Ps. 15:3 [LXX 15:3 / MT 16:3])  
*For the Martyrs:*

*Troparion for the Martyrs:* Neither flaying, nor flame, nor slaughter, nor wheels, nor tortures, nor burnings, nor any other bitter torment could separate you from the love of Christ, O passion-bearers! (Rom. 8:35–39).

*Verse:* Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen and taken to Thyself, O Lord. (Ps. 64:5 [LXX 64:5 / MT 65:4])  
*For the Departed:*

*Troparion for the Departed:* O Thou Who rulest over the dead and the living as God, Who didst put death to death and through Thy rising grantest life unto all, O Christ: give rest also unto Thy servants whom Thou hast translated!

*Heirmos [Katavasia]:* Thee, the immortal font that with holy healings ever gushes forth salvation unto the human race, do we magnify, for thou savest our souls!

*Exapostilarion [Photogogicon]:*  
O Thou Who hast adorned the heaven with stars as God, and through Thy saints hast enlightened the whole earth: O Creator of all, save them that sing unto Thee!

*Glory... Exapostilarion for the Departed:*  
O Thou Who rulest over the dead and the living as God, give rest unto Thy servants in the habitations of the elect; for even though they sinned, O Word, yet they departed not from Thee!

*Both now... Theotokion:*  
O sweetness of the Angels, joy of the sorrowing, Protectress of Christians, O Virgin Mother of God: protect us and deliver us from eternal torments!

*At the Praises: 4 Martyr Stichera in the Tone of the Oktoechos. Glory: Idiomelon for the departed. Both now: Theotokion. At the Aposticha: Stichera in the Oktoechos. After: for the Departed, by Kyr Theophanes, in the occurring Tone. Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*

*At the Divine Liturgy. The Beatitudes in the Tone on 6. After the Entrance, Troparion: Apostles, Prophets: Another: Remember, O Lord: (see fol. 213)[^1217]. Glory: Kontakion: With the saints give rest: (see fol. 40)[^1218]. Both now: Kontakion: We have thee as a rampart and haven: (see fol. 32)[^1219]. Prokeimenon: Be glad in the Lord: Verse: Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven: (Ps. 31:11, 1 [LXX 31:11, 1 / MT 32:11, 1]). Another, for the departed: Their souls shall dwell amid good things. (Ps. 24:13 [LXX 24:13 / MT 25:13]). Epistle to the Hebrews, Pericope 304 [Heb. 3:12–16]: "Brethren, take heed..." Another, to the Thessalonians, Pericope 270 [1 Thess. 4:13–17]: "Brethren, I would not have you to be ignorant..." Alleluia, for the departed: The righteous cried: Verse: Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen: (Ps. 33:18; 64:5 [LXX 33:18, 64:5 / MT 34:17, 65:4]). Gospel from Mark, Pericope 6 [Mark 1:35–44]: "Jesus went out into a solitary place..." And the other: Gospel from John, Pericope 16 [John 5:24–30]: "The Lord said unto the Jews who came unto Him..." Communion Hymn: Rejoice in the Lord, O ye righteous! (Ps. 32:1 [LXX 32:1 / MT 33:1]). Another: Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen and taken to Thyself, O Lord! (Ps. 64:5 [LXX 64:5 / MT 65:4]).*

*In this manner is celebrated the Service for the Departed on the three Saturdays of the Holy and Great Fast: when there is none of the three Feasts: the Forerunner [First and Second Finding of the Head], the Holy Forty Martyrs, or the Annunciation.*

[Woodcut engraving: St. Gregory Palamas in hierarchical vestments, holding the Gospel and blessing, surrounded by four hagiographical vignettes: The Distribution of Goods, The Consecration as Hierarch, Dwelling in the Wilderness, and The Dormition of the Saint.]

## Second Sunday of Great Lent

*The present Order of Services is chanted for our Father among the Saints, GREGORY PALAMAS, Archbishop of Thessalonica and Wonderworker, composed by the Most Holy Patriarch Philotheus.*[^1220]

*On Saturday evening [at Great Vespers], the usual order: (see fol. 150)[^1221].*

*At "Lord, I have cried", we set 10 verses, and we sing 6 Resurrection Stichera, and 3 Anatolian [Eastern] Stichera. And the present Stichera of the Saint, on 4.*

*Tone 2, Podoben: "With what crowns of praise" (Коими похвалными пѣсньми):*[^1222]

*Sticheron:* With what songs of laudation shall we hymn the Hierarch? The trumpet of theology, the fire-breathing mouth of grace, the honorable receptacle of the Spirit, the unshakable pillar of the Church, the great adornment of the inhabited earth, the river of wisdom, the lamp of the Light, the radiant star that enlightens creation!

*Sticheron:* With what flowers of hymnody shall we crown the Hierarch? The champion of piety and opponent of ungodliness, the fervent protector of the faith, the great guide and teacher, the all-fair harp of the Spirit, the golden-shining tongue, the font welling forth streams of healings for the faithful, the great and marvelous Gregory!

*Sticheron:* With what earthly lips shall we laud the Hierarch? The teacher of the Church, the preacher of the divine Light, the initiate of the Trinity, the great adornment of monastics, radiant in action and contemplation, the boast of Thessalonica, who hath as his fellow-citizen in heaven the divine and marvelous Myrrh-streamer Demetrius!

*Repeating one [Sticheron to make 4]. Glory, Tone 6:*

*Doxastikon, Tone 6:* O thrice-blessed venerable one, most holy father, good shepherd and disciple of Christ the Chief Shepherd, who didst lay down thy life for the sheep: do thou thyself now, our God-bearing father Gregory, ask through thy prayers that great mercy be granted unto us! (John 10:11).

*Both now... Theotokion:* The 1st [Dogmatikon Theotokion] of the Tone [from the Oktoechos].

*At the Departure [Litiya], the usual Litiya of the Temple.*

*At the Aposticha: Stichera in alphabetical order [from the Oktoechos]. Glory, Tone 8:*

*Doxastikon, Tone 8:* Thy vigilant tongue, sounding in the ears of the heart for instruction, raises up the souls of the slothful; and by thy God-proclaimed words a ladder is found leading up from earth unto God. Therefore, O Gregory, wonder of Thessaly, cease not to pray unto Christ that He enlighten with divine light those who honor thee!

*Both now... Theotokion:* O Unwedded Virgin: (see fol. 85)[^1223]. "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart", Trisagion, and the Troparia, and the rest of the Order of the Vigil. But if there be no Vigil: the Resurrection Troparion. Glory: to the Saint, Tone 8: O guide of Orthodoxy: look at Matins at "God is the Lord". Both now: Theotokion:*

*At Matins. After the Six Psalms, "God is the Lord":*

*Resurrection Troparion (twice). Glory: to the Saint, Tone 8:*

*Troparion of the Saint, Tone 8:* O light of Orthodoxy, teacher and pillar of the Church, beauty of monastics, unconquerable champion of theologians, O wonderworker Gregory, boast of Thessalonica, preacher of grace: pray unceasingly that our souls may be saved!

*Both now... Theotokion in the same Tone:* O Thou Who for our sake wast born of a Virgin...

*The usual Psalter readings: The Kathismata. The Amomos [Kathisma 17]. Troparia: Blessed art Thou, O Lord: The Angelic Council: Polyeleos: Reading from the Hexaemeron. The Graduals [Anavathmoi] of the Tone. And the Prokeimenon: Let every breath: Resurrection Gospel. "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ": Psalm 50. Glory: Open unto me the doors of repentance: And all the rest, right up to the Canon: (see fol. 154)[^1224].*

*Canons: The Resurrection Canon with the Heirmos and Theotokion, on 4; and in the Triodion, on 4; and of the Saint, on 6.*

*Canon [from the Triodion], whose acrostic is in alphabetical order; but in the Theotokia, by Theophanes. Tone 6. Ode 1. Heirmos: As on dry land:* [Another Heirmos:] *The armed Pharaoh:*

*Troparion:* Having lamented with warm tears, uttering the cry of the Prodigal, we fall down before Thee, the Father of all and God, crying out: We have sinned, having departed far from Thee, and having served fornication; accept our repentance! (Luke 15:11–32).

*Troparion:* I have despised the royal nobility that Thou didst grant unto me, O Word Who for my sake becamest man; grievously was I condemned to please swine with sinful tastes: but spare me, O Savior, by Thy compassion!

*Troparion:* Falling down upon my knees, even as formerly the Prodigal, O Master and Lord, do Thou run and receive me, and embracing me with Thine arms, grant unto me the pledges of Thy salvation, making me again Thy son instead of a hireling, O Lover of mankind!

*Theotokion:* Through thee was human nature vouchsafed the divine manifestation, O woman full of the grace of God; for thou, O Virgin, wast the only Mediatress...

...between God and men: therefore, as the Birthgiver of God, we all worthily glorify thee!

*Another Canon, to the Saint. Tone 4. Heirmos:* I will open my mouth:

*Troparion:* Godly orators, most distinguished theologians, and God-proclaiming tongues, come, gather yourselves together in unity, worthily to hymn the divine Gregory, breathing of the Spirit!

*Troparion:* Let the pillar of the faith, the champion of the Church, the great Gregory be praised by me: the most excellent pastor of Thessalonica, truly the beauty of the Hierarchical order!

*Troparion:* From childhood thou didst desire the better and perfect life, O father; from youth thou didst love wisdom, and didst show thyself equal in character and of one mind with him whose name thou bearest, O father Gregory![^1225]

*Theotokion:* Be thou unto me, O all-immaculate one, the path of life, directing me unto the divine habitations; for I was deceived, and slipped into the abyss of evil: lead me up from thence by thine intercession!

*Tone 6. Ode 3. Heirmos:* O Lord, Maker of the celestial vault...

*Troparion:* I was afraid of my deeds, and of my distant departure, and of Thy squandered wealth, which I consumed in prodigal impulses; in repentance I cry unto Thee, my Father and my God: I have sinned, save me!

*Troparion:* Sinning upon the earth, I was not afraid; for such will judgment be unto me, contending against me then, when all things shall cease, O Word, being judged by Thy righteous judgment!

*Troparion:* Dark and defiled thoughts fed me, when I was far from Thee, O Savior, as a prodigal; but now...

...I cry unto Thee: I have sinned, I have sinned, save me who warmly runs unto Thy tender mercy!

*Theotokion:* Embracing Adam's compound nature, O Virgin, for out of thy womb God appeared bearing flesh, we who were called back from the ancient condemnation were united through the hope of former deification![^1226]

*Another Heirmos, to the Saint. Tone 4:* O Mother of God, thy singers...

*Troparion:* Preserving the streams of thy divine teachings, we escape all the snares of the heretics, and with thy sacred writings we overthrow their hosts, O Gregory!

*Troparion:* By wisdom thou didst destroy the battle-lines of the heretics, O blessed one, having the hypostatic Wisdom of God in thy heart, whereby thou didst crush with noise their impotent insolence!

*Troparion:* Having deadened every sensual pleasure of corruptible flesh, O most wise one, thou didst as an ascetic give life to the movements of thy soul, and didst show it forth as a divine organ of theology!

*Theotokion:* In the intellect of my thoughts and impulses, I diligently loved a shameful and prodigal life; but bind me with divine love through thy prayers, [O pure one]!

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Speedily anticipate" (Скоро предвари):*[^1227]

*Sessional Hymn:* Thou didst burn up the deceit of the heretics, O most wise one; thou didst excellently proclaim the Orthodox faith, and didst enlighten the world: therefore thou wast revealed as a badge-bearing victor, a pillar of the Church, a true Hierarch! Cease not to pray unto Christ that we all may be saved!

*Glory... the same [Sessional Hymn].*

*Both now... Theotokion:* Speedily accept our supplications, O Lady, and offer them unto thy Son and God, O all-immaculate Mistress; quench the assaults of the ill-speaking adversaries of tongues; subdue the plots and cast down the audacity of the godless who arm themselves against thy servants, O immaculate one!

*Tone 6. Ode 4. Heirmos:* Thou art my strength, O Lord...

*Troparion:* Casting aside the commands of my Father, the wealth which Thou gavest unto me I consumed in sensual pleasure; I became wretched and destitute of divine gifts: therefore, since I repent with confession, abhor me not, O Master and Lord!

*Troparion:* God-befittingly taking upon Thyself my poverty, who formerly was far from Thee, Thou leadest me unto Thyself through Thyself, and dost sanctify me unto gladness, O Lover of mankind, making Thy divine Body, O Word, my restoration and joy!

*Troparion:* That far off through unceasing tears we may be delivered from eternal torments, which God prepared for the evil spirits, like the Prodigal we cry out: We have sinned against Thee, O Father, but receive all of us who run unto Thy mercy!

*Theotokion:* The Word, co-unoriginate with the Father and the Spirit, is born without law from the Virgin who knew not man. Remaining what He was, He also remained what He took for our sake; for in two natures He is one Son, preserving in both what is natural! (Chalcedonian dogma).

*Another Heirmos, to the Saint. Tone 4:* Perceiving the unsearchable divine counsel...

*Troparion:* Having opened thy mouth, O most wise father, thou didst preach the divine wisdom whereon thou didst meditate in thy heart continually, and thou didst show forth Barlaam the vain-minded as a madman and fool![^1228]

*Troparion:* Thou hast set in the earth, O sweetest sun, by the law of nature; yet on the morrow shalt thou rise with Christ, the never-setting Sun, overseeing all things by thy prayers!

*Troparion:* Grace hath revealed thee, O blessed one of God, as the praise and great confirmation of the Orthodox, and a good shepherd, and a Theo-...

...and a second Theologian, and a vigilant shepherd of the flock![^1229]

*Theotokion:* Open mine ears of the soul, O Mother of God, who didst bear Him Who formerly opened the ears of the deaf, and vouchsafe me to attend unto the divine words and to fulfill them! (Mark 7:32–37).

*Tone 6. Ode 5. Heirmos:* Why hast Thou cast me off...

*Troparion:* I was deprived of wealth and divine gifts, and came into a far country, melting away with hunger for the good things of life; but do thou, O Father, since thou art good, fill me with former glory and sweetness for the sake of thy tender heart!

*Troparion:* Having adopted the mindset of the Prodigal who spent his life in prodigality, let us run unto the merciful Father with unhesitating faith and contrition of heart, that we may receive remission of transgressions!

*Troparion:* Tarry not, O my soul, dwelling in a far country, but run quickly, confessing unto God and the Father, that thou mayest receive the dissolution of those evil things which thou hast committed, having exhausted thy life!

*Theotokion:* We know thee to be a bright cloud carrying the Sun of Righteousness carried within thee, O all-immaculate Virgin: drive away the idolatrous darkness of foolishness, and enlighten us with true understanding! (Mal. 4:2).

*Another Heirmos, to the Saint. Tone 4:* All things were amazed at thy divine glory...

*Troparion:* With the sickle of thy words and thy sacred writings, thou didst cut down the thorny heresies and the evil-born sproutings of tares; and thou didst sow the pious seeds of Orthodoxy, O sacred hierarch Gregory!

*Troparion:* Thy words, O most wise one, and thy venerable writings are heavenly dew, honey from the rock, bread of Angels... (Ps. 77:25; 80:17 [LXX 77:25, 80:17 / MT 78:25, 81:16]).

...unto them that run unto thee, nectar, sweetness of ambrosia, delight, O Gregory, and a fountain of living water!

*Troparion:* Earth and sea recognize thee as a universal teacher, a sacred pillar of Orthodoxy, and a venerable armory of divine dogmas, a sacred and most wise theologian, a fellow citizen and partaker equal in character to the Apostles!

*Theotokion:* With the arrows of compunction, wash away the defilements of my heart, O undefiled Virgin, and grant me models of repentance by thy sacred supplications unto the merciful God, Whom thou didst ineffably bear!

*Tone 6. Ode 6. Heirmos:* I will pour out my prayer unto the Lord, and unto Him will I declare mine afflictions; for my soul is filled with evils, and my life has drawn near unto Hades, and like Jonah I pray: Lead me up from corruption, O God!

*Troparion:* I was Thy younger son, and evilly did I spend Thy wealth through estrangement of an evil life, and being deprived of Thy good things, O Lover of mankind, I come unto Thee, my Father and my God, and ask for forgiveness!

*Troparion:* Inhuman sojourning was my lot, and I was condemned to feed swine, for I squandered my wealth which Thou didst mercifully and promptly grant, and I became stripped of all things; but do Thou, as my God, have compassion upon me!

*Troparion:* I have no boldness, O Lover of mankind, to look up and behold the boundless height of heaven, having sinned against heaven, nor to be called Thy prodigal son; but have compassion upon me, Thou Who alone possessest boundless mercy!

*Theotokion:* Unutterable is thy giving-birth, and ineffable is the manner of thy conceiving, O Mistress, for thou bearest God beyond all understanding while preserving undefiled virginity; therefore, we all worthily glorify thee as the true Mother of God!

*Another Heirmos, to the Saint. Tone 4:* Celebrating this divine and all-venerable feast of the Mother of God, come, O godly-minded, let us clap our hands, glorifying God Who was born of her!

*Troparion:* The vain arrogance and tongue of the foolish Barlaam is torn asunder by the words and decrees and keenness of intellect of the most wise Emperor and by thine own, O Gregory![^1230]

*Troparion:* The divine lyre of the Spirit, the trumpet openly proclaiming the divine mysteries, the primate of Thessalonica, the theological tongue, let us honor with hymns!

*Troparion:* As a pillar of fire leading a multitude of people, thou didst burn up the enemies of the faith, and didst enlighten the gatherings of the faithful, O God-wise Father Gregory! (Exod. 13:21–22).

*Theotokion:* Be thou unto me, O all-immaculate Sovereign Lady, stillness and a haven of comfort leading without stumbling unto the divine shore, having calmed the tempest of my passions!

*Kontakion, Tone 4:* Now the time for action has appeared; judgment is at the doors; let us arise, therefore, fasting; let us offer tears of compunction with prayers, crying out: We have sinned more than the sand of the sea; but remit our sins, O Creator of all, that we may receive incorruptible crowns!

*To the Saint, Kontakion, Tone 8, Podoben: "To thee, the Champion Leader" (Взбра́нной):* As the sacred and divine instrument of wisdom, and the harmonious, luminous trumpet of theology, we praise thee, O Gregory, theologian. But as a mind standing before the First Mind, direct our mind unto Him, that we may cry: Rejoice, O preacher of grace!

*Ikos, Tone 8, Podoben: "An Angel of the First Rank" (А҆́гг҃лъ предста́тель):* An Angel didst thou appear upon earth, proclaiming ineffable divine things unto men; for uttering the voices of the bodiless while being from among mortals and clothed in flesh, thou didst amaze us and persuade us to cry out unto thee, O speaker of God, these things:
Rejoice, through whom darkness was hidden!
Rejoice, through whom light arose!
Rejoice, angel of the uncreated Godhead!
Rejoice, true rebuker of the created and vain![^1231]
Rejoice, thou who didst name the divine essence an unapproachable height!
Rejoice, thou who didst name the divine energy a depth hard to fathom![^1232]
Rejoice, for the glory of God...

...thou didst well proclaim!
Rejoice, for thou didst renounce the renown and possessions of evildoers!
Rejoice, beacon who didst show forth the Sun!
Rejoice, chalice dispensing divine drink!
Rejoice, through whom the truth shines forth!
Rejoice, through whom darkness is darkened!
Rejoice, O preacher of grace!

*Synaxarion.*

*Verses:*
*A radiant preacher of the Light is truly now / Conducted by the Wellspring of unwaning Light to brilliance.*[^1233]

This son of the divine and never-waning light, a true man of the true God, and a marvelous minister and worker of divine deeds, had in truth for his homeland the city reigning over all cities [Constantinople],[^1234] and noble and renowned parents, who endeavored to adorn him not merely outwardly and according to human carnal thinking, but far more inwardly and invisibly with virtue and learning. When, therefore, while he was yet in his very early years, his father passed away, his mother nurtured and reared him, as well as his brothers and sisters, in learning and in the Law of the Lord, as also in the Holy Scriptures, and knew how to value well him who acquired outward wisdom among teachers. And having united the keenness of his natural wit with diligence in learning, in a short time he mastered all logical learning. And when he was twenty years of age, regarding all earthly things as contemptible and ultimately deceitful, he sought to flee and turn unto God, the Cause and Giver of all wisdom, and through a more perfect life to offer himself entirely and wholly unto Him. Concerning this goal and purpose, he disclosed his very great delight and burning love toward God unto his God-loving mother, whom he found, although sorrowful, yet rejoicing together with him in this. Immediately, therefore, his mother assembled the children who were with her, and saying with joy: "Behold, the children whom God has given me!" (Isa. 8:18; Heb. 2:13), she tested their disposition toward goodness, and revealed unto them the great goal and undertaking. He also addressed exhortatory words unto them, and more swiftly than can be told, he won them all over, persuaded and instructed, fleeing with zeal from this life...

...and going forth unto a like love toward God. Therefore, having also distributed his estate unto the poor according to the Gospel (Matt. 19:21; Luke 18:22), and having left with joy and a good heart earthly fortune, the imperial estate, honors, and praises in royal courts, he followed Christ. Having, therefore, placed his mother and sisters in a convent of virgins, and taking his brothers with him, he ascended the mount eponymous with sanctity [the Holy Mountain of Athos].[^1235] Yet he persuaded his brothers to dwell in other monasteries, that, being united one with another without untimely distractions, they might direct their lives toward God; while he himself submitted to the obedience and guidance of a marvelous man according to the quiet and hesychastic life, giving himself over unto that manner of life, to a father named Nicodemus;[^1236] from whom having learned every divine commandment and every virtue in spiritual humility by actual deed, and having received there in a mystical revelation the invincible and unyielding protection and defense of the All-Holy Mother of God in all things, he remained until the elder's departure unto God. And having dwelt several years in the Great Lavra [of St. Athanasius],[^1237] with very great eagerness and mature and perfected understanding, through love for the quiet and hesychastic life he departed from the Lavra and entered lovingly into the wilderness; and ever adding divine love unto love, remembering God in his heart, and desiring with his whole heart to dwell ceaselessly with God, he gave himself over unto the utmost rigorous discipline. And drawing back his senses with watchful prudence on both sides and habituating them unto temperance, elevating his thought and intellect unto God, spending all his time in prayers and contemplation of God, and ordering his life in an exquisite manner, he utterly vanquished demonic assaults by divine aid; and having cleansed his soul through all-night standing by streams of tears, he became a chosen vessel of the gifts of the Divine Spirit (Acts 9:15), and beheld frequent and almost continual divine visions. And what is most marvelous: even when compelled by Ishmaelite incursions and raids to journey unto Thessalonica and to the Skete at Veroia,[^1238] and being constrained to converse with certain townsfolk, even so he did not turn aside from his wilderness discipline unto urban pastimes. Having, therefore, over no few years thoroughly purified both body and soul, by divine decree he received the great anointing of the priesthood; and being as it were immaterial, and so to speak, outside of himself, the mysteries of that...

...priesthood did he celebrate, that many beheld how he brought the souls of those who looked upon him to compunction and tears. Great indeed was he, and known as a Spirit-bearer by those who lived according to God; and being such, he was manifested even to those who looked upon him from without, having power over demons, liberating those possessed by their deception and cunning, turning the barrenness of trees into fruitfulness, foreseeing future things, and being adorned with other gifts and fruits of the Divine Spirit. And that in truth we should labor in virtues: this is placed within our power; but falling into afflictions and temptations is not within our control. Yet without these, perfection cannot be attained, nor can proof and witness of faith toward God be shown forth. ("Activity and endurance in goodness coming together," it is said, "make a man perfect according to God.") Therefore was it permitted for this great man to fall into diverse and continual trials, that he might be shown forth essentially perfect above all things. From that time forth, what intellect can conceive, what word can tell the arts and subtle machinations, far greater than before, of the cruel adversary? As well as the insults and slander against him by newly-arisen God-fighters, such that for the sake of piety this soldier endured troubles and every kind of affliction from them for twenty-three full years![^1239] For the Italian beast, Barlaam of Calabria,[^1240] philosophizing much according to outward wisdom, and in the vanity of his intellect puffed up with empty conceits, imagining that he knew and understood all things, raised up fierce war against the Church of Christ, against our pious faith, and against those who hold fast unto it. For the common grace of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, and the light of the age to come wherewith the righteous shall shine as the sun (Matt. 13:43), even as Christ prefigured when He shone upon the mount [Tabor] (Matt. 17:1–8), and simply all power and energy—that is, the operation of the Tri-hypostatic Godhead and every excellence belonging to the divine nature—he sophistically asserted and taught with his infected reason to be created! And those who piously confess that most divine light and every power and operation to be uncreated—since nothing of those things which exist naturally in God is newly-arisen—he labeled in extensive writings as ditheists and polytheists, just as the Jews, Sabellius, and Arius label us![^1241] For this cause, therefore, the divine Gregory, as a champion of piety and an illustrious defender...

...and above all others, for the sake of piety, I say, having contended and being slanderously accused, being summoned by the Church of Constantinople, he arrived. When, therefore, the pious and constant Emperor Andronicus IV [III] Palaeologus was champion of piety,[^1242] a Holy Council was assembled [Constantinople, 1341],[^1243] where that same Barlaam also arrived with his impious teachings, slander, and insults against the pious; but the great Gregory, being filled with the Holy Spirit and invested from on high with invincible power, opening his mouth which was according to God, utterly scattered and put him to shame unto the end, and by fire-breathing words and writings burned up his brushwood-like heresies into ashes! Therefore, unable to bear the shame, this persecutor and combatant against piety fled unto the Latins, whence he had come.[^1244] And immediately after him, Gregory synodically rebuked Akindynos—that is, "dangerless," or rather Polykindynos, that is, "of many dangers"[^1245]—before the entire Council, and overturned and scattered his writings with refuting words; yet those who became partakers of their contagion ceased not even then to wage war against the Church of God. Afterwards, through the great fortification of the Holy Council, and especially persuaded and directed by the firm judgment of the Emperor himself, Gregory was elevated to the Hierarchical Throne, and was established as Pastor of the holy Church of Thessalonica.[^1246] Therefore he took upon himself and showed forth even far greater struggles and labors for the Orthodox faith, and that valiantly, steadfastly, and patiently. For against the malicious successors, that is, the followers of Akindynos and Barlaam, who showed themselves numerous and harsh—cruel whelps of cruel and venomous beasts—he overturned and silenced their teachings and writings not once, nor twice, nor thrice, but frequently and over a long period, not under one Emperor or Patriarch, but under three successive Emperors holding the scepter of the Empire, and under as many Patriarchs,[^1247] and before innumerable Synods, by God-inspired words and writings, by manifold means, overthrowing and suppressing them, and with all his might utterly demolishing and conquering them; even though certain of them, persisting willfully in their stubbornness and counting for naught his aforesaid righteous judgment and sentence, remained in their error. For of all heresies there are yet remnants that shamelessly rise up against those saints who overthrew and suppressed them...

...not to mention the all-audacious Jewish race, which even unto the present time has venom and mad fury against Christ, Whom they murdered. So many and so great, though in brief, could the victories and triumphs of this great saint be expressed! God, moreover, by ineffable means, sent him as a teacher also unto the East. For as a venerable elder he was dispatched from Thessalonica unto Constantinople, when diverse Emperors succeeded one another. But he was taken captive by the Hagarenes [Ottoman Turks],[^1248] and detained for a whole year, passing from place to place and from city to city, teaching all in the fear of Christ's Gospel; strengthening even more those who were firm and steadfast in the truth, admonishing them to abide in the faith, supporting those wavering in it, and God-wisely resolving certain doubts and questions presented concerning this matter, so that in all things he rendered the most sufficient zeal in the deeds which I have recalled. With other infidels also, and wretchedly apostate Christians who had joined them, tearing asunder our Confession concerning the dispensation in the flesh of our Lord and God, concerning the Precious Cross, and concerning the honorable icons and the veneration given unto them which we practice, he conversed and disputed frequently with great boldness.[^1249] Furthermore, concerning Mohammed, and concerning many other questions presented by them, judging powerfully and thoroughly, he had some who marveled at him, while others exhibited fury and lifted up their hands, who would even have brought his life to an end by the crown of martyrdom, had they not, by divine Providence, being enticed by the hope of ransom for him, restrained their intentions. When this took place, this great man was ransomed by Christ-lovers, and as an unbloody martyr he returned luminously again unto his flock; yet among the many other great gifts and illustrious deeds given him by Christ, he was also adorned, bearing in himself, according to Paul, the remnants of the marks of Christ (Gal. 6:17). And that we may also show forth what characterized him most distinctly: this saint possessed this as his most proper trait, that he was exceedingly meek, modest, and humble—unless the discourse concerned God and divine matters, for in those he was a very great champion—never bearing a grudge, possessing no malice, striving according to the power of his goodness to requite with kindness those who in any way showed themselves evil toward him...

...in no wise easily believing whatever someone said against another, being patient and magnanimous in every hardship of tribulations, standing superior to every luxury and vain glory, ever practicing poverty, simplicity, and frugality in all bodily necessities, and possessing steadfastness in patience through a very long time, with modesty, meekness, and joy, he ascended to such a summit of virtue that even to outsiders looking upon him it was evident and clear, and in the knowledge of all there remained veneration and wonder. His eyes were never empty of tears, but were filled with great sorrow through wellsprings of tears. Having thus from beginning unto end armed himself in fasting and waged war against passions and demons, having driven heretics far away from the Church of Christ, having expounded the Orthodox Faith by mouth and through writing, and having by these sealed all God-inspired Scripture, his life and words became as it were a kind of completion and seal of the life and words of the saints! Thereafter, having pastured his flock for about thirteen years in an apostolic and God-pleasing manner, and having directed it unto the heavenly sheepfold,[^1250] and simply speaking, having become a common benefactor of all Christians living at that time and thereafter, he was translated unto the transcendent life, having lived in all sixty-three years of age; and he gave over his spirit into the hands of God (Luke 23:46), and left his body unto his flock, which even at his departure shone radiantly and was glorified, as a kind of heritage and precious treasure. For by miracles it shows forth beneficence unto those approaching from every quarter, and grants the driving away of all diseases, whereof the history written concerning him relates not a few.[^1251] By the prayers, therefore, of that holy Gregory, O God, have mercy upon us, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

*Tone 6. Ode 7. Heirmos:* From Judea did the youths of old arrive in Babylon; and trampling upon the flame of the furnace by their faith in the Trinity, they sang: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

*Troparion:* I have no boldness to be called Thy son, O Father, Lover of mankind, but I pray to be as one of Thy hired servants (Luke 15:19); abhor me not who cry: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers! (Dan. 3:26, 52).

*Troparion:* Having defiled our life by our former conduct, and lost our pristine nobility, let us run unto the one Father...

...and God, through fervent repentance to receive salvation!

*Troparion:* Harsh is the citizen unto whom I, wretched one, was condemned to be in servitude; and the famine which I endured, tending swine, was grievous and intolerable (Luke 15:14–15); but having turned back, I pray: O Savior, have mercy upon me!

*Theotokion:* Thou didst vivify our deadened nature, O Virgin Mother of God, who alone didst bear Life; therefore, we, the faithful, know thee to be salvation, who didst bear in the flesh the God of our fathers!

*Another Heirmos, to the Saint. Tone 4:* The godly-minded worshipped not the creature rather than the Creator, but valiantly trampling the threat of fire underfoot, they rejoiced, singing: O all-hymned Lord and God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

*Troparion:* They that converse with thy words and thy writings, O Gregory, come to know the mind of God; they are shown forth full of the spiritual wisdom of God, and they theologically proclaim the uncreated grace and energy of God![^1252]

*Troparion:* Thou didst shatter the sword and arrows of the ill-believing, and the arrogance of Barlaam, and didst worthily scatter all heretical power, O Hierarch, like an immense stone cast into the abyss!

*Troparion:* By thy words and dogmas the faith of the pious has been sealed, and the fury of heresies driven away, O Gregory; and the subversion of Orthodoxy and the strength of the ill-believing have ceased!

*Theotokion:* Knowing thee truly to be a stream and fountain, we who are dried up by the diseases of passions draw forth salvation and divine streams, and cry out: Blessed, O all-immaculate one, is the fruit of thy womb! (Luke 1:42).

*Tone 6. Ode 8. Heirmos:* The furnace was once kindled sevenfold for the godly ones; but bedewed by the Spirit, they cried out: All ye works of the Lord, bless ye the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparion:* Having believed in Thee, O Master, we know the wealth of Thine unmeasured and abundant tenderheartedness; therefore, we fall down before Thee, crying warmly with the prodigal: Receive...

...us who have sinned and fled unto Thee; for there is not, yea, there is no sin, O Merciful One, that is able to overcome Thy love for mankind!

*Troparion:* For the sake of tender mercy humbling Thyself, O Master, Thou didst draw near unto Thy fallen sons; for Thou Thyself, O Lover of mankind, didst meet the fallen, and dost embrace them and grant salvation (Luke 15:20); even if one has fallen low, being merciful Thou art not angered, as Lover of mankind!

*Troparion:* The most dreadful judgment terrifies me, O Master, for seeing Thee to be the Lover of mankind and without malice, I run not unto Thee, calling with the voice of the prodigal, but spend my life in slothfulness; be Thou, therefore, merciful unto me, and snatch me from that condemnation, O Merciful One, for the sake of repentance!

*Triadikon:* We glorify not three Gods, but one Godhead; yet we truly honor three Hypostases: the unbegotten Father, and the Son begotten of the Father, and the Holy Spirit proceeding from the Father; one God in Trinity, even though each name is faithfully glorified as God!

*Theotokion:* Bowed down by many afflictions, O all-immaculate one, and drowned by the tempest of griefs, deliver me by thy prayer, O most pure haven of salvation, and snatching me from all evils save me, that I may worthily glorify thee as a fervent defender, O Mother of God, unto all ages!

*Another Heirmos, to the Saint. Tone 4:* The godly youths in the furnace were delivered by Him Who was born of the Theotokos; He Who was then prefigured is now in truth active, gathering together the whole universe to sing unto Thee: Praise ye the Lord, all ye works, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparion:* Thou hast now joined the Theologians before the throne of the All-Merciful, as like unto them and of one character, O all-wise Gregory, primate of Thessalonica, beauty of Hierarchs, radiantly adorned with the glory of the sacred hierarchy, now ministering unto God!

*Troparion:* God, knowing the purity of thy mind, even before the womb and before conception, manifestly proclaimed unto the faithful divine Emperor that thou wouldest be an invincible champion of the Church; therefore by canonical testimony wast thou sealed with the myron of the sacred hierarchy.

*Troparion:* The gathering of Polykindynos[^1253] is manifestly conquered and distressed by thy hand and by thy wise words, O all-glorious Gregory, primate of Thessalonica; and like as smoke vanishes, so is their corrupt folly vanished by thy loud-sounding and theological tongue!

*Theotokion:* The Word of God in thee, O Virgin, formed human nature by transcendent goodness, and renewed it and saved it; therefore, saved through thee, we glorify thee unto all ages!

*Ode 9. Heirmos: Be thou amazed now at this (Оудивися убо о сем):*
*Troparion:* By Thy calf slain for my sake, fill now with joy and gladness my soul that looks for this from Thee, O God! (Luke 15:23). Receive me who have gone astray, and lead me who was dead back unto life (Luke 15:24, 32), and clothe me in the divine garment of salvation, in incorruption!

*Troparion:* O souls who have strayed far from God and are deprived of divine gifts, come fervently, and taking up the repentance of the prodigal, let us cry: O good Father Who art in the heavens, we all have sinned against Thee; cleanse and save them that flee unto Thy mercy!

*Troparion:* As Thou hast an abundant multitude of tenderheartedness, turn not away in disgust from me, O Lord, O Lord, who have squandered my wealth in many pleasures, but who now flee unto Thee and call with the voice of the prodigal: I have sinned against Thee, save him that flees unto Thy mercy!

*Theotokion:* A haven and guidance and protectress of salvation have I, thy servant, obtained thee, that by thy prayers unto God, as thou art good, O Sovereign Lady, I may be delivered from all grievous hindrances; for upon thee have I placed all my hope with love, that in faith I may magnify thee!

*Another Heirmos, to the Saint. Tone 4: Every earthborn mortal (Всякъ земнородный):*
*Troparion:* A divine mirror wast thou, O Gregory, who didst preserve undefiled that which is according to the image; and having manly set the mind as master over carnal passions, thou didst receive that which is according to the likeness, whence thou becamest the most luminous dwelling of the Holy Trinity! (Gen. 1:26).

*Troparion:* The pious Emperor[^1254] manifests thee as a winged voyager of the air, aiding him as one entirely filled with the Divine Spirit against the vainly wise and raving Barlaam,[^1255] who spoke unrighteous things on high against God (Ps. 72:3, 8 LXX [73:3, 8]); and this heretic didst thou righteously conquer!

*Troparion:* Having become a god by deification,[^1256] filled with the higher wisdom, O all-glorious one, thou didst shine forth the light of Orthodoxy unto the world, establishing its dogmas; for through love of the pre-eminent philosophy, O all-wise one, thou didst conceive the divine fear in the womb, and didst bring forth the words of the Spirit! (Isa. 26:18 LXX).

*Theotokion:* A song of thanksgiving do we, the faithful, concordantly offer thee, for thou didst destroy our ancient curse, O Mother of God, and we all reap divine manifestation, salvation, enlightenment, and mercy through thee, and eternal joy!

*Exapostilarion of the Resurrection. Glory to the Saint, Tone 2, Podoben: "Let us assemble with the disciples" (Оу҆чн҃кѡ́мъ):* Rejoice, boast of the Fathers; rejoice, mouth of the Theologians, habitation of hesychia,[^1257] house of wisdom, listener unto the highest things, abyss of the words of...

...the Word, instrument of action, auditor of the vision of God, healer of human sicknesses; rejoice, chiefest dwelling of the Spirit, and Father of the dead and the living! *Both now: Theotokion: Sovereign Lady of all:*[^1258]

*At the Praises, we set 8 verses, and sing the Resurrectional stichera, 5; and the present ones, 3. Tone 4, Podoben: "Joy of the heavenly ranks" (Нб҃нымъ чи́нѡмъ):*
*Sticheron 1:* Having passed a blessed life in the world, thou now rejoicest together with the blessed; and in the land of the meek thou dwellest as meek, O Hierarch (Matt. 5:5), and thou art rich in the grace of miracles from God, which thou grantest unto them that honor thee!

*Sticheron 2:* Thou didst plant the dogmas of Orthodoxy, O blessed one, cutting down the thorns of heterodoxy, and multiplying well the seed of faith by the increase of thy words, thou didst bring forth unto God a hundredfold ear of grain, as a skillful husbandman! (Matt. 13:8, 23).

*Sticheron 3:* At the brightness of thine undefiled life, O blessed one, the assemblies of Angels and men were amazed; for by free choice thou didst show thyself a steadfast champion, an ascetic, a Hierarch, a worthy minister of God, and His true friend!

*And the verse:* Arise, O Lord my God, let Thine hand be lifted up; forget not Thy poor! (Ps. 9:33 LXX [10:12]).
*Idiomelon of the Triodion, Tone 6:* Unto them that walk in the darkness of sins, Thou hast shone forth light, O Christ, through the season of abstinence; show us also the auspicious day of Thy Passion, that we may cry unto Thee: Arise, O God, and have mercy upon us!

*Glory: the same, in a very high voice. Both now: Most blessed art thou:*
*The Great Doxology. And the rest, as indicated:* (see fol. 323).[^1259]
*At the Liturgy: The Beatitudes of the Tone, on 6:*

*...and to the Saint, Ode 3, on 4. After the Entrance, Troparion: Resurrectional, and to the Saint. Glory: Kontakion: to the Saint. Both now: Kontakion in the Triodion. Prokeimenon, Tone 2:* Thou shalt keep us, O Lord: *Verse:* Save me, O Lord, for the godly man ceases: (Ps. 11:8, 2 LXX [12:7, 1]). *The Epistle to the Hebrews, Pericope 304:* "Thou, Lord, in the beginning didst lay the foundation of the earth..." (Heb. 1:10–2:3). *Alleluia of the current Tone. The Gospel according to Mark, Pericope 7:* "At that time, Jesus entered into Capernaum..." (Mark 2:1–12). *Communion Hymn:* "Praise ye the Lord..." (Ps. 148:1). *And the entire service to the Saint is as is common for a single Hierarch.*[^1260]

## On that Same Second Sunday of Holy Lent, at Vespers

*At "Lord, I have cried": as on leaf 323* (see fol. 323).[^1261] *Penitential stichera in the Octoechos, 4; and in the Triodion, 6.*

*By Kyr Joseph, Tone 8, Podoben: "Innumerable" (Неисче́тенъ):*[^1262]
*Sticheron 1:* Having sinned innumerably against Thee, I await innumerable torments: the gnashing of teeth, and inconsolable weeping, the Gehenna of fire, darkness, and Tartarus, O most righteous Judge! Grant me, therefore, tears whereby I may find forgiveness and the loosed-bond of my wicked deeds, as I fast and cry unto Thee: O Master Christ, be compassionate unto me, according to Thy great and rich mercy!

*Sticheron 2:* Seek me out, O Word, who have gone astray upon the mountains of cruel transgressions, and call me back unto Thyself, driving far away the evil customs of my mind; make me alive again who was dead, and cleanse me by fasting, as in unceasing weeping I cry out and say: O Master Christ, be compassionate unto me, according to Thy great and rich mercy!

*Another Sticheron, by Kyr Theodore, Tone the same [Tone 8], Podoben: "O most marvelous wonder" (Пресла́вное):*
*Sticheron 3:* Having begun the third week of the Fast, let us praise the precious Trinity, O faithful, joyfully traversing the remainder, and refraining from carnal passions; let us reap divine flowers from our souls, having woven crowns...

...as lords of the day, that we all, wearing crowns, may hymn Christ as Victor! *And in the Menaion, 3. Glory, and now: Theotokion. O Gladsome Light. After the Entrance, the Great Prokeimenon, Tone 8:* Turn not away Thy face: *with its verses* (Ps. 68:18 LXX [69:17]). (see fol. 129 and 194).[^1263]

*At the Aposticha: Sticheron Idiomelon, Tone 8 (Twice):*
I cultivated not the spiritual furrows with an unslackening mind, but with bestial thoughts I reaped sin, having prodigally squandered my whole life, wretched that I am; deprived of food that strengthens the heart (Ps. 103:15 LXX [104:15]), I was filled with temporary pleasurable delight. But, O good Father, shut not against me Thy compassions of love for mankind, but open and receive me as the prodigal son, and save me!

*The usual verses:* Unto Thee have I lifted up mine eyes: (Ps. 122:1 LXX [123:1]). *Martyrikon:* O ye Martyrs of the Lord: *And Glory... Both now... Theotokion:* The heavenly choirs sing: (see the Sunday of Meatfare, at the Aposticha, fol. 72).[^1264] *Then the rest of the Aposticha* (see fol. 354).[^1265] *And the rest of the sequence as indicated for all the Sundays of Holy Lent* (see fol. 124 and 109).[^1266]

## On Monday of the Third Week of Holy Lent

*At Matins: The Triadica of the Tone. After the 1st stichology, the Sessional Hymns in the Octoechos. After the 2nd stichology, Sessional Hymn, by Kyr Joseph, Tone 8, Podoben: "That which was commanded mystically" (Повелѣ́нное та́иннѡ):*
With the fire of abstinence, let us burn up all the material uprising of the passions, and let us now quench that unquenchable flame with streams of tears! O Savior, compassionate Lord, preserve us uncondemned, granting us forgiveness of our transgressions! *Twice. Glory, and now: Theotokion:*

*Theotokion:* O Virgin graced of God, pure and blessed, by the tender mercies and compassions of Him Who was born of thee, together with the Hosts on high, and with...

...the Archangels, and with all the Bodiless Hosts, pray unceasingly for us, that before the end He may grant us forgiveness, and cleansing of sins, and amendment of life, so that we may find mercy!

*After the 3rd stichology, Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "That which was commanded mystically" (Повелѣ́нное та́иннѡ):*
*Sessional Hymn:* O holy and precious Trinity, preserve whole and uncondemned us who are spending the fast in these three weeks; make us worthy to run well unto the remainder also, and to keep all Thy commandments, so that uncondemned we may thus attain to see the all-glorious Resurrection, offering a hymn of praise! *Twice. Glory, and now: Theotokion:*

*Theotokion:* O Protectress of the faithful, Mother of God, joy of the afflicted, and great consolation of the mourning: pray unceasingly with the Angels and Principalities unto Him Who was supernaturally born of thy most holy womb, O Virgin, that we may be saved in the hour of trial from cruel condemnation!

*And we sing the Canon in the Menaion, and the present Triode Canon by Kyr Joseph, and the Biblical Ode is stichologized.*
*Ode 1. Heirmos. Tone 8: Let us send up a song, O ye peoples (Песнь возслем людие):*
*Troparion:* Having as God compassionate love,[^1267] receive me who repent, who have prodigally squandered my life, crying unto Thee: I have sinned! I need no accusers, for I bring the shame of mine own deeds!

*Troparion:* Having forsaken the angelic food, I have made myself like unto the beasts, feeding upon defiled malice; yet receive me as I turn back, as one of Thy hired servants, O Heavenly Father! (Luke 15:19).

*Troparion:* Having forsaken the night of passions that abides from food, let all of us, the faithful...

...let us draw near with zeal by the light of abstinence, that we may be accounted worthy of the light-bearing banquet!

*Theotokion:* Rejoice, all-holy temple, dew-bearing fleece, sealed fountain of immortal labors; preserve thy flock, O Sovereign Lady, unconquered by any warfare!

*Another Heirmos [Canon], by Kyr Theodore, Tone the same [Tone 8]: Let us sing a song unto God (Поем песнь Богу):*
*Troparion:* Now in these three weeks, having cleansed ourselves, O brethren, as of old Israel for three days,[^1268] let us attain unto the boundaries of prayers, and hearing the Divine Voice thence, let us hymn Christ! (Exod. 19:10–11).

*Troparion:* Come, having strengthened ourselves by fasting like Samson (Judg. 13:5, 14:6), let us strike down the crimson demon as another wild beast, O ye peoples, so that the Delilah of passions may not mock and beguile us! (Judg. 16:4–21).

*Triadikon:* Praise the Trinity Cherubically, O holy Godhead: lights and Light, and life and lives; God the Begetter, God the Begotten, God proceeding from the Father: the life-creating Spirit!

*Theotokion:* Rejoice, joy of Eve! For her sorrow ceased through thy giving-birth, O pure one; rejoice, luminous cloud of the unwaning Light, from whom Christ our God shone forth!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*
*Troparion:* Armed in faith with humility of mind like David, having cast down the proud mind of another Goliath (1 Kings 17 LXX [1 Sam. 17]), let us together conquer the darkness of passions!

*Heirmos:* Let us sing a song unto God, Who delivered Israel from the bitter bondage of Pharaoh, and guided him in a pillar of fire and a bright cloud; for He is glorified! (Exod. 13:21).

*Ode 8. Heirmos: The God-proclaiming (Богоглаголивыя):*
*Troparion:* Having squandered the Father's wealth with harlots...

...I was cast out from the court of grace, wretched that I am; yet receive me, O Father, according to Thine innumerable mercy!

*Troparion:* In the brightest dawn of the fast, illumined by prayers, let us become radiant of light, that we may escape the sinful darkness!
