*Troparion:* The choir of the Bodiless Hosts prays Thee, the Cherubim pray, and the ranks of the Saints: save our souls, O Christ, plenteous in mercy!

*Theotokion:* O thou who didst conceive the uncultivated cluster of grapes, chasten me who am darkened by the drunkenness of sin, O Virgin Mother of God, hope of our souls!

*Another Heirmos [Canon], by Kyr Theodore. Tone 8: He Who covers His chambers with waters (Покрываяй водами):*
*Troparion:* Come, O brethren, let us enjoy the fast—the treasury of the Father, the marvelous possession, the mother of all that have ministered unto the grace of Christ; for this fast strengthens the body and enlightens the mind and the heart!

*Troparion:* Imitating marvelous Gideon, O my soul, bearing the virtues—the Faith, Hope, and Love of Christ—go forth slaying the alien passions, even as he with three hundred destroyed the Midianite nation![^1269] (Judg. 7:7, 19–22).

*Triadikon:* They glorify the Trinity, and as a Monad they hymn the one Godhead: O Father Almighty, and co-beginningless Son, and Holy Spirit, all-sovereign Dominion, one Essence, one Kingdom, worshipped in three Persons!

*Theotokion:* She who in childbirth escaped pangs beyond nature, recognized them in Thy precious Passion, she who bare Thee; and she grieved, beholding Thee nailed to the Cross by the will of the Jews, Who didst establish the earth upon the waters! (Ps. 135:6 LXX [136:6]).

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*
*Troparion:* When Thou shalt come in Thy glory to judge the whole earth, with myriad myriads of the Powers, then spare me, O Lord, loose and deliver from condemnation; neither put me to shame, nor condemn me unto the eternal fire! (Matt. 25:31, 41).

*We praise, we bless, we worship the Lord.*
*Heirmos:* He Who covers His chambers with waters, Who sets the sand as a boundary for the sea, and Who upholds all things: Thee the sun hymns, Thee the moon glorifies, unto Thee all creation brings a song, as Maker and Creator unto all ages! (Ps. 103:2–3, Jer. 5:22).

*Ode 9. Heirmos: Of the manifested (Проявленнаго):*
*Troparion:* Having strayed from Thy love, O Father, and having been enslaved by voluntary rushes of pleasures, receive me as I turn back like the prodigal, for Thou alone art plenteous in mercy!

*Troparion:* A barren fig tree have I appeared (Luke 13:6–9), producing only wickedness, wretched that I am, which hath procured fire for me; do Thou, therefore, O Lord, show me forth fruitful, bringing forth good deeds unto Thee!

*Troparion:* Fasting, O my soul, from wickedness and deceit, refrain from wrath, and fury, and every sin; for of such a fast is Jesus desirous, our God and Lover of mankind! (Isa. 58:6).

*Theotokion:* Thou art our weapon and wall, O Mother of God; thou art protection unto them that flee unto thee; thee do we now stir up unto prayer, that we may be delivered from our enemies!

*Another Heirmos [Canon], by Kyr Theodore. Tone 8: We magnify thee (Величаем тя):*
*Troparion:* Let us offer pure fasting, the laying aside of evils, as acceptable gifts unto Christ our God!

*Troparion:* Having learned how of old Elisha fed the prophets,[^1270] O my soul, be thou sweetly fed, giving thanks unto Christ! (4 Kings 4:38–44 LXX [2 Kings 4]).

*Triadikon:* I hymn Thee, the one Tri-hypostatic Godhead, beholding the Persons...

...in distinguishing aspects: the unoriginate Father, the Son, and the living Spirit!

*Theotokion:* O Maiden Mother of God, bridal chamber of the heavenly King Christ: save by thy prayers them that sing unto thee with love!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*
*Troparion:* Daniel tamed the wild beasts in the den (Dan. 6:16–23); fasting with the bridle of abstinence, let us also subdue the passions!

*Heirmos:* We magnify thee, the all-undefiled Mother of Christ God, upon whom the All-Holy Spirit overshadowed! (Luke 1:35).

*Exapostilarion of the Tone.*

*At the Aposticha: Stichera Idiomela, Tone 4 (Twice):*
I have clothed myself in the grievous defilement of my transgressions, and have been cast out from the joy of the bridal chamber; make me an object of compassion by Thine ineffable tenderheartedness, as the prodigal son, O God, and have mercy upon me!

*Martyrikon:* Who would not marvel, beholding the good fight wherein ye have fought, O holy Martyrs? (1 Tim. 6:12). For how, being in the flesh, did ye conquer the bodiless enemy? Having confessed Christ and armed yourselves with the Cross, ye were therefore worthily shown forth as expellers of demons and victors over adversaries: pray unceasingly that our souls may be saved!

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:* O unquenchable lamp, Throne of righteousness, all-pure Sovereign Lady: pray that our souls may be saved!

*On Monday of the Third Week, at the Sixth Hour, Troparion of the Prophecy,[^1271] Tone 4:* As we are weak and paralyzed by sins, heal our brokenness, O Physician of our souls, Who knowest the mind of man, O Lover of mankind! *Glory... Both now... Theotokion.*
*Prokeimenon, Psalm 41, Tone 4:* A prayer unto the God of my life: *Verse:* Like as the hart desires the fountains of waters: (Ps. 41:9, 2 LXX [42:8, 1]).

*Reading from the Prophecy of Isaiah (Chapter 8:13–22 LXX):*
Sanctify the Lord of hosts Himself, and He shall be thy fear; and if thou shalt trust in Him, He shall be unto thee for sanctification, and ye shall not meet with Him as with a stumbling-stone, nor as with a rock of falling.[^1272] But the houses of Jacob are in a snare, and they that dwell in Jerusalem in a pit.
Therefore many among them shall be weak, and fall, and be broken; and they that dwell in security shall draw near and be taken.
Then shall they be manifest that are sealed, so as not to learn the law.
And one shall say: I will wait for God, Who turned away His face from the house of Jacob, and I will trust in Him.
Behold, I and the children whom God hath given me; and there shall be signs and wonders in the house of Israel from the Lord of Sabaoth, Who dwells in Mount Zion.
And if they say unto you: Seek out the ventriloquists,[^1273] and them that cry out from the earth, the belly-speakers that mutter from the belly: shall not a nation seek unto their God? Why do they seek concerning the living unto the dead?
For He hath given the Law for help, that they may not speak according to this word, concerning which there are no gifts to give.
And a sore famine shall come upon you; and it shall come to pass, that when ye shall hunger, ye shall be grieved, and ye shall speak evil of the ruler and of the fathers' houses; and they shall look up to heaven above.
And they shall look down unto the earth below, and behold, severe distress, and darkness, affliction, and anguish, and darkness such that one cannot see; and he that is in distress shall not be delivered until a time. Drink this first quickly![^1274]

Act quickly, O land of Zebulun, and land of Naphtali, and the rest that dwell by the sea-coast, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles! (Isa. 9:1 LXX).
The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light; ye that dwell in the land and shadow of death, upon you a light shall shine! (Isa. 9:2 LXX).
Thou hast brought down the greater part of the people in joy, and they shall rejoice before Thee, as they that rejoice in harvest, and even as they that divide the spoil. (Isa. 9:3 LXX).
For the yoke that lay upon them shall be taken away, and the rod that is upon their necks; for the Lord hath broken the rod of the exactors, as in the day of Midian. (Isa. 9:4 LXX).
For every garment gathered by deceit, and vesture with exchange, they shall repay; and they shall wish that they had been burned with fire. (Isa. 9:5 LXX).
For a Child is born unto us, and a Son is given unto us; Whose government was upon His shoulder, and His Name is called: (Angel of Great Counsel,)[^1275] Marvelous Counselor, Mighty God, Potentate, Prince of Peace, Father of the age to come; for I will bring peace upon the princes, and health unto Him. (Isa. 9:6 LXX).
And great is His government, and of His peace there is no end; upon the throne of David and upon His kingdom, to establish it and uphold it with judgment and with righteousness, from henceforth and unto the age: the zeal of the Lord of Sabaoth shall perform this! (Isa. 9:7 LXX).

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 42, Tone 6:* The salvation of my countenance and my God: *Verse:* Judge me, O God, and plead my cause: (Ps. 42:5, 1 LXX [43:5, 1]).

*On the same Monday of the Third Week, at Vespers, on "Lord, I have cried":*
*Stichera of Kyr Joseph.*
*Tone 1, Podoben: "Joy of the heavenly ranks" (Небеснымъ чиномъ):*
Let us love the Fast, O souls, withering away the fiercest passions by the mortification of the spirit, and by divine...

...actions; strengthening ourselves to labor, lifting our mind unto heaven, and mediating the forgiveness granted by our compassionate God for wherein we have sinned!

Having spent my whole life defiled with harlots, wretched as I am, O Lord, I cry with compunction as the Prodigal: O heavenly Father, I have sinned! (Luke 15:18, 21). Cleanse and save me, and cast me not away, who have willfully estranged myself from Thee and am now grown destitute of divine works!

*Another Sticheron, of Kyr Theodore.*
*Tone 3, Podoben: "Come, all ye" (Пріидите вси):*[^1276]
Come, all ye, embracing honorable abstinence, let us make proclamation with the cymbals of the Psalms (Ps. 150:5 LXX), and therein let us spiritually rend the serpent that is the author of evil! Therefore with boldness let us cry unto Christ: Grant us, O Savior, without condemnation to behold Thy most holy Cross, and to venerate it, celebrating splendidly with psalms and hymns!

*And 3 Stichera for the Martyrs. Glory... Both now... Theotokion.*

*At Vespers, Prokeimenon, Psalm 43, Tone 4:* In God we will boast all the day, and in Thy name will give praise unto the age: *Verse:* O God, with our ears have we heard: (Ps. 43:9, 2 LXX [44:8, 1]).

*Reading from the Book of Genesis (Chapter 6:9–12 LXX):*
Noah was a righteous man, being perfect in his generation; Noah pleased God. And Noah begat three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japhs. And the earth was corrupted before God, and the earth was filled with iniquity. And the Lord God saw the earth, and it was corrupted; for all flesh had corrupted its way upon the earth.

And the Lord God said unto Noah: The time of every man is come before Me, for the earth is filled with iniquity from them; and behold, I destroy them and the earth. (Gen. 6:13 LXX).
Make thee therefore an ark of square timbers [or squared cedar timbers],[^1277] nests shalt thou make in the ark, and pitch it within and without with asphalt. (Gen. 6:14 LXX).
And thus shalt thou make the ark: three hundred cubits the length of the ark, and fifty cubits the breadth, and thirty cubits the height thereof. (Gen. 6:15 LXX).
Narrowing it together shalt thou make the ark, and to a cubit shalt thou finish it above; and the door of the ark shalt thou make in the side; lower, second, and third stories shalt thou make it. (Gen. 6:16 LXX).
And as for Me, behold, I bring a flood of water upon the earth, to destroy all flesh wherein is the breath of life under heaven; and all things whatsoever are upon the earth shall expire. (Gen. 6:17 LXX).
And I will establish My covenant with thee; and thou shalt enter into the ark, thou and thy sons, and thy wife, and thy sons' wives with thee. (Gen. 6:18 LXX).
And of all cattle and of all wild beasts and of all flesh, two by two of all shalt thou bring into the ark, that thou mayest nourish them with thee; male and female shall they be. (Gen. 6:19 LXX).
And of all birds according to their kind, and of all cattle according to their kind, and of all reptiles creeping upon the earth according to their kind, two by two of all shall enter in unto thee to be nourished with thee, male and female. (Gen. 6:20 LXX).
And thou shalt take unto thee of all kinds of food that ye may eat, and thou shalt gather them unto thee, and they shall be food for thee and for them. (Gen. 6:21 LXX).
And Noah did all things whatsoever the Lord God commanded him, even so did he. (Gen. 6:22 LXX).

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 44, Tone 6:* I will remember Thy name in every generation and generation: *Verse:* My heart hath poured forth a good word: (Ps. 44:18, 2 LXX [45:17, 1]).

*Reading from the Proverbs (Chapter 8:1–17 LXX):*
Now do thou preach wisdom, that understanding may obey thee!
For she is upon the high ridges, and stands in the midst of the paths.
For she sits by the gates of princes, and is chanted at the entrances:
Unto you, O men, I plead, and utter my voice unto the sons of men!
O simple ones, understand subtlety, and ye undisciplined, lay it to heart!
Give ear unto me, for I will speak honorable things, and from my lips will open right things.
For my throat shall meditate truth;
And lying lips are an abomination before me. All the words of my mouth are with righteousness; there is nothing crooked or perverse in them.
They are all plain to them that understand, and right to them that find knowledge.
Receive instruction and not silver, and knowledge rather than choice gold;
[And choose knowledge rather than pure gold.][^1278] For wisdom is better than precious stones, and nothing honorable is worthy to be compared with her.
I, Wisdom, have inhabited counsel and knowledge, and I have summoned understanding.
The fear of the Lord hates unrighteousness, insolence, and pride, and the ways of evil men; and I have hated the perverse paths of wicked men.
Mine is counsel and confirmation; mine is prudence, and mine is strength.
By me kings reign, and princes decree justice.
By me nobles are magnified, and tyrants through me hold dominion over the earth.
I love them that love me, and they that seek me shall find grace.

Riches and glory are mine, yea, the possession of many things, and righteousness. (Prov. 8:18 LXX).
My fruit is better than gold and precious stone, and my produce better than choice silver. (Prov. 8:19 LXX).
I walk in the ways of righteousness, and abide in the midst of the paths of judgment: (Prov. 8:20 LXX).
That I may divide substance unto them that love me, and fill their treasures with good things! (Prov. 8:21 LXX).

*Then: "Vouchsafe, O Lord."*

*At the Aposticha: Stichera Idiomela, Tone 2:*
O good Father, my folly hath stripped me of all that Thou gavest me! I departed from Thee, and entered into servitude unto an alien citizen; I pastured abominable beasts, and was not filled even with their food. Therefore I have run unto Thee, knowing Thy tender mercy: cover my nakedness by Thy love for mankind, and save me! (Luke 15:13–16).

*Martyrikon:* As the holy Martyrs pray for us and hymn Christ, all deceit hath ceased, and the human race is saved through faith!

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:* From thy virginal loins, the Light shone forth upon the world: the Word through a word! Pray Him, O pure and all-holy Virgin, that our souls may be delivered from the snares of the enemy!

## On Tuesday of the Third Week of the Fast

*At Matins: Triadica of the Tone. After the 1st Kathisma: Sessional Hymns in the Octoechos. After the 2nd Kathisma: Sessional Hymn of Kyr Joseph.*
*Tone 1, Podoben: "When the stone had been sealed" (Камени знаменану):*[^1279]
By fasting and supplications let us cleanse ourselves, and by providing for the poor let us be well-pleasing unto God; let us sigh and weep fervently, while we have time upon earth...

...that we may be delivered from the eternal weeping in the flame of Gehenna, sending up glory unto Christ, Who hath appointed repentance for mankind, for all that turn with upright righteousness!

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:* Stretching forth thy divine hands, wherewith thou didst bear the Incarnate One through grace, O all-pure Virgin, entreat Him to deliver us from assaults, passions, and tribulations, who praise thee with love and cry unto thee: Glory to Him that made His abode in thee! Glory to Him that came forth from thee! Glory to Him that hath set us free by thy childbirth!

*After the 3rd Kathisma: Sessional Hymn of Kyr Theodore.*
*Tone 3, Podoben: "Let the heavens rejoice" (Да веселя́тся):*[^1280]
Rejoicing in the Fast, delighting in hymns, and surrounding all passions with the fortress of prayers, let us trample underfoot the snares of the enemy, and follow Christ, crying aloud: Vouchsafe us to behold Thy Cross, O compassionate One, granting us great mercy!

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:* O divinely-blessed Mother unwedded, heal my diseased soul, for I am grievously held fast by transgressions, O Mother of God! Therefore with the sighing of my heart I cry unto thee: receive me, O all-immaculate one, who have sinned much, that with boldness I may cry unto thee: Rejoice, O dwelling-place of God!

*Triodion of Kyr Joseph.*
*Ode 2, Tone 4. Heirmos:*
See, see, that I am God, Who commanded Moses to lead out in the wilderness the dispersed people of Israel, and saved them as the Mighty One by My power![^1281] (Deut. 32:39; Ex. 3:10).

*Troparion:* Merciful, O Lord of mercy, be merciful unto me! Plead my cause, O righteous Judge, accepting my small sighing in exchange for Thy great tenderheartedness, O Christ, and despise me not!

*Troparion:* Thou hast adopted me through the laver of baptism, O all-good Father, having adorned me with all wealth of good things; yet I have squandered it in barren thoughts, and am therefore grown poor!

*Troparion:* Having put off the defiled garment of intemperance, let us put on the radiant vesture of abstinence, and being made radiant, let us attain the radiant Resurrection of the Redeemer!

*Theotokion:* Save me, save me, O thou that didst bear the Savior! Behold my grief, O pure one, for a multitude of measureless evils daily besets my wretched soul unto despair!

*Another Canon, of Kyr Theodore.*
*Ode 2, Tone 3. Heirmos:*
See, see that I am God, Who as God have poured forth salvation unto you, which all ye earthborn may draw forth through abstinence! (Deut. 32:39).

*Troparion:* See, see that I am He, Who have appointed for you the sacred time and holy course of the Fast for spiritual nourishment!

*Triadikon:* Let us glorify the Trinity, let us worship the Unity: the unoriginate only-begotten Son of the unoriginate Father, and the Spirit enthroned together with Them and co-eternal with the Father!

*Theotokion:* Entreat the Savior unceasingly, O all-lauded Lady, that they who confess thee with lips and soul as Mother of God may be delivered from every affliction!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*
*Troparion:* Great art Thou, O Lord, and marvelous are Thy works! For in the den of old Thou didst show forth Daniel uneaten by the lions, protected by the Fast! (Dan. 6:16–23).

*Heirmos:* See, see that I am the Savior of the world, the true Light, the Fountain of Life, the Son of God! (John 8:12; 4:14).

*Ode 8. Heirmos: "Him at Whom the angels tremble" (Егоже ужасаются):*[^1282]
*Troparion:* I weep and lament, meditating upon the hour wherein I am to...

...stand before the dread judgment-seat, guilty of torments for my many sins, which I have committed in knowledge and in ignorance!

*Troparion:* Having found purification through fasting, Moses perceived the one pure God; O my soul, cleanse thyself by fasting, that thou mayest draw near unto Christ, the Lover of mankind! (Ex. 34:28).

*Troparion:* Let us love the Fast, the mother of virtues, and let us hate gluttony, the parent of passions; and let us cry: Our Father Who art in the heavens, save us, save us, by the prayers of Thy saints! (Matt. 6:9).

*Theotokion:* Entreat the Judge Whom thou hast borne, O Virgin Mary, that He may show compassion upon me in the hour of judgment, O pure one, and save the condemned, O thou only intercessor for the human race!

*Another Heirmos: "Unto the children in the flame" (Во пламени к дѣтем):*[^1283]
*Troparion:* Having received the all-radiant grace of the Fast, let us shine with virtues, showing forth serene countenances and gentle ways in our inward soul's disposition!

*Troparion:* Having fasted, Elisha restored the child of the Shunammite alive; by this let us understand, brethren, how good is the Fast, how great, how joyous a grace! (4 Kings 4:32–37 LXX [2 Kings 4]).

*We bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit: the Lord.*
*Triadikon:* With the Father let us worship the Son, and the Holy Spirit in one Trinity, crying aloud with the Angels from clay lips: Glory in the highest unto God Who is in Trinity! (Luke 2:14).

*Theotokion:* A Child dost thou bear while remaining a Virgin, O only full of divine joy! A great mystery, a tremendous wonder: thou hast borne God incarnate, the Savior of the world!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*

*Troparion:* Let none of us, O brethren, be encompassed by despondency and sloth! It is the time for labor, the hour of triumph! Who would not choose to labor in a single day, so as to gain all the ages?

*We praise, we bless, we worship the Lord.*
*Heirmos:* Him Who descended unto the Hebrew children in the flame by divine power, and appeared as Lord: praise Him, ye priests, and supreme exalt Him unto all ages! (Dan. 3:50, 57).

*Ode 9. Heirmos: "The light-bearing cloud" (Свѣтоносный облакъ):*[^1284]
*Troparion:* Having fallen into the abyss of sin, into the deep of despair, into the tempest of thoughts and the storm of passions, I cry aloud: O abyss of mercy, help me by Thy tenderheartedness, and rain down upon me the cleansing of sins!

*Troparion:* By fasting let us cleanse the body, by abstinence the spirit, and by tears the soul, O ye faithful; and let us radiantly behold the honors of the Pure One, gazing upon the saving Passions which the Passionless One endured for our sake!

*Troparion:* As the publican I groan (Luke 18:13); as the harlot I shed tears (Luke 7:38); as the thief I cry: Remember me, O compassionate One! (Luke 23:42); as the blind man I call out: O Son of God, open the eyes of my soul, which have been blinded by the malice of the deceitful adversary! (Mark 10:47–52).

*Theotokion:* The unhewn mountain (Dan. 2:34–35, 45), the impassable gate (Ezek. 44:1–3), higher than the heavens and all creation, the excellency of Jacob (Ps. 46:5 LXX [47:4]), the all-golden urn (Heb. 9:4), the bridge and Mother of the Creator: her, the Virgin, let us call blessed, O ye faithful!

*Another Heirmos: "On Mount Sinai" (На сїнаетстѣй горѣ):*[^1285]
*Troparion:* Having understood the present days to be sacred above all others, let us sing prayers unto God with a pure conscience, often bending our knees and saying: O Lord, accept the entreaties and supplications of Thy servants continually!

*Troparion:* The people sat down, as it is written, to eat and drink, and ro... (Ex. 32:6; 1 Cor. 10:7).

...se up to play, serving the idol Baal-peor;[^1286] behold the delusion of cruel food! But let us fast and be glorified, even as great Moses! (Ex. 32:6; 1 Cor. 10:7; Num. 25:3; Ps. 105:28 LXX [106:28]).

*Triadikon:* In mercies, the indivisible Unity is the beyond-divine Trinity, united in essence, divided distinctly in Persons; for indivisibly It is joined, and being One, It is venerated in Three: This is the Father, and the Son, and the Living Spirit, Who preserves all things!

*Theotokion:* Who hath ever heard of a Maiden that bears a child, or a Mother without a husband? O Mary, thou workest a wonder! But tell me, how? Search not into the depth of my divine childbearing; behold, this is the most true attainment beyond the mind of man!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*
*Troparion:* For Thy wrath is unendurable against sinners; who then can endure the threat of Thy anger, O Lord? Having measureless mercy, receive me through Thy compassion, O Son, and not according to my many and grievous deeds!

*Heirmos:* On Mount Sinai Moses beheld thee in the bush unburned, having conceived the fire of the Godhead in thy womb (Ex. 3:2); and Daniel beheld thee as the unhewn mountain (Dan. 2:34–35, 45); while Isaiah called thee the rod budded forth from the root of David! (Isa. 11:1).

*At the Aposticha: Stichera Idiomela, Tone 7:*
I have sinned! To confess unto Thee, O Lord, prodigal that I am, I dare not lift up my eyes unto heaven; for having fallen from thence, I became wretched: I have sinned against heaven and before Thee, and am not worthy to be called Thy son![^1287] (Luke 15:18, 21). I condemn myself; I have no need of accusers, nor yet of witnesses: I have my prodigality that convicts me, I have my wicked life that rebukes me, I have my shame and nakedness! And as for the handwriting of my hands wherewith I am clothed...[^1288]

...O compassionate Father, O Only-begotten Son, O Holy Spirit: receive me who repent, and have mercy upon me!

*Martyrikon:* Before the judgment-seat of transgressors, rejoicing, Thy passion-bearers cried aloud: O Lord, glory to Thee!

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:* Without instruction Thou wast born of the Virgin, and hast enlightened them that are in darkness, who cry aloud: O Lord, glory to Thee!

*On Tuesday of the Third Week, at the Sixth Hour, Troparion:*
*Tone 7:* Thou art our salvation, O Lord, and defender in the day of affliction: have mercy upon us according to Thy great mercy, O Lover of mankind!
*Glory... end. Both now... the same.*

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 45, Tone 4:* The Lord of hosts is with us, the God of Jacob is our helper: *Verse:* God is our refuge and strength: (Ps. 45:8, 2 LXX [46:7, 1]).

*Reading from the Prophecy of Isaiah (Chapter 9:9–14 LXX):*[^1289]
Thus saith the Lord: All the people of Ephraim shall know, and they that dwell in Samaria, in insolence and a proud heart, saying:
The bricks are fallen down, but come, let us hew stones, and cut down sycamores and cedars, and build for ourselves a tower!
And God shall dash down them that rise up against Mount Zion, and against Jerusalem upon them, and shall scatter the enemies of Judah:
Syria from the rising of the sun, and the Greeks from the setting of the sun, who devour My people with open mouth.
For all these things His anger is not turned away, but His hand is stretched out still.
And My people turned not, until they were smitten, and they sought not the Lord of hosts.
And the Lord took away from Jerusalem the head and the tail, the great and the small...

...in one day: (Isa. 9:14 LXX).
The elder and them that respect persons, these are the head; and the prophet that teaches lawlessness, he is the tail. (Isa. 9:15 LXX).
And they that call this people blessed shall cause them to err, and they shall lead them astray that they may devour them. (Isa. 9:16 LXX).
Therefore the Lord shall not rejoice over their young men, neither shall He have mercy on their orphans, nor on their widows; for they are all lawless and wicked, and every mouth speaks unrighteousness: for all these things His anger is not turned away, but His hand is stretched out still. (Isa. 9:17 LXX).
And lawlessness is burned as fire, and as dry couch-grass it shall be devoured by fire; and it shall burn in the thickets of the forest, and shall devour all the hills round about. (Isa. 9:18 LXX).
Because of the wrath of the Lord of Sabaoth the whole earth is burned up, and the people shall be as men burned by fire: no man shall spare his brother! (Isa. 9:19 LXX).
But he shall turn to the right hand, because he shall be hungry, and shall eat of the left, and a man shall not be satisfied, eating the flesh of his own arm. (Isa. 9:20 LXX).
For Manasseh shall eat the flesh of Ephraim, and Ephraim the flesh of Manasseh, for together they shall besiege Judah: for all these things His anger is not turned away, but His hand is stretched out still! (Isa. 9:21 LXX).
Woe unto them that write iniquity, for in writing they write wickedness! (Isa. 10:1 LXX).
Perverting the judgment of the poor, tearing away the judgment of the needy among My people, that the widow may be for their plunder, and the orphan for a prey! (Isa. 10:2 LXX).
And what will they do in the day of visitation? For affliction shall come upon them from afar; and unto whom will ye flee to receive help? And where will leave your glory, (Isa. 10:3 LXX).
So as not to fall into captivity? And they shall fall beneath the slain... (Isa. 10:4 LXX).

...and for all these things His anger is not turned away, but His hand is stretched out still! (Isa. 10:4 LXX).

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 46, Tone 3:* Sing praises to our God, sing praises; sing praises unto our King, sing praises: *Verse:* Clap your hands, all ye nations: (Ps. 46:7, 2 LXX [47:6, 1]).

*On the same Tuesday of the Third Week, at Vespers, on "Lord, I have cried":*
*Stichera of Kyr Joseph.*
*Tone 3, Podoben: "They weighed thirty pieces of silver" (Поставиша):*[^1290]
O Lord, Who by the Cross didst slay the deceitful one: deliver me from his deception, who sin and am deceived; and having cleansed me by fasting, grant me to do Thy will, that rejoicing, O Master, I may behold Thy venerable Sufferings!

I have been wounded by the weapon of pleasure, O Lord, and am grievously all-slain: heal and make alive my humble soul, O Master Who wast pierced with a spear (John 19:34); and as Thou art compassionate, heal me who am wounded by the arrows of the enemy, and show me forth a partaker of Thy venerable Sufferings!

*Another Sticheron, of Kyr Theodore.*
*Tone 2, Podoben: "Let Him be crucified" (Да распнется):*[^1291]
Having enlightened our souls by fasting, O Lord, may we be vouchsafed without condemnation to behold Thy Cross in joy, and to venerate it with fear and love; for it sheds radiance upon Thy voluntary Sufferings, which grant us to attain, as Thou art the Lover of mankind!

*And 3 Stichera for the Martyrs. Glory... Both now... Theotokion.*
*After "O Joyful Light": Prokeimenon, Psalm 47, Tone 3:* Great is the Lord, and greatly to be praised, in the city of our God: *Verse:* In the city of the Lord of hosts, in the city of our God: (Ps. 47:2, 9 LXX [48:1, 8]).

*Reading from the Book of Genesis (Chapter 7:1–5 LXX):*

And the Lord said unto Noah: Enter thou and all thy house into the ark, for thee have I seen righteous before Me in this generation.[^1292] (Gen. 7:1 LXX).
And of clean cattle bring in unto thee seven and seven, male and female; and of unclean cattle, two and two, male and female. (Gen. 7:2 LXX).
And of clean birds of heaven, seven and seven, male and female; and of all unclean birds, two and two, male and female, to nourish seed upon the face of all the earth. (Gen. 7:3 LXX).
For yet seven days, and I bring rain upon the earth forty days and forty nights; and I will blot out every living thing which I have made from the face of the earth, from man unto beast! (Gen. 7:4 LXX).
And Noah did all things whatsoever the Lord God commanded him. (Gen. 7:5 LXX).

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 48, Tone 2:* My mouth shall speak of wisdom, and the meditation of my heart shall be of understanding: *Verse:* Hear these things, all ye nations: (Ps. 48:4, 2 LXX [49:3, 1]).

*Reading from the Proverbs (Chapter 8:32–36 LXX):*
My son, give ear unto me, and blessed are they that keep my ways! (Prov. 8:32 LXX).
Hear instruction, and be wise, and refuse it not! (Prov. 8:33 LXX).
Blessed is the man that hears me, and the mortal who shall keep my ways, watching daily at my doors, waiting at the posts of my entrances! (Prov. 8:34 LXX).
For my outgoings are outgoings of life, and will is prepared from the Lord! (Prov. 8:35 LXX).
But they that sin against me act impiously against their own souls, and they that hate me love death! (Prov. 8:36 LXX).

*Reading from the Proverbs (Chapter 9:1–11 LXX):*
Wisdom hath built a house for herself, and set up seven pillars. (Prov. 9:1 LXX).
She hath killed her sacrifices, and mingled her wine in a bowl, and prepared her table. (Prov. 9:2 LXX).
She hath sent forth her servants, summoning with a loud proclamation to the bowl, saying: (Prov. 9:3 LXX).
Whosoever is simple, let him turn aside unto me; and to them that want understanding she saith: (Prov. 9:4 LXX).
Come, eat of my bread, and drink wine which I have mingled for you! (Prov. 9:5 LXX).
Leave folly, and ye shall live [reign for ever, and seek wisdom that ye may live];[^1293] and correct knowledge with understanding. (Prov. 9:6 LXX).
He that reproves evil men shall get to himself dishonor, and he that rebukes an ungodly man shall defame himself: [and reproofs to the ungodly are wounds to him].[^1294] (Prov. 9:7 LXX).
Rebuke not the evil, lest they hate thee; rebuke a wise man, and he will love thee. (Prov. 9:8 LXX).
Give an opportunity to a wise man, and he will be yet wiser; instruct a righteous man, and he will add to receive it. (Prov. 9:9 LXX).
The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord, and the counsel of the saints is understanding: [and to know the law is the sign of a good mind].[^1295] (Prov. 9:10 LXX).
For in this manner thou shalt live much time, and years of thy life shall be added unto thee! (Prov. 9:11 LXX).

*At the Aposticha: Sticheron Idiomelon, Tone 2:*
Thee, Father and Creator, I dare address, O Lord, earthly creature that I am, turning unto Thy image, though I have failed of sonship, having lived prodigally, and by forgetfulness of Thy gifts squandered my wealth! (Luke 15:11–14). Cast me not away therefore, Who didst deign for my sake that Thine Only-begotten Son should endure crucifixion and death in the flesh; but adopt me as near unto Thyself, O Lover of mankind!

*Martyrikon:* The choirs of the Martyrs opposed the tormentors, saying: We wage warfare for the King of hosts; though ye deliver us unto fire and torments, we will not deny the power of the Trinity!

*Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion:*
*Tone 2, Podoben: "When from the Tree" (Егда от древа):*[^1296]
When the lawless people hanged Thee upon the Tree, O Savior, Life of all, then the all-immaculate Ewe-lamb and Thy Mother, standing by, wailed weeping: O my sweetest Child, Light of my eyes! Alas, how hast Thou consented to be nailed to the Tree in the midst of transgressors, O Thou Who didst suspend the earth upon the waters, in that Thou art compassionate!

## On Wednesday of the Third Week of the Holy Fast

*At Matins: Triadica of the Tone. After the 1st Stichology: Sessional Hymns in the Octoechos. After the 2nd Stichology: Sessional Hymn.*
*Tone 3, Podoben: "Beholding the beauty of thy virginity" (Красотѣ дѣтва):*[^1297]
By the Tree Thou hast quenched the flame of transgression, O Master, when lifted up upon the Cross, and hast slain the enemy by dying voluntarily: therefore I pray Thee, slay my carnal desires, and make alive my wretched heart through passion-slaying fasting, having cleansed me from every defilement, as Thou art compassionate!

*Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion:*
A shameful death Thou didst voluntarily endure by crucifixion, O compassionate One; and she that bare Thee, O Christ, beholding Thee, was consumed with grief, wounded in her maternal womb, and wailed mother-like: by her supplications, in the loving-kindness of Thy mercy, show compassion and save the world, O Thou that takest away its sin! (John 1:29).

*After the 3rd Stichology: Sessional Hymn, Tone 2, Podoben: "Having risen from the tomb" (Воскресъ от гроба):*[^1298]
Passing through the radiant feast of the Fast, we cry aloud: Preserve all men in peace, O Lord, delivering us from every craft of the enemy; and vouchsafe us, as Thou art all-good, to kiss Thy venerable Cross with love, granting thereby Thy mercy unto the inhabited world, O Thou Who alone art plenteous in mercy!

*Glory... the same again. Both now... Stavrotheotokion:*
*Tone 2, Podoben: "Being the wellspring of loving-kindness" (Милосердія):*[^1299]
The Virgin and Thy Mother, O Christ, beholding Thee stretched out dead upon the Tree, weeping bitterly, said: O my Son, what is this strange mystery? O Thou that grantest eternal life unto all, how diest Thou voluntarily upon the Cross by a shameful death?

*Triodion of Kyr Joseph. Tone 3.*
*Ode 3. Heirmos: "The confirmation" (Утвержденіе):*[^1300]
*Troparion:* Being crucified with Him Who was crucified for our sake, let us put to death all our carnal members in fastings, supplications, and prayers! (Rom. 6:6; Col. 3:5).

*Troparion:* O Lord, Who didst uproot the thorns of sin by Thy Cross: tear up the thorny thoughts of my mind!

*Troparion:* Having armed our minds by fasting, let us conquer the alien hosts of demons, being fortified by the power of the Cross!

*Theotokion:* The Word came forth incarnate from thee, O all-immaculate one, setting right the fall of our forebears through the loving-kindness of His tender mercies!

*Another Canon, of Kyr Theodore.*
*Ode 3, Tone 2. Heirmos: "Establish us in Thyself, O Lord" (Утверди насъ съ собою):*
*Troparion:* Thy life-giving Cross, O Lord, is a seal of salvation unto me; for thereby abolishing the adversary, I hymn Thee as the mighty God!

*Troparion:* The Tree of the Cross bare for the world the fruit of everlasting life, whereof tasting, O Christ, we are delivered from death!

*Triadikon:* I glorify Three Persons of one aspect: the Father, and the Son, and the Spirit, one dominion of the Godhead; for They reign and hold sole sovereignty as God!

*Both now... Theotokion:* Thy childbearing is dread, O pure Virgin; for He that became man is God, Who before the ages was begotten of the Father, and from thee in the latter times was born without a man!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*
*Troparion:* The grace of the Cross, shining forth upon the world, summons us unto Thy divine Sufferings, O compassionate Christ: vouchsafe us to venerate them in faith!

*Heirmos:* Establish us in Thyself, O Lord, Who by the Tree didst put sin to death, and plant Thy fear in our hearts, in that Thou art the Lover of mankind!

*Ode 8. Heirmos: "Unto Him Who walked upon the unstable waters" (Непостоянному):*[^1301]
*Troparion:* Having by the Cross exposed the principalities and dark powers (Col. 2:15), O Giver of light, when Thou comest with authority to judge all the world, expose not my secret deeds, O Word, that I may glorify Thy manifold compassion!

*Troparion:* Being judged, O Judge, Thou didst stand before the judgment-seat, condemning enmity by Thy Cross, O longsuffering and righteous Judge: therefore deliver from eternal condemnation them that cry with fear and supreme exalt Thy love for mankind!

*Troparion:* Inflamed with the fire of the Fast, the godly Children truly quenched the soaring flame of old with divine dew (Dan. 3:49–50); and as we fast, let us quench the furnace of all passions, that we may escape the flame of Gehenna!

*Theotokion:* From thee the Wisdom of God built for Himself a temple (Prov. 9:1), and was incarnate by an ineffable descent, O Maiden unwedded; for thou alone art chosen from among all generations, ...uncorrupt, an incorruptible dwelling-place for the Word!

*Another Heirmos: "In the bush unto Moses" (Въ купинѣ Мѡѵсеи):*[^1302]
*Troparion:* Upholding all things by Thy word (Heb. 1:3), for my sake Thou endurest all things: buffetings, and spitting, and the Cross, O Christ: I praise the greatness of Thy love for mankind unto all ages!

*Troparion:* Thou art slain as a lamb, O Christ, pierced in Thy side (John 19:34; Isa. 53:7), that Thou mayest save me, the straying sheep, from the snare of the devil, and number me in Thy good sheepfold unto the ages! (Luke 15:4–6; John 10:14–16).

*We bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit: the Lord.*
*Triadikon:* One Godhead in Trinity, undivided essence, yet divided in Persons, co-eternal dominion: O Father, and Son, and Holy Spirit, we praise Thee in song unto all ages!

*Theotokion:* O pure Mother of God, heavenly portal, saving gate of all Christians: receive the supplication of them that call thee blessed unto all ages!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*
*Troparion:* In Thy Cross, O Christ, the saints boast, kings are strengthened, and every believer is enlightened: vouchsafe me to behold it, to venerate it, and to hymn it unto the ages!

*We praise, we bless, we worship the Lord, singing:*
*Heirmos:* Unto Him Who prefigured of old in the bush on Mount Sinai the wonder of the Virgin unto Moses: sing, bless, and supreme exalt Him unto all ages! (Ex. 3:2; Dan. 3:57).

*Ode 9. Heirmos: "In the shadow of the law" (Въ законѣ сѣни):*[^1303]
*Troparion:* Moses set the serpent upon the tree, prefiguring Thee, O Jesus, voluntarily lifted up upon the Cross (Num. 21:8–9; John 3:14–15), Who didst pour out the venomous malice of the evil one, and didst draw men unto Thyself, O Lover of mankind! (John 12:32).

*Troparion:* Cleanse with Thy fire, kindling with fear...

...my soul with Thy divine love, and fence me about with Thy Cross, lest the ancient supplanter, having darkened my mind with pleasures through deceit, [prevail over me], O Christ!

*Troparion:* Let us fast, brethren, from defiled thoughts and evil deeds, and let us cleanse our hearts; let us take wing with divine virtues, and turn aside from evil downward-dragging impulses, that we may behold in radiance the Great Pascha!

*Theotokion:* From thee He Who is rich in nature voluntarily clothed Himself in our poverty, O Virgin, and He Who is invisible and hymned by the heavenly choirs became visible unto us, renewing the shattered image by grace!

*Another Heirmos: "Thee, the noetic" (Тебе мысленную):*[^1304]
*Troparion:* Thee Who didst stretch out Thy hands upon the Cross, and didst join together the four corners [of the world], whereby we have found access unto the Father (Eph. 2:18): all of us magnify Thee, O Son of God!

*Troparion:* Thee, O Christ, having crowned with thorns, the lawless men smote and crucified, for Whose sake all heavenly things bowed down: but we, having been saved, magnify Thee!

*Triadikon:* Thee, the thrice-radiant Holy Godhead, all-sustaining and ever-preserving: Father, and Son, and Holy Spirit, we magnify with unceasing hymns!

*Theotokion:* Thee, the radiant cloud of the Spirit, from whom the unapproachable Light, Christ, the great Sun of righteousness, shone forth upon us: we magnify with songs, O Mother of God! (Mal. 4:2; 1 Tim. 6:16).

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*
*Troparion:* Thou art our light and holy configuration, the triumph of victory, O Cross of Christ: sweeten for us our abstinence, and vouchsafe us to venerate thee!

*Heirmos:*

...Thee, the noetic and living ladder upon which our God established Himself, through which we have found an entrance into heaven: we magnify with unceasing hymns! (Gen. 28:12–13).

*At the Aposticha: Stichera Idiomela, Tone 2:*
Desiring to be a son of the adoption of the good Father, senseless that I am, I understood not, but cast myself away from glory, wickedly squandering the wealth of grace; and being deprived of divine food, I hungered under a vile citizen, by whom I was sent into his soul-corrupting field, and having lived prodigally, I was pasturing with the swine, and serving pleasures, I was not satisfied (Luke 15:11–16). But having returned, I cry aloud unto the merciful and compassionate Father: I have sinned against heaven and before Thee; have mercy upon me! (Luke 15:18, 21). *(Twice)*

*Martyrikon:* Every city and country honors your relics, O passion-bearing martyrs! Having suffered lawfully (2 Tim. 2:5), ye received heavenly crowns; and therefore ye are the praise of hierarchs, the victory of kings, and the beauty of the churches!

*Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion:* Having endured many pangs at the crucifixion of Thy Son and God, O all-pure one, thou didst sigh, weeping, and didst cry out bitterly: Woe is me, O sweetest Son! How dost Thou suffer unjustly, wishing to deliver the earthborn descendants of Adam? Therefore, O all-pure Virgin, we call upon thee in faith: make Him merciful unto us!

*On Wednesday of the Third Week, at the Sixth Hour, Troparion of the Prophecy, Tone 8:*
There is no firmness of deeds in us, O Lord: Thou art merciful, O holy Lover of mankind; despise not the works of Thy hands, O sinless One! (Ps. 137:8 LXX [138:8]).

*Glory... end. Both now... the same.*
*Prokeimenon, Psalm 49, Tone 4:* Offer unto God the sacrifice of praise, and pay unto the Most High thy vows: *Verse:* The God of gods, the Lord, hath spoken, and called the earth: (Ps. 49:14, 1 LXX [50:14, 1]).

*Reading from the Prophecy of Isaiah (Chapter 10:12–20 LXX):*
It shall come to pass, when the Lord shall have finished doing all things upon Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, He shall bring [judgment] upon the stout heart of the prince of the Assyrians, and upon the haughtiness of the glory of his eyes. (Isa. 10:12 LXX).
For he said: In strength will I act, and in the wisdom of my understanding will I take away the borders of nations, and I will spoil their strength, and shake the inhabited cities; (Isa. 10:13 LXX).
And I will seize the whole world with my hand as a nest, and I will take them as abandoned eggs, and there is none that shall escape me, or speak against me, opening his mouth and chirping! (Isa. 10:14 LXX).
Shall the axe glorify itself without him that cuts with it? Or shall the saw exalt itself without him that draws it? Even so, if one take up a rod or staff, it shall not be thus; (Isa. 10:15 LXX).
But the Lord of hosts shall send dishonor upon thy honor, [O king], and into thy glory a burning fire shall be kindled. (Isa. 10:16 LXX).
And the light of Israel shall be for a fire, and He shall sanctify him in a burning flame, and it shall devour [the wood] as stacks of hay! (Isa. 10:17 LXX).
In that day the mountains shall be quenched, and the hills, and the forests, and it shall devour from soul even unto flesh, and he that flees shall be as one fleeing from a burning flame. (Isa. 10:18 LXX).
And they that are left of them shall be a [small] number, and a young child shall write them down. (Isa. 10:19 LXX).
And it shall come to pass in that day, the remnant of Israel shall no more be added to, and the saved of Jacob shall no more rely...

...shall no more rely upon them that wronged them, but they shall rely upon God, the Holy One of Israel, in truth. (Isa. 10:20 LXX).

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 50, Tone 6:* Have mercy upon me, O God, according to Thy great mercy: *Verse:* Create in me a clean heart, O God: (Ps. 50:3, 12 LXX [51:1, 10]).

*On the same Wednesday of the Third Week, at Vespers, on "Lord, I have cried":*
*We set 10 verses, and sing the Idiomelon twice, and the Martyrikon; and in the Triodion, 3 Prosomoia Stichera:*
*Tone 3. Idiomela:*
Prodigally have I squandered my fatherly wealth, and become destitute; I have dwelt in the country of evil citizens, and become likened unto the irrational beasts, and am stripped of all divine grace (Luke 15:13–15; Ps. 48:13, 21 LXX [49:12, 20]). Therefore, turning back, I cry unto Thee, the merciful and compassionate Father: I have sinned; receive me who repent, O God, and have mercy upon me! *(Twice)*

*Martyrikon:* Living priesthoods, rational whole-burnt offerings, martyrs of the Lord, perfect sacrifices of God, sheep that know God and are known of God, whose fold is inaccessible to wolves: pray that we also may be shepherded with you beside the water of rest! (John 10:14; Rom. 12:1; Ps. 22:2 LXX [23:2]).

*Other Stichera, of Kyr Joseph.*
*Tone 6, Podoben: "Having laid aside all hope" (Все отложше):*[^1305]
Ye were shown forth as rays of the noetic Sun, O God-beholding Apostles! Ask enlightenment for our souls, and pray that we may be delivered from the murky darkness of passions, and may behold the saving Day, having cleansed by fasting and prayers our hearts which the evil one defiled, that having been saved through faith, we may ever honor you who saved the world by your upright preaching!

*Sticheron:* Having departed into the prodigal land of wickedness, I wickedly squandered the wealth which Thou gavest me, O merciful Father; and I waste away with hunger for good deeds, and am clothed with the shame of transgression, and stripped of divine grace (Luke 15:13–14); and I cry unto Thee: I have sinned! For I know Thy goodness; receive me as one of Thy hired servants, O compassionate Christ, by the supplications of the Apostles who loved Thee! (Luke 15:18–19).

*Another Prosomoion, of Kyr Theodore.*
*Tone 6, Podoben: "On the right hand of the Savior" (Ѡдесную Спаса):*[^1306]
Apostles of the Savior, luminaries of the universe, and benefactors and deliverers, declarers of the glory of God as the heavens (Ps. 18:2 LXX [19:1]), adorned with the stars of wonders and signs of healings: diligently offer prayers unto the Lord for us, as a pure sweet fragrance, that our prayers may be accepted, and that we may be vouchsafed to receive the life-bearing Cross, and all of us to behold it with fear; and through the veneration thereof, send down upon us Thy mercies, O Savior, as Thou art the Lover of mankind!

*And the Martyrikon, to 4. Glory... Both now... Theotokion.*

*At Vespers, Prokeimenon, Psalm 51, Tone 4:* I have hoped in the mercy of God unto ages of ages: *Verse:* Why dost thou boast in wickedness, O mighty one? (Ps. 51:10, 3 LXX [52:8, 1]).

*Reading from Genesis (Chapter 7:6–10 LXX):*
Noah was six hundred years old, and the flood of water was upon the earth. (Gen. 7:6 LXX).
And Noah entered, and his sons, and his wife, and his sons' wives with him into the ark, because of the water of the flood. (Gen. 7:7 LXX).
And of clean birds, and of unclean birds, and of clean cattle, and of unclean cattle, and of [all] wild beasts...

...and of all reptiles that creep upon the earth, two by two entered unto Noah into the ark, male and female, even as the Lord God had commanded him. (Gen. 7:8–9 LXX).

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 52, Tone 6:* When the Lord shall turn back the captivity of His people: *Verse:* The fool hath said in his heart: There is no God: (Ps. 52:7, 2 LXX [53:6, 1]).

*Reading from the Proverbs (Chapter 9:12–18 LXX):*
My son, if thou be wise, thou shalt be wise for thyself and for thy neighbors; but if thou prove evil, thou alone shalt draw evil. (Prov. 9:12 LXX).
He that receives instruction shall be wise, but the fool shall serve him. (Prov. 9:12a LXX).[^1307]
He that supports himself upon lies feeds upon the winds, and he shall pursue flying birds; (Prov. 9:12b LXX).
For he hath forsaken the ways of his own vineyard, and hath strayed from the paths of his own husbandry; (Prov. 9:12c LXX).
And he walks through a waterless desert, and through a land stretched out in thirst, and gathers fruitlessness with his hands! (Prov. 9:12d LXX).
A foolish and bold woman, who knows no shame, comes to lack bread: (Prov. 9:13 LXX).
She sits at the doors of her house upon a seat, openly in the crossroads, (Prov. 9:14 LXX).
Calling unto them that pass by on the way, and that walk straight in their paths: (Prov. 9:15 LXX).
Whosoever is most foolish among you, let him turn aside unto me; and to them that want understanding I command, saying: (Prov. 9:16 LXX).
Touch with delight stolen bread, and drink sweet water of theft! (Prov. 9:17 LXX).
But he knows not that the earthborn perish with her, and meet in the depth of Hades! (Prov. 9:18 LXX).

"But spring away, tarry not in her place, neither direct thine eye toward her; for thus shalt thou pass through strange water, and cross a strange river: but keep aloof from strange water, and drink not from a strange fountain, that thou mayest live long, and years of life may be added unto thee!" (Prov. 9:18a–c LXX).[^1308]

*Then "Let my prayer be set forth."*
*And the rest of the Liturgy of the Presanctified Gifts.*

*Markian Chapter 4: On the Annunciation of the Most Holy Theotokos.*[^1309]
*When the Key of the Paschalion is 2 [or 35], that is: March 25.*[^1310]
*This instruction applies also on every fasting day:*
*And we begin Vespers without prostrations and without a Kathisma. At "Lord, I have cried": Stichera to 10: the Idiomelon of the day in the Triodion twice, without the Martyrikon; and 3 Prosomoia in the Triodion, and 4 for the Feast. Glory... Both now... "The Archangel Gabriel was sent." Entrance. "O Joyful Light." Prokeimenon and Readings of the day, and 3 for the Feast. Then "Let my prayer be set forth," and 3 great prostrations; and after "Now the heavenly powers" [sing it] 3 times; and at "Blessed be the name of the Lord," 3 times. And in order, the Liturgy of the Presanctified [Gifts].*
*After the dismissal, we enter the Trapeza, and we eat cooked food with oil, and we drink wine, for the sake of the Most Holy Theotokos, and because of the labor of the Vigil that is about to be. But fish we do not eat, whatsoever day it may be.*
*At the 5th hour of the night we sing Great Compline.*
*After the 1st Trisagion, the Troparion of the Feast. After the 2nd Trisagion, the Kontakion of the Feast. And after "Glory to God in the highest," we sing the Litiya, singing the Stichera of the Feast and the customary prayers. At the Aposticha, all for the Feast. At the Blessing of Loaves, the Troparion of the Feast, thrice; and the Reading for the Feast.*
*AT MATINS. At "God is the Lord," the Troparion of the Feast, thrice; and we say 3 Kathismata. After the 1st Kathisma, the Sessional Hymns in the Triodion both; and we read for the Feast in the Gospel Commentary, whereof the beginning is: "The beautiful radiance of the Feast..." and so forth, in the Festive Homilies on Festive discourses. At the other Kathismata, Sessional Hymns of the Feast and the Reading for the Feast. After the Reading, tapers are given unto the brethren. Polyeleos, and the Magnification of the Feast. Sessional Hymn. Antiphon of the 4th Tone. Prokeimenon and Gospel of the Feast. Psalm 50. Sticheron of the Feast. Canon of the Feast: the Heirmoi twice, and the Troparia to 12. Katavasia of the Feast, both choirs together. And where there is a Triodion [Triode], there we sing the Feast with the Heirmos to 6, and the Triode to 8. Katavasia: Heirmos of the Triodion...*

*...both choirs together. After Ode 3, Sessional Hymn of the Feast. After Ode 6, Kontakion of the Feast. At Ode 9, the brethren again light tapers. "More honorable" we do not sing, but the Refrain of the Feast: "O earth, announce good tidings of great joy," by both choirs. Exapostilarion of the Feast, thrice. At the Praises, all for the Feast. At the Aposticha, the Idiomelon of the day, twice, without the Martyrikon. Glory... Both now... of the Feast. And at the end of Matins, prostrations, and the dismissal.*
*The First Hour, without prostrations, with a Kathisma. Troparion and Kontakion of the Feast; 3 great prostrations, and the dismissal.*
*At the 3rd hour of the day, the procession goes forth with the Litiya outside the Monastery.*
*Having returned, we sing the Third Hour and the Sixth, with a Kathisma, without prostrations: Troparion and Kontakion of the Feast. At the Sixth Hour, the customary Troparion and the Prokeimenon; and the Reading for the Feast, whereof the beginning is: "Again the joy of the good tidings..."*
*At the 9th hour [of the day], we sing the Ninth Hour with a Kathisma; and then the Instruction of Theodore the Studite. Thereafter the Beatitudes without singing; "Remember us, O Lord"; and Psalm 30 read; "I believe in one God"; "Remit, forgive"; after "Our Father": the Kontakion of the Feast; "Lord, have mercy," 40 times; and 3 great prostrations.*
*And immediately we begin Vespers: "O come, let us worship," without prostrations and without a Kathisma. At "Lord, I have cried": Stichera to 10: the Idiomelon of the day twice, without the Martyrikon; and 3 Prosomoia in the Triodion, and 3 for the Feast, and 3 for the Archangel. Unto the first verse we sing the refrain: "Who makes His angels spirits" (Ps. 103:4 LXX [104:4]). Glory... Both now... of the Feast: "The Archangel Gabriel was sent." Entrance with the Gospel. "O Joyful Light." Prokeimenon and Reading of the day; and two for the Feast: first, "Moses entered"; second, "The Lord created me" (Ex. 3:1ff; Prov. 8:22ff). Then "Let my prayer be set forth"; Little Litany and exclamation. Then the Trisagion. Prokeimenon, Epistle, Alleluia, Gospel, and Communion Hymn of the Feast. The Liturgy of Saint John Chrysostom.*
*At the Trapeza, we eat two cooked foods with oil, and fish; and we drink wine, but only once in the day.*
*Small Compline we sing in the narthex, quickly, without singing, and without prostrations, and without a Canon. Only at "Glory to God in the highest," 3 prostrations; and at the Trisagion, 3; and at "More honorable," 3; and of the rest, 12; and at the concluding Trisagion, 3, and the dismissal.*

## On Thursday of the Third Week of the Fast

*At Matins, the Triadika of the Tone. After the 1st Stichologia, Sessional Hymns in the Octoechos. After the 2nd Stichologia, Sessional Hymn of Kyr Joseph.*
*Tone 6, Podoben: "Having placed all their hope" (Все упованїе):*[^1311]
Undeluded luminaries of the world, disciples of the Savior...

...enlighten my soul that is blinded by sins, and show me forth a partaker of the divine day, keeping the saving commandments; and deliver me from that unillumined darkness, that I may glorify you! *(Twice)*

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* O holy Lady Mother of God, Mother of Christ our God, who didst ineffably give birth to the Creator of all: with the sacred Apostles pray unto His abyss of goodness, to deliver us from passions, and to grant us remission of our transgressions!

*After the 3rd Stichologia, Sessional Hymn of Kyr Theodore.*
*Tone 6, Podoben: "The Angelic Powers" (Аггельскїя силы):*[^1312]
*Sessional Hymn:* Most radiant luminaries, godly Apostles: enlighten your singers, rewarding the time of fasting, worthily praying that all may behold the Tree of the life-bearing Cross, and touch it with undefiled lips and eyes, crying aloud in the words of the Psalm: O Lord, glory to Thee! *(Twice)*

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* Good hope of the world, O Virgin Mother of God: we urge forward thine only and dread protection; have compassion upon a distressed people; entreat the merciful God that our souls may be delivered from every threatening, O only blessed one!

*Triode of Kyr Joseph, and the Biblical Canticle.*
*Ode 4, Tone 6. Heirmos: "Christ is my power" (Христос моя сила):*[^1313]
*Troparion:* Fasting, tears, prayers, almsgiving, a tender-hearted disposition, an upright custom, purity of life: let us show forth these things, O faithful, that we may receive glory!

*Troparion:* Shining luminaries upon the firmament of the honored Church, most radiantly were ye shown forth, O Apostles: therefore enlighten our hearts by the Divine Spirit!

*Troparion:* As divine coals, inflamed with the immaterial Fire, burn up the material passions of our hearts, O holy Apostles of our God!

*Theotokion:* O unquenchable lamp, all-radiant bridal chamber, higher than the Seraphim, cherubic chariot, O all-immaculate one: deliver me from grievous sins and afflictions!

*Another Heirmos, of Kyr Theodore. The same Tone [Tone 6], Heirmos: "The Prophet heard" (Услыша пророк):*[^1314]
*Troparion:* Shown forth as luminaries of the divine epiphany, O Apostles of the Savior, ye dispersed the darkness of ignorance, and having made clear the Church, ye enlighten the universe with your fire-speaking teachings!

*Troparion:* Having traversed the world, one indeed into one country, another into another, throughout the whole universe, ye gathered all men into one faith, O Apostles (Matt. 28:19; Mark 16:15; Rom. 10:18); and having attained heavenly things, ye dance with joy, unceasingly entreating Christ for the salvation of us all!

*Triadikon:* I glorify the Son from the Father and the Spirit, as light and ray from the sun, the One indeed by generation, as offspring, and the Other by procession, as proceeding: one co-unoriginate Essence worshipped by all creation!

*Theotokion:* A virgin giving birth to an Infant, yet preserving virginity, pure one, thou wast shown forth, having given birth to God and man, one and the same in two natures! Thy wonder, O Virgin Mother, astonishes every ear and mind!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*
*Troparion:* Through your holy prayers, O Apostles of the Lord, may we be vouchsafed with pure lips and eyes to kiss the life-creating Cross, which lies before them that are in the world, being venerated!

*Heirmos:*

*Heirmos: "The Prophet heard":* The Prophet heard of Thy coming, O Lord, and was afraid, that Thou wast to be born of a Virgin and appear unto men, and he said: "I heard Thy report and was afraid; glory to Thy power, O Lord!" (Hab. 3:2 LXX).[^1315]

*Ode 8, Tone 6. Heirmos: "From the flame for the saints" (Из пламене святым):*[^1316]

*Troparion:* Fasting showed forth Moses as a beholder of God (Ex. 24:18; 34:28), and Elijah it took up in a chariot of fire (4 Kgs. 2:11 LXX [2 Kgs. 2:11]); let us be zealous, let us restrain harmful thoughts, so that, O my soul, being delivered from deception that drags downward, thou mayest be saved!

*Troparion:* Having slipped, I have fallen into worse things, and I add wound unto wound; heal, O Christ, the stony hardening of my heart, O Compassionate One, through the prayers of the Apostles!

*Troparion:* God-radiant luminaries unto the world, tear asunder the clouds of our passions, and show forth as worshippers of the radiant Resurrection those who sing of the Sun of Glory!

*Theotokion:* Generations of generations call thee blessed, O God-blessed one, even as thou didst foretell of old (Luke 1:48); for alone among men, thou didst ineffably give birth unto the blessed Word incarnate of thee!

*Another Heirmos, of Kyr Theodore. The same Tone [Tone 6], Heirmos: "Thy singing children" (Пѣнии твои отроци):*[^1317]

*Troparion:* Having caught with the simplicity of faith those swimming in the abyss of deceit, O Apostles, ye brought them unto the Lord, blessing, praising, and supremely exalting the Lord unto all ages!

*Troparion:* Great is Thy strength in the Apostles, so that their shadows and handkerchiefs heal the sick (Acts 5:15; 19:12), who bless, praise, and supremely exalt the Lord unto all ages!

*We bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, the Lord.*

*Triadikon:* By unoriginate generation and procession, we worship the Father Who begat, glorifying the Son Who was begotten, and singing of the Holy Spirit Who shone forth together with the Father and the Son!

*Theotokion:*

Pray continually unto Him Whom thou didst ineffably bear, O Virgin, as the Lover of mankind, that He may deliver from perils those who flee unto thee!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*

*Troparion:* O choir of twelve holy Apostles, vouchsafe me uncondemned to venerate the precious Cross, blessing, praising, and supremely exalting unto all ages!

*We praise, bless, and worship the Lord.*

*Heirmos:* Thy children singing in the furnace, being made like unto the Cherubim, crying aloud the thrice-holy hymn: bless, praise, and supremely exalt the Lord unto all ages!

*Ode 9, Tone 6. Heirmos: "God cannot be seen of men" (Бога человѣком):*[^1318]

*Troparion:* O God and Lord, abundant in mercy, cleanse the wounds of my heart, applying unto me the remedies of repentance! I have sinned, I have sinned against Thee; have compassion and save me through the prayers of Thine Apostles, for Thou art abundant in mercy!

*Troparion:* Following immoderate impulses with harmful mind, I was wholly outside myself, nourished with bestial pleasures, and deprived of saving meats, a prodigal; O Christ, have compassion and save me!

*Troparion:* O my soul, not having cleansed thyself from wickedness, nor distanced thyself from corrupting pleasures, why dost thou untimely rejoice in fasting? The Lord has not chosen this fast (Isa. 58:5–6), He Who alone desires our amendment!

*Theotokion:* Enlighten me with divine light, O Virgin Mother of God, mother of the Light, and drive away the gloom of my soul, that I may call thee blessed, whom all generations truly call blessed, even as thou didst foretell (Luke 1:48)!

*Another Heirmos, of Kyr Theodore. The same Tone [Tone 6], Heirmos: "Conception without seed" (Безсѣменна зачатіа):*[^1319]

*Troparion:* Rude in speech, ye were shown forth as most wise in understanding (2 Cor. 11:6), having broken the cords of the words of the wise, the foolishness of rhetoricians, and the reckoning of astrologers; therefore, O Apostles of Christ alone, ye were shown forth as teachers unto the whole universe!

*Troparion:* Peter speaks, and Plato is silent; Paul teaches, and Pythagoras is put to shame (1 Cor. 1:20); and the rest of the God-voiced assembly of the Apostles buries the dead speech of the Hellenes, and renews the world unto the service of Christ!

*Triadikon:* O Father, the One Begetter of the One Only-begotten Son; and O Holy Spirit, the One Light, Radiance of the One Light, and One with the One of the One God, truly being Lord, O Lord: O Holy Trinity, Unity, save me who theologize concerning Thee!

*Theotokion:* The wonder of thy childbearing astonishes me, O all-immaculate one: how dost thou conceive without seed the Incomprehensible One? Tell how thou remainest a virgin, having given birth as a mother? Accepting by faith what is beyond nature, I have worshipped Him Who is born, for what He wills, that He can also do!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*

*Troparion:* May we all be vouchsafed to behold and to venerate the precious Cross, the sacred Tree, which blossomed forth salvation unto the world, with precious lips and soul, through the prayers of all you holy Apostles of Christ!

*Heirmos:* Conception without seed, childbearing ineffable, a mother without a husband, reception without corruption! For the birth of God renews nature; therefore all generations, as the Mother and Bride of God, orthodoxly magnify thee!

*Then: "It is truly meet to bless thee." Exapostilarion of the Tone.*

*At the Aposticha: Idiomelon Stichera, Tone 6:*

Having fallen away from sonship, wretched that I am, living slavishly with the swine, not even filled with their food (Luke 15:15–16), I come unto Thee, compassionate Father, whence I wickedly departed; returning well in repentance, I cry: I have sinned against heaven and before Thee, O Father, grant me great mercy in my turning! *(Twice)*

*Verse: (Ps. 89:14 LXX [90:14]): Martyrikon:* God has made His chosen ones marvelous, and His saints! Rejoice and be glad, all ye His servants, for He has prepared crowns and His Kingdom for you; but we entreat you, do not forget us also!

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*

*Theotokion:* O Mother of God, thou art the true Vine that didst blossom forth the Fruit of life; unto thee we pray: intercede, O Lady, with the holy Apostles and all the saints, that our souls may find mercy!

*On Thursday of the Third Week, at the Sixth Hour:*

*Troparion of the Prophecy, Tone 3:* If Thou shouldest mark iniquities, O Lover of mankind (Ps. 129:3 LXX [130:3]), what hope of salvation is there for us? But send down Thy help from on high unto Thy people, O Lord, as Thou art compassionate! *Glory... Both now... the same.*

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 53, Tone 4:* O God, in Thy name save me, and in Thy strength judge me: *Verse:* O God, hear my prayer, give ear unto the words of my mouth (Ps. 53:3, 4 LXX [54:1, 2]).

*Reading of the Prophecy of Isaiah (Isa. 11:10–11):*

Thus saith the Lord: In that day there shall be the Root of Jesse, and He that ariss to rule the nations: in Him shall the nations hope, and His rest shall be honor (Isa. 11:10; Rom. 15:12). And it shall come to pass in that day, that the Lord shall proceed to show His hand, to be zealous and seek out the remnant of the rest of the people, whosoever is left from the Assyrians, and from Egypt, and from Babylon, and Ethiopia, and from the Elamites, and from the rising of the sun, and from Arabia (Isa. 11:11b). And He shall lift up an ensign unto the nations, and shall assemble the wanderers of Israel, and gather the dispersed of Judah from the four wings of the earth (Isa. 11:12). And the envy of Ephraim shall be taken away, and the enemies of Judah shall perish; Ephraim shall not envy Judah, and Judah shall not distress Ephraim (Isa. 11:13). And they shall fly in the ships of the aliens, together they shall despoil the sea, and them that are from the rising of the sun and the valleys, and they shall first lay their hands upon Moab (Isa. 11:14). And the sons of Ammon shall be the first to obey (Isa. 11:15a). And the Lord shall make desolate the Sea of Egypt, and shall lay His hand upon the river with a vehement wind, and strike seven streams, so that he may pass through dry-shod (Isa. 11:15b). And there shall be a highway for My people that are left in Egypt; and it shall be for Israel as in the day when he came up out of the land of Egypt (Isa. 11:16). And in that day thou shalt say: I will bless Thee, O Lord, for Thou wast angry with me, and hast turned away Thy wrath from me, and hadst mercy on me! (Isa. 12:1). Behold, my God, my Savior, and the Lord: I will trust in Him and be saved in Him, and will not be afraid; for my glory and my praise is the Lord, and He is become my salvation! (Isa. 12:2).

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 54, Tone 7:* Give ear, O God, unto my prayer, and despise not my supplication: *Verse:* Attend unto me, and hear me (Ps. 54:2, 3 LXX [55:1, 2]).

*On the same Thursday of the Third Week, at Vespers, at "Lord, I have cried":*

*Stichera of Kyr Joseph, Tone 5, Podoben: "Rejoice, O container of ascetics" (Радуйся постником):*[^1320]

O Savior, true Sweetness, Who of old didst sweeten the bitter waters of Marah (Ex. 15:23–25) by the figure then of the divine Tree of the divine Cross, stretched out upon it even as Thou wast well-pleased: for Thou didst taste gall (Matt. 27:34), pierced in the side (John 19:34), whence the water of remission poured forth unto the world for the renewal of our earthly clay! Therefore we glorify Thy power ineffable, and we pray: grant us Thy fear, O Lord, in the time of fasting, and forgiveness of transgressions, and great mercy!

*Sticheron:* O Word Who wast stretched upon the Cross, gathering those far distant from Thee (John 11:52; 12:32): having raised my thought from the foulness of passions, enrich me with all virtues, granting unto my heart Thy purest fear, and unto my soul perfect love, cutting me off from carnal love; that by self-control unto Thee, by prayer and supplication in these present days, I may well-please Thee, and behold Thy radiant day of the Resurrection, receiving great mercy!

*Another Sticheron, of Kyr Theodore. Tone 1, Podoben: "A cloud of light" (Ѡ́блакъ тя):*[^1321]

Having traversed the third week of the precious fasts, O Christ the Word: vouchsafe us to behold the Tree of Thy life-bearing Cross, and to venerate it honorably, and to sing worthily, and to glorify Thy dominion, to hymn Thy Sufferings, to anticipate cleanly Thy glorious and holy Resurrection, the mystical Pascha, through which Adam entered again into Paradise!

*And 3 Martyrika. Prokeimenon, Psalm 55, Tone 6:* Have mercy on me, O God, for man hath trodden me down: *Verse:* Mine enemies have trodden me down all the day (Ps. 55:2, 3 LXX [56:1, 2]).

*Reading of Genesis (Gen. 7:11):*

*[Woodcut: Noah's Ark upon the waters of the Deluge, with animals and birds, and rain pouring down from heaven, bearing the inscription: "The Deluge condemns the disobedience of the bitter world."]*[^1322]

It came to pass in the six hundred and first year of the life of Noah, in the second month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, on that day all the fountains of the deep were broken up (Gen. 7:11 LXX).[^1323] And the floodgates of heaven were opened (Gen. 7:12). And rain was upon the earth forty days and forty nights. In that selfsame day entered Noah, and Shem, Ham, and Japhs, the sons of Noah, and the wife of Noah, and the three wives of his sons with him into the ark (Gen. 7:13). And all the wild beasts after their kind, and all the cattle after their kind, and every creeping thing after its kind, and every winged bird after its kind (Gen. 7:14). They went in unto Noah into the ark, two and two, male and female of all flesh, wherein is the breath of life (Gen. 7:15). And they that went in, male and female of all flesh went in, even as the Lord God had commanded Noah; and the Lord God shut him in from the outside of the ark (Gen. 7:16). And the deluge was forty days and forty nights upon the earth; and the water multiplied and lifted up the ark, and it was raised high above the earth (Gen. 7:17). And the water prevailed and multiplied exceedingly upon the earth, and the ark was borne upon the water (Gen. 7:18b). And the water prevailed exceedingly upon the earth, and covered all the high mountains that were under heaven (Gen. 7:19). Fifteen cubits upward did the water rise, and covered all the high mountains (Gen. 7:20). And all flesh died that moved upon the earth, of birds, and cattle, and wild beasts, and every creeping thing that moves upon the earth, and every man (Gen. 7:21). And all things whatsoever have the breath of life, and every one that was on dry land, died (Gen. 7:22). And every living substance was blotted out that was upon the face of all the earth, from man even unto cattle, and creeping things, and the birds of heaven; and they were blotted out from the earth, and Noah alone remained, and they that were with him in the ark (Gen. 7:23). And the water was exalted upon the earth a hundred and fifty days (Gen. 7:24). And God remembered Noah, and all the wild beasts, and all the cattle, and all the birds, and all the creeping things, whatsoever were with him in the ark; and God brought a wind upon the earth, and the water ceased (Gen. 8:1). And the fountains of the deep were stopped, and the floodgates of heaven; and the rain from heaven was restrained (Gen. 8:2). And the water gave way, receding from the earth, giving way and abating, after a hundred and fifty days (Gen. 8:3).

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 56, Tone 7:* Be Thou exalted above the heavens, O God, and Thy glory above all the earth: *Verse:* Ready is my heart, O God, ready is my heart (Ps. 56:6, 8 LXX [57:5, 7]).

*Reading of Proverbs (Prov. 10:1–3a):*

A wise son makes a glad father, but a foolish son is the grief of his mother (Prov. 10:1). Treasures of the lawless shall profit nothing, but righteousness shall deliver from death (Prov. 10:2). The Lord will not kill with hunger the soul of the righteous, but the life of the ungodly He shall overthrow (Prov. 10:3b). Poverty humbles a man, but the hands of the manly make rich (Prov. 10:4). A son that is instructed shall be wise, but a foolish one shall be used as a servant (Prov. 10:5 LXX). A man of understanding is saved from scorching heat, but a lawless son is smitten by the wind in harvest (Prov. 10:5a LXX).[^1324] The blessing of the Lord is upon the head of the righteous, but unseasonable grief shall cover the mouth of the ungodly (Prov. 10:6). The memory of the righteous is with praises, but the name of the ungodly is extinguished (Prov. 10:7). The wise in heart will receive commandments, but he that is babbling with his lips shall be tripped up and stumble (Prov. 10:8). He that walks simply walks trusting, but he that perverts his ways shall be known (Prov. 10:9). He that winks with the eye deceitfully gathers griefs for men, but he that reproves with boldness makes peace (Prov. 10:10 LXX).[^1325] A fountain of life is in the hand of the righteous, but destruction shall cover the mouth of the ungodly (Prov. 10:11). Hatred stirs up strife, but love covers all that are not contentious (Prov. 10:12). He that brings forth wisdom from his lips strikes with a rod the man void of heart (Prov. 10:13). The wise will hide discernment, but the mouth of the hasty draws near to destruction (Prov. 10:14). The possession of rich men is a strong city, but the destruction of the ungodly is poverty (Prov. 10:15). The works of the righteous produce life, but the fruits of the ungodly are sins (Prov. 10:16). Instruction keeps the ways of life, but instruction unrebuked strays (Prov. 10:17 LXX). Righteous lips cover enmity, but they that utter reproaches are most foolish (Prov. 10:18). From multitude of words thou shalt not escape sin, but he that spares his lips shall be prudent (Prov. 10:19b). Tried silver is the tongue of the righteous, but the heart of the ungodly shall fail (Prov. 10:20). The lips of the righteous know high things, but the foolish die in want (Prov. 10:21). The blessing of the Lord is upon the head of the righteous; this makes rich, and sorrow in the heart shall not be added unto it (Prov. 10:22).

*Then: "Vouchsafe, O Lord."*

*At the Aposticha: Idiomelon Stichera, Tone 6:*

Having beheld the Life of all suspended upon the Tree of the Cross, O Christ God, quicken my soul that is slain by transgressions, and leave not Thy sheep utterly to perish, O Good Shepherd! For I have estranged myself from Thy commandments, and the wealth of sinlessness which Thou gavest me, I squandered with a sin-loving will, and I corrupted and defiled myself in prodigal enterprises; but renew me, drawing me unto repentance, O Thou Who alone art abundant in mercy!

*Verse: Unto Thee have I lifted up mine eyes: (Ps. 122:1 LXX [123:1]).*

*The same Sticheron. Verse 2: Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us: (Ps. 122:3 LXX [123:3]): Martyrikon:* Thy Martyrs, O Lord, denied Thee not, nor departed from Thy commandments; through their prayers have mercy on us!

*Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion, the same Tone [Tone 6], Podoben: "Having risen on the third day" (Третій день):*[^1326]

Seeing Thee crucified, O Christ, she who bare Thee cried aloud: "What strange mystery is this that I behold, O my Son? How diest Thou in the flesh, suspended upon the Tree, O Giver of life?"

*Markian Chapter 5: If the Annunciation should occur on this Friday:* We sing the entire service of the Feast with the Triodion even as was indicated yesterday (see fol. 474)[^1327].

*If the Apodosis of the Annunciation of the Most Holy Theotokos fall on the Saturday, then here on Thursday at Compline we sing the Four-Ode Canon in advance. Thus do we when it falls on the Fourth Saturday, on March 26, or on the Fifth.*[^1328]

## ON FRIDAY OF THE THIRD WEEK OF THE HOLY FAST

*At Matins, the Triadica of the Tone. After the 1st Stichology, the Sessional Hymn in the Octoechos. After the 2nd Stichology, Sessional Hymn, of Kyr Joseph. Tone 5, Podoben: "The Word co-unoriginate" (Собезнача́лное):*[^1329]

We who died of old through the eating from the tree have been quickened by Thy Cross, O compassionate One! By its power, O good One, strengthen us to pass through the season of abstinence in compunction, doing Thy will, and to behold the day of Thy radiant Resurrection! *(Twice)*

*Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion:*

Beholding Thee upon the Cross, O Christ, suspended voluntarily in the midst of thieves, Thy Mother, beating her maternal womb, cried aloud: "O sinless Son, how art Thou unjustly lifted up upon the Cross as an evildoer, desiring as Thou art compassionate to quicken the human race?"

*After the 3rd Stichology, Sessional Hymn, of Kyr Theodore. Tone 4, Podoben: "Thy tomb, O Savior" (Гро́бъ тво́й):*[^1330]

Having cleansed our flesh through abstinence, and having enlightened our souls in prayers, O Lord, vouchsafe us to behold Thy most honorable and divine Cross, and to venerate it with fear, singing in hymns and saying: "Glory to the life-bearing Cross, glory to Thy divine Spear, whereby we have been quickened, O Thou Who alone art the Lover of mankind!" *(Twice)*

*Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion, the same Podoben:*

Beholding the Lamb suspended upon the Tree with thieves, O longsuffering Word, and pierced in the ribs with a Spear, the Ewe-lamb wailed, crying aloud maternally: "What is this strange and terrible mystery, O my Jesus? And how is the uncircumscribed God covered by a tomb? Ineffable is that which is wrought! Leave me not alone who bare Thee, O my sweetest Jesus!"

*Triode, of Kyr Joseph. Tone 5.*[^1331]
