*Ode 5. Heirmos: "Thou Who coverest Thyself with light" (Ѡдѣ́ѧйсѧ свѣ́томъ):*[^1332]

*Troparion:* Heal me, O Lord, and let my soul be healed by Thy wound, having cleansed my wounds, O Christ Who in the flesh didst receive the Passions!

*Troparion:* When the sun beheld Thee suspended in the flesh upon the Tree, O Christ, it turned its light into darkness, and the earth was shaken, and the rocks were split asunder! (Matt. 27:45, 51).

*Troparion:* Having cleansed my soul that is overgrown with thorns and made desolate with the forms of material passions, O Lord Who wast crowned with thorns, grant me Thine exceeding grace!

*Theotokion:* In a new manner hast thou borne as an Infant my Creator, O pure Lady; pray Him, O Sovereign Lady, to renew me who have grown old in manifold wickedness!

*Another Heirmos, of Kyr Theodore. Tone 4.*
*Heirmos: "Rising early from the night" (Ѿ но́щи ѹ҆́треннююще):*[^1333]

*Troparion:* In the Place of the Skull, the Jews crucified Thee, O Christ, shaking their heads, mocking and scoffing; but Thou didst endure, desiring to save us! (Matt. 27:33, 39).

*Troparion:* Having written threefold upon the title of Thy Cross (John 19:19–20), Pilate revealed Thee as One of the Trinity Who didst suffer voluntarily, O Christ, ordaining salvation!

*Triadikon:* Let us, the faithful, hymn the three-hypostatic Unity of the all-radiant Trinity, honoring the Light of the Father, glorifying the Light of the Son, and proclaiming the Light of the Spirit!

*Theotokion:* He Who is higher than angels was revealed as born of thee, O pure Lady; for Him Whom they tremble to behold as God, thou barest upon thine arms as Thine own Son, O pure Maiden!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*

*Troparion of the Cross:* O all-honorable Cross, saving guardian of the world, preserve me as I fast, and show me worthy of thine honorable veneration!

*Katavasia Heirmos:* Rising early from the night, we hymn Thee, O Christ God, Who for our sake didst become poor (2 Cor. 8:9), and didst endure the Cross and death in Thy flesh!

*Ode 8. Heirmos: "Thee, the Creator of all" (Тебѐ вседѣ́телю):*[^1334]

*Troparion:* Thou didst stretch out Thy palms upon the Cross, O Christ, abolishing the incontinence of the forefather's hands; and by the Tree Thou didst heal the curse of the tree; therefore we hymn Thee unto all ages!

*Troparion:* Unto Thee, O Word, Who willest salvation, I fall down; do Thou swiftly remove all-wicked desires from my heart, O Thou Who didst voluntarily endure crucifixion and passions!

*Troparion:* Having desired a prodigal life and a defiled conduct, I, the wretched one, have been darkened; shine upon me the ray of conversion, O Word, Who didst darken the shining of the sun in Thy Passion!

*Theotokion:* Put an end to my manifold-painful, all-heartfelt malice, O Mary, Mother of Christ; crush the arrows and bows of the demons who wage war against my humble soul!

*Another Heirmos. Tone 4, Heirmos: "The hymn-singers in the furnace" (Пѣсносло́вца въ пе́щи):*[^1335]

*Troparion:* What shall we, the wretched ones, offer unto Thee Who didst suffer, O Master of all? For for our sake Thou didst accept the Cross, O Christ; we hymn the goodness of Thy boundless mercy!

*Troparion:* Having slain Thee through envy upon the accursed tree (Gal. 3:13), O Christ, the lawless Jews did not diminish the dominion of Thy glory, for Thou art the Master of all Who didst suffer voluntarily!

*We bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, the Lord:*

*Triadikon:* I honor the three Persons of the super-essential Godhead: the unoriginate Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit; I glorify the Essence unknown by nature unto the ages!

*Theotokion:* Higher than the highest, and more glorious than the Cherubim, the holy-first and undefiled Maiden, the Mother of the God of all, we hymn and supremely exalt unto the ages!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*

*Troparion of the Cross:* O most blessed Cross of Christ, uncircumscribed victory, that hast sprouted forth from the earth for us: show us all worthy of thy veneration, to behold and to venerate thee!

*We praise, we bless, we worship the Lord:*

*Katavasia Heirmos:* Singing praise unto Christ God, Who saved the children in the furnace, and changed the burning furnace into dew: hymn and supremely exalt Him unto the ages!

*Ode 9. Heirmos: "O Isaiah, dance!" (И҆са́їа ликꙋ́й):*[^1336]

*Troparion:* Soften the petrified hardness of my soul, O Christ, and grant me a fountain of divine compunction, O good One, Who from Thy ribs didst pour forth life for me, consuming the torrents of my lawlessness!

*Troparion:* Having cast myself into the depth of sins, having abandoned the height of virtues: yet draw me and save me, O Lord Who didst ascend upon the Cross and didst draw mankind unto Thyself! (John 12:32).

*Troparion:* Being Sweetness and delight, as Creator Thou didst taste gall, O Christ, correcting that falling-away from sweetness which came from Adam; therefore, having been saved by Thy Passions, we hymn Thee!

*Theotokion:*

O all-immaculate Sovereign Lady, my hope and refuge: heal the wounds of my soul, bring peace unto my mind, that I also, rejoicing, may hymn thy great deeds, O Theotokos, Ever-Virgin!

*Another Heirmos. Tone 4, Heirmos: "Thee Whom Moses beheld" (Тѧ̀ ю́же ви́дѣ):*[^1337]

*Troparion:* Thee Whom the lawless, O Christ, mockingly clothed in purple and a crown, mocking Thee as King, striking Thy head with a reed, crucifying Thee out of envy, and giving Thee gall to drink: with hymns all we the faithful magnify! (Matt. 27:28–30, 34).

*Troparion:* Thee Whom the sun, seeing Thee suffering upon the Cross, hid its light, while all creation together bowed down at the Master's outrage, and the rocks split asunder: with hymns, O Christ the Savior, we magnify!

*Triadikon:* Light and Life and Creator, the three-hypostatic Unity, God and Lord, shining with one light, flashing forth with three characters in one Godhead: let all we the faithful worship Him!

*Theotokion:* Thee whom David the psalmist proclaimed as Zion (Ps. 131:13 LXX [132:13]), wherein He dwelt Who cannot be contained by the heavens, and fashioned from thy womb a cleansing for the world: with hymns, O pure Mother, we magnify!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*

*Troparion of the Cross:* Vouchsafe us, O Lord, who run by abstinence, to anticipate, kiss, and venerate Thy saving Cross, the enlightener of the faithful, unto our sanctification, that for its sake we may magnify Thee!

*Katavasia Heirmos:* Thee Whom Moses beheld as the unburnt Bush (Ex. 3:2), and the animate Ladder which Jacob saw (Gen. 28:12), and the impassable Gate through which Christ passed (Ezek. 44:2): with hymns, O pure Mother, we magnify!

*It is truly meet:*

*Exaposteilarion, Tone 4:*[^1338]

*At the Aposticha: Idiomelon Sticheron, Tone 6:*

I have squandered the wealth of the Father's gift; in prodigality have I spent my life; by wicked thoughts I was bound in my sin, and taking pleasure in the sweetness of passion, I became like the senseless beasts through the transgression of the saving commandments! But O Thou Who wast well-pleased to be suspended upon the Cross for my sake, O Christ God, cast me not away, Thy servant, but receive me as I turn back, even as the Prodigal Son, and save me! *(Twice)*

*The verses, (see fol. 74)[^1339]:*

*Martyrikon:* O Lord, in the memory of Thy saints, all creation keeps festival; the heavens rejoice with the angels, and the earth makes glad with men; through their prayers have mercy on us!

*Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion, Tone 6, Podoben: "Having risen on the third day" (Тре́тїй дн҃ь):*[^1340]

When the all-immaculate Virgin beheld Thee suspended upon the Cross, weeping she cried aloud maternally: "O my Son and my God, my sweetest Child, how endurest Thou shameful suffering?"

*On the same Friday of the Third Week: At the Sixth Hour, Troparion of the Prophecy, Tone 8:*

By Thy word Thou hast ordered all things by Thy power, O God, and brought us from non-being into being; deliver us not up unto our iniquities, O sinless Lord!

*Glory... the end: Both now... the same.*

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 57, Tone 6:* The righteous man shall be glad when he sees the vengeance: *Verse:* If ye indeed speak righteousness (Ps. 57:11, 2 LXX [58:10, 1]).

*Reading of the Prophecy of Isaiah (Isa. 13:2):*

Thus says the Lord: Upon a level mountain lift up a standard, raise the voice, fear not; summon with the hand, open the gates, ye princes! (Isa. 13:2).

I command, and I lead them: they are sanctified, and giants come to execute Mine anger, rejoicing together and reviling (Isa. 13:3 LXX).[^1341] A voice of many nations upon the mountains, like the voice of many nations; a voice of kings and nations gathered together: the Lord of Sabaoth hath commanded an armed nation (Isa. 13:4) to come from a far land, from the utmost foundations of heaven, the Lord and His warriors, to destroy all the world (Isa. 13:5). Wail ye, for the day of the Lord is at hand, and destruction from God shall arrive (Isa. 13:6). Therefore shall every hand be enfeebled, and every soul of man shall be dismayed (Isa. 13:7). The elders shall be troubled, and their pangs shall come upon them, even as of a woman in travail; and they shall weep one to another and be amazed, and their countenance shall they change like flame (Isa. 13:8 LXX).[^1342] For behold, the day of the Lord comes, with incurable wrath and anger, to lay the whole world desolate, and to destroy sinners from it (Isa. 13:9). For the stars of heaven, and Orion, and all the host of heaven shall not give their light and shall be darkened when the sun rises, and the moon shall not give her light (Isa. 13:10 LXX).[^1343] And I will command evils for all the world, and their sins upon the ungodly, and I will destroy the insolence of the lawless, and will humble the insolence of the proud (Isa. 13:11). And they that are left shall be more precious than refined gold, and a man shall be more honored than a stone from Ophir (Isa. 13:12 LXX).[^1344] For the heaven shall be incensed, and the earth shall be shaken from its foundations, because of the wrath of the anger of the Lord of Sabaoth, in the day whereinsoever His wrath shall come (Isa. 13:13 LXX)![^1345]

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 58, Tone 7:*

O God, Thou art my defender, and Thy mercy shall anticipate me: *Verse:* Deliver me from mine enemies, O God (Ps. 58:10b, 11, 2 LXX [59:9b, 10, 1]).

*On the same Friday of the Third Week, at Vespers. At "Lord, I have cried":*

*Idiomelon Sticheron, Tone 7:*

As the prodigal I departed from Thy goodness, O Lord, and squandered the wealth of grace; unto Thee have I fled, O compassionate One, crying aloud unto Thee: "O God, I have sinned, have mercy on me!" *(Twice)*

*Then the Martyrika of the Tone, 4; and from the Menaion, 4. Glory: for the departed, of the Tone; Both now: Theotokion of the same Tone; as indicated, (see fol. 312)[^1346].*

*At Vespers, Prokeimenon, Psalm 59, Tone 4:* Give us help from trouble, for vain is the salvation of man: *Verse:* O God, Thou hast cast us off and destroyed us (Ps. 59:13, 3 LXX [60:11, 1]).

*Reading of Genesis (Gen. 8:4–9):*

The ark rested in the seventh month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, upon the mountains of Ararat (Gen. 8:4 LXX).[^1347] And the water was continually decreasing until the tenth month. And in the eleventh month, on the first day of the month, the tops of the mountains were seen (Gen. 8:5). And it came to pass after forty days, Noah opened the window of the ark which he had made (Gen. 8:6). And he sent forth a raven to see if the water had abated; and it went forth and did not return until the water was dried up from the earth (Gen. 8:7). And he sent forth a dove after it to see if the water had abated from the face of the earth (Gen. 8:8). And the dove, not having found rest for her feet, returned unto him into the ark, for water was upon all the face of all the earth; and he stretched forth his hand, took her, and brought her in unto himself into the ark (Gen. 8:9).

And having waited yet other seven days, he sent forth again the dove from the ark (Gen. 8:10). And the dove returned unto him toward evening, and she had a leafy olive twig in her mouth; and Noah perceived that the water had abated from the earth (Gen. 8:11). And having waited yet other seven days, he sent forth again the dove; and she did not resume returning unto him anymore (Gen. 8:12). And it came to pass in the six hundred and first year of the life of Noah, in the first month, on the first day of the month, the water had failed from the face of the earth; and Noah uncovered the covering of the ark which he had made, and saw that the water had failed from the face of the earth (Gen. 8:13). And in the second month, on the seventeenth day of the month, the earth was dried (Gen. 8:14). On the twenty-seventh day of the month, he opened the ark (Gen. 8:15 LXX). And the Lord God spoke unto Noah, saying (Gen. 8:15): "Come forth out of the ark, thou, and thy wife, and thy sons, and the wives of thy sons with thee (Gen. 8:16); and all the wild beasts that are with thee, and all flesh, from birds even unto cattle, and every creeping thing that moves upon the earth, lead forth with thee, and increase ye and multiply upon the earth" (Gen. 8:17). And Noah came forth, and his wife, and his sons, and the wives of his sons with him (Gen. 8:18). And all the wild beasts, and all the cattle, and every bird, and every creeping thing that moves upon the earth, according to their kind, came forth out of the ark, on the first day of the third month (Gen. 8:19 LXX).[^1348] And Noah built an altar unto the Lord, and took of all clean cattle, and of all clean birds, and offered whole-burnt-offerings upon the altar (Gen. 8:20). And the Lord God smelled a sweet-smelling savor (Gen. 8:21a).

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 60, Tone 7:* Hear my supplication, O God, attend unto my prayer: *Verse:* From the ends of the earth have I cried unto Thee (Ps. 60:2, 3 LXX [61:1, 2]).

*Reading of Proverbs (Prov. 10:31–32; 11:1–12):*

The mouth of the righteous drips wisdom, but the tongue of the unjust shall perish (Prov. 10:31). The lips of righteous men drip graces, but the mouth of the ungodly is perverse (Prov. 10:32).

False balances are an abomination before the Lord, but a just weight is acceptable unto Him (Prov. 11:1). Wheresoever insolence enters, there also is dishonor; but the mouth of the humble meditates on wisdom (Prov. 11:2). The integrity of the upright shall guide them, but the stumbling of the rebellious shall despoil them (Prov. 11:3). Possessions shall not profit in the day of wrath, but righteousness shall deliver from death; when a righteous man dies, he leaves repentance, but the destruction of the ungodly is sudden and derisive (Prov. 11:4 LXX).[^1349] The righteousness of the blameless directs ways, but ungodliness falls into injustice (Prov. 11:5). The righteousness of upright men shall deliver them, but the lawless are caught in their own thoughtlessness (Prov. 11:6). When a righteous man dies, his hope does not perish; but the boast of the ungodly perishes (Prov. 11:7 LXX).[^1350] The righteous man escapes from the snare, and in his stead the ungodly man is delivered up (Prov. 11:8). In the mouth of the ungodly is a snare to citizens, but the perception of the righteous is prosperous (Prov. 11:9). In the good things of the righteous a city is set right, and at the destruction of the ungodly there is rejoicing (Prov. 11:10). By the blessing of the upright a city shall be exalted, but by the mouth of the ungodly it is overturned (Prov. 11:11). A man void of understanding scoffs at his fellow-citizens, but a prudent man keeps silence (Prov. 11:12).

*Then: "Let my prayer be set forth." And the rest of the Presanctified Liturgy.*

*If we do not celebrate the Presanctified Liturgy, see the instruction (see fol. 493)[^1351]. Only: At the Aposticha: Glory: to the saint of the temple; Both now: Theotokion, Tone 6: "Thou art our God" (seek on Meatfare Saturday: at Matins, at the Sessional Hymns, Tone 4). On the same Friday we sing at Compline the service of the saint of the Menaion who falls on this day, on account of the Sunday of the Adoration of the Cross.*

*If there fall on this Third Saturday of the Fast the Finding of the Head of the Forerunner, or the Forty Martyrs: their service is sung as on the Second Saturday of the Fast. Only the Canon of the Temple is sung with the Heirmos to 6; and of the Forerunner, or [of the Forty Martyrs] (see fol. 493)[^1352]. And Mark's Chapter, Chapter 66.*[^1353]

*Markian Chapter 80: If there fall on the Third or Fourth Saturday of the Fast the Annunciation of the Most Holy Theotokos:*[^1354]

*On Friday evening: Kathisma: "Unto the Lord when I was in affliction" (Ps. 119 LXX [120]). Stichera on 10: Idiomelon of the day, 2; and of the feast, 8. Glory... Both now...: Of the feast. And the Readings are read: first of the day, and after them of the feast, 5: "Moses beheld" (Exod. 3:1–8), 1; "The Lord created me" (Prov. 8:22–30), 3, which shall be from that of the day; and the other two readings. And the Presanctified Liturgy.*[^1355]

*At the same hour of the night, we sing Great Compline: when we reach the Canticle of the Prophet Isaiah, we sing "God is with us" [in the same manner as we do on fast days] on both choirs. After the 1st Trisagion, Troparion of the feast. After the 2nd Trisagion, Kontakion of the feast. After "Glory to God in the highest": Procession. And the rest as above (see fol. 474).*[^1356]

*At Matins, the entire service is of the feast; for neither the Four-Ode Canon nor anything else of the Saturday is sung, but all of the feast. But the Four-Ode Canon is sung in the Narthex, or in the crypt chapel.*[^1357]

*On Saturday before the Liturgy, at the 2nd hour of the day, we make a procession outside the Monastery. And having returned, we sing the Liturgy. And the Beatitudes from the Canon of the feast: Ode 3 and Ode 6. And all the rest of the feast.*

*If the Apodosis of the Annunciation of the Most Holy Theotokos fall on the Third or Fourth Saturday: At Matins on Saturday, Troparion of the feast, thrice. After the Kathisma, Sessional Hymns of the feast, and Reading of the feast. Canon of the feast with the Heirmos to 8, and of the Archangel to 6. Katavasia of the feast. But the Four-Ode Canon is not sung here, but in advance, on Thursday at Compline. After Ode 3, Kontakion of the Archangel, and Ikos; and Sessional Hymn of the Archangel, twice. Glory... Both now...: of the feast, and Reading of the feast. After Ode 6, Kontakion of the feast, and Ikos. At Ode 9 we do not sing "More honorable," but the Refrain of the feast: "O earth, proclaim good tidings": then the Heirmos, and unto each troparion:*

*To each troparion of the feast we sing that refrain, and after the Heirmos, a prostration to the earth. Exapostilarion of the feast; Glory: to the Archangel; Both now: of the feast. At the Praises: Stichera on 6: to the feast, 3; and to the Archangel, 3. Glory... Both now...: of the feast. Great Doxology. After the Trisagion, Troparion of the feast. Litany, and Dismissal. At the First Hour, Troparion and Kontakion of the feast, and the complete Dismissal. At the Liturgy: Beatitudes of the feast, Ode 3 and Ode 6. After the Entrance, Troparion of the feast. Glory... Both now...: Kontakion. Prokeimenon of the feast. Epistle, Alleluia, and Gospel of the day, and of the feast. Instead of "It is truly meet," we sing the Heirmos of the 9th Ode of the feast with the Refrain of the feast. Communion hymn of the feast. At the Elevation of the Panagia in the refectory, after the "Our Father": Kontakion of the feast.*

## ON THE THIRD OR FOURTH SATURDAY OF THE FAST

*At Matins, the customary service, as was directed for the Second Saturday (see fol. 493)[^1358]. After Ode 3, Kontakion of the Temple; then Sessional Hymn in the Menaion and of the Temple.*

*Four-Ode Canon, bearing the acrostic: "Joseph sings these things." Tone 4. Ode 6.*[^1359]
*Heirmos: "I came into the depths of the sea" (Прїидо́хъ въ глꙋбины́):*

*Troparion:* With drops of blood ye watered the hearts of the pious, and the hosts of the impious ye manifestly drowned therein, O glorious passion-bearers!

*Troparion:* Having glorified the Master of all with your members, now are ye unceasingly glorified, being a boast unto the faithful, O passion-bearers, great defenders!

*Troparion:* Thou wast laid in the lowest pit; grant therefore unto those who have died in faith rest, O Word, and forgiveness of transgressions, through the supplications of the holy passion-bearers!

*Theotokion:* That we may praise thee with unceasing voices, O Virgin, receive these our voices, and entreat Thy Son that we may receive cleansing of sins!

*Another Heirmos, of Kyr Theodore. Tone 8.*[^1360]
*Heirmos: "Receive me who am held fast" (О҆держи́ма мѧ прїимѝ):*

*Troparion:* Now is the festival of the Martyrs: let us gather together, and blessing their honorable sufferings, let us sing of Christ Who has crowned them all!

*Troparion:* Inflamed with the divine love of Christ, ye endured upon coals of fire as in dew, singing of Him, O blessed Martyrs!

*Glory... Triadicon:* Thee, O Trinity pre-unoriginate, and divine Unity, I sing as Light and Lights, Life and Lives, Mind, Word, and Holy Spirit, and Holy, the One God!

*Both now... Theotokion:* From thy root has budded the Flower of life; leap for joy, O Forefather Jesse! Saving the world from the pure Maiden, Christ God has appeared!

*Verse: God is wonderful in His saints (Ps. 67:36 LXX).*
*Troparion:* Fearing not fire, nor sword, nor death, ye preserved the confession of salvation, being strengthened by Christ, O blessed ones!

*Verse: Their souls shall dwell among good things (Ps. 24:13 LXX).*
*Troparion:* Free among the dead (Ps. 87:6 LXX), as the Son Who art the Prince of life and death, do Thou give rest unto those whom Thou hast received, and settle them in Thy courts, O Lover of mankind!

*Heirmos: Receive me, O Lover of mankind, who am held fast by many transgressions, as I fall down before Thy compassions, like the Prophet [Jonah], O Lord, and save me!*

*Then, the Litany for the departed. Kontakion: "With the saints give rest, O Christ": and Ikos (see fol. 40).*[^1361]

*Ode 7. Heirmos: "Three youths in Babylon" (Ю҆́нѡша три въ Вавѵлѡ́нѣ):*

*Troparion:* Unto whom, loving truly irrational passions, hast thou become likened, O my soul? Whom hast thou as helper in sins? Cry aloud unto Christ: Save me, O good One!

*Troparion:* Beseech diligently the Holy of Holies Who rests in the saints, that throughout all the holy days He may cleanse the hopes of all the pious!

*Troparion:* O Most High, rich in mercy, and good, unto Thy servants...

...who have died before, grant remission, numbering them with the choirs of the righteous, as the Lover of mankind!

*Theotokion:* Thou hast given birth contrary to the laws of nature, having become the Mother of the Creator as man, O pure Lady; pray Him therefore to overlook now the lawlessness and transgressions of all!

*Another Heirmos [Tone 8, Kyr Theodore]: "The youths being sprinkled by an Angel" (А҆́гг҃ломъ дѣ́ти):*[^1362]

*Troparion:* Thou Who didst show forth the memorial of the honorable martyrs as joy unto Thy Church and consolation of soul: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers!

*Troparion:* "We do not lie unto Thee, O Christ, nor do we deny Thee," the Martyrs cried aloud in the midst of torments, astounding the lawless tormentors: "Blessed art Thou unto ages of ages, O Lord God of our fathers!"

*Triadicon:* In three Persons we venerate one Nature, the Father, and the Son, and the Spirit, crying aloud prophetically: Blessed art Thou unto ages of ages, O Lord!

*Theotokion:* "How dost thou give birth as Mother, and yet hast remained a Virgin?" "Inasmuch as I bare God, inquire not into the manner, for what He wills, He does," cried the Maiden of God!

*Verse: God is wonderful in His saints, the God of Israel (Ps. 67:36 LXX).*
*Troparion:* O choir of Martyrs chosen of God, vouchsafe your servants to become venerators of the divine and life-creating Cross of the Savior!

*Verse: Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen (Ps. 64:5 LXX).*
*Troparion:* O Treasury of life, immortal King, vouchsafe Thy servants whom Thou hast chosen in steadfast hope unto Thine eternal life!

*Heirmos: Thou Who with an Angel didst bedew the children in the furnace, and didst turn the roaring fiery furnace into dew: Blessed art Thou unto ages of ages, O Lord God of our fathers!*

*Ode 8. Heirmos: "O Redeemer of all" (И҆зба́вителю всѣ́хъ):*

*Troparion:* With uninjured resolve of soul toward painful labors, O martyrs, ye received bodily pains...

...and having passed over unto painless enjoyment, ye lighten every pain of the heart!

*Troparion:* Ye who exchanged perishable things for the highest, save me who am corrupted by carnal passions, through fasting; and by diligent prayers, O divine Martyrs, pray God for all things!

*Troparion:* By the prayers of Thy Martyrs, O Christ, send down Thy mercies upon all; and unto those who have passed over from life unto Thee in peace, grant release from debts and divine rest!

*Theotokion:* As having given birth to the sinless God, blot out our sins by thy maternal prayers, O Theotokos, and save those who cry aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Another Heirmos [Tone 8, Kyr Theodore]: "The God-proclaiming children" (Бг҃оглаго́ливыя дѣ́ти):*[^1363]

*Troparion:* Having endured fiery torments as with dew, O passion-bearers, ye cried with joy: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Troparion:* The divinely armed regiment of Martyrs, having victoriously vanquished deception, cried aloud: Bless the works of the Lord!

*We bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, the Lord.*
*Triadicon:* With the Son let us worship the Father, and the Holy Spirit; let us all faithfully cry aloud: O Trinity in Unity, save our souls!

*Theotokion:* Thou hast been revealed as both Virgin and Mother, having given birth without a man to the God of all, O all-pure Lady; but pray Him to save thy servants!

*Verse: God is wonderful in His saints (Ps. 67:36 LXX).*
*Troparion:* By the prayers of the Martyrs, O Christ, vouchsafe Thy servants both to venerate and to behold the life-creating Cross of Thy goodness!

*Verse: Their souls shall dwell among good things (Ps. 24:13 LXX).*

*Troparion:* Thou Who didst destroy the dominion of death by Thy rising from the dead, vouchsafe those who have passed over to praise Thee, the Lord, with Thine elect!

*We praise, bless, and worship the Lord.*
*Heirmos: The God-proclaiming children in the furnace, trampling the blazing fire, sang: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!*

*Ode 9. Heirmos: "Eve indeed by the disease of disobedience" (Е҆́ѵа ѹ҆́бѡ недꙋ́гомъ):*

*Troparion:* Having established hope upon the spiritual Rock, O invincible passion-bearers, ye vanquished all the wiles of the enemy; therefore establish me who am dragged toward soul-destroying passions, by your divine prayers!

*Troparion:* O divine and truly light-radiant assembly of Martyrs, pray the all-good Master, in this season of abstinence, to grant unto us all forgiveness of our transgressions and eternal rejoicing!

*Troparion:* O Lover of mankind, Who alone art good, vouchsafe Thy servants who have fallen asleep in hope of resurrection to partake of Thine eternal, unwaning light, and to receive sweetness, that in love we may magnify Thee!

*Theotokion:* A dwelling of the Light was thy womb, O all-pure Sovereign Lady; therefore faithfully we cry aloud: Enlighten the pupils of our souls, and show paths of righteousness unto those who diligently bless thee!

*Another Heirmos [Tone 8, Kyr Theodore]: "We magnify thee, the Mother of the Light" (Велича́емъ тя Мт҃рь свѣ́та):*[^1364]

*Troparion:* We, the faithful, celebrate the memorial of the Martyrs, that we may partake of their glory, praising the sufferings of their contests!

*Troparion:* At your courage the wild beasts were greatly afraid, the fire was quenched, the bows of the deceitful were shattered; in you, O passion-bearers, God is wonderful!

*Triadicon:* O pre-unoriginate Nature, Trinity in three Hypostases...

...Father, and Son, and Holy Spirit, Light and Life divinely sovereign: preserve those who give glory unto Thee!

*Theotokion:* We bless Thee, the God of Israel, Who appearedst unto the world from the Virgin, and didst raise up the horn of our salvation!

*Verse: Unto the saints that are in His earth, marvelous has the Lord made all His desires in them (Ps. 15:3 LXX).*
*Troparion:* O intercessors for the world, passion-bearers of Christ: vouchsafe all to behold and venerate His Cross, by your prayers!

*Verse: Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen (Ps. 64:5 LXX).*
*Troparion:* Where the fountain of life wells forth, O Son of God, and the visitation of the enlightenment of Thy countenance: establish those who have passed over unto Thee, and deliver them from torment!

*Heirmos: We magnify thee, the Mother of the Light, and we glorify thee, O Virgin Theotokos, as having given birth to the Savior of our souls!*

*Then: "It is truly meet." Exapostilarion: "Thou Who hast adorned the heaven with stars" (Не́бо ѕвѣ́здами). Glory: "Having dominion over the dead and the living" (Ме́ртвыми и живы́ми облада́яй). Both now: Theotokion: "The joy of angels" (Сла́дость А҆́ггеловъ). Likewise the instruction for the Praises and the Aposticha as on the Second Saturday of the Fast (see fol. 493)[^1365]. Then: "It is good to give praise to the Lord." Trisagion. After "Our Father": Troparion. Litany, and Dismissal.*

*At the Liturgy: Beatitudes of the Tone. Prokeimenon of the day, and for the departed. Epistle to the Hebrews, Pericope 325 (Heb. 10:32–38): "Brethren, call to remembrance..." Another, for the departed. Alleluia, Tone 6. Gospel from Mark, Pericope 8 (Mark 2:14–17): "At that time, Jesus passed by..." And for the departed. Communion hymn of the day, and for the departed. As we also directed for the Second Saturday.*[^1366]

*[Woodcut Engraving: The Crucifixion of the Lord, with the Mother of God, St. John the Theologian, and the holy women standing by, the two thieves, instruments of the Passion, and view of Jerusalem; inscriptions: "IC XC", "INBI", "CRUCIFIXION OF THE LORD", "ST. JOHN", "MOTHER OF GOD"; engraver's monogram lower left: "LP * 1638"].*[^1367]

## THE THIRD SUNDAY OF THE HOLY FAST: OF THE ADORATION OF THE PRECIOUS CROSS

*On Saturday evening: At Little Vespers:*

*Stichera on 4. Tone 6, Podoben: "The Angelic Powers" (А҆гг҃лскїѧ си́лы):*[^1368]

*Sticheron:* Now the angelic hosts stand round the honorable Tree, reverently encompassing it and summoning all the faithful unto adoration! Come therefore, ye who have been enlightened by the Fast: let us fall down before it in joy and fear, crying faithfully: Rejoice, O honorable Cross, confirmation of the world!

*Sticheron:* That Thou mightest abolish Adam's curse, Thou didst assume our flesh without defilement, and wast crucified and didst die, O all-good Jesus! Therefore Thy Cross, and Spear, Sponge and Reed, and Nails, we faithfully...

...venerate, and we pray to behold Thy Resurrection!

*Sticheron:* Of old the serpent closed Eden by a tree; but the Tree of the Cross opens it unto all who desire to be cleansed by fasting and tears. Come therefore, beholding it lying before us, let us fall down before it in fear, crying faithfully: Open the heavenly gates, O Cross, unto those that love thee!

*Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion:* When she who bare Thee seedlessly beheld Thee, the Word of God, nailed unto the Cross, she cried aloud, weeping: "Woe is me, my sweetest Child! What is this Thy humility, O my God? How dost Thou Who art passionless endure suffering by an unjust judgment? I confess Thine extraordinary, ultimate condescension!"

*At the Aposticha: Stichera. Tone 2, Podoben: "O House of Ephratha" (До́ме Еѵфра́):*[^1369]

*Sticheron:* Having been released from the bonds of ancient condemnation by the Tree of the Cross, let us, the faithful, glorify Christ Who was nailed upon it!

*Verse: Exalt ye the Lord our God, and worship His footstool; for He is holy (Ps. 98:5 LXX).*
*Sticheron:* Come now with us, O David, strike the psaltery: "Sing unto Christ!" faithful people, "worship His footstool!"

*Verse: But God is our King before the ages, He has wrought salvation in the midst of the earth (Ps. 73:12 LXX).*
*Sticheron:* Let us exalt, O ye people, the Tree lying before us, whereby Christ grants salvation unto us, and let us kiss it with faith!

*Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion, the same Podoben:* Seeing Thy Son lifted up upon the Cross, O Virgin, she cried aloud, lamenting: "Glory to Thy compassion!"

*Then: "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart." Trisagion. After "Our Father":*
*Troparion, Tone 1:*
Save, O Lord, Thy people, and bless Thine inheritance, granting victories to Orthodox rulers over barbarians, and preserving Thy people by Thy Cross![^1370]

*Litany, and Dismissal.*

*And after the Dismissal, the Priest enters with the Ecclesiarch into the vestry; and they take the Honorable Wood, a candle and censer preceding them, while they sing the Troparion: "Save, O Lord, Thy people": and they bring it unto the Holy Table. And they kindle a candle for the whole night.*[^1371]

*And at the Vigil, the customary Stichology.*

*At "Lord, I have cried": Stichera on 10: Resurrectional, 3; and Anatolian, 3; and of the Cross, 4. Tone 5, Podoben: "Rejoice, O container of ascetics" (Ра́дꙋйсѧ по́стникѡ):*[^1372]

*Sticheron:* Rejoice, O life-bearing Cross, fair Paradise of the Church, Tree of incorruption that didst bud forth for us the enjoyment of eternal glory, whereby the legions of demons are driven away, and the ranks of Angels rejoice, and the assemblies of the faithful keep festival; invincible weapon, unshakable confirmation, victory of rulers, boast of hierarchs: grant us also now to attain unto the Passions of Christ, and great mercy!

*Sticheron:* Rejoice, O life-bearing Cross, invincible weapon of piety, gates of Paradise, confirmation of the faithful, rampart of the Church, whereby the curse was abolished and made void, and the dominion of death was trampled down, and we were lifted up from earth unto heaven; unconquerable weapon, adversary of demons, glory of Martyrs, true ornament of venerable monastics, haven of salvation: grant unto the world great mercy!

*Sticheron:* Come, O first-fashioned pair, who fell from the celestial choir through the envy of the man-slayer, by the bitter pleasure of the tasting from the tree of old! Behold the truly all-honorable...

...Tree draws near! Running unto it, embrace it with joy, and cry out unto it with faith: "Partaking of Whose fruit, we have obtained incorruption, receiving the sure great mercy of the first Eden!"[^1373]

*Sticheron:* Shine forth, O Cross of the Lord, the light-bearing lightning-flashes of Thy grace into the hearts of them that honor thee and receive thee with acceptable love, O thou desired of the world! For by them tearful compunction is consumed, and we are delivered from the snares of death, and have arrived at everlasting gladness. Show forth the majesty of thy beauty; grant the reward of abstinence unto thy servants, who faithfully entreat thy rich protection and great mercy!

*Glory: Tone 3:* O Christ our God, Who didst accept voluntary Crucifixion for the general resurrection of the human race, and with the Reed of the Cross didst stain Thy fingers with purple dye, mercifully deigning to sign our royal remission with imperial cinnabar:[^1374] despise us not in our afflictions and in our renewed estrangement from Thee; but take pity, O Thou only Long-suffering One, on Thy people in adversity, and arise and conquer them that war against us, for Thou art almighty!

*Now and ever: Theotokion of the Tone.*

*Entrance. "O Gladsome Light." Prokeimenon: "The Lord is King." Litany. And the rest as customary.*

*At the Litiya, Stichera of the Temple.*
*Glory, and now and ever: Tone 5:*
All creation, seeing Thee hanging naked upon the Cross, the Creator and Fashioner of all, was altered with fear and wailed; the sun darkened its light, and the earth quaked, the rocks split, and the veil of the temple was rent in twain; the dead arose from the graves, and the Angelic powers were astonished, saying: "O wonder! The Judge is judged, and willingly suffers for the salvation and renewal of the world!"

*At the Aposticha, Stichera from the Oktoechos, and alphabetical.*
*Glory, and now and ever: Tone 4:*
O Lord, Who didst help the meek David to conquer the alien: assist our faithful ruler,[^1375] and by the weapon of the Cross cast down our enemies; show forth upon us, O Compassionate One, Thy ancient mercies, that they may truly know that Thou art God, and that hoping in Thee we conquer, through the customary intercessions of Thy Most Pure Mother, that there be granted unto us great mercy!

*Troparion: "Save, O Lord, Thy people," twice. If sung at Small Vespers: Glory, and now and ever: "O Theotokos Virgin," once (see fol. 170).[^1376]*

*If the Finding of the Precious Head of John the Forerunner, or the Forty Martyrs, falls on this Third Sunday of Lent:*[^1377]
*Small Vespers as customary.*
*At Great Vespers, after the Kathisma: At "Lord, I have cried": Stichera: Resurrectional, 3; and of the Cross, 4; and of the Forerunner, 3. Glory: of the Cross. Now and ever: Dogmatic Theotokion of the Tone. Prokeimenon of the day. And the Old Testament Readings of the Forerunner. At the Litiya, Stichera of the Saint of the Temple, and of the Forerunner, 3, which are at the Aposticha and at the Praises. Glory: of the Forerunner. Now and ever: of the Cross: "All creation, seeing Thee." At the Aposticha: Resurrectional. Glory: of the Forerunner: "A divine treasure." Now and ever: of the Cross: "O Lord, Who didst help." At the Blessing of the Loaves: Troparion: "O Theotokos Virgin," twice; and of the Cross, once.*

*At Matins. At "God is the Lord": Troparion: Resurrectional, twice; Glory: of the Forerunner; Now and ever: of the Cross. After the Kathismata: Sessional Hymns: Resurrectional, and their Theotokia; and a reading from the Commentary on the Gospel. The Blameless (Kathisma 17). Hypakoe of the Tone. Polyeleos of the Forerunner, and the Sessional Hymns all once; Glory, and now and ever: Theotokion; and a reading of the Forerunner. Gradual Antiphons of the Tone. Prokeimenon and Resurrection Gospel. "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ." Psalm 50. Sticheron: "Open unto me the gates of repentance" (see fol. 154).[^1378] Canon: Resurrectional with the Heirmos, on 4; and of the Forerunner on 4; and of the Cross on 6. Katavasia of the Cross, both choirs together: "In divine type of old." After Ode 3: Kontakion of the Forerunner and Ikos, and his Sessional Hymns, 2;*

*Glory, and now and ever: of the Cross: "Today the prophetic word." And a reading of the Forerunner. After Ode 6: Kontakion of the Cross and Ikos. At Ode 9: we sing: "More honorable than the Cherubim."*
*Exapostilarion: Resurrectional; Glory: of the Forerunner; Now and ever: of the Cross.*
*At the Praises: Stichera: Resurrectional on 4; and of the Cross, prosomoia, 3, with their verses: Verse 1: "Remember Thy congregation." Verse 2: "For God is our King." And then the verse: "Arise, O Lord my God" (of David); and we sing the idiomelon of the day from the Triodion. Glory: the same; Now and ever: "Most blessed art thou." Great Doxology. And the rest of the order of the veneration of the Precious Cross, as indicated in course. And the customary Litanies, and Dismissal. And the procession: Glory, and now and ever: Gospel Sticheron. Studite Catechesis,[^1379] and the First Hour in the Narthex.*

*At the Hours: Troparion: Resurrectional; Glory: of the Cross; Now and ever: Theotokion of the Hours. After "Our Father": Kontakion of the Cross. At the other Hour: Troparion: Resurrectional; Glory: of the Forerunner; Now and ever: Theotokion of the Hours. After "Our Father": Kontakion of the Forerunner.*
*At the Liturgy: The Beatitudes of the Tone on 4; and of the Cross, Ode 3, on 4; and of the Forerunner, Ode 6, on 4. After the Entrance: Troparia: Resurrectional, and of the Cross, and of the Forerunner; Glory: Kontakion of the Forerunner; Now and ever: Kontakion of the Cross. Prokeimenon, Epistle, Alleluia, Gospel, and Communion Verse: first of the Cross, then of the Forerunner.*

*(Markian Chapter 81):[^1380] If the Annunciation of the Most Holy Theotokos falls on this Third Sunday of Lent:*
*On Saturday evening, at Small Vespers: At "Lord, I have cried": Stichera: Resurrectional, 4; Glory, and now and ever: of the Feast. At the Aposticha: Resurrectional Sticheron, 1; and of the Feast, 3, idiomela, with their verses, which are written at Great Vespers: Tone 4; Glory, and now and ever: of the Feast. After the Trisagion: Troparion: Resurrectional; Glory, and now and ever: of the Feast; and Litany, and Dismissal.*

*At Great Vespers: The entire Kathisma: "Blessed is the man." At "Lord, I have cried": Stichera: Resurrectional, 3; and of the Cross, prosomoia, 3; and of the Feast, 4. Glory: of the Cross, Tone 3: "O Christ our God"; Now and ever: of the Feast, Tone 6: "The Archangel Gabriel was sent." Then: Entrance, and the Old Testament Readings of the Feast, 5.*

*At the Litiya: Stichera of the Feast: idiomela, 3, Tone 1; and Stichera of the Cross, 3, Tone 4, Podoben: "As noble among Martyrs" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ) (written at the Praises); Glory: Tone 2: "Gabriel announces the glad tidings"; Now and ever: of the Cross, Tone 5: "All creation, seeing Thee." At the Aposticha: Resurrectional, which are alphabetical; Glory: of the Cross: "O Lord, Who didst help"; Now and ever: of the Feast: "Today is the joy of the Annunciation." At the Blessing of the Loaves: Troparion of the Feast, twice; and of the Cross, once. Reading from the Apostolic Epistles, and the other readings of the Feast.*

*At Matins. At "God is the Lord": Troparion: Resurrectional, twice; Glory: of the Cross; Now and ever: of the Feast. After the Kathismata: Sessional Hymns: Resurrectional, with their Theotokia; and a reading from the Commentary on the Gospel.*

*The Blameless (Kathisma 17). Hypakoe of the Tone, and a reading from the Gospel. Polyeleos, and the Sessional Hymns of the Feast all once; Glory, and now and ever: of the Feast, and reading 1. Gradual Antiphons of the Tone. Prokeimenon, and Gospel of the Feast. "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ." Psalm 50. Sticheron of the Feast. Canon: Resurrectional on 4; and of the Cross on 4; and of the Feast on 6. But if the Canon of the Cross has a Resurrectional Troparion in every Ode, then the Resurrectional Canon of the Tone is omitted; and the Heirmos of the Canon of the Cross is sung twice, and the Resurrectional Troparion twice that is in the Canon of the Cross, and the remaining Troparia of the Cross on 4, and of the Feast on 6. Katavasia of the Feast: Heirmos: "I shall open my mouth," both choirs together. After Ode 3: Kontakion of the Cross, and Ikos, and Sessional Hymn of the Cross; Glory, and now and ever: of the Feast; Reading of the Feast. After Ode 6: Kontakion of the Feast, and Ikos, and the Prologue. At Ode 9: we sing: "More honorable than the Cherubim." Exapostilarion: Resurrectional; Glory: of the Cross; Now and ever: of the Feast. At the Praises: Stichera: Resurrectional, 4; and of the Feast, 5, Tone 1, Podoben: "Joy of the celestial ranks" (Нб҃нымъ чи́нѡмъ); and idiomela, Tone 2: "The mystery hidden from the ages," with their verses: Verse 1: "Proclaim from day to day"; Verse 2: "Sing unto the Lord a new song." Then the verse: "Arise, O Lord my God" (of David); and we sing the idiomelon Sticheron of the day; Glory: the same; Now and ever: "Most blessed art thou." Great Doxology. And the service of the Veneration of the Cross as customary, as shall be told in course. And after the prayers of the Cross: Resurrectional Prokeimenon of the Tone, and Resurrection Gospel. And we chant the Litanies: "Let us all say," and "Let us complete our prayer unto the Lord," and the Dismissal. Procession into the Narthex: Glory, and now and ever: Gospel Sticheron; Studite Catechesis. First Hour. At the First Hour: Troparion: Resurrectional; Glory: of the Cross; Now and ever: Theotokion of the Hours. After "Our Father": Kontakion of the Cross. And complete Dismissal.*

*And at the second hour of the day, we go outside the Monastery; and having returned, we sing the Hours. At the Third Hour: Troparion: Resurrectional; Glory: of the Feast; Now and ever: Theotokion of the Hours. After "Our Father": Kontakion of the Feast. At the Sixth Hour: Troparion: Resurrectional; Glory: of the Cross; Now and ever: Theotokion of the Hours. After "Our Father": Kontakion of the Cross.*

*At the Liturgy: The Beatitudes of the Tone on 4, and of the Cross, Ode 6, on 4. After the Entrance: Troparion: Resurrectional, and of the Cross, and of the Feast; Glory: Kontakion of the Cross; Now and ever: Kontakion of the Feast. Instead of the Trisagion, we sing: "Before Thy Cross we bow down in worship, O Master." Prokeimenon, Epistle, Alleluia, Gospel, and Communion Verse: first of the Feast, and then of the Cross.*
*The Liturgy of Basil the Great without change.*

*If the Synaxis of the Archangel Gabriel falls on this Third Sunday of Lent:[^1381] his service is sung in course; but the Afterfeast Canon of the Theotokos is sung previously on Saturday at Compline.*

*At Matins. At "God is the Lord": Troparion: Resurrectional; Glory: "Save, O Lord, Thy people"; Now and ever: Theotokion: "When Gabriel announced." The customary Stichology. Resurrectional Sessional Hymns. And the rest as in the past Sundays.*

*(After the Polyeleos, if there be a temple of the Cross:[^1382] Sessional Hymn of the Cross, Tone 8, Podoben: "That which was commanded secretly" (Повелѣ́нное та́иннѡ):*
*Of old in Paradise the enemy stripped us by the tree, bringing deadliness through the tasting. But the Tree of the Cross, bearing the garment of life unto men, was brought forth upon earth, and the whole world was filled with all joy; and beholding it, we bow down in worship, and with one accord in faith, O people, let us cry aloud unto God, His temple full of glory!)*

*Gradual Antiphons of the Tone. Matins Gospel. Psalm 50. "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ." Glory: Tone 8: "Open unto me the gates of repentance." And the rest: see fol. 154.[^1383]*

*Canon: Resurrectional, and of the Theotokos, on 6; and the present Canon on 8. Tone 1. Ode 1. Heirmos. By Kyr Theodore the Studite: "It is the day of Resurrection" (Въскр҃нїѧ дн҃ь):*[^1384]

*Troparion:* It is the day of celebration! By the Resurrection of Christ death is shown to be vanished, the dawn of life hath shone forth, Adam arisen dances for joy; therefore let us cry aloud, singing the song of victory!

*Troparion:* It is the day of veneration of the Precious Cross! Come unto it, all ye people, for by the Resurrection of Christ it now stretches forth light-bearing beams. Let us embrace it, rejoicing in soul!

*Troparion:* Appear, O great Cross of the Lord! Show me now the divine aspect of Thy beauty, and make me a worthy worshiper for thy praise; for as unto one animate I cry out unto thee and fall down before thee!

*Troparion:* Let heaven and earth praise in unison, for the most blessed Cross lies before all, whereon Christ was laid, nailed in the flesh. Let us embrace it, rejoicing in soul!

*Glory: Triadikon:* O Trinity in persons, O Monad in form, Father and Son and Spirit, Monad of equal power in counsel, will, and origin of dominion: preserve Thy world, granting peace!

*Now and ever: Theotokion:* O Virgin who knowest no man at all, seedlessly dost Thou bring forth a babe, purely bearing the offspring, Christ God, the Creator of the world: implore Him to pacify all things.

*Katavasia:* In divine type of old Moses, leading Israel through the Red Sea, by Thy Cross did divide the water with his staff, chanting an exodus song unto Thee, O Christ God![^1385]

*Ode 3. Heirmos: "Come, let us drink a new drink" (Прїиди́те пи́во пїемъ):*
*Troparion:* Come, let us sing a new song, celebrating the destruction of Hades, for Christ arose from the tomb, taking death captive, and saved all things!

*Troparion:* Come, O faithful, let us draw, not corruptible water pouring forth from wells, but the fountain of enlightenment through the veneration of the Cross of Christ, wherein we also boast!

*Troparion:* Embracing now Thy Cross, which of old Moses prefigured with outstretched hands, we conquer the noetic Amalek, O Master Christ, whereby we are saved!

*Troparion:* With pure eyes and lips striking up a song of rejoicing, let us, the faithful, bow down in worship with joy before the Cross of the Lord, clapping our hands with hymns!

*Glory: Triadikon:* I honor one unoriginate God in three hypostases, undivided in the form of essence: the Father, and the Son, and the Living Spirit, in Whom we were baptized!

*Now and ever: Theotokion:* In the bush Moses of old beheld in figure Thy mystery, O Pure One; for as its flame burned not, so the fire of the Godhead consumed not Thy womb!

*Heirmos (Katavasia):* Establish, O Master Christ, upon the rock of the faith of Thy Cross, my mind not to be shaken by the assaults of the enemy; for Thou alone art holy![^1386]

*Resurrectional Sessional Hymn from the Oktoechos, Tone 6:*
Thy Cross, O Lord, is sanctified, for thereby healings are wrought for them that are sick in sins. Therefore we fall down before Thee: have mercy upon us!

*Verse: Exalt ye the Lord our God, and worship the footstool of His feet, for He is holy (Ps. 98:5 LXX):*[^1387]
Today the prophetic word is fulfilled; behold, we bow down in worship in the place where Thy feet stood, O Lord; and having tasted the Tree of salvation, we have obtained deliverance from sinful passions, through the prayers of the Theotokos, O Thou only Lover of mankind!

*Glory:*
No sooner was the Tree of Thy Cross planted, O Christ, than the foundations of death were shaken, O Lord; for whom Hades had swallowed with desire, it released with trembling. Thou hast revealed unto us Thy holy salvation, and we glorify Thee, O Son of God: have mercy upon us!

*Now and ever: Theotokion:*
O Virgin Theotokos, implore Thy Son Who was nailed upon the Cross, and arose from the dead, Christ our God, that our souls may be saved!

*Ode 4. Heirmos: "Upon the divine watch" (На бж҃їи стра́жи):*
*Troparion:* "Behold, Christ is risen!" the Angel said unto the Myrrh-bearing women: "Wail not, but go and tell the Disciples: Rejoice! Today is the salvation of the world, and the tyranny of the enemy hath been destroyed by Death!"

*Troparion:* Setting forth today the venerated joy of Thy life-bearing Cross, O Christ, we most radiantly celebrate the festival of Thy Resurrection; for Thou hast wrought salvation for the world, O Savior, for Thou art almighty!

*Troparion:* Today there is joy in heaven and on earth, for the thrice-blessed Cross, the sign of Christ, is made manifest unto the world! For having been set forth, it pours forth ever-flowing joy unto them that bow down in worship before it!

*Troparion:* What shall we offer unto Thee, O Christ, that Thou hast granted us to bow down in worship before the Precious Cross, whereon Thou didst pour out Thy Most Pure Blood, and whereon Thy flesh was pierced with nails? Embracing it now, we bless Thee!

*Glory: Triadikon:* I sing of one Godhead, three hypostases, undivided; I proclaim a simple essence: the Father unoriginate, the Son, and the Holy Spirit enthroned together: one Lordship, and one Kingdom, one eternal Dominion!

*Now and ever: Theotokion:* Alone among women hast thou appeared as a most marvelous wonder, O pure Virgin, an awesome thing to hear! For thou hast surpassed nature; having given birth without a man, thou remainest again a Virgin as before childbirth; for He that was born of thee is truly God!

*Katavasia:* Seeing Thee upon the Cross, O Mighty One, the great luminary was seized with trembling, and hid its rays; and all creation sang of Thy long-suffering in Thy Passion: for the earth was filled with Thy praise![^1388]

*Ode 5. Heirmos: "Let us rise early in the morning" (ᲊтреннюемъ ᲂу҆́трꙋ):*
*Troparion:* Thou hast shone forth from the tomb, O unwaning Light, flashing forth incorruption upon the world; Thou hast consumed mortal mourning, O Lord, from the ends of the earth, as Thou art merciful!

*Troparion:* Let us draw near, purified by abstinence, warmly embracing with praise the most holy Tree whereon Christ was crucified, saving the world, for He is compassionate!

*Troparion:* The angelic ranks dance in gladness today at the veneration of Thy Cross; for thereby Thou didst cast down the demonic legions, O Savior Christ, saving mankind!

*Troparion:* The Church is known as another Paradise, having of old as a tree the life-bearing Cross of Thine, O Lord, from which through touching we have partaken of immortality!

*Glory: Triadikon:* I glorify Three co-unoriginate Persons of one essence, God the Father, the Son, and the Spirit: one three-radiant Light, jointly sovereign Kingdom, in unconfused union!

*Now and ever: Theotokion:* Thou hast given birth by the law of nature, yet above the law, for Thine alone is a seedless birthgiving! Awesome and inconceivable, both to ponder and to utter, is the manner of Thy childbearing, O All-immaculate One!

*Katavasia:* Rising early, we hymn Thee, O only Compassionate One, having found peace through Thy Cross, whereby Thou hast renewed the human race, leading us unto the never-waning light![^1389]

*Ode 6. Heirmos: "Thou didst descend into the deepest parts of the earth" (Соше́лъ є҆сѝ въ преиспо́днѧѧ):*
*Troparion:* Thou hast arisen, trampling down death, O Christ, like a great King; from the treasure-vaults of Hades Thou hast summoned us into the rest of the Heavenly Kingdom, into the land of immortality!

*Troparion:* Clapping our hands with divine hymns, O ye faithful, let us cry aloud unto God, kissing the Cross of the Lord; for it pours forth a fountain of salvation unto all that are in the world!

*Troparion:* The voice of the psalmist is fulfilled: for behold, we bow down in worship before the footstool of Thy Most Pure feet, O Almighty One, before Thy Precious Cross, the thrice-desired Tree![^1390]

*Troparion:* Embracing Thy Cross—which the weeping prophet among the prophets beheld cast into Thy bread[^1391]—we hymn Thy bonds, and Thy burial, the spear, and the nails!

*Troparion:* Embracing with our flesh the Holy Cross, which Thou didst deign to bear upon Thy shoulders, O Christ, and whereon Thou wast lifted up and crucified, we gather strength against invisible enemies!

*Glory: Triadikon:* I hymn the Monad in three Persons, and the Trinity worshiped in one essence, God triply-joined, three-sunned Light, the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit!

*Now and ever: Theotokion:* A great wonder of wonders is manifest in thee, O undefiled Ewe-lamb! For thou hast given birth to the Lamb that takes away the sins of the world; entreat Him earnestly on behalf of them that sing of thee!

*Katavasia:* Jonah, stretching out his hands in the form of a cross within the belly of the sea monster, prefigured the image of the Divine Cross; and leaping forth saved from the beast by Thy power, O Word![^1392]

*Kontakion, Tone 7, Idiomelon:*
No longer does the flaming sword guard the gate of Eden; for upon it hath come a marvelous bond: the Tree of the Cross. The sting of death and the victory of Hades have been driven away; for Thou hast come, O my Savior, crying aloud unto them that were in Hades: "Enter ye again into Paradise!"

*Ikos:*
Pilate set up three crosses upon Golgotha: two for the thieves, and one for the Giver of life, Whom Hades beheld and said unto them below: "O my servants and my power! Who hath driven nails into my heart? A wooden Spear hath suddenly pierced me, and I am torn asunder; I am in pain within, and my belly is wounded; my senses devour my spirit, and I am constrained to vomit forth Adam and them that are with Adam, who were given unto me by the tree; for the Tree leads them back into Paradise!"

*Synaxarion:*
*Verses:*
Let all the earth bow down before the Cross,
Through which it learned to worship Thee, O Word.

On this Third Sunday of the Fasts, we celebrate the veneration of the Precious and Life-giving Cross, for the following reason:[^1393] Inasmuch as through the forty-day fast, in a certain manner, we also are crucified, being mortified by passions, and having already the weariness of bitterness and hardship, living intemperately, and falling down: the Precious and Life-giving Cross is set forth, as it were giving heart, strengthening, and invigorating us; likewise bringing to our remembrance the Sufferings of our Lord Jesus Christ, and granting us consolation: if our God was crucified for us, how much more does it behoove us for His sake to do so!

...to do so; easing also our labors by setting before our eyes the afflicted suffering of Christ, and by the remembrance and hope of that glory and majesty which is given because of the Cross.[^1394] For as our Savior, having mounted the Cross, was glorified because of the unseemly degradation and mockery, and very great bitterness and torment: so it behooves us also to do, that we may be glorified together with Him, even though we suffer ungratefully and without any sweetness. And explaining this yet in another way:
As those who travel a harsh and long road, being wearied by that labor, if anywhere they find a leafy and broad-spreading tree making a great shade, sit down a little and rest, and being as it were refreshed from rest, finish the remainder of the journey: so now also in this time of the fast, on this arduous and laborious road, in this solemn course, the Life-bearing Cross hath been planted and set in the midst by the Holy Fathers, to grant us some relief and breathing space, or rather strength, and to equip those wearied for further labor with steadfastness and lightness. Or as is customary at the time of the arrival of a King, his coats of arms and scepters are carried before him, and then after them he himself arrives, rejoicing and triumphing over victory, and gladness rejoices together with all: so also our Lord Jesus Christ, desiring to show forth so great a triumph from the victory over death, and to go forth with glory on the day of His Resurrection from the dead, sent beforehand His Scepter, the Royal Sign, the Life-creating Cross, filling us with great joy and strengthening, and preparing us to be ready to receive and praise the King Himself Who comes after it, Who is to triumph gloriously. And that the Precious Cross is set forth in the middle week of the Holy Forty Days is also because the Holy Forty-Day Fast is like the spring at Marah (cf. Exod. 15:23–25),[^1395] by reason of the contrition, bitterness, and hardship that is found in us from the fast. As therefore in the midst of that spring Divine Moses placed a tree, and made it sweet: so also God, leading us through the noetic Red Sea, and delivering us from the invisible Pharaoh, by the Life-giving Tree of the Precious and Life-creating Cross sweetens the bitterness that proceeds from the Forty-Day Fast, and reminding us and granting us consolation, as if having watered those who dwell there, which is to lead us by His Resurrection from the dead even unto the noetic Jerusalem. Or since the Cross is called the Tree of Life, and that Tree of Life was planted in the midst of the Garden of Eden (Gen. 2:9):[^1396] fittingly and appropriately have the Most Divine Fathers planted the Tree of the Cross in the midst of the Holy Forty Days, both that they might bring to our remembrance the place of Adam's brightness, and that through this present tree they might depict for us the blotting out and fall of that former one; for tasting of this Tree of the Cross, we do not die from that time forth, but shall be alive. By its power, O Christ God, preserve us also from the malice of temptation and assaults, and make us worthy to render worship unto Thy Divine Sufferings and Life-bearing Resurrection from the dead; and vouchsafe to grant strength unto the joyous completion of the Holy Forty-Day Fast, and have mercy on us, as the only good and man-loving God, unto Whom belong honor, glory, and dominion, now and always, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

*Ode 7. Heirmos: "The Children from the furnace" (О҆тро́ки ѿ пе́щи):*[^1397]
*Troparion:* Thou hast arisen from the tomb on the third day, as a sleeping Lord, trampling down the gatekeepers of Hades by Divine power; and Thou didst raise up the forefather of old: O God of our fathers, Who alone art blessed and supremely glorified!

*Troparion:* Dancing with choirs of songs, let us, O people, rejoice today in the veneration of the Cross, glorifying Christ Who was nailed thereon: the only God of our fathers, Who is blessed and supremely glorified!

*Troparion:* O Thou Who didst reveal the instrument of mortification as the fashioner of life, Thy Cross, desirable for the world to embrace, O All-compassionate One: sanctify them that bow down in worship before it, O God of our fathers, Who alone art blessed and supremely glorified!

*Troparion:* O Thou Who alone art merciful and compassionate, O Jesus Who alone art holy: enlighten and sanctify them that faithfully bow down in worship before Thy Cross, and by Thy Divine Passion, O God of our fathers, Who alone art blessed and supremely glorified!

*Glory: Triadikon:* I hymn the Monad in three Persons, the Godhead: for the Father is Light, the Son is Light, the Spirit is Light, the Light remaining undivided in unity of essence, yet shining forth with the three rays of the Persons!

*Now and ever: Theotokion:* Thou art the multi-titled proclamation of all the Prophets: for thou hast appeared as the Gate of God, the Golden Urn,[^1398] the Holy Land, O unwedded Virgin, having given birth in the flesh unto Jesus Christ: the God of our fathers, Who is and is supremely glorified!

*Katavasia:* He Who delivered the Children from the flame, having taken flesh, came upon the earth, and was nailed upon the Cross, and granted salvation unto us: the only God of our fathers, Who is blessed and supremely glorified![^1399]

*Ode 8. Heirmos: "This is the chosen and holy day" (Се́й ᲂу҆́бѡ нарочи́тый и҆ ст҃ы́й):*[^1400]
*Troparion:* "Why hold ye myrrh in your hands, O blessed women? Whom seek ye?" cried the young man who now appeared in the tomb: "Christ our God is risen, Who hath raised up the nature of mankind from the treasure-vaults of Hades!" (cf. Mark 16:5–6).

*Troparion:* Rejoice manifestly, O thrice-blessed and Divine Tree, O Cross, light unto them that are in darkness, illuminating the four corners of the world with thy radiance, revealing the dawn of the Resurrection of Christ: vouchsafe all the faithful to attain unto Pascha!

*Troparion:* On this day the Divine repositories of myrrh pour forth fragrance, the life-anointed Tree, the Cross of Christ! Let us breathe in its God-inspired aromas, faithfully bowing down in worship before it unto the ages!

*Troparion:* Come, O Prophet Elisha, and tell us plainly: what is that wood which thou didst cast into the water? It is the Cross of Christ, whereby we have been drawn up from the depths of corruption (cf. 4 Kings 6:5–7 LXX [2 Kings 6:5–7]);[^1401] faithfully bowing down in worship before it unto the ages!

*Troparion:* Of old Jacob, prefiguring Thy Cross, O Christ, bowed down in worship unto the top of Joseph's divine staff (Gen. 47:31 LXX; Heb. 11:21),[^1402] foreseeing the awesome scepter of Thy Kingdom, before which we now faithfully bow down in worship unto the ages!

*Let us bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, the Lord.*
*Triadikon:* I glorify one Essence in three Persons without change, threefold in single form; nor do I sever the Persons of the Father, the Son, with the Spirit: for He is one God over all unto the ages!

*Now and ever: Theotokion:* Alone among mothers hast thou appeared as a Virgin, O Bride of God, Mary, having given birth without a husband unto Christ the Savior, preserving the sign of purity: we the faithful bless thee unto the ages!

*Katavasia:* The great among the Prophets, Daniel, casting forth his hands in the form of a cross within the lions' den of old, was saved unhurt from being devoured by them, blessing Christ unto the ages![^1403]

*Ode 9. Heirmos: "Shine, shine, O New Jerusalem" (Свѣти́ся, свѣти́ся, но́вый І҆ерꙋсали́ме):*[^1404]
*Troparion:* Thou didst descend into the tomb, O Giver of life and God, and didst shatter all the bars and bolts, and didst raise up the dead, who cry aloud: "Glory to Thy Resurrection, O Christ Savior Almighty!"

*Troparion:* Thy tomb hath poured forth life unto me, O Christ: for holding life, Thou didst stand forth and cry aloud unto them that dwell in the tombs: "Ye that are in bonds, be loosed, for I have come as redemption unto the world!"

*Troparion:* Let all the trees of the forest leap for joy with songs (Ps. 95:12 LXX), beholding the namesake Tree of the Cross embraced today, whereby Christ hath exalted the horn, even as Divine David prophesies (Ps. 148:14 LXX)![^1405]

*Troparion:* Having died by the tree, through the Tree of life I have found thee, my Christ-bearing Cross, my indestructible guardian, mighty dominion against demons! As I bow down in worship before thee today, I cry aloud: Sanctify me, O most holy one, by thy glory!

*Troparion:* Be glad and rejoice, O Church of God, bowing down in worship today before the most rich Tree, the most holy Cross of Christ, which the Angelic ranks serve and before which they stand with fear!

*Glory: Triadikon:* Three Persons, a Monad in essence, I worship Thee, the Holy Godhead: the Father, and the Son, with the Holy Spirit: one Beginning, one Kingdom, holding dominion over all!

*Now and ever: Theotokion:* A high mountain wherein Christ dwelt hast thou appeared, O Virgin, even as Divine David cries aloud (Ps. 67:16–17 LXX);[^1406] through whom we have been lifted up unto heaven, adopted as sons by the Spirit, O all-blessed one!

*Katavasia:* O Virgin Mother Theotokos, who without deceit didst bear Christ our God, Who was lifted up upon the Cross in the flesh: with Him we all, the faithful, now worthily magnify thee![^1407]

*Exapostilarion: Resurrectional.*
*Glory: of the Cross. Tone 3, Podoben: "Having adorned heaven with stars" (Не́бо ѕвѣзда́ми):*
Beholding the Precious Cross of Christ set forth today, let us bow down in worship before it, and faithfully rejoice, embracing it with love, beseeching the Lord Who was willingly crucified thereon, that we all may be vouchsafed both to worship the Precious Cross and to attain uncondemned unto the Resurrection!

*Now and ever: Theotokion:*
Unto the Tree whereon Thy Son stretched forth His Most Pure hands for us, being nailed thereon, O All-immaculate One: grant peace unto us who now piously bow down in worship before it, and grant us to anticipate the saving and all-honored Passion, and to bow down in worship before the light-bearing, world-rejoicing, Lord-named Pascha, and before that radiant day!

*At the Praises: "Let everything that hath breath." Stichera: Resurrectional, 4; and of the Cross, 4. Tone 4, Podoben: "As one valiant among martyrs" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*
With voices let us shout aloud, in songs let us sing praises, embracing the Precious Cross, and unto it let us cry aloud: O all-honored Cross, sanctify our souls and bodies by thy power, and preserve unhurt from every harm of the adversary them that piously bow down in worship before thee!

*Sticheron:* Drawing near, draw ye inexhaustible waters, poured forth by the grace of the Cross (Isa. 12:3);[^1408] beholding the Holy Tree lying before us, the fountain of gifts, watered by the Blood and water of the Master of all (John 19:34), Who was willingly lifted up thereon and hath raised up the earthly!

*Verse: Exalt ye the Lord our God, and worship the footstool of His feet, for He is holy (Ps. 98:5 LXX):*[^1409]
*Sticheron:* The confirmation of the Church, the dominion of kings, the boast and salvation of monastics art thou, O all-honored Cross! Therefore, bowing down in worship before thee, we are illuminated in heart and soul today by the Divine grace of Him Who was nailed upon thee, Who shattered the dominion of the deceiver and blotted out the curse!

*Verse: For God is our King of old, He hath wrought salvation in the midst of the earth (Ps. 73:12 LXX):*[^1410]
*Repeat the first Sticheron: "With voices let us shout aloud..."*

*Then: Tone 8, Idiomelon:*
*Verse: Arise, O Lord my God, let Thy hand be lifted up; forget not Thy poor (Ps. 9:33 LXX):*[^1411]
The Lord of all taught us by a parable to flee the haughty mind of the wicked Pharisees, and instructed all not to think more highly than one ought to think (Rom. 12:3), having Himself become an image and pattern, even unto Crucifixion and death, having emptied Himself (Phil. 2:7–8).[^1412] Giving thanks, therefore, with the Publican let us say: O God Who didst suffer for us and didst remain impassible, deliver us from passions, and save our souls!

*Glory: the same Sticheron.*
*Now and ever: "Most blessed art thou, O Virgin Theotokos." Great Doxology.*

*And when we begin to sing: "Glory to God in the highest": then the Priest comes, vested in all the priestly vestments. [Or if there be a senior priest anywhere, it is proper for this to be performed by the foremost in both of their places.] And taking the censer, he censes the Holy Table and the Precious Cross; then he takes it upon the Diskos with its case upon his head, and goes out from the left side of the altar through the north door, two candles and censers preceding him, and goes as far as the church doors.*

*And when the Doxology and the Trisagion are completed, the Priest says (if there be no Deacon):*
**Priest:** Wisdom! Stand upright!
*And he begins the Troparion: "Save, O Lord, Thy people," thrice (see fol. 506).[^1413]*

*And the Priest comes bearing the Precious Cross before the Holy Doors, and places it upon the Tetrapod prepared there [margin: *four-legged table*],[^1414] and the Precious Cross is set upon it. And opening the case, he censes the Cross in the form of a cross on four sides.*

*And immediately we sing the Troparion, Tone 2:*
**Choir:** Before Thy Cross we bow down in worship, O Master, and Thy Holy Resurrection we glorify! *Thrice.*

*And they begin to bow down in worship: if anywhere in a monastery there happens to be an Igumen, or another presiding among the clergy, likewise also the other priests, bowing down before the Precious Cross thrice. The senior venerates first, and after kissing it they bow down once again. In like manner the other priests do together, right side and left. In like manner also the brethren come, two by two, bowing down according to their rank. And while the brethren are bowing down in worship,*

*We sing the Stichera of the Cross, Idiomela, Tone 2:*
Come, ye faithful, let us bow down in worship before the Life-creating Tree, whereon Christ the King of glory, having willingly stretched forth His hands, lifted us up unto the first blessedness, whom the enemy of old stole away by deceit and made us outcasts from God! Come, ye faithful, let us bow down in worship before the Tree whereby we have been vouchsafed to crush the heads of invisible enemies! Come, all ye families of the nations, let us honor the Cross of the Lord with songs! Rejoice, O Cross, the perfect redemption of fallen Adam! For in thee our most faithful rulers boast, since by thy power the Ishmaelite people are mightily subdued! Thee now with fear we Christians kiss, and we glorify God Who was nailed upon thee, saying: O Lord Who wast nailed thereon, have mercy on us, as Thou art good and the Lover of mankind!

*Tone 2:*
Today the Master of creation and Lord of glory is nailed upon the Cross and pierced in His side; gall and vinegar does the Sweetness of the Church taste (Matt. 27:34, 48); with a crown of thorns is He enveloped Who covers the heavens with clouds; with a purple robe of mockery is He arrayed (Matt. 27:28–29); and He is buffeted by an earthly hand, Who with His hand fashioned man; upon His back is He beaten, Who clothes the heaven with clouds; spitting and wounds does He receive, and mockeries and reproaches: and all things does my Redeemer and God endure for my sake, the condemned, that He may save the world from deception, as He is compassionate!

*Glory: Tone 8:*
Today He Who is untouchable in Essence becomes touchable unto me, and endures passions, delivering me from passions; He Who gives light unto the blind is spat upon by lawless lips, and gives His back to wounds for the captives (Isa. 50:6).[^1415] Beholding Him upon the Cross, the pure Virgin and Mother cried out in anguish: "Woe is me, my Child, what is this that Thou hast done? Thou Who art fairer in beauty than all the sons of men (Ps. 44:3 LXX), Thou appearest without breath and without form, having neither sightliness nor beauty (Isa. 53:2 LXX)![^1416] Woe is me, my Light! I cannot bear to behold Thee breathless; I am wounded in my inward parts, and a cruel sword pierces my heart (Luke 2:35)![^1417] I hymn Thy Passion, I bow down before Thy compassion: O Long-suffering One, glory to Thee!"

*Now and ever: The same Tone.*

Today the prophetic word is fulfilled: for behold, we bow down in worship in the place where Thy feet stood, O Lord (Ps. 131:7 LXX);[^1418] and having tasted of the Tree of salvation, we have obtained freedom from sinful passions, through the intercessions of the Theotokos, O Thou only Lover of mankind!

*Then the Litanies, and the Dismissal. Gospel Sticheron in the Narthex, and the First Hour, and complete Dismissal.*

*At the Liturgy: The Beatitudes of the Tone on 6; and from the Canon of the Cross, Ode 3, on 4. After the Entrance: Resurrectional Troparion, and of the Cross; Glory, and now and ever: Kontakion of the Cross. But instead of the Trisagion, we sing: "Before Thy Cross we bow down in worship, O Master." Prokeimenon, Tone 6: "Save, O Lord, Thy people, and bless Thine inheritance." Verse: "Unto Thee, O Lord, will I cry." The Epistle: to the Hebrews, Pericope 311 (Heb. 4:14–5:6): "Brethren: Having a Great High Priest." Alleluia, Tone 8: "Remember Thy congregation." Verse: "For God is our King of old." The Gospel: from Mark, Pericope 37 (Mark 8:34–9:1): "The Lord said: Whosoever will come after Me." Communion Verse: "The light of Thy countenance hath been signed upon us, O Lord" (Ps. 4:7 LXX). Concerning the Trapeza: see fol. 323.[^1419]*

## On the Same Third Sunday of the Holy Fast, at Vespers

*At "Lord, I have cried": Stichera from the Oktoechos as indicated (see fol. 353);[^1420] and from the Triodion, 3. Tone 2. By Kyr Joseph. Podoben: "O Lord, though Thou didst stand before the tribunal" (Гдⷭ҇и, а҆́ще и҆ на сꙋди́щи):*
O Lord, Who didst willingly stretch forth Thy hands upon the Cross: vouchsafe us also to bow down in worship before it with compunction of heart, enlightened manifestly by fasting, and prayers, and abstinence, and good deeds, as Thou art compassionate and the Lover of mankind!

*Sticheron:* O Lord, cleanse the multitude of my sins according to the multitude of Thy compassions, O All-merciful One; and vouchsafe me with a pure soul to behold and kiss Thy Cross in the present week of abstinence, as Thou art the Lover of mankind!

*Another Sticheron. Tone 3. By Kyr Theodore, Podoben: "A great wonder" (Ве́лїе чꙋ́до):*
A great wonder is the Tree seen to be, whereon Christ was willingly crucified in the flesh! The world bows down in worship, and being enlightened cries aloud: "O power of the Cross! Even seen, it consumes demons; and depicted, it is revealed consuming them! I bless thee, O all-honored Tree, honoring and bowing down in worship before thee with fear; and I glorify God, Who through thee hath granted me endless life!"

*From the Menaion: 3. Glory, and now and ever: Theotokion. Entrance. "O Gladsome Light." Great Prokeimenon: "Thou hast given an inheritance" (Ps. 60:6 LXX), with its verses (seek on the First Sunday of Lent, see fol. 353).[^1421] Then: "Vouchsafe, O Lord." And the Great Prostrations.*

*At the Aposticha: Idiomelon Sticheron, Tone 8:*
I dare not lift up mine eyes unto heaven, wretch that I am, because of my wicked deeds! But like the Publican groaning, I cry aloud unto Thee: O God, cleanse me a sinner, and deliver me from the hypocrisy of the Pharisees, as Thou alone art compassionate! *Twice.*

*Verse 1: Unto Thee have I lifted up mine eyes, O Thou that dwellest in heaven (Ps. 122:1 LXX):*
*Verse 2: Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us (Ps. 122:3 LXX):*
*Martyrikon:*
Martyrs of the Lord, ye sanctify every place, and heal every infirmity; and now pray ye, we beseech you, that our souls may be delivered from the snares of the enemy!

*Glory, and now and ever: Theotokion:*
Taking up the voice of the Archangel Gabriel, let us say: "Rejoice, O Mother Virgin, who didst bear Christ the Giver of life unto the world!"

*(Markian Chapter 74):[^1422] If the Annunciation of the Most Holy Theotokos falls on Monday [of the 4th, 5th, or 6th week of Great Lent]:*
*On Sunday evening, at Great Vespers: "Blessed is the man": 1st Stasis (Slava). At "Lord, I have cried": Stichera on 10: in the Triodion, prosomoia, 3; and of the Feast, 7: "The eternal counsel." Glory, and now and ever: "Gabriel was sent." Entrance. Great Prokeimenon of the day. Old Testament Readings of the Feast: 3. At the Aposticha: Idiomelon of the day, twice; and Martyrikon. Glory, and now and ever: of the Feast, Tone 1: "In the sixth month." Troparion of the Feast. Then the Litany: "Have mercy on us, O God," and 3 great prostrations. We sing: "More honorable than the Cherubim." Glory, and now and ever, and Dismissal.*
*And at the 4th hour of the night, we sing Great Compline. In like manner also Matins, and all the rest of the service according to the Lenten rubrics; see fol. 474,[^1423] Chapter 74.*

## On Monday of the Fourth Week of the Holy Fast

*At Matins, after the Six Psalms, Alleluia in the Tone of the Oktoechos; then the Trinity Hymns. After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymns in the Oktoechos. After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 8. By Kyr Joseph. Podoben: "Thou art risen from the tomb" (Воскре́слъ є҆сѝ):*[^1424]
*Sessional Hymn:* Let us the faithful bow down in worship before the all-honored Tree whereon the Creator of all was lifted up! It lies before us, sanctifying those who draw near with soul and body, and cleansing the defilement of sin from those who fast faithfully and ever hymn Christ, the only Benefactor!

*Glory: the same. Both now: Theotokion:*
The Word of the Father descended upon the earth, and the radiant Angel cried aloud unto the Theotokos: "Rejoice, O blessed one, who alone hast preserved the bridal chamber, having received the conception of the pre-eternal God and Lord, that as God He may save the human race from deception!"

*After the 3rd Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 3, Podoben: "Beholding the beauty of thy virginity" (Красотѣ̀ дѣ́вства):*[^1425]
*Sessional Hymn:* Having reached the midpoint of abstinence today, and having anticipated the veneration of Thy life-bearing Cross, O Christ, falling down before Thee we cry aloud: Great art Thou, O Lover of mankind, and great are Thy works, for Thou hast revealed Thy Holy Cross, before which we bow down in worship with fear, crying aloud: Glory, O Christ, to Thine extreme tender-heartedness!

*Glory, both now: Theotokion:*
