As an uncultivated vineyard, O Virgin, thou hast budded forth the most beautiful cluster, pouring forth unto us the wine of salvation, gladdening the souls and bodies of all! Therefore, blessing thee as the cause of good things, we ever cry aloud unto thee with the Angel: Rejoice, thou who art full of grace!

*Triodion [Triōdion], by Kyr Joseph. Tone 8. Ode 1. Heirmos: "The armored Pharaoh" (Вѡрꙋже́нна Фараѡ́на):*[^1426]
*Troparion:* The radiant veneration of the Cross hath appeared unto all, sending forth the sunlike dawn of salvation, illuminating all who are held fast by the darkening of passions, as we hasten purely to embrace it!

*Troparion:* Cleansed by the grace of the fast, with a pure mind let us come and cry aloud unto the only Pure One with a voice of thanksgiving: Thou, O Word, hast poured forth Thy Blood for our sake, and by Thy Cross Thou cleansest us!

*Troparion:* Tripped up by the assaults of the serpent, I ever lie in a terrible fall! O Savior, Who by Thy Passion and Cross didst restore the fall of the first-created, restore me and guide me unto the fulfillment of Thy desires!

*Theotokion [Stavrotheotokion]:* Standing before Thy Cross, O Lord, she that knew not wedlock, beholding Thy wounds, O Master, wounded in soul, cried aloud: "Woe is me, my Child! Having escaped pangs in Thy birth-giving, now I am grievously wounded!"

*Another Canon, by Kyr Theodore. Tone 3. Heirmos: "Let us sing unto the Lord" (Пои́мъ Гдⷭ҇еви):*[^1427]
*Troparion:* This holy and light-bearing week sets forth the all-honored Cross before the world! Come, let us bow down in worship, having enlightened our souls with fear and love, glorifying in songs Christ Who was nailed thereon!

*Troparion:* Before Thy Cross we all bow down in worship, O Christ, celebrating the passage unto Thy Resurrection; we sing praises unto Thy Nails, and we revere Thy Spear, with lips and eyes, being cleansed by them in soul and body!

*Glory: Triadikon:*
O Trinity, praised as one Essence in Unity,...

...Father, and Son, with the Holy Spirit: unoriginate, co-eternal,[^1428] uncreated Godhead, Wellspring of light and life, before Thee all we of the earth bow down in worship, unceasingly magnifying Thee!

*Both now: Theotokion:*
We hymn thee, O Virgin pure Theotokos, chariot of the Cherubim, from whom God was born! For thou alone hast been a fountain of incorruption, pouring forth life unto all, drawing from which we receive healing!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*
*Troparion:* Reaching the midpoint of the forty-day stadium of the fast, come, with love let us go with Christ unto the Divine Passion, that being crucified together with Him, we may become partakers of His Resurrection!

*Katavasia: Heirmos:*
Let us sing unto the Lord Who wrought marvelous wonders in the Red Sea: for He covered the adversaries with the deep, and saved Israel (Exod. 14:28–30; 15:1); unto Him alone let us sing, for He hath been glorified!

*Ode 8. Heirmos: "Sevenfold the furnace" (Седмь седми́цею):*[^1429]
*Troparion:* Having my soul and mind wounded by poisonous passions, O Lord, have mercy, show compassion, protect me by Thy Cross, and heal me with the drops poured forth from Thy ribs (John 19:34), that I may fervently sing: "Ye Priests, bless; ye people, hymn and supremely exalt Him unto the ages!"

*Troparion:* Bent down by passions, taken captive by enemies, dragged away by evil custom: show compassion, O Merciful One, protect me with Thy Cross, that with an unwavering heart I may sing: "Ye Children, bless; ye Priests, hymn and supremely exalt Him!"

*Troparion:* Of old on the mountain Moses prefigured thee, O all-honored Cross, lifting up his hands and conquering Amalek (Exod. 17:11–12);[^1430] bowing down before which today, we conquer demonic legions and sing in faith: "Ye Priests, bless!"

*Both now: Theotokion [Stavrotheotokion]:*

...Groaning in anguish, crying out mother-like, and unable to endure the maternal yearning of thine inner parts, thou didst look upon the Cross at Him Who was born of thy womb, crying aloud: "Child, what sight is this! How sufferest Thou, Who art impassible by nature, desiring by all means to deliver the human race from corruption?"

*Another Heirmos [Tone 3, Ode 8]: "Unceasingly by Angels" (А҆́гг҃лы немо́лчнѡ):*[^1431]
*Troparion:* Beholding the Cross of Christ set forth in the church, with fear and faith, brethren, drawing near let us bow down in worship, crying aloud unto it: "Thou hast blossomed forth life unto men, O radiant one!"

*Troparion:* Victorious in battles, heaven hath revealed thee as life-creating unto us, O Cross, an invincible weapon for sovereigns, casting down of enemies, horn of the Church, and salvation for the faithful!

*Let us bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, the Lord.*
*Triadikon:* I glorify the Holy Father, and I revere the Holy Son, and I hymn the Holy Spirit: the consubstantial,[^1432] simple Trinity, each of Them God, lights and Light, proceeding as from a single sun!

*Both now: Theotokion:*
Rejoice, O impassable Gate (Ezek. 44:2); rejoice, O unburnt Bush (Exod. 3:2); rejoice, O Golden Urn (Heb. 9:4); rejoice, O Unquarried Mountain (Dan. 2:34, 45);[^1433] rejoice, O Theotokos, indestructible hope and rampart of them that put their trust in thee!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*
*Troparion:* Having reached the midpoint of the fast, let us take courage in spirit for what is to come with youthful vigor, running well with God, brethren, that we may joyfully behold also the Pascha of Christ, Who is risen!

*We praise, we bless, and we worship the Lord.*
*Katavasia: Heirmos:*
God, Who is unceasingly glorified on high by the Angels: ye heavens of heavens, earth and mountains, and hills, and the abyss, and all the human race, with hymns bless, sing praises, and supremely exalt Him as Creator and Deliverer unto the ages!

*Ode 9. Heirmos: "Heaven was astonished" (ᲊ҆страши́сѧ):*[^1434]
*Troparion:* Blessing his grandchildren of old, Jacob clearly prefigured the Precious Cross (Gen. 48:13–14);[^1435] whereby having shown compassion, bless us, granting sanctifying grace unto them that bow down in worship before it, and who glorify Thee as the Deliverer of all!

*Troparion:* Cleansed by the water of fasting in both soul and mind, ye faithful, let us embrace the Life-giving and Divine Tree! For it manifestly lies before all, pouring forth Divine forgiveness, and heavenly light, and life, and true rejoicing!

*Troparion:* I know of the awesome judgment seat coming in the glory of God, when Thou, O Lord, art about to expose the hidden secrets of all! Therefore I cry aloud unto Thee, O Good One: Forgive me who have sinned, and expose not my many and grievous transgressions!

*Theotokion [Stavrotheotokion]:* The Ewe-lamb of old, beholding the Lamb nailed upon the Cross, and the sun's radiance darkened, weeping cried aloud: "O never-setting Sun, my Son, Thou settest, being put to death! But shine forth the light of the Resurrection unto them that love Thee!"

*Another Heirmos [Tone 3, Ode 9]: "On Mount Sinai" (На Сїна́итѣй горѣ̀):*[^1436]
*Troparion:* In the place where Thy feet stood, O Master and God (Ps. 131:7 LXX),[^1437] let us all bow down in worship today before the all-honored Cross, even as David the most God-inspired cries aloud: for He Who holds all things in His palm was lifted up thereon!

*Troparion:* Ye that dwell upon earth, draw near with pure fasting, and beholding the all-honored Cross lying before you, bow down in worship with fear, rejoice in faith, and draw sanctification for your souls with joy!

*Glory: Triadikon:*
A simple, indivisible Monad in essence is the all-divine Trinity,...

...Trinity united in essence, yet divided properly in Persons: undivided yet severed, consubstantial yet revered in Trinity; This is Father, and Son, and the Living Spirit, Who preserve all things!

*Both now: Theotokion:*
"Who hath ever heard of a virgin bearing a Child, and a Mother without a husband? Mary, thou workest a wonder! But tell me, how?" "Inquire not into the depths of my God-bearing; for this is truly beyond the comprehension of the human mind!"

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*
*Troparion:* Let all of us people offer a hymn of thanksgiving unto God, as beholding now the Precious Cross, we embrace it! Understand therefore and submit yourselves, all ye nations;[^1438] understand, ye barbarian nations, and submit yourselves, for on account of Him God is with us (Isa. 8:9–10 LXX)!

*Katavasia: Heirmos:*
Moses, having seen thee on Mount Sinai in the bush, receiving unburnt the Fire of the Godhead in thy womb; and Daniel saw thee as the Unquarried Mountain; and Isaiah cried aloud: "A Rod budded forth from the root of David!"[^1439]

*Exapostilarion in the Oktoechos.*

*At the Aposticha: Stichera Idiomela, Tone 6:*
As an exalted path of exaltation, O Christ, Thou hast shown humility, having emptied Thyself and taken the form of a servant (Phil. 2:7);[^1440] not giving ear unto the boastful prayers of the Pharisee, but receiving on high the contrite groaning of the Publican as a spotless sacrifice (Luke 18:10–14)! Therefore unto us also who cry aloud: "Cleanse me, O God, cleanse me! O my Savior, save me!"

*Verse: We were filled in the morning with Thy mercy, O Lord, and we rejoiced and were glad (Ps. 89:14 LXX):*
*And: And let the brightness of the Lord our God be upon us (Ps. 89:17 LXX):*
*Martyrikon:*
O Lord, at the memory of Thy Saints all creation keeps feast: the heavens rejoice with the Angels, and the earth makes glad with men! By their prayers, have mercy on us!

*Glory, both now: Theotokion:*
Thou hast received the Archangel's word, and hast appeared as the Cherubic Throne,...

...thou hast appeared, and in thine arms thou hast borne, O Theotokos, the Hope of our souls!

*Then: "It is good to give thanks unto the Lord" (Ps. 91:2 LXX). Trisagion through "Our Father." Troparion of the Day; Litanies, and Three Great Prostrations. First Hour, and complete Dismissal.*

*At the First Hour, we perform the veneration of the Precious Cross, even as on Sunday, according to the prescribed pattern: singing instead of "Order my steps": "Before Thy Cross we bow down in worship, O Master" (see fol. 506).[^1441] In like manner also on Wednesday and Friday, these four days. And on Friday we take back the Cross, even as it shall be set forth there (see fol. 562).[^1442]*

*On Monday of the Fourth Week of Lent, at the Sixth Hour. Troparion of the Prophecy, Tone 7:*
O Lord, rebuke not in Thine anger the people who have sinned, nor punish us in Thy wrath (Ps. 6:2 LXX),[^1443] for Thou art good; for all the earth glorifies Thee, and we pray Thee: Spare us, O Holy One!

*Glory... the end: "and we pray Thee: Spare us, O Holy One!" Both now... the whole troparion.*

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 61, Tone 6: In God is my salvation and my glory (Ps. 61:8 LXX):*
*Verse: Shall not my soul be subjected unto God? For from Him is my salvation (Ps. 61:2 LXX):*

*Reading from the Prophecy of Isaiah (Isa. 14:24–32):*
Thus says the Lord of hosts: As I have spoken, so shall it be; and as I have purposed, so shall it stand: to destroy the Assyrians upon My land, and upon My mountains; and they shall be trodden under foot, and their yoke shall be taken away from them, and their dominion shall be wiped away from their shoulders. This is the purpose which the Lord hath purposed against the whole world; and this is the hand that is lifted high over all the nations. For what the Holy God hath purposed, who shall bring to naught? And His hand that is lifted high, who shall turn it away? In the year that King Ahaz died, this word came to pass: Rejoice not, all ye strangers, because ...the yoke of him that smote you is broken! For out of the serpent's seed shall come forth the offspring of asps, and their offspring shall be flying serpents. And the poor shall be pastured by Him, and needy men shall rest in peace; but He shall destroy thy seed with famine, and shall slay thy remnant. Wail, ye gates of cities! Let troubled cities cry aloud, all ye strangers! For smoke comes from the north, and there is no standing. And what shall the kings of the nations answer? That the Lord hath founded Zion, and through Him the humble of His people shall be saved!

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 62, Tone 6: Thus will I bless Thee while I live (Ps. 62:5 LXX):*
*Verse: O God, my God, at early dawn I seek Thee (Ps. 62:2 LXX):*

## On the Same Monday Evening, at "Lord, I Have Cried"

*Stichera, Tone 8, Podoben: "What shall we call you, O holy ones" (Что́ ва́съ нарече́мъ):*[^1444]
*Sticheron:* Passing today through the middle days of abstinence, by the power of the Cross we give glory unto the Savior and God Who was lifted up thereon in the midst of all the earth (Ps. 73:12 LXX),[^1445] crying aloud: Reveal us as beholders of Thy Passion, O Master, and of Thy Precious Resurrection, granting us cleansing and great mercy!

*Sticheron:* Let us subdue the carnal passions by setting aside meats and turning away from pleasures, and let us faithfully embrace the Tree of the Cross; for it is manifestly seen being worshipped, sanctifying all by Divine grace; and unto the Lord let us cry aloud: We thank Thee, O Master, Who by it savest our souls!

*Another Sticheron, Tone 8, Podoben: "The Mother of God" (Бг҃оро́дицꙋ):*[^1446]
*Sticheron:* Now bowing down in worship before the Cross, let us all cry aloud: Rejoice, O Tree of life! Rejoice, O holy scepter of Christ! Rejoice,...

...O heavenly glory of earthly men! Rejoice, O boast of sovereigns! Rejoice, O dominion of the faith! Rejoice, O invincible weapon! Rejoice, O banishment of enemies! Rejoice, O radiant illumination, salvation of the world! Rejoice, O great glory of Martyrs! Rejoice, O confirmation of the Venerable! Rejoice, O brightness of Angels! Rejoice, O all-honored one!

*And from the Menaion, 3 stichera. Glory, both now: Theotokion. Entrance. "O Gladsome Light."*

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 63, Tone 6: Hear, O God, my prayer, when I make supplication unto Thee (Ps. 63:2 LXX):*
*Verse: Deliver my soul from fear of the enemy (Ps. 63:2b LXX):*

*Reading from the Book of Genesis (Gen. 8:21–9:4):*
God said: I have considered in My heart, and I will not again curse the earth because of the works of men, for the imagination of man is inclined toward evil from youth; neither will I again smite all living flesh, as I have done. While all the days of the earth remain, seed-time and harvest, cold and heat, summer and spring, day and night, shall not cease. And God blessed Noah and his sons, and said unto them: Increase and multiply, and fill the earth, and have dominion over it. And the dread and fear of you shall be upon all the beasts of the earth, and upon all the birds of the heaven, and upon all that move upon the earth, and upon all the fishes of the sea; under your hands have I delivered them. And every creeping thing which is alive shall be meat for you; even as the green herb have I given you all things. But flesh with the life thereof, which is the blood thereof, shall ye not eat.

...For surely your blood, the life of your souls, will I require at the hand of all beasts; and from the hand of man, of a brother, will I require it. Whoever sheds man's blood, in place of his blood shall his blood be shed; for in the image of God have I made man. But as for you, increase and multiply, and fill the earth, and have dominion over it!

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 64, Tone 6: Hear us, O God our Savior, the hope of all the ends of the earth (Ps. 64:6 LXX):*
*Verse: Unto Thee, O God, praise is meet in Zion, and unto Thee shall a vow be performed in Jerusalem (Ps. 64:2 LXX):*

*Reading from the Proverbs (Prov. 11:19–28):*[^1447]
A righteous son is born unto life; but the pursuit of the ungodly is unto death. Crooked ways are an abomination before the Lord; but all that are blameless in their way are acceptable unto Him. He that lays hands unjustly hand to hand shall not go unpunished; but he that sows righteousness shall receive a faithful reward. As an earring of gold in the snout of a swine, so is beauty unto an evil-minded woman. All the desire of the righteous is good; but the hope of the ungodly shall perish. There are some who, while scattering their own, make it more; and there are some who, while gathering what is another's, suffer lack. Every simple soul is a blessed soul; but a wrathful man is unsightly. He that hoards grain, let him leave it also unto the nations; he that sells grain greedily is cursed of the people; but blessing is upon the head of him that gives. He that does good seeks good favor; but as for him that seeks evil, it shall overtake him. He that trusts in his riches, the same shall fall; but he that upholds the righteous, the same shall arise.

...He that troubles not his own house shall inherit the wind; and the fool shall be servant to the wise (Prov. 11:29 LXX). From the fruit of righteousness grows a tree of life; but the souls of the lawless are taken away untimely (Prov. 11:30 LXX). If the righteous scarcely be saved, where shall the ungodly and the sinner appear (Prov. 11:31 LXX; 1 Pet. 4:18)?[^1448]

Chapter 12: He that loves instruction loves knowledge; but he that hates reproof is a fool (Prov. 12:1 LXX). Better is he that hath found favor from the Lord God; but a lawless man shall be passed over in silence (Prov. 12:2 LXX). A man shall not be established by wickedness; but the roots of the righteous shall not be removed (Prov. 12:3 LXX). A virtuous woman is a crown to her husband; but even as a worm in wood, so does an evildoing woman destroy a husband (Prov. 12:4 LXX). The thoughts of the righteous are judgments; but the ungodly direct deceits (Prov. 12:5 LXX). The words of the ungodly are deceitful unto blood; but the mouth of the upright shall deliver them (Prov. 12:6 LXX).

*Trisagion. "Vouchsafe, O Lord."*

*At the Aposticha, Sticheron Idiomelon, Tone 8:*
*Sticheron:* The boastful Pharisee made himself loathsome by his boasting, and the humble-minded Publican, praying in silence, was justified (Luke 18:10–14).[^1449] Therefore, my soul, seeing the difference between both, receive and embrace humility; for Christ, as the Lover of mankind, hath promised to give grace unto the humble (Jas. 4:6; 1 Pet. 5:5)![^1450]

*Verse: "Unto Thee have I lifted up mine eyes" (Ps. 122:1 LXX): the same Sticheron.*

*Verse 2: "Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us" (Ps. 122:3 LXX). Martyrion, Tone 8:*
*Martyrion:* O Martyrs of the Lord, pray unto our God, and entreat for our souls a multitude of compassions, and cleansing for our many transgressions, we beseech you!

*Glory, both now: Theotokion:*
I flee unto thy protection, O Holy Virgin Theotokos; I know that I shall obtain salvation, for thou, O pure one, art able to help me!

## On Tuesday of Mid-Cross Week

*At Matins, Trinity Hymns in the Tone of the Oktoechos. After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymns in the Oktoechos. After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "The unshakable confirmation" (Непоколѣби́мое ᲂу҆тверже́нїе):*[^1451]
*Sessional Hymn:* Having enlightened our souls by abstinence, let us bow down in worship before the radiant Cross, whereon Christ was nailed, and let us cry aloud unto it: Rejoice, O sweetness of those who fast, and certain help! Rejoice, destroyer of passions, and adversary of demons! Rejoice, O most blessed Tree!

*Glory: the same. Both now: Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* The unshakable confirmation of the faith and honored gift of our souls, the Theotokos do we the faithful magnify in songs: Rejoice, thou who didst contain in thy womb the Stone of life! Rejoice, hope of the ends of the earth, helper of the afflicted! Rejoice, O unwedded Bride!

*After the 3rd Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "As first-fruits of nature" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ нача́тки):*[^1452]
*Sessional Hymn:* Even as the life of creation, the world kisses Thy Cross lying before us, O Lord, and bowing down before it, cries aloud unto Thee: by its working preserve in deep peace, through abstinence, those who hymn and glorify Thee, O Most-merciful One!

*Glory: the same. Both now: Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* Rejoice, thou who through the Angel didst receive joy for the world! Rejoice, thou who didst bear thy Creator and Lord! Rejoice, thou who wast vouchsafed to be the Mother of God!

*Triodion [Triōdion], by Kyr Joseph. Tone 8. Ode 2. Heirmos: "See, see that I am God" (Ви́дите ви́дите, ꙗ҆́кѡ а҆́зъ є҆́смъ Бг҃ъ):*[^1453]
*Heirmos:* See, see that I am God, Who of old led Israel through the Red Sea, and saved and nourished them, and freed them from the bitter bondage of Pharaoh (Exod. 14:21–31)!

*Troparion:* Before the Cross set in the midst of creation, whereon Thou didst suffer, O Messiah, Word of God, on this mid-fast day we bow down in worship with faith, entreating to behold also Thy Resurrection!

*Troparion:* By the rod of power prefigured by Moses (Exod. 14:16), cleaving the sea of passions, let us attain unto the promised land, and richly be filled with the noetic Manna (Exod. 16:14–15)![^1454]

*Troparion:* Who weeps not for thee, who mourns not, O my soul, who desirest evil things and seekest not the good with love, ever despising the righteous Judge Who is long-suffering toward thee?

*Theotokion:* Having become flesh unchangeably, O Virgin, thou bringest forth Christ; Him do thou fervently implore to deliver from carnal passions those who bow down before the Cross whereon He suffered in the flesh!

*Another Canon, by Kyr Theodore. Tone the same [Tone 8]. Heirmos: "See, see that I am God" (Ви́дите ви́дите ꙗ҆́кѡ):*[^1455]
*Troparion:* "See, see that I am God, Who have granted My Cross unto the world, the weapon of salvation, that men may now bow down in worship before it, so that they who kiss it may bring to naught the wiles of the enemy!"

*Troparion:* Great art Thou, O Lord, and Most-merciful, in that Thou hast granted us now to bow down before Thy life-creating Cross, whereon Thy hands and feet were nailed, and whereon the blood was poured forth from Thy pure ribs, welling forth life (John 19:34)!

*Glory: Triadikon:*
*Triadikon:* All-perfect Monad, pre-divine, tri-hypostatic: Unbegotten Father, and only-begotten Son, and Spirit Who proceedest from the Father and art manifested through the Son: one Essence, Nature, Lordship, and Kingdom, save us all!

*Both now: Theotokion:*

...Inconceivable is the marvel of thy birth-giving, O Virgin Mother! For how dost thou bring forth and yet remainest pure? How dost thou bear a Child, knowing not a man at all? "As He Himself knows, beyond nature, the Word of God was newly born of me!"

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*
*Troparion:* The great Moses prefigured thee unto us, O Cross, stretching out his hands and conquering Amalek (Exod. 17:11–12);[^1456] and picturing thee upon the walls and in the air, we turn back and conquer the evil-originating enemy, hymning Christ in song!

*Katavasia: Heirmos:*
*Heirmos:* See, see that I am your God, begotten before the ages without a mother, and born of the Virgin in the last times without a man, Who have loosed the sin of Adam the forefather, as I am the Lover of mankind!

*Ode 8. Heirmos: "He Who covers with waters" (Покрыва́ѧй вода́ми):*[^1457]
*Troparion:* Having shaken the foundations of all the earth when as God Thou wast lifted up upon the Tree, Thou hast granted unto the faithful, O Lord, an immovable confirmation: the saving weapon of Thy Cross; and bowing down in worship before it, we supremely exalt Thee unto all ages!

*Troparion:* Beholding the Tree of the Cross shining more brightly than the dawn of the sun, come, let us who are enlightened by the fast now embrace it, drawing forth the light-bearing grace that drives away darkness and sanctifies the hearts of all the faithful!

*Troparion:* Thou art the living Water drawn unto life eternal, O Word (John 4:14); blood and water hast Thou poured forth from Thy ribs upon the Cross, O Master (John 19:34), drying up the torrents of sin; therefore I pray Thee: dry up the evil outpourings of my passions!

*Theotokion:* As a noetic sanctification, O pure Holy Mother of God, thou bringest forth God Who rests among the saints, Who today sanctifies all the ends of the earth through the divine veneration of the most holy Tree, whereon He was nailed in the flesh, O Virgin!

*Another Heirmos [Tone 8, Ode 8]: "Angels and the heavens" (А҆́гг҃ли и҆ нб҃са̀):*[^1458]
*Troparion:* Come, ye people, let us behold the life-bearing Tree now being worshipped, whereon our God was nailed in the flesh; and singing with fear, let us bow down before it unto all ages!

*Troparion:* The three-part Cross do we hymn as the image of the Trinity,[^1459] and bowing down in worship with fear let us cry aloud, blessing, hymning, and supremely exalting Christ unto the ages!

*We bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, the Lord.*
*Triadikon:* One God indeed is the Trinity: neither the Father passing over into Sonship, nor the Son being changed into procession; but their personal properties and both, as God in Three do I glorify unto the ages!

*Both now: Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* Thou alone incorruptibly bringest forth; thou alone nursest a child without wedlock; thou alone bringest forth thy Creator and Master; even though both Mother and handmaid, thee, O Virgin Mother, do we hymn unto the ages!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*
*Troparion:* Thou Who didst give sight by Thy Word unto him who was blind from birth (John 9:1–7), open again the blinded eyes of my heart, that I may behold the light of Thy commandments, O Christ, unto the ages!

*We praise, we bless, and we bow down in worship before the Lord.*
*Katavasia: Heirmos:*
*Heirmos:* Him Who is borne upon the throne of glory, and unceasingly glorified as God by the Angels and the heavens, bless, hymn, and supremely exalt unto the ages!

*Ode 9. Heirmos: "Blessed be the Lord God" (Бл҃гослове́нъ Гдⷭ҇ь Бг҃ъ):*[^1460]
*Troparion:* Blessed is the Lord God of Israel, Who by His Cross hath destroyed the ancient curse (Gal. 3:13), and hath granted us its dominion, refuge, and firm foundation, whereby with its horns we now gore our enemies (Ps. 43:6 LXX; Deut. 33:17)![^1461]

*Troparion:* As with cords I am bound fast by measureless evils, and Thy saving paths, O Christ, I will not to understand by my own will; do Thou convert me by Thy Cross,...

...loosing my perplexity, according to the ineffable mercy of Thy tender-heartedness!

*Troparion:* Having wickedly likened myself unto the presumption of the Pharisee, I have been cast down by a grievous and painful fall, and I lie as a trampled object for enemies; but show compassion and save me, O Christ, O most high King of glory, Who for the sake of tender-heartedness didst humble Thyself (Phil. 2:7–8)![^1462]

*Theotokion:* All generations call thee blessed, O pure one (Luke 1:48); for Jesus alone, born of thy womb, as He Himself knows, hath wrought great things for thee, O Virgin; Him do thou implore that thy flock and people may be saved!

*Another Heirmos [Tone 8, Ode 9]: "Blessed be the Lord God" (Бл҃гослове́нъ Гдⷭ҇ь Бг҃ъ):*[^1463]
*Troparion:* Blessed is the Lord God of Israel, Who by His Cross hath destroyed the ancient curse, and hath set it forth unto us now for veneration; kissing it faithfully and singing praises unto it, we unceasingly praise Thy great mercy!

*Troparion:* Thou art the praise of the Church, O precious Cross, the weapon of sovereigns, and unto all the world the dispenser of humility from God, O Cross, the joy of the Orthodox, and the guardian of the inhabited earth; preserve and sanctify those who bow down before thee!

*Glory: Triadikon:*
*Triadikon:* O Holy Trinity, glory to Thee, O Monad of equal honor, Divine Nature, one awesome Kingdom: Father and Son with the Spirit, Light unapproachable unto all (1 Tim. 6:16),[^1464] unoriginate Godhead, save those who revere Thee, the Creator of all!

*Both now: Theotokion [Stavrotheotokion]:*
*Theotokion:* When Thine Ewe-lamb and Mother stood by the Cross, O Jesus, beholding her Shepherd and Master, bitterly weeping and bowing her maternal heart toward Thee, O Christ, she cried aloud: "What strange sight is this! O Life, how diest Thou?"

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*

*Troparion:* Even as Thou didst save Manasseh who repented (2 Chr. 33:12–13; Pr. Man.),[^1465] O God, save me also, who bitterly repent with tears, and cast not away Thy servant; for I have bent down my soul, living prodigally all my days like that Prodigal Son (Luke 15:11–32)![^1466]

*Katavasia: Heirmos:*
*Heirmos:* Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, Who hath raised up a horn of salvation for us in the house of His servant David; wherein the Dayspring from on high hath visited us, and guided our feet into the way of peace (Luke 1:68–69, 78–79)!

*Exaposteilarion: In the Tone of the Oktoechos.*

*At the Aposticha, Stichera Idiomela, Tone 8:*
*Sticheron:* Reflecting, O my soul, upon the condemnation of the boastful Pharisee on account of his arrogance, and recognizing the justification of the humble-minded Publican through his confession of sins (Luke 18:10–14): hasten on the one hand to cast away boldness on account of virtue, and on the other hand to receive confession of the things wherein thou hast sinned; rise up, acquiring for thyself not an ignoble height through impassioned pride, but receiving great mercy from Christ Who possesses it![^1467]

*Verse: "We were filled in the morning with Thy mercy" (Ps. 89:14 LXX).*

*Verse 2: "And let the brightness of the Lord our God be upon us" (Ps. 89:17 LXX). Martyrion, Tone 8:*
*Martyrion:* Exceedingly did ye contend, O holy ones, valiantly enduring torments from the lawless, confessing Christ before kings; and having passed away from this life, ye work powers in the world, and heal the sick of their sufferings, O holy ones: pray that our souls may be saved!

*Glory, both now: Theotokion, Tone the same [Tone 8]:*
*Theotokion:* Thy protection, O Virgin Theotokos, is a spiritual medicine; for fleeing beneath it, we are delivered from diseases of the soul!

*On Tuesday of the Fourth Week of the Fast, at the Sixth Hour.*
*Troparion of the Prophecy, Tone 2:*
**Choir:** Before Thy Cross we bow down in worship, O Master, and Thy Holy Resurrection we glorify!

*Glory... the end: "and Thy Holy Resurrection we glorify." Both now... the whole Troparion.*

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 65, Tone 6: Blessed be God, Who hath not turned away my prayer, nor His mercy from me (Ps. 65:20 LXX):*
*Verse: Bless our God, ye peoples (Ps. 65:8 LXX):*

*Reading from the Prophecy of Isaiah (Isa. 25:1–8):*[^1468]
O Lord my God, I will glorify Thee, I will hymn Thee and praise Thy Name; for Thou hast wrought marvelous things, a counsel ancient and true. So be it, O Lord! For Thou hast made cities a mound of dust, fortified cities, so that their foundations fall; the city of the ungodly shall not be built unto the age. Therefore the poor people shall bless Thee, and cities of men who suffer wrong, who fear Thee, shall bless Thee. For Thou hast been a helper unto every humble city, and a shelter unto those who fail by reason of poverty; from wicked men Thou shalt deliver them, a shelter of the thirsty; and the breath of wronged men shall bless Thee. Even as faint-hearted men thirsting in Zion, so shalt Thou deliver them from ungodly men to whom Thou didst deliver us; as heat in the shelter of a cloud, Thou shalt humble the branch of the strong. And the Lord of hosts shall make for all the nations upon this mountain a drink of sweetness, a drink of the winepress; they shall drink gladness, they shall drink wine. They shall be anointed with myrrh, and it shall be delivered upon this mountain by tradition, and they shall wait upon this mountain. Deliver all these things unto the nations; for this counsel is upon all the nations. Death having prevailed swallowed them up; and again God hath taken away every tear from every face; He hath taken away the reproach of His people from all the earth (Isa. 25:8; 1 Cor. 15:54; Rev. 7:17; 21:4)!*[^1469]

...for the mouth of the Lord hath spoken these things (Isa. 25:8). And in that day they shall say: Behold, this is our God, on Whom we have set our hope, and He shall save us; behold the Lord, we have waited for Him, and we have rejoiced and been glad in our salvation (Isa. 25:9)!

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 66, Tone 6: God, our God, bless us; God bless us (Ps. 66:7 LXX):*
*Verse: God be merciful unto us, and bless us (Ps. 66:2 LXX):*

## On the Same Tuesday Evening, at "Lord, I Have Cried"

*Stichera, Tone 6, Podoben: "Having laid aside all earthly hope" (Всѐ ѿло́жше):*[^1470]
*Sticheron:* In the midst of the earth Thou didst endure the Cross and Passion, O Compassionate One (Ps. 73:12 LXX), granting unto all immortality and deliverance, on this mid-point of the fast today! Therefore we all set it forth for veneration and embrace it with joy, entreating to behold Thy Passions and Thy life-bearing Resurrection, being enlightened by divine virtues, O Word of God most good, Who alone art Most-merciful!

*Sticheron:* As one dead wast Thou stretched upon the Cross, and pierced with a spear, and given gall to drink, O Long-suffering One (Matt. 27:34, 48; John 19:34), Who of old by the hand of Moses didst turn the bitter waters of Marah into sweetness (Exod. 15:23–25)![^1471] Therefore I pray Thee and beseech Thee: cleanse the most bitter passions of my mind, and sweetening my mind with the honey of repentance, show me forth as a worshiper of Thy precious Passions!

*Other Stichera, Tone 4, Podoben: "Of old Moses" (Дре́вле Мѡѷсе́й):*[^1472]
*Sticheron:* Beholding today before our eyes the great Cross lying before us, which of old Moses prefigured with his palms and conquered Amalek (Exod. 17:11–12),[^1473] come, ye people, let us touch it with a pure mind and with our lips,...

...whereon Christ was lifted up, and put death to death! And having all been vouchsafed such grace, with divinely inspired songs let us praise the Savior of all in song, praying to attain also unto His saving Resurrection itself!

*Other Stichera to the Precious Cross, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast given a sign" (Да́лъ є҆сѝ зна́менїе):*[^1474]
*Sticheron:* Come, let us bow down in worship before the mediator of our life, the Tree lying before us today, the Cross of Christ our God, whereby death hath been wounded, and resurrection hath manifestly been renewed for us who had fallen, crying aloud unto Him Who delivered us: O Thou Who willingly didst suffer for our sake, that Thou mightest save all things, our God, glory to Thee!

*Sticheron:* An invincible power is given unto us Christians: Thy Cross, O our Savior, whereby the multitudes of alien nations are conquered, and peace overshadows Thy Church, O Christ, which rightly glorifies Thee; kissing it now, we fervently cry aloud unto Thee: Vouchsafe us also a portion with Thy saints!

*Sticheron:* Having cleansed the senses of the soul with tears, and having purified ourselves by fasting, come, let us bow down before the Tree of the Cross, whereby through abstinence the soul-corrupting wantonness of the flesh is brought to naught, crying aloud unto Him Who was crucified: Vouchsafe us, O Savior, to bow down in worship before Thy three-day Arising!

*Glory, both now:*
We bow down before Thy Precious Cross, O Most-good One, embracing it with love, and we glorify Thy descent beyond understanding, and Thy measureless mercy and rich goodness, for the sake of which Thou hast saved the human race held fast in the darkness of transgressions; glory, O Christ, to Thy Crucifixion!

*Or after "Both now," from the Sticherarion: Tone 8: "Today the Master of creation" (see fol. 525).[^1475]*

*The Menaion is left aside; and we sing it at Compline in the evening.*[^1476]

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 67, Tone 6: Sing unto God, sing praises to His Name (Ps. 67:5 LXX):*
*Verse: Cast up a highway for Him Who rids upon the setting sun (Ps. 67:5 LXX):*

*Reading from Genesis (Gen. 9:8–17):*[^1477]
And the Lord God spoke unto Noah, and to his sons with him, saying: Behold, I establish My covenant with you, and with your seed after you, and with every living soul that is with you, of the fowl, and of the cattle, and of all the wild beasts of the earth, as many as are with you, of all that came out of the ark. And I will establish My covenant with you, and all flesh shall no more die of the water of the deluge, and there shall no more be a deluge of water to destroy the whole earth. And God said unto Noah: This is the token of the covenant which I make between Me and you, and between every living soul that is with you, unto perpetual generations: I set My bow in the cloud, and it shall be for a token of a covenant between Me and the earth. And it shall come to pass, when I bring clouds over the earth, that the bow shall be seen in the clouds; and I will remember My covenant, which is between Me and you, and between every living soul in all flesh; and the water shall no more become a deluge to destroy all flesh. And My bow shall be in the cloud, and they shall look upon it to remember My perpetual covenant between Me and between every soul that lives in all flesh upon the earth. And God said unto Noah: This is the token of the covenant which I have made between Me and between all flesh that is upon the earth.

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 68, Tone 6: Let Thy salvation, O God, set me on high (Ps. 68:30 LXX):*
*Verse: Let the poor see and rejoice (Ps. 68:33 LXX):*

*Reading from the Proverbs (Prov. 12:8–22):*[^1478]
The mouth of an understanding man shall be praised by a man, but the hard-hearted shall be mocked. Better is a man in dishonor serving himself, than one who wraps honor about himself and lacks bread. A righteous man has compassion on the lives of his beasts, but the tender mercies of the wicked are cruel. He that tills his own land shall be filled with bread, but they that pursue vanity are void of understanding. [He that finds pleasure in lingering over wine shall leave dishonor in his own strongholds.][^1479] The desires of the wicked are evil, but the roots of the righteous are in stability. By the sin of his lips a sinner falls into a snare, but the righteous man is delivered from it. He that looks on the right path shall be pitied; but he that meets people at the gates shall grieve a soul. From the fruits of his lips the soul of a man shall be satisfied with good things, and the recompense of his lips shall be rendered unto him. The ways of fools are right before them, but a wise man listens to counsels. A fool makes known his anger on the very day, but a crafty man conceals his own dishonor. A righteous man declares the open truth, but an unjust witness is deceitful. There are some who speak words that wound like a sword, but the tongues of the wise heal. True lips establish testimony, but a hasty witness has an unjust tongue. Deceit is in the heart of him that imagines...

...evil, but they that counsel peace shall rejoice. Nothing unjust shall be pleasing to the righteous man, but the ungodly shall be filled with evil. Lying lips are an abomination to the Lord, but he that deals faithfully is acceptable unto Him.

*Then: Vouchsafe, O Lord, this evening:*

*At the Aposticha, Idiomelon Sticheron, Tone 3:*
*Sticheron:* Surpassing the Publican in sins, I am not zealous for his repentance;[^1480] and not having acquired the righteous deeds of the Pharisee, I imitate his haughtiness! But by Thy measureless humility, O Christ God, Who didst lay low the demonic haughtiness upon the Cross: deliver me from the evils of the former, and from the haughtiness of the latter; and having established the good resolve of both in my soul, save me!

*Verse 1: "Unto Thee have I lifted up mine eyes, O Thou that dwellest in heaven" (Ps. 122:1 LXX). Verse 2: "Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us" (Ps. 122:3 LXX):*[^1481]
*Martyrion:* The Prophets, and the Apostles of Christ, and the Martyrs taught us to sing praises unto the consubstantial Trinity, and enlightened the deceived nations, and made the sons of men partakers with the Angels!

*Glory, both now: Tone 6:*
*"All creation, beholding Thee upon the Cross..." (see fol. 530).[^1482]*

*If the Annunciation of the Most-Holy Theotokos should fall on this Wednesday of Mid-Lent: the Canon of the Cross is omitted, and it is sung on Monday or on Friday of the same week.*[^1483]

## On Wednesday of the Fourth Week of the Holy Fast

*At Matins, the Trinity Hymns. After the first Stichology, Sessional Hymn from the Octoechos. After the second Stichology, Sessional Hymn by Kyr Joseph, Tone 6, Podoben: "The hope of the world" (Оу҆пова́нїе мі́рꙋ):*[^1484]
*Sessional Hymn:* Shining forth with the time of abstinence, the divine...

...and all-honorable Cross lies before us for veneration! Let us draw near with a pure conscience, let us draw sanctification and enlightenment, and with fear let us cry aloud: O Lover of mankind, our Savior, glory to Thy compassions! *(Twice)*

*Glory, both now: Cross-Theotokion:*
*Cross-Theotokion:* Standing by the Cross, the unwedded Mother called aloud unto Him Who was born seedlessly from her: A sword has pierced through my heart, O Son,[^1485] enduring not to behold Thee hanging upon the Tree, before Whom all things tremble as Creator and God; O Long-suffering One, glory to Thee!

*After the third Stichology, Sessional Hymn by Kyr Theodore, Tone 1, Podoben: "Thy tomb, O Savior" (Гро́бъ тво́й):*[^1486]
*Sessional Hymn:* Having been enlightened by virtues, let us draw near, having acquired the purity of abstinence; and crying aloud, let us bow down before the Precious Cross! Sanctify our souls and bodies, and vouchsafe us also to bow down before Thy Most-pure Passion, O only God of all, granting us great mercy! *(Twice)*

*Glory, both now: Cross-Theotokion, the same Tone and Podoben:*
*Cross-Theotokion:* Beholding Thee stretched out dead upon the Cross, O Christ, the all-immaculate Mother cried aloud: O My Son, co-unoriginate with the Father and the Spirit, what is this Thine ineffable dispensation, whereby Thou hast saved the creation of Thine immaculate hands, O Compassionate One!

*Canon of the Cross. A work of Kyr Theophanes. Bearing this acrostic: Let us bow down before the all-honorable Wood.*[^1487]
*Tone 4, Ode 1. Heirmos: "I will open my mouth" (Ѽве́рзꙋ ᲂу҆ста̀):*[^1488]
*Ode 1. Heirmos:* Let us bow down in worship before the Holy Tree, whereon Christ stretched out His palms, conquering the opposing principalities, having cleansed ourselves by fasting, unto the praise and glory of the Almighty!

*Troparion:* The Cross is seen lying before us, granting sanctification, the saving...

...Cross: unto this let us draw near, having cleansed body and heart, and let us draw saving grace!

*Troparion:* Cleanse me with the fire of Thy commandments, O Lover of mankind, and grant me to behold Thy saving Passions, and with love to bow down before them, being walled about and preserved by the Cross!

*Theotokion:* Beholding Thy lifting up upon the Cross, O Lover of mankind, she that bore Thee cried aloud with lamentation: How is He seen judged, Who desires to judge all? Seeing Him hanging, the Lord of glory!

*Tone 4, Ode 3. Heirmos: "Thy hymnographers, O Theotokos" (Твоѧ̀ пѣвцы̀):*[^1489]
*Ode 3. Heirmos:* Having washed our hearts with the water of the fast, let us faithfully embrace the Tree of the Cross, whereon Christ hung, pouring forth for us the water of immortality, His Cross!

*Troparion:* Winged with the sail of the Cross, the saving ship, lo, through fasting we reach mid-voyage; O Messiah Jesus our God, pilot us thereby through Thy Passion unto the havens!

*Troparion:* Moses prefigured thee upon the mountain, O Cross, unto the slaughter of the nations;[^1490] and we depict thee in our hearts, and beholding thee and bowing down before thee, we conquer our carnal enemies by thy power!

*Theotokion:* By Thine own will Thou becamest man, being God and Creator of all; and now seeing Thee hanging upon the Cross, I behold Thee, O My Son, Christ! she that bore Thee said, and her heart was consumed with sorrow!

*Triodion Canon. Tone 6, Ode 3. Heirmos: "Being Lord of all" (Гдⷭ҇ь сы́й всѣ́мъ):*[^1491]
*Ode 3. Heirmos:* Being Lord of all and Creator God, Thou wast lifted up upon the Cross in the midst of the earth, raising up unto Thyself fallen human nature, through the malice and counsel of the enemy. Therefore we faithfully glorify Thee, being confirmed by Thy Passion!

*Troparion:* Having cleansed our senses with the light of the fast, let us, the faithful, be richly illumined with the noetic rays of the Cross; and beholding it piously lying before us today, with pure lips and heart let us bow down before it!

*Troparion:* Let us bow down before the divine Cross, the place where the feet of Christ stood,[^1492] asking to be established upon the rock of God's commandments, that the steps of our souls may be guided into the way of peace by divine grace!

*Theotokion:* Thou didst come forth from the unwedded Virgin, O Christ, taking from her an intelligent and animate flesh; and by Thy Cross Thou didst cast down the enemy, and didst renew again corrupt human nature: therefore we glorify Thy tender compassion!

*Tone 1, Ode 3. Another Heirmos: "Establish, O Lord, Thy Church" (Оу҆твердѝ Гдⷭ҇и цр҃ковь):*[^1493]
*Ode 3. Another Heirmos:* Clap your hands, all ye nations, with songs, beholding the worshipful Tree whereon Christ was suspended and the devil was wounded!

*Troparion:* Life-bearing joy is set forth today; come, let us bow down with fear before the Precious Cross of Christ, that we may receive the Holy Spirit!

*Trinity Hymn:* O Sun of threefold radiance, O Light of three splendors, God, Father, and Son, and Holy Spirit, unoriginate Essence and Word: deliver from tribulations those who sing Thy praise!

*Theotokion:* The angelic ranks hymn Thee, O blessed, all-immaculate Virgin Theotokos; and with them the human race glorifies Thee as the unwedded Bride!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee:*
*Troparion:* Coming to touch thee, O life-bearing Cross, I am struck with awe in tongue and mind, seeing beforehand that upon thee was poured forth the divine Blood of my Lord!

*Ode 3. Heirmos:* Establish, O Lord, Thy Church, which Thou hast acquired by the power of Thy Cross; for thereby Thou hast conquered the enemy and enlightened the universe!

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 6, Automelon:*
*Sessional Hymn:* Today the prophetic word is fulfilled: for behold, we bow down in worship at the place where Thy feet stood, O Lord;[^1494] and having tasted of the Tree of salvation, we have obtained deliverance from the passions that arise from sins, through the intercessions of the Theotokos, O only Lover of mankind!

*Glory:*
*Sessional Hymn:* Thy Cross, O Lord, is sanctified; for in it healings are bestowed upon those who are diseased in sins: therefore we fall down before Thee; have mercy on us!

*Both now:*
*Sessional Hymn:* No sooner was the Tree of Thy Cross set up, O Christ, than the foundations of death were shaken, O Lord! For him whom Hades swallowed with desire, he let go with trembling; Thou hast shown us Thy salvation, O Holy One, and we glorify Thee, O Son of God; have mercy on us!

*Tone 4, Ode 4. Heirmos: "He Who sits in glory" (Сѣдѧ́й въ сла́вѣ):*[^1495]
*Ode 4. Heirmos:* Prefiguring the sign of the Cross, stretching out his hands crosswise of old, the glorious Jacob blessed his grandsons,[^1496] signifying the saving blessing coming upon us all!

*Troparion:* Preserved by the sign of the Cross, and kissing with joy of spirit the wood lying before us, let us go forth unto the saving Passions, having put to death the destructive passions of the flesh!

*Troparion:* A saving weapon, an unconquerable victory, a token of joy, whereby death was put to death: let us embrace thee, adorned with glory, O all-honorable Cross of Him Who was crucified upon thee!

*Theotokion:* Visible unto me, Thou wast despised, Who art unapproachable unto the Angels, O Jesus my Son, Who didst borrow flesh from me; and now beholding Thee nailed unto the Tree, I lament! the Mother of Christ said.

*Tone 4, Ode 5. Heirmos: "All things were amazed" (Оу҆диви́шася всѧ́ческая):*[^1497]
*Ode 5. Heirmos:* Dead wast Thou, nailed unto the Cross, being life and salvation unto all...

...grant unto us, therefore, O Savior, to embrace it with a cleansed soul, and to behold Thy saving Passions, rejoicing!

*Troparion:* The ranks of the bodiless hosts stand before thee, trembling, O life-giving Tree; for upon thee Christ poured forth His precious Blood, emitting a ray from afar, bringing endless destruction unto the demons!

*Troparion:* Wounded by the weapon of the enemy, heal me by Thy Blood, O Word; and with the spear tear up the handwriting of my sins, O Savior,[^1498] as I cry unto Thee: Inscribe me in the books of the saved, as Thou art compassionate!

*Theotokion:* O ripe Cluster, how art Thou suspended upon the Tree? O Sun of glory, how art Thou lifted up? darkening the radiance of the sun, O Savior, by Thy Passion! The Ewe-lamb that bore Thee of old cried aloud unto Thee, exclaiming maternally:

*Tone 4, Ode 6. Heirmos: "Prefiguring the three-day burial" (Возопѝ проѡбразꙋѧ):*[^1499]
*Ode 6. Heirmos:* Shaken wast thou, O dwelling of Hades, when the Cross was set up; but unto the faithful thou hast been an unshakable confirmation and a firm protection, O all-honorable Cross of the Lord!

*Troparion:* Having become fruitful with virtues, let us embrace the life-bearing fruits of the divine Tree, which the fruitful Vine sprouted, having stretched Himself out upon it, O Jesus![^1500]

*Troparion:* We sing to Thee, O Jesus, for Thy great grace, bowing down before Thy Cross, the spear, and the reed; for by them, O Compassionate One, Thou didst break down the middle wall of enmity!

*Theotokion:* A river flowing with life-giving healing didst thou bear, O all-pure one, as a fountain for our renewal, Who set up the Cross and poured forth drops of salvation!

*Katavasia:* Prefiguring the three-day burial, the Prophet Jonah, praying in the belly of the whale, cried aloud: Deliver me from corruption, O Jesus, King of the hosts!

*Tone 7, Kontakion, Automelon: "No longer does the fiery sword guard the gate of Eden" (Не ктомꙋ̀ пла́менное ѡ҆рꙋ́жїе):*[^1501]
*And the Ikos: "Three crosses Pilate planted on Golgotha..." (see fol. 517).[^1502]*

*Tone 4, Ode 7. Heirmos: "The godly youths did not worship creation" (Не послꙋжи́ша тва́ри):*[^1503]
*Ode 7. Heirmos:* The axe of Elisha, which divided the Jordan, prefigured the Cross, O Christ,[^1504] whereby Thou didst draw up the nations from the abyss of vanity, who sing: Blessed art Thou, the Lord and God of our fathers!

*Troparion:* Heavenly things rejoice with earthly things at the veneration of thy Cross; for through thee, O Almighty One, union was wrought for Angels and men, who cry aloud: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God!

*Troparion:* Offering compassion like the cypress, fragrant faith like the cedar, and true love like the pine,[^1505] let us bow down before the Cross of the Lord, glorifying upon it the Redeemer Who was nailed thereto!

*Theotokion:* Without shaking the heavens, God took up His abode in thy womb, O chosen city of God; but when He was suspended upon the Cross, He shook creation: pray Him that I may be preserved upon His immovable rock!

*Tone 4, Ode 8. Heirmos: "The godly children in the furnace" (Ѻ҆́троки бл҃гочести́выѧ):*[^1506]
*Ode 8. Heirmos:* Thou didst stretch out Thy hands upon the Tree, tearing up sin with unrepressed hands; and Thou wast pierced with a spear, thereby wounding the combatant, O Lord; and Thou didst taste of gall, drying up sweet wickedness; and Thou wast given vinegar to drink, O Joy of all![^1507]

*Troparion:* With a pure mind and conscience, having brightly drawn near, let us bow down in worship; for the honorable and all-pure Tree lies before us, whereby Christ endured a dishonorable death, exchanging honor for those who had been grievously dishonored through transgression!

*Troparion:* By the tree of sin was I put to death, and by sweet tasting was I buried: bring me to life, O Lord, and raise me up who lie fallen; show me forth as a worshiper of Thy Passions, and a partaker of Thy divine Resurrection, and a joint-heir with those who have loved Thee!

*Theotokion:* Beholding Him lifted up, having neither form nor beauty in His Passion, Whom incarnate I knew as fairer than the sons of men,[^1508] even Thee, O only-begotten Son: the all-pure Virgin cried aloud: Show forth Thy glory, the salvation of all!

*Tone 6, Ode 8. Another Heirmos: "In accordance with the ancestral law" (По зако́нꙋ ѻ҆́тчи):*[^1509]
*Ode 8. Another Heirmos:* When at midday Thou wast crucified voluntarily in the midst of the earth, Thou didst tear out the ends of the world from the throat of the enemy, O Compassionate One. Therefore, in the middle week of the fast, bowing down before Thy glorious Cross, we cry aloud: Praise the Lord, and exalt Him above all!

*Troparion:* Token of joy, indestructible weapon, wall of the Church, boast of Martyrs, adornment of Apostles, confirmation of Hierarchs: strengthen my exhausted soul, vouchsafe me to bow down before thee, and to sing to thee, crying aloud: Praise the Lord, all ye works, and exalt Him above all unto the ages!

*Troparion:* I lament and weep when I take to mind the unhypocritical judgment, being condemned, O Long-suffering One. Therefore spare me, and lighten the weighed-down burden of my soul, that rejoicing I may cry: Praise the Lord!

*Theotokion:* The bush prefigured the mystery of thy childbearing beyond understanding, O all-immaculate Virgin;[^1510] for even as it remained unburnt, so didst thou, having given birth to the Fire, Christ the Savior, Who was lifted up upon the Cross: entreat Him to deliver me from eternal fire, as I cry aloud: Praise the Lord, all ye works, and exalt Him above all!

*Tone 1, Ode 8. Another Heirmos: "This chosen and holy day" (Се́й ᲂу҆́бѡ нарече́нный):*[^1511]
*Ode 8. Another Heirmos:* Come, having cleansed ourselves by fasting, let us lovingly embrace the Cross of the Lord lying before us; for unto us it is a treasure of sanctification and power: therefore we sing its praise unto the ages!

*Troparion:* This tripartite and great Cross,[^1512] small though it be to look upon, is wider than the heavens by its power, ever leading men up unto God; whereby we bless Christ unto the ages!

*Trinity Hymn:* I glorify one Essence in three Persons, unconfusedly of one Hypostasis in three, neither dividing the form of the Father, and of the Son, with the Spirit; for there is one God over all in Trinity!

*Theotokion:* Thou alone among mothers hast been shown forth, O Virgin Mary, Bride of God, having given birth without a man unto Christ the Savior, having preserved the seal of virginity; we bless thee, O pure one, unto the ages!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee:*
*Troparion:* Let this Most-holy Tree be honored, which of old the Prophet proclaimed that the Israelites who crucified Him would cast into the bread of Christ;[^1513] Whom we exalt above all unto all ages!

*Katavasia:* Stretching out his hands in the form of a cross in the lions' den of old, the great among the Prophets, Daniel, was saved unharmed from their devouring,[^1514] blessing the God of all unto the ages!

*Tone 4, Ode 9. Heirmos: "Let every earthborn mortal" (Вся́къ земноро́дный):*[^1515]
*Ode 9. Heirmos:* With the spear Thou openest Thy side, pouring forth for me a fountain of forgiveness; and Thou wast nailed unto the Tree, by the Tree putting an end to the condemnation in the midst of the earth, O Lover of mankind: which Tree we now embrace through the mediation of the fast, singing the praise of Thy loving-kindness!

*Troparion:* Drop sweetness, ye mountains; and ye hills, drop rejoicing with love;[^1516] and ye trees of the plain, and ye cedars of Lebanon, dance with joy...

...at the veneration of the life-bearing Cross today: ye Prophets, Martyrs, Apostles, and spirits of the righteous, leap for joy!

*Troparion:* Look down upon Thy people and Thine inheritance, O Lord, who sing to Thee with fear, for whose sake Thou didst endure voluntary death; let not the measureless multitude of our evils overcome Thy tender mercy, but save us all, O Most-good One, by Thy Cross, as Thou art the Lover of mankind!

*Theotokion:* By Thy nod Thou shakest the visible world, yet being crucified Thou hangest suspended, the Theotokos cried aloud with lamentation, desiring to destroy the passionate imaginings of the first-fashioned man, O Christ, and to heal his contrition by Thy goodness!

*Tone 4, Ode 9. Another Heirmos: "Every tongue is at a loss" (Недоꙋмѣ́етъ вся́къ):*
*Ode 9. Another Heirmos:* Elisha of old, drawing the iron axe-head out of the river by wood,[^1517] prefigured thee, O Cross, life-giving Tree, whereby Christ, having been nailed upon thee, drew the nations out of the depth of demonic idolatry: therefore, bowing down before thee, we glorify His dominion!

*Troparion:* The rays of the sun were turned into darkness by Thy crucifixion, O Savior, and the radiance of the moon was taken away, and all the elements were changed with trembling: therefore I cry aloud unto Thee: having transformed my mind that was changed by the gloom of the passions, O Word, illumine and save me by Thy right hand!

*Troparion:* By Thy wound heal the passions of my soul; by the piercing of Thy ribs bring to an end the painful piercings of the demons; by Thy nails, O Christ, nail through my pleasurable and deceitful desires, granting me dispassionately to bow down before Thy precious Passions and Resurrection!

*Theotokion:*

Fairer in beauty did the fair Maiden bear Thee; beholding Thee in Thy Passion having neither beauty nor comeliness,[^1518] she cried aloud with lamentation, O Savior: Above all understanding do I marvel at Thy humility, O My Son, whereby Thou savest humbled human nature!

*Tone 1, Ode 9. Another Heirmos: "Shine, shine" (Свѣти́ся свѣти́ся):*
*Ode 9. Another Heirmos:* Leap for joy, be radiant, all ye people of God; and beholding beforehand the precious Wood of the Cross, kiss it with fear and receive joy, ever glorifying the Lord of glory Who was lifted up upon it!

*Troparion:* A divine weapon art thou unto my life, O Cross; the Master, mounting upon thee, saved me, pouring forth blood and water, being wounded in the ribs; whereof I partake rejoicing, glorifying Him!

*Trinity Hymn:* Three in Persons, One in Essence: I bow down before Thee, the Holy Divinity, Father, and Son, with the Holy Spirit; one Principle, one Kingdom, working good over all!

*Theotokion:* Thou art the great Mountain wherein Christ took up His abode, O Virgin, even as the blessed David cries aloud;[^1519] for whose sake we have been lifted up unto heaven, having been established in spirit, O all-blessed one!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee:*
*Troparion:* O Cross, scepter and victory unto kings, courage unto soldiers, conquering adversaries through hope in thee: grant victories over barbarians unto us who ever bow down before thee!

*Katavasia:* O Mother Virgin and true Theotokos, who without seed didst bear Christ our God Who was lifted up in the flesh upon the Cross: with Him all we, the faithful, now worthily magnify thee!

*Exapostilarion of the Tone, and the present hymn. Podoben: "In the Spirit" (Дх҃омъ):*[^1520]
*Exapostilarion:* At the mid-point of the Fast, the All-honorable Tree summons all unto veneration; as many as worthily follow Christ's Passions by their own sufferings: come, all ye faithful, let us bow down before the Tree of the awesome mystery!

*Theotokion:* Unwedded and all-pure, the good Mother of the Word, lamented crying aloud, grieving with weeping: Did Gabriel bring me such a wonder of Annunciation joy,[^1521] who came to fulfill the ineffable counsel and the divine dispensation?

*At the Aposticha, Idiomelon Stichera, Tone 8:*
*Sticheron:* Having reached the mid-point of the course of fasting, which leads unto Thy precious Cross, O Christ, to behold Thy day, which Abraham saw and rejoiced,[^1522] receiving Isaac alive from the grave of the mount: be well pleased that we also, having been delivered from enemies by faith, may partake of the Mystical Supper, crying in peace: O our Enlightenment and Salvation, glory to Thee! *(Twice)*

*The usual Verse: "We were filled in the morning with Thy mercy, O Lord" (Ps. 89:14 LXX):*
*Martyrion:* O invincible Martyrs of Christ, having conquered deception by the power of the Cross, ye received the grace of eternal life! Ye feared not the threats of the torturers; wounded with torments, ye rejoiced; and now your blood has become healing for our souls: pray that our souls may be saved!

*Glory: the same Tone:*
*Sticheron:* Having crossed the deep of abstinence, let us receive the haven of salvation: the season of Thy voluntary Passion, O Lord! But as Thou art merciful and compassionate, vouchsafe us also to behold the day of Thy glorious Resurrection in peace, O Lover of mankind!

*Both now: the same Tone:*
*The same Sticheron is repeated.*

*The veneration of the Cross takes place at the First Hour, even as was written before; during which, while the brethren are bowing down, we sing the previously written Troparia from Sunday (see fol. 524):[^1523] Idiomela to the Precious Cross, Tone 2: "Come, ye faithful" (Прїиди́те вѣ́рнїи); and the rest. And the Dismissal.*

...saving Cross:[^1524] unto this let us draw near, having cleansed body and heart, and let us draw saving grace!

*Troparion:* Cleanse me with the fire of Thy commandments, O Lover of mankind, and grant me to behold Thy saving Passions, and with love to bow down before them, being walled about and preserved by the Cross!

*Theotokion:* Beholding Thy lifting up upon the Cross, O Lover of mankind, she that bore Thee cried aloud with lamentation: How is He seen judged, Who desires to judge all? Seeing Him hanging, the Lord of glory!

*Tone 4, Ode 3. Heirmos: "Thy hymnographers, O Theotokos" (Твоѧ̀ пѣвцы̀):*[^1525]
*Ode 3. Heirmos:* Having washed our hearts with the water of the fast, let us faithfully embrace the Tree of the Cross, whereon Christ hung, pouring forth for us the water of immortality, His Cross!

*Troparion:* Winged with the sail of the Cross, the saving ship, lo, through fasting we reach mid-voyage; O Messiah Jesus our God, pilot us thereby through Thy Passion unto the havens!

*Troparion:* Moses prefigured thee upon the mountain, O Cross, unto the slaughter of the nations;[^1526] and we depict thee in our hearts, and beholding thee and bowing down before thee, we conquer our carnal enemies by thy power!

*Theotokion:* By Thine own will Thou becamest man, being God and Creator of all; and now seeing Thee hanging upon the Cross, I behold Thee, O My Son, Christ! she that bore Thee said, and her heart was consumed with sorrow!

*Triodion Canon. Tone 6, Ode 3. Heirmos: "Being Lord of all" (Гдⷭ҇ь сы́й всѣ́мъ):*[^1527]
*Ode 3. Heirmos:* Being Lord of all and Creator God, Thou wast lifted up upon the Cross in the midst of the earth, raising up unto Thyself fallen human nature, through the malice and counsel of the enemy. Therefore we faithfully glorify Thee, being confirmed by Thy Passion!

*Troparion:* Having cleansed our senses with the light of the fast, let us, the faithful, be richly illumined with the noetic rays of the Cross; and beholding it piously lying before us today, with pure lips and heart let us bow down before it!

*Troparion:* Let us bow down before the divine Cross, the place where the feet of Christ stood,[^1528] asking to be established upon the rock of God's commandments, that the steps of our souls may be guided into the way of peace by divine grace!

*Theotokion:* Thou didst come forth from the unwedded Virgin, O Christ, taking from her an intelligent and animate flesh; and by Thy Cross Thou didst cast down the enemy, and didst renew again corrupt human nature: therefore we glorify Thy tender compassion!

*Tone 1, Ode 3. Another Heirmos: "Establish, O Lord, Thy Church" (Оу҆твердѝ Гдⷭ҇и цр҃ковь):*[^1529]
*Ode 3. Another Heirmos:* Clap your hands, all ye nations, with songs, beholding the worshipful Tree whereon Christ was suspended and the devil was wounded!

*Troparion:* Life-bearing joy is set forth today; come, let us bow down with fear before the Precious Cross of Christ, that we may receive the Holy Spirit!

*Trinity Hymn:* O Sun of threefold radiance, O Light of three splendors, God, Father, and Son, and Holy Spirit, unoriginate Essence and Word: deliver from tribulations those who sing Thy praise!

*Theotokion:* The angelic ranks hymn Thee, O blessed, all-immaculate Virgin Theotokos; and with them the human race glorifies Thee as the unwedded Bride!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee:*
*Troparion:* Coming to touch thee, O life-bearing Cross, I am struck with awe in tongue and mind, seeing beforehand that upon thee was poured forth the divine Blood of my Lord!

*Ode 3. Heirmos:* Establish, O Lord, Thy Church, which Thou hast acquired by the power of Thy Cross; for thereby Thou hast conquered the enemy and enlightened the universe!

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 6, Automelon:*
*Sessional Hymn:* Today the prophetic word is fulfilled: for behold, we bow down in worship at the place where Thy feet stood, O Lord;[^1530] and having tasted of the Tree of salvation, we have obtained deliverance from the passions that arise from sins, through the intercessions of the Theotokos, O only Lover of mankind!

*Glory:*
*Sessional Hymn:* Thy Cross, O Lord, is sanctified; for in it healings are bestowed upon those who are diseased in sins: therefore we fall down before Thee; have mercy on us!

*Both now:*
*Sessional Hymn:* No sooner was the Tree of Thy Cross set up, O Christ, than the foundations of death were shaken, O Lord! For him whom Hades swallowed with desire, he let go with trembling; Thou hast shown us Thy salvation, O Holy One, and we glorify Thee, O Son of God; have mercy on us!

*Tone 4, Ode 4. Heirmos: "He Who sits in glory" (Сѣдѧ́й въ сла́вѣ):*[^1531]
*Ode 4. Heirmos:* Prefiguring the sign of the Cross, stretching out his hands crosswise of old, the glorious Jacob blessed his grandsons,[^1532] signifying the saving blessing coming upon us all!

*Troparion:* Preserved by the sign of the Cross, and kissing with joy of spirit the wood lying before us, let us go forth unto the saving Passions, having put to death the destructive passions of the flesh!

*Troparion:* A saving weapon, an unconquerable victory, a token of joy, whereby death was put to death: let us embrace thee, adorned with glory, O all-honorable Cross of Him Who was crucified upon thee!

*Theotokion:* Visible unto me, Thou wast despised, Who art unapproachable unto the Angels, O Jesus my Son, Who didst borrow flesh from me; and now beholding Thee nailed unto the Tree, I lament! the Mother of Christ said.

*Tone 4, Ode 5. Heirmos: "All things were amazed" (Оу҆диви́шася всѧ́ческая):*[^1533]
*Ode 5. Heirmos:* Dead wast Thou, nailed unto the Cross, being life and salvation unto all...

...grant unto us, therefore, O Savior, to embrace it with a cleansed soul, and to behold Thy saving Passions, rejoicing!

*Troparion:* The ranks of the bodiless hosts stand before thee, trembling, O life-giving Tree; for upon thee Christ poured forth His precious Blood, emitting a ray from afar, bringing endless destruction unto the demons!

*Troparion:* Wounded by the weapon of the enemy, heal me by Thy Blood, O Word; and with the spear tear up the handwriting of my sins, O Savior,[^1534] as I cry unto Thee: Inscribe me in the books of the saved, as Thou art compassionate!

*Theotokion:* O ripe Cluster, how art Thou suspended upon the Tree? O Sun of glory, how art Thou lifted up? darkening the radiance of the sun, O Savior, by Thy Passion! The Ewe-lamb that bore Thee of old cried aloud unto Thee, exclaiming maternally:

*Tone 4, Ode 6. Heirmos: "Prefiguring the three-day burial" (Возопѝ проѡбразꙋѧ):*[^1535]
*Ode 6. Heirmos:* Shaken wast thou, O dwelling of Hades, when the Cross was set up; but unto the faithful thou hast been an unshakable confirmation and a firm protection, O all-honorable Cross of the Lord!

*Troparion:* Having become fruitful with virtues, let us embrace the life-bearing fruits of the divine Tree, which the fruitful Vine sprouted, having stretched Himself out upon it, O Jesus![^1536]

*Troparion:* We sing to Thee, O Jesus, for Thy great grace, bowing down before Thy Cross, the spear, and the reed; for by them, O Compassionate One, Thou didst break down the middle wall of enmity!

*Theotokion:* A river flowing with life-giving healing didst thou bear, O all-pure one, as a fountain for our renewal, Who set up the Cross and poured forth drops of salvation!

*Katavasia:* Prefiguring the three-day burial, the Prophet Jonah, praying in the belly of the whale, cried aloud: Deliver me from corruption, O Jesus, King of the hosts!

*Tone 7, Kontakion, Automelon: "No longer does the fiery sword guard the gate of Eden" (Не ктомꙋ̀ пла́менное ѡ҆рꙋ́жїе):*[^1537]
*And the Ikos: "Three crosses Pilate planted on Golgotha..." (see fol. 517).[^1538]*

*Tone 4, Ode 7. Heirmos: "The godly youths did not worship creation" (Не послꙋжи́ша тва́ри):*[^1539]
*Ode 7. Heirmos:* The axe of Elisha, which divided the Jordan, prefigured the Cross, O Christ,[^1540] whereby Thou didst draw up the nations from the abyss of vanity, who sing: Blessed art Thou, the Lord and God of our fathers!

*Troparion:* Heavenly things rejoice with earthly things at the veneration of thy Cross; for through thee, O Almighty One, union was wrought for Angels and men, who cry aloud: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God!

*Troparion:* Offering compassion like the cypress, fragrant faith like the cedar, and true love like the pine,[^1541] let us bow down before the Cross of the Lord, glorifying upon it the Redeemer Who was nailed thereto!

*Theotokion:* Without shaking the heavens, God took up His abode in thy womb, O chosen city of God; but when He was suspended upon the Cross, He shook creation: pray Him that I may be preserved upon His immovable rock!

*Tone 4, Ode 8. Heirmos: "The godly children in the furnace" (Ѻ҆́троки бл҃гочести́выѧ):*[^1542]
*Ode 8. Heirmos:* Thou didst stretch out Thy hands upon the Tree, tearing up sin with unrepressed hands; and Thou wast pierced with a spear, thereby wounding the combatant, O Lord; and Thou didst taste of gall, drying up sweet wickedness; and Thou wast given vinegar to drink, O Joy of all![^1543]

*Troparion:* With a pure mind and conscience, having brightly drawn near, let us bow down in worship; for the honorable and all-pure Tree lies before us, whereby Christ endured a dishonorable death, exchanging honor for those who had been grievously dishonored through transgression!

*Troparion:* By the tree of sin was I put to death, and by sweet tasting was I buried: bring me to life, O Lord, and raise me up who lie fallen; show me forth as a worshiper of Thy Passions, and a partaker of Thy divine Resurrection, and a joint-heir with those who have loved Thee!

*Theotokion:* Beholding Him lifted up, having neither form nor beauty in His Passion, Whom incarnate I knew as fairer than the sons of men,[^1544] even Thee, O only-begotten Son: the all-pure Virgin cried aloud: Show forth Thy glory, the salvation of all!

*Tone 6, Ode 8. Another Heirmos: "In accordance with the ancestral law" (По зако́нꙋ ѻ҆́тчи):*[^1545]
*Ode 8. Another Heirmos:* When at midday Thou wast crucified voluntarily in the midst of the earth, Thou didst tear out the ends of the world from the throat of the enemy, O Compassionate One. Therefore, in the middle week of the fast, bowing down before Thy glorious Cross, we cry aloud: Praise the Lord, and exalt Him above all!

*Troparion:* Token of joy, indestructible weapon, wall of the Church, boast of Martyrs, adornment of Apostles, confirmation of Hierarchs: strengthen my exhausted soul, vouchsafe me to bow down before thee, and to sing to thee, crying aloud: Praise the Lord, all ye works, and exalt Him above all unto the ages!

*Troparion:* I lament and weep when I take to mind the unhypocritical judgment, being condemned, O Long-suffering One. Therefore spare me, and lighten the weighed-down burden of my soul, that rejoicing I may cry: Praise the Lord!

*Theotokion:* The bush prefigured the mystery of thy childbearing beyond understanding, O all-immaculate Virgin;[^1546] for even as it remained unburnt, so didst thou, having given birth to the Fire, Christ the Savior, Who was lifted up upon the Cross: entreat Him to deliver me from eternal fire, as I cry aloud: Praise the Lord, all ye works, and exalt Him above all!

*Tone 1, Ode 8. Another Heirmos: "This chosen and holy day" (Се́й ᲂу҆́бѡ нарече́нный):*[^1547][^1548]
*Ode 8. Another Heirmos:* Come, having cleansed ourselves by fasting, let us lovingly embrace the Cross of the Lord lying before us; for unto us it is a treasure of sanctification and power: therefore we sing its praise unto the ages!

*Troparion:* This tripartite and great Cross,[^1549] small though it be to look upon, is wider than the heavens by its power, ever leading men up unto God; whereby we bless Christ unto the ages!

*Trinity Hymn:* I glorify one Essence in three Persons, unconfusedly of one Hypostasis in three, neither dividing the form of the Father, and of the Son, with the Spirit; for there is one God over all in Trinity!

*Theotokion:* Thou alone among mothers hast been shown forth, O Virgin Mary, Bride of God, having given birth without a man unto Christ the Savior, having preserved the seal of virginity; we bless thee, O pure one, unto the ages!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee:*
*Troparion:* Let this Most-holy Tree be honored, which of old the Prophet proclaimed that the Israelites who crucified Him would cast into the bread of Christ;[^1550] Whom we exalt above all unto all ages!

*Katavasia:* Stretching out his hands in the form of a cross in the lions' den of old, the great among the Prophets, Daniel, was saved unharmed from their devouring,[^1551] blessing the God of all unto the ages!

*Tone 4, Ode 9. Heirmos: "Let every earthborn mortal" (Вся́къ земноро́дный):*[^1552]
*Ode 9. Heirmos:* With the spear Thou openest Thy side, pouring forth for me a fountain of forgiveness; and Thou wast nailed unto the Tree, by the Tree putting an end to the condemnation in the midst of the earth, O Lover of mankind: which Tree we now embrace through the mediation of the fast, singing the praise of Thy loving-kindness!

*Troparion:* Drop sweetness, ye mountains; and ye hills, drop rejoicing with love;[^1553] and ye trees of the plain, and ye cedars of Lebanon, dance with joy...

...at the veneration of the life-bearing Cross today: ye Prophets, Martyrs, Apostles, and spirits of the righteous, leap for joy!

*Troparion:* Look down upon Thy people and Thine inheritance, O Lord, who sing to Thee with fear, for whose sake Thou didst endure voluntary death; let not the measureless multitude of our evils overcome Thy tender mercy, but save us all, O Most-good One, by Thy Cross, as Thou art the Lover of mankind!

*Theotokion:* By Thy nod Thou shakest the visible world, yet being crucified Thou hangest suspended, the Theotokos cried aloud with lamentation, desiring to destroy the passionate imaginings of the first-fashioned man, O Christ, and to heal his contrition by Thy goodness!

*Tone 4, Ode 9. Another Heirmos: "Every tongue is at a loss" (Недоꙋмѣ́етъ вся́къ):*
*Ode 9. Another Heirmos:* Elisha of old, drawing the iron axe-head out of the river by wood,[^1554] prefigured thee, O Cross, life-giving Tree, whereby Christ, having been nailed upon thee, drew the nations out of the depth of demonic idolatry: therefore, bowing down before thee, we glorify His dominion!

*Troparion:* The rays of the sun were turned into darkness by Thy crucifixion, O Savior, and the radiance of the moon was taken away, and all the elements were changed with trembling: therefore I cry aloud unto Thee: having transformed my mind that was changed by the gloom of the passions, O Word, illumine and save me by Thy right hand!

*Troparion:* By Thy wound heal the passions of my soul; by the piercing of Thy ribs bring to an end the painful piercings of the demons; by Thy nails, O Christ, nail through my pleasurable and deceitful desires, granting me dispassionately to bow down before Thy precious Passions and Resurrection!

*Theotokion:*

...Whose likeness Thou didst bear for the sake of Thy tender mercy, O Christ: therefore we mortals sing Thy praise unto the ages![^1555]

*Tone 1, Ode 8. Another Heirmos: "The one unoriginate King of glory" (Є҆ди́нагѡ безнача́лнагѡ):*[^1556]
*Ode 8. Another Heirmos:* We honor Thy Cross-bearing Week as worthy of veneration; for bowing down before the Precious Tree within thee, we cry aloud: Sing, ye priests, and exalt [Him] above all unto all ages!

*Troparion:* Show forth Thy marvels, O King of the ages, that Thou hast vouchsafed us, Thy servants, to behold and to bow down before the Tree whereon Thou wast crucified: therefore with fear we sing to Thee unto the ages!

*We bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, the Lord:*
*Trinity Hymn:* O consubstantial, O all-holy Trinity, Father, Son, and Most-holy Spirit, Godhead: I glorify Thine undivided dominion, and I sing to the one Kingdom unto all ages!

*Theotokion:* Him Who created Adam according to His image, and Who came forth from his mingled substance, and Who destroyed the first curse: sing, ye priests, and exalt, ye people, above all unto all ages!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee:*
*Troparion:* O twelve-tubed lute of the Church, singing the Word of simplicity, the choir of Apostles in praise: entreat that we may behold the Passion of the Lord, and sing unto the ages![^1557]

*Katavasia:* The one unoriginate King of glory, Whom the heavenly hosts fear, and the angelic ranks tremble before: sing, ye priests, and exalt Him above all, ye people, unto the ages!

*Tone 1, Ode 9. Heirmos: "Shine, shine" (Свѣти́ся свѣти́ся):*[^1558]
*Ode 9. Heirmos:* Be radiant and shine, O Church of God, with the rays of the Cross, which Thou bearest lying before all the faithful for veneration; and do Thou flee from the all-wicked multitude that is filled with darkness!

*Troparion:* The divine Cross is the strength of abstinence, a helper unto those who watch, confirmation unto fasters, an ally unto those who struggle: drawing near unto it with love, ye faithful, let us joyfully bow down!

*Troparion:* Ye divine foundations of Christ's Church, preserve all by the confirmation of piety, and establish upon the unshakable rock Him Who chose you, O glorious Apostles![^1559]

*Theotokion:* Having received joy by the Archangel's voice,[^1560] do thou now consume the soul-corrupting grief of my heart, O pure one, and grant joy-creating weeping, that there I may find divine consolation!

*Tone 4, Ode 9. Another Heirmos: "Thee, the pure Mother" (Тебѣ̀ чⷭ҇тꙋю Мт҃рь):*[^1561]
*Ode 9. Another Heirmos:* Prefigured of old, thou didst sweeten the waters of Marah, O all-honorable Tree;[^1562] do thou sweeten for me the abstinence of the fast, O Cross of Christ, which art venerated today!

*Troparion:* As an unconquerable weapon of the kingdom, strength unto the army, confirmation unto the senate, O Cross of Christ: all we magnify Thee with hymns!

*Trinity Hymn:* Thee, the unoriginate Father and Master, and the co-unoriginate Word, and the Holy Spirit, piously do all we, the faithful, magnify!

*Theotokion:* Thee, glorious and only Theotokos, who didst contain in thy womb the uncontainable Word, and didst give birth to Him in the flesh: with hymns we magnify!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee:*
