*Troparion:* Thee, the fiery-sounding Apostles, who burned up all the matter of deception, and planted piety in the world: with hymns we magnify!

*Katavasia:* Thee, the pure Mother and Virgin, who didst contain in thy womb the uncontainable Word, and didst give birth to Him in the flesh: with hymns we magnify!

*Then: It is truly meet:*
*Exapostilarion of the Tone:*

*At the Aposticha, Idiomelon Sticheron, Tone 7:*
*Sticheron:* Let us, the faithful, emulate the repentance of the Publican,[^1563] and let us not boast like the Pharisee; but from the depth of the heart let us offer groaning unto God, the Benefactor of all! For He commanded, saying: Whosoever exalts himself shall be humbled, and he that humbles himself shall be exalted.[^1564] Therefore with one mind let us cry aloud unto Him: O God, cleanse us sinners, and save us!

*Verse 1: "We were filled in the morning with Thy mercy, O Lord" (Ps. 89:14 LXX):*
*Martyrion of the same Tone. Verse 2: "And let the brightness of the Lord our God be upon us" (Ps. 89:17 LXX):*
*Martyrion:* Breathing as one, looking unto one thing, the passion-bearing Martyrs, having found one way of life, death for Christ's sake, in their zeal represented death one unto another! O wonder! seizing torments like treasures, they said one to another: Even if we die not now, we shall die in any case, and pay that which is owed unto nature; let us make a necessity into an honor, choosing that which is common unto all, let us purchase life through death! By their intercessions, O God, have mercy on us!

*Glory, both now: Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* Through the intercessions of the Theotokos, make peaceful the life of us who cry aloud: O Merciful Lord, glory to Thee!

*Then: It is good to give praise:*

*On the Same Thursday of Mid-Lent, at the Sixth Hour:*
*Troparion of Prophecy, Tone 6: "Before Thy Cross we bow down in worship, O Master, and Thy holy Resurrection we glorify" (see fol. 525).[^1565]*

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 73, Tone 4: For God is our King of old, He hath wrought salvation in the midst of the earth (Ps. 73:12 LXX):*
*Verse: O God, why hast Thou cast us off unto the end? (Ps. 73:1 LXX):*

*Reading from the Prophecy of Isaiah (Isa. 28:14–22):*[^1566]
Thus saith the Lord: Give ear to the word of the Lord, ye afflicted men, and ye rulers of this people that is in Jerusalem! Because ye have said: We have made a covenant with Hades, and agreements with death; if the rushing storm should pass by, it will not come upon us, for we have made a lie our hope, and with a lie have we covered ourselves. Therefore thus saith the Lord: Behold, I lay in the foundations of Zion a costly, chosen stone, a precious cornerstone in its foundations, and he that believes on Him shall not be put to shame.[^1567] And I will set judgment for hope, and My alms in the balances; and ye that trust vainly in a lie, the storm will not pass you by; and I will not take away the covenant of death, and your hope that is toward Hades will not abide: if the rushing storm should come, ye will be trodden down by it. Whenever it passes by, it will take you; for morning by morning it will pass you by, and in the night there will be an evil hope: learn ye to give ear! Being straitened, we cannot fight, and we ourselves are powerless to gather you, like an ungodly boundary. As in the mountain of them that cut down, the Lord will arise, even as in the valley of Gibeon;[^1568] with wrath He will do His works, works of bitterness; but His wrath will be applied strangely, and His bitterness will be strange. And ye, rejoice not, neither let your bonds strengthen; for I have heard from the Lord of Sabaoth of finished and measured things, which He will accomplish throughout the whole earth.

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 74, Tone 4: But I will rejoice for ever; I will sing to the God of Jacob (Ps. 74:10 LXX):*
*Verse: We will give thanks to Thee, O God, we will give thanks to Thee, and call upon Thy Name (Ps. 74:2 LXX):*

*On the Same Thursday of the Fourth Week, in the Evening, at "Lord, I have cried":*
*Tone 4, Stichera, Podoben: "Thou hast given a sign" (Да́лъ є҆сѝ зна́менїе):*[^1569]
*Sticheron:* Having been vouchsafed, O ye faithful, to kiss Thine ever-blessed Cross, O Lord, whereby Thou hast saved us: we sing the praise of Thy tender mercy, and entreat Thee fervently: grant unto all, O Savior, the joy of Thy salvation, granting us in repentance to behold Thy Resurrection and divine Passions!

*Sticheron:* Stretching Thyself out upon the Cross, Thou didst endure putting to death, Who didst put death to death and didst raise the dead by Thy life-bearing Word! Therefore I pray Thee: bring to life my soul that is put to death by sin, O Lord, granting me contrition and deliverance from evils, in the holy days of Thy fast, O Lover of mankind!

*Tone 4, Another Sticheron by Kyr Theodore, Podoben: "The spiritual diamond" (Раꙁꙋ́мнаѧ):*[^1570]
*Sticheron:* Having been vouchsafed joyfully to behold and to bow down before Thy Precious Cross, we pray Thee, O Jesus our God: vouchsafe us also to reach Thy very Most-pure Passions, strengthened by fasting, as we worship and sing to the Crucifixion, the Spear, the Sponge, and the Reed, whereby Thou hast made us immortal, and hast brought us back again into the former life of sweetness, as Thou art the Lover of mankind: therefore we piously glorify Thee now!

*And to the Menaion, 3.*

*Then, Prokeimenon, Psalm 75, Tone 8: Vow, and pay unto the Lord our God (Ps. 75:12 LXX):*
*Verse: In Judea is God known, His Name is great in Israel (Ps. 75:2 LXX):*

*Reading from Genesis (Gen. 10:32–11:9):*[^1571]
These are the generations of the sons of Noah, according to their genealogies, according to their nations: of them were the islands of the Gentiles divided upon the earth after the deluge. And the whole earth was of one lip, and there was one speech unto all. And it came to pass, as they moved from the east, that they found a plain in the land of Shinar, and dwelt there. And a man said to his neighbor: Come, let us make bricks, and bake them with fire! And the brick was to them for stone, and asphalt was their mortar. And they said: Come, let us build for ourselves a city, and a tower whose top shall reach unto heaven; and let us make a name for ourselves, before we be scattered upon the face of the whole earth! And the Lord came down to see the city and the tower, which the sons of men were building. And the Lord said: Behold, the race is one, and there is one lip unto all, and this have they begun to do; and now nothing will fail them of all that they may desire to do. Come, let Us go down, and there confound their tongues, that each may not understand the speech of his neighbor! And the Lord scattered them from thence upon the face of the whole earth; and they ceased building the city and the tower. Therefore the name of that place was called Confusion [Babel],[^1572] because there the Lord confounded the tongues of the whole earth; and from thence the Lord scattered them upon the face of the whole earth.

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 76, Tone 4: With my voice I cried unto the Lord; with my voice unto God, and He gave ear unto me (Ps. 76:2 LXX):*
*Verse: In the day of my trouble I sought God, with my hands by night before Him, and I was not deceived (Ps. 76:3 LXX):*

*Reading from the Proverbs (Prov. 13:20–14:6):*[^1573]

The desire of the godly sweetens the soul, but the deeds of the ungodly are far from understanding. He that walks with the wise shall be wise, but he that walks with the senseless shall be known. Evils shall pursue sinners, but good things shall overtake the righteous. A good man shall leave an inheritance unto his children's children, and the wealth of the ungodly is laid up for the righteous. The righteous shall spend many years in wealth, but the unrighteous shall perish quickly. He that spares the rod hates his son, but he that loves him chastens him diligently.[^1574] The righteous man eats and satisfies his soul, but the souls of the ungodly are in want. Wise women build houses, but a foolish woman digs them down with her hands. He that walks uprightly fears the Lord, but he that is perverse in his ways shall be dishonored. From the mouth of fools comes a rod of reproach, but the lips of the wise preserve them. Where there are no oxen, the cribs are clean; but where there is much harvest, the strength of the ox is manifest. A faithful witness does not lie, but an unjust witness kindles falsehood. Thou shalt seek wisdom among the evil, and shalt not find it; but knowledge is easy among the prudent.

*Then: Vouchsafe, O Lord:*

*At the Aposticha, Idiomelon Stichera, Tone 6:*
*Sticheron:* Having learned, O my soul, from the Lord Who humbled Himself even unto the Crucifixion and death for thy sake,[^1575] concerning the humiliation of haughtiness and the exaltation of humility: lift not thyself up in virtues, neither accounting thyself righteous...

...condemning thy neighbor, like the boastful Pharisee; but in brokenness of understanding, remembering only thine own transgressions, like the Publican cry aloud: O God, cleanse me a sinner, and have mercy on me!

*Martyrion:* Thy Martyrs, O Lord, did not deny Thee, neither did they depart from Thy commandments: by their intercessions have mercy on us!

*Glory, both now: Tone 6, Cross-Theotokion, Podoben: "Having risen on the third day" (Тре́тїй де́нь):*[^1576]
*Cross-Theotokion:* When the All-immaculate one beheld Thee hanging upon the Cross, she cried aloud: What is this strange mystery that I behold, O My Son? How art Thou Who art suspended upon the Tree dying in the flesh, O Giver of life?

[Headpiece: Ornate foliated Kyivan Lavra woodcut headpiece band]
## On Friday of the Fourth Week of the Holy Fast[^1577]

*At Matins, after Alleluia, Trinity Hymns of the Tone.*
*After the first Stichology, Sessional Hymn from the Octoechos.*
*After the second Stichology, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou Who wast lifted up upon the Cross" (Вознесы́йся на крⷭ҇тъ):*[^1578]
*Sessional Hymn:* Sanctifying the season of abstinence, the all-honorable Cross is seen: bowing down before it today, let us cry aloud: O Master, Lover of mankind, by its assistance grant us to pass through the remaining season of the fast in contrition, and to behold Thy life-bearing Passions, whereby we have been set free!

*Glory, both now: Cross-Theotokion:*
*Cross-Theotokion:* She that bore Thee, Who wast born before all ages of the unoriginate Father and in the end wast born of her in the flesh, O Christ, lamented as she beheld Thee hanging upon the Cross: Woe is me...

...most beloved Jesus!" she cried aloud: "How art Thou, Who art glorified as God by the Angels, now of Thine own will crucified by lawless men? I hymn Thee, O Long-suffering One!"

*After the third Stichology, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Speedily anticipate" (Ско́ро предварѝ):*[^1579]
*Sessional Hymn:* Beholding Thy precious Cross today as the light of our souls, O Christ, and bowing down before it with joy, let us cry aloud: Glory to Thee, Who wast pleased to be lifted up upon it! Glory to Thee, Who hast enlightened all creation because of it, on account of which we unceasingly glorify Thee with hymns!

*Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* When Thy most pure Mother beheld Thee lifted up upon the Cross, O Word of God, sobbing maternally[^1580] she declared: "What is this new and fearful wonder, O My Son? How art Thou, the Life of all, drawing near unto death, desiring to give life unto the dead, as Thou art merciful?"[^1581]

*Psalm 50, and the Canon to the Precious Cross, which is appointed to be sung at Compline:*[^1582]
*Canon, whose Acrostic is: "Let all extol the Tree that is worshipped":*[^1583]
*Ode 1, Tone 8. Heirmos: "Having armed Pharaoh" (Воѡрꙋже́нна Фараѡ́на):*[^1584]
*Troparion:* Drawing near today unto the Cross of the Lord with pure mind and pious understanding, come, let us bow down! For it lies before us, bestowing cleansing and salvation, radiance, glory, and mercy upon those who bow down before it.

*Troparion:* The life-bestowing Cross, lying before us and beheld by our eyes, pours forth the luminous radiance of grace. Come, let us draw near and receive...

...and receive the illumination of gladness, and salvation, and forgiveness, offering praise unto the Lord!

*Troparion:* A marvelous vision lies before those who behold it: the precious Cross, bubbling up like a spring with divine gifts; and it quenches transgressions, dissolves infirmities, and bedews the inward parts of those who approach it with purity.

*Troparion:* The rod that divided the sea prefigured the victory of the Cross,[^1585] whereby we tempest-free sail across the unsteady water of this life, escape all the torrents of sin, and are filled with divine tranquility.

*Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* "When I ineffably gave birth to Thee, O Child, I escaped all pangs; yet how have all pangs now been fulfilled!" cried the all-pure Virgin, weeping: "For I behold Thee hanging upon the Tree like an evildoer, Who didst suspend the earth upon nothing!"[^1586]

*Ode 3. Heirmos: "Thou art the confirmation" (Оу҆твержде́нїе):*[^1587]
*Troparion:* The Cross, the bestower of all good things, is seen and bowed down to, and all creation celebrates with joy, enlightened by the grace of our God, Who of His own will was lifted up upon it.

*Troparion:* Illumined by the light of the rays of the Cross at the mid-point of sacred abstinence, let us flee the darkness of sin, and let us cry aloud: O compassionate Lord, the Enlightenment of all, glory to Thee!

*Troparion:* With hymns we embrace thee, O Cross, and we kiss thee with faith, entreating: Deliver us by thy might from the snares of the enemy, and guide all of us who honor thee unto the haven of salvation!

*Theotokion:*

*Theotokion:* Beholding Life put to death upon the Cross, unable to endure the agony of her womb, the Pure Virgin sobbed and cried aloud: "Woe is me, O My Son! What has the lawless people rendered unto Thee?"

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 6:* No sooner was the Wood of Thy Cross set up, O Christ, than the foundations of death were shaken, O Lord; for whom Hades had eagerly swallowed down, him it released with trembling. Thou hast shown us Thy salvation, O Holy One, and we glorify Thee, O Son of God: have mercy on us!

*Glory, both now: in the same Tone:* Today the prophetic word is fulfilled;[^1588] for behold, we bow down in the place where Thy feet stood, O Lord; and having tasted of the Tree of salvation, we have obtained deliverance from the passions that spring from sins, through the prayers of the Theotokos, O only Lover of mankind!

*Ode 4. Heirmos: "Thou art my strength, O Christ" (Ты́ ми Хрїсте́ Гдⷭ҇ь):*[^1589]
*Troparion:* A mighty protection and setting-aright for men, an unconquerable weapon of faith, the saving Cross is beheld lying before us, and it sanctifies and enlightens in grace the hearts of all who approach with faith.

*Troparion:* Lying before us at the mid-point of abstinence, in the midst of all, the all-good, precious Cross—at the center of the earth,[^1590] upon which Thou wast lifted up of Thine own will, O Lover of mankind—enlightens the world by its veneration and drives away the demonic hosts.

*Troparion:* Heaven and all the earth rejoice together; passion-bearing Martyrs, Apostles, and the souls of the Righteous now make glad with joy, beholding the God-given Tree that saves all lying in the midst, sanctifying the faithful in grace.

*Troparion:* Having failed to keep Thy laws, O Lord, I, covenant-breaker, am destined to be condemned when Thou shalt come, O Son, to judge the deeds of men; therefore I cry unto Thee: By the power of Thy Cross convert me, O Savior, and grant me tears of repentance!

*Theotokion:* "From a virginal womb I gave birth to Thee, O Child; and beholding Thee hanging upon the Tree, I am at a loss, and I comprehend not the height of the mystery and the depth of Thy great judgments!" cried the all-pure one, whom with unceasing voices as the Mother of God we magnify.

*Ode 5. Heirmos: "Why hast Thou cast me off" (Въскꙋ́ю мѧ̀ ѿри́нꙋлъ є҆сѝ):*[^1591]
*Troparion:* Shout aloud, ye nations! Sing and chant, ye peoples, leap for joy unto God Who has given the Cross as an unshakable confirmation, enjoying which now in the season of abstinence, we nourish both soul and mind!

*Troparion:* All the noetic hosts honor thee, O all-precious Cross, and we mortals, bowing down before thee today with clay lips, draw forth sanctification and salvation in love, glorifying Him Who was nailed upon thee!

*Troparion:* Heal the burdensome passions of my soul, O compassionate Lord, and vouchsafe me to be a worshipper of Thy holy Passions; show me to be better through the season of the fast, and grant me departure from evils, O All-good One!

*Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* Beholding Him Who for goodness' sake was born of thee beyond understanding, O all-immaculate one, hanging upon the Cross, thou wast consumed in thy womb and didst say: "Woe is me, O Divine Child, how dost Thou suffer beyond all! I bow down before Thy compassion, O Lord!"

*Triodion. Tone 4, Ode 5. Heirmos: "All things were amazed" (Оу҆диви́шася вся́ческая):*[^1592]
*Troparion:* The luminaries hid their light, beholding Thee, the only Righteous One, nailed unjustly to the Tree, O Long-suffering One, and by Thy might putting to shame the dark powers of the crafty one, O Savior!

*Troparion:* O all-precious Cross, boast of Apostles, weapon of passion-bearers, glory of priests, rampart of the venerable, guardian of all the faithful: preserve and sanctify those who bow down before thee in faith!

*Troparion:* Let us wash our faces with the water of cleansing,[^1593] and let us embrace the Tree, on which the only God of all was lifted up, having clothed Himself in mortal flesh that He might slay him who had slain us!

*Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* When the Virgin Vine beheld the Cluster of Grapes[^1594] Whom she had brought forth hanging upon the Tree, she cried: "O Child, drop down sweetness, destroying the drunkenness of the enemies who crucified Thee, Who art long-suffering throughout the ages!"

*Another Heirmos, in the same Tone: "Rising early from the night" (И҆з но́щи ᲂу҆́треннююще):*[^1595]
*Troparion:* Today Thy Cross lies before us, the Tree of life that is worshipped, and the world rejoices at the visitation of the Spirit, kissing it.

*Troparion:* Beholding Thy Cross lying before us, the heavenly ministers hymn Thee, O Lord, and demons tremble, unable to endure Thy dominion.

*Trinity Troparion:*
*Trinity Troparion:* Let us orthodoxly glorify the Trinity: with the Father and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, one Godhead, a tri-hypostatic Monad.

*Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* We the faithful orthodoxly confess thee to be Mother and Virgin, who ineffably gavest birth to Christ our God, the only Most-merciful One.

*Troparion:* Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee!
O Son of God, Who wast crucified upon the cypress, the pine, and the cedar,[^1596] sanctify us all, and vouchsafe us to behold Thy life-bearing Passion!

*Heirmos:* Enlighten me as I rise early from the night, O life-creating Cross of Christ, as with fear I bow down before thee, ever thirsting for the saving day!

*Ode 6. Heirmos: "Cleanse me, O Savior" (Ѡ҆чи́сти мѧ Сп҃се):*[^1597]
*Troparion:* When the Cross was planted upon the earth, the downfall of the demons came to pass; and beholding it now gloriously lying before us and kissing it, we arise from our sinful falls.

*Troparion:* Exalting Thee, O Christ, as King and Lord, we kiss Thy Cross which Thou hast granted us as an unbreakable rampart, rejoicing at the mid-point of divine abstinence.

*Troparion:* Bestowing great gifts upon us all, the Cross of the Lord is seen lying before us: come, ye mortals, let us receive the enlightenment of heart and soul!

*Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* Strengthen us to fast from all malice, O Pure One, and ever help us to stand aloof from evil and wicked deeds, as thou art the Protectress of all men!

*Tone 7, Automelon: "No longer does the flaming sword" (Не ктомꙋ̀ ᲂу҆же́ пла́менное ѡ҆рꙋ́жїе):*[^1598]
*Kontakion:* No longer does the flaming sword guard the gate of Eden, for upon it came a glorious bond: the Wood of the Cross; the sting of death and the victory of Hades have been driven back; for Thou didst come, O My Savior, crying unto those in Hades: "Enter ye again into Paradise!"

*Ikos:* Three crosses did Pilate plant on Golgotha: two for the thieves, and one for the Giver of life, Whom Hades beheld and said to those below: "O my servants and my power! Who has driven nails into my heart? A wooden spear has suddenly pierced me, and I am torn asunder; I am in pain in my inward parts, and my belly is wounded; my senses consume my spirit, and I am constrained to vomit forth Adam and those with Adam, who were given to me by a tree; for a Tree leads them again into Paradise!"[^1599]

*Ode 7. Heirmos: "The coming down of God" (Бж҃їя сохожде́нїя):*[^1600]
*Troparion:* He Who is before time, bearing flesh in time appears, and heals our temporal passions...

...for goodness' sake in the season of abstinence, wherein the divine Cross lies before us, sanctifying us.

*Troparion:* We hymn, we glorify, we bow down, and we magnify Thy dominion, O Lord, for Thou hast given unto us Thy servants the divine Cross as an unfailing delight, and as the guardian of our souls and bodies.

*Troparion:* Show me not, O Lord, in the day of trial humiliated by evils; cast me not away from Thy presence in shame; but show compassion and save me by Thy precious Cross, as Thou art all-good!

*Troparion:* Moses prefigured thy grace, O Cross, sweetening the bitter waters with a tree;[^1601] for we have been delivered from the bitterness of the passions by thy power. Therefore sweeten us who kiss thee now in contrition of soul!

*Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* By thy prayer, O Lady, who didst crush all the wiles of the adversary, enlarge the narrowness of my mind, and guide me upon the narrow path to walk unto the spaciousness of life, O Mother of God![^1602]

*Ode 8. Heirmos: "Sevenfold" (Се́дмъ седми́цею):*[^1603]
*Troparion:* With a piece of wood of old the divine Elisha drew forth the axe-head from the river,[^1604] prefiguring thee from afar, O all-precious Cross; for from the depth of deception we have been brought up by thee unto sure faith, and we have been vouchsafed to see this present day, and to bow down before thee in faith, embracing salvation!

*Troparion:* Jacob prefigured thee from afar most clearly in his blessings, O all-precious Cross;...

...and having been vouchsafed in grace to behold thee, we all approach with unhesitating faith, and bowing down, we embrace rich blessing, light, salvation, and the remission of sins![^1605]

*Troparion:* Made white by virtuous deeds, come, let us make glad at the mid-point of abstinence, and let us embrace the Cross of the Lord in faith, that guided by its power, we may finish the course with good resolve, and arrive illumined at the divine Passion!

*Trinity Troparion:* Consubstantial, co-unoriginate, co-eternal, co-enthroned, a simple essence yet distinct in Persons: the unbegotten Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit—all of us, hymning this uncreated essence and Godhead, sing: Ye priests, bless; ye people, highly exalt Him unto all ages!

*Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* "Beholding Thee now hanging like a gentle Lamb, nailed to the Cross by the lawless, O My Son Who art before all eternity, I am consumed with weeping and seized by maternal pangs!" cried the all-pure one, whom with unceasing voices we dutifully hymn unto all ages!

*Another Heirmos: "The pious youths" (Ѻ҆́троки бл҃гочти́выя):*[^1606]
*Troparion:* Beholding the Passion of Thee, the Passionless One, creation suffered with Thee, O Long-suffering One: the sun was darkened, the rocks were rent, and all the earth quaked, calling out in fear: "Praise the Lord, ye works, and highly exalt Him unto all ages!"[^1607]

*Troparion:* Rebuke the fierce beasts of passion that afflict me inwardly, O my compassionate God, O Savior Who didst endure dishonorable mockery, struck with a reed, O Christ, desiring to honor all those who had been dishonored by the ancient transgression!

*Troparion:* When I take to mind the fearful judgment seat,...

...O most righteous Judge, I tremble and am appalled with terror, and I lament as I ponder my deeds worthy of condemnation. Therefore let Thy great mercy, O Savior, be entreatable, lest the multitude of my evils overcome Thee!

*Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* "Having given birth to Thee without travail, I am subjected to pangs at Thy crucifixion; my womb is burned within me, for Thou hast been nailed with nails and pierced in the side with a spear, O Long-suffering One!" cried the All-pure Virgin, whom with one accord we hymn as the Theotokos.

*Another Heirmos: "All the works of God" (Вся̑ дѣла̀ Бж҃їя):*[^1608]
*Troparion:* Let the mountains spiritually drop down righteousness, and let the hills rejoice,[^1609] beholding the Wood of the Cross bowed down to, which we highly exalt, O Christ, unto the ages!

*Troparion:* The ends of the earth rejoice at the veneration of Thy Cross, O Lover of mankind; the Angels in the heavens keep festival today, highly exalting Thee, O Christ, unto the ages!

*We bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit: the Lord!*
*Trinity Troparion:* We hymn the unoriginate Father, the Son with the Holy Spirit, praising the consubstantial Trinity, one Principle, and God, singing unto Him piously unto the ages!

*Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* Every earthborn tongue hymns thee, O Theotokos, for thou hast made to dawn the unapproachable Light that enlightens the world, Christ God, Whom we highly exalt ever unto the ages!

*Troparion:* Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee!
Fearful is the grace of Thy Cross, for it casts down the demonic ranks and bestows streams of healings upon men; therefore we hymn Thee, O Christ, unto the ages!

*Heirmos:* Bless the Lord, all ye works of God and all creation; ye venerable and humble in heart, sing, ye peoples, and highly exalt Him unto the ages!

*Ode 9. Heirmos: "Be astonished, therefore" (Оу҆диви́ся ᲂу҆́бѡ):*[^1610]
*Troparion:* Thou hast healed my crushing, O All-good One, being nailed of old upon the Cross with nails in both Thy hands and feet, pierced in the ribs, given vinegar and gall to drink, Thou the gladness of all, sweetness, glory, and eternal redemption!

*Troparion:* Fairer than sapphire and gold, shining like the sun hast thou proved, O divine Cross: while lying circumscribed by place and surrounded with awe on every side by the noetic Powers, yet by the divine rays of thy power thou dost enlighten the fullness of the universe!

*Troparion:* The Cross is a haven for the tempest-tossed, a guide and confirmation for the wandering, the glory of Christ, the strength of Apostles and Prophets, the power of Fasting Ascetics, the refuge of all men: beholding it lying in the midst, let all of us embrace it through abstinence!

*Troparion:* When Thou shalt come upon earth to judge the world which Thou hast created, O Lord,[^1611] with Thine angelic hosts preceding Thee, and the Cross shining forth brighter than the rays of the sun, by its might show compassion upon me and save me, who have fallen beyond all men!

*Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* "Without corruption I gave birth from my womb unto Thee, Whom the Father begat before the ages, and how art Thou subject unto corruption? Men tear Thee asunder, O Son, dig into Thy ribs with a spear, and nail Thy hands and feet inhumanly!" cried the all-pure one, whom worthily we magnify.

*Another Heirmos: "Let every earthborn mortal" (Вся́къ земноро́дный):*[^1612]
*Troparion:* By the Wood of the Cross Thou hast withered the flame of sin, O Christ...

*Troparion (continued):* ...O Christ; and stretching out Thy hands, Thou hast delivered the hands of the combatant, who intemperately stretched out his hands to the eating of the fruit, from whose very tasting Thou didst make him escape, O most merciful Christ!

*Troparion:* Grant us with pure hearts to behold Thy Passion, O Christ, which pours forth dispassion unto all men, as in dispassion we bow down before Thy precious Cross, overlooking our sins, and making us true sons of the Resurrection!

*Troparion:* Thou Who hast raised us up that were fallen into death, and by Thy Resurrection hast destroyed death, and brought us unto Thy Father, pouring out Thy blood for our sake, O Benefactor: therefore we glorify Thee, as our all-powerful God and Deliverer!

*Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* O thou who alone didst give birth to the hypostatic Wisdom of God: make me wise by thy prayers to escape the counsels, snares, and wiles of the crafty one, O Bride unwedded, Virgin Theotokos, firm refuge of the faithful!

*Another Heirmos: "Without seed was the conception" (Безсѣ́менно Рождество̀):*[^1613]
*Troparion:* The precious Cross, which the Angelic hosts embrace, we also, bowing down, do magnify!

*Troparion:* The all-precious Tree, whereby we who were formerly dead have partaken of life, the Cross of the Savior, do we magnify!

*Trinity Troparion:* The unoriginate Father, the co-unoriginate Son, and the co-enthroned Spirit, the Holy Trinity, do we magnify!

*Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* We hymn thee, the unwedded Mother and all-precious Virgin; for without seed hast thou given birth unto the Creator!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee!*
*Troparion:* Having vouchsafed us to behold thee and to bow down before thee, grant us to pass through the remainder of the Passion,[^1614] O Cross of Christ!

*Heirmos: "Without seed was the conception" (Безсѣ́менно рождество̀):*
Without seed was thy conceiving, O pure Theotokos, and ineffable the birth of Christ our God; with unceasing hymns we magnify thee!

*Then: "It is truly meet to bless thee:" The Photagogicon.*

*At the Aposticha: Stichera Idiomela, Tone 4:*[^1615]
*Sticheron:* O Lord, Possessor of truth and Beholder of secret things, Who didst condemn the Pharisee overcome by vainglory and justifying himself by deeds of virtue, and didst justify the Publican praying with contrition and condemned by him:[^1616] show us also to be emulators of his repentance, O Thou Who wast crucified for our sake, and vouchsafe unto us remission, as Thou art the Lover of mankind! *(Twice)*

*The customary Verses. Verse: We have been filled in the morning with Thy mercy, O Lord, and we have rejoiced and been glad in all our days [Ps. 89:14 LXX].*
*For the Martyrs:*
*Sticheron:* Who does not marvel, O holy Martyrs, beholding the good contest wherein ye struggled?[^1617] How, being in the flesh, ye conquered the bodiless foe, confessing Christ and arming yourselves with the Cross! Therefore worthily have ye been revealed as expellers of demons and champions against barbarians; unceasingly pray that our souls may be saved!

*Glory... Both now... Tone 8:*
*Doxasticon:* Today the Master of creation and Lord of glory is nailed upon the Cross, and is pierced in the side;[^1618] the sweetness of the Church tastes gall and vinegar![^1619] He Who covers the heaven with clouds is crowned with thorns; He is robed in a purple garment of mockery; and He Who formed man with His hand is struck by a mortal hand! He Who robes the heaven with clouds is beaten upon His back; He receives spittings and wounds, mockery and reproaches; and all these things my Deliverer and God endures for the sake of me, the condemned, that He may save the world from deception, as He is tender-hearted!

*Then: "It is good to give praise unto the Lord:" and the rest. The First Hour, and the Dismissal.*

*ON THE SAME FRIDAY OF THE MID-LENT WEEK, AT THE SIXTH HOUR.*

*Troparion of the Prophecy, Tone 6:* Before Thy Cross we bow down, O Master, and Thy holy Resurrection we glorify![^1620]

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 77, Tone 6: But He is full of compassion, and will forgive their sins [Ps. 77:38 LXX].[^1621] Verse: Give ear, O My people, to My law [Ps. 77:1 LXX].*

*Reading from the Prophecy of Isaiah (Chapter 29):*[^1622]
Thus says the Lord: These people draw near unto Me with their mouth, and with their lips they honor Me, but their heart is far from Me; and in vain do they worship Me, teaching the commandments and doctrines of men. Therefore, behold, I will proceed to alter this people, and I will alter them; and I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and will hide the understanding of their prudent ones. Woe unto them that seek deep counsel, and not through the Lord! They that take counsel in secret, and their works shall be in darkness; and they say: "Who has seen us? And who knows us, or what we do?" Shall ye not be esteemed as the clay of the potter? Shall the work say of Him that made it: "Thou madest me not"? Or shall the thing framed say of Him that framed it: "Thou hast made me without understanding"? Is it not yet a very little while, and Lebanon shall be turned into Mount Carmel, and Carmel shall be esteemed as a forest? And in that day shall the deaf hear the words of the book, and they that are in darkness, and they that are in mist, even the eyes of the blind shall see. And the poor shall rejoice because of the Lord in gladness, and the hopeless among men shall be filled with joy. For the lawless one has vanished, and the proud has perished, and they that commit iniquity in malice are cut off; and they that make men to sin in word, and lay a stumbling-block for all that reprove in the gates, having turned aside the righteous in unrighteousness. Therefore thus says the Lord concerning the house of Jacob, whom He separated from Abraham: Jacob shall not now be ashamed, neither shall the face of Israel now change; but when their children see My works, for My sake they shall sanctify My Name, and shall sanctify the Holy One of Jacob, and shall fear the God of Israel.

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 78, Tone 6: Help us, O God our Savior [Ps. 78:9 LXX].[^1623] Verse: O God, the heathen are come into Thine inheritance [Ps. 78:1 LXX].*

*Then the Reading:*
*If not, then: "Speedily anticipate" (Ско́ро предварѝ).*[^1624]

*After the Sixth Hour, we make the Trisagion; and we bow down before the Precious Cross, singing the Stichera in Tone 2:*
*Come, ye faithful, let us bow down to the life-creating Wood (appointed on the Third Sunday of Holy Lent; see fol. 524v)[^1625]. And the Precious Cross is taken up, and they carry it into the Sacristy.*[^1626]

*ON THE SAME FRIDAY EVENING.*
*The customary service, as was directed on Wednesday of the Fourth Week of Holy Lent (see fol. 234r)[^1627].*

*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera on 10. Sticheron Idiomelon, Tone 7:*[^1628]
*Sticheron:* Having enslaved the dignity of my soul to the passions, I have become as a beast, and cannot look up unto Thee, the Most High;

*Sticheron (continued):* ...but bowing down low, O Christ, like the Publican I pray, crying unto Thee: O God, cleanse me and save me! *(Twice)*

*Then 4 Stichera for the Martyrs, in order of the Tone from the Octoechos.*
*From the Menaion of the saint, 3 Stichera, making 4. Glory... Idiomelon for the departed by Kyr John, in the present Tone.[^1629] Both now... Theotokion from the First Kathisma of the same Tone in the Octoechos. Then: "O Gladsome Light:"*

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 79, Tone 4: Give ear, O Shepherd of Israel, Thou that leadest Joseph like a sheep [Ps. 79:2 LXX].[^1630] Verse: Thou that sittest upon the Cherubim, show Thyself [Ps. 79:1 LXX].*

*Reading from Genesis (Chapter 12):*[^1631]
The Lord God said unto Abram: "Get thee out of thy land, and from thy kindred, and from the house of thy father, and come into the land that I will show thee. And I will make of thee a great and numerous nation, and I will bless thee, and magnify thy name, and thou shalt be blessed. And I will bless them that bless thee, and curse them that curse thee; and in thee shall all the tribes of the earth be blessed." And Abram departed, as the Lord had spoken unto him; and Lot went with him. And Abram was seventy and five years old when he departed out of Haran. And Abram took Sarai his wife, and Lot the son of his brother, and all their substance that they had acquired, and every soul which they had gotten in Haran; and they went forth to go into the land of Canaan; and they entered into the land of Canaan. And Abram passed through the land along its breadth, unto the place of Shechem, unto the lofty oak.

And the Canaanites then dwelt in that land. And the Lord appeared unto Abram, and said unto him: "Unto thy seed will I give this land." And there Abram built an altar unto the Lord, Who had appeared unto him.

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 80, Tone 4: Rejoice in God our Helper [Ps. 80:2 LXX].[^1632] Verse: Take a psalm, and bring the timbrel [Ps. 80:3 LXX].*

*Reading from Proverbs (Chapter 14):*[^1633]
The innocent believes every word, but the prudent man comes unto reflection. A wise man, having feared, turns away from evil; but the foolish, trusting in himself, mingles with the lawless. A hasty man acts without counsel, but a prudent man endures many things. The foolish shall distribute malice, but the prudent shall retain knowledge. The evil shall stumble before the good, and the ungodly shall wait at the gates of the righteous. Friends will hate poor friends, but the friends of the rich are many. He that dishonors the poor commits sin, but he that has mercy on the poor is blessed. The unrighteous, going astray, devise evil; but the good devise mercy and truth. The workers of evil understand neither mercy nor faith; but alms and faith are with the workers of good. In every one that is careful there is abundance; but the voluptuous and painless shall be in want. The crown of the wise is their riches, but the abode of fools is evil. A faithful witness will deliver a soul from evils, but a deceitful man kindles lies. In the fear of the Lord is strong confidence, and to His children He will leave a remnant of peace.

*Then: "Let my prayer be set forth:" And the rest, as is written on the First Sunday of Holy Lent (see fol. 234r).*
*If we do not celebrate the Presanctified Liturgy, see the rubrics on fol. 421r.[^1634]*
*Only at the Aposticha: Glory... to the saint of the temple. Both now... Theotokion, Tone 6: "Thou art our God:" Seek in the Second Saturday of Lent, at Matins, at Sticheron 4.[^1635]*
*If the feast of the Holy Forty Martyrs, or the Five Martyrs, or the Annunciation should occur, at Matins we do not say the hymns for the departed. For the rest of the rubrics, see fol. 288r, 412r, and 498r.[^1636]*

## ON SATURDAY OF THE FOURTH WEEK (OF MID-LENT)[^1637]

*AT MATINS, the service is sung as in the preceding Saturdays (see fol. 413r).*
*Only after "Alleluia," Glory... Troparion to the saint, if he has one. Both now... Theotokion.*

*THE FOUR-ODE CANON, BY KYR JOSEPH. TONE 4.*
*The Acrostic is thus: "A Song unto the Martyrs."*[^1638]
*Ode 6, Tone 4. Heirmos: "In the surge of the sea of life" (Въ пꙋчи́нѣ жите́йстѣй):*[^1639]
*For the Martyrs:*
*Troparion:* Ye passed beyond the bounds of the flesh, O Passion-bearers, by much endurance, having endured torments and afflictions; therefore do ye lighten every disease and affliction of those that praise you!

*Troparion:* The host of the holy Passion-bearers joined the myriads of Angels, *Troparion (continued):* ...and they pray the All-good God to deliver us from many transgressions, as those well-pleasing unto Christ!

*For the Departed:*
*Troparion:* Having died and slept in the tomb, O Christ, Thou hast raised the dead; and unto those that have reposed in faith Thou dost grant the wealth of Thy grace, O Christ: rest with all the saints!

*Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* God the Word of God, Who desires to bring man to life, is incarnate of thee, O pure one, and is seen as earthly; unceasingly pray Him that we may find mercy at the time of the answer!

*Another Canon, by Kyr Theodore. Tone 4, Ode 6. Heirmos: "Tossed by the tempest of sins" (Согрѣше́нїй бꙋ́рею):*[^1640]
*For the Martyrs:*
*Troparion:* Having beheld the triumph of the Martyrs, let us be enlightened by deeds, and let us cry out with divinely inspired hymns: "Ye are truly the dayspring upon earth, O Martyrs of Christ!"

*Troparion:* Not sparing flesh and blood, O holy ones, ye stood without fear against every torment, not denying Christ; therefore from the heavens has Christ sent down crowns upon you!

*Trinity Troparion:* O Holy Trinity, I glorify Thee, unoriginate Essence, one God and one Lord, three Persons: Father, Son, and Spirit; unbegotten, begotten, and proceeding; uncreated and co-eternal!

*Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* O blessed Bride of God, how didst thou give birth without a husband, and dost remain even as before? For thou hast brought forth God, an awesome wonder! But pray that they who hymn thee may be saved!

*Verse: Wondrous is God in His saints, the God of Israel [Ps. 67:36 LXX].[^1641]*
*For the Martyrs:*
*Troparion:* Beholding the severance of your limbs, ye take delight in the blood, rejoicing; but diligently pray the Lord for us, O ever-glorious Martyrs!

*Verse: Their soul shall dwell among good things [Ps. 24:13 LXX].[^1642]*

*For the Departed:*
*Troparion:* O Thou Who didst fashion me from the earth, and didst give me life, and didst say unto me that I should return again unto the earth: grant rest unto Thy servants whom Thou hast taken, and deliver them from the corruption of death, O Lord!

*Heirmos: "Tossed by the tempest of sins" (Согрѣше́нїй бꙋ́рею):*
Tossed by the tempest of transgressions, as in the belly of the sea monster I am held fast; with the Prophet I cry unto Thee: Bring up my life from corruption, O Lord, and have mercy on me!

*Kontakion of the Temple.*

*Ode 7, Tone 4. Heirmos: "When the golden image was worshipped" (Ѻ҆́бразꙋ зла́томꙋ):*[^1643]
*For the Martyrs:*
*Troparion:* Having clothed yourselves in divine incorruption by the stripping off of corruptible flesh, O Passion-bearers, ye now stand radiant before Him Who for our sake received flesh from an incorrupt woman; therefore clothe me in a pure garment, who have been stripped bare by malice!

*Troparion:* O company of Passion-bearers that lived in abstinence, do ye unhindered strengthen us to endure the course of abstinence, as ye proclaimed Christ manfully in the judgment hall, and now stand crowned before the Judge in spiritual delight with the Angels!

*For the Departed:*
*Troparion:* By the prayers of Thy holy Martyrs, O God, grant rest in faith unto those that have fallen asleep; show them to be citizens of Paradise, and vouchsafe them Thy spiritual light, as they unceasingly cry unto Thee: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* Thee alone, the good one, do we pray, O Virgin: bless us who are afflicted, and diligently pray Christ, Who is good by nature, that we may complete the time of abstinence doing good deeds, as we sing unto Him: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Another Canon, by Kyr Theodore. Ode 7, Tone 4. Heirmos: "Thou Who didst speak on the Mountain" (Гла́сый на Горѣ̀):*[^1644]
*For the Martyrs:*
*Troparion:* Thou Who hast magnified all Thy saints, having made them marvelous with signs in the world: blessed art Thou unto the ages, O Lord God of our fathers!

*Troparion:* Having passed through every form of wounds, and not consenting to bow the knee to Baal,[^1645] ye received crowns of glory from God, O Martyrs of Christ!

*Trinity Troparion:* In a Unity, O Trinity, an Essence worshipped, Father, Son, and Spirit: preserve those who hymn Thee, O God of our fathers!

*Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* O Virgin Mother, all-radiant Maiden, sole Mediatress with God: cease not, O Lady, to pray that we may be saved!

*Verse: Unto the saints that are in His earth has the Lord made wonderful all His desires in them [Ps. 15:3 LXX].[^1646]*
*For the Martyrs:*
*Troparion:* Having soldiered for the immortal King, and having shown perfect faith in Him, ye poured out your blood for His sake, O Martyrs; pray Him that we may be saved!

*Verse: Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen and taken to Thyself, O Lord [Ps. 64:5 LXX].[^1647]*
*For the Departed:*
*Troparion:* Rank the souls of those whom Thou hast taken with the righteous, O compassionate and merciful One; and unto those that have sinned, grant forgiveness, O God!

*Heirmos: "Thou Who didst speak on the Mountain" (Гла́вый на Горѣ̀):*[^1648]
Thou Who didst speak on the Mountain with Moses, and didst show forth the bush as a type of the Virgin: blessed art Thou unto the ages, O Lord God of our fathers!

*Ode 8, Tone 4. Heirmos: "In the flaming fire" (Въ ѻ҆́гни пла́меннѣ):*[^1649]
*For the Martyrs:*
*Troparion:* O renowned Passion-bearers of Christ, and honored in God: from great transgressions and from the torments yonder, deliver all of us who celebrate your memory, by your great prayers unto Him!

*Troparion:* The holy-chosen and truly firm army of Christ God, the companies of Martyrs: cleanse our mind and hearts throughout all these holy days of the fast, by your holy prayers!

*For the Departed:*
*Troparion:* Deliver from the tormenting worm, and from the gnashing of teeth, and from the outer unillumined darkness, O Lord,[^1650] all those whom Thou hast received in faith; and appoint them where the light of Thy countenance, O Christ, shines unto the ages!

*(fol. 550)*
*Theotokion:* Having beheld the precious Cross of Christ, O pure Theotokos, and having venerated it from the heart, vouchsafe us by thy prayers unto the Master to behold the precious Passions, cleansed from passions!

*Another Canon, by Kyr Theodore. Tone 4, Ode 8. Heirmos: "The earth and all that is therein" (Землѧ̀ и҆ всѧ̀ ꙗ҆́же):*[^1651]
*For the Martyrs:*
*Troparion:* O fair assembly, ye found life through death, O holy martyrs of Christ, in no wise fearing fire and sword, frost and wild beasts, and crying aloud: "Sing unto the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto all ages!"

*Troparion:* On high the angelic choir, and below we the earthborn, praise the marvelous sufferings and the struggles of your courage, O Martyrs of Christ, blessing, singing unto the Lord, and exalting Him above all unto the ages!

*Trinity Troparion:* Light and Life do I revere Thee, Father, and Son, and proceeding Spirit: one essence, three Persons, singing of the one God; I bless Thee, I sing unto Thee, O Lord, and I exalt Thee above all unto all ages!

*Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* Who among the earthborn sings not of thee, O undefiled, pure dove? For thou hast given birth for us to the great Light, the Wealth of life, Jesus the Savior, Whom praising we sing as Lord, and exalt above all unto all ages!

*Verse: Wondrous is God in His saints, the God of Israel [Ps. 67:36 LXX].[^1652]*
*For the Martyrs:*
*Troparion:* Glorifying your marvelous struggles, O Martyrs, we bless and worship God the Benefactor, Who strengthened you in the arena of contests and showed you forth as crown-bearers; we exalt Him above all unto the ages!

*Verse: Their soul shall dwell among good things [Ps. 24:13 LXX].[^1653]*
*For the Departed:*
*Troparion:* As Thou art the Lord of life and death, O God, gently raising up those who have departed, *(fol. 551)*
settle them, O Merciful One, in the dwellings of the righteous, who bless and sing unto Thee, O Lord, and exalt Thee above all unto all ages!

*Heirmos: "The earth and all that is therein" (Землѧ̀ и҆ всѧ̀ ꙗ҆́же на не́й):*
The earth and all that is on it, the sea and all springs, the heaven of heavens, light and darkness, frost and heat, ye sons of men, ye priests: bless the Lord and exalt Him above all unto all ages!

*Ode 9, Tone 4. Heirmos: "For He that is mighty has done to me" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ сотвори́ мнѣ̀):*[^1654]
*For the Martyrs:*
*Troparion:* Being unbeguiling luminaries, O Passion-bearers of Christ, enlighten our thoughts, strengthen us to do the radiant and pure wills of God!

*Troparion:* Ye are seen as weapons slaying enemies, O noble Passion-bearers of Christ; but deliver us from the arrows of the evil one by your protection!

*For the Departed:*
*Troparion:* Give rest, O compassionate One, in the bosom of Abraham, unto Thy servants who have departed from us in faith unto Thee, the tenderhearted Creator and most good!

*Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* Put to death the stirrings of my flesh, O thou who beyond understanding didst bear God in the flesh, and grant enlightenment to my thought, who art the pure cloud of Light!

*Another Canon, by Kyr Theodore. Tone 4, Ode 9. Heirmos: "Let us all magnify" (Возвели́чимъ всѝ):*[^1655]
*For the Martyrs:*
*Troparion:* We all hymn your memories, O all-praised Martyrs, beholding the struggles of your sacred passions, and we magnify Christ Who has done marvelous things!

*Troparion:* As they suffered, the Passion-bearers said one to another: "Let us not spare the flesh; come, let us die for Christ, that we may live unto all ages, rejoicing unceasingly!"

*Trinity Troparion:* Preserve unharmed by Thy mercy those who hymn Thee, the Trinity in one essence, O unbegotten Father, and begotten Son, and proceeding Spirit!

*Theotokion:*

*(fol. 552)*
*Theotokion:* Rejoice, all-honored, pure one, boast of virginity, confirmation of mothers, help of men, and joy of the world, Mary, Mother and handmaid of our God!

*Verse: Wondrous is God in His saints, the God of Israel [Ps. 67:36 LXX].[^1656]*
*For the Martyrs:*
*Troparion:* O choir of saints, accept my prayer, and as thou hast vouchsafed me to kiss the Cross and to venerate the saving Passion, pray Christ!

*Verse: Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen and taken to Thyself, O Lord [Ps. 64:5 LXX].[^1657]*
*For the Departed:*
*Troparion:* Remit, pardon, O compassionate One, those who have passed over unto Thee, the Lover of mankind, and give them rest in the dwellings of the elect; for Thou art the Life and Resurrection!

*Heirmos: "Let us all magnify" (Возвели́чимъ всѝ):*
Let us all magnify Thy love for mankind, O Lord our Savior, glory of Thy servants, and crown of the faithful, Who hast magnified the memory of her who bore Thee!

*Then: "It is truly meet to bless thee."*
*Exapostilarion: "Heaven with stars" (Нб҃о ѕвѣзда́ми): and for the saint, if he has one. All the rest as we have indicated (see fol. 420).[^1658]*
*Then at the Liturgy: the Epistle and Gospel. Pericope 313 [Heb. 6:9-12]: "Brethren, we are persuaded of better things of you." And for the reposed, to the Corinthians, Pericope 163 [1 Cor. 15:47-57]: "Brethren, the first man is of the earth." Gospel of Mark: Pericope 31 [Mark 7:31-37]: "At that time, Jesus departed from the borders of Tyre..."*[^1659]

[Woodcut tailpiece: An ornate engraving featuring a cherub's face surrounded by acanthus foliage and decorative flourishes.]

*(fol. 601)*
[Woodcut illustration: The Ladder of Divine Ascent of our Venerable Father John Climacus, engraved by Master Ilia (inscribed with monogram "ILIA AZ" and date "1640" [AXM]). At the top in the heavens, Christ welcomes and crowns the monks ascending the ladder; winged demons drag falling ascetics down with hooks into the gaping maw of Hades; at the bottom left, the monastic brotherhood stands before the monastery labeled "Holy Ladder" (СТ҃А ЛѢ́СТВ).][^1660]

## THE FOURTH SUNDAY OF THE HOLY FAST

*On Saturday evening, after the customary psalmody [kathisma]:*
*Resurrection stichera, 3; and Anatolian, 4; and of the Menaion, 3. But some more recent [typika] have appointed the service of St. John Climacus to be sung.*[^1661]

*Tone 8, Podoben: "O most marvelous wonder" (Ѡ҆ пресла́вное чꙋ́до):*[^1662]
*Sticheron 1:* O venerable Father John, thou didst truly bear the praises of God continually in thy throat [Ps. 149:6 LXX], meditating all-wisely on the most practical, divinely inspired words; and from the grace flowing thence thou hast been enriched, becoming blessed, casting down the counsels of all the ungodly!

*(fol. 602)*
*Sticheron 2:* O all-glorious Father John, having cleansed thy soul with fountains of tears, and having propitiated God by all-night vigils, thou didst soar on wings unto the love of His blessed beauty, which now thou dost worthily enjoy, endlessly rejoicing with thy fellow ascetics, O God-bearing venerable one!

*Sticheron 3:* O venerable Father John, having borne aloft thy mind unto God by faith, thou didst abhor the unstable confusion of the world; and having taken up thy cross, thou didst follow the All-seeing One, subjecting the unbridled body to the Divine Spirit through the struggles of discipline by steadfastness of thought!

*Glory: Tone 5:*
*Doxasticon:* O venerable Father, having heeded the voice of the Gospel of the Lord, thou didst forsake the world, counting wealth and glory as naught. Whence thou didst cry aloud unto all: "Love God, and ye shall find eternal grace; prefer nothing before His love, so that when He comes in His glory, ye may find rest with all the saints; by whose prayers, O Christ, preserve and save our souls!"

*Both now... Dogmatic Theotokion 1 of the same Tone [Tone 5].*
*At the Aposticha: stichera from the Octoechos. Glory: For the Venerable One, idiomelon, Tone 2:*
*Sticheron:* Let us honor John: an angel on earth and a man of God in the heavens, the adornment of the world, the enjoyment of good things, the boast of ascetic virtues! For planted in the house of God he blossomed righteously, and like a cedar in the wilderness, he multiplied the flocks of Christ's rational sheep in holiness and righteousness![^1663]

*Both now... Theotokion of the same Tone: "O new wonder" (Ѡ҆ чꙋдесѝ но́вомꙋ): (see fol. 304).[^1664] Now lettest Thou depart [Nunc Dimittis]:*

*(fol. 603)*
*Troparion, Tone 4:*
*Troparion:* A citizen of the wilderness, an angel in the flesh, and a wonderworker hast thou been shown to be, O John our Father! Having received heavenly gifts through fasting, vigilance, and prayer, thou healest the diseased and the souls of those who come unto thee in faith. Glory to Him Who gave thee strength! Glory to Him Who crowned thee! Glory to Him Who works healings for all through thee!

*Mark Chapter: If a martyr falls on the 4th or 5th Sunday of Lent:*[^1665]
*On Saturday evening, at Small Vespers: At "Lord, I have cried": Resurrection stichera as usual, in both Tones. At the Aposticha: one Resurrection sticheron, and the Aposticha stichera of the saint from Great Vespers with their verses. Glory: to the saint. Both now: Theotokion, and Dismissal.*
*At Great Vespers: the entire Kathisma, "Blessed is the man." At "Lord, I have cried": Resurrection stichera, 3; and Anatolian, 1; and for the saints, on 6. Glory: to the saint. Both now: Dogmatic Theotokion of the Tone. Entrance. Readings for the saints.*
*At the Litiya: the sticheron of the patron of the temple, and the stichera of the saint which are at the Aposticha. At the Aposticha: Resurrection stichera. Glory: to the saints. Both now: Theotokion from the alphabetical [stichera] according to the Tone of the verse. At the blessing of the loaves: Troparion, "Theotokos Virgin," twice; and for the saints, once; and reading from the Epistles of the Apostles.*
*At "God is the Lord": Resurrection Troparion, twice. Glory: to the saints. Both now: Resurrection Theotokion according to the Tone of the Troparion of the saints. After the kathismata: Resurrection Sessional Hymns with their Theotokia, and reading from the Commentary Gospel; and the Evlogitaria [Amomos] with their troparia. Hypakoe of the Tone, and reading from the Gospel. Polyeleos; Sessional Hymns of the saints, twice. Glory, both now: Theotokion; and reading for the saints. Hymns of Ascent of the Tone. Prokeimenon. Resurrection Gospel. Psalm 50. Glory: Sticheron, Tone 8: "Open the doors of repentance" (Покая́нїѧ ѿве́рзи ми), and the rest. Canons: Resurrection on 4; and in the Triodion on 4; and for the Martyrs on 6. [Or thus: Resurrection Canon on 4; and for the Theotokos on 4; and both canons for the Martyrs on 8.][^1666] Katavasia: "I shall open my mouth" (Ѿве́рзꙋ ᲂу҆ста̀). After Ode 3: Sessional Hymns of the saints, twice. Glory, both now: Theotokion; and reading for the martyrs. After Ode 6: Kontakion of the saints, and Ikos. After Ode 9: Resurrection Exapostilarion. Glory: for the Martyrs. Both now: Resurrection Theotokion.*
*At the Praises: Resurrection stichera, 4; and for the saints, 4, with the Doxasticon, with their verses. Then verse: "Arise, O Lord my God" [Ps. 9:33 LXX]; and in the Triodion, idiomelon sticheron. Glory: the same. Both now: "Most blessed art thou." Great Doxology. Resurrection Troparion only, litany, and Dismissal.*
*And procession to the narthex. Glory, both now: Gospel Sticheron. And First Hour: Resurrection Troparion. Glory: for the Martyrs. Both now: Theotokion of the Hours. After "Our Father": Kontakion of the martyrs, and final Dismissal. At the Liturgy: The Beatitudes of the Tone, on 6; and for the saints, Ode 3 on 4. And the rest of the service is of the Resurrection and of the saints.*

*(fol. 604)*
*By this rubric the service is sung whenever a martyr falls, or the Finding of the Head of John the Forerunner, or of a great saint, or the patron feast of the temple, also on the 5th Sunday of the Fast (see fol. 421).[^1667]*

*Mark Chapter 84: If the Annunciation of the Most Holy Theotokos falls on the 4th or 5th Sunday of Lent:*[^1668]

*On Saturday evening, at Small Vespers: At "Lord, I have cried": Stichera of the feast, on 4, Tone 4, Podoben: "Being called from on high" (Зва́ный свы́шше):[^1669] Sticheron 1: "Having mercy on creation"; twice. Sticheron 2: "A strange thing it is"; Sticheron 3: "In Nazareth now." Glory, both now: Tone 4: "In the sixth month." At the Aposticha: stichera of the feast, Tone 2, Podoben: "O most marvelous wonder" (Ѡ҆ пресла́вное): Sticheron 1: "The Prince of the heavenly powers"; verse or refrain: "Proclaim the good tidings from day to day of the salvation of God" [Ps. 95:2 LXX]. Sticheron 2: "What is this fiery vision of thine?"; Refrain 2: "Sing unto the Lord a new song" [Ps. 95:1 LXX]. Sticheron 3: "The Holy Spirit of God." Glory, both now: Tone 4: "In the sixth month." After the Trisagion: Troparion of the feast, Tone 4: "Today is the fountainhead of our salvation." Little Litany, and Dismissal.*

*At Great Vespers: After the Evening Psalm [Psalm 103]: "Blessed is the man," the entire Kathisma. At "Lord, I have cried": Resurrection stichera, 3; and Anatolian, 1; and of the feast, 6. Glory: Tone 6: "The Archangel Gabriel was sent." Both now: Dogmatic Theotokion of Tone 1. Entrance. Prokeimenon of the day. Readings of the feast, 3: First: "Moses went into the tent" [Ex. 3:1-8]; Second: "The Lord created Me" [Prov. 8:22-30]; Third: "It shall come to pass from the eighth day" [Ezek. 43:27-44:4].[^1670] At the Litiya: Stichera of the feast, all. At the Aposticha: Resurrection stichera. Glory, both now: for the feast, Tone 4: "Today is the joy of the Annunciation." At the blessing of the loaves: Troparion of the feast, thrice; and reading from the Epistles of the Apostles.*

*At Matins: At "God is the Lord": Resurrection Troparion, twice. Glory, both now: of the feast. After the kathismata: Resurrection Sessional Hymns with their Theotokia, and reading from the Commentary Gospel. Then the Evlogitaria [Amomos]. Hypakoe of the Tone, and reading from the Gospel. Polyeleos; and Sessional Hymns of the feast, all once; and reading for the feast. Hymns of Ascent of the Tone. Prokeimenon and Gospel of the feast. "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ." Psalm 50. Sticheron of the feast. Canon: Resurrection with Theotokion on 6, and of the feast on 8. Katavasia: Heirmos of the feast, both choirs together. After Ode 3: Sessional Hymns of the feast. After Ode 6: Kontakion of the feast and Ikos, and reading in the Prologue. At Ode 9: We sing "More honorable." Exapostilaria: Resurrection and of the feast. At the Praises: stichera on 8: Resurrection, 4; and of the feast, sung on 4: With end-rhymed acrostics: "The co-eternal Word"; "Gabriel to the Virgin"; "The transcendent Word." And the Sticheron of the feast appointed for Glory: we sing it with the verse: "Proclaim the good tidings from day to day of the salvation of our God," Tone 2: "The mystery from all eternity." We sing the verse: "Arise, O Lord my God, let Thy hand be lifted up" [Ps. 9:33 LXX], and we sing the idiomelon of the day from the Triodion. Glory: the same again. Both now: "Most blessed art thou." Great Doxology. After the Trisagion: Little Entrance with the Gospel...*

*(fol. 605)*
*...with the Gospel. Resurrection Troparion. Glory: the end [of the Troparion]. Both now: of the feast. Prokeimenon of the Tone. Resurrection Gospel. Litany: "Let us all say," and Dismissal. And holy oil is given unto the brethren from the lamp of the Holy Theotokos, while we sing the idiomelon sticheron of the feast. Glory: the Gospel Sticheron. Both now: of the feast. First Hour, and Dismissal.*

*At the First Hour during the day, the klepalo is struck;[^1671] and having gathered together, we go forth with the Litiya outside the monastery. Upon returning, we sing the Hours, and we say the Troparion and Kontakion of the feast.*

*At the Liturgy: The Beatitudes of the Tone on 6, and of the feast, Ode 3 on 4. At the Entrance we say the verse, Tone 4: "Proclaim the good tidings from day to day of the salvation of our God." We sing the Resurrection Troparion and of the feast. Glory, both now: Kontakion of the feast, and the Trisagion. Prokeimenon and Epistle, Alleluia, Gospel and Communion Verse: first of the Sunday, and then of the feast.*

*If the Synaxis of the Archangel Gabriel falls on this 4th Sunday or on the 5th of Lent:*[^1672]

*On Saturday evening, at Small Vespers, as usual. At Great Vespers: the first Kathisma, "Blessed is the man," all. At "Lord, I have cried": Stichera: Resurrection, 3; and Anatolian, 1; and of the feast, 3; and for the Archangel, 3. Glory: of the feast: "The Archangel Gabriel was sent." Both now: Dogmatic Theotokion of Tone 1. At the Litiya: for the saint whose temple it is, and of the feast, 3, Tone 4, which are at the Aposticha. Glory, both now: Tone 2: "Gabriel proclaims the good tidings." At the Aposticha: Resurrection stichera. Glory, both now: of the feast, Tone 4: "Today is the joy." At the blessing of the loaves: Troparion: "Theotokos Virgin," thrice; and reading from the Epistles.*

*At Matins: At "God is the Lord": Resurrection Troparion, twice. Glory, both now: of the feast. After both kathismata: Resurrection Sessional Hymns with their Theotokia, and the Evlogitaria [Amomos]. Hypakoe. Hymns of Ascent of the Tone. Prokeimenon: of the Resurrection. "Let every breath." Resurrection Gospel, and the rest. Canons: Resurrection on 4; and of the feast on 6; and for the Archangel on 4. Katavasia: of the feast. After Ode 3: Kontakion and Sessional Hymn for the Archangel. Glory, both now: of the feast. After Ode 6: Kontakion of the feast. At Ode 9 we sing "More honorable." Exapostilarion: Resurrection. Glory: for the Archangel. Both now: of the feast. At the Praises: Resurrection, 4; and of the feast, 3; and the idiomelon of the feast with its verse, Tone 8: "Let the heavens rejoice." Then verse: "Arise, O Lord my God" [Ps. 9:33 LXX]; and the idiomelon of the day. Glory: the same. Both now: "Most blessed art thou." Great Doxology. Resurrection Troparion, litany, and the catechesis of Theodore the Studite; and Dismissal. The customary procession. Glory, both now: Gospel Sticheron; and First Hour in the narthex.*

*At the Hours: Resurrection Troparion. Glory: of the feast. Both now: Theotokion of the Hours. After "Our Father": Kontakion of the feast. At the Liturgy: The Beatitudes of the Tone on 6, and of the feast, Ode 4 on 4. After the Entrance: Resurrection Troparion and of the feast. Glory, both now: Kontakion of the feast. Prokeimenon and Epistle, Alleluia, and Gospel; and Communion Verse of the day and of the feast.*

*Heirmos: "Unto God our Savior" (Сп҃телю Бг҃ꙋ):*[^1674]

*Troparion:* Despise me not, suffering grievously, cried he weeping, O Savior, who wasted Thy wealth upon thieves; having thus mercy on us, take compassion and save me!

*Troparion:* Heal me whose mind is slain by sins, in wounds from thieves of unjust and wicked thoughts, O Christ Savior, and save me, as Thou art plenteous in mercy!

*Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* O all-pure Mother of Christ, unceasingly pray God Who was incarnate of thee, and Who was not separated from the bosom of the Father, to save from every distress those whom He created!

*Troparion:* Having ascended from the sorrow of material things into immaterial and spiritual light, O venerable John, by thy prayers unto the Lord enlighten me!

*Troparion:* Having tasted the sweetness of abstinence, thou didst cast away the bitterness of pleasures; therefore more than honey and the honeycomb dost thou sweeten our senses, O Father!

*Troparion:* Having ascended unto the height of virtues, and having spat upon pleasures crawling below, thou hast appeared as the sweetness of salvation unto thy flock, O venerable Father!

*Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* O thou who didst ineffably give birth to the Wisdom and Word of the Father, heal the grievous wound of my soul, and subdue the pain of my heart!

*Troparion:* Journeying grievously on the way of life, O Christ, I have been wounded by thieves in passions; but raise me up, I pray Thee!

*Troparion:* Thieves have beaten my mind, and left me half-dead in the wounds of my transgressions; but heal me, O Lord!

*Troparion:* Passions have stripped me bare of Thy commandments, O Christ Savior, and I am wounded with pleasures; but pour out Thy mercy upon me!

*Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* Unceasingly pray Him Who came forth from thy loins, O pure one, that those who hymn thee as the Mother of God may be delivered from the deceit of the devil!

*Another Canon, for the Venerable One, Tone 8. Ode 3. Heirmos: "Thou art the establishment" (Ты є҆сѝ ᲂу҆твержде́нїе):*[^1678]

*Troparion:* From ascetic sweet spices, O venerable one, thou hast compounded thyself entirely as chrism of sanctification, into an odor of divine fragrance!

*Troparion:* Meditating on the training of the Law, thou didst drown the passions, as once other Pharaohites, in the streams of thy tears!

*Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* Quench the unstable confusion of my thoughts, O pure Mother of God, directing their motion unto Thy Son!

*Katavasia: "O Mother of God, thy hymnographers" (Твоѧ̑ пѣ́сносло́вцы):*[^1679]

*(fol. 608)*

Holding Thy most holy Cross, O our Savior, as a weapon of salvation, therein do we cry unto Thee: Save us, Thou Who didst suffer willingly for us, O God of all, as Thou art plenteous in mercy!

Having shone forth with virtues, holding them fixed toward heaven, thou didst lead them piously unto the immeasurable depth of the vision of God; having conquered all the wiles of demons, thou dost protect men from their vexations, O John, ladder of virtues, now praying that thy servants may be saved!

He Who sits upon the Cherubic throne and abides in the bosom of the Father, sits as upon His holy throne in thy womb, O Sovereign Lady, God in the flesh, Who hath thus reigned over all nations; and with understanding do we now sing unto Him, Whom do thou also, O pure one, entreat that thy servants may be saved!

*Canon of the Triodion, Tone 5. Ode 4. Heirmos: "I have heard, O Lord" (Ꙋ҆слы́шахъ Гдⷭ҇и):*[^1682]

*Troparion:* My unstable thoughts have drawn me away from Thy commandments, O Savior, whence I am wounded with transgressions!

*Troparion:* When the Levite saw me wounded with wounds, he passed by, O my Savior; but do Thou save me!

*Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* Divinely do we glorify thee, O Bride unwedded, and unto thy harbor do we, the faithful, flee!

*Troparion:* As a most sweet-smelling meadow and an animate paradise of virtues, thou hast made abstinence blossom forth, wherewith thou hast nourished all who honor thee!

*Troparion:* Having truly acquired thee, O Father, as a teacher of instruction and a most gentle rule for monks, even as Moses and David, we call thee blessed!

*(fol. 609)*
*Troparion:* Planted upon the waters of abstinence, O blessed one, thou hast appeared, O Father, as a most fair-flowering bough, offering clusters of piety!

*Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* Him Who became subject to time, Who shone forth timelessly from the Father, hast thou borne unto us, O Mother of God; Whom do thou entreat to save those who hymn thee!

*Canon of the Triodion, Tone 5. Ode 5. Heirmos: "Rising at dawn out of the night" (Ѡ҆ но́щи ᲂу҆́треннююще):*[^1685]
*Troparion:* O Christ, do Thou visit the wounds of my soul, even as of old him who fell into the hands of thieves, and heal my sickness, I pray Thee!

*Troparion:* Grievously have I grown weak through sinful wounds, O my Christ, and thence do I lie stripped naked of divine virtues; I pray Thee, save me!

*Troparion:* When the priest saw me, and the Levite could not help me openly, they passed by me; but do Thou Thyself, as compassionate, grant me salvation and save me!

*Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* Despise me not, wretched as I am, I pray Thee, O Master, who am grievously wounded in mind by thieves, but take pity on me through the prayers of her who gave Thee birth!

*Troparion:* Having quenched all passions with the dew of thy struggles, O blessed Father, thou wast abundantly kindled with the fire of love and faith, a lamp of abstinence and the enlightenment of dispassion, and thou didst become a son of the day!

*Troparion:* By spiritual tillage thou hast brought forth the divine cluster of faith, and hast cast it into the wine-presses, and worked it by the labors of training; and with the spiritual chalice full of abstinence thou dost gladden the hearts of thy flock!

*(fol. 610)*
*Troparion:* Having bravely endured the assaults and wounds of the adversary enemies, thou hast appeared as a pillar of patience, establishing thy flock with the divine staff upon the pasture of abstinence, and nourishing it upon the water, O blessed one!

*Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* Following the words of thy lips, O all-immaculate one, we call thee blessed; for the Lord Who in truth did great things with thee hath magnified thee, and showed thee forth as the true Mother of God by the birth from thy womb!

*Troparion:* In passions have I spent my divine life, O Master, and being grievously wounded in every way by sins, I have fled unto Thee; take pity on me, I pray!

*Troparion:* Thieves through passions plundered my wealth, and having wounded my mind, left me as dead; but taking compassion, save me, O Lord!

*Troparion:* When the Levite saw the pain of my scourgings, not enduring the sight of my wounds, he passed by me; but Thou Thyself, O Lover of mankind, hast poured out Thy rich mercy upon me!

*Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* As the Unburnt Bush, and the Mountain, and the Animate Ladder, and the Heavenly Gate, do we worthily glorify thee, O most glorious Mary, boast of the Orthodox!

*Another Canon [to the Venerable One], Tone 8. Ode 6. Heirmos: "Cleanse me, O Savior" (Ѡ҆чи́сти мѧ̀ Сп҃се):*
*Troparion:* Thou hast received into thy soul the divine wealth of the Spirit: blameless prayer, purity, honor, continual vigilance, and the labors of abstinence, whereby thou wast recognized as a house of God!

*Troparion:* Having passed beyond the baseness of material things below...

*(fol. 611)*
...and having winged thy mind with immaterial prayer, thou didst appear as an inheritor of heavenly rest, for the sake of the perfection of thy life!

*Troparion:* With ascetic sweats thou hast truly burned up the coals of enemy darts, and having kindled the fire of faith, thou hast burned up the ravings of unfaith and heresies!

*Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* From heavenly Zion hath the majesty shone forth, clothed from thee, O unwedded one, in the offering of flesh through the ineffable Union, and hath enlightened the world!

*Katavasia: "This divine and all-honorable [feast]" (Бж҃твенное сїѐ и҆ всечⷭ҇тно́е):*

*Kontakion, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast appeared today" (Ꙗ҆ви́лся є҆сѝ дне́сь):*
Upon the height of abstinence hath the Lord truly placed thee, even as an unerring star guiding the ends of the earth with light, O our father and teacher John!

*Ikos:*
As a true house of God hast thou fashioned thyself, O Father, by thy divine virtues, manifestly adorning, even as radiant gold, Faith, Hope, and true Love; setting forth divine laws, training thyself in abstinence as an incorporeal one, having acquired prudence, courage, chastity, and humility, whereby thou wast exalted; therefore thou wast also enlightened by unceasing prayers, and hast received heavenly habitations, O our father and teacher John!

## The Life of Our Holy Father John Climacus, Wonderworker, Written by Daniel the Monk[^1688]

Which city or land brought forth that divine man, and reared him with most glorious training in spiritual warfare, I could not easily recount, since this is not with sufficient certainty known unto me. But which city now holds him, and pastures him with eternal and immortal delights, Saint Paul hath long before us expressed. For altogether hath he also become an inhabitant of that heavenly Jerusalem, in which is the assembly of the firstborn: whose habitation, he says, is in the heavens (Heb. 12:22–23),[^1689] where unto the most refined spirits...

*(fol. 612)*
...and separated from all matter, insatiably enjoying divine good things, contemplating invisible beauties, he receives worthy tokens of his sweats, and carries off the most peaceful reward of his labors. For having attained the inheritance of that Kingdom, he now dances in chorus with them unto ages, and makes merry with those whose foot hath stood in uprightness (Ps. 25:12 LXX).[^1690] In what manner, then, he prepared this blessedness for himself, I will now begin to speak.

This holy man, when he attained bodily growth, being scarcely sixteen years of age,[^1691] offered himself unto Christ as a pleasing and acceptable sacrifice, placing his neck under the yoke of monastic life upon Mount Sinai. He thought in his mind that, being admonished by the visible dwelling of that place, he might be more easily trained and more fitly led unto the invisible God. And first the holy man tamed the insolence of passions, as the frequent instructor of the mind; whereby, casting away all foul and harmful presumption, and having embraced the deepest humility, he drove completely far from himself that demon of self-satisfaction by whose blast we are each moved to please ourselves and trust ourselves; and even the very beast he cast out from his heart. And bending his neck, trusting in the Lord and yielding himself entirely unto the Father who had taken him under his care,[^1692] as unto some best governor, [margin: In very great obedience] he passed through the very deep and fierce billows of this present life without danger. And so perfectly did he die unto the world and his own wills that he seemed to have a soul devoid of any reasoning and will, and entirely free of natural self-assertion. And this, indeed, was most marvelous: that along with that simple guilelessness, he was well trained in secular learning; for the conceit of philosophy is far removed from the humility of Christ, as are many other things.

Nineteen years, then, he lived thus, becoming unto all a pattern of blessed obedience. And when that holy elder who trained him departed unto Christ, he also went forth unto the discipline of the eremitic life [margin: Departing unto solitude], supported by the elder's prayers as by a most powerful weapon, for the destruction of the strongholds of Satan. At the fifth milestone from the church,[^1693] then, he established the dwelling-place of his warfare, at a place whose name is Tholas.[^1694] And there he lived for forty years, in very great greatness and clarity of heart, continually burning with most fervent prayer and the fire of divine love. Now, who could worthily express in words or praises what great labors he endured there?

*(fol. 613)*
For how can that be brought out into the light, since every labor of his was performed in secret and without a witness? Nevertheless, from certain first-fruits and incidental occasions, let us give ear to the disposition of the life of this most blessed man.

He ate indeed of everything that was lawful for him according to the vows of his monastic rule [margin: Food], yet very moderately, so that he might also cut off conceited pride from thence and prudently break the horn of haughtiness [margin: * That he might quench sin in himself]; by the shortness indeed of his food completely tormenting the unhealthy madness of gluttony, and crying out unto it through abstinence: *Be silent, be muzzled!* And tasting moderately of all things, he sent the tyranny of vainglory under the yoke. By solitariness, through which he was rarely seen by men, he so quenched the flame of that furnace—that is to say, bodily pleasure—that it was utterly smothered and laid to rest, and brought him no vexations. And concupiscence (which the Apostle defined as idolatry, Eph. 5:5)[^1695] this mighty warrior mightily struck down by the fear of God and the smallness of earthly things. And as for sloth and faintheartedness of mind (which I would rightly call the very death of the soul), he escaped and guarded against them by the remembrance of death and by training in continual piety. And since he was not marked by longing for any mortal thing, but was fed only by the consolation of eternal goods, he escaped free from harmful anxiety. The tyranny of anger he had slain within himself with the sword of obedience. And by rare bodily movement and rarer use of speech, he starved the leech of vainglory, that most deceptive fall. What, then, shall I say concerning the highest and most diligent purification of the eighth sin—that is to say, Pride?[^1696] Which this new Bezalel[^1697] began indeed through the modesty of obedience, and the Lord of the heavenly Jerusalem brought unto perfection, coming in His presence and exalting humility against it, without which it is impossible to defeat the devil and his like pitfall.

Where, then, shall I place that fountain of tears in the crown of his life? A thing truly rare, and one that is not easily found among many, whose secret workshop now remains: a very narrow cave situated at the foot of a certain mountain, and so far distant from his own and every other cell, as seemed necessary to preserve his ears from vainglory; reaching even unto heaven by groaning, sighing, weeping...

*(fol. 614)*
...by prayers and other utterances at last, such as are wont to come from those pierced by swords and those whose eyes are gouged out, reaching even unto heaven. Sleep he took only so much as he deemed sufficient to preserve the life of soul and mind, lest through excessive sleeplessness it should fail. And before sleep, he occupied himself as much as possible with prayers. He was also accustomed to copy small books, by which very work he drove away from himself the weakness of sloth. Unto this his whole life was directed: unceasing prayer, and incomparable love toward God; for looking upon Him day and night as in the most translucent mirror of purity, he would receive no satiety, nor indeed could he do otherwise. At a certain time [margin: Concerning the miracle of the holy man's disciple], one of those who had chosen the solitary life, Moses by name,[^1698] desiring to imitate the life of this divine Father, to be nourished by his teachings, and to learn from him the elements of true philosophy, brought forward many holy Fathers as intercessors, through whom he asked with great supplications that he would accept him as a disciple. Therefore, helped by their prayers, he was accepted by the holy man as he had desired.
