To him at a certain time the holy Father commanded that he should bring from a certain place soil of loamy earth, for the better cultivation of the garden and herbs. Going therefore to the place appointed for him, Moses diligently performed what had been commanded him. But when the midday hour drew near, and by the burning of the sun that place was like fire in the manner of a furnace (for it was indeed the month of August),[^1699] Moses, being exhausted and worn out from carrying the earth, considered that he needed a little rest; and letting himself rest under the shadow of a very great rock, he began to fall asleep. But the most merciful God, Who does not allow His faithful servants to be grieved in anything, when Moses was already in peril, anticipated it with His customary mercy in this manner: While that great father of ours John was in his little cell, giving heed, as was his custom, to himself and to God, he fell into a very light sleep and saw through a vision a certain man of venerable countenance and stature, who judged him and rebuked him as he slept, saying: "Dost thou sleep so carelessly, O John, while Moses is at the very brink of danger?"

*(fol. 615)*
Quickly therefore awakening [margin: * Moses is preserved from the greatest danger], he straightway armed himself with prayer, praying for his disciple. Whom, when he returned toward evening, he asked whether any adverse and unexpected thing had befallen him. Then he said: "A stone of marvelous size was within a little of crushing me and completely breaking me in pieces, while I was sleeping deeply beneath it, had I not, thinking that I heard thy voice, leapt out from the place with a swift bound, full of fear; and no sooner had I done so than I beheld that stone torn away from the rock and fallen to the earth!" Hearing this, the man of God, being truly humble in mind, telling his disciple nothing of what he had seen and heard, with secret cries and the voices of innermost love, singing a hymn, offered most abundant thanksgiving unto God.

This holy man was also a physician of secret wounds. For a certain monk, Isaac by name, burning at a certain time with a grievous inflammation of the flesh, came running unto him, encompassed with sorrow on all sides, and disclosed his inward warfare with sobbing and tears. At whose faith and humility the holy man, being struck with wonder, gently comforted him with these words, saying: "Let us both stand for prayer, my son, and the all-gracious and merciful Lord will not overlook our prayer." And when this was done, and they had not yet finished praying, while the afflicted brother was still lying prone on his face, the Lord fulfilled the will of His servant, that He might show thence that His Prophet speaks the truth: *And before they call, I will hear them; while they are yet speaking, I will say: What is it?* (Isa. 65:24),[^1700] and the burning of the flesh was immediately subdued by the fervency of diligent prayer. Afterwards, he who had formerly been sick, seeing himself healed of his illness and relieved from all such turmoil, was exceedingly astonished, and gave thanksgiving unto God and unto His renowned servant.

When, moreover, this venerable Father bountifully nourished with the word of grace those who came unto him, and poured forth streams of instruction most abundantly, certain malicious men, inflamed with the torches of envy [margin: From detractors he endures the withholding of speech], striving to stop so great a benefit as was born from his teaching, began to call him a chatterer and a liar. Seeing this, and having learned that he could do all things in Christ Who strengthened him (Phil. 4:13; cf. 2 Cor. 12:9),[^1701] and desiring to instruct those who came to him for their own profit not only by spoken admonition, but far more by silence and practical philosophy, so that, as it is written, he might cut off...

*(fol. 616)*
...an occasion from those who sought an occasion (2 Cor. 11:12), he resolved to keep silence for a certain time, and to dam up the honey-flowing river of his teaching; deeming that it was better and more profitable that the diligent lovers of good things should for that time suffer harm—unto whom, indeed, he was to be more profitable through silence—than that those ungrateful vessels should be further irritated, lest their malice and wicked will should grow any further. Therefore they also, being struck with fear at the humility and modesty of the man, and having recognized that they had dammed up for themselves the fountain of such benefit and had become the cause of so great harm unto all, came unto the man with humility and supplication, and asked for the word of teaching in the common way together with the others. He therefore straightway consented, as one who did not know how to oppose anyone, and took up again the occupation of his former estate.

When therefore he was so renowned in all good things that none like him could be found, with one common voice [margin: How he was chosen for leadership/instruction] and one will, like a new Moses, they took him, even against his will, unto the instruction and governance of the brethren; elevating him as a light upon the candlestick of leadership (Matt. 5:15), being themselves the best judges of such things; nor were they deceived in their hope. For he also ascended the mountain, and entering into the consecrated darkness, received the Law written by the hands of God; and enjoying the contemplation of God, and ascending by spiritual steps, with the word of God he opened his mouth, and drawing in the Spirit, poured forth a good word from the good treasure of his heart (Ps. 44:2 LXX; Matt. 12:35).[^1702]

Thus, then, he completed the end of his visible life in the leadership of the monastic community, differing from Moses only in this: that he entered into the heavenly Jerusalem with great ease; for he, I know not how, accounted earthly things as nothing. And witnesses unto these things which we have said are all those who through him were endowed with the eloquence and grace of the Holy Spirit; and of these, very many are they who by his grace were saved and are saved now. A best witness of this wise salvation, both simple and righteous, is a new David.[^1703] A witness also is our best shepherd John,[^1704] by whom that great man, being entreated, descending from Mount Sinai unto us with spiritual knowledge, even as some new Seer of God, showed unto us his God-written tablets—I mean the *Ladder*—instructing us from without, indeed, in the laborious life...

*(fol. 617)*
...and within possessing the teaching of the contemplation of God. And having thus lived in all God-pleasing achievements, and having left behind many writings for the instruction of the faithful, he fell asleep in the Lord. By whose prayers, O God, have mercy on us and save us![^1705]

*Canon of the Triodion, Tone 5. Ode 7. Heirmos: "The highly exalted" (Превозноси́мый):*[^1706]
*Troparion:* Thieves fell upon me, and with wounds left me dead, as one without breath; therefore I pray Thee, O God, do Thou visit me!

*Troparion:* Unstable thoughts have captured my mind, and having wounded me with passions, have left me dead through the multitude of transgressions; but do Thou heal me, O Savior!

*Troparion:* When the Levite saw me suffering with wounds, not enduring to look upon my wounds because they were incurable, he passed by me, O my Savior; but do Thou Thyself heal me!

*Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* Thou Who wast incarnate of the Virgin hast saved me, pouring out upon my wounds the rich mercy of Thy compassions, O Christ; therefore do I glorify Thee!

*Another Canon [to the Venerable One], Tone 8. Ode 7. Heirmos: "The children that went down from Judea" (Ѿ І҆ꙋде́а доше́дшїи):*[^1707]
*Troparion:* Upon the pasture of the heavenly Kingdom hast thou nourished thy flock, O Father, and with the staff of dogmas hast thou driven away the beasts of heresies, and sung: *Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!*

*Troparion:* Thou hast entered into the bridal chamber on high of the Kingdom of Christ, clad in a garment worthy of Him Who called thee, wherein thou hast reclined, crying: *Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!*

*Troparion:* As a river of abstinence unwetted by sins hast thou appeared, O Father, drowning wicked thoughts and cleansing defilement, crying in faith: *Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!*

*Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* From thy womb came forth the Lord of all, incarnate, O Virgin; therefore, rightly confessing thee as the Mother of God...

*(fol. 618)*
...we cry unto Thy Son: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Katavasia: "The godly-minded youths" (Не послꙋжи́ша тва́ри):*[^1708]

*Canon of the Triodion, Tone 5. Ode 8. Heirmos: "Unto Thee, the Creator of all" (Тебѣ̀ вседѣ́телю):*[^1709]
*Troparion:* By the thieves of my thoughts, O Savior, have I corrupted my life with the wounds of sins; therefore have I been stripped naked of the divine image, O Thou Lover of mankind and God; but take compassion on me!

*Troparion:* Thou hast come upon earth from the heights, O Savior, taking compassion on me who am wounded with wounds, all-covered with transgressions, O Compassionate One, and pouring out Thy mercy upon me, O Christ!

*Troparion:* Body and soul, O Master and Savior, hast Thou given as a ransom for me, and Thou hast saved me who was pierced by the sword of sins in incurable wounds, as Thou art merciful!

*Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* Thee, who beyond understanding didst give birth unto the Lord by a God-man word, and didst remain a virgin, do all the works of the Lord, O Virgin, bless, and highly exalt unto all ages!

*Another Canon [to the Venerable One], Tone 8. Ode 8. Heirmos: "The King of heaven" (Цр҃ѧ̀ нб҃наго):*[^1710]
*Troparion:* Having truly acquired thee as an animate pillar and an image of abstinence, O Father, we all honor thy memory, O John!

*Troparion:* The multitude of monks rejoices, and the assembly of the venerable and the righteous exults; for worthily hast thou received a crown with them!

*Troparion:* Adorned with virtues, thou hast entered into the unwaning light of ineffable glory, singing a hymn unto Christ unto ages!

*Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* Despise not those who require help from thee, O Virgin, who sing and highly exalt the Lord unto all ages!

*We praise, we bless, and we worship the Lord:*
*Katavasia: "The pious youths in the furnace" (Ѻ҆́троки бл҃гочести́выѧ):*[^1711]

*(fol. 619)*
*Canon of the Triodion, Tone 5. Ode 9. Heirmos: "Rejoice, O Isaiah" (И҆са́їа ликꙋ́й):*[^1712]
*Troparion:* Having not kept Thy commandments in my mind, O Master, but having entered into the passions of pleasures, I was stripped of grace and became naked through wounds; therefore, O Savior, by Thy mercy save me!

*Troparion:* Neither was the Levite able to wash my sores; but Thou didst come unto me compassionately, O Good One, and didst pour out the mercy of Thy compassions upon me, O Savior, healing me as a physician of great renown!

*Troparion:* As Thou art tender-hearted, Thou hast had compassion and saved me, O Christ, who was grievously slain by the wounds of thieves, O Savior; and for both soul and body, as two denarii, Thou hast given redemption![^1713]

*Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* Beyond understanding is thy childbearing, O Mother of God; for without man was the conception in thee, and virginal was the birth, for God is the Offspring; Whom magnifying, thee, O Virgin, do we call blessed!

*Another Canon [to the Venerable One], Tone 8. Ode 9. Heirmos: "Her who is more honorable and glorious" (Чтⷭ҇нꙋ́ю и҆ сла́внꙋю):*[^1714]
*Troparion:* As a physician from God for those who are sick in sins, O blessed one, and as a destroyer and expeller of evil spirits hast thou appeared; therefore do we call thee blessed!

*Troparion:* As a dwelling of corruption, thou hast left the earth, O Father, and hast settled in the land of the meek (Matt. 5:5), and dost rejoice with them, being filled with divine sweetness!

*Troparion:* Today is a festive day, for it summons all the flocks of monastics unto a spiritual chorus, unto the banquet and food of immortal life!

*Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* He Who cast down the murderer who of old maliciously deceived our first parents, took up His abode in thee, O all-immaculate one; He took up His abode and saved us all!

*(fol. 620)*
*Katavasia: "Let every earthborn mortal" (Всѧ́къ земноро́дный):*[^1715]

*Exapostilarion of the Resurrection.*
*To the Venerable One, Tone 2, Podoben: "Give ear, ye women" (Же́ны ᲂу҆слы́шите):*[^1716]
From the possessions of the world, as from something harmful, hast thou turned away; and having withered the flesh with fasting, thou hast renewed the strength of the soul, O Venerable One, and hast been enriched with heavenly glory, O most glorious one; therefore cease not to pray for us, O John!

*Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* Truly do we confess thee to be the Mother of God, O Sovereign Lady, being saved through thee; for ineffably hast thou given birth unto God, Who destroyed death by the Cross, and drew unto Himself the assemblies of the venerable; with whom also we praise thee, O Virgin!

*At the Praises: The Resurrection Stichera in the Octoechos, and the Anatolian stichera, as usual; then we say the verse:* Arise, O Lord my God (Ps. 9:33 LXX); *and we sing the Idiomelon, Tone 1:*
Come, let us work in the mystical vineyard, producing therein fruits of repentance, not laboring in foods and drinks, but in prayers and fastings fulfilling the virtues; being well-pleased with these, the Lord grants the denarius of the work, whereby souls are redeemed from the debt of sin, He Who alone is plenteous in mercy![^1717]

*Glory... the same. Both now... "Most blessed art thou" (see fol. 167)[^1718]. And the customary order, as on leaf 167.*

*AT THE LITURGY: The Beatitudes, and of the Troparia, see leaf 440[^1719]. Prokeimenon, Tone 8; and to the Venerable One, Tone 7:* The saints shall boast in glory *(Ps. 149:5 LXX); Verse:* Sing unto the Lord a new song *(Ps. 149:1 LXX). Epistle to the Hebrews, Pericope 314 [Heb. 6:13–20]:* Brethren, when God made promise to Abraham... *And another to the Venerable One: to the Ephesians, Pericope 224 [Eph. 5:9–19]:* Brethren, walk as children of light... *Alleluia, Tone 8; and to the Venerable One, Tone 7:* Planted in the house of the Lord *(Ps. 91:14 LXX). Gospel from Matthew, Pericope 40 [Matt. 9:14–17 / Mark 9:17–31]:*[^1720] At that time, a certain man came unto Jesus... *And to the Venerable One: from Matthew, Pericope 10 [Matt. 4:25–5:12]. Communion Hymn:* Praise the Lord *(Ps. 148:1); Another:* In everlasting memory *(Ps. 111:6 LXX).*

## On the Same Sunday Evening of the Holy Fast: Vespers

*And at Vespers, the Kathisma is not chanted, even as on the other Sundays never. And at "Lord, I have cried," we set 10 stichera. And the rest of the order: as indicated on leaf 167[^1721]. And of the Triodion, 3 [stichera]: by Lord Joseph, Tone 3, Podoben: "Great is the power of Thy Cross, O Lord" (Ве́лїѧ крⷭ҇та):*[^1722]

*(fol. 621)*
*Sticheron 1:* Great labors of abstinence let us show forth, ye faithful, that we may obtain great glory by the mercy of the great God, being delivered from the fire of Gehenna!

*Sticheron 2:* Having now passed the midpoint of the season of fasting, let us manifestly show forth the beginning of divine life, and let us warmly hasten to attain unto the end of a virtuous conversation, that we may receive ageless sweetness!

*Another Sticheron, by Lord Theodore, Tone 7, Podoben: "Thy protection" (Покро́въ тво́й):*[^1723]
Having passed the midpoint of this sacred course of fasting, let us joyfully run unto what lies ahead, having anointed our souls with the oil of good deeds, that we may be vouchsafed to venerate the divine Passions of Christ our God, and to arrive before His awesome and holy Resurrection!

*And of the Menaion, 3 [stichera]. And the rest according to the direction of leaf 168[^1724]. Likewise the Great Prokeimenon:* Turn not away Thy face from Thy servant *(Ps. 68:18 LXX), with its verses, seek on Cheesefare Sunday.*

*At the Aposticha: Idiomelon, Tone 7:*
He Who planted the vineyard and called the laborers, the Savior, is near; come, ye ascetics of fasting, let us receive the reward, for rich and merciful is the Giver; having labored a little, let us receive mercy for our souls!

*Verse:* Unto Thee have I lifted up mine eyes, O Thou that dwellest in heaven *(Ps. 122:1 LXX). Another Idiomelon, Tone 7:*
Into thoughts of thieves fell Adam, deceived in his mind; he wounded his soul and lay naked because of his transgression. Neither did the priest before the Law give heed unto him, nor did the Levite under the Law look upon him, but only Thou, O God Who didst come, not from Samaria, but from the Virgin; O Lord, glory be to Thee![^1725]

*Verse:* Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us *(Ps. 122:3 LXX).*

*(fol. 622)*
*Martyrikon:* Thy Martyrs, O Lord, denied Thee not, neither did they depart from Thy commandments; through their prayers have mercy on us!

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*
Archangelically let us sing, ye faithful, unto the heavenly bridal chamber and the truly sealed door: Rejoice, through whom Christ sprouted forth unto us, the Savior of all, the Giver of life and God! Cast down, O Sovereign Lady, the godless tyrants, our enemies, by thy hand, O all-pure one, hope of Christians!

*AT COMPLINE: We sing the service in the Menaion of the saint occurring on Thursday of the Great Canon.*[^1726]

*If the Apodosis of the Annunciation of the Most Holy Theotokos should occur on Friday of the Fourth Week of the Fast:*[^1727]
*On Sunday evening: At "Lord, I have cried," stichera: 3 of the Triodion; 4 of the Feast; 3 to the Archangel. Glory... to the Archangel; Both now... of the Feast. Entrance, Great Prokeimenon. Litany: "Let us complete our evening prayer." At the Aposticha: Stichera of the Triodion: the Idiomelon of the day, twice, and the Martyrikon. Glory... Both now... of the Feast. After the Trisagion, we sing the Troparion according to the Lenten order, and 3 great prostrations, and the Dismissal. Mid-Compline without prostrations; prostrations from "Glory to God in the highest"; at it, the ordinary canon in the Menaion.*

*ON FRIDAY AT MATINS: After the Psalms, we sing "Alleluia" and the Trinity Hymns of the Tone. After the first Kathisma, Sessional hymn in the Octoechos. After the 2nd and 3rd Sticherology, Sessional hymns in the Triodion. Canon in the Octoechos to 4; and of the Feast to 4; and to the Archangel to 6. Katavasia of the Feast, both choirs together. But when there is a Triodion [three-ode canon] in the Triodion: we sing the Canon of the Annunciation with the Heirmos to 4; to the Archangel to 6, two troparia for one verse; and in the Triodion to 8. Katavasia: the Heirmos that is in the Triodion. After Ode 6, forty "Lord, have mercy." At Ode 9, we sing "More honorable." Exapostilarion: Trinity Hymns of the Tone. At the Praises, Stichera to the Archangel to 4, Podoben: "Thou hast given a sign" (Да́лъ є҆сѝ зна́менїе); Glory... Both now... of the Feast, Tone 2: "Gabriel announces the good tidings." At the Aposticha, the customary stichera in the Triodion; and all the rest we sing even as always according to the Lenten order.*

*At the Refectory we eat cooked food with oil. After rising from the table, we say the Kontakion of the Feast.*

*(fol. 623)*
## On Friday of the Fifth Week of the Holy Fast[^1728]

*AT MATINS: The customary order, as we have indicated (see fol. 528)[^1729].*

*After the 2nd Sticherology, Sessional Hymn, Tone 3, Podoben: "Beholding the beauty of thy virginity" (Красотѣ̀ дѣ́вства):*[^1730]
The most fair season hath arrived, the praiseworthy day of abstinence, O brethren; let us hasten to cleanse ourselves, that we may appear pure before the Creator, and obtain His beauty through the prayers of her who gave Him birth, the only pure Mother of God!

*Glory... the same. Both now... Theotokion:*
Awed by the beauty of thy virginity and the surpassing brightness of thy purity, Gabriel cried aloud unto thee, O Mother of God: What worthy praise shall I offer unto thee? What shall I call thee, I know not and am astonished! Therefore, as I was commanded, I cry unto thee: Rejoice, thou who art full of grace!

*After the 3rd Sticherology, Sessional Hymn, Tone 7, Podoben: "Tell us" (Рцы̀ мы є҆мы̀):*[^1731]
Grant us, O Lord, from this present day, having passed through this holy week brightly, to attain unto the Resurrection of Lazarus from the dead; vouchsafe Thy servants in Thy fear to traverse the stadium of the fast, all-perfectly!

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*
Thou art more honorable than the most glorious Cherubim, O all-holy Virgin; for they, not enduring the divine power, perform their service covering their faces with their wings; but thou, beholding with thine own eyes the incarnate Word, dost bear Him; Whom do thou unceasingly entreat for our souls!

*Triodion of Lord Joseph, Tone 3. Ode 5. Heirmos: "Thou Who of old by divine beck" (Во́ды дре́вле):*[^1732]

*(fol. 624)*
*Troparion:* Having tilled our thoughts with the divine plow of the divine fast, let us bring forth an ear of virtues, that we may not hunger unto ages, rejoicing as we delight in ineffable sweetness!

*Troparion:* Passions of many years do I carry within, darkening my wretched soul; falling down with contrite heart and tender sorrow before Thy invincible power, O Word of the timeless Father, take compassion and save me!

*Troparion:* Good fasting nourishes the hearts, anoints thoughts pleasing unto God, and drying up the abyss of passions, cleanses with showers of compunction those who in faith offer praise unto the Almighty!

*Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* O Maiden of many names, rejoice, holy Virgin, Mary Mother of God, boast of the faithful, deliverance from the curse, heavenly ladder, incomprehensible wonder, unburnt bush, untilled earth!

*Another Canon, by Lord Theodore, Tone 7. Ode 5. Heirmos: "Let us sing unto the Lord" (Пои́мъ Гдⷭ҇еви):*[^1733]
*Troparion:* Having venerated the life-bearing Wood, hence we journey along the path of the fast, rejoicing towards the Passion of Christ!

*Troparion:* Following Christ, let us renounce the world and take the Cross upon our shoulder, being conformed unto His divine Passions!

*Trinity Hymn:* In three Persons, the supersubstantial one Godhead let us all hymn: Father, and Son, and Holy Spirit!

*Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* Him Whom thou didst bear incomprehensibly, having known no corruption, O pure one, Jesus the Savior, do thou entreat now for thy servants!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*
*Troparion:* When Thou shalt come in glory with the Angels to judge all things, vouchsafe us also, O Christ, to give a good defense unto Thee!

*(fol. 625)*
*Katavasia: "Let us sing unto the Lord, Who drowned all the power of Pharaoh in the sea, a song of victory, for He hath been glorified!"*[^1734]

*Canon of the Triodion [Joseph], Tone 3. Ode 8. Heirmos: "The Babylonian furnace" (Вавѷлѡ́нскаѧ пе́щь):*[^1735]
*Troparion:* Drawn out by the harmful deceits of the serpent and grievously seduced all the days, adding wound unto my wound, I cry unto Thee, O Savior, the Physician of the sick: Turn me back and save me!

*Troparion:* Having fasted, Elisha raised of old the child of the Shunammite, being strengthened by the Spirit (4 Kings 4:32–37 LXX);[^1736] let us also, ye faithful, who have been slain by voluptuousness, be revived by life-bearing fasting!

*Troparion:* Thou didst save the Ninevites of old who repented in weeping and fasting (Jonah 3:5–10), O Lord, Lover of mankind, as Thou art merciful; take compassion on us also by Thy mercy, who lack understanding how to confess unto Thee by deeds!

*Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* O all-immaculate one who after childbearing didst remain incorrupt, deliver thy servants from corruption, we pray thee, O pure one, who faithfully sing of the works of the Master with unity of mind of the soul!

*Another Canon [Theodore], Tone 7. Ode 8. Heirmos: "Him Who is fearsome unto the Cherubim" (Стра́шнагѡ Херꙋві́мѡмъ):*[^1737]
*Troparion:* Having the strength of abstinence with God, ye faithful, let us run youthfully through the rest of the holy stadium, and receive crowns!

*Troparion:* Beholding the fruitlessness of my sorely ailing soul, have patience yet, O Christ, and cut me not down like that cursed fig tree (Matt. 21:19)![^1738]

*We bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, the Lord.*
*Trinity Hymn:* O monarchical Trinity and tri-hypostatic Unity, Father, Son, and Spirit, deliver from all temptations and tribulations those who hymn Thee!

*Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* Rejoice, Mountain of God; rejoice, ever-radiant...

*(fol. 626)*
...lamp, rejoice, new heaven, rejoice, mind of brilliance, rejoice, Church of the Lord, O all-hymned Virgin!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*
*Troparion:* Meditating upon Thine awesome trial, O Christ, I am terrified and tremble and cry aloud: O Thou Who hast ineffable mercy, save me, the wretched one!

*We praise, we bless, and we worship the Lord.*
*Katavasia: "Him Who is fearsome unto the Cherubim, and marvelous unto the Seraphim, and the Creator of the world, do ye priests and servants, and the spirits of the righteous, hymn the Lord, and highly exalt Him unto all ages!"*[^1739]

*Canon of the Triodion [Joseph], Tone 3. Ode 9. Heirmos: "A new wonder" (Но́вое чꙋ́до):*[^1740]
*Troparion:* Having now filled the divine cup with compunction, the grace of the fast manifestly summons all the faithful, crying out with gladness: Come, take delight, having put away the drunkenness of passions, that ye may be vouchsafed the consolation that is to come!

*Troparion:* Near is the judgment; take heed, O my soul, take care with conscience, and do good works which always keep thee uncondemned; for if we judge ourselves here, in no wise shall we be condemned there without witnesses, where the guilty are judged (1 Cor. 11:31)![^1741]

*Troparion:* Principalities, Powers, Thrones, Seraphim, Dominions, Authorities, and Cherubim, Angels, Archangels: Entreat Christ that we may pass through the season of fasting doing things pleasing unto Him, that as well-pleasing servants we may obtain glory!

*Troparion:* With Martyrs, with Prophets, and with all the Venerable, O Christ, receive her who gave Thee birth, who continually entreats Thee for the servants who have angered Thee, the only Master Who lovest mankind, before Whom the heavenly Powers tremble!

*Another Canon [Theodore], Tone 7. Ode 9. Heirmos: "Beyond nature" (Па́че є҆стества̀):*[^1742]

*(fol. 627)*
*Troparion:* Having sailed across the tranquil course of the fast by spiritual cool breezes, let us pray to reach the haven of the Passions of Christ!

*Troparion:* Emulating the Canaanite woman, I cry unto Thee: Have mercy on me, O Son of David and God, and heal my languishing soul, even as her daughter (Matt. 15:22)![^1743]

*Trinity Hymn:* The nature of the Godhead, the united unity, tri-personally triadized in three characters, the Father, and the Son, and the Spirit, let us hymn!

*Theotokion:*
*Theotokion:* Thou who didst conceive in thy womb the uncircumscribed Word, and didst bear Him without seed in the flesh, entreat diligently that our souls may be saved!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*
*Troparion:* Thou Who didst justify the Publican (Luke 18:13–14), cleanse me as I cry out: Be merciful unto me, a sinner, O Judge of those weighed down, forgiving me my transgressions!

*Katavasia: "A Mother beyond nature, and a Virgin according to nature, the only blessed among women, do we, the faithful, magnify with mystical hymns!"*[^1744]

*Then, "It is truly meet."*

*Exapostilarion of the Tone.*

*At the Aposticha: Idiomelon, Tone 8:*
Unto him that fell among thieves have I been likened, O Master of all, stumbling through my transgressions, and by them have I been pitilessly wounded; but leave me not unhealed, O Thou Who camest not from Samaria, but from the All-pure Virgin, O Jesus, name of salvation, have mercy on me![^1745]

*Verse 1:* We were filled in the morning with Thy mercy *(Ps. 89:14 LXX); and again the same sticheron.*

*Verse 2:* And let the brightness of the Lord our God be upon us *(Ps. 89:17 LXX); then the Martyrikon:*
What shall we call you, O saints? Cherubim? For upon you Christ rested. Seraphim? For unceasingly...

*(fol. 628)*
...ye glorified Him! Angels? For ye turned away from the body. Powers? For ye work wonders. Many are your names and greater your gifts: Entreat that our souls may be saved![^1746]

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*
The heavenly hosts hymn thee, O full of grace, unwedded Mother; and we glorify thine unsearchable childbearing: O Theotokos, entreat that our souls may be saved!

*On Friday of the Fifth Week, At the Sixth Hour.*
*Troparion of the Prophecy, Tone 7:*
Forasmuch as our iniquities have risen up against us, arise, O Lord, help us, for Thou art our Father: for beside Thee we know no other![^1747]

*Glory: the conclusion. Both now: the whole troparion.*

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 83, Tone 4:* Thine altars, O Lord of hosts, my King and my God (Ps. 83:4 LXX).[^1748]
*Verse:* How lovely are Thy dwellings! (Ps. 83:2 LXX).*

*Reading from the Prophecy of Isaiah (Isa. 37:33–38; 38:1–6):*[^1749]
Thus saith the Lord concerning the King of the Assyrians: He shall not come into this city, nor cast an arrow against it, nor lift up a shield against it, nor cast a trench about it; but by the way that he came, by the same shall he return, and into this city he shall not enter, saith the Lord. And I will defend this city to save it for Mine own sake, and for David My servant’s sake. And the Angel of the Lord went forth, and slew of the camp of the Assyrians an hundred and fourscore and five thousand; and when they arose early in the morning, behold, all these were dead corpses. And Sennacherib king of the Assyrians turned and departed, and returned...

*(fol. 629)*
...and dwelt at Nineveh. And as he was worshipping in the house of Nisroch his god, Adrammelech and Sharezer his sons smote him with the sword; and they escaped into Armenia. And Esarhaddon his son reigned in his stead.[^1750]

In those days Hezekiah was sick unto death. And Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz, came unto him, and said unto him: Thus saith the Lord: Set thine house in order; for thou shalt die, and not live. Then Hezekiah turned his face toward the wall, and prayed unto the Lord, saying: Remember now, O Lord, I beseech Thee, how I have walked before Thee in truth and with a perfect heart, and have done that which is good in Thy sight. And Hezekiah wept sore. Then came the word of the Lord to Isaiah, saying: Go, and say to Hezekiah: Thus saith the Lord, the God of David thy father: I have heard thy prayer, I have seen thy tears: behold, I will add unto thy days fifteen years. And I will deliver thee and this city out of the hand of the king of Assyria: and I will defend this city.

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 84, Tone 8:* Show us Thy mercy, O Lord, and grant us Thy salvation (Ps. 84:8 LXX).[^1751]
*Verse:* Lord, Thou hast been favorable unto Thy land: Thou hast brought back the captivity of Jacob (Ps. 84:2 LXX).*

*Since it is necessary to know concerning the Kathismata of Thursday of the Great Canon, which are three, that they be read beforehand and not omitted: Look ahead, and as they are arranged in their places, so read them.*[^1752]

*(fol. 630)*
*On the same Friday of the Fifth Week of the Fast, at Vespers:*
*We recite the Kathisma instead: "Unto the Lord when I was in affliction" (Ps. 119 LXX); Kathisma in order, omitted, 18: "In the Lord have I put my trust" (Ps. 10 LXX), on account of the Great Canon.*[^1753]

*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera, Tone 3:*
*By Lord Joseph. Tone 3, Podoben: "The Sign of the Cross" (Крⷭ҇та ѡ҆́бразъ):*[^1754]
O Word of God, Who hast granted unto us the season of fasting, to turn and to live, and in no wise to perish: Vouchsafe that all may well-please Thee by faith, and with warm compunction serve Thee, O Christ, at Whose nod, even as that chaste and precious harlot of old, who with myrrh and the pouring out of warm tears received forgiveness of transgressions!

As the blind men from the heart I cry unto Thee, O Son of God: Enlighten the eyes of my heart! As the faithful Canaanite woman I cry aloud unto Thee: Have mercy on me, O compassionate One! For I have a soul possessed by a demon in pleasures; do Thou, Who hast turned me away from the darkness of passions, grant me henceforth to live in purity, that I may glorify Thy manifold goodness!

*Another Sticheron, by Lord Theodore. Tone 2, Podoben: "Divinely summoned martyrs" (Бг҃озванныѧ м҃):*[^1755]
The divinely radiant grace of abstinence, having dawned upon us today brighter than the sun, enlightens our souls, driving away the sinful clouds of passions; therefore let us all run with eagerness, greeting her with kisses: Rejoicing, let us complete her divine course, making feast in spiritual gladness, let us cry aloud unto Christ: O Good One, sanctify those who faithfully accomplish this!

*Other Stichera, Martyrika: 2.*

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 85, Tone 4:* Guide me, O Lord, in Thy way, and I will walk in Thy truth (Ps. 85:11 LXX).[^1756]
*Verse:* Incline Thine ear, O Lord (Ps. 85:1 LXX).*

*(fol. 631)*
*Reading from the Book of Genesis (Gen. 13:12–18):*[^1757]
Abram dwelt in the land of Canaan, and Lot dwelt in the cities of the surrounding country, and pitched his tent in Sodom. But the men in Sodom were wicked and sinners exceedingly before God. And God said unto Abram, after that Lot was separated from him: Lift up now thine eyes, and look from the place where thou now art northward, and southward, and eastward, and toward the sea: for all the land which thou seest, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed for ever. And I will make thy seed as the dust of the earth: so that if a man can number the dust of the earth, then shall thy seed also be numbered. Arise, walk through the land in the length of it and in the breadth of it; for I will give it unto thee and unto thy seed for ever. Then Abram removed his tent, and came and dwelt by the oak of Mamre, which is in Hebron, and built there an altar unto the Lord.

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 86, Tone 4:* The Lord loves the gates of Zion more than all the dwellings of Jacob (Ps. 86:2 LXX).[^1758]
*Verse:* His foundations are in the holy mountains (Ps. 86:1 LXX).*

*Reading from the Proverbs (Prov. 14:27–35; 15:1–4):*[^1759]
The fear of the Lord is a fountain of life, causing men to turn away from the snare of death. In a multitude of people is the king’s glory: but in the lack of people is the ruin of a prince. He that is longsuffering is abundant in understanding; but he that is faint-hearted is exceedingly foolish. A meek-spirited...

*(fol. 632)*
...man is a healer of the heart; but strife is a moth unto the bones. Whoso slanders the poor provokes his Maker; but he that honors Him has mercy on the needy. In his wickedness the ungodly shall be driven away; but the righteous has hope in his holiness. In the good heart of a man wisdom rests; but in the heart of fools it is not known. Righteousness exalts a nation; but sins diminish peoples. An understanding servant is acceptable unto the king, and by his good conduct he puts away dishonor.[^1760]

Anger destroys even the wise; but a submissive answer turns away wrath. A harsh word stirs up anger. The tongue of the wise knows good things; but the mouth of the foolish proclaims evils. In every place the eyes of the Lord behold both the evil and the good. The healing of the tongue is a tree of life; and he that keeps it shall be filled with the spirit.

*Then, "Vouchsafe, O Lord."*

*At the Aposticha: Idiomelon Sticheron, Tone 7:*[^1761]
Even as he that fell among thieves and was wounded, so have I also fallen through many sins, and my soul is wounded: Unto whom shall I flee to be healed? Unto Thee, the Physician of souls and bodies: Pour out upon me, O God, Thy great mercy!

*Another Idiomelon, Tone 4:*[^1762]
*Verse:* Unto Thee have I lifted up mine eyes, O Thou that dwellest in heaven (Ps. 122:1 LXX).*
Having sinned through transgression, we have been cast out from the former sweetness and delight of paradise into a most dishonorable life; for having been stripped of the fitting and praiseworthy life of virtues by our transgressions, we have fallen as it were among thieves, and we are half dead...

*(fol. 633)*
...having sinned against Thy saving commandments. But we beseech Thee, O Master, Who didst appear from Mary and didst approach the Passions without passion: Heal our wounds that have come upon us through sin, and pour out upon us Thine unconquerable compassion, Thy healing care, as Thou art the Lover of mankind!

*Verse:* Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us: for we are utterly filled with contempt (Ps. 122:3 LXX).* *Martyrikon:*
O Lover of mankind, Who didst accept the endurance of the holy Martyrs: Receive from us also our hymnody, and grant us through their intercessions great mercy!

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*[^1763]
From every danger preserve Thy servants, O blessed Theotokos, that we may glorify thee, the hope of our souls!

## ON TUESDAY OF THE SIXTH WEEK OF THE HOLY FAST[^1764]

*At Matins, we chant Kathisma 14: "Give ear, O my people" (Ps. 77 LXX). After it, Sessional Hymn from the Octoechos. Then Kathisma 15: "Incline Thine ear, O Lord" (Ps. 85 LXX). And Sessional Hymn by Lord Joseph, Tone 3, Podoben: "Of divine faith" (Боже́ственныя вѣ́ры):*[^1765]
With the warmth of the faith of abstinence, let us burn up the passions of incontinence, and flee from the slip of sin, and with drops of tears extinguish the eternal flame, crying aloud: O all-good One, we have sinned against Thee: cleanse us, and grant us great mercy!

*Glory: the same. Both now: Theotokion:*
Thou wast the divine Tabernacle of the Word, O only all-pure Mother of God, surpassing the angels in purity! Me, who above all have become wretched through fleshly sins, cleanse through thine intercessions, granting by divine nod, O pure one, great mercy!

*(fol. 634)*
*After the third Stychology, Kathisma 16: "It is a good thing to give praise" (Ps. 91 LXX).*
*Sessional Hymn by Lord Theodore, Tone 2, Podoben: "Most blessed art thou" (Пребл҃гослове́на є҆сѝ):*[^1766]
All-blessed is the grace of the all-honorable fast! For by it Elijah the Prophet found a chariot of fire, and Moses received the tablets of the Law, and Daniel became marvelous, Elisha raised the dead, and the Children quenched the fire, and whosoever by it is drawn unto God. Nourishing ourselves therewith, let us cry aloud: Blessed is Christ our God, Who hast thus been well-pleased! *(Twice).*

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*
Having acquired thine invincible intercession in tribulations, being delivered from them that afflict me beyond hope marvelously, O Mother of God; for thou ever hastenest unto them that entreat thee with faith, and loosest the besetting temptations. Therefore gratefully I cry unto thee: Receive, O Sovereign Lady, my brief thanksgiving, in return for thy being unto me an helper in all things, O Virgin!

*Triodion [Joseph], Tone 3. Ode 2. Heirmos:*[^1767]
*"Give ear, O heaven and earth, and listen unto my voice: for I proclaim unto them that are upon earth the marvelous works of God!"*

*Troparion:* With unceasing prayers, with abstinence and vigilance, let us lend wings to our souls toward divine desire!

*Troparion:* Having fled the precipices of incontinence, let us all be made bright by the light of abstinence in divine works!

*Troparion:* Having cast off the sinful stench by the salt of divine virtues, O my soul, cleave unto God!

*Theotokion:*
Christ rested in thee, the only blessed one, and took His flesh from thee!

*(fol. 635)*
*Another Canon [Theodore], Tone 2. Ode 2. Heirmos: "Give ear, O people" (Внемли́те лю́дїе):*[^1768]
*Troparion:* Having united pure fasting, prayers, tears, meditation on the divine Scriptures, and every other virtue, let us now offer them unto the Master Christ!

*Troparion:* Eve was cast out through tasting of the fruit: Take heed, O my soul, be not deceived, if the serpent ever draw near to counsel thee to eat the pleasurable fruits!

*Trinity Hymn:* I glorify the tri-hypostatic countenances, Father, and Son, and Spirit, one dominion of the Godhead, the Kingdom and Deity of all!

*Theotokion:* Thy childbearing, O pure one, was fearsome; for God is He Who became man, begotten of the Father without beginning, and born of thee in the last times without a man!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*
*Troparion:* Thou didst heal the woman with the issue of blood by the touch of Thy garments (Matt. 9:20–22); heal me also, O my Christ, who touch Thy mercy with faith, and make me whole from passions!

*Katavasia: "Give ear, O people, to the signs of the works of My divine power, and understand this, that I alone am the God of all!"*[^1769]

*Canon of the Triodion [Joseph], Tone 3. Ode 8. Heirmos: "By angels" (Ѿ А҆́гглъ):*[^1770]
*Troparion:* In the secret ambush of hunting, the all-wicked one seeks to destroy me and make me his prey: From his malice deliver me, O Savior, Who didst save Jonah from the whale (Jonah 2:1–10)!

*Troparion:* Having purified ourselves through fasting, let us ascend the mountain of virtues, and we shall clearly hear what God will say within us; for He will speak peace and illumination and healing unto the contrite of heart (Ps. 84:9 LXX)!

*Troparion:* Ever blinded by the darkness of sin, I cannot comprehend Thy wonders, O Lord; therefore open the eyes of my heart, O Jesus, Giver of light!

*(fol. 636)*
*Theotokion:* By the sprinklings of thy tender mercies, O ever-undefiled Virgin, wash away the passionate defilements of my heart, granting me streams of tears that bestow purity of soul!

*Another Canon [Theodore], Tone 2. Ode 8. Heirmos: "Of old Thou didst bedew" (Дре́вле ѡ҆роси́):*[^1771]
*Troparion:* The fire shall not be quenched, and the worm, He says, does not end (Mark 9:44): Fear the threat, O my soul, entreating Christ, that thou mayest find delight where the dwelling of all that rejoice is found!

*Troparion:* By Thy touch, raise up by Thy mercy my soul consumed by the burning of lusts, O Lord, even as Peter’s mother-in-law (Matt. 8:14–15), that she may be found serving Thee well-pleasingly, and confessing Thee unto all ages!

*We bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit: the Lord.*
*Trinity Hymn:* The co-eternal, unoriginate Father let us, the faithful, hymn, and the co-unoriginate Son, and the Spirit proceeding from the Father: consubstantial Hypostases, of one all-powerful principle and dominion!

*Theotokion:* O Mary, called of God, truly the purification of the faithful! For from thee forgiveness is richly bestowed upon all: Cease not to entreat Thy Son and Lord for those that hymn thee!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*
*Troparion:* Open the deafened ears of my soul, O Christ, and make my tongue clear, even as of old for the stammerer and deaf man (Mark 7:32–35), that listening unto Thy words I may sing, and with my tongue praise Thee unto all ages!

*We praise, we bless, and we worship the Lord.*
*Katavasia: "Of old the Lord, Who bedewed the Hebrew Children in the flame, and wonderfully burned up the Chaldeans therein, let us hymn, saying: Bless Him and highly exalt Him unto all ages!"*[^1772]

*(fol. 637)*
*Canon of the Triodion [Joseph], Tone 3. Ode 9. Heirmos: "Thee Who wast unburnt" (Тебѐ неѡпали́мꙋю):*[^1773]
*Troparion:* Having acquired in mind the flame of unquenchable fire, with fervent thoughts let us now draw near to the fire of repentance, burning up the passions!

*Troparion:* The word born of old from the mouth of them that fasted, going forth zealously, bows the bodily members: Emulate this, O my soul, and live righteously!

*Troparion:* Meditating upon the fearsome judgment seat, O my most wretched soul, ever adorn thy steps toward the fulfillment of the will of the Deliverer!

*Theotokion:*
Enlighten my soul darkened by the blackness of pleasures, O pure one, who didst bear the Light, that with love and faith I may ever magnify thee!

*Another Canon [Theodore], Tone 2. Ode 9. Heirmos: "Beyond nature in the flesh" (Па́че є҆стества̀ пло́тїю):*[^1774]
*Troparion:* Let us present every member of our flesh unto Christ as weapons of righteousness, lifting up, he says, holy hands without wrath and disputing (1 Tim. 2:8)!

*Troparion:* Standing of old in the boat with the Disciples, O my Christ, Thou didst calm the raging sea (Matt. 8:23–27): Calm also the surging billows of my thoughts!

*Trinity Hymn:* Worshipping the one nature, I hymn three hypostases of the one God of all, Father, and Son, and Holy Spirit, the co-eternal principle!

*Theotokion:*
O all-pure one, thou bearest a child, and, a Virgin, thou feedest with milk! How dost thou accomplish both in the same? God is He that wrought it; ask me not how!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*
*Troparion:* From the robber-passions that have defiled my soul...

*(fol. 638)*
...heal my soul, O my Christ, pouring out Thy mercy, even as for him who fell into the hands of thieves![^1775]

*Katavasia: "Thee Who beyond nature in the flesh didst conceive in the womb the Word Who shone forth timelessly from the Father, in unceasing hymns we, the faithful, magnify!"*[^1776]

*Then the Exapostilarion, Tone...*

*At the Aposticha: Idiomelon, Tone 7:*[^1777]
Visit my wounded and humbled soul, O Lord, Physician of the sick, and unstormed haven of the despairing; for Thou art the Redeemer Who camest into the world to raise up the fallen from corruption: Raise me up also who fall down before Thee, according to Thy great mercy! *(Twice).*

*With the usual verses: "We were filled in the morning with Thy mercy, O Lord..." (Ps. 89:14 LXX).*
*Martyrikon:*
In the midst of the tribunal of the lawless, the passion-bearers cried aloud rejoicing: O Lord, glory to Thee!

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*
We hymn thee, O all-undefiled Theotokos, and we glorify God the Word Whom thou didst bear, crying aloud: Glory to Thee!

*At the First Hour, we recite Kathisma 14: "Hear my prayer, O Lord, and let my cry come unto Thee" (Ps. 101 LXX).*[^1778]
*At the Third Hour, Kathisma 15: "Give thanks unto the Lord, for He is good" (Ps. 104 LXX).*
*At the Sixth Hour, Kathisma 16: "The Lord said unto my Lord: Sit Thou at My right hand" (Ps. 109 LXX).*

*On Tuesday of the Fifth Week, At the Sixth Hour.*[^1779]
*Troparion of the Prophecy, Tone 3:*
The God of Jacob is our protector and defender in the day of affliction!

*Glory: the conclusion. Both now: the whole troparion.*

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 87, Tone 6:* I am poor and in troubles from my youth (Ps. 87:16 LXX).[^1780]
*Verse:* And being exalted, I was humbled and exhausted (Ps. 87:16 LXX).*

*(fol. 639)*
*Reading from the Prophecy of Isaiah (Isa. 40:18–28):*[^1781]
Thus saith the Lord: To whom have ye likened the Lord, and with what likeness have ye compared Him? Has not a woodcrafter made an image, or a goldsmith, having melted gold, gilded it, or made it as an image? For the woodcrafter chooses wood that will not rot, and the wise man inquires how he shall set up an image so that it be not shaken. Know ye not? Have ye not heard? Has it not been told you from the beginning? Have ye not understood the foundations of the earth? It is He that holds the circle of the earth, and its inhabitants are as grasshoppers; Who has set up the heaven as a vault and stretched it out as a tent to dwell in; Who gives princes as nothing to rule, and has made the earth as nothing. For they shall not sow, neither shall they plant, nor shall their root be rooted in the earth: He blew upon them when they were parched, and a whirlwind shall take them away like stubble. To whom then have ye likened Me, and unto whom shall I be exalted? saith the Holy One. Lift up your eyes on high, and see Who has shown all these things: He that brings out His world by number, He will call them all by name by the greatness of His glory, and in the dominion of His strength nothing has escaped Thee. For lest thou shouldst say, O Jacob, and why hast thou spoken, O Israel: My way is hidden from God, and my God has taken away my judgment, and departed? And now, hast thou not known, or hast thou not heard, that the everlasting God, the God Who formed the ends of the earth, shall not hunger, neither shall He be weary, and there is no searching out of His wisdom?

*(fol. 640)*
He gives strength to them that hunger, and grief to them that are not sorrowful; for the youths shall hunger, and the young men shall be weary, and the chosen shall be strong: But they that wait upon the Lord shall renew their strength![^1782]

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 88, Tone 6:* Blessed are the people that know the festal shout (Ps. 88:16 LXX).[^1783]
*Verse:* O Lord, in the light of Thy countenance shall they walk (Ps. 88:16 LXX).*

*Concerning the Martyrs and concerning the Annunciation of the Most Holy Theotokos: (see fol. 644).[^1784]*

*At the Ninth Hour, we recite Kathisma 17: "Praise ye the name of the Lord" (Ps. 134 LXX).*[^1785]

*On the same Tuesday of the Sixth [Fifth] Week, at Vespers:*[^1786]
*Kathisma 18, the usual. At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera by Lord Joseph.*

*Tone 8, Podoben: "What shall we call you" (Что́ вы нарече́мъ):*[^1787]
Making love our food, let us, the faithful, restrain our passions by abstinence, and lead our lives pleasingly unto God Who was lifted up upon the Cross for our sake and pierced in the side with a spear, that rejoicing we may receive eternal delight, glorifying the Savior of our souls!

Of old through the tree we found death, but now again life through the Tree of the Cross! Let us, the faithful, put to death the surges of passions, and entreat the Bestower of good unto all to attain unto the saving Resurrection, shining with divine deeds and adorned with virtues, glorifying the Savior of our souls!

*Another Sticheron, by Lord Theodore. Tone 2, Podoben: "Higher than the mind" (Па́че ꙋ҆ма́):*[^1788]
We praise Thy life-giving Cross, O Lord, and the Sufferings of Thy sacred flesh endured for our sake: the spear, the slaying, the sponge, and the reed, the mockings and spitting, the buffeting, and the robe of purple, and the crown woven of thorns, whereby from the curse...

*(fol. 641)*
...having delivered all, Thou hast saved us: Therefore we beseech Thee, grant us peacefully to finish the remaining time of the fast![^1789]

*Then, 2 Martyrika.*

*At Vespers, Prokeimenon, Psalm 89, Tone 4:* Lord, Thou hast been our refuge in generation and generation (Ps. 89:1 LXX).[^1790]
*Verse:* Before the mountains came to be, or the earth and the world were formed (Ps. 89:2 LXX).*

*Reading from the Book of Genesis (Gen. 15:1–9):*[^1791]
The word of the Lord came unto Abram in a vision by night, saying: Fear not, Abram: I protect thee; thy reward shall be exceedingly great. And Abram said: Master and Lord, what wilt Thou give me, seeing I go childless, and the son of Masek my domestic maid is this Eliezer of Damascus? And Abram said: Since Thou hast given me no seed, behold, my domestic servant shall be mine heir. And immediately the voice of the Lord came unto him, saying: This one shall not be thine heir; but he that shall come forth out of thee, he shall be thine heir. And He brought him forth abroad, and said unto him: Look up now toward heaven, and count the stars, if thou be able to number them. And He said: So shall thy seed be. And Abram believed God, and it was reckoned unto him for righteousness. And He said unto him: I am God Who brought thee out of the land of the Chaldeans, to give thee this land to inherit it. And he said: Master and Lord, whereby shall I know that I shall inherit it? And He said unto him: Take Me an heifer of three years old, and a ram of three years old, and a she-goat of three years old, and a turtledove...

*(fol. 642)*
...and a young pigeon. And he took unto him all these, and divided them in the midst, and set them piece opposite piece; but the birds he divided not. And birds of prey came down upon the carved carcasses of them, and Abram sat down beside them. And about the setting of the sun, a trance fell upon Abram; and, behold, a great and dark fear fell upon him. And it was said unto Abram: Knowing thou shalt know that thy seed shall be a stranger in a land that is not theirs, and they shall enslave them, and afflict them, and humble them four hundred years. And also that nation, whom they shall serve, will I judge: and afterward shall they come out hither with great substance. And thou shalt go to thy fathers in peace, sustained in a good old age.[^1792]

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 90, Tone 4:* He that dwells in the help of the Most High shall abide in the shelter of the God of heaven (Ps. 90:1 LXX).[^1793]
*Verse:* He will say unto the Lord: Thou art my protector and my refuge (Ps. 90:2 LXX).*

*Reading from the Proverbs (Prov. 15:7–13):*[^1794]
The lips of the wise are bound with discretion, but the hearts of fools are not steadfast. The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination to the Lord, but the prayers of the upright are acceptable. The ways of the ungodly are an abomination to the Lord, but He loves those that pursue righteousness. The correction of the simple is known by passers-by, but they that hate reproofs die basely. Hades and destruction are manifest before the Lord; how much more also the hearts of men? An uninstructed man loves not those that reprove him, neither will he converse with the wise. When the heart rejoices...

*(fol. 643)*
...the face blooms, but when it is in sorrow, it is dejected. An upright heart seeks understanding, but the mouth of the untaught knows evils. At all times the eyes of the wicked expect evils, but good men are ever quiet. Better is a small portion with the fear of the Lord, than great treasures without fear. Better is an entertainment of herbs with love and grace, than a setting forth of fatted calves with enmity. A passionate man stirs up strife, but a longsuffering man pacifies even a strife that is to come. A longsuffering man quenches lawsuits, but an ungodly man stirs them up rather. The ways of the sluggards are strewn with thorns, but those of the manly are made smooth.[^1795]

*After "Vouchsafe, O Lord."*

*At the Aposticha: Idiomelon, Tone 5:*[^1796]
Wretched as I am, I slipped away from Thy right way through passions, and fell into a pit; and the Levite and the Priest, passing by, disregarded me: But Thou, O Christ, having had mercy on me, and having torn up the handwriting of sins with the weapon of the Cross, hast extinguished [my passions] by passionlessness, and made me a co-heir with the Father! Therefore I cry unto Thee: O incomprehensible Lord, glory to Thee!

*Another Sticheron, Tone 8:*[^1797]
*Verse:* Unto Thee have I lifted up mine eyes, O Thou that dwellest in heaven (Ps. 122:1 LXX).*
I went down from Jerusalem, slipping away from Thy commandments that were written therein by the tongues, and going down to Jericho with like impulse, wherein of old for their wickedness against Thee, Thy people were delivered unto murder for disobedience; I gave myself up unto soul-corrupting passions as unto robbers, and by them was wounded and left half-dead: [O Christ,] Who with nails...

*(fol. 644)*
...and spear wast willingly wounded in the flesh for the sake of human sin, and Who didst accomplish the common salvation by the Cross in Jerusalem: Heal me, O Lord, and save me![^1798]

*Verse 2:* Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us: for we are utterly filled with contempt (Ps. 122:3 LXX).*
*Martyrikon:*
Thy Martyrs, O Lord, forgetting the things of this life, disregarded tortures for the sake of the life to come, and were revealed as heirs thereof; therefore they also rejoice with the Angels: Through their prayers grant Thy people great mercy!

*Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion:*
O Lord, when the sun beheld Thee hanging upon the Tree, the Sun of righteousness, it hid its rays, and the moon turned its light into darkness; and the all-undefiled Mother was consumed in her maternal heart!

*Instruction: If the Annunciation of the Most Holy Theotokos fall on Wednesday of the Fifth Week of the Fast (Chapter 85):*[^1799]
*We chant the service of the Forefeast of the Annunciation: Stichera and the Canon in the Triodion. But for the saint of the day in the Menaion, we chant at Compline. For the Great Canon is transferred from Thursday to Tuesday of the same week; and we chant the Great Canon with the Tuesday Triodion on account of the Feast of the Most Holy Theotokos. For on Wednesday, on the very day of the Feast, there is no Kathisma and we make no prostrations; and we chant the Apodosis of the Feast; and on that account on Wednesday evening the Stichera with prostrations and the Great Canon are not chanted on Thursday.*
*On Wednesday of the Fifth Week of the Fast: We chant the entire service in the evening of the Feast and in the morning with the Triodion according to the Typikon, as indicated (see fol. 474),[^1800] Chapter 4.*
*And we chant the Apodosis of the Annunciation on Thursday at Matins, with the Triodion of the Great Canon, with the Aposticha. And we chant the Canon of the Feast with the Octoechos and with the Archangel, as is indicated (see fol. 622),[^1801] Chapter 84 of Mark, in the Triodion on the Apodosis of the Feast of the Annunciation.*

*(fol. 645)*
## ON WEDNESDAY OF THE FIFTH WEEK OF THE HOLY FAST[^1802]

*At Matins, we recite three Kathismata.*
*After the first Stychology, Kathisma 19: "Blessed be the Lord my God" (Ps. 143 LXX).*[^1803]
*Sessional Hymn from the Octoechos. After the second Stychology,*
*First Kathisma: "Blessed is the man" (Ps. 1 LXX).*
*Sessional Hymn by Lord Joseph.*
*Tone 4, Podoben: "The commanded mystery" (Повеле́нное та́инство):*[^1804]
Adam, having tasted of the tree, bitterly reaped the fruits of the unseemliness of incontinence; but being lifted up upon the Tree, O compassionate One, Thou didst deliver him from grievous condemnation: Therefore we cry aloud unto Thee: Grant us also to abstain, O Master, from the corrupting fruit, and to do Thy will, that we may find mercy!

*Glory: the same. Both now... Stavrotheotokion:*
Preserved by the Cross of Thy Son and God, O Virgin, we ever conquer the demonic assaults and craftiness, hymning thee as the true Theotokos, and in love all generations call thee blessed, O pure one, even as thou didst foretell: Therefore grant forgiveness of our transgressions through thy prayers!

*After the third Stychology, Kathisma 2: "I will confess Thee, O Lord" (Ps. 9 LXX).*[^1805]
*Sessional Hymn by Lord Theodore. Tone 1, Podoben: "Unto Thine all-pure icon" (Пре́чⷭ҇томꙋ ти ѡ҆́бразꙋ):*[^1806]
Let us hymn the all-holy Tree of the Cross, ever worshipping Thine utter goodness, O Christ God; for upon it Thou didst abolish the enemy's powers and gavest a sign unto them that believe in Thee: Therefore gratefully we cry unto Thee: Vouchsafe all who live in good cheer and peace to finish the season of the fast! *(Twice).*

*Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion:*

*(fol. 646)*
The undefiled Ewe, beholding the Shepherd lifted up upon the Tree, weeping cried aloud with a mother's grief: O Son, an ungrateful people has condemned Thee unto death, in return for Thy spreading a cloud for their passage! Woe is me, who was once great and now am childless! But arise, and be the Sun of all, glorifying Thyself in holy earthborn men![^1807]

*Triodion by Lord Joseph, Tone 8.*
*Ode 3. Heirmos: "O Maker of the vault of heaven" (Не́бномꙋ крꙋ́гꙋ):*[^1808]
*Troparion:* Condemning enmity, Thou didst stretch out Thy hands upon the Cross, O righteous Judge: Now therefore save me, the prodigal, who am condemned by transgressions, O Savior, who have embittered Thee, the longsuffering One!

*Troparion:* I have desired a brutish life producing passions; I have departed from Thy commandments, O all-good Savior, enslaved by foreign and unclean citizens: But now receive me turning back, and save me!

*Troparion:* Even as of old Thou didst open the hearing of the stammerer, open the ears of my soul deafened by evil disposition, and vouchsafe me to hear Thy saving word, O Jesus, only Lover of mankind!

*Theotokion:*
Saving door unto God, bridge for Christians, protectress, O all-pure Sovereign Lady! Guide me who am surrounded by the sorrows of life and mistreated, O Maiden!

*Another Canon [Theodore], Tone 2. Ode 3. Heirmos: "My barren mind" (Непло́днаго ми ꙋ҆ма̀):*[^1809]
*Troparion:* Through the compassions of Thy tender mercies, having ascended the Cross, Thou hast drawn me out from the pit of passions, and hast exalted me, O Christ, unto heavenly realms.

*Troparion:* Thou didst stretch out Thy palms upon the Cross, O Jesus, and didst gather Thy nations that were far off from Thee, to stand near unto Thy dominion.

*(fol. 647)*
*Trinity Hymn:* Tri-hypostatic Unity, consubstantial Trinity, one Godhead: Father, and Son, and right Spirit, save them that honor Thee![^1810]

*Theotokion:*
Who among the earthborn can worthily praise thee, O Virgin Mother? For among women thou alone hast appeared chosen and all-blessed!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*
*Troparion:* Thou wast lifted up upon the Cross, Thou wast pierced in the side, Thou didst taste gall for my sake, O Jesus, who through transgression embittered Thee!

*Katavasia: "Show my barren mind to be fruitful, O God, Husbandman of souls and Planter of good things, by Thy tender mercy!"*[^1811]

*Triodion [Theodore], Tone 2. Ode 8. Heirmos: "Seven times as much" (Се́дмъ седми́цею):*[^1812]
*Troparion:* Looking upon me with Thine unslumbering eye, have compassion on me who am possessed by the slumber of despondency, and who serve sleep upon the pleasurable bed of passions, O Thou Who didst bow Thy head upon the Cross, and willingly fell asleep, and didst dispel the darkness of sin, O Christ, being the Light of righteousness!

*Troparion:* Adorned with enriching gifts from baptism, I loved evil servitude, and I, wretched one, became a stranger to virtues, having departed into a far country of malice: Therefore turn me back and receive me, O Savior, protecting me by Thy Cross unto all ages!

*Troparion:* Cast away the drunkenness of passions, and seek tears, the cleansing fasting, O soul, the wine that gladdens the heart and anoints the soul, quenching the furnaces of the flesh: Strive to be crucified together with Christ Who was nailed upon the Tree for thy sake, and to live unto ages!

*Theotokion:*
O all-pure Mother of God, [heal] the wounds of my soul...

*(fol. 648)*
...and to cleanse the purulent sores of sin, pouring forth fountains from the side of Thy Childbearing,[^1813] and cleansing with streams from them; for unto thee I cry aloud, unto thee I flee for refuge, and thee I entreat, O full of grace!

*Another Heirmos [Tone 2]: "In voices of angels" (Въ гла́сѣхъ А҆́гг҃лскихъ):*[^1814]
*Troparion:* Praise ye Jesus, Who was crucified in the flesh and suffered not in His Godhead, ye angels and earthborn, unto all ages!

*Troparion:* In Thy Crucifixion, O Christ, having accepted a shameful death, Thou hast saved me, wretched one, delivering me from corruption.

*We bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, the Lord. Trinity Hymn:*[^1815]
In cherubic manner, O Trinity, I hymn Thee: "Holy, Holy, Holy!" one Godhead, without beginning and simple, and incomprehensible unto all!

*Theotokion:*
With praises all generations radiantly honor thee, O pure one, for thou didst bear the Creator. O awesome wonder, and most blessed deed!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*
*Troparion:* Thou didst endure all things willingly, desiring to save me, O Christ; I hymn Thy Crucifixion, the nails and the slaughter, unto all ages!

*We praise, we bless, we worship the Lord.*
*Katavasia. Heirmos: "Let us, all the earthborn, praise unto all ages Him Who is glorified in voices of angels in the heavens!"*[^1816]

*Ode 9. Heirmos: "The heaven was amazed" (У҆диви́сѧ ꙋ҆́бѡ):*[^1817]
*Troparion:* Beholding Thee stretched out upon the Cross, O King of all, a dark glow covered the sun, and the whole earth bowed down in trembling, seeing Thee willingly suffering, Who art by nature impassible: Therefore I pray Thee: Heal the passions of my soul, as a physician, O Christ!

*Troparion:* I have abandoned the ways of salvation, and have walked in those leading unto Hades, having bitter darkness round about me, the sweetness *(fol. 649)*
and slipping of passions, and a tempest of thoughts: Therefore I pray Thee: By Thy Cross save me, O Christ, as the only One Most Merciful!

*Troparion:* Held fast by the winter of temptations, submerged in the surge of passions, and grievously battered by the wave of pleasures, I have reached the calm and quiet deep of the fast; steering me therein by Thy Cross, O compassionate One, direct me unto salvation!

*Theotokion:*
Thou didst conceive without seed, O Virgin, the Word of God Who fashioned all things, without fleshly desire, and without corruption thou didst bear Him without a mother's pangs: Therefore, confessing thee in tongue and heart as the Theotokos, we magnify thee!

*Another Heirmos [Tone 2]: "Thy virginity, O Theotokos" (Дѣ́тво твоѐ Бцⷣе):*[^1818]
*Troparion:* Willingly Thou didst endure to be crucified, O our Savior, that Thou mightest grant life unto all, delivering them from death.

*Troparion:* By the tree I was put to death, and by the Tree of the Cross I have been made alive, upon which Thou, my Christ, having been nailed, didst slay my enemy.

*Trinity Hymn:* As the Son Who is with the Father, and having the Holy Spirit as Counselor, we magnify Thee with one power.

*Theotokion:*
A most glorious wonder, an awesome hearing! How, even as a Mother, dost thou bear a child, O pure one, and hast not known corruption, as a Virgin!

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*
*Troparion:* I hymn Thy spear, I sing of Thy nails, the sponge and the reed with the Cross, whereby Thou hast saved me, O Jesus God!

*Katavasia. Heirmos: "Thy spotless virginity, O Theotokos, which the fire of the Godhead did not burn, with unceasing hymns we magnify."*[^1819]

*Then, "It is truly meet". Exapostilarion, Tone...*

*At the Aposticha: Idiomelon Sticheron, Tone 8:*[^1820]
By robber-like thoughts was I wounded, wretched one, *(fol. 650)*
and was left barely alive, O Lord! The prophetic choir, looking past me and seeing me half dead, and incurable by human arts;[^1821] therefore, grievously suffering, in humility of heart I cry unto Thee, O Christ God: As Thou art tenderly compassionate, pour out Thy great mercy upon me!

*Tone 3. Verse: "We were filled in the morning with Thy mercy, O Lord, and we rejoiced and were glad" (Ps. 89:14 LXX).*[^1822]
*Sticheron:* Having abandoned the height of virtues, O my soul, thou didst descend into the depth of sin, having fallen among evil robbers, and being full of foul-smelling sores, thou liest cast down and speechless: Therefore cry aloud, O soul, unto Christ God Who was crucified for thee and willingly received wounds: Care for me, O Savior, and save me!

*Verse 2: "And let the brightness of the Lord our God be upon us, and direct Thou the works of our hands upon us" (Ps. 89:17 LXX). Martyrikon:*[^1823]
The powers of the holy angels marveled at the sufferings of the martyrs; for, compassed with the body, they took no thought of tortures, having become imitators of the sufferings of Christ the Savior, and they pray for us, that our souls may be saved.

*Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion:*
Beholding Him Who was born of thee hanging upon the Tree, O all-immaculate one, thou didst weep, crying aloud: "Woe is me, O Sun of glory! How has the beauty full of fragrance gone down, of Thee Who didst adorn the nature of mankind!"

*At the First Hour: Stychology: Kathisma 13 [Kathisma 3]: "I will love Thee, O Lord" (Ps. 17 LXX).*[^1824]
*At the Third Hour, 14 [Kathisma 4]: "Unto Thee, O Lord, have I lifted up my soul" (Ps. 24 LXX).*
*At the Sixth Hour, 15 [Kathisma 5]: "Rejoice in the Lord, O ye righteous" (Ps. 32 LXX).*

*On the same Wednesday: At the Sixth Hour, Troparion of the Prophecy:*[^1825]
*Tone 4:* Entreated by the sufferings which the saints endured for Thy sake, *(fol. 651)*
O Lord, heal all our illnesses, O Lover of mankind, we beseech Thee![^1826]
*Glory: the end [chanted]. Both now: the same.*

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 91 LXX. Tone 4:*[^1827]
It is good to give praise unto the Lord, and to chant unto Thy name, O Most High!
*Verse:* To proclaim Thy mercy in the morning, and Thy truth by night (Ps. 91:3 LXX).

*Reading from the Prophecy of Isaiah (Chapter 41):*[^1828]
Thus says the Lord: I God am the first, [v. 4] and unto the things that come after, I am. The nations saw and feared; [v. 5] the ends of the earth were terrified; they drew near and came together. Each one judging [v. 6] for his neighbor, and desiring to help his brother, and he shall say: "Be strong!" The carpenter and the coppersmith striking with the hammer [v. 7] weakened [the iron] together; then shall he say: "The joining is good!" They fastened it with nails; they will place them, and they shall not be moved. But thou, Israel, art My servant, [v. 8] Jacob whom I have chosen, the seed of Abraham whom I loved; whom I took from the ends of the earth, [v. 9] and called thee from its high places, and said unto thee: "Thou art My servant; I have chosen thee and have not forsaken thee." Fear not, for I am with thee; be not deceived, for I am [v. 10] thy God Who has strengthened thee; and I have helped thee, and have established thee with My righteous right hand. Behold, all that oppose thee shall be put to shame [v. 11] and confounded; for they shall be as though they were not, and all thine adversaries shall perish. Thou shalt seek them, and shalt not find them—the men [v. 12] who contend with thee insolently; for they shall be as though they were not, and they that fight against thee shall not be. For I am thy God, Who holds thy right hand, [v. 13] Who says *(fol. 652)*
unto thee: "Fear not, I am thy helper!" Fear not, thou worm Jacob, thou meager Israel! [v. 14] I have helped thee, says thy God, the Holy One of Israel Who redeems thee.[^1829]

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 92 LXX. Tone 6:*[^1830]
The Lord is King, and He has clothed Himself with majesty!
*Verse:* The Lord has clothed Himself with power and girded Himself (Ps. 92:1 LXX).

*At the Ninth Hour: Stychology: Kathisma 16 [Kathisma 6]: "O Lord, rebuke me not in Thine anger" (Ps. 37 LXX).*[^1831]
*On the same Wednesday of the Mid-Fast [Fifth Week]. At Vespers, instead of "Unto the Lord when I was in affliction": Stychology: Kathisma 17 [Kathisma 7]: "Clap your hands, all ye nations" (Ps. 46 LXX).*

*At "Lord, I have cried": Set 30 stichoi, beginning from: "They shall fall into their net" (Ps. 140:10 LXX):*[^1832]

*Idiomelon Sticheron, Tone 8:*[^1833]
Having fallen among robbers by my own thoughts, I was taken captive in mind, wretched one, and was grievously wounded, having injured my whole soul; and I lie utterly stripped of virtues on the path of life. The priest, seeing me suffering from incurable wounds, passed me by and looked not upon me; the Levite likewise, unable to bear soul-corrupting wounds, saw me and went by. But Thou Who wast well pleased to become incarnate, not from Samaria, but from Mary, O Christ God: in Thy love for mankind grant me healing, pouring out Thy great mercy upon me!

*Verse: "With my voice unto the Lord I cried, with my voice unto the Lord I made my supplication" (Ps. 141:2 LXX). Again the same.*

*Verse: "I will pour out my prayer before Him, my affliction before Him will I declare" (Ps. 141:3 LXX). Martyrikon:*[^1834]
If any virtue and if any praise befitting the saints: for by the sword they bent their necks for Thy sake Who didst bow the heavens and come down; they shed their blood for Thy sake Who didst empty Thyself and take the form of a servant; they humbled themselves unto death, imitating Thy poverty:

*(fol. 653)*
By their prayers, according to the multitude of Thy tender mercies, O God, have mercy on us![^1835]

*Tone 8, Podoben: "O Lord, though Thou didst stand before the tribunal" (Гдⷭ҇и а҆́ще на сꙋди́щи):*[^1836]
*Verse: "When my spirit was fainting within me, then Thou knewest my paths" (Ps. 141:4 LXX).*
*Sticheron 1:* O Lord, Thou didst reveal Thy sacred disciples as noetic heavens: By their sacred intercessions deliver me from earthly things, by abstinence ever lifting up my understanding from thoughts inclined unto passions, as Thou art compassionate and the Lover of mankind!

*Verse: "In the way wherein I walked have they privily laid a snare for me" (Ps. 141:4 LXX).*
*Sticheron 2:* Having all the season of the fast as a fellow helper unto godly deeds, let us weep from all the heart, and cry aloud unto the Savior: For the sake of Thy disciples, O most merciful Lord, save them that with fear hymn Thy great love for mankind![^1837]`

*Another Sticheron, by Lord Theodore, the same Tone [Tone 8]:*[^1838]
*Verse: "I looked upon my right hand, and beheld, but there was none that knew me" (Ps. 141:5 LXX).*
*Sticheron:* All-laudable Apostles, intercessors for the world, physicians of the sick, guardians of health! Preserve us at all times as we pass the season of the fast, divinely keeping peace in both [body and soul], delivering the powerless mind from passions, that we all may sing a hymn unto Christ risen, as Conqueror!

*Other Stichera, 24, of the Great Canon. The work of Lord Andrew of Crete, according to the Alphabet.*
*Tone 4, Podoben: "With tears I desired" (Хотѣ́хъ слеза́ми):*[^1839]
*Verse: "Refuge failed me, and there was none that cared for my soul" (Ps. 141:5 LXX).*
*Sticheron 1 [Alpha]:* All my life have I spent with harlots and publicans; shall I then be able at least in old age to repent of the things wherein I sinned, unto the Creator of *(fol. 654)*
all and Physician of the sick? O Lord, before I perish utterly, save me![^1840]

*And we make three prostrations at each verse.*[^1841]

*Verse: "I cried unto Thee, O Lord; I said: Thou art my hope, my portion in the land of the living" (Ps. 141:6 LXX).*
*Sticheron 2 [Beta]:* Held fast by the weight of negligence, wallowing in the mire, struck by the arrow of Beliar, I corrupt that which is according to Thine image, O Converter of the careless and Liberator of them that have sinned: O Lord, before I perish utterly, save me![^1842]

*Verse: "Attend unto my supplication, for I am brought very low" (Ps. 141:7 LXX).*
*Sticheron 3 [Gamma]:* I have become a stumbling-block unto men, having tilled earthly things as one earthly; by marriage I was joined according to Thy commandment, yet I transgressed and defiled my bed: O Thou Who didst form me from the earth, despise not Thine own creation! O Lord, before I perish utterly, save me![^1843]

*Verse: "Deliver me from them that persecute me, for they are stronger than I" (Ps. 141:7 LXX).*
*Sticheron 4 [Delta]:* I have become a tormentor unto my soul,[^1844] providing for it from the flesh; I have been set as a snare for demons, serving pleasures and indecency: In Thy tender mercy spare me, O Expeller of demons! O Lord, before I perish utterly, save me!

*Verse: "Bring my soul out of prison, that I may confess Thy name" (Ps. 141:8 LXX).*
*Sticheron 5 [Epsilon]:* Willingly have I sinned more than all, therefore have I been forsaken; I have an adversary unto my soul—the mind of the flesh—and it darkens me: O Light in darkness and Guide of the wandering! O Lord, before I perish utterly, save me![^1845]

*Verse: "The righteous shall wait for me, until Thou shalt recompense me" (Ps. 141:9 LXX).*

number me with Thy flock; grant me time for repentance, that groaning I may cry aloud unto Thee: O Lord, before I perish utterly, save me![^1847]

*Verse: "Out of the depths have I cried unto Thee, O Lord; Lord, hear my voice" (Ps. 129:1-2 LXX).*

*Verse: "From the morning watch until night, from the morning watch let Israel hope in the Lord" (Ps. 129:6 LXX).*
*Sticheron 11 [Lambda]:* O Thou Who didst dry up the lake of passions of the woman with the issue of blood by the touch of the hem of Thy garments![^1852] I shall receive remission of *(fol. 656)*
sins, fleeing unto Thee with unhesitating faith: Receive me also as her, and heal my diseases! O Lord, before I perish utterly, save me![^1853]

*Verse: "Praise the Lord, all ye nations; praise Him, all ye peoples" (Ps. 116:1 LXX).*
*Sticheron 13 [Nu]:* Look down with a compassionate eye, and be merciful unto me, O only Savior! Grant streams of healings unto my poor and wretched soul; wash away the filth of my deeds, that I may sing: O Lord, before I perish utterly, save me![^1855]

*Verse: "Unto Thee have I lifted up mine eyes, unto Thee that dwellest in heaven. Behold, as the eyes of servants look unto the hands of their masters, as the eyes of a maiden unto the hands of her mistress, so look our eyes unto the Lord our God, until He have compassion on us" (Ps. 122:1-2 LXX).*

*Verse: "Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us, for we are exceedingly filled with contempt; our soul is exceedingly filled: let reproach be to them that are at ease, and contempt to the proud" (Ps. 122:3-4 LXX).*

*(fol. 657)*
*Sticheron 16 [Pi]:* The harlot bedews Thy most pure and immaculate feet with tears,[^1858] exhorting all to hasten and receive remission of their sins: Grant that faith unto me also, O Savior, that I may cry aloud unto Thee: O Lord, before I perish utterly, save me!

*Unto the remaining [stichera] we chant as refrain: "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee."*[^1859]

O Lord, before I perish utterly, save me![^1860]

*Refrain: "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee."*
*Sticheron 18 [Sigma]:* Establish my soul, O Master, that it may flee unto Thee and serve Thee continually; for Thou art my protection and guardian, and help and defense: Vouchsafe me, O God the Word, to sing unto Thee in boldness: O Lord, before I perish utterly, save me![^1861]

*Refrain: "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee."*
*Sticheron 19 [Tau]:* Be Thou an unbreakable wall unto us, O Jesus Savior and merciful God! For, deceived by our dispositions and deeds, we have fallen: But raise up Thy creation, as Benefactor, and relent, as Thou art compassionate! O Lord, before I perish utterly, save me![^1862]

*Refrain: "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee."*
*Sticheron 20 [Upsilon]:* A prodigal son have I become, having squandered my wealth; now I waste away with hunger, and flee beneath Thy protection: Receive me as him, O Good Father, and vouchsafe me to be a partaker of Thy table, that I may cry aloud unto Thee: O Lord, before I perish utterly, save me![^1863]

*Refrain: "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee."*

*Both now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*

O ineffable condescension! O strange and most marvelous birthgiving! O how the Virgin carries Thee as an Infant in her arms—the Creator and God, Who wast well pleased to become incarnate of her, O Benefactor! O Lord, before I perish utterly, save me!

*Entrance. "O Gladsome Light". But if there be no Liturgy of the Presanctified:[^1867] At "Lord, I have cried" we chant in the Triodion 3 Podobni, and the 24 Stichera of the Great Canon. At the Aposticha: Idiomelon stichera of the day, 2; then: Glory... Both now... Theotokion. And the rest is omitted.*

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 93 LXX. Tone 6:*[^1868]
The Lord is the God of vengeances; the God of vengeances has acted outspokenly!
*Verse:* Be Thou exalted, O Judge of the earth; render retribution unto the proud (Ps. 93:1-2 LXX).

*Reading from the Book of Genesis (Chapter 17):*[^1869]
