Abram was ninety and nine years old; [v. 1] and the Lord appeared unto Abram, and said unto him: "I am Thy God; be well-pleasing before Me, and be thou blameless. And I will establish My covenant [v. 2] between Me and Thee, and I will multiply Thee exceedingly." And Abram fell upon his face, and God [v. 3] spoke unto him, saying: "As for Me, behold, My covenant [v. 4] is with Thee, and thou shalt be a father of many nations. And Thy name shall no more be called Abram, [v. 5] but Thy name shall be Abraham; for a father of many nations have I made Thee. And I will multiply Thee [v. 6] exceedingly, exceedingly, and I will make nations of Thee, and kings shall come out of Thee. And I will establish [v. 7] My covenant between Me and Thee, and between Thy seed after Thee throughout their generations for an everlasting covenant, to be God unto Thee, and unto Thy seed after Thee. And I will give unto Thee, and unto Thy seed after Thee, [v. 8] the land wherein thou sojournest, all the land of Canaan, for an everlasting possession; and I will be their God." And the Lord said unto Abraham: "Thou also shalt keep My covenant, [v. 9] thou and Thy seed after Thee throughout their generations."

*(fol. 660)*
*Prokeimenon, Psalm 95 LXX. Tone 4:*[^1870]
Sing unto the Lord a new song!
*Verse:* Sing unto the Lord, all the earth (Ps. 95:1 LXX).

*Reading from the Proverbs of Solomon (Chapter 15):*[^1871]
A wise son gladdens his father; but a foolish son scoffs at his mother. [v. 21] The paths of a senseless man are void of wisdom; but a wise man walks uprightly. [v. 22] The thoughts of them that honor not counsel are frustrated; but in the hearts of counselors counsel abides. [v. 23] The wicked man shall not listen unto it, nor shall he say anything useful, or good for the common weal. [v. 24] The paths of life are the thoughts of the wise man, that turning aside from Hades, he may be saved. [v. 25] The Lord pulls down the houses of the insolent; but He has established the border of the widows. [v. 26] An unrighteous thought is an abomination unto the Lord; but the words of the pure are honorable. [v. 27] A receiver of bribes destroys himself; but he that hates the taking of bribes shall be saved. [v. 28] By alms and faiths sins are cleansed; and by the fear of the Lord every man departs from evil. [v. 29] The hearts of the righteous meditate on faith; but the mouth of the ungodly answers evil things. [v. 30] The ways of righteous men are acceptable unto the Lord; for because of them even enemies become friends. [v. 31] God is far from the ungodly; but He hears the prayers of the righteous. [v. 32] Better is a small taking with righteousness, than great revenues with unrighteousness.
*(Chapter 16)*
Let the heart of a man devise righteous things, [v. 1] that his steps may be directed by God. An eye beholding good things gladdens the heart; [v. 2] and a good report makes the bones fat.

*(fol. 661)*
He that listens unto the reproofs of life shall dwell among the wise; and glory shall precede the humble.[^1872] [v. 3] He that turns away from instruction hates himself; but he that heeds reproofs loves his own soul. [v. 4] The fear of the Lord is instruction and wisdom, and the beginning of glory answers unto it; and glory shall precede the humble: unto man belongs the purpose of the heart, and from the Lord is the answer of the tongue. As much as thou art great, so much humble thyself, and before the Lord God thou shalt find grace. [v. 5] All the works of the humble are manifest before God; but the ungodly shall perish in the evil day. Commit thy works unto the Lord, and thy thoughts shall be established; the Lord has made all things for Himself, but the ungodly shall perish in the evil day. [v. 6] Everyone that is haughty in heart is unclean before the Lord; though hand join in hand unrighteously, he shall not be justified. [v. 7] The beginning of a good way is to do righteous things; and they are more acceptable with God than to sacrifice sacrifices. [v. 8] He that seeks the Lord shall find understanding with righteousness; [v. 9] and they that seek Him uprightly shall find peace. [v. 10] All the works of the Lord are with righteousness; but the ungodly is reserved for the evil day.

*Then: "Let my prayer be set forth". And in order, the Divine Liturgy of the Presanctified.*

*At the trapeza, we do not partake of oil, nor do we drink wine, on account of the labor of the vigil that is to be. And they that attend unto their salvation apply themselves unto abstinence, and especially unto unfeigned fasting.*[^1873]

*And we chant Small Compline in the cells without prostrations: after the Trisagion, the 24 [stichera] of Andrew's Canon.[^1874] Likewise also the Midnight Office. But the service of the Menaion is omitted, and is chanted at Compline.*

*If there happen to be on this Thursday a vigil [saint] of the Menaion: the canon of the Menaion is chanted for them in advance on Tuesday of the same week.*[^1875]

*(fol. 662)*
*If the Annunciation of the most holy Theotokos happen on that same Thursday: The Great Canon is chanted in advance on Tuesday of the same week, with the triodion of Tuesday. And the triodion of the Great Canon we chant with the feast of the Annunciation. The canon of the feast, with the heirmos, to 6, and the triodion to the Apostles, to 8, according to the Lenten order; and at the end, katavasia in the Triodion; and for the feast, the katavasia: "I will open my mouth".*[^1876]

## ON THURSDAY OF THE FIFTH WEEK OF THE HOLY FAST

*At Matins: In the fourth hour of the night, having gathered into the church, the beginning is made by the priest according to custom, and we read the Six Psalms; and after the Psalms we chant "Alleluia", and the Trinity Hymns of the tone. And we stychologize one Kathisma, 8 [Kathisma 8]: "Have mercy on me, O God, for man has trodden me down" (Ps. 55 LXX). And we say the sessional hymns in the Oktoechos: to the Apostles, 2, and the Martyrikon. Glory... Both now... Theotokion. And we read in Saint Ephrem. We read also the Life of Venerable Mary. Then Psalm 50. We do not stychologize the [Biblical] Canticles.*[^1877]
*And we begin the Great Canon with a contrite heart and fear. At each troparion, 3 metanias; for the canon is full of compunction and repentance. And when one choir chants, then the other makes prostrations, for the sake of good order. And the canon has 250 [troparia], and prostrations: 750.*[^1878]
*The work of Lord Andrew of Crete, the Hierosolymite.*
*Tone 6. Ode 1. Heirmos:*[^1879]
He was a Helper and Protector unto me for salvation; He is my God, and I will glorify Him, the God of my father, and I will exalt Him; for gloriously has He been glorified!

*Troparion:* Whence shall I begin to weep for the deeds of my passionate life? What beginning shall I lay, O Christ, unto my present lamentation? But as Thou art tenderly compassionate, grant me remission of sins!

*Troparion:* Come, O wretched soul, with thy flesh, confess unto the Fashioner of all, and abandon henceforth thy former unreason, and offer tears unto God in repentance!

*Troparion:* Having emulated the transgression of the first-formed Adam, *(fol. 663)*
I have recognized myself stripped of God, and of the everlasting kingdom and delight, on account of my sins!

*Troparion:* Woe is me, O wretched soul! Why hast thou likened thyself unto the first Eve? For evil didst thou see, and bitterly wast thou nourished, and thou didst touch the tree, and didst taste daringly of the irrational food![^1880]

*Troparion:* In place of sensory Eve, a noetic Eve has arisen within me—the passionate thought in the flesh, showing sweet things, yet ever tasting of a bitter drink!

*Troparion:* Worthily was Adam cast out of Eden, because he kept not Thy commandment, O Savior; but what shall I suffer, who ever cast away Thy life-giving words?

*Troparion:* Surpassing the murder of Cain, by choice I have become a murderer of the conscience of my soul, having quickened the flesh and warred against it by my wicked deeds!

*Troparion:* I have not been likened unto the righteousness of Abel, O Jesus; never have I offered acceptable gifts unto Thee: neither divine deeds, nor a pure sacrifice, nor a blameless life!

*Troparion:* As Cain, we also, O wretched soul, have offered unto the Creator of all defiled deeds and a flawed sacrifice, and an unprofitable life together; therefore have we also been condemned!

*Troparion:* Having made living clay, O Potter, Thou didst place within me flesh and bones, and breath and life; but O my Creator, my Deliverer, and my Judge: receive me who repent![^1881]

*Troparion:* I confess unto Thee, O Savior, the sins which I have committed, and the wounds of my soul and body, which murderous inner thoughts have robber-like laid upon me!

*(fol. 664)*
*Troparion:* Though I have sinned, O Savior, yet I know that Thou art the Lover of mankind; Thou chastisest with compassion, and art warmly merciful; Thou seest him that weeps, and runnest to meet him even as the father, calling back the prodigal!

*Troparion:* Being cast down, O Savior, before Thy gates, at least in mine old age cast me not empty into Hades; but before the end, as Thou art the Lover of mankind, grant me remission of my falls into sin!

*Troparion:* The one who fell among robbers by my thoughts am I, and wholly now have I been wounded by them and filled with sores; but do Thou Thyself, drawing near unto me, heal me, O Christ Savior![^1882]

*Troparion:* The priest, having seen me beforehand, passed me by, and the Levite, seeing me naked in grievous misery, looked past me; but O Jesus Who didst dawn forth from Mary, do Thou, standing by, have compassion on me!

*Troparion:* O Lamb of God, Who takest away the sins of all: take from me the heavy burden of sin, and as Thou art tenderly compassionate, grant me tears of compunction!

*Troparion:* It is the season of repentance; I come unto Thee, my Creator: take from me the heavy burden of sin, and as Thou art tenderly compassionate, grant me remission of sins!

*Troparion:* Abhor me not, O Savior; cast me not away from Thy presence: take from me the heavy burden of sin, and as Thou art tenderly compassionate, grant me remission of sins!

*Troparion:* Sins voluntary and involuntary, O Savior, manifest and hidden, known and unknown—having forgiven them all as God, cleanse and save me!

*Troparion:* From my youth, O Savior, have I transgressed Thy commandments; in all passionate carelessness, in despondency have I passed my life: therefore I cry unto Thee, O Savior: At least in the end save me![^1883]

*(fol. 665)*
...[from] shameful [passions], and reveal us that with faith and love magnificently hymn thee as partakers of the Kingdom of Christ now, we pray![^1884]

*Trinity Hymn:* O transcendent Trinity, worshipped in unity, take from me the heavy burden of sin, and as Thou art tenderly compassionate, grant me tears of compunction!

*Theotokion:* O Theotokos, hope and protectress of all that hymn thee: take from me the heavy burden of sin, and as pure Sovereign Lady, receive me who repent!

*And we conclude every Ode with the same Heirmos, both choirs together. And where in an Ode there are two creators [authors], we chant the heirmoi of both creators.*

*Ode 2. Heirmos:*[^1885]
Attend, O heaven, and I will speak, and I will chant of Christ Who came in the flesh from the Virgin!

*Troparion:* Attend, O heaven, and I will speak; give ear, O earth, unto the voice of one repenting unto God, and chanting unto Him!

*Troparion:* Attend, O God, as Thou art compassionate, with Thy merciful eye, and receive my fervent confession!

*Troparion:* I have sinned more than all men; I alone have sinned against Thee; but as Thou art good, O Savior, have compassion on Thine own creation!

*Troparion:* A tempest of evils holds me fast, O merciful Lord; but as unto Peter, extend Thy hand unto me also!

*Troparion:* As the harlot, I also, O compassionate One, offer tears; cleanse me, O Savior, in Thy tender mercy!

*Troparion:* I have darkened the beauty of my soul with the pleasures of passions, and entirely turned my whole mind into mud!

*Troparion:* I have now torn my first garment, which the Fashioner wove for me in the beginning, and thence do I lie naked!

*Troparion:* I have clothed myself in a torn robe, which the serpent wove for me by his counsel, and I am ashamed!

*(fol. 666)*
*Troparion:* I looked upon the beauty of the garden, and was deceived in my mind; therefore do I lie naked and am ashamed!

*Troparion:* All the leaders of the passions have wrought upon my back, lengthening out their iniquity upon me![^1886]

*Troparion:* I have destroyed the first-created goodness and my comeliness, and now I lie naked and am ashamed!

*Troparion:* Sin, having stripped me of the first God-woven garment, sewed coats of skin for me![^1887]

*Troparion:* I am compassed about with a garment of shame, as with fig leaves, unto the reproof of my self-willed passions!

*Troparion:* I have clothed myself with a shameful robe, and one ignominiously bloodied by the flow of a passionate and pleasure-loving life!

*Troparion:* I have defiled the garment of my flesh, and sullied that which is according to Thine image and likeness, O Savior!

*Troparion:* I have fallen into passionate ruin and into material corruption, and from that time until now the enemy insults me!

*Troparion:* Having preferred a life loving matter and loving possessions, and incontinence, O Savior, now I am compassed about with a heavy burden!

*Troparion:* I have adorned the image of the flesh with the diverse vesture of defiled thoughts, and I am condemned!

*Troparion:* I took diligent thought only for outward adornment, having neglected the inner God-fashioned tabernacle!

*Troparion:* Having depicted in myself the deformity of passions by pleasure-loving impulses, I have destroyed the noetic beauty!

*Troparion:* I have buried the goodness of the first image by passions, O Savior, which do Thou, having sought as the drachma, find!

*Troparion:* I have sinned as the harlot; I cry unto Thee: I alone *(fol. 667)*
have sinned against Thee; as myrrh, O Savior, receive my tears also!

*Troparion:* I have slipped as David profligately, and was defiled; but wash me also, O Savior, with tears!

*Troparion:* Cleanse me as the publican, I cry unto Thee, O Savior, cleanse me![^1888] For none of them that are of Adam has sinned against Thee as I!

*Troparion:* Neither tears nor repentance have I, nor compunction; but do Thou Thyself, O Savior, grant these unto me as God!

*Troparion:* Close not Thy door against me at that time, O Lord, Lord; but open it unto me who repent!

*Troparion:* O Lover of mankind, Who desirest that all men should be saved: do Thou recall me and receive me as good, repenting!

*Troparion:* Give ear unto the sighings of my soul, and receive the drops from mine eyes, O Lord, and save me!

*Theotokion:* Most pure Virgin Theotokos, only all-praised one, pray diligently that we may be saved!

*Another Heirmos [Tone 6]:*[^1889]
See, see that I am God, Who rained manna and made water flow from the rock of old in the wilderness for My people, by My sole right hand and by My power!

*Troparion:* "See, see that I am God!" Give ear, O my soul, unto the Lord crying aloud; and depart from thy former sin, and fear Him as an Avenger, and Judge, and God!

*Troparion:* Unto whom hast thou likened thyself, O much-sinning soul? Woe is me! Unto the first Cain, and that Lamech: having stoned the body with evil deeds, and slain the mind by irrational impulses!

*Troparion:* Having passed through all who were before the Law, O soul, thou hast not been likened unto Seth, nor hast thou imitated Enos, nor Enoch by translation, nor Noah; but thou hast appeared destitute of the life of the righteous![^1890]

*(fol. 668)*
*Troparion:* Alone thou hast opened the cataracts of the wrath of thy God, O my soul, and hast flooded all, as the earth, the flesh and deeds and life; and thou hast remained outside the ark of salvation![^1891]

*Troparion:* "A man have I slain," he said, "unto my wounding, and a young man to my hurt," Lamech wailing cried aloud;[^1892] but thou tremblest not, O my soul, having defiled the flesh and sullied the understanding!

*Troparion:* O how have I rivaled Lamech, the first murderer: slaying the soul as a man, the mind as a young man, and as my brother the body, like Cain the murderer, by lustful impulses!

*Troparion:* A tower thou didst contrive to build, O soul, and to establish a rampart for thy lusts,[^1893] had not the Creator restrained thy counsels, and cast down thy contrivances to the earth!

*Troparion:* I have been wounded, and I have been hurt: behold, the enemy's arrows that have wounded my soul and body! Behold, sores, and festering, and darkenings cry aloud—the wounds of self-willed passions!

*Troparion:* The Lord rained fire from the Lord of old upon iniquity that provoked His wrath, as upon the Sodomites;[^1894] but thou hast kindled the fire of Gehenna, wherein thou art to be burned, O soul!

*Troparion:* Understand, and see that I am God, examining the heart, and proving the thoughts, and reproving the deeds, and consuming sins, and judging the orphan, the humble, and the poor!

*To the Venerable Mother Mary:*
*Troparion:* Having stretched forth thy hands unto the merciful God, O Mary, when sunken in the abyss of evils; and as unto Peter the Lover of mankind stretched forth His hand of help, unto thee seeking divine conversion:[^1895]

*(fol. 669)*
with all fervor and love thou didst run unto Christ, having turned aside from the former way of sin, and being nourished in the trackless wilderness, and purely fulfilling His divine commandments!

*To St. Andrew:*
*Troparion:* We see, we see the love toward mankind, O soul, of the Master and Lord; therefore, before the end, let us fall down before Him with tears, crying: By the prayers of Andrew, O Savior, have mercy on us![^1896]

*To the Trinity:*
*Troparion:* Unoriginate, uncreated Trinity, undivided Unity: receive me who repent, save me who have sinned! I am Thy creation; despise me not, but spare me, and deliver me from the fiery condemnation!

*Theotokion:*
*Troparion:* Pure Lady, Birth-giver of God, hope of them that flee unto thee, and haven in tempest: pray the merciful Creator and thy Son, to have mercy upon me also, by thy prayers!

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*[^1897]
On the unshaken rock of Thy commandments, O Christ, establish Thy Church; for Thou alone art holy and upright!

*Troparion:* The Lord rained fire from the Lord of old, burning up the land of Sodom in ancient times!

*Troparion:* Upon the mountain save thyself, O soul, like Lot of old, and flee into Zoar![^1898]

*Troparion:* Flee the conflagration, O soul; flee the Sodomite burning; flee the corruption of the divine flame!

*Troparion:* I confess unto Thee, O Savior: I have sinned, I have sinned against Thee! But remit, forgive me!

*Troparion:* I alone have sinned against Thee; I have sinned more than all: O Christ Savior, despise me not!

*Troparion:* Thou art the Good Shepherd: seek me, the lamb; despise not me who have gone astray!

*(fol. 669)*
*Troparion:* Thou art sweet Jesus, Thou art my Creator; in Thee, O Savior, am I justified!

*To the Trinity:*
*Troparion:* O Trinity, Unity, God: save us from delusion, and temptations, and tribulations!

*Theotokion:*
*Troparion:* Rejoice, womb that received God! Rejoice, throne of the Lord! Rejoice, Mother of our Life!

*Ode 3. Another Heirmos:*[^1899]
Establish, O Lord, upon the rock of Thy commandments, my shaken heart; for Thou alone art holy and righteous!

*Troparion:* I have acquired Thee as the fountain of life, the overthrower of death; and I cry unto Thee from my heart before the end: I have sinned, cleanse and save me!

*Troparion:* In the time of Noah, O Savior, I imitated those who acted impiously; I inherited their condemnation of being submerged in the deluge![^1900]

*Troparion:* I have sinned, O Lord, I have sinned against Thee, cleanse me; for there is none among men who has sinned, whom I have not surpassed by my transgressions!

*Troparion:* Having imitated Ham of old, O soul, the scorner of his father, thou hast not covered the shame of thy neighbor, turning back with averted gaze![^1901]

*Troparion:* The blessing of Shem thou hast not inherited, O wretched one, nor a spacious possession like Japhs hast thou obtained in the land of forgiveness!

*Troparion:* Depart from the land of Haran, come forth from sin, O my soul, today unto the land that ever flows with living incorruption, which Abraham inherited![^1902]

*Troparion:* Thou hast heard of Abraham, O my soul, who of old left the land of his fathers and became a sojourner: imitate his choice!

*(fol. 670)*
*Troparion:* Having entertained the Angels, the Patriarch inherited in old age the prey of promise![^1903]

*Troparion:* Having understood the new sacrifice of Isaac, O wretched soul of mine, mystically whole burnt-offering unto the Lord, imitate his choice![^1904]

*Troparion:* Thou hast heard of Ishmael, be sober, O my soul, who was cast out as the offspring of a bondwoman; beware lest thou suffer anything similar, living in wantonness![^1905]

*Troparion:* Unto the Hagarite of old, O my soul, the Egyptian woman, thou hast become like, having enslaved thy choice, and borne a new Ishmael: insolence!

*Troparion:* Thou hast understood Jacob's ladder, O my soul, shown from earth unto heaven; why hast thou not a firm ascent: piety?[^1906]

*Troparion:* The Priest of God and solitary King, Christ's likeness, who by life in the world among men, imitate![^1907]

*Troparion:* Be not a pillar of salt, O soul, turning back! Let the Sodomite parable terrify thee; high up in Zoar be saved![^1908]

*Troparion:* Flee the conflagration like Lot, O my soul; flee from sin; flee Sodom and Gomorrah; flee the flame of every irrational desire!

*Troparion:* Have mercy on me, O Lord, have mercy on me, I cry unto Thee: when Thou comest with Thine Angels to render unto all according to the worth of their deeds!

*Troparion:* Despise not the prayer of them that sing to Thee, O Master, but be compassionate, O Lover of mankind, and grant forgiveness unto them that ask with faith!

*To the Venerable Mary:*
*Troparion:* I am held fast by tempest and surge, O mother *(fol. 671)*
of sins; but do thou thyself now save me, and lead me unto the haven of divine repentance!

*Troparion:* Having now offered a servile supplication, O Venerable Mother, unto the Mother of God who is compassionate in prayer, open the divine entrances unto me also!

*To St. Andrew:*
*Troparion:* By thy prayers grant me also the remission of debts, O Andrew of Crete, president; for thou art an exceptional mystagogue of repentance![^1909]

*To the Trinity:*
*Troparion:* Simple, uncreated Trinity, unoriginate Essence, hymned in a triad of Hypostases: save us who with faith worship Thy dominion!

*Theotokion:*
*Troparion:* The Son co-eternal with the Father in eternity, in time, O Birth-giver of God, without knowing man thou didst bear—a strange wonder!—remaining a Virgin while nursing!

*Sessional Hymn of Kyr Joseph, Tone 8, Podoben: "Thou didst arise from the tomb" (Воскреслъ еси ѿ гроба):*[^1910][^1911]
O light-bearing luminaries, Apostles of the Savior: enlighten us who are in the darkness of life, that as in the day we may now walk becomingly in the light of abstinence, fleeing the passions of the night, and may behold the radiant Passions of Christ, rejoicing!

*Glory... Another Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "That which was commanded mystically" (Повеленное таинственно):*[^1912]
O apostolic twelve, chosen of God: offer supplication, that all may now traverse the course of the fast, completing prayers in compunction, fervently performing virtues; that so we may anticipate seeing Christ God, His glorious Resurrection, offering glory and praise!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
The incomprehensible Son of God and Word, ineffably born of thee beyond understanding: do thou implore, O Mother of God, together with the Apostles, that He may grant peaceful calm unto the universe, and grant us before the end forgiveness of transgressions, and by His utmost goodness vouchsafe Thy servants the heavenly kingdom!

*Then we read the Life of our Venerable Mother Mary of Egypt in two parts. We sing the TRIODION of Thursday without prostrations. And we recite the scriptural canticle, Ode 4.*[^1913]

*(fol. 672)*
*Ode 4, Tone 8. Heirmos:*[^1914]
I heard, O Lord, the mystery of Thy dispensation, and I understood Thy works, and I glorified Thy Divinity!

*Troparion:* Having lived in abstinence, the enlightened Apostles of Christ soothe for us the time of abstinence by their divine intercessions!

*Troparion:* The twelve-stringed organ, the divine choir of the Disciples, sounded forth a saving hymn, confounding the wicked utterances![^1915]

*Troparion:* With spiritual raining ye have watered all that is under the sun, having driven away the drought of polytheism, O all-blessed ones!

*Theotokion:*
Save me who am humbled, who have lived high-mindedly, O all-pure Virgin, who didst bear Him that exalted our humble nature!

*Another [Canon], Tone 8. Heirmos: I heard, O Lord:*[^1916]
O all-honorable assembly of the Apostles: implore the Creator of all to have mercy upon us who praise you!

*Troparion:* As laborers who are the Apostles of Christ, having cultivated the whole world by the divine Word, ye ever bring forth fruits unto Him!

*Troparion:* Ye were the vineyard of Christ, truly beloved; for ye poured forth spiritual wine unto the world, O Apostles!

*To the Trinity:*
*Troparion:* Pre-unoriginate, conformed, all-powerful Holy Trinity, Father, Word, and Holy Spirit, God, Light, and Life: preserve Thy flock!

*Theotokion:*
Rejoice, fiery-radiant throne! Rejoice, light-bearing lampstand! Rejoice, mountain of salvation, ark of life, tabernacle of the Holy of holies!

*Another, of the Great Canon. Heirmos:*

*(fol. 675)*[^1917]
*Heirmos:*[^1918]
The Prophet heard of Thy coming, O Lord, and was afraid, that Thou wast to be born of a Virgin and appear unto men, and he said: I heard the report of Thee and was afraid: glory to Thy power, O Lord!

*Troparion:* Despise not Thy works, forsake not Thy creation, O righteous Judge! Though I alone have sinned as a man, more than any man, O Lover of mankind, yet hast Thou, as Lord of all, power to forgive sins!

*Troparion:* The end draws near, O soul, it draws near, and thou carest not, nor dost thou prepare! The time grows short; arise, the Judge is near at the doors! Like a dream, like a flower, the time of life runs on; why do we trouble ourselves in vain?

*Troparion:* Arise, O my soul: ponder thy deeds which thou hast done, and bring them before thy face, and shed drops of thy tears; speak with boldness thy deeds and thoughts unto Christ, and be justified!

*Troparion:* There has been no sin in life, nor deed nor wickedness, which I, O Savior, have not committed, in mind and word, and in choice, and purpose, and disposition, and action, having sinned as no other ever!

*Troparion:* Hence am I condemned, and convicted am I, the wretched one, by mine own conscience, than which nothing in the world is more compelling: O Judge and my Deliverer, Who knowest all, spare, deliver, and save me, the wretched one!

*Troparion:* The ladder which the great one among the Patriarchs saw of old is a figure, O my soul, of active ascent and noetic elevation; if then thou desirest to live in action, understanding, and contemplation, be renewed!

*Troparion:* The burning heat of the day did the Patriarch endure for the sake of privation,[^1919] *(fol. 676)*
and the night frost he bore, daily making provision, pasturing and laboring and serving, that he might wed the two wives!

*Troparion:* Understand by the two wives, action and knowledge in contemplation: Leah indeed as action, for she was rich in children; but Rachel as knowledge, for she was acquired with much labor.[^1920] For apart from labors, neither action nor contemplation, O soul, shall be set right!

*Troparion:* Watch, O my soul, and play the man, like the great one among the Patriarchs of old, that thou mayest acquire action with knowledge, that thou mayest be a mind seeing God, and reach the unsetting darkness in contemplation, and be a great merchant!

*Troparion:* Having begotten the twelve Patriarchs, the great one among the Patriarchs mystically established for thee a ladder of active ascent, O my soul: the children as foundations, the steps as ascents, he wisely placed beneath!

*Troparion:* Thou hast imitated the hated Esau, O soul; thou hast given over to thy deceiver the birthright of the first beauty, and hast fallen from thy father's prayer, and twice hast thou slipped, O wretched one, in action and in knowledge; therefore now repent![^1921]

*Troparion:* Edom was Esau called, because of his extreme woman-mad passion; for being ever inflamed by intemperance, and defiled by pleasures, he was named Edom, which is interpreted: burning, a soul that loves sin![^1922]

*Troparion:* Having heard of Job on the dunghill, O my soul, who was justified, thou hast not rivaled his courage; thou hast not acquired firmness of purpose in all things that thou knowest, wherein thou hast been tried, but hast appeared impatient![^1923]

*(fol. 677)*
*Troparion:* He who was formerly on a throne, now naked on a dunghill, is full of sores; he who was rich in children and renowned, is childless and homeless suddenly: for he accounted the dunghill a palace, and his sores as pearls![^1924]

*Troparion:* Clothed with royal rank and diadem and purple, a man of great possessions and righteous, abounding in wealth and herds, was suddenly deprived of wealth, and stripped of royal glory!

*Troparion:* If he was righteous and blameless more than all, yet fled not the snaring and net of the deceiver; what wilt thou do, O wretched soul, that art a lover of sin, if any unforeseen thing should happen unto thee?

*Troparion:* I have defiled my body, and sullied my spirit, and am all covered with sores; but as Physician, O Christ, heal both by my repentance; wash, cleanse, and show me whiter than snow, O my Savior!

*Troparion:* Thy Body and Blood, when crucified, Thou didst lay down for all, O Word: Thy Body indeed, that Thou mightest renew me; and Thy Blood, that Thou mightest wash me; and Thy Spirit Thou didst surrender, that Thou mightest bring me, O Christ, unto Thy Father!

*Troparion:* Thou hast worked salvation in the midst of the earth, O Creator, that we might be saved![^1926] Voluntarily wast Thou crucified upon the Tree; Eden, which was shut, is opened; creation on high and below, and all nations, having been saved, worship Thee!

*Troparion:* May the Blood from Thy side be unto me a laver, and together a drink that poured forth the water of remission, that on both sides I may be cleansed, being anointed and drinking, as ointment and drink, O Word, Thy life-bearing words![^1925]

*(fol. 678)*
*Troparion:* I am naked of the bridal chamber; I am naked also of the marriage and supper together! The lamp is extinguished, for it lacked oil; the bridal chamber was shut against me while I slept; the supper was eaten; and I, bound hand and foot, am cast out![^1927]

*Troparion:* The Church has acquired the cup: Thy life-bearing side, from which gushed forth for us the two-fold stream, a drop of remission and knowledge, in figure of the Old and New, of the two covenants together, O our Savior![^1928]

*Troparion:* The time of my life is small, and full of pains and wickedness; but in repentance receive me, and call me unto understanding, that I may not become a possession nor food for the stranger: O Savior, do Thou Thyself have compassion on me!

*Troparion:* I am high-speaking now, and foolish also in heart, in vain and altogether; let me not be condemned with the Pharisee, but rather grant me the Publican's humility, O only Compassionate, righteous Judge, and number me with him![^1929]

*Troparion:* I have sinned, having insulted the vessel of my flesh, I know, O Compassionate One; but in repentance receive me, and call me unto understanding, that I may not become a possession nor food for the stranger: O Savior, do Thou Thyself have compassion on me!

*Troparion:* I have become a very temple for passions, having defiled my soul, O Compassionate One; but in repentance receive me, and call me unto understanding, that I may not become a possession nor food for the stranger: O Savior, do Thou Thyself have compassion on me!

*Troparion:* I gave not ear unto Thy voice; I disobeyed Thy Scripture of the law; but in repentance receive me, and call me unto understanding, that I may not become a possession nor food for the stranger: O Savior, do Thou Thyself have compassion on me!

*To St. Mary:*

*(fol. 679)*
*To St. Mary:*
*Troparion:* Passing through a bodiless life in the flesh, thou didst truly receive great, acceptable grace with God; protect them that faithfully honor Thee; therefore we pray Thee, deliver us also from every calamity by thy prayers![^1930]

*Troparion:* Cast down into the deep of great enormities, thou wast not held fast; but thou didst run with higher understanding unto the perfection manifest in deeds of virtue, O glorious Mary, astonishing the nature of the Angels![^1931]

*To St. Andrew:*
*Troparion:* O Andrew, boast of the fathers, standing before the throne of the Trinity, cease not praying with thy prayers, that we who with love call upon thee, our divine protector, O all-blessed one, the ornament of Crete, may be delivered from torments![^1932]

*To the Trinity:*
*Troparion:* Undivided in Essence, unconfused in Persons, I theologize Thee, the one Triune Divinity, as of one kingship and co-enthroned; I cry aloud unto Thee the great song, thrice-hymned and glorified in the highest![^1933]

*Theotokion:*
*Troparion:* Both bringing forth and keeping virginity, thou remainest in both respects a Virgin by nature: by thy childbearing the laws of nature are renewed, and a womb that bare not gives birth; for where God wills, the order of nature is overcome, for He does whatever He pleases![^1934]

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*[^1935]
From night rising early, O Lover of mankind, enlighten me, I pray Thee, and guide me also in Thy commandments, and teach me, O Savior, to do Thy will!

*Troparion:* In night have I passed my life continually, for night was it, and a deep mist unto me, the night of sin; but show me, O Savior, as a son of the day![^1936]

*Troparion:* I, wretched one, have rivaled Reuben, having wrought an unlawful and law-transgressing counsel against the Most High God, having defiled my bed, as he did his father's![^1937]

*(fol. 680)*
*Troparion:* I confess unto Thee, O Christ King: I have sinned, I have sinned, as of old the brothers who sold Joseph, the fruit of purity and chastity![^1938]

*Troparion:* By his kinsmen was that righteous soul bound; that sweet one was sold into bondage, as a type of the Lord; but thou, O my soul, hast wholly surrendered thyself unto thine evil deeds![^1939]

*Troparion:* Emulate the righteous and chaste mind of Joseph, O wretched and untried soul, and commit not fornication with lawless impulses, ever transgressing the law![^1940]

*Troparion:* Even if Joseph dwelt for a time in a pit, O Master and Lord, yet it was in the figure of Thy Burial and Rising; but what such thing shall I ever bring unto Thee?[^1941]

*Troparion:* Thou hast heard of old, O soul, of the ark of Moses, borne by the waters and the waves of the river as in a bridal chamber, fleeing the bitter work of Pharaoh's decree![^1942]

*Troparion:* If thou hast heard of the midwives of old who slew the male infants, O wretched soul, suck thou now wisdom, the work of chastity, like great Moses![^1943]

*Troparion:* As great Moses smote the Egyptian, having wounded thy mind, O wretched soul, thou hast not slain him; and how, tell me, wilt thou dwell in the wilderness of passions through repentance?[^1944]

*Troparion:* Great Moses dwelt in the wilderness; come, therefore, emulate his life, that thou, O soul, mayest also come to the vision of God in the Bush![^1945]

*Troparion:* Picture to thyself, O soul, the rod of Moses striking the sea and solidifying the deep, in the figure of the divine Cross, through which thou also canst accomplish great wonders![^1946]

*Troparion:* Aaron offered unto God unblemished fire, *(fol. 681)*
without deceit; but Hophni and Phinehas, even as thou, O soul, offered unto God that which was strange, a defiled life![^1947]

*Troparion:* Like hard-hearted Jannes and Jambres unto bitter Pharaoh have I become, O Master, plunged in soul and body and mind; but help Thou me![^1948]

*Troparion:* In the mire have I been mingled, wretched in my mind; wash me, O Master, in the laver of my tears, I pray Thee, making the garment of my flesh white as snow![^1949]

*Troparion:* Though I examine my deeds, O Savior, I see that I have surpassed every man in sins; for I have sinned in the knowledge of my mind, and not in ignorance![^1950]

*Troparion:* Spare, spare, O Lord, Thy creation! I have sinned, forgive me; for Thou alone art pure by nature, and none other besides Thee is without defilement![^1951]

*Troparion:* Being God, for my sake Thou didst take form in me; Thou didst display wonders, healing lepers, and strengthening the paralytic, and stopping the flow of the woman with the issue of blood, O Savior, by the touch of Thy garments![^1952]

*Troparion:* Emulate the woman with the issue of blood, O wretched soul; run, take hold of the hem of Christ, that thou mayest be freed from plagues, and hear from Him: "Thy faith has saved thee!"[^1953]

*Troparion:* Emulate the woman bowed down to the earth, O soul; come, fall down at the feet of Jesus, that He may straighten thee, and that thou mayest walk upright in the paths of the Lord![^1954]

*Troparion:* Though Thou art a deep well, O Master, gush forth for me water from Thy most pure veins, that, like the Samaritan woman, I may thirst no more; for Thou pourest forth the streams of life![^1955]

*Troparion:* May my tears be Siloam unto me, O Master and Lord, *(fol. 682)*
that I may wash therewith the pupils of my heart, and behold Thee with understanding, O Light before the ages![^1956]

*To St. Mary:*
*Troparion:* Exceedingly rich with eminent desire, longing to venerate the Life-giving Tree, thou wast vouchsafed thy desire; vouchsafe therefore unto me also to obtain the glory on high![^1957]

*Troparion:* Having crossed the streams of the Jordan, thou didst find rest from the suffering flesh, having escaped pleasures; from which do thou also deliver us by thy prayers, O venerable mother![^1958]

*To St. Andrew:*
*Troparion:* Knowing thee to be most eminent among pastors, O all-wise Andrew, and most honorable, with great love and fear I pray thee: by thy prayers may I obtain salvation and life eternal![^1959]

*To the Trinity:*
*Troparion:* Thee, O Trinity, we glorify, the one God: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, Father, and Son, and Spirit, simple Essence, Unity ever worshipped![^1960]

*Theotokion:*
*Troparion:* From thee did God Who created the ages clothe Himself in my clay, O undefiled, unwedded Mother and Virgin, and united human nature unto Himself![^1961]

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*[^1962]
I cried with all my heart unto the merciful God, and He heard me from the lowest hell, and brought up my life from corruption!

*Troparion:* The tears of mine eyes, O Savior, and the sighs from the depth I offer purely, while my heart cries: O God, I have sinned against Thee, cleanse me![^1963]

*Troparion:* Thou hast turned aside, O soul, from thy Lord, even as Dathan and Abiram; but cry aloud from all thy heart: "Spare!", that the chasm of the earth may not cover thee![^1964]

*Troparion:* Like an enraged heifer, O soul, thou hast likened thyself unto Ephraim; like a gazelle from the snare, preserve thy life, having soared aloft by action and contemplation![^1965]

*(fol. 683)*
*Troparion:* May the hand of Moses assure us, O soul, how God is able to make white and cleanse a leprous life; and despair not of thyself, even if thou art leprous![^1966]

*Troparion:* The waves of my sins, O Savior, returning as in the Red Sea, have suddenly covered me, even as once the Egyptians and their captains![^1967]

*Troparion:* An unreasoning inclination hast thou acquired, O soul, as of old did Israel; for more than the divine Manna didst thou senselessly prefer the pleasure-loving gluttony of the passions![^1968]

*Troparion:* Swine's flesh and cauldrons and Egyptian food didst thou prefer above the heavenly, O my soul, even as the unreasoning people of old in the wilderness![^1969]

*Troparion:* The wells of Canaanite thoughts hast thou preferred, O soul, above the cleft of the rock, from which the river of wisdom pours forth streams of theology![^1970]

*Troparion:* When Moses Thy servant struck the rock with his rod, he prefigured in type Thy life-creating ribs, from which we all draw the drink of life, O Savior![^1971]

*Troparion:* Search, O soul, and see, like Joshua the son of Nun, what the land of promise is, and dwell therein through good obedience to the law![^1972]

*Troparion:* Arise and conquer the carnal passions, as Joshua conquered Amalek, ever overcoming the Gibeonites, the deceitful thoughts![^1973]

*Troparion:* Pass through the flowing nature of time, as the Ark of old, and possess that land of promise, O soul; God commands it![^1974]

*Troparion:* Even as Thou didst save Peter when he cried "Save me!", do Thou anticipate me, O Savior, *(fol. 684)*
and deliver me from the beast, stretching forth Thy hand, and lead me up from the deep of sin![^1975]

*Troparion:* A tranquil haven do I know Thee to be, O Master Christ; but anticipate me and save me from the trackless depths of sin and despair![^1976]

*Troparion:* I am that royal drachma which was lost of old, O Savior; but having kindled the lamp, Thy most pure flesh, O Word, seek out and find Thine image![^1977]

*To St. Mary:*
*Troparion:* That thou mightest quench the flame of passions, thou didst ever pour forth drops of tears, O Mary, being kindled in soul; the grace of which grant unto me also, thy servant![^1978]

*Troparion:* Dispassion indeed didst thou acquire by thy supreme life upon earth, O Mother; therefore pray ever for them that praise thee, that they may be delivered from passionate assaults![^1979]

*To St. Andrew:*
*Troparion:* Knowing thee to be pastor and presiding hierarch of Crete, and intercessor for the whole universe, I run unto thee, O Andrew, and cry aloud: Deliver me, father, from the deep of sin![^1980]

*To the Trinity:*
*Troparion:* I am a simple, undivided Trinity, divided in Persons, and I am a Unity united in essence: the Father, saith He, and the Son, and the Divine Spirit![^1981]

*Theotokion:*
*Troparion:* Thy womb bare the Lord for us, formed like unto us; Him do thou pray, as the Creator of all, O Birth-giver of God, that by thy prayers we may be justified![^1982]

*Kontakion, Tone 6:*[^1983]
My soul, my soul, arise! Why sleepest thou? The end draws near, and thou wilt be confounded! Rouse thyself, therefore, that Christ God may spare thee, Who is everywhere present and fills all things!

*Ikos:*[^1984]
Seeing Christ's dispensary opened, and health flowing thence unto Adam, the devil suffered and was wounded; and as one in perils he wailed, *(fol. 685)*
and cried aloud unto his friends: "What shall I do unto the Son of Mary? The Bethlehemite slays me, Who is everywhere present and fills all things!"

*Synaxarion:*[^1985]
*Verses:*
*Christ, give me images of compunction,*
*Unto them that now sing Thy Great Canon.*

On this day, according to ancient tradition, we chant the Order of the Great Canon. For this canon, the greatest among all canons, our holy father Andrew, Archbishop of Crete, who is called the Hierosolymite, exquisitely and learnedly composed and wrote:

Who came forth indeed from Damascus, and around his fourteenth year of age, having been given over unto the school of grammar and having excelled in all the liberal arts, and having come to Jerusalem, embraced the monastic life;[^1986] and living there steadfastly and pleasingly unto God in a tranquil and untroubled life, left behind for the Church of God many other writings profitable for human life, as well as many sermons and canons; and most especially in his panegyrics—that is, festal eulogistic sermons—he proved himself most brilliant and beloved.[^1987]

And alongside his many other writings, he also composed this present Great Canon, having an exceedingly great compunction or contrition. For having gathered all the histories of the Old and New Covenants, and having assembled them together, he crafted this song—that is, from Adam even unto the Ascension of Christ Himself and the apostolic preaching.[^1988] He admonishes, therefore, by this canon every soul: to love whatsoever is good in history, and according to one's strength to imitate it; and from whatsoever is evil to beware, and ever to flee unto God through repentance, through tears, through confession of sins, and through other things pleasing unto God.

Moreover, it is so beautifully flowing in speech and harmonious in composition that it is sufficient to soften even the hardest soul, and to awaken it unto compunction and unto turning toward good, if only it be sung with a contrite heart and diligent attentiveness.[^1989] And he composed this canon at the very time when the Patriarch of Jerusalem, the great Sophronius, wrote down the Life of Mary of Egypt; for that Life also sets forth great compunction for us, and unto them that have sinned...[^1990]

*(fol. 686)*
...and do sin, it offers consolation, if only they would desire to depart from their evils.[^1991] And it was ordained that both this Canon should be chanted and this Life read on this present day for the following reason: Because the holy Forty-Day Fast is drawing toward its close, lest people, becoming sluggish, should grow faint in spiritual labors and struggles, and altogether cease to live steadfastly and temperately in all things.

Great Andrew indeed, as a teacher through the narratives of the Great Canon, reciting the virtue of great men and likewise the wickedness of the evil, renders them that fulfill virtue more valiant and whole-hearted, and stoutly to set themselves against adversaries.[^1992] And holy Sophronius, through his comprehensive and beautiful sermon, likewise renders them steadfast in virtues and stirs them up toward God: and not to fall down nor despair—that is, to lose hope of their salvation—if they should have been captured by any sins. For how great is the divine goodness and mercy toward them that with all their soul turn from former sins before their end, the history of Mary of Egypt clearly demonstrates.

The Great Canon is also so named by reason of its conception and comprehension; for its creator is sufficient and bountiful, who exquisitely composed and arranged it; and whereas other canons have thirty or fewer troparia, this one runs to two hundred and fifty verses, having in itself ineffable sweetness.[^1993] Fitly and properly, therefore, was this Great Canon, having great compunction, appointed in this holy Great Forty Days.

This most exquisite and Great Canon, and the Life of Venerable Mary, this our father Andrew first brought unto Constantinople at that time when he arrived, sent by Patriarch Theodore of Jerusalem as an aid unto the Sixth Council.[^1994] For having then stood forth excellently against the Monothelites—that is, against the single-will heretics—while yet being a simple monk, he was numbered among the clergy of the Church of Constantinople; thereafter he was appointed deacon and orphanotrophos—that is, provider of the poor—therein; and shortly thereafter he became Archbishop of Crete.[^1995]

Finally, having arrived in Mytilene very near unto a place called Hierissos, he departed unto the Lord, having abundantly ordered his see.[^1996]

By his prayers, O God, have mercy on us!

*(fol. 687)*
*Then, The Beatitudes, Tone 6. We chant with prostrations. 16 verses:*[^1997]

*In Thy Kingdom when Thou comest, remember us, O Lord!*

*Troparion:* Thou didst make the Thief a citizen of Paradise, O Christ, when He cried unto Thee upon the Cross: "Remember me!" Vouchsafe unto me also, unworthy though I be, his repentance![^1998]

*Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the Kingdom of heaven.*

*Troparion:* Having heard of Manoah of old, O my soul, when God appeared unto him, and who then received from a barren woman the fruit of promise: let us emulate his piety![^1999]

*Blessed are they that mourn now, for they shall be comforted.*

*Troparion:* Emulating Samson's indolence, thou hast shorn the head of thy good deeds, O soul, having surrendered unto foreigners through pleasure-loving lust a chaste and blessed life![^2000]

*Blessed are the meek, for they shall inherit the earth.*

*Troparion:* He who of old with the jawbone of an ass conquered foreigners was afterwards found a captive to passionate lust; but do thou, O my soul, flee his imitation, his conduct, and his weakness![^2001]

*Blessed are they that hunger and thirst after righteousness, for they shall be filled.*

*Troparion:* Barak and Jephthah, the captains and judges of Israel, were highly honored, and with them manly-minded Deborah; by their brave deeds, O soul, take courage and be strengthened![^2002]

*Blessed are the merciful, for they shall obtain mercy.*

*Troparion:* Thou hast known the valor of Jael, O my soul, who of old pierced Sisera and wrought salvation with a sharp wood, as thou hearest, whereby the Cross is figured unto thee![^2003]

*Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God.*

*Troparion:* Offer a sacrifice of praise, O soul; bring forth action as a daughter purer than Jephthah's, and slaughter as a sacrifice the carnal passions unto thy Lord![^2004]

*Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called the sons of God.*

*(fol. 688)*
*Troparion:* Ponder Gideon's fleece, O my soul; receive the dew from heaven, and bow down like a dog and drink the water flowing from the law through the pressing out of the letter![^2005]

*Blessed are they that are persecuted for righteousness' sake, for theirs is the Kingdom of heaven.*

*Troparion:* Thou hast received the condemnation of Eli the priest, O my soul, through lack of understanding, having acquired passions for thyself, even as he did his children, to commit lawless deeds![^2006]

*Blessed are ye when they shall revile you and persecute you, and shall say all manner of evil against you falsely for My sake.*

*Troparion:* In the Book of Judges the Levite, on account of negligence toward his wife, divided her unto the twelve tribes, O my soul, that he might expose the lawless defilement from Benjamin![^2007]

*Rejoice and be glad, for great is your reward in heaven.*

*Troparion:* Wise Hannah when praying moved indeed her lips unto praise, but her voice was not heard; yet, being barren, she bare a son worthy of prayer![^2008]

*Remember us, O Lord, when Thou comest in Thy Kingdom.*

*Troparion:* Among the judges judged Hannah's offspring, great Samuel, whom Ramah nurtured in the house of the Lord; emulate him, O my soul, and judge thine own deeds before those of others![^2009]

*Remember us, O Master, when Thou comest in Thy Kingdom.*

*Troparion:* David, chosen for kingship, was royally anointed with the horn of divine chrism; if, therefore, thou desirest the Kingdom on high, O my soul, anoint thyself with the chrism of tears![^2010]

*Remember us, O Holy One, when Thou comest in Thy Kingdom.*

*Troparion:* Have mercy on Thy creation, O Merciful One; have compassion on the work of Thy hands, and spare all who have sinned, and me above all, who have despised Thy commandments![^2011]

*Glory:*
*Troparion:* I worship the unoriginate Father Who begat, in begetting and proceeding; I glorify the Son Who was begotten;[^2012]

*(fol. 689)*
I sing also of the Holy Spirit, Who shone forth together with the Father and the Son.[^2013]

*Now and ever:*
*Theotokion:* We worship thy supernatural childbearing, not dividing according to nature the glory of Thy Child, O Theotokos; for He Who is one in Person is confessed twofold in natures.[^2014]

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*[^2015]
We have sinned, we have committed iniquity, we have done unrighteously before Thee; neither have we kept, nor have we done as Thou hast commanded us; yet deliver us not up to the end, O God of the fathers!

*Troparion:* I have sinned, I have committed iniquity, and I have rejected Thy commandment, for in sins was I brought forth, and I have added wounds to my sores; but do Thou Thyself have mercy on me as Thou art compassionate, O God of the fathers![^2016]

*Troparion:* The secrets of my heart have I confessed unto Thee, my Judge; behold my lowliness, behold my affliction, and give ear now unto my judgment, and do Thou Thyself have mercy on me as Thou art merciful, O God of the fathers![^2017]

*Troparion:* When Saul of old lost his father's asses, O my soul, he suddenly found a kingdom unto renown; but take heed, forget not thyself, having preferred thy bestial lusts above the Kingdom of Christ![^2018]

*Troparion:* If David the forefather of God sinned doubly of old, O my soul, pierced with the arrow of adultery and captive to the spear of murder's torment, yet thou thyself art sick with heavier deeds, through self-willed impulses![^2019]

*Troparion:* David joined iniquity to iniquity of old, mingling adultery with murder, yet he showed forth a twofold repentance; but thou, O most wicked soul, hast done worse deeds, not having repented unto God![^2020]

*(fol. 690)*
*Troparion:* David depicted of old, composing as on an icon a song whereby he rebukes the deed he had done, crying: "Have mercy on me! For against Thee only have I sinned, the God of all; do Thou Thyself cleanse me!"[^2021]

*Troparion:* When the Ark was being carried on a cart, that Uzzah, when the heifer overturned it, only touched it, and made trial of the wrath of God; but fleeing his presumption, O soul, revere divine things honorably![^2022]

*Troparion:* Thou hast heard of Absalom, how he rose up against nature; thou hast known his vile deeds, wherewith he defiled the bed of David his father; yet thou hast followed after his passions and lustful impulses![^2023]

*Troparion:* Thou hast subjected thy freeborn dignity unto thy body; for finding the enemy to be another Ahithophel, O soul, thou didst listen to his counsels; but Christ scattered them, that thou by all means mightest be saved![^2024]

*Troparion:* Solomon the marvelous, filled with the grace of wisdom, when he did evil of old before God, departed from Him; unto him thou also, O soul, hast become like through thy cursed life![^2025]

*Troparion:* Carried away by the pleasures of his passions, he defiled himself—alas for me!—a lover of wisdom, yet a lover of wanton women, and estranged from God; him hast thou also emulated in mind, O soul, through vile sensualities![^2026]

*Troparion:* Thou hast emulated Rehoboam, who listened not to his father's counsel, together with that most wicked servant Jeroboam, the apostate of old, O soul; but flee their emulation, and cry aloud unto God: "I have sinned, have compassion on me!"[^2027]

*(fol. 691)*
*Troparion:* Thou hast emulated Ahab's defilements, O my soul—alas for me! Thou hast been an abode of carnal defilements and a vessel of vile passions; but flee his emulation, and confess thy sins unto God![^2028]

*Troparion:* Elijah burned up of old twice fifty of Jezebel's men, when he destroyed the shameful prophets to rebuke Ahab; but flee the emulation of those two, O soul, and exercise self-control![^2029]

*Troparion:* Heaven was shut against thee, O soul, and a famine from God overtook thee, when, like Ahab of old, thou didst not believe the words of Elijah the Tishbite; but emulate the woman of Zarephath, and feed the Prophet's soul![^2030]

*Troparion:* Thou hast gathered the transgressions of Manasseh by deliberate choice, setting up the passions as abominations, and multiplying wrath, O soul; but zealous for his repentance, acquire fervent compunction![^2031]

*Troparion:* I fall down before Thee, and I offer unto Thee my words as tears: I have sinned as the harlot never sinned, and I have committed iniquity as no other on earth; but have compassion, O Master, on Thy creation, and call me back![^2032]

*Troparion:* I have buried Thine image and corrupted Thy commandment; all my beauty has been darkened, and the lamp has been quenched by passions, O Savior; but having compassion, restore unto me, as David sings, joy![^2033]

*Troparion:* Turn back, repent, uncover what is hidden, say unto God Who knows all things: "Thou knowest my secrets, O only Savior; yet do Thou Thyself have mercy on me, as David sings, according to Thy mercy!"[^2034]

*(fol. 692)*
*Troparion:* My days have vanished like the dream of one awakening; therefore, like Hezekiah, I weep upon my bed, that years may be added to my life; but what Isaiah shall stand before thee, O soul, if not the God of all?[^2035]

*To St. Mary:*
*Troparion:* Having cried aloud unto the All-pure Mother of God, thou didst first reject the madness of the passions that violently afflicted thee, and didst put to shame the enemy that tripped thee up; but grant help now from affliction unto me also, thy servant![^2036]

*Troparion:* He Whom thou didst love, He Whom thou didst desire, in Whose footsteps thou didst walk, He found thy repentance and granted it, as the only compassionate God; Whom unceasingly beseech, that we may be delivered from passions and distress![^2037]

*To St. Andrew:*
*Troparion:* Establish me on the rock of faith by thy prayers, O father, fencing me about with divine fear; and grant me repentance, O intercessor Andrew, and save me from the snare of the enemies that seek me![^2038]

*To the Trinity:*
*Troparion:* O simple, undivided Trinity, consubstantial and Holy Unity: Lights and Light, three Holy Ones and one Holy, God the Trinity is praised; but hymn and glorify, O soul, Life and Lives, the God of all![^2039]

*Theotokion:*
*Troparion:* We hymn thee, we bless thee, we worship thee, O Mother of God, for from the undivided Trinity thou didst bring forth Christ God, and thou thyself hast opened heavenly realms unto us that dwell on earth![^2040]

*Triodion without Prostrations.*
*Tone 8. Ode 8. Heirmos:*[^2041]
The unoriginate King of glory, Whom the heavenly hosts tremble before, and the angelic ranks quake at: sing, ye consecrated people, and exalt Him above all forever!

*To the Apostles:*
*Troparion:* As coals of immaterial fire, burn up *(fol. 693)*
material passions, kindling now within me zeal for divine love, O Apostles![^2042]

*Troparion:* Let us honor the sweetsounding trumpets of the Word, whereby the unstable walls of the enemy fell down, and the ramparts of the knowledge of God were established![^2043]

*Troparion:* Shatter the passionate idols of my soul, ye who shattered the temples and pillars of the enemy, O Apostles of the Lord, consecrated temples![^2044]

*Theotokion:*
*Troparion:* Thou didst contain Him Who is uncontainable by nature; thou didst bear Him Who bears all things; thou didst suckle, O pure Virgin Theotokos, Christ the Giver of life, Who nourishes creation![^2045]

*Another Triodion. Same Heirmos.*
*To the Apostles:*
*Troparion:* Having built the whole Church of Christ by the sovereign artistry of the Spirit, O Apostles of Christ, bless Christ within her unto the ages![^2046]

*Troparion:* Having sounded the trumpet of teaching, the Apostles cast down all the deceit of idols, exalting Christ above all unto all ages![^2047]

*Troparion:* O Apostles, noble colony, overseers of the world, citizens of heaven, deliver from calamities them that ever praise you![^2048]

*To the Trinity:*
*Troparion:* Tri-hypostatic, all-radiant Godhead, consubstantial Nature of equal glory and equal throne: O all-creating Father, Son, and divine Spirit, I sing of Thee unto the ages![^2049]

*Theotokion:*
*Troparion:* As the honorable and exalted throne let us unceasingly praise the Mother of God, O ye people, who alone after childbearing is Mother and Virgin![^2050]

*Of the Great Canon.*
*Ode 8. Tone 6. Heirmos:*[^2051]
Him Whom the heavenly hosts glorify, and Cherubim and Seraphim tremble before: let every breath and creature sing, bless, and exalt Him above all unto all ages!

*Troparion:* Have mercy on me who have sinned, O Savior; raise up my *(fol. 694)*
mind unto conversion; receive me repenting, have compassion on me crying: "Against Thee only have I sinned, I have done iniquity, have mercy on me!"[^2052]

*Troparion:* Elijah the charioteer, mounting the chariot of virtues, was borne aloft as unto heaven of old, above earthly things; meditate, O my soul, upon his ascent![^2053]

*Troparion:* The stream of the Jordan stood still of old on this side and on that through Elisha by the mantle of Elijah; but thou, O my soul, hast not partaken of that grace through lack of self-control![^2054]

*Troparion:* Elisha of old, taking up the mantle of Elijah, received a twofold grace from the Lord; but thou, O my soul, hast not partaken of this grace through lack of self-control![^2055]

*Troparion:* The Shunammite woman of old entertained the righteous man, O my soul, with good disposition; but thou hast brought into thy house neither stranger nor traveler; therefore shalt thou be cast out weeping from the bridal chamber![^2056]

*Troparion:* Ever hast thou emulated Gehazi's vile mind, O soul; cast off his love of money, at least in old age; flee the fire of Gehenna, departing from thine evil deeds![^2057]

*Troparion:* Emulating Uzziah, O soul, thou hast acquired his leprosy doubly within thyself, for thou thinkest unfitting things and committest unlawful deeds; leave what thou holdest, and hasten unto repentance![^2058]

*Troparion:* Thou hast heard, O soul, of the Ninevites repenting before God in sackcloth and ashes; thou hast not emulated them, but hast shown thyself more wicked than all that have sinned before the law and after the law![^2059]

*Troparion:* In the mire of the pit thou hast heard, O soul, of Jeremiah crying for the city *(fol. 695)*
of Zion with lamentations and seeking tears; emulate his tearful life, and thou shalt be saved![^2060]

*Troparion:* Jonah fled to Tarshish, foreseeing the conversion of the Ninevites; for as a prophet he understood the lovingkindness of God, yet he was jealous that the prophecy might not prove false![^2061]

*Troparion:* Thou hast heard, O soul, how Daniel in the pit shut the mouths of the wild beasts; thou hast known how the Children with Azariah quenched by faith the fiery flame of the furnace![^2062]

*Troparion:* All the figures of the Old Testament have I brought before thee, O soul; emulate the God-loving deeds of the righteous, and shun again the sins of the wicked![^2063]

*Troparion:* O Righteous Judge, Savior, have mercy and deliver me from the fire, and from the condemnation which I am justly to endure at the judgment; grant me remission before the end through virtue and repentance![^2064]

*Troparion:* Like the thief I cry unto Thee: "Remember me!"; like Peter I weep bitterly: "Forgive me, O Savior!"; I call aloud like the Publican, I shed tears like the harlot; receive my weeping, as of old the Canaanite woman's![^2065]

*Troparion:* Heal the festering of my wretched soul, O Savior, the only Physician; apply to me a plaster, and oil and wine: the deeds of repentance, compunction with tears![^2066]

*Troparion:* Emulating the Canaanite woman, I also cry: "Have mercy on me, O Son of David!"; I touch the hem of Thy garment like the woman with the issue of blood; I weep as Martha and Mary over Lazarus![^2067]

*Troparion:* Pouring out the alabaster flask of tears like myrrh upon Thy head, O Savior, I call unto Thee like the harlot seeking mercy; I offer supplication, and ask to receive forgiveness![^2068]

*(fol. 696)*
*Troparion:* Even if no one has sinned against Thee as I have, yet receive even me, O compassionate Savior, repenting with fear and calling with love: "Against Thee only have I sinned, I have done iniquity, have mercy on me!"[^2069]

*Troparion:* Spare, O Savior, Thine own creation, and seek as a shepherd that which is lost; anticipate the wanderer, snatch me from the wolf, make me as a sheep in the pasture of Thy sheep![^2070]

*Troparion:* When Thou sittest as Judge, being compassionate, and showest forth Thy dread glory, O Savior: oh, what fear will there be then, when the furnace is burning, while all stand in dread of Thine unendurable judgment-seat![^2071]

*To St. Mary:*
*Troparion:* The Mother of the Unwaning Light, having enlightened thee, loosed thee from the darkening of passions; therefore, having entered into spiritual grace, enlighten, O Mary, them that praise thee with faith![^2072]

*Troparion:* Seeing a new wonder, the godly Zosimas was truly astonished in thee, O mother; for he beheld an Angel in the flesh and was filled with all awe, singing of Christ unto the ages![^2073]

*To St. Andrew:*
*Troparion:* As one having boldness before the Lord, O Andrew of Crete, honorable boast, pray and intercede that I may find release from the bond of iniquity by thy prayers, as the teacher of repentance and the glory of the venerable![^2074]

*We bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit: the Lord.*
*To the Trinity:*
*Troparion:* O unoriginate Father, and co-unoriginate Son, good Comforter, upright Spirit: Begetter of the Word of God, Word of the unoriginate Father, living and creating Spirit, Trinity in Unity, have mercy on me![^2075]

*(fol. 697)*
*Theotokion:*
*Troparion:* As from dipping, O all-pure one, the noetic purple shell of Emmanuel, His flesh, was woven within thy womb; therefore we truly honor thee as Theotokos![^2076]

*We praise, we bless, we worship the Lord.*
*And again the Heirmos.*

*Triodion. Ode 9, without Prostrations. Heirmos:*[^2077]
Truly we confess thee to be the Mother of God, saved through thee, O pure Virgin; with the bodiless choirs we magnify thee!

*To the Apostles:*
*Troparion:* Ye were shown forth as springs of saving water, O Apostles; refresh my soul, wasting away with the thirst of sin![^2078]

*Troparion:* I am tossed upon the deep of perdition, and have already sunk down; by Thy right hand, O Lord, save me as Thou didst Peter![^2079]

*Troparion:* Being salt unto our minds, O disciples, dry up the rottenness of my mind, and drive away the darkness of ignorance![^2080]

*Theotokion:*
*Troparion:* As thou didst give birth unto Joy, grant me weeping, whereby I may be able to find divine comfort, O Sovereign Lady, in the coming day![^2081]

*Another Heirmos:*[^2082]
All generations magnify thee, the Mediatress of heaven and earth, for in thee dwelt bodily the fullness of the Godhead, O Virgin!

*To the Apostles:*
*Troparion:* We magnify thee in hymns, O glorious gathering of the Apostles; for ye were shown forth as radiant luminaries unto the universe, driving away delusion![^2083]

*Troparion:* Having caught the noetic fish with your net of the Gospel, ye ever bring them as an offering unto Christ, O holy and blessed Apostles![^2084]

*Troparion:* By your intercession unto God, remember us, O Apostles, we pray, that we who sing of you with love may be delivered from every temptation![^2085]

*To the Trinity:*
*Troparion:* Thee, the tri-hypostatic Unity: Father, and Son, with the Spirit, one consubstantial God do I sing, the Trinity of equal power and without beginning![^2086]

*(fol. 698)*
*Theotokion:*
*Troparion:* As thou didst bear a child and remain a virgin, all generations call thee blessed, for through thee we were delivered from the curse; for thou hast brought forth for us joy, God and the Lord![^2087]

*Of the Great Canon. Tone 6. Ode 9. Heirmos:*[^2088]
A seedless conception, a childbearing past telling; an uncorrupt birth of a mother who knew not man; for the birth of God renews natures; therefore all generations orthodoxly magnify thee as Mother and Bride of God!

*Troparion:* The mind is covered with wounds, the body is stricken with sickness, the spirit ails, speech has grown weak, life is deadened, the end is at the doors; therefore, O my wretched soul, what wilt thou do when the Judge comes to examine thy deeds?[^2089]

*Troparion:* I have brought before thee Moses' account of the creation of the world, and therefrom all the testamentary Scripture, which tells thee of the righteous and the unrighteous; of whom, O soul, thou hast emulated the second and not the first, having sinned against God![^2090]

*Troparion:* The law has grown weak, the Gospel is idle, all Scripture has been neglected in thee, the Prophets have lost their strength and every righteous word; thy sores have multiplied, O soul, with no physician healing thee![^2091]

*Troparion:* I have brought before thee examples of the New Scripture to lead thee, O soul, unto compunction; emulate therefore the righteous, turn away from the sinful, and propitiate Christ by prayers, and fasts, and purity, and reverence![^2092]

*Troparion:* Christ became man, calling unto repentance thieves and harlots; repent, O soul: the door of the Kingdom is opened already, and Pharisees and publicans and repentant adulterers are snatching it beforehand![^2093]

*Troparion:* Christ became man, partaking of my flesh, and everything that belongs to our nature He fulfilled by His own will, sin...[^2094]

*(fol. 699)*
apart, an image unto thee, O soul, and an example showing beforehand His condescension.[^2095]

*Troparion:* Christ saved the Magi, called the shepherds, showed the multitude of infants to be martyrs, glorified the elder and the aged widow; whom thou, O soul, hast not emulated, neither in deed nor in life; but woe unto thee when thou shalt be judged![^2096]

*Troparion:* The Lord fasted forty days in the wilderness, and afterward hungered, showing forth His human nature; O soul, grow not negligent, if the enemy assault thee, that by prayer and fasting he may be driven back from thy feet![^2097]

*Troparion:* Christ was tempted, the devil tempted Him, showing Him stones that they might become bread; he led Him up into a mountain to behold all the kingdoms of the world in a moment; be afraid, O soul, of this ensnarement, be sober and pray at every hour unto God![^2098]

*Troparion:* The desert-loving turtle-dove, the lamp of Christ, the voice of one crying aloud, proclaimed repentance; Herod committed iniquity with Herodias; take heed, O my soul, lest thou be caught in lawless snares, but embrace repentance![^2099]

*Troparion:* The Forerunner of grace made his dwelling in the wilderness, and all Judea and Samaria, hearing it, ran and confessed their sins, being eagerly baptized; whom thou, O soul, hast not emulated![^2100]`

*Troparion:* Marriage is honorable, and the bed undefiled, for Christ blessed both beforehand, eating in the flesh, and at Cana at the marriage turning water into wine, and showing forth His first miracle, that thou, O soul, mightest be changed![^2101]

*Troparion:* Christ strengthened the paralytic, who took up his bed;

*(fol. 700)*
and He raised up the deceased youth, the widow's son, and the centurion's servant, and appearing unto the Samaritan woman, depicted beforehand unto thee, O soul, worship in Spirit.[^2102]

*Troparion:* The Lord healed the woman with an issue of blood by the touch of the hem of His garment; He cleansed lepers; giving light to the blind and straightening the lame, the deaf and the dumb, and the woman bowed down to the earth He healed by a word, that thou, O soul, mightest be saved![^2103]

*Troparion:* Healing sicknesses, Christ the Word proclaimed glad tidings unto the poor; He cured the injured, ate with tax-collectors, conversed with sinners; and the departed soul of the daughter of Jairus He called back by the touch of His hand![^2104]

*Troparion:* The publican was saved, and the harlot was made chaste, while the boasting Pharisee was condemned; for the one cried: "Cleanse me!", and the other: "Have mercy on me!"; but he boasted, crying: "O God, I thank Thee," and other foolish words![^2105]

*Troparion:* Zacchaeus was a publican, yet he was saved; and Simon the Pharisee was offended, while the harlot received remission and release from Him Who hath power to forgive sins; whom, O soul, hasten to emulate![^2106]

*Troparion:* O my wretched soul, thou hast not emulated the harlot, who, taking the alabaster flask of myrrh, with tears anointed the Savior's feet, and wiped them with her hair, while He tore up the handwriting of her ancient transgressions![^2107]

*Troparion:* O my soul, thou hast known how the cities unto which Christ gave the Gospel were cursed; fear the parable, lest thou become like them, whom the Master, having likened unto the Sodomites, condemned even unto Hades![^2108]

*Troparion:* Lest thou appear worse, O my soul, through despair, *(fol. 701)*
having heard the faith of the Canaanite woman, for whose sake her daughter was healed by the word of God: "O Son of David, save me also!" cry aloud from the depths of thy heart, as she unto Christ![^2109]

*Troparion:* Have compassion, O Savior, Son of David, have mercy, Who by a word didst heal the demon-possessed; and speak unto me also that merciful voice, as unto the thief: "Truly I say unto thee, with Me shalt thou be in Paradise, when I come in My glory!"[^2110]

*Troparion:* One thief reviled Thee, and the other thief confessed Thee as God, for both hung with Thee upon the Cross; but O most merciful One, as unto Thy faithful thief who recognized Thee as God, open unto me also the door of Thy glorious Kingdom![^2111]

*Troparion:* Creation shuddered, beholding Thee crucified; mountains and rocks were rent with fear, and the earth quaked, and Hades was laid bare, and the light grew dark by day, beholding Thee, O Jesus, nailed unto the Cross![^2112]

*Troparion:* Require not of me fruits worthy of repentance, for my strength hath failed within me; grant me ever a contrite heart and spiritual poverty, that I may offer these unto Thee as an acceptable sacrifice, O only Savior![^2113]

*Troparion:* My Judge and my Knower, Who art to come again with the Angels to judge all the world: beholding me then with Thy merciful eye, spare and have compassion on me, O Jesus, who have sinned beyond all human nature![^2114]

*To St. Mary:*
*Troparion:* Thou didst astonish all by thy strange life, the ranks of Angels and the gatherings of men, having lived immaterially and transcended nature, whereby as with bodiless feet, O Mary, having walked, thou didst cross the Jordan![^2115]

*(fol. 702)*
*Troparion:* Entreat the Creator for all that praise thee, O venerable mother Mary, to be delivered from tribulations and afflictions rising up round about; that, delivered from perils, we may unceasingly magnify God Who hath glorified thee![^2116]

*To St. Andrew:*
*Troparion:* O venerable Andrew, thrice-blessed father, pastor of Crete, cease not to pray for them that hymn thee, that we who ever honor thy memory may be delivered from all wrath, and affliction, and corruption of unforgiven sins![^2117]

*To the Trinity:*
*Troparion:* O consubstantial Trinity, Tri-hypostatic Unity, we hymn Thee, glorifying the Father, magnifying the Son, and worshiping the Spirit: the one Nature, truly God, Life, and living Kingdom without end![^2118]

*Theotokion:*
*Troparion:* Preserve thy city, O all-pure Theotokos; for faithfully reigning in thee, in thee it is also strengthened, and overcoming through thee, it turns back every temptation, captures the warriors, and exercises governance![^2119]

*Then: It is truly meet: Photogogikon:*

*At the Aposticha: Stichera Idiomela, Tone 8.*
By my own free will was I stripped of the beauty of virtues through the first transgression, and I was clothed with shame; but by Thy descent unto me, O Word of God, Thou hast not despised me fallen into grievous passions, and wounded by thieves upon the way; but having succored me by Thine all-powerful might, Thou hast deemed me worthy of protection, O most merciful One![^2120]

*Martyrikon:*
Having clad yourselves well in the armor of faith, and having armed yourselves with the sign of the Cross, ye were shown forth as mighty warriors; manfully ye resisted tyrants, and trampled upon the deceit of the devil, and having become victors, *(fol. 703)*
ye were deemed worthy of crowns; pray unceasingly for us, that our souls may be saved.[^2121]

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion. Same Tone.*
Receive the voices of thy servants, O all-pure Virgin Theotokos, and unceasingly pray that remission of sins and peace may be granted unto us.[^2122]

*Then: It is good to give praise:*
*And we join also the First Hour, without stichology.*
*After the Trisagion, at all the Hours, Kontakion: "O my soul, my soul:"*
*And the customary dismissal.*
*At the Third Hour, Kathisma 14: "Praise is meet for Thee:" And at the Sixth, Kathisma 15.*[^2123]

*On Thursday of the Fifth Week of the Holy Fast, at the Sixth Hour,*
*Troparion of the Prophecy, Tone 6:*
Compassionate and long-suffering Almighty Lord, send down Thy mercy upon Thy people![^2124]

*Glory... the end:*
*Both now... the second. Prokeimenon, Psalm 96, Tone 6:*
The Lord is King, let the earth rejoice!
*Verse:* Let the many islands be glad![^2125]

*Reading from the Prophecy of Isaiah (Chapter 42).*
Thus saith the Lord God, Who made heaven and fixed it, Who established the earth and that which is therein, and Who gives breath unto the people that are upon it, and spirit unto them that walk thereon:
I the Lord God have called Thee in righteousness, and have taken hold of Thy hand, and will strengthen Thee for a covenant of My people, for a light to the Gentiles:
to open the eyes of the blind, to bring forth them that are bound from fetters, and them that sit in darkness out of the prison house.
I am the Lord God, that is My name;

*(fol. 704)*
My glory will I not give to another, neither My praise to graven images.[^2126]
The things from the beginning, behold, they are come to pass, and new things which I declare, and before they are announced, they are declared unto you.
Sing unto the Lord a new song; His beginning is glorified on high, and glorify His name from the ends of the earth, ye that go down to the sea, and sail upon it, and the islands, and they that dwell therein.
Let the wilderness rejoice, and the villages thereof, its dwellings, and they that dwell in Kedar; let them that dwell upon the rocks rejoice, from the tops of the mountains let them cry out.
Let them give glory unto God, let them proclaim His praise in the islands.
The Lord God of hosts shall go forth, and shall crush war; He shall stir up jealousy, and shall cry out against His enemies with might.
I have held My peace from of old; shall I also forever be silent and endure? I have endured like a woman in travail; I will destroy and root out, and dry up together.
I will make desolate mountains and hills, and all grass will I dry up; and I will make the rivers into islands, and dry up the groves.
And I will bring the blind by a way that they knew not, and along paths that they have not known will I make them to tread; I will make darkness into light for them, and crooked things into straight: these words will I do for them, and will not forsake them, saith the Lord.[^2127]

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 97, Tone 6:*
Sing unto the Lord a new song, for the Lord hath done marvelous things!
*Verse:* All the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God.[^2128]

*At the Ninth Hour, Kathisma 16:*
Give ear, O my people, to my law.[^2129]

*(fol. 705)*
