*On the same Thursday of the Fifth Week, the klepalo is sounded for Vespers rather quickly (as we also sing the whole service quickly), because of the labor of the vigil. After "Bless the Lord, O my soul:" we stichologize, instead of "Unto the Lord when I was afflicted:" the kathisma occurring in course, the 12th: "Bow down Thine ear, O Lord:"*[^2130]

*At "Lord, I have cried:" we set 10 stichera. Stichera Idiomela, Tone 8.*
By my own free will was I stripped of the beauty of virtues through the first transgression, and I was clothed with shame; but by Thy descent unto me, O Word of God, Thou hast not despised me fallen into grievous passions, and wounded by thieves upon the way; but having succored me by Thine all-powerful might, Thou hast deemed me worthy of protection, O most merciful One![^2131]

*Martyrikon:*
Martyrs of the Lord, ye sanctify every place and heal every sickness; and now pray that we may be delivered from the snares of the enemy, we beseech you, for our souls![^2132]

*Other Stichera. Tone 1, Podoben: "O all-lauded martyrs" (Прехва́льніи мꙋ́ченицы):*
Nailed unto the Cross, O Lord, Thou didst tear up the handwriting of Adam with the divine spear; therefore break asunder my bonds, O Word, that in faith I may sacrifice unto Thee a sacrifice of praise, rejoicing, having now found the acceptable time of fasting, which Thou hast shown forth unto all for salvation![^2133]

Shining of old with the brightness of fasting, Moses beheld the glory of God; emulating him, O my humble soul, by deeds please Him Who endured the Crucifixion graciously for thy sake, by self-control and prayer, that thou mayest obtain divine radiance![^2134]

*Another Sticheron.*
*Tone 6, Podoben: "Archangelically let us sing, ye faithful" (А҆рха́ггельски воспое́мъ вѣ́рніи):*

*(fol. 706)*
Worshiping Thy life-creating Cross, the immeasurable and unutterable goodness toward us of Thy love, O Christ, and having enlightened our souls therein, we praise Thee unceasingly, asking with good courage to complete the course of the fast with joy, and to attain unto Thy Passion, to hymn Thee, O Lord, for Whose sake Thou hast saved us![^2135]

*Other stichera of the Menaion: 4.*
*Prokeimenon, Psalm 98, Tone 7:*
Exalt ye the Lord our God, and worship the footstool of His feet, for He is holy!
*Verse:* The Lord is King, let the peoples rage![^2136]

*Reading from Genesis (Chapter 18).*
The Lord said: The cry of Sodom and Gomorrah is multiplied unto Me, and their sins are very great.
Having gone down therefore, I will see whether their deeds are consummated according to their cry which comes unto Me; and if not, that I may know.
And the men turned thence and came to Sodom; but Abraham was still standing before the Lord.
And Abraham drew near and said: Wilt Thou destroy the righteous with the wicked, and shall the righteous be as the wicked?
If there be fifty righteous in the city, wilt Thou destroy them? Wilt Thou not spare the place for the fifty righteous, if they be in it?
That be far from Thee to do according to this saying, to slay the righteous with the wicked, and that the righteous should be as the wicked; in no wise! He that judges all the earth, shalt Thou not execute judgment?
And the Lord said: If I find in Sodom fifty righteous in the city, I will spare the whole place for their sakes.
And Abraham answered and said:

*(fol. 707)*
Now have I begun to speak unto my Lord, who am but earth and ashes:
What if there shall lack five of the fifty righteous? Wilt Thou destroy the whole city for five? And He said: I will not destroy it, if I find there forty and five.
And he spoke unto the Lord yet again, and said: What if there be found forty there? And He said: I will not destroy it, for the forty's sake.
And he said: Let not my Lord be angry, if I shall speak: What if there be found thirty there? And He said: I will not destroy it, for the thirty's sake.
And he said: Seeing that I have taken upon me to speak unto the Lord my God: What if there be found twenty there? And He said: I will not destroy it, for the twenty's sake.
And he said: What if my Lord be not angry, if I speak yet once more: What if there be found ten there? And He said: I will not destroy it, for the ten's sake.
And the Lord departed as soon as He had left off speaking with Abraham, and Abraham returned unto his place.[^2137]

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 99, Tone 6:*
Shout with jubilation unto the Lord, all the earth!
*Verse:* Serve the Lord in gladness![^2138]

*Reading from Proverbs (Chapter 16).*
He that receives instruction shall be in prosperity, and he that keeps reproofs shall become wise. He that keeps his ways preserves his soul, and he that loves his life spars his mouth.
Before destruction comes haughtiness, and before a fall, an evil mind.
Better is the meek-spirited with humility, than he that divids spoil with the haughty.

*(fol. 708)*
He that is understanding in matters shall find good, and he that hopes in the Lord is blessed.[^2139]
The understanding and the wise shall be called evil, but they that are sweet in speech shall hear more.
Understanding is a fountain of life unto them that possess it, but the instruction of fools is evil.
The heart of the wise shall understand that which proceeds out of his own mouth, and in his lips he shall carry knowledge.
Pleasant words are honeycomb, and the sweetness thereof is the healing of the soul.
There are ways which seem right unto a man, but the end thereof looks into the depths of Hades.
A man in labors toils for himself, and forcs on his own destruction; but the perverse in his own lips bears ruin.
A foolish man diggs evil for himself, and in his lips he hids fire.
A perverse man sends forth evil, and kindls a lamp of deceit for the wicked, and separats friends.
A lawless man entices friends, and leads them into ways that are not good.
He that fixes his eyes with deceit deviss perverse things, and biting with his lips he commands all evil: [This man is a furnace of wickedness.][^2140]
Old age is a crown of praise, and it is found in the ways of righteousness.
A long-suffering man is better than a strong one; [and a man having understanding than a great husbandman;][^2141] and he that rules his anger is better than he that takes a strong city.
All things come into the lap of the unrighteous, but from the Lord are all righteous things.

*(Chapter 17).*
Better is a morsel of bread with pleasure in peace, than a house full of many good things and unrighteous sacrifices.[^2142]

*(fol. 709)*
of contention in the house.[^2143]

A wise servant shall have rule over foolish masters, and among brethren he shall divide portions.[^2144]

As gold and silver are tried in a furnace, so are chosen hearts with the Lord.[^2145]

An evil man gives ear to the tongue of the lawless, but the righteous man heeds not lying lips.[^2146]

He that mocks the poor provokes Him that made him; [and he that hath compassion shall obtain mercy;] but he that rejoices over the perishing shall not go unpunished.[^2147]

Children's children are the crown of old men, and the boast of children is their fathers. To the faithful man belongs the whole world of riches, but to the unfaithful not even a penny.[^2148]

Faithful lips become not a fool, neither do lying lips become a righteous man.[^2149]

Instruction is a reward of graces unto them that use it; and whithersoever it turns, it shall prosper.[^2150]

He that conceals wrongs seeks friendship; but he that hates to conceal separates friends and household.[^2151]

A threat breaks the heart of a wise man, but a fool when whipped feels it not.[^2152]

Every evil man stirs up gainsaying, but the Lord will send an unmerciful angel unto him.[^2153]

Care falls upon a man of understanding, but a fool devises evil.[^2154]

Whoso rewards evil for good, evil shall not depart from his house.[^2155]

Authority gives beginning of righteousness to words; but discord and strife precede poverty.[^2156]

He that judges the righteous unrighteous, and the unrighteous righteous, is unclean and abominable before God.[^2157]

To what purpose are riches unto a fool? For a senseless man cannot purchase wisdom;[^2158]

*(fol. 710)*
[he that builds his house high seeks destruction; and he that is negligent to learn shall fall into evils.][^2159]

Let a friend be unto thee at all times; and let brethren be useful in necessities, for for this cause are they born.[^2160]

*Then: "Let my prayer be set forth:" And the Divine Liturgy of the Presanctified Gifts is celebrated, at which, having been made worthy, we partake of the Holy Mysteries of Christ.*

*At the trapeza we eat oil and drink wine, because of the labor of the vigil.*

*In the Studite Typikon, however, it is commanded to eat dry food during all this week, more than the others; for these are days of weeping, and not of feast, for in them it is also proper to sing "Alleluia."*[^2161]

*In the Typikon of the Holy Mountain, it is judged concerning the Holy Forty Martyrs, the Finding of the Head of the Forerunner, Wednesday of the Cross, the Great Canon, and the Akathist [Hymn], to eat two cooked dishes with oil, and to drink two cups of wine.*[^2162]

*These things we have indicated unto your love concerning both; that he who desires to be saved may choose what is more well-pleasing before God.*

*If the Annunciation of the Most Holy Theotokos fall on this day: First, the Office of the Great Canon is sung in the night, from Monday to Tuesday; and the Feast takes place on this day without change (see fol. 661).[^2163]*

*If the Annunciation of the Most Holy Theotokos fall on Friday of the Fifth Week of the Fast: We sing the Forefeast of the Annunciation, the Stichera and the Canon beforehand on Wednesday, alongside the Great Canon. To the Saint in the Menaion we sing at Compline. On Thursday evening: Vespers, and the Presanctified Liturgy, and the trapeza (see fol. 774).[^2164] At the sixth hour of the night, we sing Great Compline. After "Glory to God in the highest:" the exit into the narthex, and the Stichera of the Feast; and the entire Matins service, as is clearly indicated there.*

*(fol. 711)*
## On Friday of the Fifth Week of the Holy Fast

*At Matins, after "Alleluia," Triadica of the Tone.*

*After the 1st Stichology, Sessional Hymn in the Octoechos. After the 2nd Stichology:*

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 1, Podoben: "Thy tomb, O Savior" (Гро́бъ тво́й):*
Thou didst stretch forth Thy palms upon the Tree, O Christ, healing the wound of Adam by Thy wounds; therefore I pray Thee, heal my wounds which the deceiver hath inflicted upon my soul, and vouchsafe that in prayer and fasting, O Savior, I may please Thee.[^2165]

*Glory... the same. Both now... Stavrotheotokion:*
Beholding Thee dead, O Christ, stretched out upon the Cross, Thine all-immaculate Mother cried aloud: "O my Son, co-unoriginate with the Father and the Spirit, what is this Thine unutterable dispensation, whereby Thou hast saved the creation of Thine all-pure hands, O compassionate One?"[^2166]

*After the 3rd Stichology, Sessional Hymn, Tone 6, Podoben: "The hope of the world" (Оу҆пова́нїе мі́рꙋ):*
O Cross, guardian of the world, driver away of demons, invincible unto them that have acquired thee in every protection: vouchsafe us to pass through the remainder of the fast with a pure conscience, directing our souls before Christ, O most blessed Tree![^2167]

*Glory... the same. Both now... Stavrotheotokion:*
Honorable Virgin and honorable glory of the Angels, when thou didst stand by the Cross of Thy Son and God, unable to endure beholding the mockery of the enemies, thou didst call out, crying in motherly grief: "How dost Thou endure the threats of all, O Lover of mankind? Glory to Thy long-suffering!"[^2168]

*At the 4th Ode, Sessional Hymn in the Menaion.*

*Triode, by Lord Joseph. Tone 1, Ode 5. Heirmos: "O Thou Who didst enlighten" (Просвѣще́нїе сїѧ́):*
O Thou Who didst stretch out the heaven like a curtain,[^2169] Thou didst stretch out Thy palms upon *(fol. 712)*
the Cross, O Jesus, all-good Lord; therefore I pray Thee, show compassion unto me who am laid low by the temptations of the enemy.[^2170]

*Troparion:* Thou didst fall asleep upon the Cross, O Jesus, Lover of mankind, granting the wakefulness of salvation unto all that lie in lowest perdition, O Lord; therefore in faith we glorify Thee.[^2171]

*Troparion:* Vouchsafe Thy servants to behold the day of Thy Passion, with hearts enlightened by brightness, and singing the dominion of Thy Kingdom, O Savior, the resurrection of life-giving power.[^2172]

*Theotokion:* Beholding Thee lifted up upon the Cross, the all-immaculate Virgin wept, consumed in her womb, and said: "Because of the tender mercy of Thy compassions, O Lord, Thou hast endured the Passions, granting dispassion unto all!"[^2173]

*Another Heirmos, by Lord Theodore. Tone 6. Heirmos: "Rising early from the night" (И҆з̾ но́щи ᲂу҆́тренююще):*
*Troparion:* Upon the Cross, O Lover of mankind, Thou didst spread out Thy hands, and the Jews nailed Thee with nails and pierced Thy side with a spear, and Thou dost endure all things, O Christ, that we may be saved.[^2174]

*Troparion:* By eating of the tree, Adam once died; but again through the Tree of the Cross he found life, through which he enjoys the delight of the food of compassions inside Paradise.[^2175]

*Trinity:* I hymn Thee, the Trinity single in essence: unoriginate, uncreated, sovereign, royal, all-perfect Unity, God, and Light, and Life, Creator of the world.[^2176]

*Theotokion:* In thy divine birthgiving, O pure Lady, the laws of nature are manifestly dissolved through thee; for without seed thou barest the pre-eternal God, Begotten of the Father.[^2177]

*Refrain:* Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.
*Troparion:* The Cross, and the Nails, and Thy Spear we venerate, *(fol. 713)*
O Master; for thereby Thou hast delivered us from corruption, who through Thy Passions, O Christ, were slain.[^2178]

*Heirmos:* Rising early out of the night, O Lover of mankind, enlighten me, and guide me in Thy commandments, and teach me, O Savior, to do Thy will.[^2179]

*Ode 8. Heirmos: "The wonder that surpasses nature" (Чꙋ́да преесте́ственнагѡ):*
*Troparion:* Thou hast blunted the sting of the subtle one, O Savior, being nailed with nails upon the Tree; clothed with a crown of thorns, Thou hast uprooted the thorns of the reproach of transgression; therefore singing unto Thee, we cry aloud: Let all creation bless the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto all ages![^2180]

*Troparion:* Thou didst stretch out Thy palms upon the Cross, O Christ, gathering mankind to knowledge of Thyself, and Thou didst endure having Thy side pierced with a spear, pouring forth for us the fountain of salvation, as we sing: Let all creation bless the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto all ages![^2181]

*Troparion:* With the streams of Thy mercy, O compassionate Christ, cleanse my heart which hath been defiled by the biting of sins, and vouchsafe me to pour forth rivers of compunction, O Christ Jesus, that I may cry: Let all creation bless the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto all ages![^2182]

*Theotokion:* As the divine Jar containing the Manna of the Godhead we have known thee, O Maiden, Ark and Table, Candlestick, Throne of God, and Palace, and Bridge leading unto divine life them that sing: Let all creation bless the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto all ages![^2183]

*Another Heirmos. "The song of the children" (Ѻ҆тро́ческꙋю пѣ́снь):*
*Troparion:* Christ is crucified, and I am brought to life; sing with the children: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, sing and exalt Him above all unto all ages![^2184]

*Troparion:* The world, delivered from corruption by Thy Crucifixion, sings with the children: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, sing and exalt Him above all unto all ages![^2185]

*Let us bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, the Lord.*
*Trinity:*

*(fol. 714)*
O Trinity equal in glory, co-eternal Unity, Father, and Son, and Spirit, save them that sing unto Thee in faith.[^2186]

*Theotokion:* Worshiping the childbearing of the pure Theotokos, sing with the children: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord![^2187]

*Refrain:* Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.
*Troparion:* I sing of Thy Cross, whereby Thou hast saved me, O Christ; sing with the children: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord![^2188]

*Heirmos:* Emulating the song of the children, cry aloud, sing with the youths: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto all ages![^2189]

*Ode 9. Heirmos: "The image of the pure childbearing" (Ѻ҆́бразъ ч[ис]та́гѡ):*
*Troparion:* Elijah beheld the Lord in a subtle whirlwind, having first refined the flesh by prayers and fasting; whom emulating, O my soul, cast away the grossness of pleasures, that thou mayest see Him Who is desired.[^2190]

*Troparion:* Moses of old lifted up the serpent upon the tree, O Savior, prefiguring Thy lifting up, which was upon the Cross, O all-good One, against the venomous malice of the serpent; whereby Thou hast delivered all nations that worship Thee.[^2191]

*Troparion:* Lying in the tomb of despondency, having the heavy stone of perplexity, not understanding the ever-living word of Thy saying, O Savior, and feeling not Thy fear: show compassion on me and save me by Thy goodness, O most merciful One![^2192]

*Theotokion:* O Lady higher than all, show me to be above the passions of malice, who glorify thee as true Theotokos, and sing of thy childbearing, O pure one, revered beyond comprehension, O thou full of God's grace![^2193]

*Another Heirmos. "Seedless conception" (Безсѣ́менна зача́тїа):*
*Troparion:* Thou art crucified and dost save me; Thou diest and givest me life. O the tender compassion, O the love for mankind *(fol. 715)*
of Thine! Who hath seen, or who hath heard of a Master accepting a shameful death for a servant? But glory to Thine unutterable goodness, O Lord![^2194]

*Troparion:* The sun set when it beheld Thee crucified, for how could it shine, seeing the reproach of its Creator? So also all creation, bowing down, cried out to the crucifiers in silence: "Thou art the God of all, even though Thou art suffering in the flesh!"[^2195]

*Trinity:* O Father of the One, the only Begetter of the only-begotten Son, and one Radiance of the light of the one Light, and one Holy Spirit of the one God, Lord, truly being Lord: O Holy Trinity, Unity, save me who theologize Thee![^2196]

*Theotokion:* The wonder of thy childbearing amazes me, O all-immaculate Lady: how dost thou conceive without seed Him Who is incomprehensible? Tell how thou remainest a virgin, having given birth as a Mother? Which, accepting by faith beyond nature, worship Him that is born; for whatsoever He wills, He can also do.[^2197]

*Refrain:* Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.
*Troparion:* For our sake each of Thy members received suffering: Thy head the blows, Thy cheeks the slapping, Thy hands the nailing, Thy side the spear, and the Crucifixion on the Cross; but glory to Thine unutterable tender compassion, O our Savior![^2198]

*Heirmos:* Seedless conception, ineffable childbearing, of a mother that knew no man, an undefiled gestation; for the birth of God renews nature; therefore all generations, as Mother unwedded of God, orthodoxly magnify thee.[^2199]

*Then: It is truly meet:*
*Photogogikon.*

*At the Aposticha, Idiomelon, Tone 8:*
Nailed unto the Cross with thieves, O Christ *(fol. 716)*
God, and Who by Thy wound didst heal human nature: despise me not, who have fallen among mental bandits and bodiless thieves, and have been stripped by them of virtues, and grievously wounded, who could not be healed by any of the righteous; for I am half-dead, having a wretched body of life, having only hope in Thee, Who grantest life unto the dead. But bind up my wounds, dripping Thy goodness upon me, O only Lover of mankind![^2200]

*Verse: We were filled in the morning with Thy mercy:*
*And again the same Sticheron. Verse 2:*
*And let the brightness of the Lord our God be upon us:*
*Martyrikon:*
What shall we call you, O saints? Cherubim, for Christ rested upon you; Seraphim, for ye unceasingly glorify Him; Angels, for ye turned away from the body; Powers, for ye work miracles. Many are your names, and greater are your gifts; pray that our souls may be saved.[^2201]

*Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion. Same Tone.*
*Podoben: "O most marvelous wonder" (Ѽ пресла́вное чꙋ́до):*
O most marvelous wonder and new mystery! O fearful undertaking! The Virgin said, when she beheld Thee suspended upon the Cross between two thieves, Whom she bare without travail and corruption: "How hath the lawless and ungrateful people nailed my Heart to the Cross, O sweetest Jesus?"[^2202]

*On Friday of the Fifth Week, at the Sixth Hour,*
*Troparion of the Prophecy, Tone 8:*

*(fol. 717)*
All-hymned art Thou, O Christ our God, Who shakest the earth, so as to turn back and save them that dwell upon it, and Who again dost establish it according to Thy goodness and unutterable tender compassion; by the intercessions of the Theotokos, have mercy on us![^2203]

*Glory... the end. Both now... all. Prokeimenon, Psalm 100, Tone 4:*
Mercy and judgment will I sing unto Thee, O Lord!
*Verse:* I will sing and have understanding in a blameless way.[^2204]

*Reading from the Prophecy of Isaiah (Chapter 45).*
Thus saith the Lord God, the Holy One of Israel, Who made him and created the things to come: Ask Me concerning My sons and concerning My daughters, and give Me command concerning the works of My hands.
I have made the earth, and man upon it; I with My hand have established the heaven, I have given command to all the stars.
I have raised him up with righteousness as a king, and all his ways are right; he shall build My city, and shall turn back the captivity of My people, not for price nor for reward, saith the Lord of hosts.
Thus saith the Lord of hosts: Egypt hath labored, and the merchandise of the Ethiopians, and the Sabeans, men of stature, shall pass over unto thee, and they shall be thy servants, and they shall follow after thee, bound with hand-fetters, and they shall pass over unto thee, and shall bow down unto thee, and make supplication in thee, for God is in thee, and there is no God beside thee.
For Thou art God, and we knew it not, the God of Israel, the Savior.
All that oppose Him shall be ashamed and confounded, *(fol. 718)*
and shall walk in shame. Be ye renewed unto Me, ye islands of Israel; be ye saved of the Lord with an everlasting salvation; ye shall not be ashamed neither confounded, even forevermore, saith the Lord Almighty.[^2205]

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 101, Tone 4:*
O Lord, hear my prayer, and let my cry come unto Thee!
*Verse:* Turn not away Thy face from me.[^2206]
*Then: Let Thy compassions quickly go before us:*

*On the same Friday of the Fifth Week, in the evening:*
*After the customary Stichology. At "Lord, I have cried," we set 10 stichera, and sing Idiomela of the day, 2, Tone 6:*
Departing as from Jerusalem from Thy divine commandments, and having arrived at the passions of Jericho, drawn away by the glory of dishonor of worldly pursuits, I have fallen among bandit thoughts, and have been stripped by them of the robe of the adoption of grace, and I lie as one lifeless with wounds. But the priest came, and seeing the wound, took no heed; and the Levite also, abhorring me, passed by. But Thou, O Lord, Who wast ineffably incarnate of the Virgin, having poured out from the saving wound of Thy side the blood and water that voluntarily flowed forth, dripping it like oil, O Christ God, bind up the sores of my wounds with softness, and unite me unto the heavenly choir, as Thou art tender-hearted![^2207]

*Then Martyrikon:*
Thy martyrs, O Lord, denied Thee not, neither departed from Thy commandments; by their intercessions have mercy on us![^2208]

*Then Prosomoia Stichera to the Most Holy Theotokos. We make 3 [stichera] into 6. Tone 6, Podoben: "Having laid aside all earthly hope" (Всѐ ѿло́жше):*

*(fol. 719)*
*Sticheron 1:* Revealing unto thee the pre-eternal counsel, O Maiden, Gabriel stood before thee, greeting thee and saying: "Rejoice, unsown Earth! Rejoice, unburnt Bush! Rejoice, Depth hard to fathom! Rejoice, Bridge leading unto Heaven, and lofty Ladder which Jacob beheld! Rejoice, divine Urn of Manna! Rejoice, loosening of the curse! Rejoice, recall of Adam: the Lord is with thee!" (sung twice)[^2209]

*Sticheron 2:* "Thou appearest unto me as a man," said the undefiled Maiden unto the Archangel, "and how dost thou utter words beyond man? For thou hast said that God is to be with me, and to make His dwelling in my womb. And how, tell me, shall I become a spacious dwelling and a holy place of Him Who excels the Cherubim? Do not beguile me with deceit, for I have known no pleasure, and am not a partaker of marriage: how then shall I bear a child?" (sung twice)[^2210]

*Sticheron 3:* "Where God wills, the order of nature is overcome," said the bodiless one, "and things beyond man are accomplished; believe my true words, O all-holy and all-undefiled one!" And she cried aloud: "Be it unto me now according to thy word, and I shall bear the Bodiless One, Who borrows flesh from me, that He, as the only Mighty One, may restore man unto his first dignity through the intermingling!" (sung twice)[^2211]

*Verse: For His mercy is confirmed upon us:*
*Again: Revealing unto thee the pre-eternal counsel:*
*Glory... Both now... Tone 2:*
The mystery hidden from the ages is revealed today, and the Son of God becomes the Son of man, that receiving the worse, He may impart unto me the better. Of old Adam was deceived, and desiring to become God...[^2212]

*(fol. 720)*
...he became not so; but God becomes man, that He may make Adam god. Let creation rejoice, let nature dance in triumph, for the Archangel stands with fear before the Virgin, bringing the "Rejoice," the reverse of sorrow. O Thou Who through the tender compassion of Thy mercy didst become man, our God, glory to Thee![^2213]

*If the Liturgy of the Presanctified Gifts is not celebrated, we set the Stichera of the Theotokos to 8. At the Aposticha, Idiomela of the day, 2, and the Martyrikon. Glory... Both now... "The language which he knew not:" Written at the Praises on Saturday.*[^2214]

*In the evening, Prokeimenon, Psalm 102, Tone 4:*
The Lord is full of compassion and merciful, longsuffering, and of great mercy.
*Verse:* Bless the Lord, O my soul, and all that is within me, bless His holy name.[^2215]

*Reading from Genesis (Chapter 22).*
And it came to pass after these things, that God did tempt Abraham, and said unto him: "Abraham, Abraham!" And he said: "Behold, here am I."
And He said: "Take now thy son, thine only-beloved son Isaac, whom thou lovest, and get thee into the high land, and offer him there for a whole burnt-offering upon one of the mountains which I will tell thee of."
And Abraham rose up early in the morning, and saddled his donkey, and took two of his young men with him, and Isaac his son; and having split the wood for the whole burnt-offering, he arose and went, and came unto the place of which God had told him on the third day.
And Abraham lifted up his eyes, and saw the place afar off.
And Abraham said unto his young men: "Abide ye here with the donkey; and I and the lad will go yonder and worship, and come again to you."[^2216]

*(fol. 721)*
And Abraham took the wood of the whole burnt-offering, and laid it upon Isaac his son; and he took the fire in his hand, and a knife; and they went both of them together.
And Isaac spoke unto Abraham his father, and said: "Father!" And he said: "What is it, my child?" And he said: "Behold the fire and the wood, but where is the sheep for a whole burnt-offering?"
And Abraham said: "God will provide for Himself a sheep for a whole burnt-offering, my child." So they went both of them together.
And they came to the place which God had told him of; and Abraham built an altar there, and laid the wood in order, and bound Isaac his son, and laid him on the altar upon the wood.
And Abraham stretched forth his hand, to take the knife to slay his son.
And the Angel of the Lord called unto him out of Heaven, and said: "Abraham, Abraham!" And he said: "Behold, here am I."
And He said: "Lay not thine hand upon the lad, neither do thou anything unto him; for now I know that thou fearest God, and hast not spared thy beloved son for My sake."
And Abraham lifted up his eyes, and looked, and behold a ram held fast by his horns in the plant of Sabek; and Abraham went and took the ram, and offered him up for a whole burnt-offering in the stead of Isaac his son.
And Abraham called the name of that place: "The Lord hath seen," so that they say today: "In the mount the Lord was seen."
And the Angel of the Lord called unto Abraham a second time out of Heaven, saying: "By Myself have I sworn, saith the Lord, because thou hast done this thing, and hast not spared thy beloved son for My sake:
Surely blessing I will bless thee, and multiplying I will multiply thy seed as the stars of heaven, and as...[^2217]

*(fol. 722)*
...the sand which is upon the seashore; and thy seed shall inherit the cities of their adversaries; and in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed, because thou hast obeyed My voice."[^2218]

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 103, Tone 4:*
O Lord, how magnificent are Thy works, in wisdom hast Thou made them all!
*Verse:* Bless the Lord, O my soul; O Lord my God, Thou art become exceedingly great.[^2219]

*Reading from Proverbs (Chapter 17).*
Brethren, in necessities let them be useful; for for this cause do they show kindness.
A senseless man clapps his hands, and rejoices in himself, as also he that strikes hands pledgs his friend.
He that loves sin rejoices in strifes; and upon his own lips he gathers fire.
He that exalts his own house seeks destruction.
The hard-hearted finds not good things.
A man that is fickle in tongue will fall into evils.
The heart of a senseless man is grief unto him that possesses it.
A father has no joy over an undisciplined son; but a wise son gladdens his mother.
A merry heart makes a man thrive, but the bones of a sorrowful man dry up.
The ways of him that takes unjust gifts in the bosom shall not prosper; and the ungodly man turns aside from the ways of righteousness.
The countenance of a wise man is prudent, but the eyes of a senseless man are on the ends of the earth.
A senseless son is wrath unto his father, and grief unto her that bare him.
To impose a fine upon a righteous man is not good, neither is it right to plot against the mighty concerning righteous things.
He that spars to utter a harsh word is understanding, and a longsuffering man...[^2220]

*(fol. 723)*
...man is very wise: [better than he that seeks not to learn].
Even a fool, when he asks of wisdom, shall be counted wise; and he that makes himself dumb shall seem to be wise.
*(Chapter 18)*
A man that desires to separate himself from friends seeks pretexts, and at all times he will be liable to reproach.
A man lacking understanding has no need of wisdom, for he is rather led by folly.
When the wicked man comes into the depth of evils, he despises them; and dishonor and reproach come upon him.
A deep water is the word in a man's heart, but a gushing river is the fountain of life.
It is not good to respect the person of the wicked, neither is it right to turn aside the righteous in judgment.[^2221]

*And the rest of the Liturgy of the Presanctified Gifts. At Compline we chant the Great Prayers.*[^2222]

*Typikon Chapter 78: If on this Saturday of the Akathist the memory of the Forty Martyrs should occur:*[^2223]
*The service is chanted to the Akathist and to the saints as follows: On Friday evening, Kathisma: "Unto the Lord when I was afflicted:" At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera to 10: Idiomela of the day, 2; and of the Theotokos, 5; and of the saints, 3. Glory... to the saints, Tone 2: "Passion-bearers of Christ." Both now... of the Theotokos: "The mystery hidden from the ages." Entrance. Prokeimenon of the day, and readings of the day, and to the saints, 3. After "Let my prayer be set forth," 3 great prostrations. And after "Now the heavenly hosts," 3. And at "Blessed be the name of the Lord," 3. And at the dismissal, 3 prostrations; and the rest of the Presanctified. Then we chant the Triodion of Matins at Compline instead of the Canon of the departed. But the Canon of the departed we chant when the superior wills, either before sitting down at the trapeza, or after rising up from the trapeza.*
*At Matins, at "God is the Lord," Troparion of the feast, twice; Glory... to the saints; Both now... of the feast. After the 1st Kathisma: Kondakia of the feast, 3, and Ikoses, 3; and again the first Kontakion. Then the reading of the feast. In like manner also after the 2nd Kathisma. Then Psalm 50. Canon of the feast with the Heirmos to 8, and of the saints to 6. Katavasia, the Heirmos of the Theotokos, both choirs together. After Ode 3, Kondakia of the feast, 3, and Ikoses. Then Kontakion and Ikos to the saints, and their Sessional Hymns, 2.*

*(fol. 724)*
*Glory... Both now... of the Theotokos. And the reading: the Encomium of Basil the Great upon the holy Forty Martyrs. After Ode 6, Kondakia and Ikoses of the feast, 3; and again the first Kontakion and Ikos. Then the Prologue and the Synaxarion. At Ode 9 we sing "More honorable." Exaposteilarion of the feast; Glory... to the saints; Both now... of the Theotokos. At the Praises, Stichera of the Theotokos, 3; and to the saints, 3. Glory... to the saints, Tone 2: "The true cup." Both now... of the feast, Tone 4: "The language which he knew not." Great Doxology. Troparion to the saints; Both now... of the feast. Litanies and dismissal. Exit and the First Hour. At the First Hour, Troparion of the feast; Glory... to the saints; Both now... Theotokion of the Hours. After the third [prayer], Kontakion of the feast. At the Third Hour, Troparion of the feast; Glory... to the saints; Both now... Theotokion of the Hours; after the third [prayer], Kontakion to the saints.*
*At the Divine Liturgy, the Beatitudes of the Theotokos, Ode 3 to 4; and to the saints, Ode 6 to 4. After the Little Entrance, Troparion of the Theotokos, and to the saints. Glory... Kontakion to the saints; Both now... Kontakion of the Theotokos. Prokeimenon, Epistle, Alleluia, Gospel, and the rest, first of the feast, then to the saints.*[^2224]

*Typikon Chapter 88: If on this Saturday of the Akathist the Annunciation of the Most Holy Theotokos should occur:*[^2225]
*On Friday evening, at "Lord, I have cried," Stichera to 10: Idiomela of the day, 2; and of the feast to 8. Glory... Both now... of the feast, Tone 6: "The Archangel Gabriel was sent." Entrance. Reading of the day, and of the feast, 5. And after "Let my prayer be set forth," 3 great prostrations; and after "Now the heavenly hosts," 3; and at "Blessed be the name of the Lord," 3; and at the dismissal, 3 prostrations; and the rest of the Presanctified.*
*At the 3rd hour of the night, the klepalo strikes two, and then all the heavy bells. When the priest has given the blessing, we chant Great Compline. The priest censes according to custom. After "Glory to God in the highest," we perform the customary Litiya, wherein we chant Idiomela of the feast, 3, Tone 1. Glory... Both now... of the feast, Tone 2: "Gabriel announcs good tidings." And the customary prayer. After the conclusion, we re-enter the church, and chant Idiomela of the feast, 3, Tone 4. We chant the verses: "Proclaim the good tidings of His salvation from day to day;" Verse 2: "Sing unto the Lord a new song." Glory... Both now... Tone 4: "Today is joy." At the blessing of the loaves, Troparion of the feast, thrice; and the reading of the feast.*
*At Matins, at "God is the Lord," Troparion of the feast, thrice. After the 1st Kathisma: "To thee, the Champion Leader;" Kondakia, 3, and Ikoses, 3; and again Kontakion 1; and the reading of the Akathist. After the 2nd stichology: Kondakia, 3, and Ikoses, 3; and again Kontakion 1; and the reading of the Akathist. Polyeleos; and Sessional Hymn of the feast, and reading of the Polyeleos. 1st Antiphon of the 4th Tone. Prokeimenon and Gospel of the feast. Psalm 50. Sticheron of the feast. Canon of the feast with the Heirmos to 8, and of the Akathist to 6. Katavasia, the Heirmos of the feast, both choirs together. The Four-ode Canon is not chanted here, but ahead, on...*

*(fol. 725)*
*...at Small Compline. After Ode 3, Kondakia, 3, and Ikoses, 3; and again Kontakion 1. After this, Sessional Hymn and reading of the feast. After Ode 6, Kondakia, 3, and Ikoses, 3. Then Kontakion: "O all-hymned Mother," thrice; and again Ikos 1 and Kontakion 1; and the reading in the Prologue and the Synaxarion. At Ode 9, we do not sing "More honorable." Exaposteilarion of the feast, thrice. At the Praises, Stichera of the feast to 4, Tone 4, Podoben: "As one noble among the martyrs" (Нб҃нымъ чиномъ: "To the heavenly ranks"):*
*Glory... Both now... Tone 8: "Let the heavens rejoice." Great Doxology. Troparion of the feast. Litanies. And the Studite Catechesis, and the dismissal. And the brethren are anointed with holy oil. And the First Hour in the Narthex; and the procession outside the monastery.*
*At the Divine Liturgy, the Beatitudes of the feast, Ode 3 and 6 to 4, or to 8. Prokeimenon and Epistle, Alleluia, Gospel, and Communion Verse, all of the feast.*[^2226]

*Typikon Chapter 86: If the Apodosis of the feast of the Annunciation of the Most Holy Theotokos should occur on the Saturday of the Akathist:*[^2227]
*On Friday evening, we chant Stichera to 10: in the Triodion, Idiomela of the day, 2; and of the feast of the Theotokos, Tone 6: "The eternal counsel," to 8. Glory... in the Triodion, Tone 2: "The mystery hidden from the ages." Both now... of the feast, Tone 6: "Gabriel was sent." Entrance; and the reading of the day, and of the feast, 5. And after "Let my prayer be set forth," 3 great prostrations. And after "Now the heavenly hosts," 3 prostrations. And at "Blessed be the name of the Lord," 3. And in order the Liturgy of the Presanctified, and the rest; and at the dismissal, 3 great prostrations.*
*At Matins, at "God is the Lord," Troparion of the Akathist, thrice. After the 1st Kathisma: Kondakia, 3, and Ikoses, 3; and again Kontakion 1; and reading of the Akathist. After the 2nd Kathisma: Kondakia, 3, and Ikoses, 3; and again Kontakion 1; and the reading. Psalm 50. Canon of the feast with the Heirmos to 6, and of the Akathist to 8. Katavasia: "I will open my mouth," both choirs together. The biblical odes are not said. The Four-ode Canon is not sung here, but was sung ahead on Thursday at Small Compline. After Ode 3, Kondakia, 3, and Ikoses, 3; and again Kontakion 1. And after that, Sessional Hymn of the feast, and reading of the feast. After Ode 6, Kondakia, 3, and Ikoses, 3; then: "O all-hymned Mother," thrice; and again Kontakion and Ikos 1; and reading in the Prologue. At Ode 9, we do not sing "More honorable." We chant the refrain of the feast: "O earth, proclaim the great joy;" then the Heirmos; to each troparion of the feast we sing the same refrain; and at the end the Heirmos, and a prostration to the ground. Exaposteilarion of the feast, twice. At the Praises, Stichera in the Triodion to 4, Tone 4, Podoben: "As one noble among the martyrs" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ): "The hidden mystery." Glory... Both now... together, of the Akathist and of the feast, Tone 8: "Let the heavens rejoice." Great Doxology. After the Trisagion, Troparion of the feast; litany, and dismissal, and the First Hour. At the First Hour, Troparion of the feast; after the Trisagion, Kontakion of the feast, and the rest, and the complete dismissal.*
*At the Divine Liturgy, the Beatitudes of the Akathist, Ode 3 and 6. Prokeimenon of the Theotokos of the Akathist: "My soul doth magnify the Lord." Epistle to the Hebrews, section 322: "Brethren, Christ being come an High Priest of good things to come, by a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands..." Then Epistle of the Theotokos to the Hebrews, section 320: "Brethren, the first tabernacle had also ordinances of divine service..." Alleluia of the Theotokos. Gospel according to Mark, section 35: "At that time, Jesus went forth..." Then Gospel of the Theotokos according to Luke, section 4: "At that time, Mary arose..." Communion Verse: "I will take the cup of salvation."*[^2228]

*(fol. 726)*

## ON SATURDAY OF THE FIFTH WEEK OF THE HOLY FAST (THE AKATHIST SATURDAY)

*At Matins, the semantron is struck upon the great and heavy bell at the 4th hour of the night for the sake of the Supplicatory Office of the Akathist. And when we have gathered in church, and the priest has given the blessing, he begins Matins; and the priest censes the whole church.*

*After the Six Psalms and the litany, "God is the Lord," in Tone 8; and we sing the Troparion thrice, slowly, Tone 8:*[^2230]

*Troparion, Tone 8:* Having mystically received the command in his understanding, the bodiless one stood quickly in the dwelling of Joseph, saying unto her that knew not wedlock: "He Who bowed the heavens by His descent is contained wholly and immutably in thee; and beholding Him in thy womb...[^2231]

*(fol. 727)*
...taking the form of a servant, I am astonished and cry unto thee: Rejoice, unwedded Bride!"

*And at the last: Glory... Both now...*

*Then we stichologize Kathisma 16 of the Psalter: "The Lord said unto my Lord:"*

*And after its completion, litany. And we sing the Kontakion in the midst of the church (or to 8 tones) with melody, slowly and harmoniously. The deacon censes the holy icons and all the brethren in order. And he does this at all four beginnings.*[^2232]

*Kontakion 1, Tone 8:* To thee, the Champion Leader, we thy servants inscribe hymns of victory and thanksgiving, having been delivered from afflictions, O Theotokos! But as thou hast invincible might, deliver us from all dangers, that we may cry unto thee: Rejoice, unwedded Bride![^2233]

*And we read 6 of the Ikoses. These Ikoses are according to the alphabet: that is, 24. And they are recited by the priest vested in all the sacred vestments, in the holy Altar. When the priest reads the Kondakia and Ikoses, we do not sit down then, but listen standing; and the paraecclesiarch places before the Holy Doors a lamp upon a candlestick, and a censer with fragrant incense.*[^2234]

*Ikos 1 (Alpha):*
An Archangel was sent from Heaven to say unto the Theotokos: "Rejoice!" And beholding Thee taking flesh with a bodiless voice, O Lord, he was astonished and stood, crying unto her such things as these:
Rejoice, through whom joy shall shine forth!
Rejoice, through whom the curse shall vanish!
Rejoice, recall of fallen Adam!
Rejoice, deliverance from the tears of Eve!
Rejoice, Height hard to climb by human thoughts!
Rejoice, Depth hard to fathom even by the eyes of Angels!
Rejoice, for thou art the King's throne!
Rejoice, for thou bearest Him Who bears all things!
Rejoice...[^2235]

*(fol. 728)*
...Star revealing the Sun!
Rejoice, Womb of the divine incarnation!
Rejoice, through whom creation is renewed!
Rejoice, through whom we worship the Creator!
Rejoice, unwedded Bride![^2236]

*Kontakion 2 (Beta):* Seeing herself in purity, the Holy One said boldly unto Gabriel: "The marvel of thy word appears hard for my soul to accept; for thou proclaimest a childbearing of a seedless conception, crying: Alleluia!"[^2237]

*Ikos 2 (Gamma):* Seeking to know the unknowable knowledge, the Virgin cried unto him that served: "Tell me, how is it possible for a Son to be born from a pure womb?" Unto whom he spoke with fear, yet crying thus:
Rejoice, initiate of the ineffable counsel!
Rejoice, faith of them that pray in silence!
Rejoice, beginning of the miracles of Christ!
Rejoice, foundation of His doctrines!
Rejoice, heavenly Ladder, by which God came down!
Rejoice, Bridge leading them that are from earth unto Heaven!
Rejoice, wonder much-renowned among the Angels!
Rejoice, wound much-lamented among the demons!
Rejoice, who ineffably gavest birth to the Light!
Rejoice, who hast taught none the manner thereof!
Rejoice, surpassing the knowledge of the wise!
Rejoice, enlightening the minds of the faithful!
Rejoice, unwedded Bride![^2238]

*Kontakion 3 (Delta):* The power of the Most High then overshadowed her that knew not wedlock unto conception; and her fruitful womb He showed forth as a sweet field unto all that desire to reap salvation, when chanting thus: Alleluia![^2239]

*Ikos 3 (Epsilon):* Having received God within her womb, the Virgin hastened...[^2240]

*(fol. 729)*
...unto Elizabeth; and her babe immediately, having recognized her salutation, rejoiced, and with leapings as with songs cried aloud unto the Theotokos:
Rejoice, Vine of the unfading shoot!
Rejoice, possession of the immortal fruit!
Rejoice, who workest for the Husbandman Who loves mankind!
Rejoice, who didst bear the Planter of our life!
Rejoice, Furrow producing an abundance of compassions!
Rejoice, Table laden with an abundance of purification!
Rejoice, for thou blossomest forth as a paradise of delights!
Rejoice, for thou preparest a haven for souls!
Rejoice, acceptable Incense of intercession!
Rejoice, cleansing of the whole world!
Rejoice, good will of God towards mortals!
Rejoice, boldness of mortals before God!
Rejoice, unwedded Bride![^2241]

*Kontakion 4 (Zeta):* Having within a storm of doubting thoughts, the chaste Joseph was troubled, looking upon thee, unwedded one, and suspecting a stolen wedlock, O undefiled one; but learning that thy conception was of the Holy Spirit, he said: Alleluia![^2242]

*And again the Kontakion:*
*To thee, the Champion Leader: (see fol. 726).*[^2243]

*And we read from the Homily of the Akathist, Part 1; all of this is divided into eleven parts:*[^2244]

*A profitable history compiled from ancient writings, demonstrating and recalling the marvel which conspicuously came to pass, when the Persians and barbarians besieged Constantinople with war, who also perished by the divine judgment, while the City remained unharmed; and from that time, a prayer of thanksgiving is celebrated, and that day is named "The Akathist," that is, "The Unseated Hymn." Bless, father, to read.*[^2245]

*(fol. 730)*
During the reign of Heraclius, Emperor of the Greeks, Khosrow, who held the Persian realm, sent Sarbaros [Shahrbaraz], his commander, with a multitude of soldiers throughout all the Eastern Country, seeking vengeance against the Greeks, that he might march through and overrun it like a fiery lightning bolt, burning, scorching, and destroying.[^2246] And he, with great rashness and unmercifulness, traversing the Eastern country, storming and slaying the Greeks found therein, where there was none to defend it or cut short his frequent onslaught, and especially at that time when the Greek power was exceedingly worn down and humbled through the heavy and truly bestial cruelty of him who at that time governed the Greek realm tyrannically and not imperially—Phocas, I say, the soldier.[^2247] Sarbaros therefore, having reached even unto Chalcedon and surrounded it with soldiers, made ready everything whatsoever pertained to the dominion of that great imperial City; for this indeed he devised, regarding this he took counsel, and toward this he strove by all means.

Beholding such things, Emperor Heraclius—who, after the tyrant Phocas, had recently ascended the imperial throne, and being in great sorrow and affliction—leaving behind the capital, sailed across the Euxine Pontus, that is, across the great sea; and having gathered some further military force, suddenly, when none knew of it, departed into the Persian lands.[^2248] Learning of this departure of the Emperor, the Scythian Chagan immediately threw himself into the enterprise; and he filled the sea with vessels hollowed out of a single tree along their length (and therefore called in the Hellenic tongue *monoxyla*, that is, dugouts)[^2249], and the land he filled with horsemen and foot soldiers.

Those people, however, who remained in Constantinople were comforted and instructed by Sergius, who at that time was Patriarch, that they should not lose hope. "Nay, let us trust, children," said he, "and let us place our hope of salvation and deliverance in God; and unto Him let us lift up our hands and our eyes from our whole soul; and let us believe that He will deliver us from the affliction that has encompassed us, and will scatter all the pagan counsels and plots against us." Being strengthened by such words from the Patriarch, the people found in the City stood firm in faith, having recourse unto the Most Pure Theotokos and unto Christ God, Who through His tender compassion deigned to take flesh from her, waiting to experience His loving-kindness upon themselves...

*(fol. 731)*
...patiently enduring in hope, of which they were afterward accounted worthy, and were not deceived in their trust. The Patrician left by the Emperor to guard the City, Bonus by name, so far as was possible to counter the warriors, directed and executed everything without indolence; "for God wills," said he, "that we should not sit in idleness and do nothing, but that we should manage and devise whatever is according to our strength, while placing our whole hope of salvation in the Most High." For in like manner did Joshua the son of Nun command stratagems and ambushes to be laid against the men of Ai,[^2250] and Gideon armed his soldiers against the Midianites with pitchers and torches;[^2251] and the Patrician Bonus strengthened the city walls, and prepared everything whatsoever pertained unto military necessity.

Patriarch Sergius, moreover, having taken the holy icons of the Mother of God—especially those whereon the Savior is depicted as an Infant carried in maternal arms—walked along the city walls, thereby granting greater strength to our people, but unto the barbarian adversaries fear, flight, and destruction; for those enemies had almost assaulted the City, but soon afterward perished. When, therefore, those Persians who had besieged the city of Chalcedon began to burn the nearby surrounding towns and to do all else that they were accustomed to do when pillaging and ruining cities; and likewise the Scythians and barbarians showed themselves doing even as the Persians: the Patriarch again took the Icon Not-Made-by-Hands of the Lord God and our Savior Jesus Christ, and the divine Robe of the Most Pure Theotokos, and in addition the Life-Creating Wood;[^2252] and walking along the city walls, praying with tears, he said: "Arise, O Lord, help us; and let our enemies be scattered, and let them vanish as smoke, and melt as wax before the face of fire!"[^2253]

And not yet three days had passed after that fearful conflagration, when the whole army of the Scythian leader advanced unto the City; and so great was the multitude of the adversaries, deployed in countless numbers and armored with weapons and mail, that truly speaking, ten Scythians could stand against a single Greek. Nevertheless, the Champion Leader who cries aloud for Christians, the Most Pure Lady, a swift helper unto them that call upon her, especially for those soldiers who at that time happened to be in her divine church called the Source (Pege), slew many of the warring Scythians.[^2254] Such help having come to pass for Christians from the almighty Leader...

*(fol. 732)*
...the Mother of God not only brought about the downfall of the enemy warriors before the Greeks, but also plunged the Scythian leader into alarm and doubt: for seeing so great a downfall of his own men before the citizens through such great assistance of the Mother of God, he understood the beginning of his own destruction, and foresaw that his own final ruin was swiftly approaching. Christians, therefore, perceiving and observing this in them, were filled with great boldness, and made ready their forces for battle day by day, having the Mother of God helping them, showing them to be stronger, and checking the Scythian stratagems, might, and experience in war.

Afterward, by common consent of the Patriarch, the governor of the City, and all the commonalty, certain men were dispatched from the City with gifts to speak of truce unto the Scythians, and to summon them unto peace and accord. But that Chagan, being of bestial and not human character, and rather seized with greed and excessive love of silver, accepted indeed the gifts, but neglecting the talk of truce, dismissed the envoys with nothing, having spoken unto them only this: "Do not deceive yourselves in the God in Whom ye believe; tomorrow I will surely take your city like a bird, and make it desolate; and out of my mercy, I will release each of you in a single garment, and ye shall depart from the city whithersoever ye will; but other kindness than this I will not show toward you." For that wretch also spoke much evil and blasphemed against Christ our God, and against her that bare Him.[^2255]

Hearing therefore such words from the envoys, the inhabitants that were in the City—as many as there were priests, clerics, and others, and the whole assembly of the people—groaning from the inwardness of the heart, and having recourse unto God's holy churches, and lifting up their hands unto Heaven, and praying with many tears, said: "O Lord, our Defender, look down from Thy holy dwelling-place, and behold that vile barbarian and them that are with him, how they dare to blaspheme Thy holy and great Name! Trample him underfoot and bring him to naught, O Lord our Defender, lest He say: 'Where is their God?' For Thou art our God, Who dost resist the proud, but lookest attentively upon the humble;[^2256] for Thine is the unshakeable power and the dominion unassailable. Receive into Thine ears the words of this barbarian, who hath sent to reproach and mock Thee, Who rulest over all things; deliver the city of Thine inheritance, and the people called by Thy Name!"[^2257]

*(fol. 733)*
And thus the people prayed with weeping. And God hindered the passage of the Persians unto the Chagan which they had prepared for themselves, slaying not a few of those whom they sent one unto another. Fighting for two and three days upon the shores, attacking the settlements, and making war, they ceased not; and their work was prepared according to agreement from both sides: on land indeed they brought up artillery fit for storming and demolishing the wall; while on the sea they marshaled Scythian *monoxyla* in great numbers, so that at one time and in one hour they struck with might against the City both by land and by sea.

And while such war was being waged, the Chagan, taking as many of his cavalry as were most select, came unto the region of the mouth of the great sea, displaying himself unto the Persian soldiers; likewise also the Persian general showed himself unto him, the one from Asia and the other from Europe, roaring like wild beasts and raging against the imperial City, supposing that it was easy and ready for them to capture. But who can tell the divine wonders which came to pass at that time? Or who shall be able to express in words the loving-kindness and willing help of the Most Pure Theotokos toward us? For when the Chagan filled the gulf of the sea called the Horn [the Golden Horn][^2258] with *monoxyla*—that is, ships fashioned out of a single tree—and with other fighting men, he strove and planned to overturn the city walls by those who fought by land, and by those who were in the gulf of the Horn to have ready and suitable access unto the City.

Yet He Whom they had blasphemed, the Lord and our God, Who is everywhere and rules over all things, through the prayers of the Virgin Theotokos who bare Him, showed their hopes to be mistaken and vain; for so great a multitude of the adversaries did the Greek soldiers slay upon every wall, that the living could not bury the dead; and this defeat befell those who fought on dry land, striving to cast down the walls and throw them to the earth. And those ships called *monoxyla*, together with all the men that were in them, opposite the Church of God at Blachernae,[^2259] the Lady Theotokos suddenly submerged, having stirred up a marvelous, fearful, and violent tempest of the sea: for as soon as they drew near unto her divine church, the sea, having risen exceedingly high, was cleft by divine providence into a chasm, and straightway submerged and drowned them all, together with the very...

*(fol. 734)*
...ships; and there was truly seen there a great and unutterable marvel: for the sea raised waves equal to mountains, and raged in the likeness of a wild beast, and foaming against the enemies of God's Mother, sprang fiercely upon them and consumed them unmercifully, even as once it did unto the Egyptians who pursued after ancient Israel as they passed through on foot in a marvelous and extraordinary manner.[^2260] Thus in the first war, protecting her city without shedding of blood, the Most Pure Theotokos displayed victory by such means and leadership: those indeed who had brought unmeasured war against her inheritance, and borne weapons against them, she swiftly submerged, terminating their labor with the surges of the sea; while those who placed in her their sole trust of salvation, she preserved as her inheritance from the tribulations that fell upon them, without harm in every place.

For at that time their supreme leader, the Chagan, seeing with his own eyes the destruction of his soldiers, standing there upon a high place with his most select cavalry, beat himself with his hands upon the face and upon the breast. And they that were within the City and waged war against the enemies, when they beheld that the enemies had perished in the sea, immediately strengthened by divine power and walled around by the might of the Most Pure Virgin Theotokos, threw open the city gates, and shouting and crying out, rushed forth upon the enemies; and exceedingly great as was the joy and might among the city soldiers, so great was the fear and dread among the barbarians. And it was marvelous to behold the eminent leadership of the Lady our Theotokos, so that even small children and women went forth with great courage against the barbarians, and fell upon the very soldiers of their enemies, and wrought so great a slaughter among the barbarians as cannot be told in words. There truly was fulfilled that which is spoken: "One chased a thousand, and two put ten thousands to flight."[^2261] Such power did the Most Pure Virgin Theotokos, our Lady, grant unto the feeble, and such strength unto the weak.

And when the sun had set and night came on, all the military engines which the barbarians had brought on wheels for the taking of the City they delivered to fire to be burned, commanding their laborers to set torch to their own engines, through the bestowal of such favor upon them by the holy Theotokos. And the clergy and all the citizens, lifting up their hands unto Heaven, with tears sang thanksgiving and said: "Thy right hand, O Lord, is glorified in power; Thy right hand, O Lord...

*(fol. 735)*
...hath broken the enemies, and in the multitude of Thy glory Thou hast crushed the adversaries!"[^2262]

And thus the senseless Chagan, having come with a multitude of countless soldiers, turned back with shame; likewise also that general who had brought the Persian soldiers, having laid his hand upon his mouth and covered his face because out of so many thousands he saw but a tiny number, departed with shame unto his own territories. Thus the minister of divine providence and loving-kindness, the Most Pure and Undefiled Theotokos, the mighty Defender of Christians, showed forth her power in our defense, and granted us so great and notable a deliverance. In remembrance of which so great a beneficence we now perform this prayerful gathering of all the people, and celebrate the All-Night Festival, offering songs full of thanksgiving—which Feast the Holy Fathers named *Akathistos*, that is, "The Unseated Hymn," and decreed to be celebrated on this day unto the Mother of God, because so great a victory and defeat of the enemies came to pass through the Virgin Theotokos; and because the clergy and all the people of the City at that time enjoyed such a triumph, praising God One in Trinity, unto Whom belongs honor and glory unto ages of ages. Amen.[^2263]

*Then we stichologize: The Blameless (Kathisma 17).*[^2264]

*And again we say [or the 2nd choir sings] the Kontakion:*
*To thee, the Champion Leader: (see fol. 726). And the second set of Ikoses, 6:*[^2265]

*Ikos 4 (Zeta):* Hearing the Angels hymning the incarnate coming of Christ, and hastening as unto a Shepherd, the shepherds beheld Him as a blameless Lamb, pastured in Mary's womb; whom hymning, they said:
Rejoice, Mother of the Lamb and Shepherd!
Rejoice, Fold of rational sheep!
Rejoice, torment of invisible enemies!
Rejoice, opening of the gates of Paradise!
Rejoice, for heavenly things rejoice together with earthly things!
Rejoice, for earthly things dance together with heavenly things!
Rejoice, unceasing mouth of the Apostles!
Rejoice...

*(fol. 736)*
...unconquerable courage of the passion-bearers!
Rejoice, steadfast foundation of faith!
Rejoice, radiant knowledge of grace!
Rejoice, through whom Hades was stripped bare!
Rejoice, through whom we have been clothed with glory!
Rejoice, unwedded Bride![^2266]

*Kontakion 5 (Eta):* Beholding the God-running star, the Magi followed after its brightness; and holding it as a lantern, by it they sought the mighty King; and having reached the Unreachable, they rejoiced, crying unto Him: Alleluia![^2267]

*Ikos 5 (Theta):* The sons of the Chaldeans beheld upon the Virgin's hand Him Who with His own hands fashioned man; and knowing Him to be the Master, though He had taken the form of a servant, they hastened with gifts to serve Him, and to cry unto the Blessed One:
Rejoice, Mother of the Unwaning Star!
Rejoice, Dawn of the mystical day!
Rejoice, who hast quenched the furnace of delusion!
Rejoice, who protectest the initiates of the Trinity!
Rejoice, who castest out the inhuman tyrant from his dominion!
Rejoice, who hast shown forth the Lord Christ Who loves mankind!
Rejoice, who deliverest from barbarian worship!
Rejoice, who drawest us forth from the mire of deeds!
Rejoice, who hast quenched the worship of fire!
Rejoice, who coolist the flame of the passions!
Rejoice, Guide of the faithful unto chastity!
Rejoice, gladness of all generations!
Rejoice, unwedded Bride![^2268]

*Kontakion 6 (Iota):* Having become God-bearing heralds, the Magi returned unto Babylon, fulfilling Thy prophecy; and having preached Thee as the Christ unto all, they left Herod as a babbler, who knew not how to sing: Alleluia![^2269]

*Ikos 6 (Kappa):* Having shone forth in Egypt the illumination of truth...

*(fol. 737)*
...Thou didst drive away the darkness of falsehood; for its idols, O Savior, not enduring Thy strength, fell down; and they that were delivered from them cried unto the Theotokos:
Rejoice, restoration of men!
Rejoice, downfall of the demons!
Rejoice, who hast trampled down the dominion of delusion!
Rejoice, who hast exposed the deceit of idols!
Rejoice, Sea that drowned the spiritual Pharaoh!
Rejoice, Rock that gave drink unto them that thirst for life!
Rejoice, Pillar of Fire that guides them that are in darkness!
Rejoice, Protection of the world, wider than a cloud!
Rejoice, Nourishment, successor of the Manna!
Rejoice, Minister of holy delight!
Rejoice, Land of Promise!
Rejoice, from whom flows milk and honey!
Rejoice, unwedded Bride![^2270]

*Kontakion 7 (Lambda):* When Simeon was about to depart from this present deceitful age, Thou wast delivered unto him as an infant; yet Thou wast recognized by him also as perfect God; therefore He marveled at Thine ineffable wisdom, crying: Alleluia![^2271]

*And again the Kontakion:*
*To thee, the Champion Leader: (see fol. 726).*[^2272]

*Then we read further from the Homily of the Akathist:*
*Part Two of the first history read: that is, concerning the second wonder against the Saracens, and concerning the third wonder against the Agarites, which came to pass from God through the prayers and leadership of the Most Pure Lady our Theotokos. Bless, father, to read.*[^2273]

After that first wonder of the Most Pure Theotokos which she showed forth against the Scythian Chagan and the Persians, when thirty-six years had passed, during the reign of Constantine Pogonatus [Constantine IV], there came again a great Saracen leader with a multitude of vessels against that same imperial City, against Constantinople...

*(fol. 738)*
...I say; and immediately they put in at the shore by Cyzicus, whence assaults by sea upon the City were made every day from springtime until autumn; and they departed to winter at Cyzicus, and again in the spring returned to Constantinople and waged battle from the sea; and for seven years they fought mightily, and lost many of their ships and armored soldiers, and all the equipment which they had brought with them for necessity they squandered, and returned with great loss unto their own land.[^2274] And what is yet more marvelous: being in the regions of Syllaeum, when a fierce and violent gale struck them, by the righteous judgment of God they all perished and were drowned in the sea; and this came to pass through the intercession of God's Mother. Likewise also at diverse times when those ungodly ones returned against that God-guarded City, seeking to fulfill that mad intent of theirs, they returned empty-handed and filled with shame.

*The Third Wonder Against the Agarites:*[^2275]

Yet again that pagan people, after forty-six years, attempted to assault that City. For their might was rising everywhere into greatness, and had multiplied immensely from the east and from the west; when first they had entered the Kingdom of the Persians, and thence into Egypt and Libya, promising the Christians that they would not compel them to apostatize from the Orthodox and undefiled faith in Christ our God, they did not keep this promise, but made many into martyrs because they would not at their command trample upon the Precious Cross, which they compelled the Christians to do. And to speak briefly, when they had traversed all the earth pillaging—India, Europe, Spain, the Berber people, and Libya—finally they also deployed in arms against that very imperial City, desiring to take it into their power.[^2276]

And when Emperor Leo the Isaurian had accepted the empire by treaty, he promised to give them tribute; but they compelled them also to admit their garrison into the City; for they placed their confidence and hope in their great multitude, and also relied upon those soldiers who had been hired for pay, being in the preparation of countless provisions in their ships—for there were one thousand eight hundred ships in number, as diligent historians have written.[^2277] And when the malicious Christ-fighters had encamped their armies beneath the City, no...

Not only did they not make an assault or approach to the city walls: for they occupied themselves with building houses, thinking that they would live there as at home, and that they had already subjected the city to their will and thought; but the Lord God made their counsels and plottings void and vain. And those Christ-loving people who were in the City unceasingly celebrated the Liturgies, just as they were accustomed to do in time of peace and order. At that time, having taken the Wood of the Cross, worthy of all honor, of God our Savior Jesus Christ, and the holy Icons of the Most Pure Mother of God, they conducted processions along the city walls, and lifting up their hands to God, they cried out and said: "Arise, O Lord, help us, and do not cast away Thy people to the end; for behold, Thine enemies have raged, and those who hate Thee have lifted up their head: give not up therefore Thine inheritance unto derision, that the pagans should rule over us, lest they should ever say: 'Where is their God?' But let them know that Thy name is the Lord Jesus Christ, unto the glory of God the Father."[^2278] And when they had fervently conducted divine worship for many days, a certain one from among the opposing Saracens on horseback, uttering blasphemous words against Constantinople and calling the Church by the plain name of Sophia, in a single moment[^2279] fell with his horse and perished. Moreover, their crier[^2280], having climbed a tall tree that he might proclaim their abomination and foul prayer, fell down in like manner, and miserably and wretchedly vomited out and cast forth his runaway soul. Afterwards, those impious ones standing there held counsel and made an agreement to wage war against the Bulgarians; for they had two commanders: one of them indeed remained to besiege the imperial City, while the other went off to fight against the Bulgarians; and having joined battle with them, he was defeated and vanquished by the Bulgarians, so greatly that more than twice one hundred thousand of his soldiers fell on the field, and the remainder returned unto their own with shame and disgrace.[^2281]

Having then turned back from the Bulgarians, they moved by ships, desiring to press upon the City from the Blachernae side; but by the stretching of the iron chain from Constantinople even unto Galata they were hindered, being unable to bring their counsel and design to effect; and having sailed unto the place called Sosthenes and unto other small harbors, very many of them, from the severity of the winter and dreadful winds, split asunder and were wrecked, and a multitude of other great ships the Greeks burned with fire.[^2282] The City, on...

...the other hand, was in great distress and lack of human necessities. Likewise also the adversaries, when they had consumed everything they had, fell into so severe a deprivation and hardship from famine that they were compelled to eat and feed upon human corpses and carrion cattle, and even the filthiest abominations; and on account of such cruel misery, many of their notable and valiant men deserted and surrendered to the City.[^2283] As therefore He plunged the Egyptians pursuing Israel into the depths like a stone, and brought upon them the sea water, likewise also upon the Saracens who made war upon the City and the Christ-named People the Lord brought a similar punishment, when they were fleeing from the reigning City. For by a dark wind and a dreadful and fiery tempest, the sea surged up and boiled, destroying those thousandfold ships. For in the Aegean Sea, when very many ships were sailing, hail suddenly fell from heaven, and just as iron brought near to fire boils cold water, so also that hailstorm falling into the sea water caused it instantly to boil; and when the sea boiled from the hail fallen from heaven, it melted the pitch of the Saracen ships, and drowned and plunged them all into the deep of the sea, leaving only three ships intact to proclaim so great a defeat and to bring terror upon those who remained.[^2284] And it was a sight to behold: upon all the islands, shores, havens, and bays, that is, heaps and mounds of pagans lying dead and cast ashore. Let all such deeds therefore, according to the Psalmist, be told and proclaimed to other nations, and let all Christian lips chant the triumphal word, saying with David: *Thou, O Lord, didst crush the heads of the dragons in the water* [Ps. 73:13 LXX].[^2285] And unto that song let them add also the song of Israel sung by them at the time of their departure from Egypt: *Let us sing unto the Lord, for He is gloriously magnified* [Ex. 15:1 LXX].[^2286]

Having arrived at this place in my discourse and narrative, and contemplating the loftiness of the great wonders of God and of the Most Pure, sole Theotokos, I remain altogether struck with wonder in my voice, and find no words worthy of these deeds. For what eloquent tongue is able worthily to praise the Virgin Theotokos? Or with what noble song shall one hymn Her most sovereign grace? And with what words shall one praise the fountain of Her goodness, and in what manner shall one offer thanksgiving? Truly, it is fitting for us to render thanksgiving unto the Mother of God by deeds, since She delights in such things far more than in verbal praises; and not only She, but also Her Son: not in flutes, not in organs, nor in musical songs, nor in mere...

...rhetorical eloquence; rather, He loves a pious life and virtues, that is, as the Lord also said: unfeigned love, which is the head of the Law and the Prophets; unalterable brotherly love; unwavering mercy; virginity and steadfast purity; lawful marriage; modesty and sedate wisdom; ordered justice; lawful courage over the passions; understanding and wisdom ordered according to God; kindness that never wrongs; temperance without pride; well-reasoned humility; and moreover, a life undefiled and unblemished, good conduct, humble demeanor, a pious mind, lips speaking well, a praising tongue, a single and unmeddlesome eye, hands not rapacious, feet not swift unto evil, anger not unreasonable and not dragging down thoughts into the streams of madness, and the other attributes wherewith man, created in the image and likeness of God and united with God, is adorned as with certain precious and renowned jewels.[^2287] With such things is it fitting to render thanksgiving unto the Theotokos, since the wise also have said that thanksgiving consists in the effect of deeds, and not in words alone.[^2288] But since the infirmity of our nature, and the sluggishness and slothfulness of our mind, make us careless and sluggish toward laboring in virtues, and we touch them gently, so to speak, only with the tip of our finger; therefore, having a deficiency in deeds for the rendering of due thanksgiving, let us at least bring words of song. Having lifted up our voices therefore and elevated our mind, let us speak and cry aloud: Truly, O Sovereign Lady Theotokos, possessing kindness toward mankind by nature, Thou hast not ceased defending our race, as a Mother unto the Christian people, both child-loving and merciful; and in general Thou dost continually bestow Thy benefactions upon us, saving, covering, and preserving, delivering from perils, and freeing from misfortunes.

We in turn render thanksgiving for this, and proclaim Thy grace, concealing not Thy benefactions; we sing Thy wonders with a loud voice, we praise Thy help and deliverance, we magnify Thy providence and guardianship, we extol Thy defense; we possess Thee as a beneficent helper, we exalt Thy mercy in words; and truly calling to mind Thy great gifts and our great perils from which we have been delivered through Thee, we offer unto Thee these songs full of thanksgiving as a debt, and these, though they be not worthy of Thy benefaction, nevertheless favorably and...

*Marginal Note on the Ruthenian Translation of the Synaxaria:* This extensive history, in part on account of the difficulty of the Slavonic syntax, has been translated from the Slavonic into the Ruthenian dialect (*ру́сскїй дїале́ктъ*). There are seven such translated Synaxaria; and although it is not proper to the Slavonic liturgical register, yet for one who believes the wonders, it is in no way contrary to reason.[^2292]

...receive them as from babes and sucklings. Concerning our present assaults and tribulations that distress us, we ask Thy swift and ready help, we need Thy succor: crush the temptations and scandals being in our midst, disperse the cloud and gloom that have beset us, by which also as in a night battle we are wounded, and to speak plainly, as madmen we devour our own flesh, not considering kinship and taking no thought of blood relationship; and some dare to commit such things who have been made worthy of the same Spirit, the one Christ, the same Faith, the one Baptism, and one Church, and the same Mysteries.[^2289] Therefore we pray Thy goodness, O All-Holy Sovereign Lady, that Thy people and Thine inheritance may obtain Thy mercy and bountifulness; arise as an intercessor unto God our Savior born of Thee, that He may succor us who are perishing unto the end, and deliver us from incurable assaults. Thou seest, O Sovereign Lady, with what great tears we are flooded. Have compassion therefore, and cast us not off unto the end; turn not away Thy countenance, and forget not our poverty and our distress; disperse and drive away fear and trembling that attack us; soothe and quiet the wrath of God and destruction stirred up against us; calm and restrain the strifes and turmoil that are among us, and give quietness and peace unto Thy servants, that unto Thy many accustomed benefactions toward us we may add these also, and continually and in every place proclaim Thy wonders. Amen.[^2290]

And thus, the ship of narrative guided by me having sailed in, now also having lowered the sails of speech, let us rest in the firm haven of silence; admonishing and reminding this assembly and the governors of the city that we should not appear senseless and ungrateful for the benefactions of our Sovereign Lady Theotokos, but being adorned with Her effective good deeds, let us not be slothful to offer at least verbal thanksgiving. For in turn benefit shall return unto us: for if we are grateful for Her past benefactions toward us, we shall prepare for ourselves great security also for future things, and shall attain unspeakable goods. By the grace and loving-kindness of our Lord Jesus Christ, unto Whom belong glory, dominion, honor, and worship, with His unoriginate Father, and the All-Holy, Good, and Life-creating Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.[^2291]

*Psalm 50. We sing: "Lord, have mercy," we do not read the Psalter.*[^2293]

*Canons: To the Saint of the church temple, with the Heirmos, to 6; and to the Most Pure Theotokos of the Akathist, to 8.*[^2294]

*If it be a Temple of the Theotokos: we sing to the Saint whose day it is, that is, of the Menaion, to 4; and to the Feast of the Theotokos, with the Heirmos, to 10; the Heirmos twice, the Troparia to 8.*[^2295]

*Canon, The Composition of Kyr Joseph. Whose Acrostic is:* ***To the receptacle of joy, it is fitting for thee alone to rejoice.***[^2296] *Ode 1. Tone 4.*

*Heirmos: I shall open my mouth, and it shall be filled with the Spirit, and I shall utter a word unto the Queen Mother, and I shall be seen radiantly celebrating, and rejoicing I shall sing Her wonders.*[^2297]

*Troparion:* Beholding Thee, the animate Book, sealed by the Spirit, the great Archangel cried aloud unto Thee: Rejoice, O receptacle of joy, through whom the curse of the first mother was destroyed![^2298]

*Troparion:* The restoration of Adam, rejoice, O Virgin Bride of God: the slaying of Hades! Rejoice, O all-immaculate palace of the King of all! Rejoice, O fiery throne of the Almighty!

*Troparion:* O flower unfading, rejoice, who alone didst bud forth the sweet-smelling apple! Rejoice, who didst bear the fragrance of the only King! Rejoice, O unwedded Maiden, salvation of the world!

*Theotokion:* O treasury of purity, rejoice, through whom we rose from our fall! Rejoice, O sweet-smelling lily, O Sovereign Lady, perfuming the faithful: fragrant censer, and costly myrrh!

*Katavasia:* *I shall open my mouth, and it shall be filled with the Spirit, and I shall utter a word unto the Queen Mother, and I shall be seen radiantly celebrating, and rejoicing I shall sing Her wonders.*

*Ode 3. Heirmos: O Theotokos, living and inexhaustible fountain, spiritually establish Thine assembled hymnographers...*[^2299]

*Troparion:* Having sprouted the divine Ear of corn, as a field untilled...
