...manifestly: Rejoice, O animate Table, who didst contain the Bread of Life! Rejoice, O Sovereign Lady, inexhaustible fountain of living water![^2300]

*Troparion:* O Heifer who didst bear the unblemished Heifer, rejoice, unto the faithful! Rejoice, O Ewe who didst bear the Lamb of God Who takes away the sins of the whole world! Rejoice, O fervent mercy-seat![^2301]

*Troparion:* Most radiant dawn, rejoice, who alone bearest the Sun Christ unto us, dwelling-place of light! Rejoice, who didst destroy the darkness and utterly drive away the gloomy demons!

*Theotokion:* Rejoice, sole Portal through which the Word alone did pass: who by Thy Nativity didst shatter the bars and gates of Hades, O Sovereign Lady! Rejoice, divine entrance of the saved, O Bride of God!

*Katavasia:* *O Theotokos, living and inexhaustible fountain, spiritually establish Thine assembled hymnographers, and in Thy divine glory vouchsafe them crowns of glory.*

*Little Litany.*

*And after the Exclamation, Kontakion: "To thee, the Champion Leader" (see fol. 727)[^2302]. And we read the second six Ikoses.*[^2303]

*Ikos 7:* A new creation did the Creator display, appearing unto us who were made by Him, budding forth from a seedless womb, and keeping it incorrupt even as it was; that beholding the wonder, we might hymn Her, crying aloud: Rejoice, flower of incorruption! Rejoice, crown of temperance! Rejoice, shining forth the image of the Resurrection! Rejoice, displaying the angelic life! Rejoice, tree of goodly fruit, whereon the faithful are nourished! Rejoice, tree of fair-shading foliage, beneath which many are sheltered! Rejoice, who didst bear the Deliverer...

...of captives! Rejoice, who didst bear the Guide of the straying! Rejoice, appeasement of the righteous Judge! Rejoice, forgiveness of many transgressions! Rejoice, robe of boldness for the naked! Rejoice, love that overcomes all desire! Rejoice, O Bride unwedded![^2304]

*Kontakion 8:* Seeing a strange Nativity, let us become strangers unto the world, transferring our mind unto heaven: for for this cause the high God appeared on earth as a humble Man, wishing to draw unto the heights those who cry unto Him: Alleluia![^2305]

*Ikos 8:* Wholly was the uncircumscribed Word among those below, yet in no wise departed from those on high; for a divine descent occurred, not a change of place, and a birth from the Virgin who received God, who hears these things: Rejoice, container of the uncontainable God! Rejoice, portal of the august mystery! Rejoice, doubtful report of the unbelieving! Rejoice, undoubted boast of the faithful! Rejoice, all-holy chariot of Him Who sits upon the Cherubim! Rejoice, most glorious habitation of Him Who is upon the Seraphim! Rejoice, who didst unite opposites in the same! Rejoice, who didst weave together virginity and childbirth! Rejoice, through whom transgression was dissolved! Rejoice, through whom Paradise was opened! Rejoice, Key to the Kingdom of Christ! Rejoice, hope of eternal good things! Rejoice, O Bride unwedded![^2306]

*Kontakion 9:* All angelic nature was amazed at the great work of Thine Incarnation; for they beheld Him Who as God is unapproachable, as a Man approachable unto all, abiding with us, and hearing from all: Alleluia![^2307]

*Ikos 9:* Eloquent orators do we behold mute as fishes before Thee, O Theotokos: for they are at a loss to say how Thou remainest a Virgin and wast able to give birth. But we, marveling at the mystery, cry out with faith: Rejoice, receptacle of the Wisdom of God! Rejoice, treasury of His providence! Rejoice, who provest philosophers foolish! Rejoice, who convictest craftsmen of words of speechlessness! Rejoice, for subtle questioners are made foolish! Rejoice, for myth-makers have withered away! Rejoice, who tearest apart the tangled webs of the Athenians! Rejoice, who fillest the nets of the Fishermen! Rejoice, who drawest up from the abyss of ignorance! Rejoice, who illuminest many in knowledge! Rejoice, bark of those who wish to be saved! Rejoice, haven of the voyages of life! Rejoice, O Bride unwedded![^2308]

*Kontakion 10:* Desiring to save the world, the Adorner of all came unto this by His own promise; and being our Shepherd as God, for our sake He appeared as a Man like unto us; for having called like by like as God, He hears from all: Alleluia![^2309]

*And again the Kontakion: "To thee, the Champion Leader" (see fol. 727)[^2310].*

*If we sing the Menaion, read its Kontakion and Ikos, and its Gospel(?); Glory... Both now... Kontakion of the Feast. But if we do not sing in the Menaion, then:*[^2311]

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "While the soldiers were guarding Thy tomb" (Гро́бъ тво́й):*[^2312] The great warrior of the immaterial Angels, having appeared in the city of Nazareth, announces the King, Thy Son, O pure Lady, and Lord of ages, saying unto Thee: Rejoice, blessed Mary, unsearchable and ineffable depth, salvation of mankind!

*Glory... Kontakion. Both now... Sessional Hymn. And again a reading, if it be early.*[^2313]

*Ode 4. Heirmos: Seated in glory...*[^2314]

*Troparion:* ... In voices of song, O Virgin, we cry unto Thee, O all-hymned Lady: Rejoice, fertile Mountain, curdled by the Spirit! Rejoice, lampstand, and jar bearing the Manna, which sweetens the senses of all the pious![^2315]

*Troparion:* Mercy-seat for the world, rejoice, O Most Pure Sovereign Lady! Rejoice, Ladder that by grace didst raise all from earth! Rejoice, Bridge truly leading all who sing of Thee from death unto life![^2316]

*Troparion:* Higher than the heavens, rejoice, who without labor didst bear in Thy womb the Foundation of the earth, O Most Pure! Rejoice, scarlet dye who didst dip the divine purple robe for the King of hosts from Thine own blood![^2317]

*Troparion:* Rejoice, O Sovereign Lady, who didst bear the true Lawgiver, Who freely purges the iniquities of all: unfathomable depth, ineffable height, unwedded Maiden, through whom we have been deified![^2318]

*Theotokion:* We hymn Thee who didst weave an unhandwoven crown for the world, crying unto Thee: Rejoice, O Virgin! Treasury and hedge of all, and confirmation, and sacred refuge!

*Katavasia:* *Seated in glory upon the throne of the Godhead, upon a light cloud, Jesus the most divine came from the Most Pure Virgin, and saved those who cry: Glory to Thy power, O Christ!*

*Ode 5. Heirmos: All things were amazed at Thy divine glory: for Thou, O unwedded Virgin, didst hold in Thy womb the God Who is over all, and didst bear the timeless Son, Who grants peace unto all who hymn Thee.*[^2319]

*Troparion:* Rejoice, O all-immaculate Maiden, who didst bear the Way of life, who didst save the world from the flood of sin! Rejoice, Bride of God, hearing and report fearful! Rejoice, habitation of the Master of creation![^2320]

*Troparion:* Strength and confirmation of men, rejoice...

...O Sovereign Lady: place of sanctification of glory, slaying of Hades, all-radiant bridal chamber! Rejoice, joy of the Angels! Rejoice, helper of those who pray unto Thee with faith![^2321]

*Troparion:* Fiery chariot of the Word, rejoice, O Sovereign Lady, animate Paradise: having in Thy midst the Tree of Life, the Lord, Whose sweetness gives life unto those who partake with faith, even though they had bowed down unto corruption![^2322]

*Troparion:* Strengthened by Thy power, with faith we cry unto Thee: Rejoice, city of the King of all, concerning which things most glorious and worthy to be heard were clearly spoken, Mountain unhewn! Rejoice, abyss immeasurable![^2323]

*Theotokion:* Spacious habitation of the Word, rejoice, O Most Pure Lady: vessel that didst bring forth the divine Pearl! Rejoice, all-praised reconciliation unto God of all who ever bless Thee, O Theotokos![^2324]

*Katavasia:* *All things were amazed at Thy divine glory: for Thou, O unwedded Virgin, didst hold in Thy womb the God Who is over all, and didst bear the timeless Son, Who grants peace unto all who hymn Thee.*

*Here ceases the Canon to the Saint whose Temple it is (see fol. 713)[^2325].*

*Ode 6. Heirmos: Celebrating this divine and august feast of the Mother of God, come, O divinely wise, let us clap our hands, glorifying God Who was born of Her.*[^2326]

*Troparion:* Undefiled bridal chamber of the Word, cause of the deification of all: rejoice, O all-immaculate Lady, preaching of the Prophets! Rejoice, ornament of the Apostles![^2327]

*Troparion:* From Thee the Dew dripped down, extinguishing the flame of polytheism. Therefore we cry unto Thee: Rejoice, O animate Fleece, which Gideon foresaw, O Virgin![^2328]

*Troparion:* Behold, we cry: Rejoice! unto Thee, O Virgin: be Thou a haven and calm shelter unto us who are tossed upon the sea, in the abyss of tribulations and all the scandals of the adversary![^2329]

*Troparion:* O cause of joy, grant grace unto our thoughts to cry unto Thee: Rejoice, unburnt Bush! Rejoice, all-radiant Cloud that continually overshadows the faithful![^2330]

*Then the Four-Ode Canon, whose acrostic is: "This song is of Joseph."[^2331] Ode 6, Tone 6.*
*Heirmos: Beholding the sea of life surging with the tempest of temptations, and fleeing unto Thy calm haven, I cry unto Thee: Lead up my life from corruption, O Most Merciful One!*[^2332]

*Troparion:* Having been wounded, O holy Martyrs, and rolling upon the ground like chosen stones, you utterly overturned every edifice of the enemy, and showed yourselves to be temples of the Living God![^2333]

*Troparion:* We beseech you, O holy Martyrs, who have finished the good course: strengthen us to run well the course of the Fast, having shone forth through the perfection of virtues![^2334]

*Troparion:* O Master, make Thy servants, who have passed away from earth unto Thee, the All-Good, partakers of Thy Kingdom, through the sacred intercessions of Thy divine martyrs, O Plenteous in mercy![^2335]

*Theotokion:* O only All-Hymned Lady, pray Thou unto the Good Word, that unto those who hymn Thee with faith there may be granted the remission of transgressions and a portion of divine gifts![^2336]

*Another Heirmos, Tone 5. From the sea-monster:*[^2337]

*Troparion:* Celebrating the memory of the Martyrs, O Lord, we offer up songs, rejoicing divinely this day![^2338]

*Troparion:* Fearing neither swords nor fire, being courageous in faith, O passion-bearers, in this you wounded the tormentor![^2339]

*Triadikon:* The choirs hymn Thee, O Trinity; the monads worship Thee according to essence: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit![^2340]

*Theotokion:* Thou art the praise of Angels and men, for Thou didst bear...

...Christ, the Savior of our souls, O Virgin![^2341]

*Verse: God is marvelous in His saints, the God of Israel.*[^2342]
*Troparion:* Having exchanged life for death, you rejoice, dwelling in the heavens, O most glorious passion-bearers of Christ God![^2343]

*Verse: Their soul shall dwell among good things.*[^2344]
*Troparion:* O Christ, Who rulest over death and life, with Thy saints grant rest unto those who with faith have passed away from this life![^2345]

*Katavasia:* *From the sea-monster Thou didst deliver the Prophet, and from the deep of transgressions lead me up, O Lord, and save me!*[^2346]

*And again we sing the Kontakion: "To Thee, the Champion Leader..." (see fol. 427)[^2347].*
*And we read the remaining six Ikoi.*

*Ikos 10.*
A wall art Thou unto virgins, O Theotokos Virgin, and unto all who run unto Thee; for the Creator of heaven and earth fashioned Thee, O Most Pure One, dwelling in Thy womb, and teaching all to address Thee:
Rejoice, pillar of virginity!
Rejoice, gate of salvation!
Rejoice, source of spiritual rebuilding!
Rejoice, bestower of divine goodness!
Rejoice, for Thou didst renew those shamefully conceived!
Rejoice, for Thou didst admonish those despoiled in mind!
Rejoice, who didst nullify the corrupter of minds!
Rejoice, who didst bring forth the Sower of purity!
Rejoice, bridal chamber of seedless betrothal!
Rejoice, who didst unite the faithful unto the Lord!
Rejoice, good nursing-mother of virgins!
Rejoice, bridal chamber of holy souls!
Rejoice, O Bride unwedded![^2348]

*Kontakion 11.*
Every hymn is overcome that strives to expand itself unto the multitude of Thy many compassions...

...for if we offer unto Thee, O Holy King, psalms and songs equal in number unto the sand, we accomplish nothing worthy of what Thou hast given unto us who cry unto Thee: Alleluia![^2349]

*Ikos 11.*
As a light-receiving beacon, appearing unto those in darkness, do we behold the Holy Virgin; for kindling the immaterial Fire, She guides all unto divine knowledge, illuminating the mind with radiance, and honored with these invocations:
Rejoice, ray of the spiritual Sun!
Rejoice, luminary of unwaning brilliance!
Rejoice, lightning that illuminates souls!
Rejoice, who, as thunder, terrifies the enemies!
Rejoice, for Thou makest radiant enlightenment to shine forth!
Rejoice, for Thou pourest out a river of abundant waters!
Rejoice, who depictest the image of the font!
Rejoice, who takest away the defilement of sin!
Rejoice, bath that washes the conscience!
Rejoice, chalice that draws up joy!
Rejoice, fragrance of Christ's sweet odor!
Rejoice, life of mystical gladness!
Rejoice, O Bride unwedded![^2350]

*Kontakion 12.*
Wishing to grant grace for ancient debts, the Reliever of all human debts came of His own accord unto those who had departed from His grace, and having torn up the handwriting of debt, He hears from all: Alleluia![^2351]

*Ikos 12.*
Hymning Thy childbearing, we all praise Thee as an animate temple, O Theotokos; for the Lord Who holds all things in His hand, having dwelt in Thy womb, sanctified and glorified Thee, and taught all to cry unto Thee:
Rejoice, tabernacle of God and the Word!
Rejoice, holy one, greater than the holies!...

...Rejoice, ark gilded by the Spirit!
Rejoice, inexhaustible treasury of life!
Rejoice, precious crown of pious kings!
Rejoice, venerable boast of reverent priests!
Rejoice, unshakable pillar of the Church!
Rejoice, indestructible wall of the Kingdom!
Rejoice, through whom trophies are raised up!
Rejoice, through whom enemies fall down!
Rejoice, healing of my body!
Rejoice, protection of my soul!
Rejoice, O Bride unwedded![^2352]

*Kontakion 13.*
*This Kontakion is said thrice, with a metania at each:*[^2353]
O All-Hymned Mother, who didst bear the Word, the most Holy of all the saints: having accepted our present offering, deliver all from every affliction, and rescue from the torment to come those who cry unto Thee: Alleluia!

*And again the first Ikos is read: "An Archangel was sent..." (see fol. 427)[^2354].*
*And again the Kontakion: "To Thee, the Champion Leader..." (ibid.).*
*Then the Synaxarion is read: first from the Menaion, then the present one.*[^2355]

*Verses:*[^2356]
*With sleepless hymns gratefully,*
*The City sings to its watchful Defender in battles.*

*Synaxarion on Saturday of the Akathist.*
On this day we celebrate the Akathist [Unseated] Hymn unto our Most Holy Lady the Theotokos, for the following reason:[^2357]
When the Emperor Heraclius held the Roman [Byzantine] Empire, the Persian King Chosroes [Khosrow II], seeing the Romans sorely humbled and oppressed by the tyrant Emperor Phocas, sent one of his chief commanders named Sarbaros [Shahrbaraz], with very many thousands, that they might subjugate the entire Eastern realm unto him and bring it into subjection. For it had come to pass even earlier that Chosroes destroyed up to ten millions [myriads] of Christians, when the Jews bought them from him and put them to death. The archisatrap therefore, that is, the chief general Sarbaros, having subjugated the Eastern realm and ravaged it entirely, arrived even unto Chrysopolis itself, that is...

...the Golden City, which is now called Scutarion [Üsküdar].[^2358] The Emperor Heraclius, however, finding himself lacking in common civic funds, having melted down the sacred church vessels into coinage, under a promise to return them more abundantly and perfectly, passed across the Euxine Sea [Black Sea] into the lands of Persia, and there spent that coinage; and Chosroes, with all his army, was mightily struck down and vanquished by him. Shortly thereafter, Siroes [Kavad II], the son of Chosroes, having rebelled against his father, seized and held the realm for himself, and having killed his father Chosroes, concluded a peace with the Emperor Heraclius. The Chagan, however, the ruler [Hetman] of the Mysians and Scythians [Avars], having received word that the Emperor had crossed the sea into Persia, broke the peace with the Greeks; and bringing innumerable hordes of warriors in their myriads, led them from two sides against Constantinople, uttering blasphemous shouts against God. Immediately therefore the sea was indeed full of vessels, and the land was full of unnumbered foot-soldiers and horsemen. The Patriarch Sergius, however, strongly exhorted the people of Constantinople not to lose heart, but with all their soul to place all their hope in God and in His Mother, the All-Holy Theotokos. Moreover, the Patrician Bonus, who at that time governed the City, prepared everything necessary for repelling the enemy. For together with the help that comes from on high, it is needful that we also manage our own responsibilities. And the Patriarch, with the divine icons of the Mother of God, together with the whole assembly of the multitude of the people, processed along the wall from on high, imparting unto it strength and firm defence from thence. When therefore Sarbaros from the east and the Chagan from the west began to burn the suburbs of the city, the Patriarch, bearing the Icon of Christ Not-Made-by-Hands, and the precious, worthy Wood of the Life-giving Cross, and also the venerable Robe of the Mother of God, made a procession along the walls.[^2359] And the Scythian Chagan came up to Constantinople past the Charisian walls, with an innumerable host powerfully armed with weapons, and so exceedingly numerous that for every single Greek ten Scythians could be seen. Yet the invincible Warrior Maiden, through a very few soldiers who were found in Her church named Pege [the Spring], slew very many of them. And thenceforth the Greeks, emboldened and rejoiced under their invincible Commander, the Mother of God, continually and mightily struck them down. And the citizens who sought peace were turned away; for the Chagan declared: "Deceive not yourselves in the God in Whom you believe, for tomorrow without fail I will take your city."[^2360] And the citizens...

...having heard this, lifted up their hands unto God. The Chagan and Sarbaros, therefore, having taken counsel and joined together, approached by land and by sea, intending through siege-engines and archery to take the city by storm. Yet they were so sorely vanquished by the Greeks that the living were not sufficient to bury the dead; and when the monoxyla [single-log boats] full of armed warriors, directed through the gulf called Kerato [the Horn] toward the Church of the Mother of God which is in Blachernae, were struck suddenly upon the sea by a storm and violent gale, they were broken and smashed into many pieces, and together with all the ships of the enemies sank and perished.[^2361] And it was a thing to behold and marvel at the marvelous deed of the Most Pure Theotokos, for She drowned them all near the seashore which is at Blachernae. And the people, as soon as the gates and city portals were opened, slew them all utterly; even small children and women stood up bravely and valiantly against them, while their idols and commanders returned weeping and lamenting. And the God-loving people of the city of Constantinople, rendering thanksgiving unto the Mother of God, performed an All-night Vigil and chanted the Akathist [Unseated] Hymn unto Her, as unto Her who had not slept on their behalf, and who by supernatural power had wrought and shown forth the triumph of victory.[^2362] From that time therefore, in remembrance of so great and supernatural a miracle, the Church received the tradition to celebrate this Feast unto the Mother of God at this season, when the victory and triumph were accomplished for Her. And they called it Akathist [Unseated] because both the church clergy and the populace of the city performed these songs full of thanksgiving unto the Most Pure Theotokos not sitting, but standing.

And when thirty-six years had passed thereafter, during the reign of Constantine Pogonatus—that is, the Bearded—the Agarenes [Saracens], having brought an unnumbered army, came again against Constantinople, and waged war against it for seven years; and having wintered in the regions of Cyzicus, they lost many of their men; and in short, not returning with their entire army, and having arrived at Syllaeum, they all sank in the sea, through the succour and help of the Most Pure Mother of God.[^2363]

Yet a third time also, under Leo the Isaurian, the descendants of Hagar, in numbers of a hundred thousand and more, first ravaged the Persian Empire, and then Egypt and Libya; and having invaded also the Indians, Ethiopians, and Spaniards, they attacked even the Imperial City itself with an army, having brought one thousand eight hundred boats.[^2364] Having encircled the city, when they persisted in storming it relentlessly, the noble people of the capital city, bearing the precious and worthy Wood...

...of the precious and Life-giving Cross, and the venerable Icon of the Mother of God the Hodegetria, went round the walls, with tears beseeching God to be merciful. The Agarenes therefore divided into two parts: some raised war against the Bulgarians, and there fell more than two millions [tens of thousands], while the others remained to take the city. And being barred by the iron chain that was stretched from Galata unto the very city wall, they were driven unto the place named Sosthenion; and there, when a severe north wind blew, all their boats filled with armed men were broken to pieces and sank. And those who remained were struck by famine and severe pestilence, falling so grievously that they even touched human flesh and fell into cannibalism; and afterwards, when fleeing and sailing unto the Aegean Sea, they consigned all their boats and themselves unto the depths of the sea and sank; for a severe and violent hailstorm fell from heaven, and causing intense heat upon the sea, melted the pitch of the ships; and so that great and truly unnumbered army perished with all their vessels, so that only three remained to report so fearful a disaster.[^2365]

For all these supernatural miracles of the Most Pure Theotokos, therefore, do we observe and celebrate the present Feast. And it is called Akathist—that is, Unseated—because at that time all the people, standing upright throughout that night, sang the song unto the Mother of God; and whereas on all other Ikoi it is customary to sit, on the present Ikoi of the Mother of God we listen standing upright and straight.[^2366]

By the prayers of Thine all-valiant and unconquered Mother, O Christ God, deliver us also from the tribulations and calamities that encompass us, and have mercy upon us, for Thou alone art compassionate; and unto Thee is due glory and honor, with Thine unoriginate Father, and Thine All-Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.[^2367]

*The Eighth Ode is chanted. For the rest (see fol. 413)[^2368].*

*Ode 7. Heirmos: The godly-minded youths worshipped not the creature rather than the Creator, but trampling the threat of fire underfoot, they rejoiced, singing: Blessed art Thou, O all-hymned Lord God of our fathers!*[^2369]

*Troparion:* We hymn Thee, crying aloud: Rejoice, chariot of the spiritual Sun! Rejoice, true Vine that didst cultivate the ripe cluster, which pours forth wine that makes glad the souls of those who glorify Thee with faith![^2370]

*Troparion:* Rejoice, O Bride of God, who didst bear the Physician of all men; mystical rod that didst blossom with the unfading Flower...

...Rejoice, O Sovereign Lady, through whom we are filled with joy and inherit life![^2371]

*Troparion:* No eloquent tongue can hymn Thee worthily, O Sovereign Lady; for Thou wast exalted above the Seraphim, having borne Christ the King. Beseech Him to deliver this city from many temptations![^2372]

*Troparion:* The ends of the earth praise Thee, blessing Thee, and with love cry unto Thee: Rejoice, Scroll wherein the Word was written by the Father's finger, O Pure One! Pray Thou unto Him, O Theotokos, that Thy servants may be written in the Books of Life![^2373]

*Troparion:* We Thy servants pray, and bend the knees of our hearts: incline Thine ear, O Pure One, and save those who are ever engulfed by afflictions, and preserve Thy City, O Theotokos, from all enemy captivity![^2374]

*Another Heirmos, Tone 6. Unto the Lord:*[^2375]

*Troparion:* The all-radiant choir of Thy divine martyrs, O Plenteous in mercy, dwells in Thy never-setting light; by their prayers, O Christ, grant unto all enlightenment and cleansing of sins![^2376]

*Troparion:* How fair is the time of abstinence which Thou hast granted unto us, O Lord! In it have compassion upon our souls, as Thou art good, by the prayers of the holy passion-bearers, who loved Thy fair and precious sufferings![^2377]

*Troparion:* Direct Thy servants, who have passed through the much-afflicted storm of life, into the haven of life, O Master, that with all the chosen they may cry: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers![^2378]

*Theotokion:* Pray Thou, O Ever-Virgin...

...who didst bear the Lawgiver, that all lawlessness may be dried up in this present time, for those who have well chosen to maintain the diligence of the divine Fast![^2379]

*Another Heirmos, Tone 5. Blessed art Thou, O God:*[^2380]

*Troparion:* Blessed art Thou, O God, Who hast shown forth the noble martyrs who suffered for Thy sake, all-hymned and glorified above all![^2381]

*Troparion:* Blessed art Thou, O God, Who grantest unto us the passion-bearers as intercessors unto Thee, all-hymned and glorified above all![^2382]

*Triadikon:* Blessed art Thou, O God, One indeed in essence, but known in three Persons, all-hymned and glorified above all![^2383]

*Theotokion:* Blessed art Thou, O God, Who hast shown Her that bore Thee seedlessly to be most pure in virginity, all-hymned and glorified above all![^2384]

*Verse: Unto the saints that are in His earth, the Lord hath made marvelous all His will in them.*[^2385]
*Troparion:* Blessed art Thou, O God, Who didst tame the wild beasts and extinguish the fire, unto the glory of Thy saints, all-hymned and glorified above all![^2386]

*Verse: Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen and taken to Thyself.*[^2387]
*Troparion:* Blessed art Thou, O God, Who hast translated from death unto endless life those who in this life served Thee with faith, all-hymned and glorified above all![^2388]

*Katavasia:* *Blessed art Thou, O God, Who beholdest the depths, Who sittest upon the Cherubim, all-hymned and glorified above all!*[^2389]

*Ode 8. Heirmos: The Offspring of the Theotokos saved the godly youths in the furnace; what was then figured forth is now accomplished, and it moves the whole universe to sing: Praise the Lord, all ye works, and exalt Him above all unto all ages!*[^2390]

*Troparion:* Thou didst receive the Word into Thy womb; Thou didst carry Him Who carries all things; Thou didst feed with milk Him Who by His will feeds the whole universe, O Pure Lady! Unto Him do we sing: Praise the Lord, all ye works, and exalt Him above all unto all ages![^2391]

*Troparion:* Moses understood in the Bush the great mystery of Thy childbearing; and the Children clearly prefigured this...

...standing in the midst of fire and not being consumed, O uncorrupt, Holy Virgin! Therefore do we honor Thee unto all ages![^2392]

*Troparion:* We who formerly were stripped bare by deceit have been clothed in a robe of incorruption through Thy childbearing; and we who sat in the darkness of transgressions have seen the Light, O Maiden, habitation of Light! Therefore do we hymn Thee unto all ages![^2393]

*Troparion:* Through Thee the dead are brought to life, for Thou didst bear Personal Life; they who were previously speechless now speak well; lepers are cleansed, diseases are driven away, the multitudes of the spirits of the air are conquered, O Virgin, salvation of men![^2394]

*Troparion:* O Thou who didst bear the Salvation of the world, through whom we were lifted up from earth unto the heights: Rejoice, all-blessed one, protection and dominion, wall and confirmation of those who sing, O Pure One: Praise the Lord, all ye works, and exalt Him above all unto all ages![^2395]

*Another Heirmos, Tone 6. Out of the flame for the saints:*[^2396]

*Troparion:* The heavenly minds were astonished at the noble deeds of the holy Martyrs; by their prayers, O Master, richly show forth the wonder of Thy mercy upon us, O Compassionate One![^2397]

*Troparion:* Ye who by divine dew trampled down the fire, O truly marvelous sufferers of the Lord, deliver us from the tormenting fire, through your fervent prayers unto the Theotokos![^2398]

*Troparion:* O All-Good Word, vouchsafe the life which is in the heavens and the brightness of the saints unto those who have departed from us in the Orthodox faith, by the prayers of the victor-martyrs![^2399]

*Theotokion:* By the prayers of Her that bore Thee, O Compassionate One, and of the holy Martyrs and Thine Apostles, enlighten our souls, that we may glorify Thee in spiritual gladness unto ages![^2400]

*Another Heirmos, Tone 6. The Creator of creation:*[^2401]

*Troparion:* O holy choirs of Martyrs, remember in love those who praise you, and who supremely exalt Christ unto the ages![^2402]

*Troparion:* Being cut down by the sword, the Martyrs rejoiced, praising Christ and supremely exalting Him unto all ages![^2403]

*Verse: Let us bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, the Lord.*[^2404]
*Triadikon:* Strangely and wondrously the Trinity is divided, and remains undivided as God; supremely exalt Her unto all ages![^2405]

*Theotokion:* The young Virgin brought forth, for God was incarnate of Her; let all creation praise Him unto the ages![^2406]

*Verse: God is marvelous in His saints, the God of Israel.*[^2407]
*Troparion:* Pillars of fortitude were the Martyrs shown to be, rejoicing at the downfall of the devil, praising Christ and supremely exalting Him unto the ages![^2408]

*Verse: Their soul shall dwell among good things.*[^2409]
*Troparion:* In the bosom of Abraham, vouchsafe Thy servants to abide, O Lord, who have passed away unto Thee in faith and hope![^2410]

*Verse: We praise, bless, and worship the Lord, singing:*[^2411]
*Katavasia:* *The Creator of creation, before Whom the Angels tremble, praise, O ye peoples, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!*[^2412]

*Ode 9. Heirmos: Let every earthborn mortal leap for joy in spirit, bearing his torch; and let the nature of the bodiless minds celebrate with honor the sacred festival of the Mother of God, and cry aloud: Rejoice, all-blessed Theotokos, pure Ever-Virgin!*[^2413]

*Troparion:* That we the faithful may cry unto thee: "Rejoice!", having through thee become partakers of everlasting joy: deliver us from the assaults of barbarian captivity, and from every other plague, O Maiden, which comes upon sinful men on account of the multitude of transgressions![^2414]

*Troparion:* Thou hast appeared as our enlightenment and confirmation; therefore do we cry unto thee: Rejoice, never-setting Star, introducing the great Sun into the world! Rejoice, O Pure One, who didst open closed Eden! Rejoice, Vessel that received the inexhaustible myrrh poured out upon thee![^2415]

*Troparion:* Let us stand reverently in the House of our God, and let us cry aloud: Rejoice, Sovereign Lady of the world! Rejoice, Mary, Mistress of us all! Rejoice, only undefiled and fair among women! Rejoice, fiery Pillar, leading mankind into the life on high![^2416]

*Troparion:* O Dove who didst bring forth the Merciful One, rejoice, Ever-Virgin! Rejoice, Boast of all the venerable, and Crowning of the sufferers! Rejoice, divine Adornment of all the righteous, and Salvation of us the faithful![^2417]

*Troparion:* Spare Thy heritage, O God, overlooking all our sins now, having Her to intercede with Thee Who on earth bore Thee without seed, O Christ, Who because of Thy great mercy didst desire to take human form![^2418]

*Another Heirmos, Tone 6. It is not possible for man to see God:*[^2419]

*Troparion:* Having shone forth like light and like the sun, the Martyrs enlightened all the earth with the rays of piety and with the beacons of wonders, and dispersed the darkness of polytheism; by their prayers, O our God, have mercy upon us![^2420]

*Troparion:* O invincible host of martyrs, strengthen us all to struggle well and to complete the stadium of the Fast, that having accomplished the work of divine life, we may be partakers of life, dwelling therein![^2421]

*Troparion:* Let Thy grace anticipate, O Lord, those who have departed from us by Thy awesome command; let Thy mercy encompass them, and guide them unto the enlightened habitations by the light of Thy countenance![^2422]

*Theotokion:* By the voice of the Angel, O Theotokos, thou didst ineffably bear the Angel of the Father's Counsel. Receive therefore the voices of thy servants...

...which we offer in this time of the Fast, and present them unto God as incense![^2423]

*Another Heirmos, Tone 5. Rejoice, O Isaiah:*[^2424]

*Troparion:* Celebrating the feast of the Martyrs, today, O ye people, let us cry aloud in songs, praising Christ the Bestower of the contest, Who granted them victory over their enemies, Whom in hymns we magnify![^2425]

*Troparion:* Torn by iron claws and severed limb by limb by swords, you appeared well-pleasing unto Christ, O all-praised Martyrs; therefore, now dwelling in the heavens, pray for us all![^2426]

*Triadikon:* One in essence do we hymn Thee, O beginningless Trinity, honored, life-originating, indivisible Unity: unbegotten Father, and begotten Word and Son, and Holy Spirit; save us who hymn Thee![^2427]

*Theotokion:* Beyond understanding is thy childbearing, O Mother of God, for without a man was the conception in thee, and virginal was the birth, for He that was born is God; Whom magnifying, we call thee blessed, O Virgin![^2428]

*Verse: Unto the saints that are in His earth, the Lord hath made marvelous all His will in them.*[^2429]
*Troparion:* The valiant army of the King of all and God, the martyrs, let us crown with songs, O ye people; for they visibly conquered the demonic hosts, and praising them, we magnify the Master![^2430]

*Verse: Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen and taken to Thyself, O Lord.*[^2431]
*Troparion:* When Thou shalt raise up all Thy creation to be judged, O Christ, have mercy on Thy faithful servants whom Thou hast received, forgive them their transgressions committed in this life, and give them rest with Thy saints unto the ages![^2432]

*Katavasia:* *Rejoice, O Isaiah! The Virgin was with child, and brought forth a Son, Emmanuel, God and man, Dayspring is His name; Whom magnifying, we call thee blessed, O Virgin!*[^2433]

*Exapostilarion, Tone 2, Podoben: "Give ear, ye women" (Жены оуслышите):* The mystery which was from the ages is made known today: God the Word, the Son of the Virgin Mary, out of compassion becomes man, and Gabriel announces the joy of the Annunciation. With him let us all cry aloud: Rejoice, O Mother of the Lord![^2434]

*At the Praises: Let every breath. We set 4 stichera, and we sing Stichera, Tone 4, Podoben: "As one noble among the martyrs" (Я́кѡ до́бля):*[^2435]

*Sticheron 1:* The hidden mystery and unknown unto Angels, Gabriel the Archangel confirms; and he comes now unto thee, the only incorrupt and fair Dove, the recall of our race, and he cries unto thee, O Most Pure One: Rejoice! Prepare thyself through the word to receive God the Word in thy womb![^2436]

*Sticheron 2:* A light-bearing bridal chamber is prepared for Thee, O Master: the pure womb of the Maiden of God; come unto her and descend, have compassion upon Thy creation, which out of envy received warfare, was held in the servitude of the deceiver, lost its former beauty, and awaits Thy saving descent![^2437]

*Sticheron 3:* Gabriel the Archangel visibly comes unto thee, O All-Undefiled One, and cries unto thee: Rejoice, release from the curse, restoration of the fallen! Rejoice, thou who alone wast chosen for God! Rejoice, Chariot of the Sun of Glory: receive the Bodiless One Who desires to dwell in thy womb![^2438]

*Repeat the 1st [sticheron].*[^2439]

*Glory... Both now... Idiomelon, Tone 4:*
A tongue which she knew not did the Theotokos hear, for the Archangel spoke unto her the words of the Annunciation. Whence, having received the salutation in faith, she conceived Thee, the Pre-eternal...

...God. Therefore we also rejoicing cry unto Thee: O God Who wast unchangeably incarnate of Her, grant peace unto the world, and great mercy unto our souls![^2440]

*Great Doxology.*
*Troparion of the Feast. Litany, and Dismissal, and the First Hour.*
*At the First Hour, Troparion and Kontakion of the Feast.*

*At the Liturgy:*
*The Beatitudes, from the Canon of the Akathist, Ode 3 and Ode 6, and of the Four-Ode Canon.*[^2441]

*Prokeimenon, Tone 3. Song of the Theotokos: My soul doth magnify the Lord, and my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Savior.*[^2442]
*Verse: For He hath regarded the low estate of His handmaiden.*[^2443]

*Epistle: One for the day, to the Hebrews, Pericope 322: "Brethren, Christ having come..." (Heb. 9:11-14). Another, for the Theotokos, to the Hebrews, Pericope 320: "Brethren, the first tabernacle had..." (Heb. 9:1-7).*[^2444]

*Alleluia, Tone 8: Give ear, O daughter, and see, and incline thine ear.*[^2445]
*Verse: The rich among the people shall entreat thy countenance.*[^2446]

*Gospel: For the day, from Mark, Pericope 35: "At that time, Jesus went out and His disciples..." (Mark 8:27-31). Another, for the Theotokos, from Luke, Pericope 54: "At that time, Jesus entered into a certain village..." (Luke 10:38-42; 11:27-28). According to others, Pericope 4: "At that time, Mary arose..." (Luke 1:39-49, 56).*[^2447]

*Communion Verse: I will take the cup of salvation, and call upon the name of the Lord. Alleluia.*[^2448]

*At the Trapeza: We eat two cooked dishes with oil, and we drink wine, giving thanks unto our all-hymned Sovereign Lady, the Theotokos, for the miracle that was wrought by Her.*[^2449]

*Know: If we sing the service of the Venerable Mary on this Sunday, then the service of the saint of the day in the Menaion is sung at Compline, or when the ecclesiarch wills.*[^2450]

*If the Apodosis of the Annunciation, which is also the Synaxis of the Archangel Gabriel, falls on the 5th Sunday of the Fast, see Chapter 84 of Mark, on the page which is folio 125 (see fol. 125)[^2451], above, on the Fourth Sunday of the Holy Great Fast.*

[Woodcut Illustration: Five-panel woodcut engraving of the Life of the Venerable Mary of Egypt. Center panel: The Venerable Mother Mary standing in prayer in the wilderness, naked, covered by her long hair, inscribed: "Ven. Mary of Egypt" (Пр: бнаа Марїа На Єгипетъ), with the date inscribed at the base: "1639". Four surrounding narrative panels: 1) Upper left: "Ven. Zosimas finds her" (Пр: zосїѡ[б]рѣпостяж); 2) Upper right: "Ven. Zosimas communicates Mary" (Пр: zосї причати марю); 3) Lower left: "Ven. Mary stands in prayer" (П: Марїа ста на мод[литву]), elevated above the earth; 4) Lower right: "Ven. Zosimas with the lion buries Mary" (Пр: zосї со лво[мъ] погреб[аетъ] м[арїю]).][^2452]

## FIFTH SUNDAY OF THE HOLY FAST

*Wherein we sing the service as was ordered also in the other past Sundays.*[^2453]

*We sing also the Menaion of the occurring saint.*

*Other later [fathers] handed down to sing on this Sunday the Order of:*
*OUR VENERABLE MOTHER MARY OF EGYPT.*[^2454]

*On Saturday Evening, after the customary stichology, at "Lord, I have cried," we set 10 stichera: in the Octoechos, 3 Resurrectional, and 3 Eastern [Anatolian]; and 4 for the Saint.*[^2455]

*Tone 6, Podoben: "Having laid aside all earthly hope" (Всѐ ѿло́жше):*

*Sticheron 1:* The corruption of defilements previously contracted hindered thee indeed from the contemplation of the precious [Cross]; but thy perception and thy God-wise conscience concerning the things thou hadst committed wrought in thee a turning unto better things...

...for having looked upon the icon of the blessed Maiden of God, having repented of all thy former sins, O All-Praised One, in boldness thou didst venerate the precious Wood![^2456]

*Sticheron 2:* Having joyfully venerated the holy places, thou didst receive from thence the most saving viaticum of virtue, and didst run exceedingly well on the good course; and having crossed the streams of the Jordan, thou didst zealously dwell in the habitation of the Forerunner, and by thy way of life didst wither the ferocity of the passions, in boldness attenuating, O all-hymned Mother, the wanton properties of the flesh![^2457]

*Sticheron 3:* Having settled in the wilderness, thou didst wipe away the images of thy passions from thy soul, and didst inscribe in thy soul the most Godlike depiction, the icons of virtues; and thou didst shine forth so greatly, O Blessed One, that thou didst lightly walk upon the waters, and didst rise up from the earth in thy supplications unto God. And now in boldness standing before Christ, O all-glorious Mary, pray for our souls![^2458]

*Glory... Tone 4:*
The wonderworking power of Thy Cross, O Christ, is marvelous, for she who was formerly a harlot struggled in the ascetic contest! Therefore, casting off human weakness, she courageously resisted the devil. Therefore, bearing the trophy of victory, she prays for our souls![^2459]

*Both now... Theotokion, the 1st of the Tone [Dogmatikon].*[^2460]

*At the Aposticha: Stichera of the Octoechos; Glory... of the Venerable Mother, Tone 2:*
The snaring of the soul and the passions of the flesh thou didst cut down with the sword of abstinence; the inclinations of sinful thoughts thou didst stifle by the silence of ascetic training...

...and with the streams of thy tears thou didst water the whole desert, and didst cause to sprout forth for us the fruit of repentance. Therefore, O Venerable Mother, we celebrate thy memory![^2461]

*Both now... Theotokion, in the same Tone: "A new wonder of wonders..." (see fol. 304)[^2462].*

*Resurrectional Troparion; and of the Venerable Mother, Tone 8:*

*Troparion:* In thee, O Mother, was preserved with certainty that which is according to the image; for taking up the Cross, thou didst follow Christ, and by thy deeds didst teach [us] to overlook the flesh, for it passes away, and to be attentive to the soul, an immortal thing; therefore together with the Angels rejoices thy spirit![^2463]

*Concerning occurring feasts, see above: folio 124 or 125 (see fol. 124, 125)[^2464].*

*At Matins: According to the entire customary order, as was indicated above, folio 423 (see fol. 423)[^2465].*

*Canons, 3: The Resurrectional Canon with its Theotokion on 6; the present Triodion on 4; and of the Venerable Mother on 4.*[^2466]

*Canon on the Rich Man and Lazarus. Ode 1, Tone 8.*
*Heirmos: Having crossed the water as if it were dry land, and having escaped the wickedness of Egypt, the Israelite cried aloud: Let us sing unto our Deliverer and God!*[^2467]

*Troparion:* The wealth of pleasures hath forsaken me, who rejoiced each day in wanton pleasure like the rich man; therefore I pray Thee, O Savior: deliver me from the fire, even as Thou didst Lazarus![^2468]

*Troparion:* I was clothed in pleasures, O Savior, as one who arrayed himself in fine linen and gold, and in golden raiment; but send me not into the fire, even as that man![^2469]

*Troparion:* The Rich Man rejoiced in wealth and pleasure of old in this corruptible life, therefore he was condemned unto torments; but Lazarus the poor man was refreshed with dew![^2470]

*Theotokion:* The ranks of Angels and men, O unwedded Mother...

...praise Thee unceasingly; for Thou didst carry in Thine arms their Creator as a Babe![^2471]

*Second Canon of the Venerable Mother. Tone 6. Heirmos: By a wave of the sea:*[^2472]

*Troparion:* Send down light unto me who celebrate with love thy light-bearing and divine memory, O venerable one standing before Christ the unapproachable Light, delivering me from all temptations of life![^2473]

*Troparion:* He Who went unto the Egyptians in the flesh, the Uncircumscribed and Pre-eternal, shows thee forth out of Egypt as an all-radiant star: the Lord Who knows all things before their birth![^2474]

*Troparion:* Not knowing how to honor the divine commandments, thou didst defile the divine image of God, O blessed woman; but by divine providence thou didst cleanse it again, O all-praised one, having been deified, O venerable mother, by thy divine deeds![^2475]

*Theotokion:* O the multitude of Thy tender mercy, O my God, and Thine ineffable condescension: how through the consolations of Thy Mother, Thou didst liken her who was formerly a harlot unto the Angels, as pure and undefiled![^2476]

*Ode 3. Heirmos: Thou art the confirmation of those that run unto Thee, O Lord; Thou art the light of the darkened, and my spirit hymns Thee!*[^2477]

*Troparion:* Even as Thou didst save Lazarus from the flame, O Christ, so deliver me, Thine unworthy servant, from the fire of Gehenna![^2478]

*Troparion:* I am rich in passions and pleasures, O Christ, and like Lazarus poor through lack of virtues; but save Thou me![^2479]

*Troparion:* In scarlet and fine linen was the rich man arrayed, with pleasures and sins; therefore he burns in the flame![^2480]

*Theotokion:* Grant me help by Thy prayers, O All-Pure One, repelling the assaults of grievous adversities![^2481]

*Another Heirmos, Tone 6. Upon the waters:*[^2482]

*Troparion:* Unto thee who hadst drawn near unto the gates of destruction by unfitting deeds, He Who of old broke down the gates of Hades by the power of His Divinity opens the gates of repentance, O all-honored one, being Himself the Gate of Life![^2483]

*Troparion:* Unto her who was formerly a weapon of sin, O Long-suffering One, through veneration of the weapon of the divine Cross Thou hast shown forth, O Compassionate One, as conquering in every way all the weapons and wiles of the demons![^2484]

*Troparion:* He Who previously poured out His blood as a ransom for His testament, by the bath of tears makes thee clean who wast diseased with the grievous leprosy of evil doing, He Who in every way gave being unto all![^2485]

*Theotokion:* Higher than every word is that which hath come to pass in Thee, O Virgin; for the Word of the Father divinely dwelt in Thee, granting remission of sins unto all who sin, by a single Word![^2486]

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "Of Wisdom and the Word" (Премꙋ́дрости и҆ сло́во):*
Having bridled all wanton fleshly stirrings by ascetic labors, thou didst show forth the courageous disposition of thy soul; for desiring to see the Cross of the Lord, O all-honored one, thou didst crucify thyself unto the world, whence also thou didst lovingly direct thyself unto the desire of an angelic life, O all-blessed one! Pray thou unto Christ God to grant remission of sins unto those who honor thy holy memory with love![^2487]

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion, Podoben:*
The Heavenly Gate and the Ark, the All-Holy Mountain, the radiant Cloud let us hymn, the Unburnt Bush, the spiritual Paradise, the recall of Eve, the great treasure of all the universe; for in Her salvation was wrought for the world, and remission of ancient transgressions. Therefore also we cry unto Her: Pray Thou unto Thy Son and God to grant remission of sins unto those who piously worship Thy all-holy childbearing![^2488]

*Ode 4. Heirmos: I have heard, O Lord, the mystery of Thy dispensation; I have considered Thy works, and have glorified Thy Divinity!*[^2489]

*Troparion:* The rich man delighted in meats, and rejoiced in garments; but Lazarus desired to be filled with the crumbs from his table![^2490]

*Troparion:* Truly the dogs licked with their tongues the sores of poor Lazarus, being more compassionate to the beggar than the rich man's mind![^2491]

*Troparion:* Before the gates of the rich man Lazarus lay wallowing of old, O Savior, tormented by the afflictions of poverty; therefore now he is glorified unto me![^2492]

*Theotokion:* Pray Thou unto God, Whom Thou didst bear, O Pure One, that they may be saved who hymn Thee, from the bondage of the deceiver; for Thou alone art our protectress![^2493]

*Another Heirmos, Tone 6. Upon the Cross Thy divine emptying:*[^2494]

*Troparion:* As the Creator of human nature, as the Fountain of mercy and the Wealth of loving-kindness, Thou hadst compassion, O Lover of mankind, upon her who fled unto Thee, and didst snatch her from the destructive beast![^2495]

*Troparion:* Striving to behold the Cross, O Mary, thou wast illumined with the enlightenment of the Cross, by the divine nod of Him Who communed with the Cross, having crucified thyself unto the world, O marvelously renowned one![^2496]

*Troparion:* Having formerly been the cause of evils and deceitful pleasure unto many, thou didst shine forth after the likeness of the sun, and wast revealed, O venerable one, as a guide unto all that sin![^2497]

*Theotokion:* Thou didst surpass even the heavenly mind, O spiritual heaven of the King of all; for outside the laws of nature, O Pure One, Thou didst bear the Lawgiver and Creator of all![^2498]

*Ode 5. Heirmos: Why hast Thou cast me off from Thy presence, O Light never-setting, and alien darkness has covered me, wretched that I am? But turn me, and direct my paths unto the light of Thy commandments, I pray Thee!*[^2499]

*Troparion:* When the rich man saw Lazarus in the bosom of Abraham, rejoicing in light and glory, he cried out: "Father Abraham, have mercy on me who am held fast in the fire, and have my tongue grievously in flame!"[^2500]

*Troparion:* "Thou didst enjoy thyself, delighting in the wealth of life," Abraham said unto the rich man; "therefore thou art tormented here, being in the eternal fire; while Lazarus the poor man rejoices in unending joy!"[^2501]

*Troparion:* Through the deceit of life I became like the rich man, O Lover of mankind, having squandered all my life in pleasures; but I pray for Thy mercies, that I may be freed from the fire, even as Lazarus was, O Savior![^2502]

*Theotokion:* Having acquired maternal boldness toward Thy Son, O All-Pure One, despise not kindred care for us, we pray Thee; for Thee alone, as Christians, do we offer unto the Master as an acceptable propitiation![^2503]

*Another Heirmos, Tone 6. Of Thy theophany, O Christ:*[^2504]

*Troparion:* Moses was glorified of old on Sinai, the most glorious one mystically beholding the back parts of God (Exod. 33:23); he described the strange wonder; and now Mary, fervently falling down before the all-pure image of the Manna-receiving Urn, leads an angelic life![^2505]

*Troparion:* Desiring to behold the beauty of Thy temple after the manner of the Psalms, and the noetic habitation of Thy glory (Ps. 25:8 LXX), she who had defiled Thy temple, having through noetic prayers become the temple of Thy Virgin Mother, [cried]: O Christ, make me a temple of the All-Effecting Spirit![^2506]

*Troparion:* Having through the eyes ensnared the members of many by the flesh with brief pleasure...

...and made them food for the devil, she was truly captured by the divine grace of the precious Cross, having become sweeter food for Christ![^2507]

*Theotokion:* Taught concerning the mystery that is in Thee by mystical theologies, O All-Pure One, the choir of Prophets foretold Thee in diverse manners; and now this Mary, falling down before the all-pure image of the Manna-receiving Urn, is a pledge for sinners unto God![^2508]

*Ode 6. Heirmos: Cleanse me, O Savior, for many are my iniquities, and bring me up from the abyss of evils, I pray Thee; for unto Thee have I cried, and give ear unto me, O God of my salvation!*[^2509]

*Troparion:* The rich man condemned himself unto the fiery flame by a voluptuous life; but Lazarus the poor man, encompassed by poverty in life, was accounted worthy of unending joy![^2510]

*Troparion:* In the bosom of Abraham, Lazarus is accounted worthy to delight in eternal life; but in the fire the rich man is condemned in soul and body, being tormented![^2511]

*Troparion:* The rich man is condemned unto the fire because of Lazarus: condemn me not, a wretched man, I pray Thee, O Lord Lover of mankind; but like Lazarus, account me worthy of Thy radiance![^2512]

*Theotokion:* May we be delivered from grievous transgressions by Thy prayers, O pure Mother of God, and may we receive divine illumination from the Son of God, Who was ineffably incarnate of Thee![^2513]

*Another Heirmos, Tone 6. The lowest abyss:*[^2514]

*Troparion:* The angelic hosts rejoice over thee, O Mary, beholding in thee, O venerable one, a life equal unto theirs, and they cry aloud glory unto God![^2515]

*Troparion:* The assemblies of gloomy demons are struck with dread at the strength of thy patient endurance, seeing how as a woman, glorious, naked, and alone, thou didst prevail over them![^2516]

*Troparion:* Thou didst shine forth even as the sun, O Mary all-praised...

...and with wonders hast enlightened all the wilderness; therefore clarify me also with light![^2517]

*Theotokion:* The Angels, enlightened by the glory of Thy childbearing, cried aloud, O Virgin: "Peace on earth unto all of us, and good will unto men!" (Luke 2:14).[^2518]

*Kontakion, Tone 3, Podoben: "Today the Virgin" (Дѣ́ва дне́сь):*
Having formerly been filled with all manner of harlotry, she is shown forth today through repentance as the bride of Christ, following the angelic citizenship; she destroys all demons by the weapon of the Cross; therefore thou hast been revealed as a betrothed of the Kingdom, O Mary most glorious![^2519]

*Ikos:* Let us hymn now with songs the ewe-lamb and daughter of Christ, Mary ever-memorable, who was revealed as a sheep of Egypt, who also escaped from all their deceit, and was brought unto the Church as a whole offering, struggling in temperance and prayer beyond the measure of human nature; therefore the One Almighty Sovereign exalted the life and deeds of Mary most glorious![^2520]

*On the Fifth Sunday of the Holy Great Fast, we celebrate the memory of our Venerable Mother Mary of Egypt, according to the ordinance of the later Holy Fathers. Father, be pleased to read.*[^2521]

*Verses:*
*The spirit struck down the body, and cast it down again;*
*The gates of the earth have concealed Mary in death;*
*On the first of April Mary found death in the wilderness.*[^2522]

The venerable Mary was from Egypt. From her youth she lived at first in wantonness for seventeen years unrestrainedly; and through this cause she came unto repentance: She beheld certain young men embarking upon a ship, and asked them whither they were going; and they said unto her: "Unto Jerusalem, for the sake of the veneration of the precious Cross." And she begged them to take her with them, not because she desired to venerate the precious Cross, but because she was burned with the insatiability of sin; and having entered into the ship, she defiled many. And being in Jerusalem, she was forbidden by an Angel to enter the church gates where the saving Wood of the precious Cross was; and having tried three times and striving to enter, she entered not; and having recalled unto her mind all her sins, she withdrew into a corner of the church porch, and there beheld an icon of the All-Pure...

...Theotokos; and deeply repenting of her sins, she said: "O All-Pure Theotokos, who didst bear Christ the Savior for all the world! I know, yea, I know that it is not fitting for me, unclean and wanton, to look upon Thy holy icon; and indeed it is a just thing that I should remain in hatred and abomination before God; yet do Thou be a surety for my repentance!" And having said this, she departed into the wilderness, and gave herself over unto great penitence and virtues; and she was so greatly exalted by dispassion that she even crossed watery rivers on foot. And when she prayed unto God, then she was borne aloft in the air. And having crossed the Jordan, she lived in the wilderness forty-seven years,[^2523] toiling uncovered and naked, and saw no man, except the blessed Father Zosimas who saw her, and she never abandoned human nature. And at last, according to God's providence, she appeared unto holy Elder Zosimas, when he had entered into the inner wilderness; and having spoken with him and related everything concerning herself, in the following year she crossed the Jordan on foot again, and having partaken of the All-Pure and Life-Creating Mysteries from the holy man, returned unto her place; and by the stream where she had spoken with Zosimas, she fell asleep [in the Lord]. And the following year, when Zosimas went, he found her relics; and when he could not bury her, a lion came and with its forepaws dug a grave for the blessed woman, by the providence of God; and Elder Zosimas buried her in the Mayum mountains,[^2524] and returned, giving glory unto God, One in Trinity, always, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.[^2525]

*[Admonition: Whosoever desires to know more perfectly concerning the Life of this Venerable Mother, let him read the Account concerning her by Saint Sophronius, Patriarch of Jerusalem, which is placed at the very end of this Book (see fol. 870–896)[^2526]. For not only on Thursday of the Fifth Week of the Fast, of the Great Canon, where it is properly appointed to be used, but also here it may be read with spiritual profit by the diligent.]*[^2527]

*Ode 7. Heirmos: Having arrived from Judea in Babylon of old, by faith in the Trinity the Children trod down the flame of the furnace, singing: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!*[^2528]

*Troparion:* Even as Job of old [sat] in the dunghill of worms, so also Lazarus sat in the dunghill before the gates of the rich man, crying: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou![^2529]

*Troparion:* Wallowing before the gates of the unmerciful rich man...

...Lazarus of old desired crumbs from his table, but no one gave unto him; and instead of them he found the bosom of Abraham![^2530]

*Troparion:* From the portion of the heartless rich man, O my Christ, deliver me, I pray Thee; and number me with poor Lazarus to sing unto Thee: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou![^2531]

*Theotokion:* Incarnate from the virginal womb, Thou wast revealed for our salvation; therefore knowing Thy Mother to be the Theotokos, gratefully we cry aloud: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou![^2532]

*Another Heirmos, Tone 6. The Children in Babylon:*[^2533]

*Troparion:* The most great among fathers, traversing the wilderness, the wise Zosimas was accounted worthy to behold the venerable woman, and cried: Blessed is the God of our fathers![^2534]

*Troparion:* "Why, O father, hast thou come to see a strange woman destitute of every active virtue?" the venerable woman cried unto the elder; and she called out: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers![^2535]

*Troparion:* Having mortified the itchings of thy passions, O blessed woman, thou hast now hastened unto the haven of dispassion, crying: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers![^2536]

*Theotokion:* Ineffably Thou didst conceive, remaining a virgin, O All-Pure One, and didst bear for the world salvation, Christ our God; therefore all we the faithful magnify Thee with hymns![^2537]

*Ode 8. Heirmos: Sevenfold the tyrant of the Chaldeans madly kindled the furnace for the pious Children; but seeing them saved by a higher power, he cried unto the Creator and Deliverer: Ye Children, bless; ye priests, hymn; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages!*[^2538]

*Troparion:* In scarlet raiment, and fine linen, and purple, the wretched rich man arrayed himself brightly of old; while poor Lazarus lay grievously at his gates, desiring to be filled with the crumbs falling from the table, and no one gave unto him; therefore he reigns with Christ in glory![^2539]

*Troparion:* At the gates of the rich man lay Lazarus, rotting in his body...

...with wounds, and desired to be filled with food, and no one gave unto him, but even the dogs compassionately licked with their tongues his pus and sores; therefore he was accounted worthy of the paradise of delight![^2540]

*Troparion:* I have become rich in pleasures, even as the rich man of old, arraying himself each day in purple; and I, O Plenteous in mercy, in the delights of this life condemn myself by pleasures and deceits; therefore I pray Thee: deliver me from eternal fire, O Christ, unto all ages![^2541]

*Triadikon:* O thrice-radiant Godhead, shining forth a single radiance from one tripersonal nature: the Unoriginate Begetter, the Word consubstantial with the Father, and the co-existing consubstantial Spirit: ye Children, bless; ye priests, hymn; ye people, supremely exalt unto all ages![^2542]

*Another Heirmos, Tone 6. Be astonished, O heaven, and afraid:*[^2543]

*Troparion:* Thou Who searchest the depths of the heart, foreknowing all our affairs before being: from a distressing life Thou didst snatch her who fled unto Thee, O Savior, who cries out incessantly unto Thy love for mankind: Ye priests, bless; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto ages![^2544]

*Troparion:* O honorable change, and thy transformation unto the better, O honorable woman! O divine love that didst hate the passions of the flesh! O fervent and divine faith, O all-praised Mary, which we faithfully hymn and supremely exalt![^2545]

*Troparion:* Thou hast found recompense for thy toils, and reward for thy sweats, O honorable Mary, by which thou didst cast down the ancient enemy, and now with the Angels...

...thou singest a hymn, incessantly calling and supremely exalting Christ unto ages![^2546]

*Theotokion:* He Who is Master of all the ages renewed me wholly for the sake of goodness in Thy womb, O Pure One, without departing from the properties of His own nature; therefore as the cause of our salvation, we hymn Thee with songs unto all ages![^2547]

*Ode 9. Heirmos: Thee, the unwedded Mother of God the Most High, Whom ineffably through the Word Thou didst conceive, higher than the transcendent Hosts: with ceaseless doxologies we magnify!*[^2548]

*Troparion:* Make me like poor Lazarus, O Christ, I pray Thee, destroying my desires for pleasures, as Thou art God by nature; and make me rich in virtues, that in faith I may magnify Thee in hymnody![^2549]

*Troparion:* Rich and heartless, I have sinned with my mind against the faith of Thy commandments, O Lover of mankind, cast down grievously before the gates; but as Thou art compassionate and plenteous in mercy, raise me up even as of old Thou didst raise Lazarus, Thy four-days-dead friend![^2550]

*Troparion:* We have all learned from the Master's parable; let all of us, the faithful, hate the heartlessness of the rich man, that we may escape torment, and ever dance in the bosom of Abraham![^2551]

*Theotokion:* Thee, who didst bear in Thine arms the invisible God Who is hymned in the heavens by every creature, and through Thee ever grants us salvation, we magnify in faith![^2552]

*Another Heirmos, Tone 6. Lament Me not, O Mother:*[^2553]

*Troparion:* Readily didst thou endure the wilderness toil, O mother, strengthened by the sovereign power of Christ; for with streams of divine tears didst thou quench the defiled thoughts that assailed thee, O honorable one, height of ascetics, boast of the venerable![^2554]

*Troparion:* With all-radiant beams the Virgin and Pure One, who alone bare Christ the Light, enlightens thee; she renders thee terrible unto enemies, O honorable woman, and makes thee manifest unto all, O Mary: beauty of fast-runners,[^2555] confirmation of the venerable!

*Troparion:* Having abandoned all earthly things as a yoke, thou wast revealed as an honorable dwelling of the Spirit; pray thou unto Christ, the only Deliverer, that they who faithfully celebrate thy divine memory may be freed from worldly evils![^2556]

*Theotokion:* Hidden beyond nature from the laws of nature, O Virgin, Thou didst bear on earth a new Babe, O Pure One, Who is the Lawgiver and the Ancient of Days (Dan. 7:9), the noetic Heaven, the Creator of all; therefore in faith and love we call Thee blessed![^2557]

*Exapostilarion, Resurrectional.*[^2558]

*Then of the Venerable Mother, Tone 3, Podoben: "Having adorned heaven with stars" (Не́бо ѕвѣзда́ми):*
Having thee as a pattern of repentance, O all-venerable Mary, pray thou unto Christ that in the time of the fast this may be granted unto us, so that in faith and love we may praise thee with hymns![^2559]

*Theotokion, Podoben:*
O Sweetness of the Angels, Joy of the afflicted, Protectress of Christians, O Virgin Mother of the Lord: intercede for me, and save me from eternal torments![^2560]

*At the Praises: Resurrection Stichera of the Oktoechos, 4; and Anatolian, 4. Then we say the verse: "Arise, O Lord my God, lift up Thine hand, forget not Thy poor for ever" (Ps. 9:33 LXX [10:12]): Idiomelon, Tone 1:*[^2561]
The Kingdom of God is not food and drink, but righteousness and temperance with holiness (Rom. 14:17); therefore the rich shall not enter into it, but whosoever lay their treasures into the hands of the poor. These things David the Prophet also teaches, saying: "Righteous is the man that shows mercy all the day (Ps. 36:26 LXX [37:26]); delighting in the Lord, and walking in the light, he shall not stumble!"[^2562]

All these things he writes for our admonition, that fasting we may do good, and the Lord shall give us heavenly things instead of earthly![^2563]

*Glory: again the same. Both now: Most blessed art Thou: Great Doxology: and the rest according to custom.*[^2564]

*At the Liturgy: The Beatitudes, and the rest, of the Tone. Epistle to the Hebrews, Title 321 [Heb. 9:11–14]: "Brethren, Christ being come an High Priest..." Alleluia: of the Tone. Gospel from Mark, Pericope 47 [Mark 10:32–45]: "At that time, Jesus took the twelve..." Communion Hymn: "Praise the Lord from the heavens..." (Ps. 148:1).*[^2565]

*At table we are consoled even as on previous Sundays.*[^2566]

*On the same Sunday, at Vespers: The customary beginning. Stichera on 10: of the Oktoechos, 4, as was indicated folio 333 (see fol. 333)[^2567]; and of the Triodion, 6. Tone 1, Podoben: "O all-lauded martyrs" (Прехва́льнїи му́ченицы):*
Becoming poor though Thou wast rich, O Christ, Thou hast enriched men with immortality and radiance (2 Cor. 8:9); therefore enrich me with virtues, who have become poor through the pleasures of life, and number me with poor Lazarus, delivering me from the rich man's torment, and from the Gehenna set before me![^2568]

I have become rich in malice grievously, and have loved wanton feeding, and have delighted in the sweet things of life, O Lord, and am condemned unto the fire of Gehenna; melting away with hunger in mind, despised like Lazarus, cast down before the gates of divine deeds, have compassion on me, O Master![^2569]

*Other Stichera. Tone 1, Podoben: "A light cloud" (О҆́блакъ тѧ̀ ле́гкїй):*
Diligently beginning the sixth week of the honorable fasts, O faithful, let us offer unto the Lord a forefeast hymn of the Palms, unto Him Who comes in glory by the power of the Godhead into Jerusalem to slay death; therefore let us piously prepare symbols of victory, branches of virtues, crying aloud: "Hosanna!" unto the Creator of all![^2570]

*Then those in the Menaion.*
*Glory...*[^2571]

*Glory: (unto the Saint, if he have one,) Both now: Theotokion.*[^2572]

*The customary Entrance. Great Prokeimenon, Tone 8:*
*Thou hast given an inheritance: With its verses, seek in the 1st Sunday of the Fast, folio 333 (see fol. 333).[^2573] And the rest with prostrations.*

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 4:*
Wonderful is the Savior's disposition of love for mankind toward us! For possessing as passing knowledge the things that are to come, He exposed the life of Lazarus and of the rich man. Considering the end of both, let us flee from the pitilessness and inhumanity of the one, and emulate the patience and longsuffering of the other, that being comforted with him in the bosom of Abraham, we may cry aloud: O righteous Judge, Lord, glory to Thee![^2574]

*Martyrikon:*
By the prayers of all the saints and of the Theotokos, O Lord, grant us Thy peace, and have mercy upon us, as Thou alone art compassionate![^2575]

*Theotokion:*
O Joy of the heavenly ranks, and mighty helper of men on earth, O pure Virgin: save us who flee unto thee, for, next to God, we have placed our hope in thee, O Mother of God![^2576]

## MONDAY OF THE SIXTH WEEK OF THE HOLY FAST

*At Matins: After Alleluia, the Hymns to the Trinity of the Tone. After the 1st Stichology, the Sessional Hymns in the Oktoechos. After the 2nd Stichology: Sessional Hymn, Tone 1, Podoben: "When the stone had been sealed" (Ка́мени зна́менану):*[^2577]
Thou hast rolled away the stone of ignorance, O Lord, from my heart; raise up my soul which is slain by passions, O Good One, and vouchsafe me in compunction, O Master, to offer unto Thee branches of virtues, as unto the Conqueror of Hades, that...

...I may obtain eternal life, hymning Thy power and Thy compassion, O only Lover of mankind![^2578]

*Theotokion:*
O wonder of wonders, thou who art full of grace! Beholding thee, creation rejoices; for thou didst conceive without seed, and didst bear ineffably Him Whom the ranks of the Angels cannot behold; pray Him, O Mother of God, for our souls![^2579]

*After the 3rd Stichology, Sessional Hymn, Tone 1, Podoben: "When the stone had been sealed" (Ка́мени зна́менану):*
Having the sixth week of the fast, let us offer unto Christ a forefeast hymn of palms, unto Him Who comes for our sake to sit upon the foal of an ass, to bow the irrationality of the Gentiles unto His Father as King; let us all prepare for Him branches of virtues, that rejoicing we may behold His Resurrection![^2580]

*Glory: again the same. Both now: Theotokion:*
Having divinely stretched forth thy hands, with which thou didst carry the Creator, O all-pure Virgin, implore the incarnate Goodness to deliver us from temptations, passions, and perils, who praise thee with love and cry aloud unto thee: Glory to Him that made His abode in thee! Glory to Him that came forth from thee! Glory to Him that hath freed us by thy childbearing![^2581]

*Ode 1, Tone 1. Heirmos: "A song of victory" (Пѣ́снь побѣ́дную):*[^2582]

*Troparion:* Let us slay our passions by abstinence, and let us revive the spirit by divine deeds, that with pure mind we may behold the all-honorable Passion of Christ![^2583]

*Troparion:* Having emulated the pitiless one in the manner of the rich man, O many-merciful Lord, I pray Thee: number me with poor Lazarus, delivering me from the flame and the unquenchable fire![^2584]

*Troparion:* I have fasted from all righteous deeds, and have been filled unto satiety with the sweetness of...

...transgressions, O Lord; do Thou now fill me who hunger with saving and honorable food![^2585]

*Theotokion:* O all-pure Sovereign Lady, who didst bear the all-compassionate Judge: save me and have pity on me who am condemned in judgment, cast down by my deeds![^2586]

*Another Canon. Ode 1, Tone 1. Heirmos: "Unto God Who helped" (Помо́гшому Бг҃у):*[^2587]

*Troparion:* O faithful, who await the flowery feast, celebrating its forefeast brightly from today, let us be vouchsafed to see the Life-bearing Passion![^2588]

*Troparion:* Christ comes, He advances toward Jerusalem as King, sitting upon the foal of an ass, to bow down the irrationality of the Gentiles beneath the yoke of the Father![^2589]

*Triadikon:* In one Godhead, O Tri-hypostatic Unity: unbegotten Father God, and only-begotten Son, and one Holy Spirit, one imperial Sovereign Power: save them that worship Thee![^2590]

*Theotokion:* Most glorious things have been spoken of thee by all in the Spirit, for in the flesh thou didst bear the Creator of all, O Mary Mother of God, all-praised and unwedded![^2591]

*Refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*
*Troparion:* Behold, Christ comes to the town of Bethphage; rejoice, Bethany, fatherland of Lazarus! For unto thee He shall show forth a great wonder, raising Lazarus from the dead![^2592]

*Katavasia (Heirmos):* Unto God Who helped Moses in Egypt, and thereby drowned Pharaoh with all his host: let us sing a song of victory, for He is glorified![^2593]

*Ode 8, Tone 1. Heirmos: "Him Whom the Angels fear" (Е҆го́же ᲂу҆жаса́ютсѧ):*[^2594]

*Troparion:* Wretched that I am, I have become rich in barren thoughts, I have defiled my soul with unclean pleasures, and the darkness of despair encompasses me; shine forth upon me the radiance of repentance, O my God![^2595]

*Troparion:* Even as of old Thou didst enlighten the man blind from birth, enlighten my soul which sees not Thy light, O Merciful One, but is buried in bitter darkness of bitter oblivion and in worldly cares![^2596]

*Troparion:* Elijah, having fasted, opened the heavens, and with showers gave drink to the thirsty earth (3 Kgs. 18:41–45 LXX [1 Kgs. 18:41–45]); let us fast, drawing streams of tears of the soul, that we may find mercy![^2597]

*Theotokion:* As a living vine thou hast blossomed forth for us a ripe cluster, pouring out for us, O pure Virgin, the wine of forgiveness, which dries up the drunkenness of sin![^2598]

*Another Canon. Ode 8, Tone 1. Heirmos: "A hymn we offer Thee" (Пѣ́снь ти прино́симъ):*[^2599]

*Troparion:* The vestibule of Lazarus' revitalization has opened, for Christ comes to raise the dead one as if from sleep, and by life to conquer death![^2600]

*Troparion:* Great is thy boast, O Bethany! For thou wast vouchsafed to receive as a guest the Creator, crying aloud: "Bless the works of the Lord, ye works of the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!"[^2601]

*Refrain: We bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit: the Lord.*
*Triadikon:* Thee, the superessential, threefold Unity, united in divinity though divided in the appearance of Persons: Father, and Son, and divine Spirit, do we glorify![^2602]

*Theotokion:* Together with the Angels we proclaim unto thee "Rejoice," for thou didst raise up joy: the Savior of the world; implore Him, O all-praised Virgin![^2603]

*Refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*
*Troparion:* A hymn we offer Thee, who ridest upon a foal, riding in the highest upon the Cherubim, that Thou mayest subdue all unto Thy dominion, O Christ![^2604]

*Refrain: We praise, we bless, and we worship the Lord.*
*Katavasia (Heirmos):* A hymn we offer Thee of the bodiless hosts, as did the Children in the furnace, and singing we say: Bless and supremely exalt Christ unto the ages![^2605]

*Ode 9, Tone 1. Heirmos: "The Life-bearing Spring" (Живоно́сный и҆сто́чникъ):*[^2606]

*Troparion:* Slain by many transgressions of negligence, I am held fast in the tomb, having the stone of despair lying upon me; rolling it away by Thy mercy, O Christ, as Thou didst Lazarus of old, do Thou now raise me up![^2607]

*Troparion:* Let us flee from the likeness of the rich man who was condemned to the unquenchable flame, and let us love the patient endurance of Lazarus in afflictions, that when we depart hence, Abraham may receive us into his bosom![^2608]

*Troparion:* Let us love the Fast that slays the passions, let us diligently give ourselves over to prayer, let us weep, lament, and warmly sigh, that Jesus may comfort us and make us partakers of His Kingdom![^2609]

*Theotokion:* Divine vessel of virginity, the only restoration of our Forefathers, spring pouring forth an abyss of loving-kindness, Beauty of Jacob: O Mother of God, saved through thee, we praise thee![^2610]

*Another Canon. Ode 9, Tone 1. Heirmos: "Thee, the gate seen" (Тебѐ ви́дѣнїи):*[^2611]

*Troparion:* Today Christ, walking on the other side of the Jordan, is told of the sickness of Lazarus, and as a seer He says: "This sickness is not unto death now!"[^2612]

*Troparion:* Make ready, O Bethany; adorn thy divine entrances, expand thy vestibules; for behold, the Master comes with the Apostles, to give life to His sheep![^2613]

*Triadikon:* Thee, the tri-hypostatic Unity, the indivisible Essence, Whom the six-winged armies glorify, we, the race of men, magnify with hymns![^2614]

*Theotokion:* Thee, Who wast born of the Father timelessly, and of a Mother ineffably in time for the salvation of all, as...

...Creator and Master, we magnify with hymns![^2615]

*Refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*
*Troparion:* With branches of good works, and bearing palms of purity, let us all make ready to meet Christ, Who comes unto Jerusalem as our God![^2616]

*Katavasia (Heirmos):* Thee, the gate seen by Ezekiel the Prophet, through which no one has passed save God alone: O Virgin Theotokos, we magnify with hymns![^2617]

*It is truly meet: Then, the Exapostilarion.*

*At the Aposticha, Stichera Idiomela, Tone 1:*
Condemn me not, O Christ, to the flame of Gehenna, as Thou didst the rich man on account of Lazarus; but grant unto me also, who weep and beg for even a drop of Thy love for mankind, O God, and have mercy upon me![^2618]

*Martyrikon:*
Blessed is the army of the heavenly King! For though the passion-bearers were earthly-born, yet they hastened to attain unto the angelic dignity, taking no heed for their bodies; by their sufferings they were vouchsafed the honor of the bodiless ones; therefore by their prayers, O Lord, save our souls![^2619]

*Glory: Both now: Theotokion, the same Tone:*
O gracious Lady, intercede by thy prayers, and obtain for our souls a multitude of compassions and cleansing from many transgressions, we pray thee![^2620]

*On the same day of the Sixth Week of the Fast, at the Sixth Hour:*

*Troparion of the Prophecy, Tone 6:*
This is our God, terrible in day, Whom reaching until evening we hope not; and to behold Him Thou hast vouchsafed us in Thy love for mankind: O Thrice-Holy, glory to Thee![^2621]

*Glory: conclusion. Both now: the same. Prokeimenon from Psalm 104, Tone 6:*

Let the heart of them rejoice that seek the Lord! *Verse:* O give thanks unto the Lord, and call upon His Name![^2622]

*Reading from the Prophecy of Isaiah (Chapter 48):*
Thus saith the Lord that delivers thee, the Holy One of Israel: I am the Lord thy God, Who hath shown thee how thou shouldest find the way wherein thou shouldest walk.[^2623]

And if thou hadst given ear to My commandments, then had thy peace been as a river, and thy righteousness as the wave of the sea.[^2624]

And thy seed would have been as the sand of the sea, and the offspring of thy belly as the dust of the earth; neither shouldest thou now be utterly destroyed, nor should thy name perish before Me.[^2625]

Go forth from Babylon, fleeing from the Chaldeans; declare the voice of joy, and let this be heard, declare it even unto the ends of the earth; say ye: The Lord hath delivered His servant Jacob![^2626]

And if they thirst in the desert, He shall lead them; He shall bring water out of the rock for them; the rock shall be cleft, and water shall flow, and My people shall drink.[^2627]

There is no rejoicing unto the ungodly, saith the Lord.[^2628]

Give ear unto Me, ye islands, and attend, ye nations; through a long time it shall stand, saith the Lord: from the womb He called Me, and from the belly of My mother He named My name.[^2629]
