And He hath made My mouth as a sharp sword, and under the shelter of His hand hath He hid Me; He hath made Me as an elect shaft, and in His quiver hath He sheltered Me.[^2630]

And He said unto Me: Thou art My servant, O Israel, and in Thee I will be glorified.[^2631]

And I said: In vain have I labored, for vanity...

...and for nought have I spent My strength; therefore My judgment is with the Lord, and My labor before My God![^2632]

*Prokeimenon from Psalm 105, Tone 6:* Blessed be the Lord God of Israel from everlasting to everlasting! *Verse:* O give thanks unto the Lord, for He is good![^2633]

*On the evening of the same day of the Sixth Week, at "Lord, I have cried":*

*Stichera of Sir Joseph, Tone 6, Podoben: "Having laid aside all earthly hope" (Всѐ ѿло́жше):*
With many transgressions and the pleasures of life diseased, wretched that I am, I have acquired an ailing soul, and I lie upon the bed of sloth always, O Master; and I cry unto Thee, O Merciful One: come and visit me, granting me health and mercy, and leave me not, lest at any time I sleep unto death, and the enemy rejoice over my destruction, who seeks always to cast me down into the depth of Hades, O Savior![^2634]

Having emulated the pitilessness of the rich man in foolishness, I delightfully rejoice, plunging myself into pleasures and passions; and seeing the repentance of my mind lying always before the gates like Lazarus, O Lord, I heedlessly pass him by, ailing with hunger and covered with sores of passions; therefore I have become liable unto the fire of Gehenna, from which deliver me, O Master, Who alone art many-merciful![^2635]

*Another Sticheron of Sir Theodore, Tone 5, Podoben: "Lord, in the days of Moses" (Гдⷭ҇и при Мѡѵсе́ин):*
O Lord, journeying in the flesh beyond the Jordan, Thou didst foretell that the sickness of Lazarus was not unto death, but that it should be for the glory of Thine exceeding goodness; glory to the greatness of Thy deeds and to Thine almighty dominion, for Thou hast cast down death through Thy manifold mercy, O Lover of mankind![^2636]

*Then those of the Menaion. In the evening, Prokeimenon from Psalm 106, Tone 4:*

O give thanks unto the Lord, for He is good, for His mercy endures unto the ages! *Verse:* Let the redeemed of the Lord say so, whom He hath redeemed![^2637]

*Reading from Genesis (Chapter 27):*
And it came to pass after Isaac was grown old, that his eyes were dim so that he could not see; and he called Esau his elder son, and said unto him: My son! And he said: Behold, here am I.[^2638]

And he said unto him: Behold, I am old, and know not the day of my death.[^2639]

Now therefore take thy weapons, thy quiver and thy bow, and go out to the field,[^2640]

and hunt me venison, and make me savory meat, such as I love, and bring it to me that I may eat, that my soul may bless thee before I die.[^2641]

And Rebekah heard Isaac speaking unto Esau his son; and Esau went to the field to hunt for venison for his father.[^2642]

And Rebekah spake unto Jacob her younger son, saying: Behold, I heard thy father speaking unto Esau thy brother, saying:[^2643]

Bring me venison, and make me savory meat, that I may eat and bless thee before the Lord before my death.[^2644]

Now therefore, my son, obey my voice, according as I command thee;[^2645]

and go to the flock, and fetch me thence two kids of the goats, tender and good, and I will make them savory meat for thy father, such as he loves;[^2646]

and thou shalt bring it to thy father, and he shall eat, that thy father may bless thee before his death.[^2647]

And Jacob said unto Rebekah his mother: Behold, Esau my brother is a hairy man, and I am a smooth man;[^2648]

lest perhaps my father feel me, and I shall be before him...

...as a mocker, and I shall bring upon myself a curse, and not a blessing.[^2649]

And his mother said unto him: Upon me be thy curse, my child; only obey my voice, and go fetch them to me.[^2650]

And he went, and fetched, and brought them to his mother; and his mother made savory meats, such as his father loved.[^2651]

And Rebekah took goodly raiment of her elder son Esau, which was with her in the house, and put it upon Jacob her younger son.[^2652]

And with the skins of the kids of the goats she bound his arms,[^2653]

and she gave the savory meats and the loaves, which she had made, into the hands of Jacob her son.[^2654]

And he brought them unto his father, and said: My father! And he said: Behold, here am I; who art thou, my child?[^2655]

And Jacob said unto his father: I am Esau thy firstborn; I have done according as thou didst bid me; arise, sit and eat of my venison, that thy soul may bless me.[^2656]

And Isaac said unto his son: How is it that thou hast found it so quickly, my child? And he said: That which the Lord God delivered before me.[^2657]

And Isaac said unto Jacob: Come near, I pray thee, that I may feel thee, child, whether thou art my son Esau or not.[^2658]

And Jacob went near unto Isaac his father, and he felt him, and said: The voice indeed is Jacob's voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau.[^2659]

And he recognized him not, for his hands were as his brother Esau's hands, hairy; and he recognized him not, and blessed him.[^2660]

And he said: Art thou my son Esau? And he said: I am.[^2661]

And he said: Bring it near to me, and I will eat of thy venison, child, that my soul may bless thee. And he brought it near to him, and he ate; and he brought him wine, and he drank.[^2662]

And Isaac his father said unto him:[^2663]

...Come near unto me, and kiss me, my child! And he came near and kissed him; and he smelled the smell of his raiment, and blessed him, and said: Behold, the smell of my son is as the smell of a full field, which the Lord hath blessed;[^2664] and may God give thee of the dew of heaven, and of the fatness of the earth, and plenty of corn and wine;[^2665] and let nations serve thee, and princes bow down unto thee; and be thou lord over thy brother, and let the sons of thy father bow down unto thee; he that curses thee is cursed, and he that blesses thee is blessed![^2666]

And it came to pass after Isaac had ceased blessing Jacob his son, and it came to pass as soon as Jacob had gone out from the face of Isaac his father, that Esau his brother came from his hunting.[^2667]

And he also had made savory meat, and brought it unto his father, and said: Let my father arise, and eat of his son's venison, that thy soul may bless me.[^2668]

And Isaac his father said unto him: Who art thou? And he said: I am thy son, thy firstborn, Esau.[^2669]

And Isaac was amazed with an exceeding great amazement, and said: Who then is he that hunted game for me, and brought it to me, and I ate of all before thou camest, and blessed him? Yea, and he shall be blessed![^2670]

And it came to pass when Esau heard the words of Isaac his father, he cried out with an exceeding great and bitter cry, and said: Bless me also, O father![^2671]

And he said unto him: Thy brother came with subtlety, and took away thy blessing.[^2672]

And Esau said: Rightly was his name called Jacob; for he hath supplanted me now this second time: my birthright he took, and now he hath taken my blessing. And Esau said unto...

...his father: Hast thou not reserved a blessing for me, O father?[^2673]

And Isaac answered and said unto Esau: If I have made him thy lord, and all his brethren have I made his servants, and with corn and wine have I sustained him: what then shall I do unto thee, child?[^2674]

And Esau said unto his father: Hast thou but one blessing, O father? Bless me also, O father! And Isaac being moved to compunction, Esau cried aloud with a great voice and wept.[^2675]

And Isaac his father answered and said: Behold, of the fatness of the earth shall be thy dwelling, and of the dew of heaven from above;[^2676]

and by thy sword shalt thou live, and thou shalt serve thy brother; and it shall come to pass when thou shalt cast down and loose his yoke from off thy neck.[^2677]

And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing wherewith his father had blessed him.[^2678]

*Prokeimenon from Psalm 56, Tone 7:* Be Thou exalted, O God, above the heavens, and Thy glory above all the earth! *Verse:* My heart is ready, O God, my heart is ready![^2679]

*Reading from Proverbs (Chapter 19):*[^2680]
He that keeps the commandment preserves his own soul; but he that despises his ways shall perish.[^2681]

He that hath pity upon the poor lends unto God; and according to his giving, it shall be repaid him.[^2682]

Chasten thy son, for so he shall be hopeful; but unto insolence be not lifted up in thy soul.[^2683]

A malicious man shall be greatly penalized; and if he do harm, he shall add unto his soul.[^2684]

Hear, my son, the instruction of thy father, that thou mayest be wise in thy latter days.[^2685]

Many thoughts are in the heart of a man...

...but the counsel of the Lord abides unto the ages.[^2686]

Mercy is fruit unto a man; and better is a poor righteous man than a rich liar.[^2687]

The fear of the Lord is unto life for a man; but the fearless man shall lodge in places where knowledge visits not.[^2688]

He that hides his hands in his bosom unrighteously will not even bring them unto his own mouth.[^2689]

When a pestilent man is scourged, a fool becomes more subtle; and if thou reprove a wise man, he will understand discernment.[^2690]

*Then: "Vouchsafe, O Lord."*

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Idiomelon, Tone 4:* Deliver us from soul-harming extortion, and number us with poor Lazarus in the bosom of Abraham, O Savior; for being rich in mercies, Thou didst willingly become poor for our sake, and hast translated us from corruption unto incorruption, as Thou art a merciful God and the Lover of mankind![^2691]

*The usual verses. Martyrikon:* Thou Who didst accept the endurance of the holy Martyrs, accept also our hymn, O Lover of mankind, and grant us by their prayers great mercy![^2692]

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:* Deliver us from our necessities, O Mother of Christ God, who didst bear the Creator of all, that we all may cry unto thee: Rejoice, Protectress of our souls![^2693]

## TUESDAY OF PALM WEEK (THE SIXTH WEEK OF THE FAST)[^2694]

*At Matins: After Alleluia, the Hymns to the Trinity of the Tone. After the 1st Stichology, the Sessional Hymn in the Oktoechos. After the 2nd Stichology, Sessional Hymn of Sir Joseph, Tone 6, Podoben: "The Angelic Powers" (А́ггельскїя силы):* Being wasted with the disease of sin, upon the bed of despair I lie prostrate; therefore, O Physician of the ailing...

...visit me in Thy love for mankind, and suffer me not to sleep grievously unto death, O all-bountiful One, that I may cry fervently unto Thee: O Giver of mercy, Lord, glory to Thee![^2695]

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:* The beginning of salvation was Gabriel's greeting unto the Virgin; for hearing the "Rejoice," she fled not from the salutation, nor did she doubt like Sarah in the tent, but spake thus: Behold the handmaid of the Lord, be it unto me according to thy word![^2696]

*After the 3rd Stichology, Sessional Hymn of Sir Theodore, Tone 5, Podoben: "Today shines forth" (Сїѧ́етъ дне́сь):* Yesterday and today is the sickness of Lazarus, for his kinsfolk announce this unto Christ: make ready the abode with joy to entertain the Giver of life and the King, and to cry with us: Lord, glory to Thee![^2697]

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:* All-holy Mother of God, rampart of Christians: deliver thy people as is thy wont, who cry diligently unto thee; stand against defiled and haughty thoughts, that we may cry unto thee: Rejoice, ever-Virgin![^2698]

*Triodion Canon of Sir Joseph, Tone 6. Ode 2. Heirmos:* See, see that I am God, Who rained down manna, and poured forth water from the rock of old in the wilderness for My people, by My right hand alone and by My power![^2699]

*Troparion:* Thou didst willingly become poor, O Christ Who art rich by nature; Thou didst willingly hunger, Who fillest every living thing: therefore I pray Thee, satisfy me who hunger for Thy grace, and show me, O Word, to be a partaker of the banquet there![^2700]

*Troparion:* Show me to be poor like Lazarus in sins, O Christ, and scatter the riches which I have evilly gathered; and having fulfilled Thine absolute manifestation, O Compassionate One, deliver me from the fearful torment there![^2701]

*Troparion:* Having strengthened the Children, Thou didst make them firmer than fire of old in Babylon as they sang: therefore, emulating them, O my soul, despond not, but quench the fire of passions with the dew of the Spirit![^2702]

*Theotokion:* Rejoice, we cry unto thee who didst bear Joy, O Virgin Theotokos full of grace: pray God Whom thou didst bear, that they may be delivered from perils and corruption who ever hymn thee![^2703]

*Another Canon of Sir Theodore, Tone 5. Ode 2. Heirmos: "See, see that I am God" (Ви́дите, ви́дите ꙗ҆́кѡ а҆́зъ є҆́смъ Бг҃ъ):*[^2704]
*Troparion:* See, see that I am God, Who walk on the other side of the Jordan, having heard that Lazarus is sick, and having said that he shall not die, for this is for My glory![^2705]

*Troparion:* Encompassed with weeping, the sisters of Lazarus stand before Thee, manifesting him unto Thee Who knowest all things; but Thou abidest a little while, that Thou mayest raise up a wonder, and show awesome things unto Thy disciples![^2706]

*Triadicon:* Single-stemmed, three-hypostatic Unity, Lordship and Kingdom of the ages: the multitude of Angels and all human nature glorify Thee, Father, and Son, and Holy Spirit![^2707]

*Theotokion:* Who would not marvel, beholding in thee the Creator, O Virgin, Who fashioned anew fallen Adam, ineffably united and born of thee in the flesh without change, unto our salvation![^2708]

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee!*
*Troparion:* Now adorn thyself with joy, O Bethany, having become the hostess of the King of all; for He comes unto thee, that He may show Lazarus flowing again from corruption into life![^2709]

*Katavasia Heirmos:* See, see that I am God, Who clothed Myself in flesh of Mine own free will, that I might save Adam fallen through the deceit of the serpent's transgression![^2710]

*Ode 8. Heirmos: "From the flame Thou didst pour forth dew for the holy ones" (И҆з пла́мене ст҃ы́мъ ро́су и҆сточи́):*[^2711]

*Troparion:* Pondering the multitude of my transgressions, and wounded by the sting of conscience, as in the flame I cry, wretched that I am: Have compassion upon me, O Word of God, by Thy mercy![^2712]

*Troparion:* Despising the righteous deeds of Lazarus, I envied the disposition of the merciless rich man, O merciful Christ: turn me and have compassion on me, that I may glorify Thee unto all ages![^2713]

*Troparion:* Held fast by sickness of soul, and ready to die in despair, I need Thy visitation, O Jesus, Who givest life unto those that call upon Thee![^2714]

*Theotokion:* All-pure Virgin, do thou save me; be a help unto my weakness, who didst bear the Benefactor of mercy, Whom we exalt unto all ages![^2715]

*Another Canon of Sir Theodore, Ode 8. Heirmos: "Thy venerable Children" (Преподо́бнїи твоѝ ѿро́цы):*[^2716]
*Troparion:* Rejoice, O Bethany, homeland of Lazarus; for Christ coming unto thee shall accomplish a great deed, having revived Lazarus![^2717]

*Troparion:* Lazarus is sick, that Thou, O Son of God, mayest be glorified in him; and he hymns Thee unceasingly: All ye works of the Lord, bless the Lord, and exalt Him above all forever![^2718]

*Let us bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, the Lord.*
*Triadicon:* Hymning the Trinity enthroned together in Father, and Son, and Holy Spirit, we sing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and hymn the Lord![^2719]

*Both now... Theotokion:* All of us hymn thine ineffable childbearing, O pure one; and honoring Him as God, all ye works bless Him as Creator and Lord![^2720]

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee!*
*Troparion:* Preparing branches of virtues unto the meeting of Christ, we cry: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and exalt Him above all![^2721]

*We praise, we bless, and we worship the Lord, hymning the Lord.*
*Katavasia Heirmos:* Thy venerable Children in the furnace, singing, praised Christ: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and exalt Him above all forever![^2722]

*Ode 9. Heirmos: "God cannot be seen of men" (Бо́га человѣ́комъ):*[^2723]
*Troparion:* The bitter tasting of the first-created man of old cruelly cast him out of Paradise, and bound him unto the corruption of death: fast, O my soul, flee imitation, flee the enjoyment of much-painful pleasure![^2724]

*Troparion:* Taking into mind Thy judgment-seat and the unquenchable flame, O most righteous Judge, I condemn myself before the judgment; for I am amazed and I tremble, having immeasurably sinned against Thee as no one else on earth: therefore I pray Thee, have compassion upon me![^2725]

*Troparion:* Let us wash away the stains of passions with radiant prayers, and bearing branches of virtues, let us hasten to meet Christ, Who now comes to sit upon the foal of an ass, preparing Himself for the Passion, for our salvation![^2726]

*Theotokion:* From thee, O Virgin full of God's grace, upon those held fast in the night of passions a Light hath shone forth, and the Giver of peace, Christ, loosing the transgression of the embrace, and clearly granting redemption unto us![^2727]

*Another Canon of Sir Theodore, Ode 9. Heirmos: "Rejoice, O Isaiah" (И҆са́їа лику́й):*[^2728]
*Troparion:* Now prepare thy burial garments, O dead Lazarus, for thou art departing from life, being about to die tomorrow; behold the grave wherein thou shalt dwell; but Christ shall again revive thee, raising thee on the fourth day![^2729]

*Troparion:* Rejoice, O Bethany, for Christ comes unto thee to accomplish a great and awesome wonder: having bound death, He will wholly raise up as God the dead Lazarus, who magnifies the Creator![^2730]

*Triadicon:* One Essence I hymn Thee, O beginningless...

...Trinity, honorable, life-originating, and indivisible Unity: unbegotten Father, and begotten Word and Son, and Holy Spirit: save us who hymn Thee![^2731]

*Theotokion:* Beyond understanding is thy childbearing, O Mother of God; for without man was conception in thee, and virginal was the childbearing, for God is the Born One, Whom magnifying, we call thee blessed, O Virgin![^2732]

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee!*
*Troparion:* Come, let us prepare for the Lord, bearing branches of virtues unto His meeting, so that we may receive Him into our soul as into the city of Jerusalem, worshipping and hymning Him![^2733]

*Katavasia Heirmos:* Rejoice, O Isaiah: for a Virgin had in womb, and bare a Son, Emmanuel, God and man: Dayspring is His name, Whom magnifying, we call thee blessed, O Virgin![^2734]

*Then: "It is truly meet." Exapostilarion of the Tone.*

*At the Aposticha, Idiomelon, Tone 5:* Having slipped through transgressions, and bound with the cords of sins, O soul, why dost thou despond? Why art thou slothful? Flee ever as Lot from Sodom and Gomorrah, from the burning of uncleanness; turn not back, lest thou become as a pillar of salt; be saved on the mountain of virtues; flee ever from the merciless rich man's pitiless burning; pass over into the bosom of Abraham, like Lazarus, and in humility of mind cry: My Hope and my Refuge, O Lord, glory to Thee! *(Twice)*[^2735]

*Martyrikon:* Thy passion-bearers, O Lord, having emulated the angelic ranks, endured torments as if bodiless, possessing of one mind the hope of the enjoyment of the promised good things: by their prayers, O Christ...

...our God, grant peace unto Thy world, and unto our souls great mercy![^2736]

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:* We pray thee, as the Mother of God, O blessed one: pray that our souls may be saved![^2737]

*On the same Tuesday, at the Sixth Hour.*

*Troparion of the Prophecy, Tone 5:* An invincible rampart hast Thou given unto our city, the Virgin who bare Thee: by her, O Savior, deliver our souls, we pray Thee, from the evils that encompass us! *Glory... Both now... the same.*[^2738]

*Prokeimenon from Psalm 108, Tone 4:* Help me, O Lord my God, and save me according to Thy mercy! *Verse:* O God, hold not Thy peace at my praise![^2739]

*Reading from the Prophecy of Isaiah (Chapter 49):*[^2740]
Thus saith the Lord: Behold, I have given Thee for a covenant of a race, for a light of the Gentiles, that Thou mayest be for salvation unto the ends of the earth.[^2741]

Thus saith the Lord, the God of Israel that hath redeemed thee: Sanctify Him that is despised, sanctify Him that abhorrs His soul, Him that is abominable unto the nations, a servant of rulers. Kings shall see Him, and princes shall arise and bow down to Him for the Lord's sake, because the Holy One of Israel is faithful, and I have chosen Thee.[^2742]

Thus saith the Lord: In an acceptable time have I heard Thee, and in a day of salvation have I helped Thee; and I have formed Thee, and given Thee for a covenant of the Gentiles, to establish the earth, and to inherit the heritage of the wilderness;[^2743]

saying to them that are in bonds: Go forth! and to them that are in darkness...

...Show yourselves! They shall feed in all the ways, and on all paths shall be their pasture.[^2744]

They shall not hunger, neither shall they thirst; neither shall the heat smite them, nor the sun; but He that hath mercy on them shall comfort them.[^2745]

*Prokeimenon from Psalm 109, Tone 4:* Thou art a priest forever after the order of Melchizedek. *Verse:* The Lord said unto my Lord: Sit Thou at My right hand![^2746]

*On the same Tuesday Evening, at "Lord, I have cried":*

*Stichera of Sir Joseph, Tone 1, Podoben: "When from the Tree" (Е҆гда̀ ѿ дре́ва):*
By all the assaults of the crafty one, my much-suffering heart, having grown weak, hath been opened as a tomb of grievous despondency, and is covered with insensibility as with a stone: O Savior, Who by the Wood of Thy life-bearing Cross didst give life unto all that were in Hades, raise me up, give me life, that with fear I may glorify Thy Godhead![^2747]

Riches of corrupting pleasures have I ever acquired through the working of the crafty one, vainly making merry, foolish that I am; and I have despised my mind as another Lazarus, groaning and hungering for divine victuals, O Word: deliver me from the future flame by Thy tender mercy, that I may glorify Thee, the Lover of mankind![^2748]

*Another Sticheron of Sir Theodore, Tone 3, Podoben: "They weighed thirty pieces of silver" (Поста́виша):*
Today Lazarus dies, and Bethany weeps for him, whom Thou, O Savior of others, shalt raise from the dead, and shalt fully convince Thy friends of Thine awesome Resurrection, the slaying of Hades, and the reviving of Adam: therefore we hymn Thee![^2749]

*Then: "Blessed..."*[^2750]

*At Vespers: Prokeimenon from Psalm 110, Tone 4:* The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom.[^2751] *Verse:* I will confess Thee, O Lord, with my whole heart.

*Reading from Genesis (Chapter 31):*[^2752]
The Lord said unto Jacob: Return into the land of thy father, and unto thy kindred, and I will be with thee.[^2753]

And Jacob sent and called Leah and Rachel to the field, where the flocks were,[^2754]

and said unto them: I see the face of your father, that it is not toward me as yesterday and the third day; but the God of my father hath been with me.[^2755]

And ye yourselves know that with all my power I have served your father.[^2756]

And your father hath wronged me, and changed my wages ten lambs; yet the God of my father suffered him not to hurt me.[^2757]

If he said thus: The speckled shall be thy wages, then all the sheep bare speckled; and if he said: The white shall be thy wages, then all the sheep bare white.[^2758]

And God hath taken away all the cattle of your father, and given them to me.[^2759]

And it came to pass at the time when the sheep conceived, that I saw with mine eyes in a dream: and behold, the he-goats and rams leaping upon the sheep and the goats were white and speckled, and ash-colored and dappled.[^2760]

And the Angel of God said unto me in a dream: Jacob! And I said: What is it?[^2761]

And He said: Lift up thine eyes, and behold the he-goats and the rams leaping upon the sheep and the goats, white and speckled, and ash-colored and dappled; for I have seen all that Laban doth unto thee.[^2762]

I am thy God Who appeared unto Thee in the place of God, where...[^2763]

...thou anointedst a pillar unto Me, and vowedst a vow unto Me there. Now therefore arise, and go forth out of this land, and go into the land of thy nativity, and I will be with thee.

And Leah and Rachel answered and said unto him: Is there yet any portion or inheritance for us in the house of our father?[^2764]

Are we not counted of him as strangers? For he hath sold us, and hath quite devoured our silver;[^2765]

all the riches and glory which God hath taken away from our father shall be ours and our children's. Now then, whatsoever God hath said unto thee, do![^2766]

*Prokeimenon from Psalm 111, Tone 4:* Merciful, and compassionate, and righteous.[^2767] *Verse:* Blessed is the man that fears the Lord.

*Reading from Proverbs (Chapter 21):*[^2768]
My son, to do righteous things and to speak truth are more acceptable to God than the blood of sacrifices.[^2769]

He that is high-minded in reproach is a bold-hearted man; and the lamp of the ungodly is sin.[^2770]

The thoughts of the diligent tend only to plenty; but everyone that is hasty comes only to want.[^2771]

He that gathers treasures with a false tongue pursues vanity, and falls into the snares of death.[^2772]

Destruction shall fall upon the ungodly; for they will not to do righteous things.[^2773]

Unto the crooked God sends crooked ways; for His works are pure and upright.[^2774]

It is better to dwell in a dark corner with love, than in plastered rooms with unrighteousness and in a shared house.[^2775]

The soul of the ungodly desires evil things, and finds no mercy from any man.[^2776]

When the extortioner is punished, the simple becomes wiser; and when the wise considers, he will receive knowledge.[^2777]

The righteous understands the hearts of the ungodly, and brings the ungodly into trouble in their wickedness.[^2778]

He that stops his ears from hearing the weak, he also shall call, and there shall be none to hear.[^2779]

A secret gift turns away wrath; but he that spares gifts stirs up strong rage.[^2780]

It is the joy of the righteous to do judgment; but the holy is abominable to evildoers.[^2781]

A man that wanders out of the way of righteousness shall rest in the assembly of the giants.[^2782]

A needy man loves mirth, and he that loves wine and oil shall not grow rich.[^2783]

The transgression of the ungodly is an offscouring of the righteous, and in the place of the upright is the simple.[^2784]

It is better to dwell in a wilderness, than with a contentious and wrathful and talkative woman.[^2785]

A desirable treasure rests upon the mouth of the wise; but foolish men swallow it up.[^2786]

The way of righteousness and mercy finds life and glory.[^2787]

*Then: "Vouchsafe, O Lord."*[^2788]

*At the Aposticha, Sticheron Idiomelon, Tone 4:* Clad in the God-woven purple of autocracy and the scarlet robe of incorruption, O my soul, thou hast disgraced thy dignity, having made sin thy riches and luxury, and despising thy kinsman, even as the rich man despised poor Lazarus: but that thou be not tormented with him, become poor in spirit, and cry unto the Lord Who became poor for thy sake: O Thou Who before the Crucifixion wast clothed with the purple robe of mockery...[^2789]

...and on the Cross was crucified naked for my sake, deliver me, O Christ, from eternal torment there, through the garment of Thy Kingdom!

*Martyrikon:* O marvelous commerce was yours, holy martyrs! For ye gave your blood, and inherited the heavens; and having been tried for a season, ye rejoice eternally. Truly good was your commerce: for leaving corruptible things, ye received incorruptible things, and dancing with the Angels, ye sing unceasingly to the consubstantial Trinity![^2790]

*Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion, Tone 1, Podoben: "O all-lauded martyrs" (Прехва́льнымъ):* A sword hath passed through my heart, O Master, cried the Virgin, as she beheld Christ hanging upon the Tree, and it rends me, even as Simeon foretold unto me of old: but arise, O Immortal One, and glorify together Thy Mother and Handmaid, we pray Thee![^2791]

## WEDNESDAY OF PALM WEEK, AT MATINS[^2792]

*After Alleluia, the Hymns to the Trinity of the Tone. After the 1st Stichology, the Sessional Hymn in the Oktoechos. After the 2nd Stichology, Sessional Hymn of Sir Joseph, Tone 2, Podoben: "The stone of the tomb" (Ка́мень гро́бный):* As weighed down by a stone with many sins, I lie in the tomb of negligence, O Compassionate One: deliver me therefrom, O merciful Lord![^2793]

*Glory... the same again. Both now... Stavrotheotokion, Tone 2, Podoben: "Being the wellspring of loving-kindness" (Милосе́рдїѧ):* Preserved by the precious Cross of Thy Son, O pure Lady Theotokos, we ever valiantly repel every assault of the adversary: therefore, as is our duty, we glorify thee as the Mother of the Light and the only hope of our souls.[^2794]

*After the 3rd Stichology, Sessional Hymn of Sir Theodore, Tone 2, Podoben: "Beholding the beauty of thy virginity" (Красотѣ̀):* Today Lazarus having died is buried, and a lamentation...[^2795]

...sing his kinsfolk; but as Foreseer and God, having beforehand declared His Passion, Thou didst proclaim unto the Disciples: Lazarus is fallen asleep, but now I go to raise up him whom I created! Therefore we all cry unto Thee: Glory to the dominion of Thy might!

*Stavrotheotokion:* The unwedded pure One and Thy Mother, O Christ, beholding Thee hanging dead upon the Tree, weeping maternally, cried aloud: What hath the lawless, ungrateful synagogue of the Hebrews rendered unto Thee in return for Thy many and great gifts, O my Son and Delight? I hymn Thy divine condescension![^2796]

*Triodion Canon of Sir Joseph, Tone 2. Ode 3. Heirmos:* By the power of Thy Cross, establish my mind, which hath grown weak through the assaults of the crafty one, and direct it unto Thy will, O Lord![^2797]

*Troparion:* Awaken me, O Lord, who sleep with the slumber of despondency upon the bed of passions, and show me forth a worshipper of Thy Sufferings![^2798]

*Troparion:* Enlightened in our souls, let us go forth to meet in honorable manner Christ Who comes in the flesh unto Jerusalem![^2799]

*Troparion:* By the malice of the enemy I have put my soul to death, and I lie in the tomb of much despondency: but make haste, O Christ, to raise me up![^2800]

*Theotokion:* O pure Lady who was not burned by the fire of the Godhead, consume the material impulses of my passions, that with faith I may glorify thee, O Maiden![^2801]

*Another Canon of Sir Theodore, Tone 3. Ode 3. Heirmos: "O barren soul" (Непло́дная душѐ):*[^2802]

*Troparion:* Today Lazarus having died hath not been hidden from the all-seeing eye of Jesus: therefore He declares this unto the Disciples, crying: Lazarus our friend is fallen asleep, I go to raise him up![^2803]

*Troparion:* Saying that Thou wouldst go again into Judea, O Lord, Thou didst make the Disciples fearful; but Thomas cried boldly: He is Life, let us go, and even if we die, we shall straightway live![^2804]

*Triadicon:* Consubstantial Trinity, all-ruling Father, co-unoriginate Son, with the enthroned divine Holy Spirit, one adoration, uncreated Godhead: all we men sing unto Thee![^2805]

*Theotokion:* O Virgin Mother all-pure, Root of Jesse, from whom Christ shone forth, the life-bearing Flower for earthborn men, through whom we have been delivered from corruption and death: praising thee, all we earthborn sing unto thee![^2806]

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee!*
*Troparion:* Rejoice now, O Zion: thy King comes meek, as the Prophet cried aloud; and a colt carries Him in the flesh Who holds all things in His hand: we hymn His dominion![^2807]

*Katavasia Heirmos of Sir Theodore, Tone 3:* O barren and childless soul, acquire blessed fruit, and rejoicing cry aloud: I have been established by Thee, O God, there is none holy, and there is none righteous beside Thee, O Lord![^2808]

*Triodion Canon of Sir Joseph, Tone 2. Ode 8. Heirmos: "In the bush" (Въ купинѣ̀):*[^2809]

*Troparion:* Roll away from my humble soul the heavy stone of grievous despondency, O Christ, and raise me up from the tomb of insensibility unto Thy glory, O Word![^2810]

*Troparion:* Thou didst foretell unto Thy friends the death of Thy friend, through tender mercy, O all-foreseeing God, whom Thou wast about to raise from the tomb on the fourth day, unto Thine own doxology.[^2811]

*Troparion:* Thou comest again into Judea, O Christ, which seeks to slay Thee, the Tree of Life, upon a tree, because Thou desirest to make immortal those who were slain through tasting of the tree.[^2812]

*Theotokion:* In thee, O pure Virgin, were truly seen...[^2813]

...the footsteps of God, Who preserved Thy purity after childbearing sealed unto all ages.

*Another Canon of Sir Theodore, Tone 3. Ode 8. Heirmos: "From the Father without mother" (И҆з̾ Ѻ҆тца̀ без̾ ма́тере):*[^2814]

*Troparion:* Lazarus, having died today, is carried out, the friend of Christ; and all that are with Mary and Martha weep: but Christ with joy comes unto him to show unto men that He is the Life of all.[^2815]

*Troparion:* As from the Mount of Olives, cutting branches of virtues from the height of almsgiving, come, O ye people, let us prepare for the spiritual coming of Christ unto us, singing, blessing Him, and supremely exalting Him unto all ages![^2816]

*We bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, the Lord.*
*Triadicon:* Tri-hypostatic Unity, Father, and Son, and living Spirit, one Godhead and one Kingdom: the angelic hosts of unwaning Light praise Thee, and we earthborn sing, bless, and supremely exalt Thee unto all ages![^2817]

*Theotokion:* Behold, all generations call thee blessed, O all-pure Lady, beholding all thy greatness: for beyond nature thou bearest the Creator of all, truly God and man: therefore we bless and supremely exalt thee![^2818]

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee!*
*Troparion:* With the Children let us also go forth to meet Christ God, offering alms instead of palm branches, in contrite heart, crying Hosanna with branches: Bless and supremely exalt Him![^2819]

*Katavasia Heirmos of Sir Theodore, Tone 3:* We praise, we bless, we worship the Lord. God begotten before the ages from the unoriginate Father, and in the latter times clothed in flesh from the Virgin, as perfect man and true God, we sing, bless, and supremely exalt Him unto the ages![^2820]

*Triodion Canon of Sir Joseph, Tone 2. Ode 9. Heirmos: "What earthborn man" (Земноро́дный кто̀):*[^2821]

*Troparion:* Daniel, hedged about by fasting, shut the mouths...[^2822]

...of beasts. Emulating him, O my soul, drive away by the help of the Cross the serpent that roars like a lion, seeking to make every soul his food!

*Troparion:* O Word of God, having raised up by Thy life-giving word my soul slain by sins and shut up in the tomb of transgression: make me worthy, O Conqueror of death, to offer Thee the branches of virtues![^2823]

*Troparion:* Having heaven as His throne and earth as His footstool, the Word of God the Father, carried upon a colt, enters into the Holy City, to bring to perfection from the mouths of infants beauteous praise, as King of all.[^2824]

*Theotokion:* Among women thou alone wast adorned, O all-marvelous pure Lady, having brought forth the most beauteous Word, Who appeared fairer than all the sons of men: pray Him therefore, O Maiden, to cleanse the filth of my heart![^2825]

*Another Canon of Sir Theodore, Tone 3. Ode 9. Heirmos: "Upon Mount Sinai" (На Сїна́йстѣй горѣ̀):*[^2826]

*Troparion:* The sisters of Lazarus pour out tears over his tomb, beholding their kinsman today under the bitter stone: but my Christ, declaring this from afar, said unto His Apostles: I rejoice for your sake that I was not there in the flesh.[^2827]

*Troparion:* Again Christ comes unto Thee, O murderous Judea, desiring as God to accomplish the saving Passion, Whom thou didst seek to kill with stones: behold, He comes unto Thee of His own will, unsummoned, so that He may cut short thy defiled murder.[^2828]

*Triadicon:* Unity in Godhead, and Trinity in nature: O most glorious mystery! United in nature, It is divided in Hypostases; in distinctive manner, without division, It is parted; being a Unity, It is triune: This is the Father...[^2829]

...the Son, and the living Spirit, which preserves all things!

*Theotokion:* Who ever heard of a Virgin giving birth to a Child, and a Mother without a husband? A wonder dost thou accomplish in me! But tell me, how? Search not into the depth of my divine childbearing: for truly this is beyond the comprehension of the human mind![^2830]

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee!*
*Troparion:* Having spiritually woven branches of palm, let us in sensory manner make a meeting for the Master Who comes unto us: for blessed is He that comes in the Name of the Lord, and of the Father as the true Son![^2831]

*Katavasia Heirmos of Sir Theodore, Tone 3:* Upon Mount Sinai, Moses saw thee in the bush, having conceived without being consumed the fire of the Godhead in thy womb; and Daniel saw thee as the uncut Mountain; Isaiah cried aloud: A Rod sprouted from the root of David![^2832]

*Then: "It is truly meet." Exapostilarion of the Tone.*[^2833]

*At the Aposticha, Idiomelon, Tone 4:* Israel was arrayed in purple and scarlet, shining with holy and royal garments, and enriched with the Law and the Prophets, making merry with legal services. But having crucified Thee outside the gates, the Benefactor Who becamest poor, and having rejected Thee Who after the Crucifixion art alive, ever being in the bosom of God the Father, he now thirsts for a drop of grace: even as the merciless rich man, being clad in purple and scarlet, was burning in unquenchable fire, and seeing, he is in pain, beholding the once poor Gentile peoples, who lacked the crumbs of truth, now warmed in the bosom of the faith of Abraham, wearing the purple robe of Thy Blood with the scarlet of Baptism, and being renewed and delighting in Thy gifts, and crying: O Christ our God, glory to Thee![^2834]

*Verse 1:* We were filled in the morning with Thy mercy, and we rejoiced and were glad: *and the same sticheron.* *Verse 2:* And let the brightness of the Lord our God be upon us.[^2835]

*Martyrikon:* Neither tribulation, nor distress, nor famine, nor persecution, nor stripes, nor the rage of wild beasts, nor the sword, nor threatening fire were able to separate you from God, O all-praised martyrs: but rather moved by love toward Him, as if in alien bodies, ye forgot nature and despised death; therefore also according to the worthiness of your afflictions ye have received the reward, and have become heirs of the Kingdom of Heaven: pray ye for our souls![^2836]

*Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion, Tone 1, Podoben: "O all-lauded martyrs" (Прехва́льныи):* Beholding Thee suspended upon the Tree, O Christ, the pure One who bare Thee, O Lover of mankind Who didst suspend the earth upon the waters, cried aloud: Woe is me! What strange sight is this? How hath the solar beauty set, O incomprehensible Son? I magnify Thy mercy, for of Thine own will Thou sufferest for all![^2837]

## ON THE SAME WEDNESDAY, AT THE SIXTH HOUR[^2838]

*Troparion of the Prophecy, Tone 5:* Work Thy mercies with us, O Lord, and deliver us not over unto our iniquities, O Holy Master Almighty: we pray Thee! *Glory... Both now... the same.*[^2839]

*Prokeimenon from Psalm 112, Tone 4:* Praise the Lord, O ye servants, praise the Name of the Lord![^2840] *Verse:* Blessed be the Name of the Lord from this time forth and forevermore.

*Reading from the Prophecy of Isaiah (Chapter 58):*[^2841]
Thus saith the Lord: Cry aloud in strength, and spare not; lift up thy voice as a trumpet, and declare unto My people their sins, and to the house of Jacob their iniquities.[^2842]

Yet they seek Me day by day, and desire to know My ways...[^2843]

...desire, as a people that did righteousness and did not forsake the judgment of their God; they ask of Me now a righteous judgment, and desire to draw near to God,

Saying: Why is it that we have fasted, and Thou hast not seen? We have humbled our souls, and Thou hast not known? For in the days of your fasts your own will is found, and ye drive all your debtors.[^2844]

Ye fast for judgments and strifes, and ye strike the humble with fists; why do ye fast unto Me, so that your voice may be heard today with a cry?[^2845]

Not such a fast have I chosen, and a day for a man to humble his soul; even if thou shouldest bow down thy neck like a sickle, and spread sackcloth and ashes under thee, neither so shall ye call it a fast and an acceptable day.[^2846]

Not such a fast have I chosen, says the Lord, but loose every bond of unrighteousness, loose the entanglements of forced contracts, let the oppressed go free, and tear up every unjust writing of thine.[^2847]

Break thy bread for the hungry, and bring the homeless poor into thy house; if thou seest the naked, clothe him, and hide not thyself from the offspring of thine own seed.[^2848]

Then shall thy light break forth early, and thy healings shall swiftly shine forth; and thy righteousness shall go before thee, and the glory of God shall encompass thee.[^2849]

Then shalt thou call, and God shall hear thee; while thou art yet speaking, He shall say: Behold, here I am.

If thou take away from thee the bond, and the pointing of the hand, and the word of murmuring,

And givest thy bread from thy soul to the hungry, and [satisfy] the soul [humble...][^2850]

...humble soul, and satisfy it; then shall thy light shine forth in darkness, and thy darkness shall be as the noonday:

And thy God shall be with thee continually.

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 113, Tone 6:*
**Reader:** *Blessed are ye of the Lord, Who made heaven and earth.*
**Choir:** *Blessed are ye of the Lord, Who made heaven and earth.*
**Reader:** *Stichos: The heaven of heaven belongs to the Lord, but the earth has He given to the sons of men.*
**Choir:** *Blessed are ye of the Lord, Who made heaven and earth.*[^2851]

## ON THE SAME WEDNESDAY OF THE SIXTH WEEK, AT VESPERS[^2852]

*On "Lord, I have cried," Stichera Idiomela, Tone 5:*
Being rich in passions, I am clothed with the deceitful garment of hypocrisy, taking delight in the evils of intemperance, and showing forth boundless unmercifulness, despising my mind which lies cast down before the doors of repentance, hungering after every good thing, and ailing through my neglectfulness. But do Thou, O Lord, make me a Lazarus poor in sins, lest desiring, I fail to receive a dipped fingertip to cool my tongue which suffers in unquenchable fire; but settle me in the bosom of the Patriarch Abraham, as the Lover of mankind![^2853]

*Martyrikon, Tone 5:*
With insatiable love of soul, ye denied not Christ, O holy martyrs; having endured diverse wounds of sufferings, ye cast down the cruelty of the torturers; having preserved unswerving and unharmed faith, ye were translated unto heaven: therefore, having attained boldness before Him, pray ye that great mercy may be granted unto us![^2854]

*Other [Stichera], by Sir Joseph. Tone 5, Podoben: "Rejoice, O container of ascetics" (Ра́дꙋйся по́стническихъ):*
Walking in the flesh on the other side of the Jordan, O Jesus, Thou didst cry aloud to those who were with Thee: Our friend Lazarus is already dead, and [is given over to burial...][^2855]

...and is given over to burial. Therefore I rejoice for your sakes, my friends, that ye may know that I know all things, being immutable God, even though I appear visible as a man. Let us go therefore and awaken him, that death may know his victory, and the perfect dissolution which I shall accomplish, granting great mercy to the world.

Let us the faithful make ourselves like Martha and Mary, and send godly deeds unto the Lord, that having come, He may raise up our mind, which lies dead, grievously insensible in the tomb of slothfulness, in no wise beholding the divine fear, and having now no life-giving activity, crying aloud: Look, O Lord, even as by a fearful presence Thou didst raise up Thy friend Lazarus, O Thou Who alone art compassionate; so give life unto us all, granting great mercy![^2856]

*Another [Sticheron], by Sir Theodore. Tone 6, Podoben: "Lord, [standing] at the tomb of Lazarus" (Гдⷭ҇и на гро́[бѣ Ла́заревѣ]):*
Lazarus has spent two days in the tomb; he sees those who have died from the beginning of the age; there he beholds strange peoples, an unnumbered multitude, held fast by the bonds of Hades; therefore his kinswomen weep bitterly, seeing his tomb beforehand. But Christ comes to give life unto His friend, to accomplish a single concord of all: Blessed art Thou, O Savior, have mercy upon us![^2857]

*Then, the Martyrikon. And for the rest: as on (see fol. 236)[^2858].*

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 114, Tone 4:*
**Reader:** *I will please the Lord in the land of the living.*
**Choir:** *I will please the Lord in the land of the living.*
**Reader:** *Stichos: I have loved, because the Lord will hear the voice of my supplication.*
**Choir:** *I will please the Lord in the land of the living.*[^2859]

*Genesis Reading (Chapter 43).*[^2860]
[When...][^2861]

The brethren of Joseph brought the gifts which they had in their hands into the house unto him, and bowed down their faces to the earth before him.[^2862]

And he asked them: How are ye? And he said unto them: Is your father in health, the old man of whom ye spoke, is he yet alive?[^2863]

And they said: Thy servant our father is in health, he is yet alive; and he said: Blessed be that man of God; and bowing their heads, they did obeisance unto him.[^2864]

And Joseph, lifting up his eyes, saw Benjamin his brother, his own mother's son, and said: Is this your younger brother, whom ye spoke of bringing unto me? And they said unto him: Yea, this is he. And he said: God have mercy on thee, my child.[^2865]

And Joseph was troubled, for his bowels yearned over his brother, and he sought to weep; and entering into his chamber, he wept there.[^2866]

And having washed his face, he refrained himself.[^2867]

*Chapter 45.*
And Joseph could not refrain himself before all who stood by him; but he said: Send everyone out from me; and there stood no man with Joseph, while he made himself known unto his brethren.[^2868]

And he wept aloud; and all the Egyptians heard, and it was heard in the house of Pharaoh.[^2869]

And Joseph said unto his brethren: I am Joseph; does my father yet live? And his brethren could not answer him, for they were troubled.[^2870]

And Joseph said unto his brethren: Come near to me. And they came near. And he said: I am Joseph your brother, [whom ye sold...][^2871]

...whom ye sold into Egypt.

Now therefore be not grieved, nor let it seem hard unto you, that ye sold me hither: for God sent me before you for life.[^2872]

For this is the second year that famine is upon the earth; and there are yet five other years, in which there shall be neither plowing nor harvest.[^2873]

For God sent me before you to leave you a remnant upon the earth, and to nourish your great remnant.[^2874]

Now therefore it was not you that sent me hither, but God; and He has made me as a father to Pharaoh, and lord of all his house, and ruler over all the land of Egypt.[^2875]

Haste ye therefore, and go up unto my father, and say unto him: Thus says thy son Joseph: God has made me lord of all the land of Egypt; come down unto me, and tarry not.[^2876]

And thou shalt dwell in the land of Goshen of Arabia, and thou shalt be near unto me, thou, and thy sons, and thy sons' sons, and thy sheep, and thine oxen, and all that thou hast.[^2877]

And I will nourish thee there; for yet five years the famine shall be upon the earth, lest thou be consumed, thou, and thy sons, and all that thou hast.[^2878]

Behold, your eyes see, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin, that it is my mouth that speaks unto you.[^2879]

Tell my father therefore of all my glory that is in Egypt, and of all that ye have seen; and make haste, and bring down my father hither.[^2880]

And falling upon the neck of Benjamin his brother, he wept; and Benjamin wept upon his neck.[^2881]

And Joseph kissed all his brethren, and wept over them; and after these things [his brethren talked...][^2882]

...his brethren talked with him.

And the voice was proclaimed in the house of Pharaoh, saying: The brethren of Joseph are come; and Pharaoh rejoiced, and all his servants.[^2883]

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 115, Tone 4:*
**Reader:** *I will pay my vows unto the Lord in the presence of all His people.*
**Choir:** *I will pay my vows unto the Lord in the presence of all His people.*
**Reader:** *Stichos: I believed, therefore have I spoken; but I was humbled exceedingly.*
**Choir:** *I will pay my vows unto the Lord in the presence of all His people.*[^2884]

*Proverbs Reading (Chapter 21).*[^2885]
He that keeps his mouth and his tongue preserves his soul from grief.[^2886]

The bold, and insolent, and boastful is called a pestilence; and he that remembers injuries is a transgressor.[^2887]

The lusts of the sluggard kill him, for his hands choose not to do anything.[^2888]

The ungodly desires evil desires all the day; but the righteous shows mercy and pities unsparingly.[^2889]

The sacrifices of the ungodly are an abomination to the Lord, for they offer them unlawfully.[^2890]

A false witness shall perish; but an obedient man speaks cautiously.[^2891]

An ungodly man impudently hardens his face; but the upright himself understands his ways.[^2892]

There is no wisdom, there is no courage, there is no counsel in an ungodly man.[^2893]

A horse is prepared for the day of battle, but help is from the Lord.[^2894]

*Chapter 22.*
A good name is more desirable than great riches, and good favor more than silver and gold.[^2895]

The rich and the poor meet together: the Lord made them both.[^2896]

A prudent man, seeing a wicked man severely punished, is himself instructed; but fools passing by [are punished...][^2897]

...passing by are punished.

The offspring of wisdom is the fear of the Lord, and riches, and glory, and life.[^2898]

*Then: "Let my prayer arise," and the rest of the Liturgy of the Presanctified Gifts.[^2899] But where there is no Presanctified [Liturgy], see the Rubric, (see fol. 240)[^2900].*

## ON THURSDAY OF THE SIXTH WEEK OF THE FAST, AT MATINS[^2901]

*After Alleluia, the Hymns to the Trinity of the Tone. After the 1st Stichology, the Sessional Hymn in the Oktoechos.*
*After the 2nd Stichology, Sessional Hymn of Sir Joseph. Tone 5, Podoben: "The Word co-unoriginate" (Собезнача́льное [Сло́во]):*
Having yoked contemplation and action together, let us make haste to send forth unto Christ's mercy our mind which has died, like another Lazarus, that He may give it life by His fearful presence, to bring unto Him branches of righteousness, and to cry: Blessed is He that comes in the Name of the Lord![^2902]

*Glory... the same. Both now... Theotokion:*
Heal swiftly the many-painful passions of my soul and the illnesses of my flesh, O all-immaculate one; quench the perversities of my mind, and in tranquility of thought, vouchsafe me, O Mother of God, to offer pure prayers unto the King of all, and to ask remission of sins![^2903]

*After the 3rd Stichology, Sessional Hymn of Sir Theodore. Tone 6, Podoben: "The Angelic Powers" (А҆́ггелскїя си́лы):*
Lazarus who died has spent two days [in the tomb] today, and over him his kinswomen, Mary [with Martha...][^2904]

...with Martha, pour out tears of sorrow, seeing beforehand the gravestone; the Creator with His disciples has come to take death captive, granting life; therefore we cry aloud unto Him: O Lord, glory to Thee!

*Glory... the same. Both now... Theotokion:*
O Holy Lady, Mother of our God, as having ineffably given birth unto Him, the Creator of all, pray with the holy Apostles unto His goodness everywhere, that He may deliver us from passions, and grant us remission of iniquities![^2905]

*Triodion, by Sir Joseph. Tone 2, Ode 4. Heirmos: Perceiving Thy divine [emptying]...*[^2906]
*Troparion:*
With the ray of your consolation, enlighten those who are shut up in the shadow of sin, O ye light-bearers, Apostles who piously praise you![^2907]

*Troparion:*
Having yoked the days together with compassion, let us the faithful make haste to send them forth unto Christ for supplication, that He may raise us also up from the tomb of our secret passions![^2908]

*Troparion:*
Let us not spare carnal love which has put the soul to death, and let us cleave with love unto the Redeemer, that He may deliver us from the fearful condemnation of Hades![^2909]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst foretell the falling asleep of Lazarus, whom after a little while having raised, Thou didst receive praise from the flower-bearing youths, prefiguring Thy divine passions, O my Savior![^2910]

*Theotokion:*
The divine water of immortality and life has poured forth from thee, O all-immaculate Mother of God, tasting whereof, O pure one, they are delivered from deadly thirst![^2911]

*Another [Canon], by Sir Theodore. Tone 6, Ode 4. Heirmos: I have heard, O Lord, the report of Thee...*[^2912]
*Troparion:*
Lazarus is buried; and at the tomb those with Martha now weep and lament, desiring to stand before Thee, the Giver of life.[^2913]

*Troparion:*
Death begins to flee, knowing Thy descent unto it, O Christ; for Thou hast shown forth ageless life unto the ends of the earth![^2914]

*Triadicon:*
O simple Unity, uncreated, unoriginate in essence, hymned in Trinity of Persons: save us who in faith bow down before Thy dominion![^2915]

*Theotokion:*
Thou hast given birth in time unto the ageless Son of the Father, O Mother of God, without knowing man—a strange wonder!—remaining ever a Virgin![^2916]

*Troparion:*
*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*
Assemble yourselves, come ye that are in the wildernesses and caves, to meet Him Who comes upon a colt, speaking of His glory in hymns![^2917]

*Katavasia Heirmos:*
*I have heard, O Lord, the report of Thee, and I was afraid; I understood Thy works, and was filled with wonder. Glory to Thy power, O Lord!*[^2918]

*Ode 8. Heirmos: Unto Thee the Creator of all...*[^2919]
*Troparion:*
Entreat the all-compassionate One to take away the heavy stone from my heart, O ye God-preaching Apostles of the Lord, who have shown yourselves to be stones of the Cornerstone![^2920]

*Troparion:*
Let us go, He proclaimed unto His friends: My friend Lazarus already sleeps; I will raise him up, putting to sleep the all-destructive malice of death unto ages![^2921]

*Troparion:*
Being meek in soul and humble in disposition through grace, let us receive the meek Master of all Who comes to crush the pride of the crafty one![^2922]

*Theotokion:*
The Prophet sees thee, O all-immaculate one, as an enlightened Gate of Light; for thou dost ineffably give birth unto the Giver of light, Who made Himself like unto us, Whom we exalt unto all ages![^2923]

*Another [Canon], by Sir Theodore. Ode 8. Heirmos: Thy venerable Children...*[^2924]

*Troparion:*
Mary and Martha now weep, seeing Lazarus lying in the tomb, and painfully they cry aloud: If Christ had been here, our kinsman had not died![^2925]

*Troparion:*
Hades expects to be destroyed, for Life comes, crying aloud to raise up Lazarus: Bless and praise [the Lord]![^2926]

*Triadicon:*
*We bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, the Lord.*
By unoriginateness, and by begetting, and by procession: unto the Father Who begot I bow down, the Son Who was begotten I glorify, and the Holy Spirit Who proceeds from the Father, co-equal with the Father and the Son, I sing![^2927]

*Theotokion:*
Cease not ever to entreat Him Whom thou hast ineffably borne, O Virgin, as the Lover of mankind, that He may save from perils those who flee unto thee![^2928]

*Troparion:*
*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*
Let us prepare virtues as branches, and as palms, for the meeting of the King Christ, crying aloud: Bless, praise, and highly exalt Him unto all ages![^2929]

*Katavasia Heirmos:*
*We praise, bless, and worship the Lord, saying:*
*Thy venerable Children in the furnace were made like unto the Cherubim, crying aloud the Thrice-Holy hymn: Bless, praise, and highly exalt [the Lord] unto all ages!*[^2930]

*Ode 9. Heirmos: Rejoice, O Isaiah...*[^2931]
*Troparion:*
Deliver me from deceitful friendship, O Master Christ, Who didst show forth Thine own disciples as friends, with whom having gone, Thou didst raise up Thy friend, faithful Lazarus, O Savior, who piously praise Thee![^2932]

*Troparion:*
At the completion of the Fast, O Lord, fill our hearts and mind with joy, O compassionate One, through the prayers of Thine Apostles who purely loved Thee, the Savior of our souls![^2933]

*Troparion:*
Bound with the evil cords [of sin], I live in the tomb of slothfulness...[^2934]

...of slothfulness, O Christ; therefore I pray Thee: raise me up, that I also, with branches of virtues, may meet Thee, crying: Hosanna to God![^2935]

*Theotokion:*
In two wills and essences hast thou given birth for us unto the Father's only-begotten Son, O Virgin, Who became man, that the supremely divine One might show us to be partakers of the divine nature, O most pure one![^2936]

*Another [Canon], by Sir Theodore. Tone 6, Ode 9. Heirmos: Conception without seed...*[^2937]
*Troparion:*
Lazarus spends a second day in the tomb today, and over him Mary and Martha shed tears as his devoted sisters; but Christ comes unto him with the divine Apostles, to show forth a great sign![^2938]

*Troparion:*
O all-destructive death, receive thou dissolution, and let thy gatekeepers watch the bolts; for Christ shall crush thy gates like a thunderbolt, having raised up Lazarus; drink this first, O Hades! The Prophet cries aloud to thee with us![^2939]

*Triadicon:*
O Father of the One, Sole Begetter of the only-begotten Son; and O One of the One, Light, Radiance of the Light; and Thou alone One of the One God, Holy Spirit of the Lord, truly being the Lord: O Holy Trinity, Unity, save me who theologize Thee![^2940]

*Theotokion:*
The wonder of thy childbearing astonishes me, O all-immaculate one: how dost thou conceive without seed Him Who cannot be contained? How alone dost thou remain a virgin having given birth as a mother? Accepting with faith that which is above nature, bow down to Him Who is born, for whatsoever He wills, He also can do![^2941]

*Troparion:*
*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*
The Lord comes to sit upon a colt, even as it is written. Ye peoples, prepare yourselves with fear to receive the King of all...[^2942]

...with palms, as the Conqueror of death, Who raised Lazarus from Hades![^2943]

*Katavasia Heirmos:*
*The ineffable birthgiving of a conception without seed, of an unwedded Mother; the corruption-free reception of God renews nature in birthgiving; therefore all generations orthodoxly magnify thee as the Bride of God and Mother!*[^2944]
*Then: It is truly meet... Say the Exapostilarion.*

*At the Aposticha, Idiomelon, Tone 5:*
Come before the end, all ye brethren; let us draw near to the merciful God with a pure heart; having cast aside worldly cares, let us take care for our souls; through abstinence let us hate the sweetness of foods; let us apply ourselves to almsgiving, for through this, even as it is written, some unawares entertained Angels. Let us feed the poor for the sake of Him Who fed us with His flesh; let us clothe ourselves in Him Who covers Himself with light as with a garment; that through the prayers of the all-immaculate Mother of God and Virgin Mother, we may obtain remission of transgressions, crying aloud unto Him with compunction: O Lord, deliver us from that [dreadful] answer, and make us worthy to stand at Thy right hand, as Thou art merciful and the Lover of mankind![^2945]

*Verse 1:* We were filled in the morning with Thy mercy, O Lord...[^2946] *And again the same [Sticheron].*
*Verse 2:* And let the brightness of the Lord our God be upon us...
*Martyrikon:*
Being in torments, the holy ones cried aloud, rejoicing: This is our commerce with the Master: instead of present bodily wounds, radiant raiment blossoms forth for us in the resurrection; for reproach, crowns; for prison bonds, Paradise; for condemnation to death with evildoers, the life of Angels. Therefore by their prayers, O Lord, save our souls![^2947]

*Glory... both now... Theotokion.*[^2948]

Chosen out of all generations, give ear unto our voice, and grant the requests of our souls, deliverance from passions and sicknesses, for the sake of the Apostles, O thou who canst do all things as the Mother of God![^2949]
*Then: It is good to give praise unto the Lord...*[^2950]

## ON THE SAME THURSDAY, AT THE SIXTH HOUR[^2951]

*Troparion of the Prophecy, Tone 7:*
Forget not the voices of Thy suppliants, O Lord; remember that we have ever placed our trust in Thee, the Almighty, and help us, O Merciful One![^2952]
*Glory... End: and help us, O Merciful One. Both now... the whole [Troparion].*

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 117, Tone 4:*
**Reader:** *This is the gate of the Lord: the righteous shall enter into it.*
**Choir:** *This is the gate of the Lord: the righteous shall enter into it.*
**Reader:** *Stichos: Give thanks unto the Lord, for He is good.*
**Choir:** *This is the gate of the Lord: the righteous shall enter into it.*[^2953]

*Reading from the Prophecy of Isaiah (Chapter 65:8–16):*[^2954]
Thus says the Lord: In the manner that a berry is found in a grape-cluster, and they say: Destroy it not, for a blessing of the Lord is in it; so will I do for the sake of him that serves Me; for his sake I will not destroy all. [8][^2955]

And I will bring forth a seed out of Jacob and out of Judah, and it shall inherit My holy mountain; and My chosen ones and My servants shall inherit it, and shall dwell there. [9]

And there shall be folds for flocks in the woodland pasture, and the valley of Achor shall be a resting-place of herds for My people who have sought Me. [10]

But as for you that have forsaken Me, and that forget My holy mountain, and prepare a table for the demon, and fill a mingled cup for Fortune: [11]

I will deliver you up to the sword; ye all shall [fall by slaughter...][^2956]

...fall by slaughter; because I called you, and ye gave no ear; I spoke, and ye refused to hear, and did evil before Me, and chose that wherein I delighted not. [12]

Therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, they that serve Me shall eat, but ye shall hunger; behold, they that serve Me shall drink, [13]

But ye shall thirst; behold, they that serve Me shall make merry, [14]

But ye shall be ashamed; behold, they that serve Me shall exult in gladness of heart, but ye shall cry aloud for sorrow of your heart, and [15]

Shall wail for crushing of your spirit. For your name shall be left for a fullness unto My chosen; [16]

And the Lord God shall slay you, but unto them that serve Me shall a new name be given, which shall be blessed upon the earth: for they shall bless the true God![^2957]

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 118, Tone 4:*
**Reader:** *I have run the way of Thy commandments, when Thou didst enlarge my heart.*
**Choir:** *I have run the way of Thy commandments, when Thou didst enlarge my heart.*
**Reader:** *Stichos: Set before me for a law the way of Thy statutes, O Lord.*
**Choir:** *I have run the way of Thy commandments, when Thou didst enlarge my heart.*[^2958]
*Then: Let Thy tender mercies speedily anticipate us...*

## ON THE SAME THURSDAY OF PALM WEEK, AT VESPERS[^2959]

*On "Lord, I have cried," Stichera of Sir Joseph.*
*Tone 4, Podoben: "Being called from on high" (Зва́нный свы́ше):*
Knowing Thee, O Christ, as the One of the Trinity, the sacred pair of Apostles is now sent by Thee to bring the colt, the foal of an ass, even as it is written, whereon sitting in Thy lowliness, O compassionate One, Who by Thy will hast prepared the seat on high for all that love Thee, Thou makest them that were bowed down under brute irrational passions to become rational, crying aloud unto Thee: Hosanna![^2960]

Receive the King, O Zion: behold, the most meek One comes willingly unto thee, Who raised Lazarus and overthrew the bitter kingdom of death! O God-chosen multitude of holy monastics, assemble yourselves with the simple children, to meet Christ with palms, crying aloud: Blessed is He that comes to save the human race through the suffering of the Cross, and to grant dispassion unto all according to His grace![^2961]

*Another [Sticheron], by Sir Theodore. Tone 8, Podoben: "In Eden of old" (И҆́же въ є҆де́мѣ):*
Borne in the heights upon the awesome Seraphim, O Christ, as both God and Creator of all: Thou Thyself goest upon the earth to sit upon a colt, as having human nature for our sake. Bethany is glad, having received Thee, O Savior; Jerusalem rejoices, as receiving Thee for Whom she hoped; death is slain, foreknowing that Lazarus is to be raised from the dead; and we, accomplishing the meeting with palms in joy, hymn the dominion of Thy goodness, O Lord![^2962]
*Then, 6 [stichera] from the Menaion.*
*Glory... both now... Theotokion.*

*Evening Prokeimenon, Psalm 119, Tone 6:*
**Reader:** *Unto the Lord, when I was in affliction, I cried, and He heard me.*
**Choir:** *Unto the Lord, when I was in affliction, I cried, and He heard me.*
**Reader:** *Stichos: O Lord, deliver my soul from unjust lips, and from a deceitful tongue.*
**Choir:** *Unto the Lord, when I was in affliction, I cried, and He heard me.*[^2963]

*Reading from Genesis (Chapter 46:1–7):*[^2964]
Israel himself set out, and all that he had, and came to the Well of the Oath, and offered sacrifice there unto the God of his father Isaac. [1]

And God spoke unto Israel in a vision of the night, saying: Jacob, Jacob! And he said: What is it? [2]

And He said unto him: [3][^2965] ...I am the God of thy fathers; fear not to go down into Egypt, for I will make thee into a great nation there. [3]

And I will go down with thee into Egypt, and I will bring thee up at the end; and Joseph shall put his hands upon thine eyes. [4]

And Jacob rose up from the Well of the Oath; and the sons of Jacob took Israel their father, and their goods, and their wives, upon the wagons which Joseph had sent to carry him. [5]

And having taken all their possessions, and all the wealth which they had acquired in the land of Canaan, they entered into Egypt: Jacob, and all his seed with him: [6]

His sons, and his sons' sons with him, his daughters, and his daughters' daughters; and all his seed he brought into Egypt. [7][^2966]

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 120, Tone 6:*
**Reader:** *The Lord shall preserve thee from all evil, the Lord shall preserve thy soul.*
**Choir:** *The Lord shall preserve thee from all evil, the Lord shall preserve thy soul.*
**Reader:** *Stichos: I have lifted up mine eyes unto the mountains, whence comes my help.*
**Choir:** *The Lord shall preserve thee from all evil, the Lord shall preserve thy soul.*[^2967]

*Reading from Proverbs (Chapter 23:15–24:5):*[^2968]
My son, if thy heart be wise, thou shalt gladden my heart also; [15]

And thy lips shall converse with my lips, if they be right. [16]

Let not thine heart envy sinners, but be in the fear of the Lord all the day; [17]

For if thou keep these things, thou shalt have an offspring, and thine expectation shall not depart. [18]

Hear, my son, and be wise, and direct the thoughts of thy heart. [19]

Be not a wine-bibber, neither stretch thyself out with feasts and buyings of flesh: [20][^2969] ...for every drunkard and whoremonger shall become poor; and every slumberer shall clothe himself with torn rags and tatters. [21]

Give ear unto thy father that begot thee, and despise not thy mother when she is old. [22]

Acquire truth, and reject not wisdom, instruction, and understanding. [23]

A righteous father trains up his child well; and over a wise son his soul rejoices. [24]

Let thy father and thy mother rejoice over thee, and let her that bore thee be glad! [25]

My son, give me thine heart, and let thine eyes observe my ways. [26]

For a strange house is a broken vessel, and a strange well is narrow. [27]

For such shall perish quickly, and every transgressor shall be consumed. [28]

To whom is woe? To whom is tumult? To whom are lawsuits? To whom are brawlings and quarreling? To whom are wounds without cause? Whose eyes are livid? [29]

Are they not theirs that tarry long at wine, and watch where banquets are held? [30]

Be not drunken with wine, but converse with righteous men, and converse in public gatherings. For if thou set thine eyes upon bowls and cups, afterwards thou shalt go about naked as a mortar. [31]

And at the last he stretches himself out as one bitten by a serpent, and his venom is diffused as by a horned viper. [32]

When thine eyes shall behold a strange woman, then thy mouth shall speak perverse things. [33]

And thou shalt lie as in the heart of the sea, and as a steersman in a great wave. [34]

And thou shalt say: They smote me, and I was not hurt; and they mocked me, and I knew it not; when will it be morning, that I may go and seek them with whom I may keep company? [35][^2970] My son, envy not evil men, neither desire to be with them; [1]

For their heart meditates falsehood, and their lips speak troubles. [2]

With wisdom a house is built, and with understanding it is established; [3]

And by knowledge the storehouses are filled with all precious and good wealth. [4]

A wise man is better than a strong man; and a man possessing prudence than a great husbandman. [5][^2971]
*Then: Vouchsafe, O Lord...*

*At the Aposticha, Sticheron Idiomelon, Tone 8:*
From the likeness of the rich and unmerciful man, and from an ungenerous disposition, deliver me, O Christ God, Who by Thy Cross didst make purification for our sins; and show me forth as an emulator of the thankful endurance of poor Lazarus, and alienate me not from the bosom of the Patriarch Abraham, for the sake of Thy great mercy![^2972]

*Verse 1:* Unto Thee have I lifted up mine eyes...[^2973] *And again the same Sticheron.*
*Verse 2:* Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us...
*Martyrikon:*
O Martyrs of the Lord, ye sanctify every place and heal every sickness; and now pray ye, we beseech you, that our souls may be delivered from the snares of the enemy![^2974]

*Glory... both now... Stavrotheotokion. Tone 8, Podoben: "O most marvelous wonder" (Ѡ пресла́вное чꙋ́до):*
O most marvelous wonder! O awesome mystery! O fearful undertaking! cried the Virgin, when she saw Thee hanging upon the Cross between two thieves; she that without pain fearfully bore Thee wept, saying: Woe is me, most beloved Child! How has an ungrateful assembly painfully nailed Thee to the Cross![^2975]

## ON FRIDAY OF THE SIXTH WEEK OF THE HOLY FAST[^2976]

*At Matins: After Alleluia, the Trinity Hymns in the Tone. After the 1st Stichology, Sessional Hymns in the Oktoechos. After the 2nd Stichology:*
*Sessional Hymn of Sir Joseph. Tone 4, Podoben: "Speedily anticipate" (Ско́рѡ предварѝ):*
A pair of disciples is sent to bring the colt, even as it is written, whereon Christ, having mounted, shall enter in beauty, to receive divine praise from infants. Therefore let us eagerly go to meet Him, bringing unto Him the branches of virtues by our deeds![^2977]
*Glory... the same. Both now... Stavrotheotokion:*
O all-hymned Virgin, Mother of Christ God, a sword pierced through thine all-holy soul when thou sawest Thy Son and God voluntarily crucified; Whom cease not to entreat, O blessed one, that He may grant unto us remission of sins in the season of the Fast![^2978]

*After the 3rd Stichology, Sessional Hymn of Sir Theodore. Tone 4, Podoben: "Having risen from the dead" (Въскрⷭ҇съ и҆ме́:):*
A pair of disciples is sent today to bring the colt unto the Master of all; He comes to sit upon it, Who is borne by the multitudes of Seraphim; He begins to make manifest unto the human race the One Who first took captive through Lazarus all-destroying death, ruler of the world![^2979]
*Glory... the same. Both now... Stavrotheotokion:*
Standing by the cross of her Son, the pure one wept bitterly, crying aloud with songs: How have the Hebrew children brought Thee, O Son, to the judgment seat of Pilate—Thee Who art unceasingly glorified with angelic hymns? I sing praise unto Thy manifold and ineffable tender mercy![^2980]

*Triode Canon, by Sir Joseph. Tone 4, Ode 5. Heirmos: Shine forth upon me, O Lord, the light...*[^2981]

*Troparion:*
Having fallen asleep upon Thy Cross, O Lord, Thou didst turn death into sleep, O Master; for Thou didst cry aloud: Our friend Lazarus sleeps, but let us go to awaken him now![^2982]

*Troparion:*
Fulfilling the prophecies of the Prophets' preaching, Thou hast come, O compassionate Christ, unto the prophet-slaying city, voluntarily to be slain, saving those slain by corruption![^2983]

*Troparion:*
Subjecting the corruptible body unto the mind through fasting and prayers, ye monks and simple people, meet Christ Who sits upon a colt and comes to suffer![^2984]

*Theotokion:*
With the sprinkling of thy mercy water my mind, O all-immaculate one, which is dried up by the flame of sin, and rekindle the extinguished lamp of my heart, O Gate of Light![^2985]

*Another [Canon], by Sir Theodore. Tone 8, Ode 5. Heirmos: Dispel the darkness of my soul...*[^2986]
*Troparion:*
When Thou wast about to reach Bethany, O Christ, Thou dost send a pair of Thy disciples to bring Thee the colt whereon no man ever sat; for except Thee, O Savior, none has subdued the irrational nations.[^2987]

*Troparion:*
A multitude of Judeans came together from Jerusalem unto Bethany, and today they mourn with the kinswomen of Lazarus; but on the morrow, perceiving that he has leaped forth from the tomb, they are stirred up to murder Christ.[^2988]

*Triadicon:*
O all-immaculate Trinity, Father, Son, and all-creating Spirit, blessed Godhead, unoriginate Essence, Tri-radiant Light, Almighty Power: preserve Thy servants![^2989]

*Theotokion:*
Beholding Thee unjustly nailed to the Cross, O Christ, she that bore Thee, seeing the blood and water flowing from Thy life-bearing ribs, was consumed with motherly compassion; for she knew Thee as her Son![^2990]

*Troparion:*
*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*
[Redouble...][^2991]

...Behold, Christ has prepared Himself to stand before Jerusalem; all ye who dwell in the mountains and in the deserts, assemble yourselves, ye monks, to meet Him with joy, with all your branch-bearing![^2992]

*Heirmos:*
*Dispel the darkness of my soul, O Giver of light, Christ God, Who didst drive away the prince of darkness from the depths of the abyss; and grant unto me the light of Thy commandments, O Word, that waking at dawn I may glorify Thee!*[^2993]

*Ode 8. Heirmos: Earth and all that is therein...*[^2994]

*Troparion:*
Having the resurrection and the life, why weep ye bitterly, O affectionate women? He goes to revive His close friend, by His resurrection proclaiming the rising of all, the only Benefactor![^2995]

*Troparion:*
Open wide, ye dwellings of monks, as sheep endowed with reason! Go to meet Christ the Chief Shepherd, bearing branches; for the Lord comes voluntarily to be slaughtered as a lamb, that He may deliver the sheep from the tormentor![^2996]

*Troparion:*
When Thou wast drawing near to Bethany, Hades, the enemy, perceived the tread of Thy feet; and touching the feet of Lazarus, he said: If the Life will call thee, hesitate not, but come forth; for I have perceived my speedy destruction![^2997]

*Theotokion:*
Sacred voices of the Prophets proclaim thee figuratively: Door, and Mountain, and Shadow, Holy Earth, Radiant Cloud, from whom upon them that are in darkness and sitting in the shadow, has shone forth the Sun of righteousness, O Virgin, the only Giver of light![^2998]

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos: Angels and the heavens upon the throne...*[^2999]

*Troparion:*
A pair of disciples is sent to bring the colt unto Him Who sits upon the clouds, Whom they hymn and supremely exalt unto the ages![^3000]

*Troparion:*
Christ is at the doors; henceforth weep not, O Bethany; for He will turn thy weeping into joy, having raised up Lazarus, thy child, from the tomb, singing and supremely exalting Christ unto the ages![^3001]

*Let us bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit: the Lord.*

*Triadicon:*
One God indeed is the Trinity: neither the Father proceeding into Sonship, nor the Son changing into procession; but properly and distinctly, the Light of God, I glorify the Three unto the ages![^3002]

*Theotokion:*
Thou alone corruptionlessly givest birth; thou alone dost nurse an Infant, being unwedded; thou alone givest birth to the Creator and thy Master, although both Mother and handmaid: we hymn thee, O Virgin, unto the ages![^3003]

*Troparion:*
*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*
With plantations of virtues, and sensibly with branches, as twofold let us all prepare to receive Christ, borne upon a colt, Whom we supremely exalt unto all ages![^3004]

*We praise, bless, and worship the Lord, singing the Heirmos:*
*Ye Angels and Heavens, bless, hymn, and supremely exalt unto all ages Him Who sits upon the throne of glory, and is unceasingly glorified as God!*[^3005]

*Ode 9. Heirmos: For He that is mighty has done to me...*[^3006]

*Troparion:*
Behold, He has proclaimed beforehand: We go up with Jesus to the Holy City; into the hands of murderers I shall truly be betrayed to the Cross, and I shall be slain in the flesh![^3007]

*Troparion:*
Desiring to snatch Thy friend from death, O Word, Thou art nailed to be slain in the flesh for our sake, making faithful men immortal, O Thou Who alone art immortal![^3008]

*Troparion:*
Let us bring branches of chastity unto Christ, riding in the flesh upon a colt, and let us say unto Him: Blessed art Thou, O Savior, Who hast come unto the Passion![^3009]

*Theotokion:*
Awesome is thy childbearing, O Mother of God, Mother of Christ; therefore...[^3010]

...therefore all generations of generations faithfully bless thee and purely glorify thee unto ages. Amen.[^3011]

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos: That which was made manifest upon the mountain...*[^3012]

*Troparion:*
Now sending the disciples, Christ said: Having untied the colt for Me, bring it for Me to sit upon, that I may break down the irrationality of the nations, and subdue them as the Son to the Father![^3013]

*Troparion:*
The Lord comes: open thy doors, O Bethany; receive the Master with faith, for He comes to raise Lazarus, as the only Almighty One![^3014]

*Triadicon:*
The tri-radiant Godhead of Thy monarchy, illuminating our mind with radiant splendors, turns it away from manifold delusion unto deification in union with Thee.[^3015]

*Theotokion:*
Rejoice, Palace of the King of all, through whom the Heavenly Kingdom was opened unto them that are upon earth, O Virgin Mother of God, and dwelling with the Angels![^3016]

*Troparion:*
*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*
Ye that are in deserts, and mountains, and dens, come, gather yourselves together with us bearing branches, to meet the King and Master, for He comes to save our souls![^3017]

*Katavasia Heirmos:*
