*That which was made manifest upon the Mountain to the Lawgiver through fire and the bush: the birthgiving of her that has come for the salvation of us faithful, with unceasing hymns we magnify!*[^3018]

*Then: It is truly meet... Say the Exapostilarion, Tone 2.*[^3019]

*At the Aposticha, Stichera Idiomela, Tone 1. The work of Emperor Leo:*
Having set at naught the divine unctions, O my soul, thou wast cast out through the wiles of the enemy, voluntarily surrendering thyself to corruption; and having lost thy senses through manifold sin, thou hast defiled the God-woven garment, and rendered it unready for the royal wedding; but that thou mayest not be dragged away with sin, and called covered...[^3020]

...called covered with the garment of passions, and deprived of the entrance of the righteous, and cast out from the bridal chamber, cry aloud unto the Savior: O awesome Eye, Who didst take what I am and didst not leave what Thou wast, and Who before the Cross wast clothed in the cloak of mockery for my sake: tear asunder my sackcloth, and clothe me in gladness, and deliver me from outer darkness and eternal weeping, and have mercy on me![^3021]

*Verse 1: We were filled in the morning with Thy mercy, O Lord, and we rejoiced and were glad. Verse 2: And let the brightness of the Lord our God be upon us, and the works of our hands do Thou direct upon us; yea, the work of our hands do Thou direct.*

*Martyrikon:*
Come, all ye peoples, let us honor the Passion-bearers of Christ with hymns and spiritual songs, the beacons of the world and preachers of the faith, the ever-flowing springs whence healings stream forth unto the faithful: by their prayers, O Christ our God, grant peace unto Thy world, and unto our souls great mercy![^3022]

*Glory... Tone 8:*
Having accomplished the Forty Days that profit the soul, we pray to see the Holy Week of Thy Passion, O Lover of mankind, that we may glorify therein Thy marvelous deeds, and Thine ineffable dispensation for us, crying aloud with one mind: O Lord, glory to Thee![^3023]

*Both now... the same.*

*Then: It is good to give praise unto the Lord... Trisagion. After Our Father, the First Troparion. And the Dismissal.*[^3024]

## ON FRIDAY OF THE SIXTH WEEK OF THE FAST, AT THE SIXTH HOUR[^3025]

*Troparion of the Prophecy, Tone 3:*
Invincible is the wrath of Thy threat against sinners, O Lord, and we are not worthy to gaze upward and ask mercy of Thee; yet destroy us not in Thine anger nor in Thy wrath, whom Thou didst fashion from the earth with Thine own hand![^3026]

*Glory... the end: Destroy us not... Both now... the whole Troparion.*

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 121, Tone 4:*
**Reader:** *For the sake of the house of the Lord our God, I sought good things for thee.*
**Choir:** *For the sake of the house of the Lord our God, I sought good things for thee.*
**Reader:** *Stichos: I was glad because of them that said unto me: We will go into the house of the Lord.*
**Choir:** *For the sake of the house of the Lord our God, I sought good things for thee.*[^3027]

*Reading from the Prophecy of Isaiah (Chapter 66:10–24):*[^3028]
Rejoice, O Jerusalem, and keep festival in her, all ye that love her and dwell in her; rejoice together with her joy, all ye that mourn over her: [10]

That ye may suck and be satisfied from the breast of her consolation; that having milked out, ye may delight yourselves from the influx of her glory. [11]

For thus says the Lord: Behold, I incline peace upon them like a river, and like a flooding torrent the glory of the Gentiles; their children shall be carried upon shoulders, and be comforted upon knees. [12]

As a mother comforts whomsoever, so will I comfort you, and in Jerusalem shall ye be comforted. [13]

And ye shall see, and your heart shall rejoice, and your bones shall flourish like grass; and the hand of the Lord shall be known unto them that fear Him, and He shall threaten the adversaries. [14]

For behold, the Lord shall come like fire, and His chariots like a whirlwind, to render His vengeance in fury, and His rebuke in a flame of fire. [15]

For with the fire of the Lord shall all the earth be judged, [16a]

And all flesh with His sword; many shall be the slain of the Lord. [16b]

They that consecrate and purify themselves in the gardens and in the outer porches, eating swine's flesh, and abominations, and the unclean thing, shall perish together, says the Lord. [17][^3029] And I know their works and their imagination; and I am coming to gather all nations and tongues; and they shall come and see My glory. [18]

And I will leave a sign upon them, and I will send forth the saved of them unto the nations: to Tarshish, and Pul, and Lud, and Meshech, and Tubal, and Hellas, and unto the isles afar off, that have not heard My Name, neither have seen My glory; and they shall declare My glory among the Gentiles. [19]

And they shall bring your brethren out of all nations as an offering unto the Lord, with horses and chariots, in canopied litters with mules, unto the Holy City Jerusalem, says the Lord, as though the children of Israel should offer their sacrifices unto Me with gladness and with psalms in the house of the Lord. [20]

And of them will I take for priests and Levites, says the Lord. [21]

For in the manner that the new heaven and the new earth which I make remain before Me, says the Lord, so shall your seed and your name stand. [22]

And it shall come to pass from month to month, and from Sabbath to Sabbath, all flesh shall come to worship before Me in Jerusalem, says the Lord. [23]

And they shall go forth, and look upon the carcasses of the men that have transgressed against Me; for their worm shall not die, and their fire shall not be quenched; and they shall be a spectacle unto all flesh. [24][^3030]

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 122, Tone 6:*
**Reader:** *Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us.*
**Choir:** *Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us.*
**Reader:** *Stichos: Unto Thee have I lifted up mine eyes, unto Thee that dwellest in heaven.*
**Choir:** *Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us.*[^3031]

---

# PART III: APPENDICES: HYMNS TO THE TRINITY, SESSIONAL HYMNS, AND PHOTAGOGIKA OF THE EIGHT TONES

## HYMNS TO THE TRINITY IN THE EIGHT TONES[^3032]

*(These are sung in the Holy Great Fast, and in the other Fasts, when we do not sing: "God is the Lord," nor the Troparion, but "Alleluia" with its stichoi: "From night my spirit wakes at dawn unto Thee, O God..." and so forth. Look on Friday of the 1st Week of the Fast, (see fol. 173)[^3033], in the current Tone of the Oktoechos.)*

*Hymns to the Trinity, Tone 1:*
Through bodily representations of the Bodiless Powers being led up in mind unto the immaterial and noetic, and receiving the tri-radiant illumination of the three-hypostatic Godhead through thrice-holy singing, with Cherubim we cry aloud unto the One God: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, our God![^3034]

*[And it is meet to say at the end of each Troparion in each Tone thus:]*
*On Monday:* Through the intercessions of Thy Bodiless Powers, have mercy on us.
*On Tuesday:* By the prayers of Thy Forerunner, have mercy on us.
*On Wednesday:* By the prayers of the Mother of God, have mercy on us; *or also on Friday.*
*On Thursday:* By the prayers of Thine Apostles, and of Thy Hierarch Nicholas.
*On Friday:* By the power of Thy Cross preserve us; *(when it is not Wednesday).*[^3035]

*Glory...*
With all the heavenly powers, with Cherubim we cry aloud unto Him Who is in the highest, sending up thrice-holy praise: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, our God![^3036]

*Unto Saturday:* *And on the middle [Troparion] always:* By the prayers of all Thy Saints, have mercy on us.

*Both now...*
Having risen from sleep we fall down before Thee, O Good One, and we cry aloud unto Thee the angelic hymn, O Mighty One: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, our God. *[And on the third always:]* For the sake of the Mother of God, have mercy on us![^3037]

*Hymns to the Trinity, Tone 2:*
Imitating the Powers on high: upon earth we offer the victory song unto Thee, O Good One: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, our God![^3038]

*Glory...*
O uncreated Nature, Creator of all, open our lips, that we may proclaim Thy praise, crying aloud: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, our God![^3039]

*Both now...*
From the bed and sleep Thou hast raised me up, O Lord: enlighten my mind and my heart, and open my lips, that I may hymn Thee, O Holy Trinity: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, our God: for the sake of the Mother of God, have mercy on us![^3040]

*Tone 3:*
O Trinity consubstantial and undivided, Unity in three hypostases and co-everlasting: unto Thee as God we cry aloud the angelic hymn: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, our God![^3041]

*Glory...*
The Father without beginning, the co-unoriginate Son, and the co-everlasting Spirit, one Godhead, daring to glorify with Cherubim we say: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, our God: by the prayers of all Thy Saints![^3042]

*Both now...*
Suddenly the Judge shall come, and each man's deeds shall be laid bare; but with fear let us cry aloud at midnight: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, O God: for the sake of the Mother of God, have mercy on us![^3043]

*Tone 4:*
Daring to offer the prayerful hymn of Thy noetic servants, we say: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, our God![^3044]

*Glory...*
As the Angelic ranks now in heaven, and with fear the assemblies of men upon earth, we offer the victory song unto Thee, O Good One: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, O God: by the prayers of all Thy Saints![^3045]

*Both now...*
The Father without beginning, and Thee, O Christ God, and Thy Most Holy Spirit...[^3046]

...and Thy Most Holy Spirit, daring to glorify with Cherubim we say: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, our God: for the sake of the Mother of God, have mercy on us![^3047]

*Tone 5:*
It is the time of singing, and the hour of prayer; fervently let us cry aloud unto the One God: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, our God![^3048]

*Glory...*
Daring to represent Thine intelligible hosts, O unoriginate Trinity, with unworthy lips we cry aloud: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, our God: by the prayers of all the Saints![^3049]

*Both now...*
Contained within the Virgin's womb, yet not departing from the Father's bosom: receive also us with the Angels, O Christ God, as we cry aloud unto Thee: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, O God: for the sake of the Mother of God, have mercy![^3050]

*Tone 6:*
The Cherubim standing before Thee with fear, and the Seraphim in awe with trembling, offer the thrice-holy song with unceasing voice; with them also we sinners cry aloud: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, O God![^3051]

*Glory...*
With bodiless lips, with unceasing glorifications, the six-winged beings cry aloud the thrice-holy song unto Thee, our God; and we upon earth with unworthy lips send up praise unto Thee: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, O God: by the prayers of all the Saints![^3052]

*Both now...*
The Trinity Unity Godhead we glorify in unconfused union, and we cry aloud the angelic hymn: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, O God: for the sake of the Mother of God, have mercy on us![^3053]

*Tone 7:*
Hymned with the power on high in the manner of the Cherubim, and worshipped with divine glory in the manner of the Angels: receive also us upon earth, sending up a song unto Thee with unworthy lips: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, O God![^3054]

*Glory...*
Having cast aside slothfulness like sleep, O soul, show forth an amendment unto singing to the Judge, and cry aloud with fear: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, our God: by the prayers of all Thy Saints![^3055]

*Both now...*
Sending up Seraphic thrice-holy praise unto the unapproachable Godhead, the Trinity in Unity, with fear we cry aloud: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, O God: for the sake of the Mother of God, have mercy on us![^3056]

*Tone 8:*
Having our hearts toward Heaven, let us be likened unto the Angelic rank, and with fear let us fall down before the Judge, sending up the victory praise: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, our God![^3057]

*Glory...*
Not daring to gaze upon Thee, the Cherubim flying cry aloud with acclamation the divine song of the thrice-holy voice; with them also we cry aloud unto Thee: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, O God: by the prayers of all the Saints![^3058]

*Both now...*
Bowed down by the multitude of our transgressions, and not daring to look up to the height of heaven, having inclined our souls with bodies, with Angels we cry aloud the hymn unto Thee: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, our God: for the sake of the Mother of God, have mercy on us![^3059]

*Sessional Hymns from the Oktoechos, which we sing after the first Stichology during the Holy Forty Days:*[^3060]

*([Whichever Tone of the Oktoechos occurs on Cheesefare Sunday, that one we begin on Monday of the 1st Week of the Fast, in weekly order.])*[^3061]

*On Friday at Matins, after the 1st Stichology:*

*Penitential Sessional Hymn, Tone 1:*
In iniquities was I conceived, prodigal that I am, and I dare not look up to the height of heaven; but daring upon Thy love of mankind, I cry: O God, cleanse me and save me![^3062]

*Stichos: O Lord, rebuke me not in Thine anger, neither chasten me in Thy wrath. The same verse. Both now... We say...*[^3063]

*(We say [it] simply without chanting, in whichever Tone on Monday; to it the verse:)*

*Troparion:*
If the righteous scarcely be saved, where shall I appear, a sinner, who have not borne the burden and heat of the day?[^3064] But with the hirelings of the eleventh hour, number me, O God, and save me![^3065]

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*
A wonder of wonders, O thou full of grace! Seeing thee, creation rejoices; for thou didst conceive without seed, and didst bear ineffably Him Whom the ranks of Angels cannot gaze upon: pray Him, O Mother of God, that our souls may be saved![^3066]

*(At Ode 6, the Martyrikon is said, if the Menaion does not have a Kontakion; but if it has [one], this Martyrikon is said together with the Sessional hymns, before the stichos:[^3067] "Marvelous is God in His saints, the God of Israel."[^3068] After this, the Theotokion. And thus we do throughout the whole Fast.)*

*Martyrikon, Tone 1:*
Clothed with the boast of sufferings and with the honour of the crown by Thee, O Lord, the glorious Passion-bearers, by the endurance of wounds, overcame the lawless, and by divine power received victory from heaven: by their prayers grant us, O God, Thy great mercy![^3069]

*On Tuesday, after the 1st Stichology, Penitential Sessional Hymns, Tone 1:*

*Troparion:*
Hasten to open unto me Thy Fatherly embrace! I have prodigally spent my life, gazing upon the inexhaustible wealth of Thy compassions, O Savior; despise not now my heart that has become impoverished, for unto Thee, O Lord, with compunction I cry: I have sinned against heaven and before Thee![^3070]

*Troparion:*
Thy judgment seat is awesome, and the judgment is righteous, but my deeds are grievous; yet do Thou Thyself, O Merciful One, anticipate and save me, and delivering me from torment, rescue me, O Master, from the parts on the left, and vouchsafe me to stand at Thy right hand, O most righteous Judge![^3071]

*Theotokion:*
O unwedded, pure Virgin Mother of God, the only protectress and shelter of the faithful: deliver from afflictions, and sorrows, and grievous distresses all that place their hope in thee, O Maiden; and save our souls by thy divine prayers![^3072]

*At Ode 6, Martyrikon:*
As noble soldiers, with one mind having believed, ye feared not the threats of the tormentors, O Saints; ye came eagerly unto Christ, having taken up the precious Cross; and having finished your course, ye received victory from heaven: glory to Him that strengthened you; glory to Him that crowned you; glory to Him that through you works healings for all![^3073]

*On Wednesday, after the 1st Stichology, Sessional Hymns to the Cross, Tone 1:*

*Troparion:*
When Thou wast crucified, O Christ, the tyranny perished; the might of the enemy was trampled down; for neither Angel nor man, but Thou Thyself, O Lord, hast saved us: glory to Thee![^3074]

*Stichos: Exalt ye the Lord our God, and worship the footstool of His feet, for it is holy.[^3075] We say the same verse.*

*Troparion:*
We worship the wood of Thy Cross, O Lover of mankind, for upon it Thou didst nail the Life of all; Thou didst open paradise, O Savior, unto the thief who came to Thee with faith, and didst vouchsafe Him delight when he confessed unto Thee: Remember me, O Lord! Receive us also as Him, as we cry aloud: We all have sinned; in Thy tender mercy despise us not![^3076]

*Stavrotheotokion:*
The Ewe-lamb, seeing upon the Wood the Lamb, Thee, O Word, patiently crucified with two thieves, and pierced in the side with a spear, cried out, exclaiming as a mother: What is this strange and awesome mystery, O my Son?[^3077]

...how the tomb covers the uncircumscribed God: ineffable is that which is accomplished! Leave not me that gave Thee birth, O my sweetest Son![^3078]

*At Ode 6, Martyrikon:*
By the wounds of the Saints which they suffered for Thy sake, be Thou implored, O Lord, and heal all our sicknesses, O Lover of mankind, we pray Thee![^3079]

*On Thursday, after the 1st Stichology, Sessional Hymns to the Apostles, Tone 1:*

*Troparion:*
Having torn asunder the rhetorical embroideries with the spiritual net of the Cross, the simple fishermen enlightened the Gentiles piously to glorify Thee, the true God; therefore we also cry aloud a song unto Thee that didst strengthen them: Glory to the Father and to the Son; glory to the consubstantial Spirit; glory to Him that for their sake enlightened the world![^3080]

*Stichos: Their sound has gone forth into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the world.[^3081]*

*Troparion:*
All-wise fishermen of the universe, having received mercy from God, pray now also for us who cry aloud: O Lord, save the King and Thy City, and for the sake of the Apostles deliver our souls from the evils that encompass us![^3082]

*Theotokion:*
Without a mother in heaven, beyond understanding and hearing, on earth without a father thou didst give birth to Him: pray Him, O Mother of God, for our souls![^3083]

*At Ode 6, Martyrikon:*
We all pray the Martyrs of Christ, for they pray for our salvation; and let us all come unto them with faith: for they pour forth the grace of healings; they drive away the demonic legions, as guardians of the faith![^3084]

*On Friday, after the 1st Stichology, Sessional Hymns to the Cross, Tone 1:*

*Troparion:*
The weapon of the Cross was shown forth of old in battles unto the pious Emperor Constantine, an aid unto victory...[^3085]

...against the enemies, for the sake of faith. At this the powers of Hades tremble; this has become both salvation for the faithful, and the boast of Paul![^3086]

*Troparion:*
Thou Who of old didst fashion Adam from the earth, wast struck with a blow by a clay hand, O Compassionate One, and didst endure crucifixion, mockings, and wounds. O wonder, O Thy great longsuffering! Glory, O Lord, to Thy life-bearing Passion, whereby Thou hast saved us![^3087]

*Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion:*
Seeing Thee, O Christ, stretched out dead upon the Cross, the all-immaculate Mother cried aloud: O my Son, Who art co-unoriginate with the Father and the Spirit, what is this Thine ineffable dispensation, whereby with Thy pure hand Thou hast saved Thy creation, O Master?[^3088]

*At Ode 6, Martyrikon:*
*By the boast of sufferings... Seek [it] on Monday of this Tone.*[^3089]

*(And as we have indicated in this First Tone: thus it is meet to do in each Tone throughout the whole holy Forty Days.)*[^3090]

*On Monday, after the 1st Stichology, Penitential Sessional Hymns, Tone 2:*

*Troparion:*
Like the waves of the sea, my transgressions have risen up against me; like a ship in the deep, I alone am tempest-tossed by many trespasses; but guide me, O Lord, into the calm haven of repentance, and save me![^3091]

*Troparion:*
I am an unfruitful tree, O Lord, not bringing forth at all the fruit of repentance; and I fear cutting down, and I dread that unquenchable fire; therefore I pray Thee, before that calamity, turn me back and save me![^3092]

*Theotokion:*
Being a fountain of tender mercy, vouchsafe us mercy, O Mother of God; look upon the people that have sinned; show forth as...[^3093]

...ever thy power, for hoping in thee, we cry aloud unto thee: Rejoice! as once Gabriel, Archistrategos of the Bodiless Powers![^3094]

*After Ode 6, Martyrikon: The same on Monday of this Tone:*
Having Thee, Who clothest the heaven with clouds, as their clothing in the world, the Saints endured torments from the lawless, and abolished the deception of idols: by their prayers deliver us also from the invisible enemy, O Savior, and save us![^3095]

*On Tuesday, after the 1st Stichology, Penitential Sessional Hymns, Tone 2:*

*Troparion:*
Have mercy on me, said David; and I cry unto Thee: I have sinned, O Savior; having cleansed my sins, have mercy on me![^3096]

*Troparion:*
Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me! For two sins David wept bitterly, but from myriad transgressions I cry unto Thee: he drenched his couch with tears, but I have not acquired even a single tear; having despaired, I pray: Have mercy on me, O God, according to Thy great mercy![^3097]

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*
We became partakers of the divine nature through thee, O Ever-Virgin Mother of God; for thou didst bear God incarnate for us; therefore as is due we all piously magnify thee![^3098]

*After Ode 6, Martyrikon:*
Passion-bearers of the Lord, blessed is the earth that drank in your blood, and holy the shrines that received your bodies! For at the judgment seat ye convicted the enemy, and with boldness proclaimed Christ: pray Him as God, we pray, that our souls may be saved![^3099]

*On Wednesday, after the 1st Stichology, Sessional Hymns to the Cross, Tone 2:*

*Troparion:*
The life-creating Cross of Thy goodness, which Thou hast granted unto us who are unworthy, O Lord, we offer unto Thee in prayer: save the King and Thy City who pray, for the sake of the Mother of God, O Thou Who alone art the Lover of mankind![^3100]

*Troparion:*
Thou Didst work salvation in the midst of the earth, O Christ God, having stretched out Thy pure hands upon the Cross, gathering all nations who cry aloud: O Lord, glory to Thee![^3101]

*Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion:*
We magnify thee, O Mother of God, crying aloud: Rejoice, Rod from which without seed thou didst bud forth God, Who by the Wood destroyed death![^3102]

*After Ode 6, Martyrikon:*
Thou Who didst enlighten Thy Saints more than gold, and didst glorify Thy Venerable Ones as Good: being implored by them, O Christ God, pacify our life, as Lover of mankind, and direct our prayer as incense, O Thou Who alone restest in the Saints![^3103]

*On Thursday, after the 1st Stichology, Sessional Hymns to the Apostles, Tone 2:*

*Troparion:*
Having made the fishermen wiser than rhetoricians, and sent them forth as preachers unto all the earth by Thine ineffable love of mankind, O Christ God: for their sake establish Thy Church, and send down Thy blessedness upon the faithful, O Thou Who alone restest in the Saints![^3104]

*Troparion:*
The fishermen, having caught the nations and taught the ends of the earth to worship Thee, by Thine ineffable love of mankind, O Christ God: for their sake establish Thy Church, and send down Thy blessing upon the faithful, O Thou Who alone art most merciful and Lover of mankind![^3105]

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*
We magnify thee, O Mother of God, crying aloud: Rejoice, Cloud of the unwaning Light! For thou didst bear Him in thy bosom, the glory of the Lord![^3106]

*After Ode 6, Martyrikon:*
Apostles, Prophets, and Martyrs, Hierarchs, Venerable, and Righteous Ones, who have fought the good fight well, and kept the faith...[^3107]

...having boldness toward the Savior on our behalf: pray Him as Good, we pray, that our souls may be saved![^3108]

*On Friday, after the 1st Stichology, Sessional Hymns to the Cross, Tone 2:*

*Troparion:*
Thou Who didst enlighten the earthly by the Cross, and called sinners unto repentance: separate me not from Thy flock, O Good Shepherd, but seek me, O Master, who have strayed, and number me with Thy holy flock, O Lover of mankind![^3109]

*Troparion:*
We worship Thine immaculate Icon, O Good One, asking forgiveness of our trespasses, O Christ God; for of Thine own will Thou wast pleased to ascend the Cross, that Thou mightest deliver them whom Thou hadst fashioned from the bondage of the enemy; therefore with thanksgiving we cry aloud unto Thee: Thou hast filled all things with joy, O our Savior, Who didst come to save the world![^3110]

*Stavrotheotokion:*
The Virgin and Thy Mother, O Christ, seeing Thee stretched out dead upon the Wood, weeping bitterly, said: O my Son, what is this strange mystery? Thou Who grantest eternal life unto all, how dost Thou die of Thine own will upon the Cross by a reproachful death?[^3111]

*After Ode 6, Martyrikon:*
*Thou Who clothest [the heaven with clouds]... Look on Monday of this Tone.*[^3112]

*On Monday, after the 1st Stichology, Penitential Sessional Hymns, Tone 3:*

*Troparion:*
Living upon the earth, O my soul, repent! For the dust in the tomb sings not, nor does it deliver from transgressions; but cry aloud unto Christ God: O Knower of hearts, I have sinned; before Thou condemnest me, have mercy on me![^3113]

*Troparion:*
How long, O my soul, dost thou abide in transgressions? How long dost thou receive the neglect of repentance? Receive in thy mind the coming Judgment; cry aloud unto the Lord: I have sinned, O sinless Lord, save me![^3114]

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*...[^3115]

*Theotokion:*
Marveling at the beauty of thy virginity and the surpassing radiant purity of thine, Gabriel cried aloud unto thee, O Mother of God: What worthy praise shall I bring unto thee? And what shall I call thee? I am in doubt and astonished! Therefore, as I was commanded, I cry unto thee: Rejoice, O thou full of grace![^3116]

*After Ode 6, Martyrikon:*
By the magnanimity of your endurance, ye overcame the wiles of the evil-originating enemy, O all-praised Passion-bearers, and therefore were vouchsafed eternal blessedness; but pray unto the Lord to save the flock of Christ-loving people, as ye are martyrs in truth![^3117]

*On Tuesday, after the 1st Stichology, Penitential Sessional Hymns, Tone 3:*

*Troparion:*
At the awesome judgment seat, being convicted without accusers, and condemned without witnesses; for the books of conscience are unfolded, and hidden deeds are uncovered; before on that universal amphitheater Thou wilt examine the deeds done by me, O God, cleanse me and save me![^3118]

*Troparion:*
The awesome judgment seat awaits me, O Lord; for while I keep silence, my deeds cry aloud; but look past me who have evilly wandered; turn me back, O Christ God, and save me![^3119]

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*
Our refuge and strength, O Mother of God, mighty helper unto the world, by thy prayers save thy servants from every affliction, O thou who alone art blessed![^3120]

*After Ode 6, Martyrikon:*
Ye shine in the faith as most radiant luminaries, O Saints, physicians of piety, most praised Passion-bearers; for ye feared not the wounds of the tormentors, and cast down the impiety of idols, having as invincible victory the true Cross![^3121]

*On Wednesday, after the 1st Stichology, Sessional Hymns to the Cross, Tone 3:*

*Troparion:*
The Cross was set up on the earth, and touched the heavens; not that the wood had attained such height, but because Thou upon it fillest all things: glory to Thee![^3122]

*Troparion:*
Upon the cypress, the pine, and the cedar Thou wast lifted up, O Lamb of God, that Thou mightest save them that worship with faith Thy voluntary crucifixion, O Christ God: glory to Thee![^3123]

*Stavrotheotokion:*
Having acquired as a rod of strength the Cross of thy Son, O Mother of God, thereby we cast down the haughtiness of the enemy, and unceasingly magnify thee![^3124]

*After Ode 6, Martyrikon:*
The memory of Thy Passion-bearers, O Lord, Thou hast made radiant as Almighty, for Thou didst strengthen them to be conformed unto Thy Passion; for they manfully overcame the power of Beliar, therefore they also received gifts of healings: by their prayers, O Lover of mankind, grant peace unto our souls![^3125]

*On Thursday, after the 1st Stichology, Sessional Hymns to the Apostles, Tone 3:*

*Troparion:*
Come, all ye faithful, let us praise the Apostles as helmsmen; for they drove away the deception of idols, and led the people up unto the light of life, and taught them to glorify the Trinity; therefore today, celebrating their precious memory, let us glorify the Savior![^3126]

*Troparion:*
All the Apostles watered the earth with the Word as with divine dew, and caused the ear of grain of faith to grow; and they filled the ends of the world with Thy grace, O Lord, and cut down all the tares; therefore they brought all unto Christ God, King of all, baptizing them into the uncreated Trinity; therefore, all of us, celebrating their all-precious memory, glorify them in orthodox manner![^3127]

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*

*Theotokion:*
Prophets proclaimed, Apostles taught, and Martyrs confessed, and we have believed, truly to magnify thee as Mother of God in orthodox manner![^3128]

*After Ode 6, Martyrikon:*
Armed with the help of Christ, and clad in the armor of faith, like archers ye cast down the encampments of the enemy; for eagerly in hope of life ye endured all things, the threats and the wounds of the tormentors; therefore ye also received the crown, O Martyrs of Christ, longsuffering in soul![^3129]

*On Friday, after the 1st Stichology, Sessional Hymns to the Cross, Tone 3:*

*Troparion:*
Having willed to suffer the Cross and death, Thou didst plant it in the midst of creation. When Thou wast pleased, O Savior, to have Thy body nailed, then also the sun hid its rays. Seeing these things, the thief sang of Thee as God, crying aloud unto Thee: Remember me, O Lord! and having believed, He received Paradise![^3130]

*Troparion:*
At Thine uncircumscribed power and Thy voluntary crucifixion, the angelic hosts beholding were astonished: how He Who is invisible received wounds in the flesh, desiring to deliver mankind from corruption! Therefore as unto the Benefactor we cry aloud unto Thee: Glory, O Christ, to Thy tender compassion![^3131]

*Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion:*
A reproachful death, O Compassionate One, and crucifixion Thou didst endure of Thine own will. Seeing this, she that bare Thee, O Christ, was wounded; by her prayers, in the tender compassion of Thy mercy, O Lord Who alone art all-good and Lover of mankind: have compassion and save the world, O Thou that takest away the sins of the world![^3132]

*After Ode 6, Martyrikon:*
*Magnanimity of endurance... Look on Monday of this Tone.*[^3133]

*On Monday, after the 1st Stichology, Penitential Sessional Hymns, Tone 4:*[^3134]

*Troparion:*
Visit my humble soul, O Lord, which has spent all its life in sins; like the harlot receive me also, and save me![^3135]

*Troparion:*
Voyaging over the abyss of this life, I contemplate the deep of mine many evils; having no helmsman through my thoughts, I utter unto Thee Peter's cry: Save me, O Christ; save me, O God, for Thou art the Lover of mankind![^3136]

*Theotokion:*
Thou art an invincible rampart unto us Christians, O Virgin Mother of God; for fleeing unto thee we remain unharmed, and though we sin again, we have thee as an intercessor; therefore with thanksgiving we cry unto thee: Rejoice, O full of grace, the Lord is with thee![^3137]

*After Ode 6, Martyrikon:*
Today the angelic hosts have come at the memory of the Passion-bearers, to enlighten the minds of the faithful, and to illumine the universe with grace; being implored by them, O God, grant us great mercy![^3138]

*On Tuesday, after the 1st Stichology, Penitential Sessional Hymns, Tone 4:*

*Troparion:*
Quickly let us enter into the bridal chamber of Christ, that we all may hear the blessed voice of that God of ours: Come, ye that love heavenly glory, being partakers with the wise virgins, let us make bright our lamps by faith![^3139]

*Troparion:*
By the multitude of my transgressions I am condemned, by the fear of torment I am consumed, O Christ our God. Tears of repentance from the heart I offer unto Thee Who hast power over life and death, and I cry unto Thee with compunction: I have sinned, O Lord, save me![^3140]

*Theotokion:*
The Word of the Father, Christ our God, Who became incarnate of thee, we have come to know, O Virgin Mother of God, who alone art pure...[^3141]

...who alone art blessed; therefore unceasingly, chanting hymns to thee, we magnify thee![^3142]

*After Ode 6, Martyrikon:*
Armed with the Cross, Thy Passion-bearers overcame the wiles of the evil-originating enemy, O Christ our God; they shone forth as luminaries instructing men; they grant healings unto them that ask with faith: by their prayers save our souls![^3143]

*On Wednesday, after the 1st Stichology, Sessional Hymns to the Cross, Tone 4:*

*Troparion:*
Thou hast redeemed us from the curse of the law by Thy precious Blood; having been nailed to the Cross and pierced with a spear, Thou didst pour forth immortality unto men: O our Savior, glory to Thee![^3144]

*Troparion:*
Upon the Cross the Jews nailed Thee, O Savior, through which Thou didst call us from the nations, O Lord, Lover of mankind; Thou didst stretch out Thy hands upon it of Thine own will; and with a spear Thou wast pleased to have Thy side pierced: glory to the multitude of Thy compassions, O Longsuffering One![^3145]

*Stavrotheotokion:*
O all-immaculate Virgin, Mother of Christ God, a sword pierced thy most pure soul when thou didst behold crucified of His own will thy Son and God: Whom do thou, O most blessed one, pray unceasingly, to grant us the forgiveness of our transgressions![^3146]

*After Ode 6, Martyrikon:*
Having contended well by the power of the Cross, ye cast down the adversary enemy mightily by your endurance, O holy Passion-bearers; therefore, celebrating with faith your precious memory, we are sanctified by the operation of the grace of the All-Holy Spirit: by your prayers, O sacred warriors of Christ, pray unto the Savior for the world![^3147]

*On Thursday, after the 1st Stichology, Sessional Hymns to the Apostles, Tone 4:*[^3148]

*Troparion:*
As luminaries unto the ends of the earth Thou hast shown forth Thy disciples, O Christ, shining through Thy preaching, enlightening our souls. The deception of idols Thou didst darken through them, having enlightened the world with the teachings of piety: by their prayers save our souls![^3149]

*Troparion:*
As preachers of the faith Thou hast revealed Thy disciples unto the world, O Savior, guiding through them the nations unto the knowledge of Thyself; for with the beams of the Word they enlightened all, having driven away the darkness of ignorance by faith: by their prayers save our souls![^3150]

*Theotokion:*
Since thou art better than all creatures, and we are at a loss to glorify thee worthily, O Mother of God: therefore we pray thee, have mercy on us![^3151]

*After Ode 6, Martyrikon:*
Manfully having endured wounds, ye worthily received the incorruptible crown of the kingdom; for drawn by desire unto the un-aging life, ye endured torments in the flesh, O Passion-bearers: therefore pray that we may find mercy![^3152]

*On Friday, after the 1st Stichology, Sessional Hymns to the Cross, Tone 4:*

*Troparion:*
Hasten to anticipate before we are enslaved, for enemies blaspheme Thee and threaten us, O Christ God; destroy by Thy Cross them that wage war against us, that they may understand how great is the power of the Orthodox faith, by the prayers of the Mother of God, O Thou Who alone art the Lover of mankind![^3153]

*Troparion:*
When Thy divine side was wounded with the spear, O Master, the weapons of the invisible enemy failed completely, and all violence of his malice ceased; therefore we worship Thy saving Passion, glorifying Thy divine dispensation![^3154]

*Stavrotheotokion:*...

*Stavrotheotokion:*
When Thy most pure Mother, O Word of God, beheld Thee lifted up upon the Cross, weeping maternally, she said: What new and strange wonder is this, O my Son? How dost Thou, the Life of all, taste of death, desiring to give life unto the dead, as Thou art merciful![^3155]

*After Ode 6, Martyrikon:*
*Today the angelic hosts... Look on Monday of this Tone.*[^3156]

*On Monday, after the 1st Stichology, Penitential Sessional Hymns, Tone 5:*

*Troparion:*
When the Judge sits, and the Angels stand by, the trumpet sounding and the flame burning: what wilt thou do, O my soul, when led unto judgment? For then thine evil deeds will stand before thee, and thy secret sins will be exposed; therefore before the end cry aloud unto Christ God: O Knower of hearts, I have sinned, have mercy on me![^3157]

*Troparion:*
Let us all keep vigil, and let us all meet Christ with a multitude of oil and bright lamps, that we may be accounted worthy to enter inside the bridal chamber; for he who is found outside the doors will cry aloud unto God without success: Have mercy on me![^3158]

*Theotokion:*
With the Angels the heavenly things, and with men the earthly things, in a voice of rejoicing we cry unto thee, O Mother of God: Rejoice, door wider than the heavens! Rejoice, only salvation of earthly men! Rejoice, pure one! Rejoice, full of grace, who didst bear God incarnate![^3159]

*After Ode 6, Martyrikon:*
Today the memory of the Passion-bearers shines, for it has radiance from the heavens; the choir of Angels keeps festival, and the human race celebrates together; therefore they pray unto the Lord that our souls may find mercy![^3160]

*On Tuesday, after the 1st Stichology, Penitential Sessional Hymns, Tone 5:*

*Troparion:*
O soul, things here are temporal, but things there are...[^3161]

...eternal; behold the judgment seat, and the Judge upon the throne, and tremble at the answer! Therefore, O soul, turn back, for the judgment is unsparing![^3162]

*Troparion:*
Lying upon a bed of many sins, I am robbed of the hope of my salvation; for the sleep of sloth procures torment for my soul; therefore spare me, O Christ God, as Thou alone art the Lover of mankind![^3163]

*Theotokion:*
A strange mystery of the Virgin has appeared unto the world as saving; for of her was born without seed, and in the flesh was revealed without corruption, the Joy of all: O Lord, glory to Thee![^3164]

*After Ode 6, Martyrikon:*
Having granted us the wonders of the holy Martyrs as an invincible rampart, O Christ God: by their prayers destroy the counsels of the nations, establish the scepters of the Tsardom, as Thou alone art good and the Lover of mankind![^3165]

*On Wednesday, after the 1st Stichology, Sessional Hymns to the Cross, Tone 5:*

*Troparion:*
The Place of the Skull became Paradise; for no sooner was the Wood of the Cross set up, than immediately it budded forth the Cluster of Life, Thee, O Savior, unto our rejoicing: glory to Thee![^3166]

*Troparion:*
The crucified Savior and our Deliverer, Who of His own will, as He knew and as He was well pleased, let us, the faithful, hymn and glorify; for He nailed upon the Cross the sins of earthly men, delivering the human race from deception, and vouchsafed us the Kingdom![^3167]

*Stavrotheotokion:*
When she that bare Thee without pain, O Savior, beheld Thee lifted up upon the Wood, she wailed with weeping and cried aloud: Woe is me, my sweetest Son! I am consumed in soul, seeing Thee upon the Cross, nailed between two malefactors by an unjust judgment![^3168]

*After Ode 6, Martyrikon:*
O Lord, Thy Passion-bearers...

...having desired the cup of Thy suffering, abandoned the beauty of life, and became fellow-partakers with the Angels: by their prayers grant unto our souls propitiation and great mercy![^3169]

*On Thursday, after the 1st Stichology, Sessional Hymns to the Apostles, Tone 5:*

*Troparion:*
As eyewitnesses and ministers of the Word, praise the all-wise Apostles in spiritual songs and hymns, all ye earthly; for they diligently pray unto Christ for us who chant their sacred memory and venerate their relics![^3170]

*Troparion:*
Let us harmoniously praise the Apostles, as they preached unto all in Orthodox manner the Lord's teaching, and drove away the gloom of heresies, and shone forth spiritual enlightenment in the world by the grace of teaching, and pray that we may be saved![^3171]

*Theotokion:*
Condemned by the judgment of conscience, and meditating upon the judgment before the judgment, I, wretched one, tremble, reflecting upon the multitude of mine evils; but unto thine unbreakable wall and protection I cry out in compunction: deliver me from that judgment, and save me by thy prayers![^3172]

*After Ode 6, Martyrikon:*
The righteous deeds of the holy Martyrs astonished the Heavenly Hosts; for in mortal body, having contended well by the power of the Cross, they overcame the bodiless, invisible enemies; and they pray unto the Lord that our souls may find mercy![^3173]

*On Friday, after the 1st Stichology, Sessional Hymns to the Cross, Tone 5:*

*Troparion:*
Thou didst endure the Cross of Thine own will, and didst deliver men from corruption, O Savior; we, the faithful, hymn and worship Thee, for Thou hast enlightened us by the power of the Cross; and we all glorify Thee, O Lover of mankind and Compassionate One, as the Giver of life and the Lord![^3174]

*Troparion:*
Of Thine own will, O Compassionate One, Thou didst endure crucifixion, and having been buried as almighty God, [Thou didst destroy] the ancient curse for the sake of the eating...[^3175]

...therefore Thy divine and precious Sufferings, O Master Christ, we hymn and worship, unceasingly glorifying Thy dispensation that surpasses speech![^3176]

*Stavrotheotokion:*
By the Cross of thy Son, O thou who hast been made glad in God, all the deception of idols has been abolished, and the demonic might trampled down; therefore we, the faithful, as is due, ever bless thee and hymn thee, and confessing thee to be the true Mother of God, we magnify thee![^3177]

*After Ode 6, Martyrikon:*
*Today shines... Look on Friday of this Tone.*[^3178]

*On Monday, after the 1st Stichology, Penitential Sessional Hymns, Tone 6:*

*Troparion:*
I contemplate the awesome day, and weep for my evil deeds: how shall I answer the immortal King? With what boldness shall I gaze upon the Judge, I the prodigal? O Father of tender compassion, O only-begotten Son, O Holy Spirit: have mercy on me![^3179]

*Troparion:*
In the valley of weeping, in the place which Thou hast appointed, when Thou shalt sit, O Merciful One, to execute righteous judgment: expose not my hidden things, neither put me to shame before the Angels; but spare me, O God, and have mercy on me![^3180]

*Theotokion:*
The most glorious Mother of God, who is holier than the holy Angels, let us praise without ceasing, with heart and lips confessing her to be the Mother of God, as she truly bare God incarnate, and prays unceasingly for our souls![^3181]

*After Ode 6, Martyrikon:*
Light is ever unto the righteous; for the Saints, having been enlightened by Thee, shine ever as luminaries, having extinguished the lamps of the ungodly; by whose prayers, O our Savior, Thou enlightenest my lamp, O Lord, and save me![^3182]

*On Tuesday, after the 1st Stichology, Penitential Sessional Hymns, Tone 6:*

*Troparion:*
Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us; for being at a loss for any defense, this prayer we sinners offer unto Thee as Master: Have mercy on us![^3183]

*Troparion:*
O Lord, have mercy on us, for in Thee have we put our trust; be not exceedingly wroth with us, neither remember our iniquities; but look upon us even now as Thou art merciful, and deliver us from our enemies; for Thou art our God, and we are Thy people; we are all the work of Thy hands, and we call upon Thy Name![^3184]

*Theotokion:*
Open unto us the doors of tender compassion, O blessed Mother of God, that we who hope in thee may not perish, but that we may be delivered through thee from adversities; for thou art the salvation of the Christian race![^3185]

*After Ode 6, Martyrikon:*
Having endured the struggle of suffering, the Saints received from Thee the honors of victory; they abolished the thoughts of the lawless, and received crowns of incorruption: for their sakes, O God, grant us great mercy![^3186]

*On Wednesday, after the 1st Stichology, Sessional Hymns to the Cross, Tone 6:*

*Troparion:*
Thy Cross, O Lord, is sanctified, for through it healings are wrought unto them that are sick with sins; therefore we fall down before Thee: have mercy on us![^3187]

*Troparion:*
No sooner was the Wood of Thy Cross set up, O Christ, than the foundations of death were shaken, O Lord; for him whom Hades swallowed with greediness, it cast out with trembling; Thou hast shown us Thy salvation, O Son of God, and we glorify Thee: have mercy on us![^3188]

*Stavrotheotokion:*
O Virgin Mother of God, pray thy Son, Who of His own will was nailed upon the Cross, and rose from the dead, Christ our God, that our souls may be saved![^3189]

*After Ode 6, Martyrikon:*
The sufferings of resistance in the struggles, the tormenting wounds upon the martyrs! And the bodiless ranks stood by, holding victory prizes; the all-wise ones astonished the tormentor and the king, and cast down Beliar by the confession of Christ: O Lord Who didst strengthen them, glory to Thee![^3190]

*On Thursday, after the 1st Stichology, Sessional Hymns to the Apostles, Tone 6:*[^3191]

*Troparion:*
As Thou didst come into the midst of Thy disciples, O Savior, giving them peace: come also unto us, and save us![^3192]

*Troparion:*
Thy disciples, O Jesus, being sent unto the ends of the earth, having piously caught the nations, as it were, brought them unto Thy grace, O Lord; therefore for their sake we cry unto Thee, O Lover of mankind: Grant unto Thy people great mercy![^3193]

*Theotokion:*
Most holy Mother of God, in the time of my life forsake me not, and entrust me not unto human help, but do thou thyself defend me, and save me![^3194]

*After Ode 6, Martyrikon:*
O Lord, the memory of Thy Saints today has been shown forth like the Paradise that is in Eden; for in it all creation rejoices: and grant us by their prayers compunction and great mercy![^3195]

*On Friday, after the 1st Stichology, Sessional Hymns to the Cross, Tone 6:*

*Troparion:*
Today the prophetic word is fulfilled: for behold, we worship in the place where Thy feet stood, O Lord; and having tasted of the tree of salvation, we have obtained freedom from sinful passions: by the prayers of the Mother of God, O Thou Who alone art the Lover of mankind![^3196]

*Troparion:*
O Lord, the Jews condemned Thee unto death, the Life of all; they that passed through the Red Sea by a rod nailed Thee to the Cross; and they that sucked honey from the rock brought Thee gall; but of Thine own will Thou didst endure it, that Thou mightest free us from the bondage of the enemy, O Christ our God: glory to Thee![^3197]

*Stavrotheotokion:*
O only immaculate ewe-lamb, Virgin Mother of God, beholding Him Who was incarnate of thy pure blood hanging of His own will upon the Cross, thou didst cry aloud, O Maiden, with bitter tears: O my gentle Son, I hymn Thine all-awesome dispensation![^3198]

*After Ode 6, Martyrikon:*
*Light is ever unto the righteous... Look above on Monday of this Tone.*[^3199]

*On Monday, after the 1st Stichology, Penitential Sessional Hymns, Tone 7:*[^3200]

*Troparion:*
Having the medicine of repentance, O my soul, draw near, crying out with tears and sighing: O Physician of souls and bodies, O Lover of mankind, free me from my transgressions; number me with the harlot, the thief, and the publican, and grant me, O God, forgiveness of mine iniquities, and save me![^3201]

*Troparion:*
Peter's denial Thou didst wash away with tears, and the publican's transgressions and sighing Thou didst forgive: O Lord, Lover of mankind, have mercy on me![^3202]

*Theotokion:*
Thou dost surpass the heavenly hosts, for thou wast a divine temple, O blessed Mother of God, who didst bear Christ the Savior of our souls![^3203]

*After Ode 6, Martyrikon:*
O holy Saints, pray that forgiveness of our transgressions may be granted, and that we may be delivered from impending evils and bitter death, we pray![^3204]

*On Tuesday, after the 1st Stichology, Penitential Sessional Hymns, Tone 7:*

*Troparion:*
I have not emulated the publican's repentance, and have not acquired the harlot's tears; for in ignorance I am at a loss for such correction; but by Thy tender mercy save me, O God, as Thou art the Lover of mankind![^3205]

*Troparion:*
Thou Who didst accept the tears of the harlot and Peter, and didst justify the publican who sighed from the depths: have compassion on me who am in despair because of my deeds, O Savior, and save me![^3206]

*Theotokion:*
Rejoice, O Mother of God, who didst contain in thy womb Him Whom the heavens cannot contain; rejoice, O Virgin, preaching of the Prophets, through whom Emmanuel has shone forth unto us; rejoice, O Mother of Christ God![^3207]

*After Ode 6, Martyrikon:*
Thy Saints, O Lord, having contended upon earth, abolished the deception of idols; therefore they also received crowns from Thee, O Lover of mankind...[^3208]

...and cypress; granting victories unto our Tsars, for the sake of the Mother of God, as we worship Thee: have mercy on us![^3209]

*Troparion:*
Thou Who didst accept crucifixion for my sake, accept also my vigilant praise, O Christ God, as Thou art the Lover of mankind![^3210]

*Stavrotheotokion:*
Unceasingly pray Christ God, Who was crucified for our sake and cast down the power of death, O Virgin Mother of God, that He may save our souls![^3211]

*After Ode 6, Martyrikon:*
Rejoice, ye righteous; let the heavens be glad! For the Martyrs, having contended upon earth, abolished deception. Let the triumphant Church leap for joy, celebrating unto the Author of the contest and the only Victor, Christ God, Who grants unto the world great mercy![^3212]

*On Thursday, after the 1st Stichology, Sessional Hymns to the Apostles, Tone 7:*

*Troparion:*
As helmsmen of our salvation, let us duly honor in chants and songs the all-wise Apostles of Christ God; for having driven away the deception of impiety, they save the world, having become eyewitnesses, servants, friends, and brethren of the Word![^3213]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst show forth Thine Apostles, O Word, as laborers for Thy field, cutting down idols; therefore, preaching Thee as Master among the nations, they piously magnified Thee![^3214]

*Theotokion:*
Though creation knew thee as a Mother, yet the Creator showed thee forth as a Virgin; for thou didst bear in the flesh Christ God, Who continually saves our souls![^3215]

*After Ode 6, Martyrikon:*
Having endured bonds and torments, the holy Martyrs put to shame the deception of idols; therefore also chanting with the Angels, we cry aloud a praiseworthy solution of songs, glorifying Thee, O Christ: by their prayers, grant unto our souls cleansing and great mercy![^3216]

*On Friday, after the 1st Stichology, Sessional Hymns to the Cross, Tone 7:*[^3217]

*Troparion:*
Brighter than fire, more effectual than flame, Thou hast shown the Tree of Thy Cross to be, consuming the sins of the ailing and enlightening the hearts of them that chant Thy voluntary crucifixion: O Christ God, glory to Thee![^3218]

*Troparion:*
O Lord, beholding Thy Cross exalted, I ever draw near in faith, embracing it with fear and joy in chants and songs: sanctify Thy servants and pacify Thy world by its manifestation, O Thou Who alone art the Lover of mankind![^3219]

*Stavrotheotokion:*
O pure Mother of God, ever-virgin, all-immaculate one, beholding thy Son hanging upon the Cross, weeping maternally, thou didst magnify His awesome descent![^3220]

*After Ode 6, Martyrikon:*
*The Saints pray... Look above on Friday of Tone 7.*[^3221]

*On Monday, after the 1st Stichology, Penitential Sessional Hymns, Tone 8:*

*Troparion:*
With a merciful eye, O Lord, behold my humility, for little by little my life is spent, and from works there is no salvation for me; therefore I pray: with a merciful eye, O Lord, behold my humility, and save me![^3222]

*Troparion:*
As the Judge has come, be vigilant, O my soul, and meditate upon the hour of that awesome day; for judgment is without mercy to them that have not shown mercy; therefore spare me, O Savior, for Thou alone art the Lover of mankind![^3223]

*Theotokion:*
Rejoice, thou who through the Angel didst receive joy for the world! Rejoice, thou who didst bear the Creator of creation! Rejoice, thou who wast accounted worthy to be the Mother of Christ God![^3224]

*After Ode 6, Martyrikon:*
Today the memory of the Passion-bearers shines with heavenly light; for in it the angelic hosts rejoice, and with them the human ranks make merry: by their prayers, send down upon Thy world reconciliation, O Christ, and great mercy![^3225]

*On Tuesday, after the 1st Stichology, Penitential Sessional Hymns, Tone 8:*[^3226]

*Troparion:*
Like the harlot I fall down before Thee, that I may receive forgiveness; tears from my heart I offer unto Thee, O Christ God, that Thou mayest cleanse me, O Savior, and grant forgiveness of sins; for like her I cry unto Thee: deliver me from the mire of my deeds![^3227]

*Troparion:*
Reflecting upon that awesome day, be watchful, O my soul, kindling thy lamp, enlightening it with oil; for thou knowest not when the voice shall come unto thee, saying: Behold thy Bridegroom! Beware therefore, O my soul, lest thou slumber and remain outside knocking, like the five virgins; but wait vigilantly, that thou mayest meet Christ with rich oil, and He will give thee the divine bridal chamber of His glory![^3228]

*Theotokion:*
O all-pure Virgin, save us by thy prayers, moving thy maternal compassion toward thy Son and God![^3229]

*After Ode 6, Martyrikon:*
Spiritual luminaries ye appeared, O holy Martyrs; for by faith ye abolished the deceptive gloom; ye enlightened the lamps of your souls, and with glory entered with the Bridegroom into the heavenly bridal chamber; and now pray that our souls may be saved![^3230]

*On Wednesday, after the 1st Stichology, Sessional Hymns to the Cross, Tone 8:*

*Troparion:*
Beholding the Author of life hanging upon the Cross, the thief said: If He Who is crucified with us were not God incarnate, the sun would not have hidden its beams, nor would the earth have shaken with trembling; but O Thou Who endurest all things, remember me, O Lord, in Thy Kingdom![^3231]

*Troparion:*
Between two thieves Thy Cross was found to be a righteous balance: for the one it weighed down into Hades by the weight of his blasphemy, but for the other it was lightened of sins unto the knowledge of theology: O Christ God, glory to Thee![^3232]

*Stavrotheotokion:*
Beholding the Lamb, the Shepherd, and the Savior of the world upon the Cross, she that bare Him said, weeping: The world indeed rejoices, receiving redemption, but my womb burns, beholding Thy crucifixion which Thou endurest for all, O my Son and God![^3233]

*After Ode 6, Martyrikon:*
Ever-shining luminaries unto the universe ye were shown forth through faith, O Martyrs: ye placed all your hope in the Lord, and with the spiritual oil of the Holy Spirit ye enlightened the lamps of your souls; therefore ye were shown to be spiritual chalices of the Church, pouring forth blood like water: O all-praised Passion-bearers, pray Christ God to grant forgiveness of sins unto them that celebrate with love your holy memory![^3234]

*On Thursday, after the 1st Stichology, Sessional Hymns to the Apostles, Tone 8:*

*Troparion:*
Luminaries unto the world and guides, first-fruits of our salvation, let us hymn the divine Disciples of our God; for they shone forth like light unto us that were in darkness, and proclaimed the Sun of glory unto all; therefore they also cast down the deception of idols, having preached the Trinity in one Godhead: for this cause we pray: O Apostles of Christ God, grant that forgiveness of transgressions may be given unto them that honor with love your holy memory![^3235]

*Troparion:*
Into all the earth, as the Prophet said, went forth the proclamation of the all-wise Apostles; for having preached the Word, they enlightened all nations; therefore, duly praising them, let us honor them with songs, as they ever pray Christ that our souls may be saved![^3236]

*Theotokion:*
O Protection of the faithful, Mother of God, joy to the sorrowful and great consolation to the weeping: unceasingly pray Him Who was born of thy womb beyond nature, O all-pure Virgin...[^3237]

...pray with the Apostles for us, that we may be delivered in the hour of trial![^3238]

*After Ode 6, Martyrikon:*
Having mortified the fiery appearances and motions of the body, the Martyrs of Christ received grace to drive away ailments from the sick, and being alive and after their repose to work wonders: truly a most glorious wonder, that bare bones pour forth healings! Glory to the only God and Creator![^3239]

*On Friday, after the 1st Stichology, Sessional Hymns to the Cross, Tone 8:*

*Troparion:*
In the midst of Eden a tree blossomed forth death, but in the midst of all the earth a tree blossomed forth life: having tasted of the first, though incorruptible, we became corruptible; but having attained the second, we enjoyed incorruption; for by the Cross Thou savest the human race, as Thou art God![^3240]

*Troparion:*
In Paradise the enemy formerly stripped me bare by the tree through tasting, bringing in mortification; but the Tree of the Cross brought unto men the garment of life: it was planted upon the earth, and the whole world was filled with all joy; beholding it exalted, we, the people, cry aloud unto God in faith with one accord: Full of glory is His temple![^3241]

*Theotokion:*
Being ever preserved by the Cross of thy Son and God, O Virgin, we overcome the demonic assaults and wiles; chanting of thee in love as the true Mother of God, all generations bless thee, O all-pure one, even as thou didst foretell; therefore grant forgiveness unto our transgressions by thy prayers, and send down upon Thy world reconciliation and great mercy![^3242]

*After Ode 6, Martyrikon:*
*With heavenly light... Look on Friday of this Tone.*[^3243]

*Photagogika from the Octoechos, which we chant during the Holy Forty Days, and during the other Fasts: when the Triadica are chanted, then also chant these Photagogika in that Tone.*[^3244]

*Exaposteilarion, Tone 1:*
O Lord Who didst cause the light to shine, cleanse my soul from every sin by the intercession of the Bodiless Hosts, and save me![^3245]

*Tone 2:*
Send forth Thy co-eternal light, O Christ God, and enlighten the secret eyes of my heart by the protection of the Bodiless Hosts, and save me![^3246]

*Tone 3:*
Send forth Thy light, O Christ God, and enlighten my heart by the intercession of the Bodiless Hosts, and save me![^3247]

*Tone 4:*
O Thou Who didst cause light to shine forth unto Thy world, cleanse my soul that is in darkness from every sin by the intercession of the Bodiless Hosts, and save me![^3248]

*Tone 5:*
O Giver of light, O Lord, send forth Thy light and enlighten my heart by the intercession of the Bodiless Hosts, and save me![^3249]

*Tone 6:*
By the intercession of the Bodiless Hosts, O Lord, send down upon our souls Thy co-eternal light![^3250]

*Tone 7:*
Raise me up, O Lord, unto Thy hymnody, and teach me to do Thy holy will, by the protection of Thy Bodiless Hosts, and save me![^3251]

*Tone 8:*
O Christ Who art light, enlighten me with Thyself, by the intercession of the Bodiless Hosts, and save me![^3252]

---

# PART IV: THE LIFE OF OUR VENERABLE MOTHER MARY OF EGYPT BY ST. SOPHRONIUS OF JERUSALEM AND CONCLUDING COLOPHON

## On Thursday of the Great Canon

*The Life and Conduct of Our Venerable Mother Mary of Egypt, Written by the Most Holy Sophronius, Patriarch of Jerusalem.*[^3253]

It is good to keep close the secret of a king, but it is honorable to reveal the works of the Lord openly. For so said the Angel unto Tobit, after the marvelous restoration of the sight of his blinded eyes, and after those tribulations through which he passed, and from which he was delivered by grace. For not to keep the secret of a king is perilous and ruinous; but to keep silence concerning the marvelous works of God brings peril unto the soul. Therefore, seized with fear of keeping silence concerning His divine proclamations, and fearing the threatened peril of the servant who received a talent from the Master and buried it in the earth, hiding without profit that which was given him for trading, I shall in no wise keep silence concerning the sacred narrative that has reached me.[^3254]

Therefore let no one disbelieve me, for I write that which I have heard; nor let any marvel at me, as though I were contriving something beyond all others. Far be it from me to tell falsehoods concerning divine things, or to make merchandise of the word wherein God is commemorated! Rather than meditating upon lesser things that are unworthy of the majesty of God the Word Incarnate, or disbelieving them that speak thus, it does not seem unto me to be praiseworthy.[^3255]

If any, receiving such writings and marveling at the sublime wonder of the account, should be reluctant to believe, may the Lord be merciful also unto them; for they, considering the infirmity of human nature, deem it impossible for marvelous things to be spoken concerning men.[^3256]

I shall proceed therefore to the very subject of the narrative, that is to say, to that which took place in our generation, which a sacred man, accustomed from infancy to speak and do divine things, has related. But let not even this draw unto disbelief those who find such a wonder in our generation...[^3257]

...nor let them deem this to be impossible; for the grace of the Spirit entering from generation to generation into holy souls makes them friends of God and Prophets, as the divine Solomon taught. But it is time to begin that sacred narrative.[^3258]

There was a certain man in the monasteries of Palestine, adorned in life and word, who from his very swaddling clothes had remained in monastic customs and practices. Zosimas was the name of this elder; and let no one, because of the common name of Zosimas, suppose me to speak of that Zosimas who was once cast out of the dogmas as heretical. For the one is different from the other, and there is a great distinction between them both, even though both have the same name. For that one was Zosimas the heretic; but this was Zosimas the Orthodox, who lived as a monk from the beginning in one of the sacred monasteries in Palestine, having traversed every form of ascetical struggle, and having become zealous for every word of self-restraint. For every rule handed down in the arena wherein he walked he preserved intact. He also devised many things of his own, in order to subdue the flesh unto the spirit. Therefore he did not fail of this purpose; for the elder was so eminent in practical virtue that many from the neighboring monasteries (and sometimes even from afar) used to come unto him, to be trained and guided toward self-restraint by his teaching.[^3259]

And so, having such vision in active deed, the elder never neglected the study of the divine words; but both lying down and rising up, he held handiwork in his hands, and food (if indeed it is meet to call it food) he tasted, partaking of it according to custom, having one unceasing and never-ending work: to chant continually and ever to meditate upon the sacred words. Many times, indeed, it was said that the elder was accounted worthy of divine vision, illumination having come unto him from God; and this is neither marvelous nor incredible. For if, as the Lord said, *Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God*, they that manifestly purify their flesh and are ever vigilant in sobriety behold with the eye of their soul the vision of divine illumination, receiving from thence the pledge of those abiding good things.[^3260]

The blessed Zosimas himself used to relate that from his very swaddling clothes, so to speak, he had been given to the monastery, and had traversed the course of ascetical struggle therein until his fifty-third year. But after this he was troubled (as he said) by certain thoughts, as though he were perfected in all things and in no wise needed the instruction of others. For he thought within himself, saying...[^3261]

"Can there be any monk capable of delivering unto me something strange, or able to profit me, or to show me a form of asceticism which I know not and have not accomplished? Can there be found among the philosophers who dwell in the wilderness one who is superior to me in action or contemplation?" While the elder was meditating in this manner, someone stood before him and said: "O Zosimas, well indeed hast thou contended, as far as it is possible for a man; well hast thou run the course of asceticism. Yet there is no one among men who possesses perfection, but the contest that lies ahead is greater than that which is already past, of which thou knowest not. That thou mayest know also thyself how many other ways there are unto salvation: go forth out of thy land, and from thy kindred, and from thy father's house, even as that renowned Abraham among the Patriarchs, and come unto one of the monasteries situated near the river Jordan."[^3262]

Straightway the elder, following the one who commanded him, went forth from the monastery wherein he had lived as a monk from infancy; and having reached the Jordan (which is the holiest among rivers), he was guided by the one who called him unto that monastery wherein God had commanded him to be. Having knocked with his hand upon the gate of the courtyard, he met the monk who guarded the gate, and the latter announced him unto the Abbot, who received him. And the Abbot, beholding his reverent appearance and manner, and seeing that he made the customary monastic metania and received a blessing, questioned him in this manner:[^3263]

"Whence art thou, brother, and why hast thou come unto us humble elders?"[^3264]

Zosimas answered: "Whence I come it is not necessary to say, but for the sake of profit have I come, O father; for I have heard great and praiseworthy things concerning you, which are able to strengthen the soul unto union with Christ our God."[^3265]

The Abbot said unto him: "God alone, brother, is He Who heals human infirmity; may He teach both thee and us His divine will, and guide all to do what is profitable. For a man cannot profit a man unless each gives heed unto himself continually, and is sober in mind, doing what is necessary, having acquired God as a fellow-worker in his deeds. Yet since, as thou hast said, the love of Christ has moved thee to see us, humble elders, abide with us if for this cause thou hast come; and the Good Shepherd, Who gave His life as a ransom for us and calls His own sheep by name, will feed all of us with spiritual grace." When the Abbot had spoken these things unto Zosimas, the latter straightway made a metania, asked for a prayer, and having said "Amen," remained in that monastery.[^3266]

And seeing the elders shining in action and contemplation, burning in spirit, and serving the Lord—for their chanting was unceasing, and their standing was all-night; in their hands was constant handiwork, and the Psalms were in their mouths; no idle word had any dwelling among them, and there was no care for material things in their midst; uncounted years of revenues and worldly anxieties cursed by toil were not even known among them by name; but their single, first, and urgent care was that each of them should be dead in the body, as having once for all died and ceased to be unto the world and all things in the world. They had as inexhaustible food the divinely-inspired words; and they nourished their body only with what was strictly necessary, bread and water, according as each had the burning of the love of God. Seeing these things, Zosimas (as He said) was greatly edified, pressing forward unto what lay ahead, ever increasing his course, and He was found to be a good fellow-laborer with them that cultivate the divine Paradise.[^3267]

When sufficient days had passed, the time drew near when it is handed down for Christians to keep the holy Fast; for they purify themselves beforehand unto the veneration of the divine Passions and the Resurrection of the Lord. The gates of the monastery were never opened, but were always shut; and the monks performed their ascetical struggle without distraction; nor was it ever opened, unless somewhere one of them went forth for some urgent necessity. For the place was desolate, and to the neighboring dwellers and monks it was not only inaccessible, but even unknown. Now such a rule had been preserved in the monastery from the beginning, for the sake of which God, through a revelation, had brought Zosimas unto that monastery. And what that rule was and how it was kept, I shall relate here.[^3268]

Now on the Sunday which is customarily called the first of the fasting weeks, the Divine Liturgy was celebrated according to custom, and each became a partaker of the most pure and life-creating Mysteries, and tasted of a little food according to custom. Then all gathered into the church; and when fervent prayer had been made and sufficient knee-bowings, the elders kissed one another, and each, embracing the Abbot, made a metania, asking to receive his blessing and prayer, to have it as an aid and companion in the struggle that lay before him. When this was done, the monastery gates were opened; and chanting in unison: *The Lord is my light and my Savior, whom shall I fear? The Lord is the defender of my life, of whom shall I be afraid?* and the rest of the Psalm, all went forth, leaving one or two elders as guardians of the monastery—not to guard the property within, for there was nothing in their possession to be stolen by thieves, but that the church might not be without divine service.[^3269]

...might not be without divine service.

For each nourished himself as he was able and as he wished: one indeed carried bread measured according to bodily necessity; another carried twice-baked bread, another dried dates, another lentils soaked in water; and another carried nothing at all, save only his body and the rags wherewith he was clothed; and he nourished himself whenever nature constrained him upon the herbs growing in the wilderness.[^3270]

Now there was a rule for each of them, and an inviolable law among them, that none should see how another lived in self-restraint, or how he passed his time. For having straightway crossed the Jordan, they dispersed far apart from one another, and made the wilderness their city; nor did any come unto another. But if one should see from afar another walking toward him, he immediately turned aside to go in the opposite direction and departed unto another place. And each lived unto himself and unto God, chanting unceasingly and partaking of food at its proper time.[^3271]

In this manner, therefore, they passed all the days of the Fast, and returned unto the monastery on the Sunday that precedes the Life-creating Resurrection of the Savior, the Forefeast of which celebration the Church has received to celebrate with the Palm Branches.[^3272] Each returned having the cultivation of his own labor, his own conscience bearing witness how he had labored and what manner of seeds of toil he had sown. And none among them asked another how or in what manner he had traversed the contest set before him. Such indeed was the monastic rule, and thus well was it accomplished. For each of them, being in the wilderness for the sake of God the Author of the contest, contended for himself, in order not to seek to please men or to practice self-restraint for display before men, being completely free from this on every side. For deeds done for the sake of men, and wickedly performed to please men, it is not even meet to say that they bring no profit unto him that performs them, but rather they become the cause of much loss unto the doer.[^3273]

At that time, therefore, Zosimas also,[^3274] according to the customary rule of the monastery, crossed the Jordan, carrying a few small things for bodily necessity on the way, and the very rags wherewith he was clothed. And he fulfilled his rule walking through the wilderness, and at the time of food he satisfied natural necessity; and he tasted of a little sleep at night, reclining upon the earth wherever the evening hour overtook him. In the deep of the morning he would go forth again upon his journey, having ever the continuous strength of ascetical endeavor. And he came into the desire (as he said) to enter into the inner wilderness, hoping to find one of the fathers dwelling in the wilderness and fasting,[^3275] who might be able to help him unto what he desired; and so he courageously held fast unto his journey...

...holding fast unto his journey, pressing forward as though toward some bright and manifest dwelling place. Having traversed a journey of twenty days, when the time of the sixth hour arrived, he halted toward the East and performed his customary prayer. For he was accustomed, having interrupted his traveling course at the appointed hours of the day, to pray and rest a little from toil; and standing, he chanted, bowed down, and thus made his prayer.[^3276]

While he was standing, chanting, and gazing toward heaven with an unswerving eye, he beheld on his right hand (where he stood chanting the sixth hour) a shadow appearing like unto a human body. At first he was seized with fear, supposing that he beheld some demonic illusion, and he began to tremble. But having signed himself with the sign of the Cross and cast off fear (for his prayer had now come to an end), he turned his eyes and saw someone in truth walking toward the south. The figure seen was unclothed, the body black, as though darkened by the heat of the sun; and the hair was white as wool, and that also short, reaching no further than down to the neck.[^3277]

Zosimas, having beheld this and being filled as with sweetness with joy at so marvelous a sight, began to run toward that side whither the figure was hastening. For he rejoiced with unspeakable joy; for in all the distance of that region he had not seen a human form, nor any form of any living creature. And when he beheld the shadow, he sought to understand what and of what manner the sight might be, hoping that he would become an eyewitness of some great marvel.[^3278]

Now when that figure saw Zosimas approaching from afar, it began to run and flee toward the inner wilderness. But Zosimas, as though forgetting his old age and accounting the toil of the way as nothing, pressed onward to overtake the fleeing figure. Thus he pursued, and that figure fled. But the running of Zosimas was swifter, and after a little while he drew near unto the one who fled. When he was near enough for his voice to be heard, Zosimas began to cry aloud, and with tears he uttered such words as these:[^3279]

**Zosimas:** "Why dost thou flee from me, an aged and sinful man, O servant of the true God? Wait for me, whosoever thou art, for the sake of God for Whose sake thou dwellest in this wilderness! Wait for me, weak and unworthy, for the sake of the hope that thou hast of recompense for thy toils! Halt and grant a prayer unto an elder, for the sake of God Who disdains no one!"[^3280]

While Zosimas was speaking these words with tears, they came running unto a certain place that resembled a dry watercourse, where, as I suppose, a stream had once flowed. Now because of the nature of such a place, when the one of whom I have spoken reached the place, that figure ran down into it and ascended again unto the other side. But Zosimas was exhausted and unable to run any further...

...unable to run any further, he stood on the other side of the dry stream-bed. And he added tears unto tears and weeping unto weeping, so that the sound of his lamentation could be heard even further. Then that fleeing body uttered these words:[^3281]

**Mary:** "Father Zosimas, forgive me for the Lord's sake, for I cannot turn about and show myself unto thee face to face in this manner; for I am a woman, and unclothed as thou seest, having the shame of the flesh uncovered. But since thou hast desired to grant a single prayer unto a sinful woman, cast unto me the cloak wherewith thou art clothed, that therewith I may cover female weakness, and turning unto thee, receive thy prayers."[^3282]

Then terror and fear seized Zosimas (as he said, and trembling), hearing that she called him Zosimas by name. For being a man of swift understanding and wise in divine things, he perceived that she would never have called him by name, whom she had never seen and of whom she had never heard, had she not been manifestly illumined by the gift of clairvoyance. Therefore he made haste to do what was commanded; and stripping off the worn and torn garment that he wore, he cast it toward her, and turned his back and stood.[^3283]

And taking it, she girded herself as best she could, covering those parts of her body that it was most necessary to cover. Then turning unto Zosimas, she said unto him:[^3284]

**Mary:** "Why did it please thee, O father, to see a sinful woman? What seekest thou to see from me or to learn, that thou hast not been sluggish to undergo so great a labor?"

He, however, fell upon his knees upon the earth, asking to receive a blessing according to custom. She likewise, seeing this, made a prostration. And both lay upon the earth, each begging to be blessed by the other; and nothing could be heard from either of them, save only: "Bless!" After a long time had passed, the woman said unto Zosimas:[^3285]

**Mary:** "Father Zosimas, it is fitting for thee to bless and to pray; for thou art honored with the rank of the priesthood, and for many years hast stood before the holy Altar, and hast many times been a minister of the divine Mysteries."

These words cast Zosimas into greater fear and awe; and trembling, the elder was bathed in tears, groaning, and his voice failed him. Then with weary and breathless speech, terrified and pale of countenance, he said unto her:[^3286]

**Zosimas:** "O spiritual Mother, that thou hast drawn near unto God, having departed from the world, and hast for the most part died unto the world, the gift granted unto thee makes manifest, in that thou hast called me by name and named me a presbyter, whom thou hast never seen! But since grace is recognized not by dignities, but is accustomed to be shown forth by the disposition of the soul, do thou bless for the Lord's sake, and grant a prayer unto me who am lesser than thy perfection!"

Having received this resistance from the elder...

...having received this resistance from the elder, the woman said:

**Mary:** "Blessed is God, Who wills the salvation of human souls!"

And Zosimas having said: "Amen," both arose from kneeling. And the woman said unto the elder:[^3287]

**Mary:** "For what cause hast thou come unto me, a sinful woman, O man? Why hast thou come to see a woman stripped of every virtue? Yet the grace of the Holy Spirit has guided thee, that thou mightest perform some service for me in an appointed time. Tell me, how does the Christian realm fare today? How are the Emperors? How are the affairs of the Church governed?"[^3288]
